title: Tyrant Abuses Me? Turn Around and Collude with the Eunuch to Seize His Empire
author: Qing Shan You Ci
synopsis:
Xiang Jun entered the palace eight years ago, striving relentlessly, currying favor everywhere, yet she was still ground down, used, humiliated, and abandoned by the noble masters of the palace...
The nobles lounged in luxury atop piles of bones, mocking her desperate efforts and ignorance of her place.
In the end, the children she had fought to bear called another woman "Mother," and she was vivisected to take the child from her womb, dying with her eyes wide open in resentment.
After her death, only that cold and distant eunuch, whom she had met but a few times, gave her a proper burial, granting her the last shred of dignity.
Upon reawakening, Xiang Jun realized she was nothing more than a cannon fodder female antagonist in a story.
In this life, Xiang Jun would carve a different path for herself.
If those noble masters refused to treat them—those of lowly birth—as human, then she would conspire with the equally lowly eunuch, stirring up storms and turning the world upside down.
"Tingxue, in this life, let us be a pair of power-hungry, scheming villains—a treacherous eunuch and a bewitching concubine."

chapters.title: Awakening
chapters.content:
"Cut her open and take the child."

After the emperor coldly issued the command outside, the four matrons inside pinned Xiang Jun’s limbs, rendering her unable to struggle.

The imperial physician’s blade, glinting with a cold light, sliced across Xiang Jun’s abdomen. Blood splattered everywhere, staining everyone’s faces.

The pain was unbearable—she wished she could die instantly.

But unfortunately, she was the most stubborn and tenacious of them all.

She didn’t die when they cut her open.

She didn’t die when they pulled the child from her womb.

Even when she was left alone in the delivery room, her abdomen splayed open, waiting for death, she still clung to life, refusing to close her eyes.

And then, in a daze, Xiang Jun awoke.

She had actually been a female antagonist in a story...

All the hatred, anger, self-improvement, and struggles of her life had been nothing more than a foil to highlight Xue Jiaojiao’s effortless grace and her refusal to compete or fight.

"Hand her three sons over to the empress to raise," the emperor’s icy voice rang out again.

Xue Jiaojiao, in her kindness, held the newborn child, wanting to give Xiang Jun one last look, as if to fulfill their mother-child bond.

Xiang Jun was already on her last breath.

She couldn’t speak, so she could only glare with venomous eyes at Xue Jiaojiao.

Xue Jiaojiao, however, looked at Xiang Jun with pity in her eyes and said, "A woman of such lowly birth, who resorts to underhanded means—having the prince reincarnate in your womb was already your fortune. Yet you were never satisfied. Now, your fate is of your own making. Rest assured, I will treat your children as my own. You may now close your eyes in peace..."

Xiang Jun’s eldest son, the seven-year-old Third Prince, stood beside Empress Xue and tugged at her sleeve. "Mother, let’s go. This place is filthy. Your shoes are stained with this lowly woman’s blood."

Hearing her own son say this, Xiang Jun finally widened her bloodshot eyes and took her last breath.

Even her own child despised her.

Xiang Jun’s resentment soared to the heavens, dying with her eyes wide open.

She reflected on her life, wondering—had she really been wrong?

But where had she gone wrong?

When she was six, her father, to save the life of his benefactor’s daughter, Xue Jiaojiao, had sent Xiang Jun’s sixteen-year-old sister to the imperial prison in her place.

Her beautiful sister, who had never known a day of luxury, was branded a criminal’s daughter and forced into military prostitution. In less than a month, she was tortured to death.

What had her sister done wrong?

When Xiang Jun saw her sister’s mangled body, she asked her father, "Father, if you wanted to repay a debt, why didn’t you go die yourself? Why did you use Sister’s life to repay it?"

That day, if Xue Jiaojiao hadn’t stopped him, her father would have beaten her to death.

Her father cursed her for being heartless, disrespectful, and ungrateful.

Xue Jiaojiao, however, hugged Xiang Jun and cried, begging her father not to hit her sister—it was all her fault.

But the more Xue Jiaojiao protected her, the more Xiang Jun hated her.

She hated her for taking her sister’s place, hated her false kindness.

Later, against her father and mother’s objections, Xue Jiaojiao insisted on going to the Qin Huai River to become a courtesan.

But less than half a year later, the new emperor ascended the throne.

The new emperor found Xue Jiaojiao on a boat, playing the guqin for the scholar Song Feijing.

Xue Jiaojiao returned to the capital and became the noble and honored Concubine Xue.

But Xiang Jun’s family, as the benefactors of Concubine Xue, did not receive any imperial rewards. Instead, they were met with the emperor’s elite guards sent to silence them.

Because the noble Concubine Xue could not have a past as a courtesan.

So, anyone who knew the truth had to die.

...

That day, the fire at the dock was enormous.

Her father was the first to be beheaded.

Then her mother was shot through the heart with an arrow.

Even her little dog, Mantou, was kicked to death.

Only Xiang Jun, as if saved by the heavens, managed to survive, hiding at the bottom of the boat, unscathed in the inferno.

At that time, Xiang Jun didn’t know that the reason she survived wasn’t divine intervention—it was because her predestined role in the story wasn’t over yet.

So, filled with hatred, she sold herself.

She was bought by a wealthy merchant from Jiangnan, who educated her meticulously for ten years.

She studied the pipa, xiao, poetry, calligraphy, painting, Go, and every kind of "lewd" skill with all her might.

All so she could be more valuable, climb higher, and be given to a noble in the capital to find an opportunity for revenge.

Fortunately, at seventeen, Xiang Jun got a chance to enter the palace.

But after eight years in the palace, scheming, vying for favor, and harming other concubines, she not only failed to bring down the female lead, Xue Jiaojiao, but also gave her three sons for free, allowing Xue Jiaojiao to ascend to the throne as empress.

It wasn’t until the moment of her death, as her consciousness flickered, that she was transported to another world and awoke to the realization that she was the villainess. She saw the entire story’s plot.

...

But what good did that do?

Her life was already over.

Xiang Jun’s soul hovered above the Forbidden Palace, watching her mangled body lying there.

A young eunuch said, "The emperor does not allow her to be buried in the concubine’s mausoleum. Wrap her in a straw mat and burn her."

In the dark of night, Xiang Jun watched as her body was dragged away, wrapped in a straw mat, and pulled along the empty palace path. She didn’t even have a complete set of clothes.

Until someone blocked the young eunuch’s path.

From afar, Xiang Jun recognized the qilin robe the man wore.

It was the qilin robe personally bestowed by the emperor upon his most trusted eunuch, Gu Tingxue—the only one in the entire court permitted to wear it.

This powerful eunuch, whom Xiang Jun had never even spoken to, defied the emperor’s decree. He had her broken body sewn back together, her skin cleaned, and dressed her in clean clothes before burying her in an unmarked grave in the outskirts of the capital.

How ridiculous.

All the nobles in the palace, who considered themselves noble, lounged in luxury atop piles of bones, yet they couldn’t perform a single act of kindness.

In the end, the one who gave Xiang Jun her final dignity was a lowly-born eunuch, just like her.

At this moment, Xiang Jun’s resentment threatened to shatter the entire Forbidden Palace.

She refused to dissipate like this, refused to let her life end so shabbily.

If she were given another chance, she wouldn’t let them off—including that high-and-mighty dog emperor!

...

"Xiang Jun, what’s wrong with you?"

Meng Mei, hearing Xiang Jun’s scream, lifted the bed curtain, only to be met with a pair of sinister, resentful eyes.

In the moonlight, the girl sitting on the bed, dressed in a white undergarment, her delicate features breathtakingly beautiful, stared blankly into the void.

Her pale face was devoid of color, and her eyes, burning with resentment, stared straight ahead, like a demon crawling out of hell.

"Xiang Jun, what’s wrong? Did you have a nightmare? Don’t scare me."

Although she was afraid, Meng Mei still grabbed Xiang Jun’s hand.

Xiang Jun looked at the familiar yet distant face before her and finally struggled free from the tidal wave of hatred, slowly regaining her senses.

"Meng Mei... it’s you..."

Xiang Jun had actually returned to eight years ago, to the time before she entered the palace.

---

chapters.title: First Meeting with Gu Tingxue
chapters.content:
"Meng Mei!"

Xiang Jun tightly hugged Meng Mei, tears falling like rain.

Meng Mei and Xiang Jun had been sold to the Xu family together.

Xiang Jun was a first-class "slim horse" (a high-ranking courtesan-in-training), allowed to study music, chess, calligraphy, and painting. Meng Mei was a third-class "slim horse," who had only learned needlework, tailoring, literacy, and accounting.

They had promised each other that no matter where Xiang Jun went in the future, she would take Meng Mei with her.

But Xiang Jun unexpectedly entered the palace, and from then on, she lost all contact with the outside world.

In her past life, when Xiang Jun finally found out what had happened to Meng Mei, she was already dead.

In the second year after Xiang Jun left Jiangnan, Meng Mei had been sold to a fifty-year-old minor official as his second wife. She died less than two years later from abuse.

"What’s wrong? Did something happen?"

Xiang Jun, tears in her eyes, gripped Meng Mei’s hand and shook her head.

"It’s nothing. I just had a nightmare."

"That’s good. You scared me to death. Hurry up and get dressed. The master is looking for you."

"Now?" Xiang Jun glanced outside. It wasn’t even dawn yet.

Meng Mei worryingly said, "The master returned from the Provincial Administration Office two hours ago. He’s been alone in the study ever since. Then he opened the door and called for you. I don’t know what it’s about."

Xiang Jun remembered what day it was.

Today was the day the master was sending her to the Salt Inspection Censor, Gu Tingxue.

...

Half a month ago, a powerful eunuch had arrived in the capital from the imperial court.

This eunuch, by imperial decree, had been appointed as the Salt Inspection Censor and led three thousand elite imperial guards to Jiangnan to investigate the illegal salt trade. Upon his arrival, he had executed over a dozen officials.

Master Xu, Xiang Jun’s owner, was one of the largest salt merchants involved in the illegal trade.

He couldn’t escape the investigation, so he tried to use his connections in the Provincial Administration Office to bribe and flatter the Salt Inspection Censor. He had already sent three beautiful women to him, but the censor had accepted them without even meeting them. He simply kept them in a separate courtyard and continued his busy schedule.

So, Master Xu gritted his teeth, stamped his foot, and made the painful decision to send Xiang Jun.

Xiang Jun was the treasure he had been saving to sell at a high price, but now, with his life at stake, he had no choice.

Xiang Jun, following the master’s orders, was carried in a small sedan chair to the residence of the Suzhou General.

This general had been beheaded by Lord Gu a half-month ago for his involvement in the illegal salt trade.

Now, the residence was occupied by none other than the Salt Inspection Censor, Commander of the Imperial Guards, and the powerful eunuch, Lord Gu Tingxue.

After the sedan chair stopped, a guard led Xiang Jun inside.

Xiang Jun, holding her pipa, walked and recalled.

In her past life, she had gone through this same experience.

But unfortunately, Lord Gu hadn’t even seen her.

Just like the three beautiful women sent before her, Xiang Jun was thrown into a separate courtyard upon arrival. She had food and drink, but no contact with the outside world.

A month later, Xiang Jun and eleven other "Yangzhou slim horses" were secretly taken to the capital and entered the palace as musicians of the Imperial Music Bureau.

At that time, all twelve of them had been filled with hope, believing that with their beauty and talents, they would have a chance to become imperial concubines.

Little did they know, it was only the beginning of their tragedy.

It wasn’t until she awoke to the full plot that Xiang Jun realized they had all been brought to the palace to "treat" the emperor’s illness.

The emperor had been poisoned by a rare toxin from Nanyue. Every month, for several days, he would turn into a ravenous, violent beast.

The cure was simple: release all the poison from his body.

The noble consorts in the palace were naturally above being used as the emperor’s tools for release.

So, the emperor had people search far and wide for lowly commoner women to bring into the palace.

The dog emperor had high standards—he didn’t want daughters from good families, but they had to be virgins, and they couldn’t be ugly, lest they offend his imperial eyes.

Their batch was the third and final group of beautiful women sent into the palace.

Out of the thirty-six women across the three batches, all but Xiang Jun had been tortured to death.

They weren’t people—they were nothing more than the emperor’s discarded medicine.

Xiang Jun tightened her grip on the pipa.

When she awoke, Xiang Jun not only saw the complete story in that otherworldly illusion but also read tens of thousands of "comments and reviews."

Xiang Jun had already summarized the reasons for her utter failure in her past life: lowly birth, acting alone, showing off her talents, and becoming arrogant after success.

This time, she couldn’t repeat the same mistakes and enter the palace the same way.

She not only needed to give herself a higher status but also find a reliable ally.

Gu Tingxue, the eunuch who had buried her—perhaps he would help her.

...

"The lord is resting. I’ll take you to the side courtyard to rest," the guard announced.

Xiang Jun saw that the lights in the room were still bright—Gu Tingxue must still be awake.

She knew she only had one chance.

"Could you trouble you to relay another message? I’ve heard Lord Gu enjoys music. This servant is skilled with the pipa, especially *Hegemon King Doffs His Armor*. I’d like to ask Lord Gu to appraise it."

After saying this, Xiang Jun also slipped the guard a pouch of money.

The guard accepted it and went back inside to relay her request.

Xiang Jun was nervous. If she couldn’t meet Gu Tingxue today, she would be sent into the palace as a "cure."

She didn’t dare imagine having to go through the emperor’s bedchamber again...

In her past life, the first time she had served the emperor, he had been like a mad beast.

Xiang Jun had been carried out of the Tai Chi Hall covered in blood, even her hands—her hands that played the pipa—broken.

She had been left to die in the servants’ quarters. If not for a shadowy figure who had forced a life-saving medicine down her throat when she was burning with fever, she would have died long ago.

...

"Follow me."

The guard’s voice pulled Xiang Jun from her memories.

Gu Tingxue was willing to see her?

Xiang Jun suppressed her excitement, gave a shy smile, and quickly followed the guard inside, still holding her pipa.

The door behind her was closed again by the guard outside. Xiang Jun, holding her pipa, walked into the main room.

The main room was lit, but there was no one there.

Suddenly, a man’s voice came from somewhere.

"Come this way."

She hadn’t seen him yet, but she heard his voice first.

Xiang Jun realized this was the first time in two lifetimes she had heard Gu Tingxue’s voice.

In her past life, she hadn’t been worthy of speaking to Gu Tingxue.

To her surprise, Gu Tingxue’s voice was unlike any other eunuch she had met—it wasn’t sharp or piercing but deep and melodious.

"West warm chamber," Gu Tingxue said again.

His voice was soft, but the emphasis was clear, like a muffled drum beating in one’s heart, making her feel a sudden flutter.

chapters.title: How Do You Want Me to Cherish You
chapters.content:
Xiangjun followed the sound and walked over.

She saw a green gauze curtain hanging in the warm pavilion, with two lamps lit beside it.

The light was not too bright, and in the hazy glow, Xiangjun saw someone with loose hair sitting inside the gauze curtain.

The person held a book in their hand, looking relaxed and somewhat languid.

This must be Gu Tingxue.

Xiangjun gracefully bowed. "Xiangjun greets Lord Gu."

The person inside the gauze curtain was still reading, their voice tinged with weariness. "Play."

Without another word, Xiangjun sat down with her pipa and began to play *The Hegemon Removes His Armor*.

In her past life, though her hands had been broken and she could no longer play the pipa, she often accompanied the emperor to listen to music.

Once, a musician played *The Hegemon Removes His Armor*, and the emperor casually remarked, "This is Tingxue's favorite piece, but no one plays it to his satisfaction."

At that time, Xiangjun thought that if her hands hadn't been broken during her first night with the emperor, she could have played it better than any court musician.

Who cares what kind of "snow" he is? He would definitely be satisfied.

That was why Xiangjun had taken the initiative to play this piece today.

In her past life, she had schemed endlessly, only to meet utter failure. She had considered herself extraordinary, yet ended up with a heart full of sorrow and resentment—fitting the mood of this very piece.

The person inside the green gauze curtain seemed moved as well. Slowly putting down the book, they looked through the gauze at the young woman playing.

A girl in her teens, yet she played the piece with such depth and sorrow—it was truly unusual.

After the song ended, Gu Tingxue slowly asked, "Why did you play this piece?"

Xiangjun pondered how to answer to satisfy Gu Tingxue...

She didn't know why Lord Gu favored this piece, nor had the emperor ever explained.

In the storybooks, Gu Tingxue was merely a supporting character, a eunuch who handled the emperor's dirty work. There wasn't much description about him.

Xiangjun thought for a moment and decided on a safe answer.

"The king's intentions were not in vain, only Yuji and Zheng Jun remained loyal." Xiangjun's voice was soft and enchanting, like a nightingale's song. She spoke shyly, "This servant admires Yuji's unwavering loyalty, following her lord even in death."

A faint, almost inaudible scoff came from inside the gauze curtain.

"Enough. You may leave."

Xiangjun's heart sank.

That was the wrong answer.

But it was fine—he didn't sound angry, just slightly mocking.

Xiangjun couldn't leave.

Though she felt a pang of anxiety, her face remained the picture of pitiful innocence.

The book had mentioned that Gu Tingxue had helped her three times in her past life without her knowing.

Even if she didn't understand why he had shown her kindness three times, someone who had helped you once was more likely to help you again.

Gu Tingxue handled the emperor's affairs and knew that these "Yangzhou skinny horses" sent to the palace were being sent to their deaths.

If he had even a shred of pity or kindness for her and was willing to give her a way out, she could enter the capital under a different identity.

Xiangjun slowly put down the pipa and walked to the front of the gauze curtain, kneeling on the footstool before the warm pavilion.

"Please, Lord Gu, have mercy on this servant. Give me a way out, allow me to stay and serve you."

Xiangjun looked at the person inside the gauze curtain with her most pitiful and moving expression.

She decided to take a gamble.

A eunuch known for being cold-blooded and ruthless—why would he help a lowly singer? Unless it was because of her face?

They had no prior connection. Maybe she resembled someone? Or perhaps he simply liked her appearance?

Xiangjun knew how to exploit her body's appeal to the fullest.

She lifted her head, hoping he would get a better look at her face.

When Gu Tingxue lifted the gauze curtain, he saw a face that was both alluring and sorrowful, as if she had suffered the greatest injustice.

What a shame—he despised pitiful looks the most.

...

When Gu Tingxue's long, fair hand lightly lifted the gauze curtain, Xiangjun was prepared to see a handsome face.

But when she did, her heart still raced at the sight.

It was a face so handsome it bordered on the demonic.

Especially those danfeng eyes, slightly upturned at the ends, with a captivating and commanding presence.

Gu Tingxue wore only a white inner robe, loosely tied, revealing a large expanse of solid muscle.

A eunuch, yet he looked so firm and imposing.

Xiangjun recalled that in her past life, she had seen him a few times.

But each time was at a palace banquet. With her low status and lack of the emperor's favor, she was always seated far from the emperor, so she could only catch fleeting glimpses of Gu Tingxue.

She had also heard the palace maids gossip about him. It seemed many palace maids secretly admired him.

There were even rumors that the noble consort herself favored him.

Unfortunately, Xiangjun had been consumed by thoughts of revenge and paid little attention to such matters.

In her memory, Gu Tingxue's image was vague.

She only remembered that his demeanor was too noble for a eunuch. Though he was a servant, he always stood straight and proper, elegant and cold. Even when bowing, his back remained perfectly straight.

This was the first time Xiangjun had made eye contact with Gu Tingxue.

With just one glance, she felt a chill run through her body.

Why was he so different from what she had imagined?

Gu Tingxue's gaze was too cold and sinister. When he looked at people, he resembled a venomous snake, ready to strike at any moment.

But Xiangjun hesitated only for a moment before stepping forward and gently embracing Gu Tingxue's leg.

In the next instant, her eyes filled with tears.

She had practiced in front of the mirror—her look of pear blossoms in the rain, tears on the verge of falling, was the most pitiful sight.

With a choked, tender voice, she pleaded, "If my family's master finds out I haven't gained your favor, he will surely think me useless. I don't want to be punished. Please, my lord, have some pity on me."

As she spoke, her hand seemingly unintentionally climbed up Gu Tingxue's thigh.

Xiangjun knew that eunuchs had desires too.

In fact, a eunuch's desires could be even more intense than those of ordinary men. Because their desires could never be truly satisfied.

Gu Tingxue's gaze fell on the small, fair, tender, and incredibly nimble hand.

Quite bold, unafraid of him.

The corner of his mouth hooked slightly, but his snake-like eyes grew even colder.

"Oh? How do you expect me to pity you? I am a eunuch. I don't pity people. Everyone in this world knows that what I am best at is killing."

Xiangjun watched Gu Tingxue's expression change and thought, *This is not good.*

What was happening?

Gu Tingxue's expression... seemed to indicate he was annoyed by her?

Could it be... he didn't like the pitiful act?

---

chapters.title: Do You Want Me Dead
chapters.content:
Xiangjun's mind raced as she recalled the fragments of information about Gu Tingxue from the storybooks.

Suddenly, she remembered a passage:

[The young eunuch reported to Gu Tingxue about the condition of the twelve singers who had been sent.

This month, three of the singers had already served the emperor. Two were dragged out of the Tai Ji Hall and died that very night. Following Lord Gu's instructions, they had been properly buried.

But there was a pipa player named Xiangjun. Perhaps because the emperor particularly favored her, she had been tormented the most—her arm was even broken.

Everyone thought such a young girl wouldn't survive the night, but Xiangjun had lasted seven days without dying.

Every time the young eunuch delivered meals, she would beg him to call a physician, promising any favor in return. She even said that once she became a proper consort, she would take him as her chief eunuch. As if she had any say in such matters.

But today, when he went to deliver food, she had developed a high fever. It seemed she wouldn't last much longer.

Gu Tingxue rarely smiled upon hearing this.

He said: *She's a tough one with ambition. Then I'll help her once. The rest will depend on her luck.*]

Recalling this passage, Xiangjun suddenly had an epiphany.

Could it be that Lord Gu didn't like women who appeared pitiful but actually admired those who were resilient and ambitious?

Suddenly, Gu Tingxue pinched Xiangjun's chin.

His cold eyes now held a hint of killing intent. "Speak. How do you want me to cherish you?"

Xiangjun decided to gamble again and immediately changed her strategy.

A fierce ambition flashed in Xiangjun's eyes. She gritted her teeth and put on a desperate look.

"Please help me, my lord. This servant no longer wishes to be a pipa player. I want to enter the palace to serve the emperor. Please grant my wish."

Gu Tingxue finally stopped looking at her with disdain.

The corner of his mouth slightly lifted, showing a hint of interest.

"You?" Gu Tingxue scoffed. "A lowly pipa player dares to dream of becoming a palace consort?"

Xiangjun's gaze was resolute.

"Why can't I? I may be of low birth, but with your influence, Lord Gu, raising my status would be no difficult task. I am confident that in terms of beauty and talent, I am no worse than the noble consorts in the palace. Moreover, a renowned monk once read my fortune and said I would bear three sons in this life. If I must bear children for someone, why not for the most noble man in the world?"

Of course, the part about the monk was a lie Xiangjun had fabricated.

She said this because she knew Gu Tingxue had another task to handle during his trip to Jiangnan.

The emperor's favored consort, Xue Jiaojiao, also known as Rong Guifei, had enjoyed his favor for many years but had yet to bear any children.

The emperor, pitying her lack of support, wanted to find a woman of humble background to help her secure her favor by bearing children. He specifically sought someone with a face and birth chart suitable for bearing sons.

Once she had borne a few children, he would find a way to separate mother from child, eliminating any future trouble. After all, it wasn't uncommon for consorts to die of illness in the palace.

The emperor had entrusted this task to Gu Tingxue.

In the book, Gu Tingxue had brought a young woman from a minor official's family in Jiangnan back to the palace, claiming that a fortune-teller had deemed her the perfect candidate for bearing sons.

However, the woman had a beloved, and the distress of this situation, combined with the arduous journey, led to her falling ill and dying soon after arriving in the capital, before she could even serve the emperor.

When Rong Guifei learned of what the emperor had done for her, she was both touched and angry that he had caused the death of an innocent woman for her sake.

She refused to allow the emperor to do such a thing again.

How could she, in good conscience, take another woman's child? If there were motherless children, she would be willing to help raise them, but she could never bring herself to separate a mother from her child.

The two quarreled for a while until the emperor swore never to do such a thing again. Only then did Rong Guifei forgive him and reconcile.

The young woman from the minor official's family had died pointlessly and mysteriously.

If Xiangjun took her place, she would be saving that woman's life.

Anyway, Xiangjun wasn't afraid of being separated from her child. This time, entering the palace, she would either be a tool for pleasure or a tool for reproduction.

A tool for reproduction could at least live a little longer.

Gu Tingxue seemed to finally take some interest in Xiangjun's words.

He lifted her chin, examining her face from all angles. Her face was as beautiful as a peach blossom, flawless from every perspective. He smiled in satisfaction.

Hmm, she seemed usable.

But to survive in the palace, to make it to the end, it took more than just a pretty face and the ability to play the pipa.

"What makes you think I should help you? What's in it for me?"

Xiangjun thought for a moment. This man already held great power, and as a eunuch, he couldn't become emperor. She truly had nothing to offer him.

So, Xiangjun let her peach-blossom eyes well up with tears, and in a coquettish voice, she said, "This servant is willing to serve you, my lord."

"Oh? You're willing to serve a eunuch?"

Xiangjun seemed to scoff at such worldly notions. "What does it matter if he's a eunuch?"

Xiangjun's small hand once again climbed up Gu Tingxue's body.

"Lord Gu, a eunuch is still a man, with a man's desires. As long as..."

Xiangjun's actions were bold, but her expression was shy.

Because she knew that men were all the same—they enjoyed wantonness but didn't want others to know, fearing it made them seem vulgar.

So, it was best to appear reserved in public but be alluring in private. That was the most pleasing.

Xiangjun's entire face blushed with shame.

"As long as what?"

"This servant has learned every way to serve a man... Lord Gu, I can definitely bring you relief. My lord, please let me try..."

Xiangjun carefully observed Gu Tingxue's reaction.

His hand lightly clenched, then relaxed. Then, in that deep, melodious voice, he softly said, "A eunuch is still a man? You're the only one who thinks so."

"Does being a man or not have anything to do with that thing?"

Xiangjun's hand began to untie her own clothes, revealing her fair, smooth shoulders and the pink undershirt beneath.

She was all in. When two strangers wanted to cooperate, one side had to make the first sacrifice.

This kind of relationship, if discovered, was punishable by death. It was the best way to bind two people together.

"To this servant, the one who saves me from despair is the true man."

Xiangjun slowly stood up and wrapped her arms around Gu Tingxue's waist.

It was slender but seemed strong.

She looked at him with seductive eyes, her gaze like rippling spring water. She didn't believe he could remain unmoved by her.

Suddenly, a powerful force pushed Xiangjun onto the bed.

Gu Tingxue grabbed her by the throat and squeezed tightly, almost cutting off her breath.

"You must not want to live."

Gu Tingxue's mouth held a smile, but his voice was ice-cold.

"You want me to send you into the palace as a consort, yet you also want to serve me. Do you know that if this ever comes to light, it will be a crime punishable by death? Do you want to kill me?"

chapters.title: The Troublesome Woman
chapters.content:
On the bed, Xiangjun’s clothes were in disarray, her outer robe completely undone from her struggles. Her skin, pale as light, was dazzling to the eye.

Gu Tingxue’s gaze flickered imperceptibly away from her delicate shoulders, only to meet a pair of wide, innocent eyes like those of a startled fawn.

For some reason, Xiangjun felt certain that Gu Tingxue would not kill her.

After all, he was the only person in her life who had helped her without asking for anything in return. He took no money, showed no lust for her body, and even did good deeds without leaving his name.

So, even if others saw him as a merciless killer, a living Yama, Xiangjun believed Gu Tingxue was the only good man in the entire imperial capital.

There was not a trace of fear in her eyes. She gently placed her hand on his, her gaze filled only with grievance, not fear or blame.

Seeing Xiangjun’s face flush slightly from the mild suffocation, Gu Tingxue felt a strange and unfamiliar sensation stir in his heart.

As if startled by his own thoughts, he released his grip.

With his hand loosened, the thought of killing her vanished like smoke.

Gu Tingxue impatiently snapped, “Get out.”

Yet the moment he let go, the woman shamelessly wrapped her arms around his waist again.

The red marks on her neck were still visible, and she hadn’t even caught her breath before she started seducing him again.

“My lord, I truly wish to serve you with all my heart.”

Xiangjun lifted her head, looking at Gu Tingxue as if he were the love of her life.

If Gu Tingxue didn’t know this was their first meeting, he might have thought they had been in love for years, deeply devoted to each other.

Hmph, what an actress.

With such skill, she’d thrive in the imperial harem.

“I guarantee, no one else will ever know about this,” Xiangjun added.

Gu Tingxue laughed, deliberately threatening, “Oh? So eager to serve me. Why not just follow me? Then you won’t have to serve the emperor.”

Xiangjun didn’t flinch in the slightest.

“But I still have three children to bear in this life. My lord, you are so young and will surely live a long life. Even for the sake of your future glory and wealth, I must consider your best interests. I’ll bear the children first, then stay by your side forever.”

Her words practically declared that the emperor wouldn’t outlive Gu Tingxue—utter treason.

Yet Gu Tingxue’s tone was teasing. “You’ve got quite the nerve, spouting such nonsense.”

Xiangjun took it as agreement. She reached out to untie his belt, but her hands were suddenly seized.

“My lord? You’re hurting me…”

She pouted, looking like a wronged little wife neglected by her husband.

Gu Tingxue hadn’t expected to find such a bold woman on his trip to Jiangnan.

Truly, she was relentless.

“This official is loyal to His Majesty. If I hear you speak such treasonous words again, I will surely kill you.”

He said he would kill her, but there was no real intent in his voice.

Xiangjun, tears welling in her eyes, nodded obediently. “Yes, my lord. I understand. You are the most loyal, devoted only to His Majesty. I dare not speak out of turn again.”

Gu Tingxue suspected she was mocking him, but he found no evidence.

His expression darkened. “Get off the bed.”

Xiangjun, sensing she had pushed far enough, reluctantly climbed down, not even bothering to fix her clothes. She knelt by the bed, her bare shoulders exposed, looking pitiful.

“Why are you still kneeling there?” he demanded.

“My lord, you haven’t answered my earlier request…”

Gu Tingxue had never encountered such a shameless person.

They had just met, and she dared to cling to him for help.

Did she truly believe she was so irresistibly beautiful, or did she think he, Gu Tingxue, was a lecher?

“If you pester me any further, I will kill you. Get out.”

Xiangjun had no choice but to rise, pouting as she slowly fastened her robe, sneaking glances at Gu Tingxue all the while.

Gu Tingxue could tell—she wasn’t afraid of him at all.

In this world, apart from the emperor, the empress dowager, and that favored imperial concubine whom the emperor doted on, she was the first person who showed no fear of him.

Seeing that Gu Tingxue had no intention of stopping her, Xiangjun picked up her pipa and left, turning back every few steps.

She moved so slowly that even an ant could have outpaced her.

Watching her sluggish retreat, Gu Tingxue felt an inexplicable surge of irritation.

He had never met anyone so exasperating.

Suddenly, a voice came from behind her:

“I can help you, but only this once. After that, your fate is in your own hands.”

Xiangjun turned in excitement at the words she had been waiting for.

But before she could speak, Gu Tingxue continued, “I’ll count to three. If you’re still in my sight, our deal is off.”

Xiangjun didn’t dare linger. She turned and fled like a bird, without a hint of hesitation.

Gu Tingxue, for some reason, felt a strange sense of frustration.

After a long silence, he spoke to the empty room: “Investigate her.”

“Yes.”

A sharp, cold voice came from the rafters, followed by a shadow leaping down and swiftly exiting.

After such a commotion, Gu Tingxue lay back down, but sleep eluded him.

He tried to pick up the book he had set aside earlier, but a faint, lingering fragrance clung to his nose, refusing to fade.

The woman had only been on his bed for a short while, yet the scent persisted. No wonder she was called Xiangjun—Fragrant Lady.

The fragrance annoyed him.

“Someone, change the bedsheets for me.”

---

Xiangjun was escorted to a separate courtyard to stay after leaving the room.

Today, though she had secured Gu Tingxue’s promise to help her once, she still felt a pang of disappointment.

Because she hadn’t slept with him.

It wasn’t that she lusted after his body, nor that she was willing to degrade herself to serve a eunuch.

She had simply wanted to test his courage.

What a shame. If he wouldn’t even sleep with the emperor’s future woman, he probably wouldn’t dare conspire with her to kill the emperor either.

Xiangjun sighed. In this world, finding someone as bold and ambitious as her was truly difficult.

---

Over the next few days, Xiangjun stayed in a side courtyard of the General’s residence. Unlike her past life, two matrons arrived at her courtyard the very next day.

Rumor had it these two had once served in the palace, and Gu Tingxue had specifically sent them to teach Xiangjun proper etiquette.

Xiangjun breathed a sigh of relief. She had temporarily escaped the fate of being a mere tool for the emperor’s pleasure.

After all, a simple tool for the emperor’s pleasure and health didn’t need to learn such rules.

The matrons, under Gu Tingxue’s orders, were extremely strict in their teaching.

But Xiangjun proved to be an excellent student. No matter how long she had to stand, she endured without complaint, even seeming to enjoy it. The matrons were quite pleased with her.

When the news reached Gu Tingxue, he said little, only ordering the matrons to continue with the strictest standards, not allowing Xiangjun to have it too easy.

So when Gu Tingxue came to see her, Xiangjun had three large bowls of water balanced on her head and shoulders, having already stood for half a day.

---

chapters.title: Dowry Required
chapters.content:
“Lord Gu, why have you come?”

Upon seeing Gu Tingxue enter, Xiangjun beamed as if his visit were the greatest joy in the world.

Looking at the three large bowls on her, Gu Tingxue scoffed. “You can still smile?”

“Why can’t I smile?”

“Aren’t you suffering?”

“I’m not afraid of hardship. As long as I can become better, I’ll endure any hardship with joy.”

Even as a courtesan in Yangzhou, she had to learn etiquette, but not the kind for the palace.

Women like them were never meant to be proper wives, so they learned the manners of a concubine.

Standing perfectly straight wasn’t important; standing with weak, swaying grace to evoke pity was.

If she were just a concubine in a wealthy household, winning her master’s heart with a bit of petty behavior wouldn’t matter much.

But in the palace, every concubine had a rank. No matter how they behaved in private, when walking through the palace, the most important thing was to appear dignified and composed.

In her past life, because no one had taught her palace etiquette, she was often mocked and punished by the noble consorts for her “vulgar” demeanor.

This time, someone was willing to teach her, and she was overjoyed—how could she find it hard?

“I only hope to make the matrons more satisfied with me each day,” Xiangjun added.

This pleased Gu Tingxue.

Not bad. She was teachable.

Gu Tingxue picked up his teacup, took a sip, and said slowly, “You’re quite ambitious.”

“Naturally. In everything I do, I strive to be the best.”

“Other women value knowing their place, avoiding competition, fearing standing out too much. Aren’t you afraid?”

Xiangjun thought of the noble concubine in the palace and couldn’t help but sneer. “That’s because they don’t have to compete or fight—someone will feed them without effort. I was sold at seven. To eat, I had to fight. To learn skills, I had to fight. Even to find a good master, I had to fight. If I hadn’t fought to be the best in everything, I would’ve been sent to some ancient old man as a concubine long ago. How would I have the chance to stand before Lord Gu and receive your guidance?”

Gu Tingxue raised an eyebrow. “You make it sound as if you endured all that suffering just to stand before me.”

Xiangjun still smiled sweetly. “I didn’t suffer for you, my lord. But now that I’ve met you, I feel all my past suffering was worth it.”

Gu Tingxue’s expression shifted, and for some reason, he seemed annoyed again.

“Save those words for the emperor when you enter the palace.”

Xiangjun huffed coquettishly. “I wouldn’t say such things to the emperor. These words, I’ll only ever say to you, my lord.”

After all, that dog emperor didn’t like strong, competitive women. He preferred delicate, helpless little flowers.

“Flattery and false affection.”

“How does my lord know my words aren’t sincere?”

Xiangjun, with three bowls balanced on her, slowly approached where Gu Tingxue sat.

She walked with perfect stability, not a drop of water spilling, exuding both poise and a delicate beauty. It was unclear how she managed it.

As if showing off her balance, she even knelt halfway beside Gu Tingxue, lightly resting her hand on his knee.

“My lord, would you like to hear my true heart?”

Gu Tingxue narrowed his eyes. This woman was always scheming to seduce.

The lingering fragrance at his nose stirred strange emotions in him again.

“I said I’d help you once. Don’t waste your efforts, young lady.”

Gu Tingxue abruptly stood, and the gust from his movement forced Xiangjun to stumble back. She barely managed to keep the bowls from falling, but the water splashed out.

Especially the bowl on her head—it drenched her completely!

Seeing her disheveled state, Gu Tingxue finally felt satisfied.

He turned his back to her, smiling as he walked out.

Xiangjun, furious, stood up and glared at his retreating figure, stomping her foot in frustration.

What a waste of her charm on a blind man!

Suddenly, Gu Tingxue turned around, startling her. She quickly resumed her soft, delicate demeanor.

“Lord Gu, do you have more business with me?”

“Your old master wishes to see you. I’ve allowed him to enter the residence in three days.”

“Really? Thank you, Lord Gu!”

Gu Tingxue glanced at her drenched head and added, “The water’s spilled. It shows your practice isn’t good enough. Keep the bowls on for another hour.”

Xiangjun looked aggrieved.

“Yes… I understand, my lord.”

---

Three days later, Master Xu San entered the residence with a calling card.

This was something that had never happened in her past life.

This time, Master Xu San was permitted to visit because Gu Tingxue had previously sent word, stating that Xiangjun would be entered into the Xu family’s genealogy as his daughter, a lady of the Suzhou Xu clan, before entering the palace as an imperial concubine.

Upon receiving this news, Master Xu San had been so overjoyed that he had jumped in excitement.

In the days since, he had swiftly arranged for Xiangjun’s entry into the family registry.

Today, he had finally been granted permission to see her.

The moment Master Xu San entered the room, Xiangjun immediately knelt before him. Before he could react, she had already cried out emotionally, “Honorable Father!”

Master Xu San was taken aback. He had always known this girl was quick to adapt, saying whatever suited the person she was with.

But to call him “Father” so quickly still caught him off guard.

Master Xu San cleared his throat and helped her up.

“Child, rise at once. Don’t kneel and hurt yourself.”

Xiangjun, tears streaming, let him help her up.

“Xiangjun has drifted through half her life. From now on, she finally has a father, a maternal family, a reliance! Honorable Father, rest assured—once Xiangjun enters the palace, she will serve His Majesty well and bring blessings to the family!”

After they sat down, Xiangjun served Master Xu San tea. After a few pleasantries, she finally revealed her true purpose.

“Honorable Father, Xiangjun has the family’s best interests at heart. However, Xiangjun has nothing to her name. The palace is a complex place, and many things will require… greasing palms. I don’t understand these matters, so I’ll need Father to help me think them through.”

Xiangjun’s goal today was to ask Master Xu San for money.

In her past life, she had entered the palace with nothing but a few hairpins, which left her struggling even after bearing a prince and receiving the emperor’s rewards. In the depths of the palace, she had lived in constant hardship.

After all, plotting required money.

This time, before entering the palace, she was determined to secure both wealth and connections. She couldn’t afford to lack either.

Thus, she needed Master Xu San to provide a dowry.

Master Xu San hadn’t expected her to be so direct.

But then again, that was exactly why he had come today. He agreed immediately.

“Rest assured, my child. Your father will arrange everything for you.”

“Father is a busy man. How could I bear to trouble you? So I’ve prepared a list of everything I need. Father can follow it to make the arrangements, and if there’s anything I’ve overlooked, Father can add it.”

Xiangjun handed him a list.

Master Xu San skimmed it, and his eyelids twitched uncontrollably.

Gold, silver, fine fabrics, jewelry, rare medicines—everything on the list was fit for palace use.

And this girl was truly clever. The list was both exorbitant and cunningly calculated to be just painful enough for him, yet not so much that he could refuse.

chapters.title: Entering the Family Genealogy
chapters.content:
Old Master glanced at Xiangjun, seemingly hesitant.

Xiangjun smiled and said, "Old Master, if one day I become a concubine and perhaps bear a son or a daughter, our entire Xu family will truly have a powerful backing."

Xu San, the Old Master, thought about how this girl had even managed to win over Lord Gu, making him go to such lengths for her, and how she, a mere Yangzhou courtesan, was being sent into the palace as a concubine. He realized that this girl was far more formidable than he had thought.

Hmm, she was worth the gamble.

"Look at what you're saying. You are my daughter, and of course I care for you. Whatever I have, I will give to you. As long as you live well in the palace, I will be content. Don’t worry, I will have these things sent to you in a few days."

Xiangjun was satisfied and added, "Let me take Mengmei and Mengzhu with me as well."

"Mengzhu too?" Old Master Xu was truly reluctant to part with Mengzhu.

Mengzhu and Mengmei were siblings. Mengzhu was the elder brother, and his younger sister Mengmei was nine years old.

The siblings were born in a brothel. Due to a stroke of luck, Mengzhu had become the apprentice of a divine doctor who was being hunted by his enemies.

He had learned medical skills and, combined with his natural talent and upbringing in the brothel, he became particularly skilled in treating various gynecological diseases.

When Old Master had bought them, it was mainly for Mengzhu’s skills; Mengmei was just an added bonus.

"Father, Mengzhu will be most useful to me. Think carefully..."

Old Master pondered and realized she was right.

As long as Mengzhu could help Xiangjun bear a prince, the Xu family would have nothing to worry about.

"But Mengzhu is a man. How can he enter the palace with you?"

"He has the skills, so naturally, he will have the opportunity."

The noble concubine in the palace had been favored for many years but could not bear children. If she knew there was a medical expert in folk medicine, she would surely invite him to the palace to regulate her body.

"Alright, take both Mengzhu and Mengmei."

Seeing how generous Old Master was, Xiangjun decided to help him as well.

In her previous life, this smuggling case had implicated Old Master.

Now that he was her father, Xiangjun naturally wanted to protect him.

"Father, the illegal salt trade has always been happening in secret among the people. Do you know why the court is taking such drastic measures this time, insisting on punishing you salt merchants?"

"Did Lord Gu tell you something?" Old Master looked tense and somewhat surprised. How did Lord Gu end up telling Xiangjun about such matters?

Of course, Lord Gu had not told her anything.

Xiangjun could only vaguely say, "Father, it's better to sacrifice wealth to preserve life."

There was nothing harder than making a merchant abandon their wealth.

Seeing Old Master’s expression change instantly, Xiangjun added, "The first to surrender will gain the greatest benefit. Those who follow will lose both their lives and wealth."

Seeing that Old Master still didn’t understand, Xiangjun continued to persuade him gently:

"The court wants money and doesn’t care about the troubles in Jiangnan. After the matter is settled, Jiangnan will still need salt merchants to continue their business. By then, those who deserve to die will be dead, and Father will have gone from being one of the largest salt merchants in Jiangnan to the largest. Are you afraid that the wealth you give up won’t be recovered?"

Xiangjun knew that many people would die in this incident. The court needed money for war, and Gu Tingxue needed to raise funds for the emperor. Unfortunately, these wealthy merchants were all miserly.

Eventually, the emperor’s wrath would lead to thousands of corpses floating down the river, and many of the old masters she knew would be beheaded.

Old Master Xu was also a shrewd man. He knew that this matter could not end well, so he finally gritted his teeth and nodded.

"Daughter, rest assured. Father understands. Our Xu family will not hold you back."

The two exchanged a few more false pleasantries before Old Master finally left.

...

The next day, Xu San went directly to the yamen where Gu Tingxue was stationed.

Not only did he voluntarily donate a huge amount of silver as military pay, but he also provided evidence of the salt merchants' illegal salt trading.

Over the next half month, the entire Jiangnan region was engulfed in bloodshed.

Someone had calculated that in just half a month, Gu Tingxue had beheaded over a thousand people.

Following that, there were confiscations of property and imprisonments.

The entire Xu family became the only salt merchant family to survive the storm.

Only then did Old Master Xu realize that Xiangjun’s words had truly saved his life. So, he quickly had more dowry added for Xiangjun, as if he wanted to empty out his entire fortune.

It wasn’t until the case was closed that Gu Tingxue arranged for someone to take Xiangjun to the Xu family ancestral hall.

After paying respects to the ancestors and meeting the clan elders, Xiangjun, now officially a Xu family girl, boarded the carriage and set off for the capital without delay.

As she was getting into the carriage, Lord Gu suddenly appeared again, giving Xiangjun a hand as she boarded.

"Lord Gu!" Xiangjun still wore that look of tender affection and surprised delight.

Gu Tingxue remained unmoved and said in a low voice, "Miss Xu has surprised me."

Xiangjun didn’t know what Gu Tingxue was referring to.

Seeing her confusion, Gu Tingxue added, "To make the Xu family cut their losses to survive, Miss Xu is quite decisive. With such determination, you will surely have a bright future in the palace."

Xiangjun smiled and thanked Gu Tingxue.

"Then I will take Lord Gu’s kind words to heart."

Gu Tingxue nodded at her, then turned and mounted his horse, riding to the front of the procession without looking back. For the rest of the journey back to the capital, Xiangjun did not see this elusive lord again.

...

The carriage finally reached the official road.

Looking at Mengmei sitting beside her, Xiangjun finally let out a sigh of relief.

Mengzhu had already, through Old Master’s recommendation and his medical skills, gained Lord Gu’s recognition. He would enter the capital under the alias Liu Xiuzhu, and Gu Tingxue would arrange for him to enter the palace. She didn’t need to worry about him.

She had finally taken the first step, and her fate would be rewritten from here.

In this life, Xiangjun had a humble but not despicable status, a considerable amount of wealth, trustworthy sisters by her side, a reliable doctor, and Lord Gu’s "three points of affection upon meeting."

Although compared to the noble ladies in the capital, what she had was still insignificant, it was already infinitely better than her previous life.

In her past life, with such a lowly beginning, apart from a good body, she had nothing, yet she had still managed to outmaneuver many people, bear three sons, and attain the status of a noble concubine.

This life...

Well, regardless of the outcome, she would first make sure that those high and mighty nobles were restless day and night!

...

The convoy finally arrived in the capital.

The journey had been uneventful.

Although Xiangjun was already destined to be the emperor’s concubine, she had not yet formally entered the palace and was not an official mistress, so she was not qualified to be escorted by Gu Tingxue.

The one responsible for protecting her and the twelve beauties on the journey was Zhou Zidu, the captain of the Imperial Guards.

Although Zhou Zidu was only nineteen years old and his official rank was not high, Xiangjun knew that he would become one of the emperor’s trusted aides in the future.

Later, it would be he who replaced General Wang in guarding the northern border.

chapters.title: Entering the Palace
chapters.content:
Xiangjun’s nature had always been that everything could be used for her benefit. Although she couldn’t win over Zhou Zidu at the moment, it didn’t matter. "Three points of affection upon meeting" and "a smiling face disarms a raised hand" were her mottos.

Moreover, Xiangjun had been trained in the art of seducing men.

Whether it was useful or not, it never hurt to try.

Therefore, throughout the journey, Xiangjun took good care of Captain Zhou.

From time to time, she would send food and drinks to him, saying that the guards had worked hard and he should share them.

She had judged that Captain Zhou was a simple and honest man. To deal with such a person, she needed to be not only pure but also direct.

Xiangjun knew how to maintain the right degree of interaction. Every time she spoke to Captain Zhou, she maintained proper etiquette, but her eyes were full of admiration, eagerness, and innocence.

She couldn’t let anyone catch her in the wrong, but she wanted Captain Zhou to feel that she treated him differently.

After more than a month of Xiangjun’s careful cultivation, Captain Zhou would now blush every time he saw her.

Good, Xiangjun was reassured. The three points of affection had been planted.

This way, if an opportunity arose in the future and she needed to win over this Marquis of Zhenyuan, she wouldn’t be completely without leverage.

When the convoy arrived at the imperial palace, Zhou Zidu and his men withdrew, and eunuchs took over to lead Xiangjun and the others into the palace.

The twelve beauties, as in her past life, were sent directly to the Teaching and Music Department.

After all, what the emperor was doing was somewhat damaging to the royal family’s reputation, so it couldn’t be done openly. Thus, these beauties didn’t even receive any titles.

Xiangjun, however, was entering the palace as a concubine. Her belongings were first sent into the palace to be inspected and registered before being taken to her residence.

She, on the other hand, was taken by the eunuchs to be examined for her virginity.

This examination was the final step before entering the palace. First, the eunuchs would measure her body, and then the matrons would check if she was a pure and untouched maiden.

Once she passed this step, she would only need to wait for the emperor’s decree to officially become a concubine.

After the measurement, the young eunuchs retreated, and Xiangjun walked behind the screen to undress.

In her past life, she hadn’t received the privilege of a private examination. A dozen beauties had been examined together.

After all, they were just tools for pleasure, used once or twice and then discarded. There was no need for respect.

Thinking of the twelve beauties, Xiangjun still felt a pang of distress.

Most of them, like her, had studied various skills painstakingly from a young age to make their bodies more appealing to men, enduring hardships that ordinary people couldn’t bear.

Moreover, Jiangnan was known for its cultural prosperity and wealth, and although they were of slave status, they had been cultivated with immense resources. There were likely many among them with extraordinary talents.

But none of that mattered.

Because of their lowly birth, everything was meaningless.

Xiangjun thought she should find a way to help them. She couldn’t always fight alone in the palace; having more allies would be beneficial.

As she was thinking this, she heard someone enter the room.

Xiangjun assumed it was the matron for the examination, so she walked out draped in a cloak.

She didn’t think there was anything wrong with being naked, but now, as a chaste young woman from a modest family entering the palace, she had to feign maidenly shyness.

However, as Xiangjun stepped out from behind the screen, she saw Gu Tingxue, dressed in the red python robe of the Chief Eunuch, sitting leisurely there.

After a moment of surprise, Xiangjun’s face showed joy, and her tone was full of delight. "Since when does the verification of chastity require the trouble of Lord Gu?"

Outside, she called him Lord Gu. Now that he was dressed as the Chief Eunuch, she addressed him as Lord Gu (public).

Gu Tingxue’s sinister gaze once again fixed on Xiangjun’s body.

Xiangjun felt a chill run down her spine, as if she were being stared at by a venomous snake.

This atmosphere was not right...

It was different from what she had imagined.

Could it be that calling him "Lord" had angered him?

Gu Tingxue glanced at the table nearby and coldly said, "Lie down."

Xiangjun didn’t know how she had offended Gu Tingxue, so she could only go and lie down on the table.

Gu Tingxue walked to the side of the table and extended a finger, lightly hooking it under the cloak, which he then easily pulled open.

Although he already knew what he would see, Gu Tingxue was still momentarily dazzled by the sight before him.

Yangzhou courtesans were indeed raised with a certain standard. Xiangjun was truly fair-skinned with a flawless, curvaceous figure.

Gu Tingxue did not look away. His hand lightly slid from Xiangjun’s cheek to her neck, and once again, he grabbed her by the throat.

Not again, Xiangjun thought to herself. Why does he keep grabbing her like this?

But this time, Gu Tingxue did not apply much pressure; he only restrained her from moving.

"Give me a reason not to kill you."

Looking at the veins bulging on Gu Tingxue’s hand from restraint, Xiangjun truly did not understand why this Lord Gu wanted to kill her so much.

Xiangjun’s eyes welled up with tears. "This humble servant doesn’t know what she did wrong. Lord Gu, at least let me die with understanding."

"Do you think I couldn’t see what you were doing along the way? Do you think I don’t know that even a mere captain of the guards has caught your eye?"

Xiangjun was momentarily speechless.

When had Gu Tingxue noticed her?

She remembered that the Imperial Guards were far away from the ladies’ carriages.

Xiangjun knew that lying to Gu Tingxue would not be very effective.

"I am alone and helpless in the capital. Isn’t it natural to want more friends and more paths to rely on? If I had Lord Gu to depend on, I wouldn’t bother with others."

Gu Tingxue had not expected her to admit it so readily. She was truly shameless.

Gu Tingxue tightened his grip slightly.

Xiangjun felt a wave of suffocation. Seeing her face turn red again and her breathing become difficult, Gu Tingxue finally let go.

Xiangjun coughed a couple of times and asked, "Is Lord Gu so angry because he is jealous?"

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun as if she were a fool.

"You are entering the palace to be the emperor’s woman. If you don’t understand that, there’s no need to continue. You can stay here."

Stay here?

Xiangjun felt a chill run down her spine.

This was the place for the chastity examination. Telling her to stay here was the same as telling her to die here.

Xiangjun didn’t know why, but this Lord Gu seemed to really want to kill her. Yet, he was also very conflicted, always giving her a chance to plead her case.

So, Xiangjun quickly pleaded.

Perhaps this Lord Gu simply enjoyed people begging him?

"Xiangjun understands, Lord Gu, please don’t be angry. Everything Xiangjun has is given by Lord Gu, and she will listen to Lord Gu. Xiangjun only hopes that after achieving a good future, she can repay Lord Gu."

"I cannot accept your gratitude."

"How can you not? If Lord Gu had not been willing to promote me, I would just be a lowly Yangzhou courtesan. How could I have obtained a proper identity to enter the palace? My father would not have been willing to spend so much silver to pave the way for me. Everything I have is given by Lord Gu, isn’t it?"

Xiangjun’s gaze was sincere, as if she were truly looking at her savior.

Gu Tingxue coldly humphed and finally withdrew his hand.

"I said I would help you once. I do not like things that go beyond my expectations. You were brought into the palace by me, so behave yourself and do not cause trouble."

"I understand. Xiangjun will keep Lord Gu’s words in her heart and will not forget them."

"Get up, put on your clothes. I will take you to see Noble Consort first."

Xiangjun was puzzled. "Why see Noble Consort first?"

"The Empress is ill and does not see many people. Currently, Noble Consort is managing the six palaces."

Gu Tingxue did not tell Xiangjun that entering the palace was to bear children for Noble Consort.

It wasn’t the right time yet; he wanted to see her capabilities first.

Gu Tingxue’s gaze slid over Xiangjun’s slender waist.

In any case, with such a slender waist, she really didn’t look like she could bear children.

Xiangjun thought to herself that even at this moment, Gu Tingxue still wouldn’t remind her about Noble Consort’s situation. He really didn’t care if she was used as a surrogate.

Sigh, how cruel...

Gu Tingxue extended his hand and used the cloak to cover Xiangjun’s exposed body again. He turned to leave but was suddenly grabbed by Xiangjun.

"Aren’t you going to continue the examination, Lord Gu? The steps for my chastity verification are not yet complete."

Gu Tingxue’s body froze.

The chastity examination, apart from checking for scars and blemishes on the body, also involved verifying if one was a virgin.

To verify virginity, it wasn’t just about checking for the presence of the "guardian sand" (a mythical substance said to be present in virgins in ancient Chinese folklore), as that could be faked.

As for how it was checked...

That was done by experienced matrons.

Xiangjun looked at Gu Tingxue with a hint of mischief. "Lord Gu should know how to verify chastity, right?"

Gu Tingxue glared at Xiangjun, this woman was truly a vixen, with no sense of shame.

"I’ll have the matron come in."

Gu Tingxue flicked his sleeve and left.

chapters.title: First Meeting with the Noble Consort
chapters.content:
After the matron's inspection, Xiangjun changed her clothes and followed Gu Tingxue to meet the Noble Consort.

Normally, such tasks would not fall to Gu Tingxue, as his status had long exempted him from attending to the emperor and his consorts.

However, except for the days he was sent out on official business, Gu Tingxue still had to serve as the emperor’s personal eunuch in the palace.

Emperor Yanqing’s reasoning was: “I am not at ease without Gu Tingxue by my side.”

But the book had revealed the emperor’s true thoughts: he wanted Gu Tingxue, who maintained such dignity before the officials, to continue serving him. This was to remind Gu Tingxue that everything he had was granted by the emperor, to make him understand that he would forever be the emperor’s slave. Such was the emperor’s imperial strategy.

Thinking of this plot, Xiangjun could only conclude: the dog emperor was truly a dog.

...

Noble Consort Rong, Xue Jiaojiao, resided in Ganlu Palace.

True to the palace’s name, Noble Consort Rong indeed received the emperor’s exclusive favor.

When Gu Tingxue led Xiangjun into the main hall, the Noble Consort was already waiting there.

Xiangjun had learned palace etiquette well. She kept her head lowered as she followed Eunuch Gu inside.

From the corner of her eye, she saw Gu Tingxue respectfully greet the Noble Consort with a proper salute, a smile on his face.

Tsk, tsk. Outside, Gu Tingxue could summon winds and rains, and even order the execution of court officials with a word. Yet, in front of the emperor’s favored consort, he still had to humble himself and bow.

At this moment, Xiangjun truly understood what power meant.

Power was a hierarchy of oppression. To avoid being crushed, one had to stand at the very top.

After Gu Tingxue introduced her, Xiangjun immediately knelt and performed a grand kowtow to the Noble Consort.

Even though the woman before her was the enemy of her two lifetimes, even though this woman had caused the death of her entire family, Xiangjun still knelt without hesitation, her face filled with joy.

“This concubine, Xu Xiangjun, pays respects to Noble Consort. May Noble Consort be in good health.”

Noble Consort Rong’s gentle and cool voice rang out, “You are quite well-mannered. Lift your head.”

Xiangjun raised her head, but her gaze still did not dare to meet the Noble Consort’s.

Not looking was both etiquette and because she feared that if she met her eyes, she might not be able to control the hatred in her heart.

Noble Consort Rong was momentarily stunned when she saw Xiangjun’s face.

This woman was simply too beautiful. She might even rival the bewitching Consort Qin in looks.

Noble Consort Rong looked at Gu Tingxue, who stood composed and at ease by the side.

This Eunuch Gu was truly the emperor’s good servant. Even when finding a surrogate to bear a child, he had to choose such a beautiful one. No wonder the emperor favored him.

Noble Consort Rong did not want a surrogate child, but when His Majesty mentioned it to her, the woman had already arrived in the capital.

She was kind-hearted and knew that if this woman could not enter the palace, she would have no chance to return home and marry.

So, today, she had no choice but to have someone bring her over for a look.

If she was obedient, keeping her in the palace might not be a bad idea.

But seeing Xiangjun’s appearance, Noble Consort Rong still had some concerns. She feared that Xiangjun might be another troublemaker like Consort Qin, who would stir up the imperial harem.

“Rise.”

The Noble Consort’s tone was indifferent, and Xiangjun quickly stood up.

The Noble Consort then looked at Gu Tingxue and asked, “Has a palace been arranged for Sister Xiangjun?”

Gu Tingxue was slightly surprised.

Xiangjun had entered the palace to bear a child for the Noble Consort, so naturally, she should live in Noble Consort Rong’s Ganlu Palace, where it would be convenient for the Noble Consort to supervise her. This was also the emperor’s intention.

Hearing the Noble Consort’s words, did she not intend to keep Xiangjun?

Gu Tingxue glanced at Xiangjun, who was putting on a very convincing act of “innocent anticipation.” He thought, perhaps it was because she was too beautiful. Even if she pretended to be obedient, she was still feared.

Gu Tingxue knew his master’s intentions and replied, “His Majesty has granted her the position of a Caifu (a low-ranking concubine), but her palace has not yet been decided. As Noble Consort oversees the Six Palaces, it would be best if you decide, Noble Consort.”

Noble Consort Rong looked at Xiangjun and said gently, “I recall that Chengxiang Hall is still vacant. Since your name is Xiangjun, you may live there for now. It suits you.”

Noble Consort Rong thought that it would be better to keep her at a distance for now and observe her for a while.

If she really caused trouble, living in such a remote place where she couldn’t see the emperor would prevent any incidents.

Gu Tingxue understood. The Noble Consort did not want Xiangjun to see the emperor.

In the palace, there were consorts who never saw the emperor their entire lives.

Xiangjun naturally knew what Chengxiang Hall was. It was very remote. Unless the emperor specifically went there, one could go a lifetime without ever setting foot in that place.

But Xiangjun still pretended not to know and happily thanked the Noble Consort for her grace.

Seeing Xiangjun’s innocent appearance, Noble Consort Rong softened a little. Thinking that it was because of her that Xiangjun had entered the palace and was forced to face the loneliness of the deep palace, she gave Xiangjun some additional rewards.

Xiangjun was overjoyed and expressed her gratitude repeatedly before leaving with Gu Tingxue.

As Gu Tingxue and Xiangjun walked along the palace path, the palace servants all avoided them from afar upon seeing Gu Tingxue.

Seeing Xiangjun’s happy smile all the way, Gu Tingxue could not help but remind her, “Do you not know that the Noble Consort does not intend for you to serve the emperor?”

Xiangjun smiled. “I know.”

“If that’s the case, there’s no need to pretend. There’s no one else here.”

Xiangjun widened her eyes slightly and looked at Gu Tingxue. “I’m not pretending. I’m genuinely happy.”

“What is there to be happy about?”

“Entering the palace, opportunities must be seized by oneself. I never expected the Noble Consort to promote me. Now, I have my own position and palace. I am a proper concubine. I have obtained everything I sought. Of course, I’m happy.”

Gu Tingxue sneered mockingly, “That is not your palace. You can only live in the side hall there. Only when you reach the rank of a Pin (a higher-ranking concubine) can you be the mistress of a palace. Only then can Chengxiang Hall truly be your palace.”

Xiangjun was not discouraged at all. Instead, she cheerfully replied, “Yes, thank you for your guidance, Eunuch Gu. I will remember and strive to be promoted to the rank of Pin as soon as possible.”

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun’s radiant smile and did not say another word the entire way.

It was infuriating to watch.

Gu Tingxue took Xiangjun to Chengxiang Hall.

The palace had been vacant for a long time, with only two palace maids responsible for cleaning in the outer courtyard.

Gu Tingxue led Xiangjun to the side hall and prepared to leave.

“Eunuch Gu, when can Mengmei come to my side?”

“Palace maids also need to be inspected. Later, I will have someone send Mengmei and your things over together.”

“What about Mengzhu?”

“I will report to His Majesty and have him first go to attend to Noble Consort Rong. If the Noble Consort finds him useful, he can stay in the palace.”

Gu Tingxue was always able to accomplish what he set out to do. Xiangjun was not worried. She nodded happily.

“Thank you, Eunuch Gu, for your trouble.”

After some thought, Xiangjun took out a bag of silver from her pocket.

“I know you look down on these things, but right now, I have nothing else to thank you with.”

Gu Tingxue looked at the bag of silver, unsure how to react for a moment.

“No need.” Gu Tingxue said with a dark face. “I have already done what I promised you, but only this once. In the future, I fear there will be no more interactions between me and Lady Xu.”

Xiangjun pouted slightly, feeling wronged. There was no need to constantly emphasize “only this once.”

Because Xiangjun would definitely seek out Gu Tingxue again. If she didn’t ask for help from someone who had helped her before, would she ask someone who hadn’t?

“Can I ask you one more question, Eunuch Gu?”

“Ask.”

“Why did you agree to help me?”

Gu Tingxue had asked himself this question before. Maybe it was the ambition and unwillingness in her eyes that moved him.

It was a feeling of seeing a kindred spirit.

Xiangjun stood up and walked to Gu Tingxue. The distance between them was so close that they were almost touching.

Xiangjun’s breath was as fragrant as an orchid. She said softly, “Eunuch Gu, do you really expect no reward at all?”

Seeing the change in Xiangjun’s gaze, Gu Tingxue feared she might say something reckless again and his face darkened.

“Behave yourself. That is enough of a reward for me.”

Gu Tingxue turned and left quickly.

Xiangjun felt it was a pity. Right now, in the side hall, it was just the two of them. Such a good opportunity, and Eunuch Gu didn’t know how to seize it. He was so timid. How could he help her kill the emperor in the future?

---

chapters.title: Lady Xu, the Selected Attendant
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue worked quickly.

In less than an hour, Xiangjun’s belongings and Mengmei were sent to Chengxiang Hall.

In addition, a small palace maid named Xiyu was also sent.

As an adopted lady, Xiangjun could have at most two attendants. On the way, Mengmei had asked a few questions and found that Xiyu was clever and steady.

Just as she was about to say a few good words about Xiyu to Xiangjun, she saw that Xiangjun’s eyes were red.

“Lady Xu, what’s wrong?”

“Nothing.” Xiangjun suppressed her sobs. She glanced at the still confused Xiyu and smiled as she took her hand. “From now on, you and Mengmei will serve me together.”

Perhaps it was fate. In her previous life, the first palace maid Xiangjun had in the palace was Xiyu.

Unfortunately, later, Xiyu had died for her.

In this life, such a thing would never happen again.

...

That night, the emperor came to Ganlu Palace to see Noble Consort Rong.

As expected, the Noble Consort was upset with the emperor for finding someone to bear a child for her.

“Your Majesty, do you find Jiaojiao unworthy because she cannot bear children?”

“How could that be? If I found you unworthy, would I have favored you exclusively all these years?”

The emperor was in his prime. The palace had no shortage of consorts, but his heirs were few. The main reason was that his favors were almost exclusively bestowed upon Noble Consort Rong, who could not bear children.

Currently, the emperor had only two sons and one daughter.

The empress had given birth to one son, securing her position. That was because on the first and fifteenth days of the month and major festivals, the emperor had no choice but to visit the empress’s palace. Thus, three years ago, she had given birth to a son, the emperor’s second son.

Consort De had also given birth to a son. Although she was not favored, she was lucky. Before Noble Consort Rong entered the palace, the emperor had favored her once, and she became pregnant, giving birth to the emperor’s eldest son, who was now ten years old.

After Noble Consort Rong entered the palace, almost no other consorts became pregnant.

It was not until three years ago, when the emperor could no longer endure the censure from the court, that he began to favor the Six Palaces again. However, he still visited Noble Consort Rong’s palace more often.

Unfortunately, in the past two or three years, only two consorts had become pregnant, and they had both given birth to daughters.

“Then, Your Majesty, do not do such a thing as finding a surrogate for me. Although Lady Xu’s rank is low, and by the rules, she would not be allowed to raise a prince, I cannot bear to separate a mother from her child. Does Your Majesty really think I am such a cruel person?”

The emperor sighed. To prevent the Noble Consort from overthinking, he had to agree. “Alright, I will not do such a thing again.”

The emperor thought that since he had not even seen Lady Xu, and could not favor her, he said, “I have allowed her to enter the palace, but I will not favor her. I will promote her to the rank of Selected Attendant. She can just live in the palace.”

Noble Consort Rong could not hide her joy. “Then, this concubine will thank Your Majesty on behalf of Lady Xu.”

The emperor also said, “This time, Tingxue has found a skilled obstetrician from the common folk. He says the medical skills are excellent. Tomorrow, I will have him bring the person here so that the doctor can examine you. If you find him useful, you can keep him in the palace to regulate your body.”

“Your Majesty... I fear I will disappoint you.”

The emperor pinched Noble Consort Rong’s nose, his eyes full of tenderness.

“Silly Jiaojiao, no child is as good as ours. My vast empire can only be inherited by our own child.”

...

Xiangjun learned that she had become a Selected Attendant the next day.

As a Selected Attendant, she could have an additional young eunuch to attend to her, which made her quite happy.

This young eunuch was named Xiaoluzhi. True to his name, although he was young, he had some connections and was quite useful.

A few days later, Xiaoluzhi found out that the doctor, Liu Xiuzhu, who had been brought to treat Noble Consort Rong, had been retained in the Imperial Physicians’ Office.

A few more days passed, and it was the day when, in her previous life, Xiangjun had first served the emperor.

Xiangjun’s Chengxiang Hall was close to the Teaching and Entertainment Office. She stood at the palace gate and watched from afar as a beautiful woman carrying a pipa followed a few palace servants along the palace path.

The pipa-playing beauty’s face was filled with joy and infinite expectations for the future, unaware that she was walking a blood-stained path to the underworld.

Xiaoluzhi thought that Xiangjun was upset about not being summoned by the emperor and tried to comfort her. “Lady Xu, do not be disheartened. Your appearance is among the best in the palace. As long as you have the chance to see His Majesty, you will surely receive great favor.”

Xiangjun sighed and turned back into the palace.

“Lock the door.”

Xiangjun returned to her room to rest.

Unexpectedly, she had a nightmarish night.

In her dreams, she relived the scenes of her first time serving the emperor.

She woke up in the middle of the night, drenched in sweat. Even after two lifetimes, that night remained the deepest shadow in her heart. Every time she thought about it, she was filled with grief, indignation, and humiliation, hating it to the core of her being.

Tonight, Mengmei was on night watch duty.

“Young lady, did you have a nightmare?”

Xiangjun grabbed Mengmei’s hand, rarely showing a trace of unease.

“Mengmei, the path in the palace is treacherous. Will you always stay by my side?”

“Of course,” Mengmei, who was two years older than Xiangjun, had always treated Xiangjun like a younger sister. She sat down by the bed and held Xiangjun’s slightly trembling body. “Young lady, don’t be afraid. I’m here with you.”

...

Over the next two days, every night two more courtesans were sent to the Taiji Hall.
