Because on the last three days of every month, the emperor had to vent and detoxify. Only after venting enough could a new month begin, during which he would favor the consorts in the palace again. So, with twelve beauties, His Majesty could use them for at least four months.

Xiangjun did not dare to speak out of turn. Even if she warned them, it would be useless. If one dared to interfere with the emperor’s affairs, the only outcome was death.

She could only have Xiaoluzhi secretly investigate and find a way to see those three women.

When Xiaoluzhi returned with the news, his entire face was pale with fear.

He had secretly taken a look and said that the three women were covered in bruises, not a single patch of good skin. Their lower bodies were bleeding, and some even had their intestines hanging out.

Xiaoluzhi felt he had seen something he shouldn’t have and was terrified.

“Don’t be afraid. There are so many eyes in the palace. Three living people entered Taiji Hall and were carried out. It’s not just you who saw it. Everyone else is just pretending to be blind and deaf.”

After all, before their batch entered the palace, twenty-four people had already died.

It was likely that many in the palace knew about this.

Probably only the naive Noble Consort was unaware.

Oh, and the remaining beauties in the Teaching and Entertainment Office knew nothing.

They thought that the courtesans who had served the emperor first had already become mistresses and were looking forward to the day they too could rise to prominence.

No one would tell them the truth.

...

Xiangjun knew that after these twelve women were used, the emperor’s condition would improve, and he would be able to impregnate women again.

So, during this time, Xiangjun had not thought about seeking favor.

Although unfavored consorts, apart from not being starved to death, were deprived of everything else.

But with money, one could live comfortably anywhere.

In the palace, as long as one was willing to spend silver and did not overstep the rules, anything could be bought. Therefore, Xiangjun and her three attendants did not suffer any hardships.

Then, another month passed, and three more women had served the emperor.

This time, Xiaoluzhi reported that one of the dancers had survived and was now thrown into the servants’ quarters, waiting to die.

This dancer had not entered the palace in her previous life.

Thinking that it was because she had replaced the little official’s daughter to enter the palace that the dancer had taken her place, Xiangjun felt a great deal of guilt toward the dancer.

Taking the expensive medicine she had obtained from “Father,” Xiangjun dressed as a palace maid and, under the cover of night, sneaked into the servants’ quarters.

When Xiangjun arrived, the girl was already burning with fever and delirious.

She fed the girl a life-saving pill and treated her external injuries, applying a wound medicine.

She carefully examined her. The dancer’s injuries were much lighter than what she had suffered in her previous life. Perhaps she could pull through.

After doing all this, Xiangjun carefully closed the door and left. However, as soon as she turned around, she saw someone standing in front of her.

“Eunuch Gu...”

chapters.title: Do You Think I'm Easy to Fool?
chapters.content:
Before Xiangjun could speak, Gu Tingxue stuffed a handkerchief into her mouth and hoisted her up, carrying her away from the servants' quarters.

By the time Xiangjun’s feet touched the ground again, she was already back in her own palace.

Along the way, Xiangjun had truly felt the influence of their esteemed Chief Eunuch in the palace. Despite how conspicuous the two of them were, they hadn’t encountered a single person on their way back.

She didn’t know if it was because the emperor’s harem wasn’t very populated, or if Gu Tingxue’s management of the harem was so meticulously strict that it bordered on the pathological.

Gu Tingxue carried Xiangjun in through the window, then set her down steadily on the master’s chair.

Xiangjun tried to stand, but Gu Tingxue suddenly bent over, pressing his hands against the armrests of the chair and leaning in close.

Staring at the face just inches away, Xiangjun was so frightened that she quickly leaned back, pressing against the chair’s backrest, not daring to move.

With the handkerchief still in her mouth, Xiangjun widened her deer-like, panic-stricken eyes and looked at Gu Tingxue pitifully.

Gu Tingxue was almost amused by her act.

How could someone so audacious pretend to be a timid little rabbit in front of him?

He reached out and removed the handkerchief from her mouth.

“Was it uncomfortable with that in?” Gu Tingxue asked.

Xiangjun pouted, her eyes reddening as she said aggrievedly, “It was unbearable.”

“If it was uncomfortable, why didn’t you take it out yourself? I didn’t tie your hands.”

“This servant was the one who put it in. Without your permission, Xiangjun didn’t dare remove it.”

Gu Tingxue sneered. “Now you’re acting timid? Where was this caution when you were prying into the emperor’s secrets?”

Cold sweat nearly dripped from Xiangjun’s forehead as she quickly tried to think of an explanation. But then she saw Gu Tingxue produce a small knife, pressing it against her neck.

Not again—was he really going to take her life?

This time, Xiangjun truly didn’t dare move. The cold glint of the blade told her that if she so much as shifted forward an inch, blood would spill instantly.

“Eunuch Gu, what are you doing? I never pryed into the emperor’s secrets! I only heard that some of the musicians who entered the palace with me had been summoned to the emperor’s bed. I thought they might become the emperor’s concubines, and since we’d be sisters in the future, I just went to see them.”

“Is that so? Then how did you know they had been summoned?”

“My palace is close to the Teaching and Entertainment Office. I saw it at night.”

Gu Tingxue sneered. “Do you think I’m easy to fool?”

Seeing the blade’s cold glint flicker again, Xiangjun quickly said, “Alright, alright, I’ll tell the truth! I had my maid, Xiaoluzi, keep an eye on them. I was just… worried.”

“Worried about what?”

“Worried about my identity.” Xiangjun said pitifully, “Among those musicians, three of them, like me, were raised by the Xu family. I was afraid that if they gained the emperor’s favor and became concubines, they might reveal that I’m also from Yangzhou’s skinny horse trade—not a proper young lady from a respectable family…”

Gu Tingxue found this explanation somewhat believable.

If this were exposed, it would indeed be a crime of deceiving the emperor.

“I handle things, and you don’t trust me?”

“Xiangjun wouldn’t dare! It’s just… Eunuch Gu, you know me. I’m a suspicious person. If I don’t figure things out, I tend to overthink.”

“You were raised in the Xu family for so many years. With so many people around, it wouldn’t do to say you were their biological daughter, so they told the world you were an orphan picked up by Master Xu during a famine and raised as his own. They didn’t add you to the family genealogy before because a Taoist said you’d face disaster before the age of sixteen—your three souls and six spirits were unstable. Only by keeping a low profile could you stay safe. After you turned sixteen and your soul stabilized, you could formally be recognized as part of the family. As for your official records of lowly status and the contract of sale, they’ve all been destroyed. No one can find any evidence now. With that said, is Lady Xu satisfied?”

Xiangjun reached out, cautiously tugging at Gu Tingxue’s sleeve, subtly pulling the knife away from her neck.

“Eunuch Gu, just call me Xiangjun, won’t you? ‘Lady Xu’ sounds so distant.”

Gu Tingxue wasn’t fooled by Xiangjun’s little tricks, but he didn’t feel like arguing with her. He coldly huffed and put the knife away.

Just then, a creak sounded as the door behind them was pushed open.

Tonight’s guard was Mengmei. Hearing noises in her mistress’s room, she thought thieves had broken in. She never expected that upon opening the door, she’d see her mistress with Eunuch Gu.

From Mengmei’s angle, it looked like Gu Tingxue was pressing Xiangjun down on the chair, their faces extremely close. She couldn’t tell if they had just finished doing something or if she had interrupted them before they started.

Even someone as steady as Mengmei was stunned by the scene before her, her eyes widening.

Her mistress was the emperor’s concubine—how could she be involved with Eunuch Gu?

Gu Tingxue turned his head and glared at Mengmei. The cold, sinister look made her shiver, as if the next second, this all-powerful eunuch would slash her throat.

Just as she stammered, unable to speak, she noticed Xiangjun’s hand secretly stretching out from under the chair, signaling her to leave.

Xiangjun even tilted her head slightly, revealing her eyes to give Mengmei a meaningful look.

Seeing that her mistress didn’t look afraid, Mengmei quickly pretended she hadn’t seen anything. She lowered her head, retreated, and closed the door again.

Relieved to see Mengmei escape safely, Xiangjun let out a breath, only to meet Gu Tingxue’s burning gaze once more.

“Eunuch Gu…” Xiangjun tugged at Gu Tingxue’s sleeve, “You must be tired from standing. Why not sit down?”

Gu Tingxue coldly huffed, straightened up, and walked over to sit in another master’s chair nearby.

Xiangjun quickly stood up, poured him a cup of water, and handed it to him gently. “Please, Eunuch Gu.”

Gu Tingxue took the water and drank a sip. Xiangjun didn’t sit back down; she remained standing beside him, attending to him.

“Lady Xu is the mistress; there’s no need to lower yourself like this.”

“Even though I am now a palace concubine, Eunuch Gu will always be my benefactor. This kindness, Xiangjun will never forget for the rest of her life.”

Gu Tingxue coldly huffed again and was about to put down the cup when Xiangjun quickly took it from him.

“I’ll do it!”

Seeing Xiangjun’s obedient and gentle demeanor, even though he knew it was an act, Gu Tingxue’s mood improved slightly.

Xiangjun prayed that Gu Tingxue would let her go soon, but it seemed he had no intention of doing so.

He continued to ask, “Did you also go see the musicians who were summoned before?”

“No, I had Xiaoluzi go. Xiaoluzi said… they’re already dead…”

Gu Tingxue didn’t doubt that Xiangjun could find out such information. After all, she was clever and willing to spend money. In the two months since she’d entered the palace, this little Lady Xu had been living better than some noblewomen.

Moreover, the fact that the emperor used women sent from outside the palace to treat his illness was practically an open secret.

After all, twenty-six people had already died, and ten more lives were on the line. How could such a thing be hidden?

It was just that no one dared to speak of it, no one dared to ask. Everyone tacitly turned a blind eye, pretending not to know.

“Since you know what’s happening, why did you still go to see that dancer today?”

Only now did Xiangjun seem to show belated fear as she slowly sat back down in the chair.

She gripped the armrests tightly, her face pale.

“Xiaoluzi told me that of the three who were summoned, one was still alive, just left abandoned in the servants’ quarters with no one to care for her. I thought I’d go see if there was still a chance to save her.”

“You certainly like meddling in other people’s business.”

“Do I?” Xiangjun’s eyelashes trembled slightly, as if saddened. “Outside the palace, if people see an injured cat or dog by the roadside, and they have the means, they’ll help. But in this richest place in the world, a living person’s life is ignored by everyone. Why is that?”

Gu Tingxue was actually stumped by Xiangjun’s question. After a long pause, he said, “In this palace, kind-hearted people have long since died out. Lady Xu should just take care of herself.”

“Who says that? Aren’t you a kind-hearted person, Eunuch Gu? Otherwise, why would you help me?”

“A eunuch can’t be considered a person.”

Gu Tingxue stood up to leave, but Xiangjun grabbed his sleeve.

“Eunuch Gu, can I ask you something?”

“Ask.”

“Is the emperor really that terrifying? Why does every woman who attends his bed meet such a tragic end… I… I don’t want to serve the emperor anymore. I don’t want to die.”

Gu Tingxue sighed and pulled his sleeve free from Xiangjun’s grip.

“It’s not always like that. The emperor doesn’t treat the ladies of the palace this way.”

Hearing this, Xiangjun gave a bitter smile, full of self-mockery.

“I see… So that’s how it is… In that case, Eunuch Gu, you haven’t just helped me—you’ve saved my life. If it weren’t for your arrangements, would I have ended up serving the emperor only to be wrapped in a blanket and thrown away like them?”

Xiangjun stared fixedly at Gu Tingxue, her gaze making him uneasy.

For some reason, Gu Tingxue felt that if it were Xiangjun, she would probably be able to survive.

Her vitality was so strong, like a wild weed.

“Eunuch Gu, can I still go see that dancer?” Xiangjun asked again.

“Why do you want to see her?”

“Because I feel a kinship with her, I suppose.”

Gu Tingxue thought for a moment, then only said, “You must not act so recklessly again,” before leaving.

Only after Gu Tingxue left and the palace gates were locked did Mengmei dare to enter carefully.

She wanted to ask something, but Xiangjun waved her hand, signaling her not to speak.

“First, call Xiaoluzi in.”

…

Xiaoluzi knelt on the ground, cautiously observing his mistress.

Xiangjun sat on the soft couch, smiling gently, but the words she spoke made his heart race with fear.

“I know you’re Eunuch Gu’s man. But a servant cannot serve two masters. Do you understand?”

chapters.title: Seeking Favor
chapters.content:
Xiang Jun had long suspected Xiao Luzi.

Xiao Luzi always gathered information so quickly and accurately—it was impossible for a lowly eunuch with no background to achieve that.

Of course, there was no information that money couldn’t buy.

But one thing was truly unreasonable.

How could Xiao Luzi have seen the bodies of those two singing girls so clearly?

The people in the emperor’s presence wouldn’t be so careless. Handling two corpses was a simple task—how could they have made a mistake?

If the noble consort’s palace maids wanted to see the bodies, they could. Xiang Jun could understand that.

But Xiao Luzi was a lowly eunuch from her own unfavored and low-ranking concubine’s palace. Could this really be accomplished just by spending money?

If so, the emperor was utterly useless—how could he govern the world with such poor control over his subordinates?

Moreover, even if the emperor lacked control, Gu Tingxue would never make such a mistake.

So, with a little thought, Xiang Jun realized: Xiao Luzi was Gu Tingxue’s man.

And Gu Tingxue had tacitly allowed her to investigate, allowed Xiao Luzi to tell her everything, allowed her to see that dancer.

How interesting. Why did Gu Tingxue keep testing her?

Was Gu Tingxue, like her, also assessing her?

Did he want to see if she could be his accomplice?

“I wouldn’t dare!” Xiao Luzi said excitedly. “This servant only serves one master! My loyalty to the honored consort is known to heaven and earth!”

Xiang Jun didn’t press him further. “Don’t be afraid. Lord Gu has been kind to me, and you are his man. I won’t make things difficult for you. However, I only want servants who are loyal to me alone. My servants cannot serve two masters. So, from now on, you will serve outside. When you’ve made up your mind, come find me.”

With that, Xiang Jun didn’t give Xiao Luzi a chance to speak. She waved her hand, and Meng Mei took him away.

…

Two more days passed. A young eunuch came to Chengxiang Hall.

The eunuch told Xiang Jun that the dancer in the servants’ quarters was on a hunger strike.

The eunuch didn’t say who sent him, but Xiang Jun knew he must also be Gu Tingxue’s man.

That evening, when Xiang Jun went to see the dancer, she was lying motionless, staring at the ceiling.

Even when Xiang Jun entered, the dancer remained numb, not even lifting an eyelid.

Xiang Jun didn’t speak. She went straight to examine the dancer’s wounds.

Perhaps because she had danced since childhood, the dancer’s body was still strong. Combined with the best wound medicine Xiang Jun had used, some of the wounds had already scabbed over.

But clearly, the dancer hadn’t applied any medicine to herself in the past two days.

Xiang Jun took out the medicine bottle to treat her, but the dancer suddenly grabbed her hand.

“Why did you save me? I saw it—it was you who forced the medicine down my throat that day. Why didn’t you let me die?”

“Why do you want to die?”

The dancer wanted to cry but had no tears. “Even though I’m a dancer, I shouldn’t be treated like this. The emperor… he doesn’t even see me as a person!”

Xiang Jun remained calm. She had experienced all of this before—her suffering had been even worse than the dancer’s.

“In the eyes of those nobles, we were never human to begin with,” Xiang Jun said indifferently.

The dancer looked at Xiang Jun, her eyes filled with humiliation.

Xiang Jun continued, “Rest assured. Even if you die, they won’t treat you as a person. They’ll just wrap you in a blanket and throw you naked into a mass grave. Your fate would be to be eaten by wild dogs. They wouldn’t even remember your name.”

Xiang Jun quickly applied the medicine to the dancer, then picked up the bowl of congee beside her.

“Eat something. Stay alive. Only by living do you have a chance to be treated as a person. If you die, you’re just a pile of rotten flesh.”

Xiang Jun fed her the congee, and the dancer finally opened her mouth and drank.

After finishing the bowl, Xiang Jun said, “When you recover, they’ll definitely arrange for you to attend the emperor again.”

The dancer was so distressed she could spit blood.

“Don’t panic. I have a way to help you survive.”

In her past life, Xiang Jun had attended the emperor twice and even conceived a child the second time.

The first time, she had been unprepared, but the second time, she had used some methods to ensure she survived without serious injury.

“Listen carefully. There are many ways to serve a man. No matter how afraid you are of the emperor, you must take the initiative. Use other parts of your body more. A few external injuries don’t matter—you won’t die from them. Just don’t harm your insides. Don’t let the emperor focus on one place. Understand?”

“How do you know all this?” the dancer asked, biting her lip in shame and anger. “How do you know what the emperor did to me?”

“Everyone in the palace knows the emperor is ill. With a little effort, anyone can find out. You’re the only ones kept in the dark.”

Xiang Jun covered her with a blanket.

“Endure it for now.”

“But what awaits me at the end?” the dancer asked.

“I don’t know. But it’s better than dying silently and unnoticed.” Xiang Jun looked at the dancer with a burning gaze. “I see many calluses on your hands and feet. To be sent into the palace, your skills must be extraordinary. You must have worked hard since childhood, whether because you loved dancing or wanted to change your fate. You must be an ambitious person. Think of who you used to be. Don’t let yourself break here.”

Xiang Jun stood up to leave.

“Benefactor, what is your name?”

Xiang Jun turned back and looked at her, sighing. “If you survive, we’ll get to know each other properly then.”

…

For the next half month, Xiang Jun went to pay her respects to Noble Consort every day.

Even when she clearly sensed Noble Consort’s impatience, she continued without fail.

It didn’t matter. After all, Noble Consort was famous for treating the concubines of the harem well. As long as Xiang Jun went, Noble Consort would see her.

Moreover, Xiang Jun always went when the emperor was in the front court, so it was impossible to encounter him. Over time, she gained an impression in Noble Consort’s mind as honest, simple, and non-competitive for favor.

Thus, Noble Consort bestowed gifts upon Xiang Jun.

When leaving, Noble Consort’s senior palace maid, Cai Wei, subtly hinted that Xiang Jun should visit less often.

“Noble Consort’s body is delicate. You come daily with good intentions, but accompanying you still tires her.”

Xiang Jun quickly promised that she would not disturb Noble Consort again without a summons. Then, she proudly returned to Chengxiang Hall with Noble Consort’s gifts.

She even deliberately took a detour to let the entire palace know that Noble Consort favored her.

After that, Xiang Jun stayed obediently in her Chengxiang Hall, going nowhere. Occasionally, she would have Meng Mei do some needlework to send to Ganlu Palace.

Noble Consort accepted them and, every three times, would reward Xiang Jun once in return.

Thus, in the eyes of the harem, Xiang Jun truly became one of Noble Consort’s people. Otherwise, why would Noble Consort reward her so frequently?

Only Xiang Jun herself knew that all of this was due to her shamelessness.

…

Several months passed like this. The twelve beauties had all attended the emperor.

In the end, only the dancer survived.

Xiang Jun was somewhat curious—would the dancer share her fate and conceive an imperial heir?

But she didn’t stay curious for long. When the autumn wind rose and the weather turned cold, a decree was issued to the six palaces: the dancer had conceived an imperial descendant and was granted the title of Lady Li.

Although she had survived against all odds, she was still only given the lowest rank of Lady. It was said that even this status was obtained through Noble Consort’s efforts.

Because of Noble Consort’s kindness, Lady Li moved into Noble Consort’s Ganlu Palace, and her pregnancy was personally overseen by Noble Consort.

This was exactly the same path Xiang Jun had taken in her past life.

“Mistress, why don’t you visit Noble Consort’s palace? You could also get closer to Lady Li.” Meng Mei was somewhat worried about Xiang Jun’s current situation. “After all, you saved Lady Li’s life. We have no one to rely on in the palace. If we get closer to the mother of the imperial heir, it wouldn’t be a bad thing.”

Xiang Jun shook her head and continued to focus on copying sutras.

“This matter isn’t urgent, but I have something else for you to do.”

Now that the emperor had recovered, Xiang Jun still needed to find a way to attend him.

After all, in the harem, the emperor’s favor was always the most important.

---

chapters.title: First Meeting with His Majesty
chapters.content:
After the strange poison afflicting the emperor was resolved, he began staying overnight at Ganlu Palace again.

He visited Ganlu Palace for three consecutive days, then on the fourth day, he went to Nanxun Hall to see Consort Qin. After that, he spent another two days with Noble Consort.

For a time, Noble Consort once again monopolized the emperor’s favor.

Meng Mei couldn’t help but sigh, “Noble Consort has accompanied His Majesty for ten years, and her favor remains undiminished. Even celestial beings would grow tired of it. Our emperor is truly a man of deep affection.”

In reality, based on Xiang Jun’s understanding of the emperor, he wasn’t a man of little desire—he was just addicted to playing the role of a devoted lover.

The emperor also believed that Noble Consort was a pure white jasmine flower. He felt that by loving such a pure woman, he, a filthy man, seemed to be cleansed by this love and become pure as well. That was why he was so infatuated.

In Xiang Jun’s opinion, the emperor actually wanted to favor new concubines—he just needed to find a reason to convince himself.

Once he found that reason, he could be quite enthusiastic about sleeping with beauties.

Otherwise, how had Xiang Jun conceived three children in her past life?

What nonsense was that about the emperor being forced to distribute his favor equally?

She didn’t know how the scholars who wrote those commentaries in the storybooks had come to that conclusion.

In any case, when he was with her, she hadn’t felt the slightest reluctance from the emperor.

“You’re right,” Xiang Jun said, looking at the falling leaves outside. “Even a celestial being would grow tired after ten years.”

So, nearly half a year after entering the palace, Xiang Jun, who had never wandered aimlessly before, chose a beautiful day with gentle breeze and sunshine to stroll through the imperial garden.

The autumn begonia flowers were in full bloom.

She had heard that Consort Qin loved begonia flowers. Recently, Consort Qin had been in a bad mood and had no close friends among the concubines, so she often spent time in the imperial garden, appreciating the flowers and feeding the fish to pass the time.

Sure enough, as soon as Xiang Jun picked an autumn begonia and placed it in her hair, she heard a coquettish and sticky-sweet voice behind her.

“Oh my, which palace’s sister are you? How come I’ve never seen you before?”

Consort Qin had a slight accent.

She was from Nanyue, and the women from there were particularly coquettish. Though her speech was a bit sticky, it had a certain unique charm.

Xiang Jun examined Consort Qin.

Consort Qin wasn’t the kind of pale woman—her skin was wheat-colored, but not dull. She had a vibrant spirit and exquisite features, making her a rare and beautiful exotic flower in the harem.

It was no wonder that as soon as she entered the palace, she had caused several arguments between Noble Consort and the emperor.

In her past life, Xiang Jun and Consort Qin had clashed several times—they could be considered enemies.

Unfortunately, Xiang Jun had never gotten the chance to strike back at Consort Qin before she destroyed herself.

Because Consort Qin wasn’t very clever. The harder she tried, the more heartbroken she became. Every time she schemed, she not only failed to harm Noble Consort but also made the emperor grow colder toward her.

In the end, the emperor lost even the last bit of pity he had for her.

Only because she was a princess of Nanyue, and Nanyue had recently been incorporated into the Great Qi, the emperor spared her life to appease the people. He simply kept her in the palace.

Her Nanxun Hall had become her own cold palace.

Seeing Xiang Jun standing there in a daze, Consort Qin’s senior palace maid, Zhu Jin, sternly said, “Why haven’t you greeted Consort Qin?”

Xiang Jun hurriedly bowed to Consort Qin in a fluster.

“This concubine… this concubine is Xu Xiang Jun, a selected attendant from Chengxiang Hall. I pay my respects to Consort Qin.”

Upon hearing Xiang Jun’s name, Consort Qin’s beautiful willow-leaf eyebrows lightly lifted.

“It’s you. I’ve ding heard of you…”

Xiang Jun blinked her eyes, looking at Consort Qin innocently.

“Ding heard? This concubine doesn’t understand what Consort Qin means.”

At these words, Consort Qin’s face immediately darkened.

“How dare you mock Consort Qin!” Zhu Jin said sternly.

Xiang Jun had done it on purpose. She knew Consort Qin hated it when people mocked her accent.

Consort Qin glared at Zhu Jin beside her.

Zhu Jin realized she had spoken out of turn and quickly fell silent.

Consort Qin looked back at Xiang Jun, her beautiful almond eyes seemingly about to spit fire. “You’ve done wrong. Why aren’t you kneeling before me?”

Xiang Jun put on a look as if she were about to cry, trembling as she knelt on the ground.

“This concubine truly doesn’t know how I’ve offended Consort Qin. I beg Consort Qin to forgive me.”

Consort Qin hated it most when people mentioned her Nanyue accent, so she naturally wouldn’t admit that this was the reason for her anger.

“Did you not know that I love autumn begonia the most? You dared to pick one before I could even appreciate it?”

“Consort Qin, I truly didn’t know that you love autumn begonia the most. This concubine only picked one flower—it shouldn’t affect your appreciation. Please spare me, Consort Qin.”

Consort Qin was annoyed by Xiang Jun’s affected demeanor.

“Still daring to talk back?”

Zhu Jin, having accidentally offended her mistress earlier, now eagerly stepped forward to vent Consort Qin’s anger.

“What kind of thing are you? You haven’t even seen the emperor’s face. You’re just a lowly selected attendant, yet you dare to be disrespectful to our Consort Qin! Don’t think that just because you have Noble Consort’s backing, our mistress won’t dare to deal with you!”

Consort Qin despised Noble Consort the most.

She had heard that this newly entered selected attendant, Xu Xiang Jun, was Noble Consort’s person. Even her rank was elevated because the emperor had given face to Noble Consort.

“An insolent thing who doesn’t know her place. You probably only know Noble Consort and not me. Since you love autumn begonia so much, you can kneel in the sun for three hours. Go!”

Xiang Jun had wanted to ask where “the sun” was, but she held back.

Consort Qin was not someone to be trifled with.

Consort Qin left with her entourage in a grand procession.

Xiang Jun knelt obediently in front of the autumn begonia, while Meng Mei stood beside her, quietly accompanying her mistress.

Xiang Jun knelt for a full two hours before finally encountering the emperor, who had finished dinner and was taking a digestive stroll with Noble Consort.

From a distance, seeing someone kneeling under the begonia tree, the emperor stopped in his tracks.

“Who is kneeling there?”

Noble Consort glanced over and frowned. “It seems to be Xu Selected Attendant.”

The emperor thought for a moment before remembering—she was the fertile one Gu Tingxue had found for him.

chapters.title: Attending the Emperor's Bedchamber
chapters.content:
"Why are you kneeling there?" Noble Consort Rong was also curious.

"Let's go see."

The Emperor, holding the Noble Consort's hand, walked over. Only when they got closer did they see how beautiful the person before them was.

The setting sun's gentle glow bathed the begonia flowers, and beneath them knelt a beauty on the verge of collapse. The sunset draped a faint golden veil over her, adding an otherworldly charm to her already enchanting face.

Perhaps from kneeling too long, Xiangjun's face was pale, giving her an air of sorrow and melancholy that tugged at the heartstrings.

A young eunuch said, "The Emperor is here, why don't you pay your respects?"

Only then did Xiangjun and Mengmei seem to react.

Mengmei hastily knelt down, while Xiangjun, already on her knees, kowtowed and said, "Long live the Emperor!"

"Why are you kneeling here?" Noble Consort Rong, who was kind-hearted, asked softly, "Your face is all pale. How long have you been kneeling?"

"It... it's because I offended Consort Zhao, so Consort Zhao punished me."

Xiangjun's pitiful appearance was like that of an injured little rabbit, making one want to pamper her.

"How did you offend Consort Zhao?" the Emperor asked.

Xiangjun didn't dare to answer. The Emperor pointed at Mengmei and said, "You tell me."

Mengmei, still kneeling, explained, "We selected attendants were admiring the begonia flowers in the imperial garden today when we encountered Consort Zhao. Consort Zhao blamed us selected attendants for only knowing Noble Consort Rong and not her. She also said... that we haven't received the Emperor's favor and have never attended His Majesty's bedchamber. Even with Noble Consort Rong's support, we are not worthy to appreciate the same flowers as her. So, she punished us selected attendants."

Xiangjun quickly kowtowed to the Emperor.

"It's all my fault for not educating the palace servants properly, letting her spout nonsense and criticize Consort Zhao. Your Majesty, please don't punish her, punish me instead."

"She only told the truth. Why should I punish you? Get up."

Xiangjun still looked hesitant and carefully asked, "Is it allowed?"

"If I tell you to get up, can't I even overrule Consort Zhao?"

Only then did Xiangjun pitifully get up.

Unfortunately, she had been kneeling for too long, and her body staggered. The Emperor had to steady her.

The Emperor was briefly captivated by the soft, boneless hand, but in just a moment, before he could savor it, Xiangjun quickly withdrew her hand.

Xiangjun took a step back, lowering her head in a honest and aggrieved manner.

"Consort Zhao is indeed a bit willful, but she doesn't have a bad heart. Don't take it to heart."

"I wouldn't dare."

Having achieved her goal of making an impression on the Emperor, Xiangjun quickly took her leave. She couldn't stay any longer, lest she offend Noble Consort Rong.

She knew that soon, the Emperor would be unable to resist the petitions from the imperial court and would begin to favor the six palaces again. Today, she only wanted to leave a good impression on the Emperor.

"Your humble servant will return to the palace now and won't disturb Your Majesty and Noble Consort Rong's flower appreciation."

The Emperor nodded, and only then did Mengmei help Xiangjun, who was limping, walk back.

Watching Xiangjun's retreating figure, Noble Consort Rong also let out a sigh of relief. She hadn't taken this opportunity to seek favor, so it seemed that Selected Attendant Xu was indeed a well-behaved and law-abiding person.

After returning to the palace, Mengmei immediately had Xiyu fetch some medicinal oil to massage Xiangjun's knees.

"You are too honest, my lady. Two hours, how could you endure that?"

Xiyu was so heartbroken she almost cried.

Previously, she had served in Concubine Cao's palace.

Concubine Cao was not a tolerant person and often cut down on the allowances for her servants. Since Xiyu was not one of Concubine Cao's personal attendants, her days were extremely difficult.

It wasn't until Concubine Cao was bestowed death for framing Noble Consort Rong that Xiyu returned to the Shanggong Bureau, waiting to be reassigned.

Later, Xiyu was chosen to serve Selected Attendant Xu in Chenxiang Palace, and only then did she realize that a palace maid's days could be this good.

Although Selected Attendant Xu had never even seen the Emperor's face, she was generous with her money and treated the servants in the palace very well.

Moreover, Selected Attendant Xu had a good temper. In the more than half a year that Xiyu had served her, the Selected Attendant had never spoken a harsh word to her.

How could she not cherish such a mistress?

Seeing Xiyu's tearful appearance, Xiangjun and Mengmei exchanged helpless glances.

Mengmei and Xiangjun had grown up together. Although she also felt heartbroken for Xiangjun, she knew Xiangjun's character.

In this world, there was no pain that she couldn't endure. Kneeling for a while was nothing for someone of their background.

But Mengmei was still somewhat touched by Xiyu's sincerity.

"It's fine. You just need to properly massage the medicinal oil for the Selected Attendant. She'll be better in a couple of days," Mengmei said.

Xiyu, being young, puffed up her cheeks and said, "How is it fine? Such a large bruise, she won't be able to walk properly for days! Sister Mengmei, how did you serve the mistress? Didn't you even find something for the mistress to kneel on? You just let her kneel on that stony path?"

"We had to make the act convincing. How could we use a cushion?" Mengmei consoled Xiyu, "If we were found out, wouldn't all of the mistress's plans for today be in vain?"

Mengmei wasn't angry at Xiyu for her rebuke. Instead, she felt that the little girl had a spirited nature, which wasn't a bad thing.

Xiyu continued to gently massage Xiangjun, aggrieved as she said, "I know, but I just feel heartbroken."

Xiangjun smiled and pinched Xiyu's chubby cheeks, "Don't worry. You underestimate me too much. Your mistress can endure anything."

If Xiyu had seen how she was carried out of the Taiji Hall in her previous life, she might have smashed her head against the pillars of the Taiji Hall.

Afraid that Xiyu would dwell on this topic, Xiangjun asked, "Did you see Lady Li today? How is she?"

Xiyu replied, "I told Lady Li what the mistress instructed. Lady Li didn't ask anything; she just told me to rest assured and that she would handle this matter for you."

Mengmei whispered, "Lady Li is indeed grateful. She managed to bring the Emperor and Noble Consort Rong here, so the mistress's effort to save her life wasn't in vain."

Xiangjun asked Xiyu again, "How has she been recently?"

"Since she's carrying the imperial heir, naturally no one dares to mistreat her. The food on her table is all of the finest quality. However..." Xiyu hesitated before saying, "Lady Li has lost a lot of weight. She doesn't look like someone who is with child, and her spirits aren't good either."

Xiangjun sighed. She couldn't think of a way to comfort her at the moment.

In her previous life, Xiangjun had experienced what Lady Li was going through.

Even she had taken a long time to come to terms with it and swallow the bitterness and humiliation in her heart.

However, this bitterness was hard to swallow. If one couldn't come to terms with it themselves, no one else could persuade them.

...

Xiangjun's prediction was correct.

Half a month later, the Emperor finally couldn't bear the criticism from the officials and began to summon other concubines to his bedchamber.

Emperor Yanqing didn't have many concubines in his harem. There were only a little over ten, and several had died over the years. There really wasn't much to choose from.

Thus, without much hesitation, he summoned Xiangjun.

Finally, the day of attending the Emperor's bedchamber arrived. As she stepped onto the steps of Taiji Hall once again, Xiangjun's feelings were a mix of emotions.

In her previous life, the first time she stepped onto these steps, she had been full of ambition and wild aspirations. In the end, she was carried out in utter shame and agony.

Now, having lived two lives, she once again entered the depths of the palace without hesitation.

She stepped onto these steps solely for revenge, solely for the day when she could trample the most supreme man in the world under her feet.

chapters.title: A Fatal Question
chapters.content:
After entering Taiji Hall, the Emperor had not yet arrived. A wet nurse instructed Xiangjun on what to pay attention to when attending the Emperor for the first time.

Xiangjun lowered her head, listening with a seemingly shy expression, but her mind was elsewhere.

To ensure her first night with the Emperor left an impression, Xiangjun had planned for a long time.

She not only repeatedly recalled the content of the storybooks she had seen in the illusion but also endured her disgust to repeatedly remember every detail of her interactions with the Emperor in her previous life.

Compared to the judgments in the books, Xiangjun trusted her own memory more.

It wasn't that she didn't trust the book; she just felt that books were written by people and would inevitably carry the author's personal feelings. The same event could sometimes be described differently, leading to vastly different interpretations.

Therefore, Xiangjun only believed the concrete events in the book, not its judgment of Emperor Yanqing.

The book said that Emperor Yanqing was a strong ruler, but he was introverted and restrained, which led to many misunderstandings and a long, abusive love affair with Xue Jiaojiao.

Xiangjun found this inaccurate.

Based on her interactions with Emperor Yanqing in her previous life and what she had learned about his upbringing from the book, Xiangjun was certain that this man was not strong at all.

The dog emperor was all bluster, filled with inferiority and arrogance due to being bullied by the entire palace as a child. He cared most about others' opinions of him and was extremely concerned with face.

Xiangjun, coming from the common folk, knew how rotten the prosperity of the Great Qi was beneath its flourishing surface.

After ten years as emperor, the dynasty had not prospered under his rule, nor had the people lived in peace and contentment. How could he be considered a strong ruler?

Hah, he wasn't even a strong person...

So Xiangjun's feelings were complex. She truly looked down on this dog emperor.

Although his appearance was top-tier, his inner self was rotten to the core. The stench of his despicable nature couldn't be masked even by the finest dragon's saliva incense.

She really disdained serving such a rotten person, but for her future and to gain power, she had to fawn over him in every way possible.

The wet nurse finished her instructions and left, leaving Xiangjun alone to sit by the bed and wait.

Outside the green gauze canopy, two young eunuchs stood guard.

They stood there like two ornaments, motionless, and one might easily forget they were there.

In her previous life, Xiangjun had been very uncomfortable with the idea of having people watch during such intimate moments.

But later, she learned that for the Emperor, eunuchs weren't considered people. Since they weren't people, naturally, there was no shame in doing anything in front of them.

Unfortunately, after two lifetimes, Xiangjun still couldn't learn how to not treat people as people.

Footsteps were heard outside the warm chamber. Xiangjun looked up and saw a figure in bright yellow approaching—it was the Emperor.

Upon seeing the Emperor enter, Xiangjun immediately squatted down and performed a deep curtsy.

"Long live the Emperor."

Xiangjun immediately lowered her head, hiding the disgust in her eyes.

When she looked up again, her face was filled with the shyness of a young girl and complete admiration for a powerful man.

Xiangjun felt that if she could endure such hardship, she would succeed in anything she did in this life.

"Why are you looking at me like this?" the Emperor asked.

Xiangjun lifted her head and said the words she had prepared.

"Your humble servant... admires Your Majesty..."

"Admire me? Have you seen me before?"

The Emperor sat down by the bed, seemingly disbelief in his tone.

Xiangjun thought it was normal for the Emperor not to believe her.

Although he was arrogant, he was also insecure.

So, Xiangjun continued with eyes full of admiration, "Your humble servant is not like the other noble consorts in the palace, born of high status. I was raised among the common folk and naturally have never seen Your Majesty's divine countenance. But even in the common folk, I have heard of Your Majesty's literary and martial achievements. My father also taught me that the people of Jiangnan live in peace and prosperity because Your Majesty is a wise ruler."

The Emperor smiled. No one in this world disliked flattery.

"Your father is quite good at teaching his daughter."

"But Xiangjun admires Your Majesty not because you are a wise ruler, but because... because..." Xiangjun lowered her head coyly, her voice as soft as a mosquito's buzz, "Because when I first saw Your Majesty in the imperial garden, I could never forget you. Your Majesty is the most handsome man I have ever seen in my life..."

The Emperor had inherited the Empress Dowager's looks, and the Empress Dowager was famously known as the most enchanting beauty of her generation. So naturally, the Emperor's appearance was beyond reproach.

Xiangjun's compliment on this point wouldn't make the Emperor feel it was insincere.

The Emperor shook his head helplessly, a hint of indulgence in his eyes as if looking at a child.

"How old are you? How many people have you seen?"

Xiangjun looked at the Emperor and immediately put on a defiant expression.

"Although Your humble servant may not be as nobly born as the other consorts in the palace, I was born in the prosperous land of Jiangnan. My father, though a merchant, has relatives who are officials. I have seen many scholarly and talented figures since I was young."

The Emperor became interested, "Oh, then tell me, who have you seen?"

Xiangjun mentioned some famous scholars from Jiangnan. For each one, she could find a point where they fell short compared to the Emperor. In short, the Emperor was the most extraordinary and heroic man she had ever seen in her life, and she had fallen for him at first sight. That was absolutely genuine.

Seeing the young girl speak with such sincerity and lively wit, the Emperor's heart softened.

Men always easily believe that women love them, especially an emperor who rules over all. Facing a young girl like Xiangjun, how could he feel inferior? It would only stir his arrogance.

The Emperor was greatly pleased by Xiangjun's flattery.

Xiangjun continued to praise him, talking about the many legendary tales of the Emperor in Jiangnan and the numerous storybooks written about him by scholars in secret. The Emperor listened with great delight.

However, suddenly, he thought of someone else.

"Have you heard of Grand General Wang in Jiangnan?"

Well, Xiangjun thought, this is a fatal question.

This Grand General Wang was the Emperor's half-brother from a different mother.

When the previous emperor was alive, Grand General Wang's mother concubine was one of the Emperor's favored consorts and came from a distinguished military family. However, she eventually died at the hands of the current Empress Dowager.

But that wasn't important. What was important was that Grand General Wang was a devoted follower of Noble Consort Rong!

He was also the Emperor's number one rival in love, as depicted in the book.

This Grand General Wang had been exiled to his northern fief by the Emperor but still harbored feelings for Noble Consort Rong.

Seeing that Xiangjun wasn't speaking, the Emperor's expression turned displeased. "Why aren't you speaking?"

chapters.title: Pitying the Beauty
chapters.content:
The emperor was deeply jealous of the dashing General Wang in his heart, after all, the general had been cherished by the late emperor since childhood.

Xiangjun pondered for a moment before softly saying, "This subject concubine is not refusing to speak. I have heard of General Wang, but as a woman from Jiangnan, I dislike those martial men and do not enjoy listening to stories of war, so I am not very familiar with him."

The emperor looked at Xiangjun’s delicate and frail appearance and thought she was probably not lying.

Jiangnan was known for its literary culture, and most people there admired scholars.

Satisfied, the emperor asked again, "What about Prince Jin?"

Xiangjun’s heart skipped a beat.

Prince Jin had once been the crown prince under the late emperor.

Prince Jin was the emperor’s elder brother. Back when the emperor was just a pitiful child, bullied by the other princes, it was this illustrious crown prince who had always helped him.

However, the more pure and gentle this elder brother was, the more it highlighted the emperor’s own darkness, so the emperor despised this former crown prince the most.

Not to mention, Prince Jin was also the white moon of Noble Consort, whom Noble Consort had secretly admired in her youth.

Unfortunately, they had missed each other, and it became a lifelong regret.

Xiangjun stammered, "This subject concubine is young and has never heard of Prince Jin’s affairs... I’m sorry, it’s my lack of knowledge..."

The emperor thought it made sense. Xiangjun was only seventeen years old.

When he ascended the throne, she was probably only six or seven, too young to understand such matters. Over the years, Prince Jin had traveled the world, almost in seclusion, so it was normal that she didn’t know about the former crown prince.

"Have you heard of Prime Minister Song? He is from Jiangnan."

Xiangjun was speechless. Was this interrogation never going to end?

This question was even harder to answer.

Song Feijing was indeed famous. Everyone called him the Jade-Faced Prime Minister. At the age of thirty, he had already risen to the position of the second most powerful man in the previous dynasty.

Moreover, he was extremely handsome and talented, a renowned literary figure.

If she said she hadn’t heard of him or didn’t admire him, it would seem disingenuous.

"I have heard of him..." Xiangjun’s face showed a shy expression.

The emperor’s expression darkened slightly.

Before the emperor could get angry, Xiangjun pretended to be embarrassed and said, "It’s just that what I’ve heard are all folk rumors. I’m afraid they might sully Your Majesty’s ears or offend Prime Minister Song."

"Speak."

"This subject concubine has heard... that Prime Minister Song has a preference for men... that he remains unmarried because of it."

The emperor’s face darkened further, but he was not angry with Xiangjun.

He was angry with Song Feijing.

If such rumors were already circulating among the people, and he still refused to marry!

It wasn’t because of his preference for men that Song Feijing refused to marry—it was for *her*!

How dare he covet the emperor’s women? He truly deserved to die.

"Ah..."

A soft, tender moan sounded, and only then did the emperor notice that Xiangjun had been kneeling the whole time.

"Your Majesty, this subject concubine’s legs have gone numb."

"If I don’t tell you to rise, you won’t do it on your own? You foolish thing."

"This subject concubine respects Your Majesty."

"Rise."

Xiangjun struggled to her feet, but as soon as she stood, her legs gave out, and she collapsed into the emperor’s arms.

Instinctively, the emperor caught her and pulled her into his embrace.

The refreshing fragrance that filled his senses stirred his heart.

Xiangjun acted surprised, trying to get up, but in her panic, she tore open her collar, revealing her fair and delicate shoulder.

The emperor’s expression darkened, and he scooped her up horizontally.

"The spring night is short, and it’s late. Let us retire early."

...

When Xiangjun left the Tai Ji Hall, her entire body ached.

But no matter how exhausting it was, tonight had been a normal duty in the bedchamber. Compared to the torture-like, death-defying experiences of her past life, this time felt almost like child’s play.

Apart from feeling mentally drained, she didn’t have any other strong feelings.

Perhaps because Xiangjun had performed well today, the emperor took pity and rewarded her with a palanquin.

A young eunuch led Xiangjun out of the Tai Ji Hall.

Unexpectedly, as soon as she stepped out, she ran into someone—Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue was dressed in a black python robe today, looking travel-worn, as if he had just returned from an errand outside the palace.

"Eunuch Gu."

Upon seeing Xiangjun, Gu Tingxue’s face showed no extra emotion. He merely greeted her indifferently, saying, "Greetings, Beauty Lian."

As she passed by Gu Tingxue, Xiangjun caught a strong scent of blood.

But tonight, Gu Tingxue was wearing black, and in the darkness, nothing was visible. She didn’t know if the blood on him was his own or someone else’s.

The eunuch guarding the door, seeing that Xiangjun had come out, immediately went inside to announce her departure. By the time Xiangjun boarded her palanquin, Gu Tingxue had already entered the hall.

Apart from the moment when Gu Tingxue glanced at her during the greeting, he didn’t spare her another look.

Xiangjun felt a pang of disappointment. *He’s so cold.*

She wondered when she would finally be able to cling to this powerful figure.

...

The next morning, the news of Xiangjun being bestowed the title of Beauty Lian was announced throughout the six palaces.

In the rear palace, there were not many concubines with official titles.

The emperor had never been one to waste effort on such matters. After all, apart from Noble Consort, he rarely visited the palaces of the other consorts.

Thus, Xiangjun was the first concubine after Noble Consort to receive an official title.

For a moment, the women in the rear palace were filled with various thoughts.

*Could it be that as soon as the emperor shifted his gaze away from Noble Consort, he had already found a new favorite?*

Even Xiangjun herself was somewhat surprised.

*Hmm? What did she do right last night to make the emperor so generous? This was important!*

Xiangjun racked her brains but couldn’t find an answer.

Even though the emperor had been satisfied with her performance, it wasn’t to *this* extent, was it?

Unable to figure it out, Xiangjun gave up and set out early to pay her respects to Her Majesty the Empress.

Now that the Empress had recovered from her illness, she had also regained some authority in the rear palace.

According to custom, after a concubine’s first night of attending the emperor, she was to pay her respects to the Empress the next day.

Xiangjun had arrived quite early, but to her surprise, when she arrived, the Empress was already receiving De Consort and Lady Sun.

---

chapters.title: Noble Consort’s Jealousy
chapters.content:
De Consort was the mother of the eldest prince. Her grandfather had once been a high-ranking official governing a province, and now he was an honored retiree of the first rank. She had a honest and kind appearance, and preferred to dress in dark colors. She looked older than the emperor.

Lady Sun was the mother of the second princess. She was younger, only twenty-five this year. Her father was a Grand Secretary, and she could be considered a gem of a commoner’s family, with some beauty.

There weren’t many children in the palace, so these two naturally held high status due to their children.

Today wasn’t a grand day for all the palace ladies to pay their respects to the Empress, so why were these two here?

Could it be that they had heard about the new title of Beauty Lian and came to see the commotion?

Xiangjun had learned the rules well in this life. She paid her respects to the Empress, then greeted De Consort and Lady Sun with proper etiquette, without a single flaw.

The Empress examined Xiangjun. She was truly beautiful, with a charming allure unique to women from Jiangnan. No wonder the emperor favored her.

However, her words and actions were not frivolous, and she didn’t seem like the type to rely on favoritism. The Empress thus took a slight liking to her.

The Empress didn’t feel much about Xiangjun receiving a title; in fact, she even felt a little happy.

In the rear palace, as long as someone could make Noble Consort seem less special, the Empress was pleased.

The Empress rewarded Xiangjun and gave her a few words of advice before letting her leave.

After Xiangjun left, De Consort and Lady Sun looked at the Empress with some concern.

"Your Majesty, this Beauty Lian is Noble Consort’s person. Now that she has received a title, and it seems the emperor favors her, if you do nothing, aren’t you afraid she will join forces with Noble Consort to captivate the emperor, leading him to become even more unrestrained?"

The Empress took a sip of tea, appearing quite calm.

"She lives in Chengxiang Hall, which Noble Consort arranged for her. If Noble Consort truly wanted to promote her, why would she let her live in such a remote place, unseen by the emperor for over half a year? If it weren’t for Qin Zhao Yi punishing her and the emperor encountering her by chance, the emperor might never have noticed her existence in this lifetime... I think Noble Consort is wary of her youthful and delicate face... The fact that she is Noble Consort’s person might not be taken seriously."

Looking at the incompetent De Consort and Lady Sun, the Empress sighed helplessly.

"What are you panicking about? You have a prince and a princess respectively, and both of you come from prestigious families. Even if new faces enter the palace in the future, your positions will remain secure. If one Beauty Lian can make you panic, how will you survive when the selection of new consorts happens next year?"

"His Majesty is selecting new consorts next year?" De Consort asked in surprise.

After ascending the throne, the emperor had not held a selection due to his promise to Xue Jiaojiao.

Currently, among the dozen or so women in the palace, the Empress, De Consort, and Wang Wan Yi had been bestowed by the late emperor when the current emperor was still the crown prince. Noble Consort was the emperor’s first love. The rest were mostly daughters of officials the emperor needed to use, all sent into the rear palace for political reasons.

"Yes, His Majesty has relented and agreed to hold a selection next year."

Given the emperor’s nature, if he agreed to take in new women, he would naturally favor them and not just keep them in the palace without attention.

After all, the emperor was now thirty years old. He had been emperor for nearly ten years, and his relationship with Noble Consort, no matter how deep, had lost its novelty.

Now, for the emperor, imperial power was more important.

And the imperial heir was the most crucial part of that power.

Watching De Consort and Lady Sun with their worried expressions, the Empress was truly annoyed.

These two were useless. Although they had children, neither was particularly beautiful, and with their good family backgrounds, they were not easy to control. Apart from occasionally coming to chat with her, they served no other purpose.

Once new faces arrived, they would no longer be needed.

"I am also tired. You may leave."

De Consort and Lady Sun had no choice but to rise and take their leave.

...

After returning to her palace, Xiangjun received rewards from Noble Consort.

Without delay, Xiangjun, accompanied by Meng Mei, went to Noble Consort’s palace to express her gratitude.

She had been pretending to be Noble Consort’s person all along, so she had to play her part well.

Xiangjun could clearly sense that Noble Consort’s attendant, Cai Wei, was glaring at her coldly.

*Honestly, Noble Consort didn’t show any jealousy on her face, so why was Cai Wei so concerned about the emperor favoring other concubines?*

It didn’t matter. Xiangjun could pretend not to notice her hostility and continue to smile sweetly.

She happily thanked Noble Consort for the reward and exaggeratedly expressed how much she loved the golden hairpin Noble Consort had given her, saying she had never seen such a exquisite item in her life.

Noble Consort still maintained her graceful and generous demeanor, but Xiangjun detected a hidden sorrow in her eyes.

She and the emperor were in "true love," so any time the emperor favored another woman, she would feel sorrow.

Since Noble Consort was uncomfortable, Xiangjun was even happier. She continued to animatedly express her sincere devotion to Noble Consort.

It wasn’t until Cai Wei noticed that Noble Consort’s expression was truly unsightly that she dismissed Xiangjun on the pretext of Noble Consort’s indisposition.

As soon as she stepped out, Xiangjun encountered Li Gengyi.

Li Gengyi had become alarmingly thin.

If she continued to lose weight like this, she might not survive until the child was born.

After exchanging greetings, Xiangjun went over and took her hand. "This is the first time I’ve seen you, Li Gengyi. You are blessed to carry His Majesty’s child, but you must take good care of yourself."

Li Gengyi also smiled at Xiangjun. "Thank you for your concern, Beauty Lian."

"Are you here to pay your respects to Noble Consort?"

Li Gengyi nodded and was about to go inside when she saw Cai Wei coming out.

"Li Gengyi, you don’t need to come pay your respects to Her Ladyship these days. Her Ladyship is unwell, so you should return for now."

Xiangjun quickly interjected, "I just saw Noble Consort. She is truly unwell. She could barely speak a few words to me before getting tired. It was my fault for talking too much and tiring her out. I have nothing to do now, so how about I go to Li Gengyi’s place for a visit? You can keep me company."

Li Gengyi put on an expression of helplessness, as if she couldn’t refuse, and nodded.

...

Xiangjun followed Li Gengyi into her room.

Li Gengyi dismissed the servants, leaving only the two of them in the room to talk.

Without a word, Xiangjun rolled up Li Gengyi’s sleeve and looked.

She was shocked by what she saw.

Li Gengyi’s arm was so thin it was almost skeletal.

"How did you get so thin? Did Noble Consort mistreat you?"

Li Gengyi shook her head. "No, she doesn’t pay attention to me at all, so she doesn’t mistreat me either."

"You’re carrying a child under her roof, and she should take care of you. How can she just wash her hands of responsibility? Don’t worry, I’ll have someone send you some tonics when I return."

"It’s not necessary. Since I’m carrying the emperor’s child, the imperial kitchen doesn’t dare neglect me, and the Empress Dowager also sends good food every day. It’s just that I can’t eat much."

Xiangjun was very anxious. "You have to take care of yourself, if not for the child, then for your own sake!"

Xiangjun would never advise Li Gengyi to consider the child.

The emperor’s child was not as important as Li Gengyi’s own life!

Li Gengyi smiled bitterly, her voice filled with sorrow. "What’s the point of taking care of myself? Once I give birth to this child, I’ll be of no use. They’ll probably take the child and discard me. I’m only living a few more months at most."

The daughters of Jiangnan merchants were not naive fools.

After all, the inner chambers of noble families were just as filthy, filled with dark and secretive affairs.

So Li Gengyi naturally understood the dark secrets of the rear palace.

"It’s possible, but Noble Consort is a kind-hearted person..." Xiangjun thought carefully about her wording before continuing gently, "She is soft-hearted. You need to take advantage of her kindness. As long as she says a word, you can still live."

Li Gengyi’s hollow eyes suddenly filled with terror. "What’s the point of living? Wouldn’t I still be neither human nor ghost? Beauty Lian, do you know that whenever I close my eyes, I see the emperor on top of me?"

chapters.title: Contraceptive Decoction
chapters.content:
"That time, his neck was covered in black veins, his eyes bloodshot—he looked like a demon. I was truly afraid of him; just seeing him made me tremble. Do you know? Now, I’m not only afraid of His Majesty, but of all men. I can’t even have eunuchs attend me… Tell me, even if I stay in the palace, what use am I?"

Xiangjun saw that Consort Li seemed to be suffering from depression.

That dog emperor truly committed atrocities—he deserved to die!

Xiangjun understood. Not everyone was like her, growing more defiant the more they were bullied. When she was a child, her parents had said she had a bad temper—she never let an insult go unanswered.

But she couldn’t expect everyone to be like her.

Consort Li’s mind was on the verge of collapse. Though she feared death, she couldn’t find the will to live.

But this was a mental affliction—Xiangjun had no idea how to cure it.

She couldn’t very well tell Consort Li now: *Just endure for now. When I kill the emperor in the future, you won’t be afraid anymore.*

Helpless, Xiangjun called for Consort Li’s maid and asked what she had eaten that day.

Learning that she hadn’t eaten anything since morning, Xiangjun quickly ordered a meal to be prepared.

"I’m not hungry."

"Even if you’re not, I am. I’m just a lowly beauty—I’ve never had the food meant for the mother of an imperial heir. Sister, let me experience it through you."

Consort Li had no choice but to agree.

...

From a distance, Caiwei saw Xiangjun enter Consort Li’s palace before returning to report to Noble Consort.

"That wretched Beauty Lian is so vulgar—she really is from a lowly family. She chattered away and went to disturb Consort Li, not even caring if she startled the child in her womb."

Noble Consort looked listless.

Though she knew His Majesty favored other women for his own reasons, she still couldn’t help feeling distressed.

"Beauty Lian is young, so naturally she’s lively. You shouldn’t speak so harshly."

"Your Grace… don’t be sad. I think His Majesty favors Beauty Lian for your sake. Have you forgotten? His Majesty brought Beauty Lian in for you…"

Noble Consort’s eyes lit up for a moment. Yes, His Majesty had said before that Beauty Lian’s child would be raised by her.

But soon, her gaze darkened again.

"But there’s already a Consort Li in my palace."

His Majesty had placed Consort Li in her palace precisely so she could raise the child in her womb.

So His Majesty’s favor toward Beauty Lian wasn’t for having a child—he simply liked her a little.

If he didn’t like her, why would he summon her three times in one night?

And why would he bestow a title upon her?

Before this, she had been the only one in the entire palace with a title.

"Now she’s already a Beauty. In the future, if her rank rises, who knows—His Majesty might let her raise her own child." Noble Consort muttered, "Wasn’t that how Consort Sun rose to the rank of Concubine after bearing a princess?"

Thinking of Beauty Lian’s exquisite, androgynous beauty, Noble Consort felt even more distressed.

Why couldn’t she bear a child for the man she loved?

Seeing her mistress’s sorrow, Caiwei couldn’t help but offer advice.

"Your Grace, that Beauty Lian is just from a lowly family. If you don’t want her to have a child, it’s just a matter of a word."

"How could I do such a thing?" Noble Consort waved her hand. "I’m tired. Help me rest."

Caiwei supported Noble Consort into the room to rest.

After settling her mistress, Caiwei called for De Bao, the chief eunuch of Ganlu Palace, and whispered a few words to him.

De Bao looked incredulous. "Does Her Grace know about this?"

"Some things, even if Her Grace doesn’t say them, you and I should understand."

...

After persuading Consort Li to eat something, Xiangjun returned to her own Chengxiang Palace.

As soon as she arrived, Xiangjun had Xiyu deliver some gifts to Consort Li.

They were all items brought from Jiangnan, hoping they might ease her homesickness.

Other than that, Xiangjun couldn’t think of anything else to do.

For a moment, she felt genuinely distressed.

She wondered—had she ruined Consort Li?

If she hadn’t taken that official’s daughter’s place in the palace, Consort Li wouldn’t have filled her vacant position.

But she quickly reasoned it out.

What did it have to do with her? She was a victim too. A victim saving herself was nothing wrong.

The real culprit was that high-and-mighty dog emperor.

He was the one who caused the harm—he truly deserved to die.

As Xiangjun sat there, gnashing her teeth in fury, she saw De Fu, the chief eunuch of Noble Consort’s palace, enter carrying a food box.

Mengmei called out, "Beauty Lian, De Fu has come to deliver medicine to you."

Xiangjun snapped back to reality. "What medicine?"

De Fu bent down with a smile. "In response to Beauty Lian, this is a pregnancy-preserving decoction bestowed by Noble Consort."

Xiangjun was very suspicious of whether this was really a pregnancy-preserving decoction.

"Thank you for your trouble, De Fu. It must have been a hard journey. Put it down first—I’ll drink it later."

"Noble Consort cares for Beauty Lian. It would be unwise to waste her kindness. This medicine should be drunk while hot."

This was forcing her to drink it.

Noble Consort had the authority to manage the Six Palaces and was the emperor’s most favored concubine. If she ordered Xiangjun to drink, Xiangjun had no room to refuse.

Realizing this, Xiangjun had no more hesitation.

Playing the part of an obedient girl, she immediately said, "How could I waste Noble Consort’s kindness? I adore her the most—why wouldn’t I drink it? I was just thinking of having some preserved fruits before drinking, but since De Fu says so… I’ll drink it right away!"

Xiangjun picked up the bowl and drank the medicine in one go.

She knew Noble Consort—she was capable of murder.

The people around her were all gilded spears—none were truly kind, yet none were ruthless enough.

Otherwise, in her past life, they wouldn’t have given her so many opportunities to exploit.

So as long as it wouldn’t kill her, Xiangjun dared to drink it.

Seeing that she had obediently finished it and even looked grateful, the little eunuch assumed she had no suspicions about Noble Consort’s intentions and no guard up at all. Thinking her foolish, he left satisfied.

As soon as the eunuch left, Xiangjun immediately called for Mengmei.

"Take this bowl to your brother and have him examine what kind of medicine this is."

Soon, Xiangjun got her answer—it was a contraceptive decoction.

She had suspected as much, but she still found it strange.

Noble Consort would do this? This hadn’t happened in her past life.

According to the annotations in the book, this was a move to ruin someone.

"Beauty, this contraceptive decoction is harmful to the body. You mustn’t drink it often." Mengmei cautioned. "My brother said drinking it a few times is fine, but if you take it for too long, it might affect your fertility."

"I’ll keep that in mind."

"Then should I have my brother prepare some tonics for you?"

Xiangjun laughed. "What, do you want to help me recover already?"

"Of course! Beauty, you still need to have a child to truly have support in the palace."

"It’s fine. As long as I don’t serve the emperor every night, I won’t have to drink it constantly. Once or twice won’t matter."

Xiangjun thought she had to leave some traces of having consumed the contraceptive decoction.

She couldn’t rush to recover just yet.

---

chapters.title: Disloyal Intentions
chapters.content:
Xiangjun never expected that very night, the emperor would summon her again.

She was truly surprised.

Apart from Noble Consort and Qin Zhao Yi, who had been favored not long ago, no other concubine in the palace had ever been summoned consecutively.

And that half-year when Qin Zhao Yi was in high favor, it was only because the emperor’s illness hadn’t fully healed.

Even though there were three designated "treatment days" each month, on the other days, his body still carried the poison.

He didn’t care about the body of a foreign concubine, which was why he had favored only her.

Qin Zhao Yi had thought the emperor truly adored her—how pitiful.

But now, why was the emperor favoring Xiangjun two days in a row?

Had she performed *that* well?

...

Xiangjun put on an act of gentle obedience as she entered the Tai Ji Hall.

To her surprise, the person waiting outside the green gauze partition was Gu Tingxue.

That dog emperor was truly a dog emperor.

Just yesterday, he had sent someone through a bloody storm, returning covered in blood, and today he had that person standing night watch like a servant. How could he treat people like this?

If he didn’t know how to cherish such a good minister, she wouldn’t blame herself for stealing him away.

Gu Tingxue kept his gaze fixed ahead, and Xiangjun didn’t dare say much. Maintaining her act of a shy, innocent girl, she walked past the partition into the warm chamber.

The emperor was sitting on the bed reading a book, which reminded Xiangjun of Gu Tingxue.

The first time she had seen him, he too had been reading in bed.

This master and servant pair were quite alike.

Upon seeing Xiangjun, the emperor dropped the pretense, tossing the book aside and pulling her into his embrace.

"What are you daydreaming about? Come here."

...

While serving the emperor, Xiangjun finally understood why he had summoned her again today.

It was indeed because of how well she had performed yesterday.

In her past life, she had always been too restrained during such moments.

Because everyone in the palace looked down on her, she had tried even harder to mimic their noble demeanor, to prove she was just as refined as them.

This life, she had changed her approach—and unexpectedly, it had won the emperor’s favor.

Truly, that dog emperor was despicable.

...

Fortunately, the emperor couldn’t see Xiangjun’s expression or know how impatient she felt.

Xiangjun turned her head slightly, gazing wearily at the glass decanter beside the dragon bed—when suddenly, she saw it.

She saw the flaw she had been waiting for...

...

After returning to Chengxiang Palace, Xiangjun took a thorough bath.

She couldn’t scrub too hard in Tai Ji Hall—otherwise, it would seem like she disdained the emperor.

Today, Xiangjun had figured it out: the emperor’s desire for her was purely physical.

Physical desire wouldn’t last. So she couldn’t let him be truly satisfied. She had to make him crave her, to want what he couldn’t have.

After all, only through comparison would he realize who was truly good, right?

But what made her happiest was what she had seen in Tai Ji Hall—those eyes.

In the past, there had been incidents of palace maids assassinating the emperor during intimate moments. So when concubines came to Tai Ji Hall to serve him, eunuchs would always be present. Since eunuchs weren’t considered men, they were no different from the glass decanter beside the dragon bed.

The emperor didn’t need to hide such matters from eunuchs.

In fact, there were even specialized eunuchs who recorded the emperor’s intimate affairs in detail.

But a eunuch truly loyal to the emperor shouldn’t have such a look in his eyes.

In that one glance, Xiangjun had seen beneath Gu Tingxue’s respectful facade—a trace of disgust, a hint of disdain for imperial power.

Perfect. It seemed Gu Tingxue wasn’t truly loyal to that dog emperor either.

Previously, Xiangjun had always seen Gu Tingxue as the greatest obstacle on her path to revenge.

From what she knew, Gu Tingxue was ten years younger than the emperor. At just seven years old, he had been taken in by the emperor to serve him.

What could a seven-year-old do? Nothing but be raised like a child at his side.

It was said the emperor had even taught him how to write. One could say Gu Tingxue was entirely the emperor’s creation.

Xiangjun felt that apart from treating him as a servant, the emperor had been good to him. He had even granted him the privilege of not having to bow to court officials.

Even as a servant, Gu Tingxue was the emperor’s alone—it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say he was second only to the emperor himself.

She had worried that Gu Tingxue harbored genuine loyalty to the emperor. No matter how hard she tried to win him over, he might remain a loyal subject.

But that glance in Tai Ji Hall had revealed a crack.

Xiangjun knew she had finally found a kindred spirit.

She had found someone with disloyal intentions.

...

On the third day, the emperor wanted to summon Xiangjun again.

He hadn’t intended to favor Beauty Lian three days in a row, but among the young concubines in the harem, apart from Qin Zhao Yi, only Xiangjun was new. The others had been serving him for years.

None of them brought him as much pleasure in bed as Xiangjun did.

But the emperor thought that even the most beautiful woman would lose her charm with too much frequency. Better to indulge now, satisfy his desire, and perhaps after some time, his interest would wane.

But when he went to select her token, he didn’t see Beauty Lian’s green plaque.

"Where is Beauty Lian?" the emperor asked.

"Beauty Lian is ill."

"She was fine yesterday. How is she sick today?"

"Beauty Lian…" The eunuch from the Bedchamber Service hesitated before forcing himself to say, "After serving His Majesty yesterday, Beauty Lian was… somewhat injured. We consulted an imperial physician, and he advised that Beauty Lian rest for a few days to recover. So the Bedchamber Service has temporarily removed her plaque."

The emperor felt a pang of embarrassment. He cleared his throat, recalling that he had indeed been less than gentle the night before.

So the emperor called for Gu Tingxue. "Tingxue, take some gifts from my private treasury to Beauty Lian. Find things she would like."

"I, your servant, do not know what Beauty Lian likes."

Among all the eunuchs in the palace, only Gu Tingxue was permitted to refer to himself as "your servant"—a special privilege granted by the emperor.

"She is a woman from Jiangnan. Just find things that women from Jiangnan would like."

"Yes."

Gu Tingxue withdrew.

The emperor looked at the dozen or so plaques of his concubines and felt his interest wane.

Recalling that it had been some days since he had seen Noble Consort, he finally selected her plaque. "Then I shall visit Noble Consort today."

chapters.title: She Was Overjoyed
chapters.content:
When Gu Tingxue led the people to deliver the imperial rewards, the gates of all the palaces were already locked.

Xiangjun suspected that Gu Tingxue had deliberately come so late.

Xiangjun had already gone to bed. Upon hearing that it was Eunuch Gu, she couldn’t be bothered to change her clothes. She simply wore her sleeping attire and had someone invite Eunuch Gu in for tea.

When Gu Tingxue entered the room, Xiangjun was lying on the daybed, dressed in a lotus-pink sleeping gown, with her eyes closed in meditation.

She truly suited the lotus-pink color—it made her look so tender that one could almost pinch water from her skin.

As soon as Gu Tingxue entered, Meng Mei quickly slipped out and closed the door behind her.

For some reason, Gu Tingxue felt a hint of awkwardness.

"Aren’t you inviting me for tea, Beauty? Where is it?"

Only then did Xiangjun rise gracefully, walking leisurely to the table. She personally picked up a cup of tea and approached Gu Tingxue with a charming demeanor.

"I will serve you the tea myself, Eunuch."

Gu Tingxue lowered his gaze, glanced at her, then reached out to take the teacup and took a sip.

The two fell silent for a while, neither bringing up the lingering gaze they had shared the previous night.

When Gu Tingxue finished his tea, Xiangjun took the cup from him and set it down.

"Eunuch, why have you come so late?"

"The Emperor instructed me to select gifts that the Beauty would like, so I took some time."

"Is that so? Then what did Eunuch choose for me?"

"Nothing but some gold and silver hairpins. However, there is one item that is quite fine—it would suit Beauty Lian well."

Xiangjun was curious. If even Gu Tingxue found it pleasing, it must be extraordinary.

"What is it?"

Gu Tingxue replied, "It is a cape made of black fox fur, flawless without a single stray hair. I wonder if Beauty Lian would like it?"

Xiangjun was absolutely delighted—she was over the moon.

In her past life, she had seen this fox fur cape before. Back then, she had been so envious of it.

This item had been sent to the capital by Great General Wang Zhongqiu as a tribute to the Emperor.

Though it was presented to the Emperor, it was a cape meant for a woman. Thus, General Wang’s true intention was to hope that the Emperor would bestow it upon Noble Consort Gui.

Even though the Emperor was displeased, he still gave the cape to Noble Consort Gui during the first snowfall of winter that year. After all, there was no finer fox fur cape in the entire palace.

Who would have thought that in this life, Gu Tingxue would bring this very cape to her at this moment?

She was overjoyed!

Xiangjun was not one for simplicity—she adored luxury.

If one lived without truly enjoying life, without grandeur and splendor, how dull would that be?

Seeing Xiangjun so ecstatic, Gu Tingxue couldn’t help but curve the corners of his lips.

"Beauty Lian hasn’t even seen it, yet you are already this happy?"

"Eunuch’s taste is impeccable. Winter is approaching, and I was just thinking of wanting such a cape. Eunuch, you’ve truly read my mind."

Gu Tingxue corrected her, "It is the Emperor’s reward to Beauty Lian, not a gift from this humble servant."

"Though the Emperor may have casually ordered the reward, it is still Eunuch who selected it. The Emperor is too busy with state affairs to remember every item in the treasury. Only Noble Consort Gui can make the Emperor personally choose a gift or two."
