Normally, when bestowing rewards to other concubines, it was entirely up to the servants to decide.

Thus, one should not underestimate the palace eunuchs.

Sometimes, those in key positions held as much power as the noble consorts themselves.

"I don’t care. I’ll consider it a gift from Eunuch."

Xiangjun reached out to loop her arm through Gu Tingxue’s, but he took a step back, gracefully evading her.

If she had leaned in completely, she might have fallen.

Even so, she still staggered, barely managing to steady herself.

Tsk, so cold.

Xiangjun shot Gu Tingxue a resentful glance.

Gu Tingxue concealed the smile in his eyes and said formally, "This humble servant has finished his tea. I shall take my leave."

"Eunuch, must you leave so soon? What about the reward?"

"I dare not accept Beauty Lian’s reward. I bid you farewell."

Gu Tingxue turned and left without a trace of hesitation.

Sigh, how heartbreaking. She had wasted her lotus-pink sleeping gown on him. Meng Mei and Xi Yu had both said it made her look tender and fair.

This Gu Tingxue was truly blind.

...

Over the next few days, the Emperor visited Noble Consort Gui once more, then Consort Qin.

On the fifteenth, he went to the Empress’s palace.

After that, he did not return to the rear palace for seven days.

It wasn’t until Xiangjun’s plaque was hung again that the Emperor finally summoned her.

This time, the Emperor was more cautious, fearing he might hurt this delicate one again.

However, before he could fully enjoy himself, Xiangjun’s menses arrived the very next day, forcing her plaque to be removed once more.

The Emperor’s newly reignited interest was once again frustratingly interrupted.

To be honest, the Emperor was somewhat annoyed.

But he also knew it wasn’t Beauty Lian’s fault, so his enthusiasm for attending to his concubines waned. He still dined daily with Noble Consort Gui, though.

Noble Consort Gui also sensed a subtle change in the Emperor, though she couldn’t quite pinpoint what it was. She only felt that the Emperor seemed different somehow.

Yet he still treated her well, dining with her every day. It was just that every evening, he was always discussing state affairs with his ministers, claiming that the south was still in turmoil and he couldn’t find the time to see her.

...

Xiangjun’s menses were particularly painful this time.

Meng Mei went to fetch Physician Liu.

Physician Liu said that Xiangjun’s frequent consumption of contraceptive tea this month had taken a toll on her body.

"As long as Beauty replenishes her qi and blood in time, it will be fine. Shall I prescribe some medicine for you?"

"No need. Just record the pulse diagnosis as usual. But you must pretend we never had this conversation. Understood?"

"Why is that? Beauty, you must not continue drinking that tea. Prolonged use of contraceptive medicine will truly harm your body."

"Rest assured, I won’t need to drink it much longer."

Though Xiangjun was bold, she still cherished her own body and wouldn’t recklessly harm herself.

...

In the blink of an eye, it was the first day of the month.

Every first day of the month was the day when all the concubines paid their respects to the Empress.

Previously, since Xiangjun had not attended the Emperor, she had no right to enter and sit.

Now that she finally had her own position, though it was still at the very end.

Lady Li, because she was with child, was excused by the Empress from the greetings. Thus, Xiangjun did not see her today.

Noble Consort Gui sat in the innermost position on the left. Today, she seemed somewhat listless, likely having quarreled with the Emperor again.

While waiting for the Empress, the other concubines all examined Xiangjun.

Especially Consort Qin, whose eyes seemed to bore holes into Xiangjun.

"This Beauty Lian has such a good complexion. No wonder she has gained the Emperor’s favor. I am just a little curious—what does your title mean?"

"Lian" naturally meant "lovable."

In fact, when the Emperor had told Xiangjun the meaning, she had been at a loss for words.

So Xiangjun had asked the Emperor: "Is it the 'Lian' from 'Still cherishing the old love, I take pity on the one before me'?"

The Emperor, upon hearing this, found it even more interesting and happily agreed: "Yes, it is the 'Lian' from 'Still cherishing the old love, I take pity on the one before me'."

Xiangjun was about to speak when Consort Qin continued mockingly: "Or is it the 'Lian' of 'pitiable'? Or perhaps the 'Lian' of 'fawn and beg for pity'?"

chapters.title: Lian, the One Before Me
chapters.content:
Consort Qin couldn’t resist her cold mockery of Xiangjun.

De Fei and Sun Guipin, who usually didn’t get along with Consort Qin, also joined in with quiet laughter.

Xiangjun felt that some noble ladies were, at their core, no different from shrewish market women.

But she could also understand their malice toward her.

The women of the rear palace had grown accustomed to the Emperor’s favor toward Noble Consort Gui. No matter how the Emperor treated her, everyone had become numb to it.

But they were not used to the Emperor favoring Xiangjun, so they couldn’t resist mocking her.

It was fine. They would slowly get used to it.

Xiangjun pretended not to understand Consort Qin’s sarcasm and replied with a smile, "In response to Consort Qin, my title is not the 'Lian' of 'pitiable.' The Emperor said it is the 'Lian' from 'Still cherishing the old love, I take pity on the one before me'."

At these words, the faces of everyone in the room darkened.

Especially Noble Consort Gui, whose body visibly trembled.

As a talented woman, Noble Consort Gui naturally understood the meaning of this poem.

"Still cherishing the old love, I take pity on the one before me" meant that the old affection once held for someone in the past was now being bestowed upon the person currently by one’s side.

Noble Consort Gui must have felt the sting. Judging by her pale and trembling appearance, it was clear she was overthinking.

After saying this, Xiangjun happily picked up her teacup and took a sip.

The tea in the Empress’s palace was the best. She must drink more.

When Xiangjun set down her teacup, the Empress arrived.

After all the concubines had paid their respects to the Empress, Consort Qin, having just sat down, eagerly continued to find fault with Xiangjun. A few other concubines who rarely saw the Emperor also joined in the mockery.

Xiangjun truly didn’t understand why everyone hated her so much.

Was it the Emperor who made them live in such a way? Then they should blame the Emperor.

What was the point of attacking her? It wasn’t as if she could help them find men. And even if she did, they probably wouldn’t dare use them anyway.

In the end, the Empress couldn’t bear to watch any longer. She reprimanded Consort Qin and the others, then impatiently dismissed everyone, keeping only Xiangjun behind for a private conversation.

The Empress had deliberately kept Xiangjun because her palace maid, Fang Guigu, had reminded her: Why wait for new concubines to enter the palace? Wasn’t there already a useful woman without a noble background in the palace now?

Although everyone said Xiangjun was Noble Consort Gui’s person, it wasn’t as if Noble Consort Gui had ever shown her any particular favor.

The Empress had observed that when so many people attacked Xiangjun, Noble Consort Gui hadn’t even spoken up to stop them.

Where was the attitude of someone protecting their own?

Even if Xiangjun’s heart leaned toward Noble Consort Gui, the Empress believed that with a little provocation, the two could easily become enemies.

Thus, the Empress kept Xiangjun behind.

Xiangjun sat obediently, her bright eyes fixed on the Empress. Even knowing she wasn’t a simple person, it was hard to feel any annoyance toward her.

The Empress first expressed concern for Xiangjun, then praised her, saying she served the Emperor well. She even rewarded Xiangjun with a pair of jade earrings.

"Thank you, Empress. This subject is so happy. I have never seen jade with such fine quality before."

Fang Guigu beside her immediately said, "These were part of our Empress’s dowry. That she has given them to you today shows how much our Empress values Beauty Lian."

Xiangjun joyfully expressed her gratitude, immediately putting on the jade earrings. She happily showed them to the Empress, asking if they looked good.

No giver of gifts could hope for a more enthusiastic thanks.

"Enough, don’t just focus on being happy. You should still strive to conceive an imperial heir as soon as possible. When that happens, I will reward you with a pair of bracelets even finer than these."

Xiangjun beamed. "Yes, Empress, rest assured. I will serve the Emperor well and strive to conceive as soon as possible. Empress, you must believe me—I am truly trying my best. Every time after attending to the Emperor, Noble Consort Gui rewards me with a bowl of pregnancy-securing medicine the next day. Though it is very bitter, I always drink it all in one go."

Hearing this, the Empress’s expression shifted slightly as she exchanged a glance with Fang Guigu beside her.

...

After Xiangjun left happily with her reward, Fang Guigu, standing behind the Empress, finally spoke.

"Your Majesty, pregnancy-securing medicine is taken before attending to the Emperor. There is no reason to take it afterward. Medicine taken after... is for preventing conception."

"Do not spread this. Send someone to the Imperial Physician’s Office to investigate. We must find out what is really going on. Be careful not to let Noble Consort Gui’s people discover."

"Yes, this servant will take care of it immediately."

...

Xiangjun was in no hurry to attend to the Emperor again. After her menses ended, she delayed for another three days before hanging her green plaque.

On the day she hung the plaque, she was once again summoned by the Emperor to attend to him.

When it was known that the Emperor had summoned Xiangjun again, it nearly drove Consort Qin to madness.

It was one thing to lose to Noble Consort Gui, but was she now unable to compete even with a small beauty from a Jiangnan merchant family?

Consort Qin was so furious that she smashed countless treasures in her Nanxun Hall.

...

The next morning, before Xiangjun had even risen, Eunuch De Fu arrived with the pregnancy-securing medicine.

Xiangjun had someone ask Eunuch De Fu to wait a moment. Then, she leisurely had Xi Yu help her dress, and then slowly applied her own makeup in the style of Xi Shi, the beauty who suffered from a heart ailment.

After checking the time and seeing it was about right, she finally made her way to the main hall.

Eunuch De Fu had waited a long time and was growing anxious. "Greetings to Beauty Lian. This is the pregnancy-securing medicine bestowed by Noble Consort Gui. Please drink it quickly so I can return and report."

"Forgive me for keeping Eunuch waiting. I have not been feeling well lately, so I rose a bit late. Thank you for the trouble, Eunuch De Fu. Please have some tea."

"I won’t drink, Noble Consort Gui is still waiting for me to return and attend to her. Beauty Lian, please drink the medicine quickly."

Only then did Xiangjun sit down gracefully.

Meng Mei picked up the bowl of medicine for her. But just as Meng Mei brought the bowl to Xiangjun, before she could hand it to her,

a voice came from the doorway.

"Beauty Lian, don’t drink it. Please wait a moment."

Everyone turned to look at the door.

They saw Fang Guigu from the Empress’s palace, leading the Imperial Physician and several palace servants into Chengxiang Hall.

Upon seeing their formation, De Fu instantly understood the situation and immediately tried to knock the bowl of medicine from Meng Mei’s hands.

However, because Xiangjun had delayed for so long earlier, the medicine was no longer scalding. Meng Mei held the bowl extremely steady.

Thus, Meng Mei only staggered slightly, spilling a little over half the bowl, but the rest remained safely in the bowl.

Meng Mei even put on a panicked expression and cried out, "Oh no, Eunuch De Fu, be careful! This is the pregnancy-securing medicine bestowed by Noble Consort Gui. If it spills, it would be a waste of her kind intentions!"

"Restrain him!" Fang Guigu ordered, pointing at De Fu.

Several palace servants immediately moved to hold De Fu down.

De Fu struggled, shouting angrily, "How dare you! I am the chief eunuch of Noble Consort Gui’s palace. Who do you think you are, to lay hands on me?"

"Is that so? I was unaware that the mistress of the rear palace had become Noble Consort Gui."

Finally, the Empress, supported by her maids, arrived slowly.

chapters.title: The Most Difficult to Deal With is the Emperor's Love
chapters.content:
Xiangjun saw the Empress Dowager approaching and quickly stood up to pay her respects.

After the Empress Dowager sat down, she darkened her face and said, "Where is Physician Wang? Go and check that medicine immediately."

Mengmei was still steadily holding the medicine bowl and immediately handed it to Physician Wang.

Physician Wang stepped forward to inspect it. After a moment, he reported, "Your Majesty, this medicine is not a pregnancy-sustaining tonic but a contraceptive! Moreover, the potency of this medicine is fierce. If taken long-term, it can render a woman permanently infertile."

Xiangjun was so "shocked" that she collapsed onto the ground, her face pale and trembling. "How... how could this be!"

"Good, while I was ill for a few months, the harem has fallen into such chaos. Baohe, go and summon His Majesty and Noble Consort."

Baohe, the senior eunuch by the Empress's side, immediately went to fetch them.

Only then did the Empress turn to Mengmei and Xiyu, saying, "Hurry and help Consort Lian up. Don’t you fear she’ll catch a chill sitting on the ground?"

Xiangjun was then helped up by two palace maids and seated on a high-backed chair.

By the time the Emperor arrived, hand in hand with Noble Consort, the Empress had already investigated the matter thoroughly.

Physician Liu from the Imperial Medical Office had also been summoned, along with his prescriptions, the dispensed medicines, the medical records from the Imperial Medical Office, and his pulse diagnosis notes for Xiangjun.

The Empress had even ordered Physician Wang to take Xiangjun’s pulse again, confirming the symptoms of having consumed a contraceptive.

The Empress spoke clearly and concisely, quickly explaining the situation to the Emperor.

The Emperor’s face darkened.

But Xiangjun could see that the Emperor was not angry with Noble Consort but with the Empress.

This damn Emperor was just like that—even with irrefutable evidence, he would not believe that his beloved Noble Consort would do such a thing. Instead, he would blame the person who uncovered the evidence for having ulterior motives.

Xiangjun thought that the phrase "the jealousy of a noble consort is unmatched" from the book reviews she had read probably meant exactly this.

Seeing that the Emperor remained silent, the Empress fixed a fierce gaze on Xue Jiaojiao and said sternly, "Noble Consort Rong, His Majesty already has few heirs. You receive the most favor, yet you have been unable to bear children for many years. This alone is a crime against the nation. Now, you’ve even done something as despicable as giving contraceptives to a favored concubine out of jealousy. You have truly betrayed the trust His Majesty and I have placed in you."

"Your Majesty!" Noble Consort finally spoke her first words since entering the hall. "This concubine did indeed send pregnancy-sustaining medicine to Consort Lian, but I absolutely did not send her contraceptives."

"Who doesn’t know that pregnancy-sustaining medicine is taken before attending the Emperor? Only contraceptives are taken after," said Caiwei, the Empress’s trusted maid.

"I..."

Noble Consort truly had no idea about this.

Unlike the other concubines in the palace, she had enjoyed almost all of the Emperor’s favor in the past years. She had never needed to take pregnancy-sustaining medicine.

When Caiwei suggested bestowing pregnancy-sustaining medicine upon Consort Lian to demonstrate her generosity and prevent the harem from speculating that she was jealous or monopolizing the Emperor, she agreed.

But she had never actually looked into the details.

The Emperor saw that the Empress was relentlessly pressing Noble Consort, who had nothing to say in her defense. He turned to Xiangjun, "You, tell me, what exactly happened? Why did the pregnancy-sustaining medicine the Noble Consort sent you turn into a contraceptive?"

Xiangjun nearly died of anger at this damn Emperor.

What did he mean by "turned into a contraceptive"? Was he trying to shift the blame onto her?

Seeing the Emperor’s impatient expression, Xiangjun quickly knelt down, her voice trembling with tears as she said, "Your Majesty, this concubine also doesn’t know why the pregnancy-sustaining medicine became a contraceptive! Every time after I attended to Your Majesty, the next day, Eunuch Defu would personally deliver a bowl of pregnancy-sustaining medicine. He always brought it himself, never through others, and he would watch me drink it every time. I knew this medicine was a kind gesture from Noble Consort and was deeply grateful. Every time Eunuch Defu brought it, I would drink it immediately!"

Seeing Xiangjun’s sincere and emotional state, the Emperor believed her somewhat.

She came from a humble background and had not been in the palace for long. She didn’t have the power to harm Noble Consort.

"Where is the physician?"

Physicians Wang and Liu immediately stepped forward to answer.

"Who prepared this pregnancy-sustaining medicine?"

Physician Liu stepped forward and replied, "Your Majesty, this prescription was prepared by me, but I prepared a contraceptive, not a pregnancy-sustaining medicine. Every time, it was Eunuch Defu who came to collect it. I did not know for whom this medicine was intended."

Beside him, Physician Wang said, "Physician Liu, your words are incorrect. Looking at the pulse records, you diagnosed Consort Lian just a few days ago. The records clearly show that your medical skills are well-known in the Imperial Medical Office. How could you fail to notice that Consort Lian had traces of having consumed contraceptives?"

Physician Wang, of course, would not let Physician Liu off the hook.

There was only one position for Deputy Director of the Imperial Medical Office. He was the Empress’s man, while Physician Liu was Noble Consort’s. They were destined to compete.

Upon hearing this, Xiyu immediately jumped in and cursed Physician Liu, "No wonder our mistress had such painful menstruation last month. It turns out it was because she drank the contraceptive! Physician Liu, why didn’t you tell our Consort when you noticed? Our Consort trusted you because you are Noble Consort’s physician. Who would have thought you would harm our mistress!"

Physician Liu was terrified and immediately knelt down, kowtowing to the Emperor, "Your Majesty, I only realized after diagnosing Consort Lian that the contraceptive I prepared was the one she had consumed. Although excessive consumption can harm fertility, a few doses are not a problem. As for the affairs of the mistresses, we subordinates dare not ask too much. I thought that Consort Lian had asked Noble Consort for the medicine herself, so I did not speak up."

Hearing Physician Liu say this, the Empress immediately darkened her expression, "Nonsense! Which palace concubine would not want to become pregnant?"

Caiwei, who had been distrustful of Physician Liu, a commoner, from Noble Consort’s palace, now looked at him with a bit more appreciation after seeing him single-handedly turn the situation around.

Caiwei quickly followed Physician Liu’s words, saying, "Yes, it’s possible that Consort Lian, being newly favored, did not want to become pregnant so soon and wanted to enjoy His Majesty’s favor for a longer time."

Xiangjun looked at Physician Liu with despair and anger, "You... you are slandering me!"

Then, Xiangjun knelt and crawled to the Emperor, clutching his robe as she wept, "Your Majesty, it is against palace rules for a concubine to secretly drink contraceptives. How would I dare to do such a thing?"

Tears poured down Xiangjun’s face as she sobbed bitterly, her heartbreak evident.

But the damn Emperor ignored it.

When Xiangjun then crawled to Noble Consort and, clutching her robe, said sorrowfully, "Noble Consort, you know me. I truly never asked you for contraceptives."

Xiangjun’s mouth pleaded with Noble Consort to tell the truth, but in her heart, she prayed that Noble Consort would lie.

Anyone with eyes could see what was going on.

The claim that she had asked Noble Consort for contraceptives was completely baseless.

Not to mention that Noble Consort had already admitted that she had bestowed pregnancy-sustaining medicine upon Xiangjun after listening to the palace servants. Even the flimsy excuse of "drinking contraceptives to compete for favor" made no sense.

Everyone knew that concubines competed for favor to bear royal sons!

However, given the Emperor’s deep affection for Noble Consort, if she said that Xiangjun had asked her for contraceptives, the Emperor would make Xiangjun take the blame.

When Xiangjun had pleaded with the Emperor earlier, and he had remained silent, that was exactly what he had meant.

So, for today’s matter, the best outcome for Xiangjun was to take the blame for Noble Consort.

She not only wanted to gain the Emperor’s sympathy but also wanted to tarnish Noble Consort’s pure and flawless image in the Emperor’s heart, even if just a little.

Once there was a blemish, no matter how small, it would be easier to cast further aspersions in the future.

Because once trust had the slightest crack, it could easily crumble afterward.

Xiangjun had always known that harming Noble Consort was useless.

Noble Consort was not useful at all.

The most difficult to deal with was the Emperor’s love for her.

---

chapters.title: Noble Consort is Punished
chapters.content:
Seeing Noble Consort biting her lip, her face pale, her body trembling, yet not saying a word, Xiangjun immediately put on a look of despair.

She slowly closed her eyes, a line of clear tears falling, her heart like dead ash, resembling a withered flower drifting in the wind.

The Emperor, seeing Xiangjun in this state, felt a pang of unwillingness to be harsh.

He was not stupid. Things had come to this point—how could he not see that Xiangjun was an innocent victim?

But he had no choice. He had to protect Jiaojiao.

The Empress had always hated Noble Consort. If she caught Noble Consort harming another concubine, she would definitely make a big deal out of it.

The Empress also saw that the Emperor was going to protect that wretched woman again.

"Noble Consort Rong, tell me, was this medicine bestowed by you, or did Consort Lian ask you for it?" the Empress demanded sternly.

Noble Consort felt as if she was being pierced by the Empress’s sharp gaze.

Beside her, Caiwei gently tugged at her mistress’s sleeve.

She must not soften her heart now.

Noble Consort trembled, her face pale, as if she had made up her mind. She knelt on the ground.

"Your Majesty... Consort Lian did not ask this concubine for contraceptives. It is true that this concubine bestowed pregnancy-sustaining medicine upon Consort Lian, but this concubine truly does not know why it turned into a contraceptive. It was this concubine’s oversight. This concubine is guilty."

"Your Highness!"

Caiwei was desperate, but when she saw Noble Consort looking at her with a face full of disappointment, she was so frightened that she swallowed all the words she had been about to say.

The Empress looked at Noble Consort with a very complicated expression.

The physician had already found a breakthrough, yet she still refused to falsely accuse someone.

She truly was useless.

If it weren’t for the Emperor’s unconditional favor, Noble Consort would have died a hundred times over with her temperament.

Xiangjun was shocked.

She had underestimated Noble Consort’s integrity.

She didn’t know if Noble Consort had chosen to tell the truth out of kindness or because she refused to be tainted by falsehood.

The Emperor felt a mix of emotions. On one hand, he was troubled that Noble Consort had not taken the opportunity he had given her to shift the blame. On the other hand, he was happy that his Noble Consort was still so sincere and pure.

The Emperor sighed and asked again, his tone gentle, "Noble Consort, are you sure this medicine was not requested by Consort Lian?"

This time, Noble Consort’s face showed not the slightest hesitation as she said, "No, Consort Lian is an innocent victim."

Xiangjun looked at the Emperor.

She saw that upon hearing Noble Consort’s answer, the Emperor not only showed no disappointment but also revealed a relieved expression.

The Empress finally showed a victorious smile.

Caiwei and Eunuch Defu, however, looked ashen.

Xiangjun let out a heavy sigh in her heart.

The Empress still did not understand the Emperor. No wonder she ended up losing everything, allowing Xue Jiaojiao to seize the throne of Empress.

The matter had developed to this point, and Defu knew he could not be saved.

He seemed to have finally made up his mind. He crawled on his hands and knees to the Emperor and Noble Consort, kowtowing so hard that his forehead bled.

"Your Majesty, Noble Consort, this matter was all this slave’s doing! Noble Consort deeply loves Your Majesty, and Your Majesty often goes to be with Consort Lian. This slave could not bear to see Her Highness sad, so I made a mistake in judgment. I beg Your Majesty for mercy, I beg Noble Consort for mercy!"

The Empress could not let Noble Consort off so easily. She coldly laughed, "Noble Consort Rong, His Majesty has only favored Consort Lian a few times, and you are already heartbroken? In this entire palace, who can compare to you in terms of His Majesty’s favor? Not only are you ungrateful, but you are also jealous of the younger concubines! Such jealousy is unbecoming of a Noble Consort. Your Majesty, can you continue to indulge Noble Consort’s behavior?"

The Emperor was left speechless by the Empress’s question, not knowing how to defend Noble Consort.

After all, the Empress had not relied on the Emperor to become Empress.

The Empress’s maiden name was Yang.

The Yang family was a founding meritorious official, and this surname represented the court’s civil official faction.

Currently, the most powerful force in the imperial court was Left Chancellor Yang Jun and the clean-stream literati faction behind him.

The only one who could slightly counter Yang was the Right Chancellor, Song Feijing, whom the Emperor had later promoted, along with the Jiangnan faction behind Song Feijing.

But even that was only enough to counter a few moves.

Thus, the Emperor both respected and feared this Empress Yang.

Now that Empress Yang had caught Noble Consort’s mistake, he could not avoid punishing her.

Xiangjun saw the Emperor’s dilemma and knew that the best outcome she had hoped for was now out of reach.

But she still had to secure the second-best outcome for herself.

Xiangjun immediately said, "Your Majesty, Your Majesty the Empress, this concubine has not truly been harmed. The physician said that this medicine is not a problem if taken only a few times, right? Since I am unharmed, and Noble Consort truly did not know, at most it was the subordinates acting on their own. I beg Your Majesty and Your Majesty the Empress not to punish Noble Consort."

The Emperor looked at Xiangjun with satisfaction. She was indeed clever. It seemed her usual deference to Noble Consort was not feigned.

With the victim herself pleading for leniency, the Empress could not insist on severe punishment. She said resentfully, "Your Majesty, although Consort Lian is kind-hearted, this matter must have a resolution. Otherwise, the other concubines in the harem will feel uneasy. By doing this, isn’t Noble Consort telling everyone in the palace that no one can compete with her for favor? Otherwise, even if they are rendered infertile, they deserve it."

The Emperor thought for a moment, then said with a stern face, "Noble Consort has indeed failed to properly manage her servants. She is to be confined to Ganlu Palace for one month and have her stipend halved for half a year. As for Defu, he is to receive fifty strokes of the rod. After that, if he is still alive, he need not return to Noble Consort’s palace. Throw him into the laundry bureau."

The Emperor’s word was law, and the matter had to end here. Although the Empress felt the punishment was too lenient, she did not say anything more.

Seeing the Empress’s unhappy expression, the Emperor comforted her, "The Empress has worked hard managing the harem for me. I will accompany you back to Weiyang Palace and taste the dishes from your private kitchen."

The Emperor’s willingness to go to the Empress’s palace was also a way to give her face. The Empress naturally could not continue to nag and simply smiled gently in agreement.

The Emperor and Empress left hand in hand.

After the Emperor and Empress had left, Defu was dragged away to receive his punishment.

Two palace servants approached Noble Consort and said, "Your Highness, you should return to Ganlu Palace for confinement."

Xiangjun reached out to support the disoriented Noble Consort.

Noble Consort looked at Xiangjun with a complex expression and said, "Thank you for speaking up for me today. This matter was the fault of my servants. I have wronged you."

"Your Highness, please do not say that. You have always been kind to me. So many things in my palace were bestowed by you. Xiangjun will not blame you for this."

Noble Consort nodded and left with Caiwei, not even sparing a glance at Defu.

Everyone else also withdrew.

Now, the entire Chengxiang Hall was left with only Xiangjun’s palace servants and those who stayed to administer Defu’s punishment.

Xiangjun took Mengmei and Xiyu to the front courtyard.

Mengmei handed a large bag of silver to the eunuch in charge of the punishment, then pointed to a small path in the courtyard and said, "Could you let our palace’s Xiaoluzi come and administer the punishment?"

chapters.title: The Confidence of a Yang Family Daughter
chapters.content:
The eunuch accepted the money without hesitation.

After all, this wasn’t a good task—hitting someone with a board was quite exhausting.

Xiao Luzi froze.

What did this have to do with him?

During this time, although Xiao Luzi couldn’t serve by Lady Lian’s side and could only do outdoor chores, he hadn’t suffered at all. In fact, his life might be more comfortable than that of many senior eunuchs in the palace.

After all, Lady Lian was generous with money.

Today, he had only wanted to watch the excitement, but unexpectedly, Lady Lian had ordered him to carry out the punishment.

Xiao Luzi quickly accepted the task and stepped forward.

Picking up the board, Xiao Luzi’s mind raced.

Did the mistress want De Fu dead or not?

Xiao Luzi quickly figured it out.

Just now, inside the room, the mistress had spoken up for Noble Consort Rong. She probably still wanted to maintain a good relationship with Noble Consort Rong.

Therefore, De Fu must not die; otherwise, it would be a slap in Noble Consort Rong’s face.

But it was also De Fu who had delivered the contraceptive soup to the mistress, causing her such pain during her monthly cycle. The mistress needed to vent her anger.

So after fifty strikes, De Fu would be alive but would suffer from chronic pain for the rest of his life.

After finishing the task, Xiao Luzi took the initiative to request an audience with Lady Lian.

When he entered the room, Xiang Jun was at the desk writing.

Xiao Luzi glanced at it and was somewhat surprised. He hadn’t expected Lady Lian’s handwriting to be so good.

Xiang Jun put down her brush, and Xiao Luzi, with perfect timing, stepped forward to support her to the noble consort’s couch. Then, bending over, he presented a cup of tea.

Xiang Jun took the tea and asked, “Have you thought it through?”

Xiao Luzi grinned and said, “This servant has thought it through. I am willing to be a good servant to the mistress alone. From now on, I will serve the mistress with my life, without hesitation.”

Xiao Luzi had been contemplating this for a while.

Eunuch Gu had sent him to Chengxiang Hall to monitor Lady Lian, but without specific instructions—just to observe carefully.

If he couldn’t serve her closely, he wouldn’t be able to observe much and would be of no use.

Like today’s incident—he hadn’t even known what was happening. Eunuch Gu probably wouldn’t value him anymore. He might as well devote himself wholeheartedly to serving Lady Lian.

Moreover, he had observed that Lady Lian was generous with money, had a good temper, was ambitious, and was intelligent.

A servant should follow such a capable mistress.

Otherwise, even if the mistress was favored, the servant wouldn’t last long in the palace.

Wasn’t De Fu the best example of that?

Xiang Jun let out a cold humph and said leisurely, “There’s no need to talk about dying for me. My servants don’t need to die.”

Xiao Luzi, upon hearing this, immediately knelt on the ground, smiling as he kowtowed. “The mistress is right. The mistress will surely rise swiftly and reach the heavens in one step!”

Xiang Jun glanced at him. “Don’t use idioms if you don’t know how to.”

Meng Mei and Xi Yu both giggled behind him.

Xiao Luzi, still kneeling, asked with a smile, “Does the mistress blame me for taking so long to decide?”

Xiang Jun chuckled softly. “If you had decided immediately, I wouldn’t have dared to trust you. For a servant, choosing a good mistress is the most important decision in life. If you don’t observe carefully and weigh your options, but rush into a choice, I wouldn’t want you.”

Xiang Jun had great plans for the future, and the people around her must be reliable.

Xiao Luzi felt that he had made the right choice. He grinned and kowtowed again. “Thank you, mistress, for your recognition!”

“Enough, don’t try to be cute.” Xiang Jun’s voice turned serious. “How is De Fu now? Is he dead?”

“Mistress, rest assured, he’s not dead. But De Fu will probably suffer from chronic back pain for the rest of his life. Back pain may seem minor, but when it flares up, it can be agonizing.”

Xiang Jun raised her eyebrows. This Xiao Luzi was quite good at guessing her intentions.

Indeed, she didn’t want De Fu dead—after all, he might still be useful in the future. But she did want him to suffer.

She still remembered the cold mockery De Fu had subjected her to when he took away her first child:

*“It is already your fortune that the prince was born to Concubine Xu. Someone of your lowly status is unworthy of raising a prince. The fact that the noble consort did not order your death is already an act of grace toward you.”*

Every time she tried to see her child afterward, De Fu would mock her.

Once, that dog of a slave had even struck her with a dust whisk.

Now, Xiang Jun had finally vented a little of her anger.

“It depends on whether Noble Consort Rong will go to the laundry bureau to pull strings for him.” Xiang Jun said with a hint of melancholy.

Xiao Luzi understood immediately and said, “This servant understands. I will keep a close watch on De Fu for Lady Lian.”

Xiang Jun smiled in satisfaction. “You’ve done well. Here’s your reward.”

---

Ganlu Palace.

Cai Wei knelt on the ground, crying uncontrollably.

Noble Consort Rong was so angry she almost fainted.

“How dare you act on your own! Do you know that what you did is no different from what I would do? It is because I have been too kind to you that you have the audacity to harm another consort! Since that is the case, I cannot allow you to continue serving me. Leave.”

Cai Wei crawled and rolled her way to Noble Consort Rong, clinging to her.

“Noble Consort, I have been by your side since I was a child. I know I was wrong, but I only wanted to make you happy. I hate everyone who competes with you for His Majesty’s affection. I... I only wish for you and His Majesty to be as happy as you were before, instead of you always crying alone...”

Hearing this, Noble Consort Rong’s heart softened.

“Forget it. You did it for my sake, but Cai Wei, you must promise me never to do such a thing again.”

Cai Wei nodded.

Noble Consort Rong sighed. “Today’s matter, we have wronged Lady Lian.”

---

Yongchang Palace.

After having lunch with the empress, the emperor left without saying he would return in the evening.

Once the emperor was gone, Aunt Fang said, “His Majesty actually let Noble Consort Rong off so lightly. That Lady Lian is truly ungrateful. She wasted all of Your Majesty’s planning, was harmed, and yet she still sides with Noble Consort Rong.”

The empress sat in front of the vanity table, eyes closed, as Aunt Fang removed her hairpins for her.

“Lady Lian is clever. Mo Fang, you misjudged her this time.”

Aunt Fang was confused. “Your Majesty, what do you mean?”

“That day, she intentionally mentioned the pregnancy-preserving medicine to me so that I would notice something was wrong. But she knew that the emperor favors Noble Consort Rong, so the matter would not be pursued. Therefore, she took the opportunity to curry favor, ensuring His Majesty would remember her kindness. She is not siding with Noble Consort Rong. Now, I have avenged her, Noble Consort Rong is confined, and she no longer has to drink the contraceptive soup. Tell me, who is the biggest winner in this matter?”

“Then Your Majesty has been used by her.”

“It doesn’t matter. I was a willing participant. If it can make Noble Consort Rong suffer, what does it matter if I lose a little?”

“This servant is just afraid that His Majesty will be angry with Your Majesty. Although he dined with you, he didn’t say he would come to see you tonight...”

“What if His Majesty is angry with me? I am a Yang family daughter, the empress, and the mother of a prince. My position is stable and unshakable. Even if the emperor is angry with me, doesn’t he still have to dine with me? Doesn’t he still have to stay in Yongchang Palace on the first and fifteenth of every month? What do I have to fear?”

Seeing the empress like this, Aunt Fang felt a pang of sadness.

In her youth, hadn’t the empress also hoped for mutual affection with her husband, living in harmony?

But over these ten-plus years, the empress had been hurt by the emperor time and time again.

After the second prince was born, the empress seemed to give up on the emperor entirely, devoting herself solely to raising the second prince.

“Your Majesty, this servant feels heartbroken for you. You used to...”

“Don’t bring up the past.” The empress sat in front of the mirror, looking at the faint lines at the corners of her eyes, her expression darkening. “You only need to know that I am the empress, and in the future, I will be the empress dowager. That is enough.”

---

chapters.title: Siding with the Winner
chapters.content:
The news of Noble Consort Rong’s confinement quickly spread throughout the palace.

Over the next few days, all sorts of rumors circulated.

That evening, Xiang Jun lay on the noble consort’s couch while Xiao Luzi massaged her legs, recounting the various opinions of the consorts in other palaces.

Xi Yu listened with great interest.

“Hey, how do you get your information so quickly?” Xiang Jun asked curiously.

“I used to work in the imperial kitchen delivering meals, so I know people from all the palaces.”

“The imperial kitchen is a good post. How did you end up here?”

Xiao Luzi smiled sheepishly. “I offended someone and was sent back to the Shanggong Bureau for reassignment.”

“Then how did Eunuch Gu know about you?”

“I’m not sure about that, but...” Xiao Luzi lowered his voice. “There’s nothing in this palace that Eunuch Gu doesn’t know.”

Xiang Jun couldn’t help but laugh. “Why are you whispering? Do you think he can hear you?”

“Eunuch Gu!”

“What about Eunuch Gu?”

Xiao Luzi pointed at the door. “Mistress, Eunuch Gu is here.”

Xiang Jun turned her head and saw Gu Tingxue walking in, holding a tray with one hand.

Gu Tingxue was wearing a red python robe today, with a black velvet smoke-stand hat. He stood straight under the intricately carved wooden screen, looking like a painting.

“Greetings to Lady Lian.”

“What wind brings Eunuch Gu here? You could have had someone announce your arrival,” Xiang Jun said, feeling inexplicably guilty.

“In the future, when Lady Lian speaks ill of others, it’s better to have someone guarding the door.”

Meng Mei had gone to visit her brother tonight and hadn’t returned yet, so there was no one outside to announce visitors.

But she hadn’t said anything bad, had she?

Gu Tingxue’s visit at this hour was unusual, and Xiang Jun felt uneasy. She waved her hand, and Xi Yu and Xiao Luzi quickly withdrew.

“I have come on His Majesty’s orders to deliver something to Lady Lian.”

Gu Tingxue didn’t stand on ceremony. He placed the tray on the octagonal table, then sat down at the side of the Kang table as if he were the master of the place, pouring himself a cup of water.

Seeing Gu Tingxue’s demeanor, Xiang Jun was actually quite angry.

Even if Gu Tingxue looked down on all the noble consorts in the palace, he wouldn’t be this rude if he went to another lady’s palace.

Was it because he knew Xiang Jun had no one to rely on in the palace that he deliberately treated her this way?

It didn’t matter. Xiang Jun could endure it. She had even served her enemy; serving a eunuch was nothing.

Soon, she would make him her own servant!

Xiang Jun endured her anger and walked to Gu Tingxue’s side, speaking softly as if she were still the same thin horse from Yangzhou. “Eunuch Gu, what has His Majesty sent me?”

Gu Tingxue’s lips curled slightly, as if smiling, but there was no warmth in it.

For some reason, Xiang Jun felt a chill run down her spine.

She watched as Gu Tingxue opened the lid of the medicine pot and poured the contents into a bowl.

A strong medicinal smell filled the air.

“This is medicine? I... I’m not sick.”

Gu Tingxue’s face still wore that emotionless smile, his tone flat. “This is the sterility medicine His Majesty has bestowed upon Lady Lian.”

Xiang Jun’s legs went weak, and she nearly fell.

Her face turned pale, and she staggered back a few steps, steadying herself against the octagonal table.

“Why would His Majesty bestow this upon me?”

“What does Lady Lian think?”

Xiang Jun’s mind raced, and she quickly understood.

It must be for Noble Consort Rong.

The emperor probably didn’t believe De Bao. The emperor never considered servants as people, so he wouldn’t believe De Bao had acted on his own.

Even though Noble Consort Rong hadn’t confessed, the emperor still believed she had ordered De Bao to do it.

Noble Consort Rong had grown jealous of Xiang Jun.

The emperor, in his own mind, was a romantic hero. He lusted after Xiang Jun’s body but felt guilty toward his true love, Noble Consort Rong. Thinking that Noble Consort Rong was jealous of Xiang Jun, he wanted to express his love in this way.

If Noble Consort Rong didn’t want Xiang Jun to have children, then Xiang Jun would never have children. If Noble Consort Rong still doubted the emperor’s love after that, the emperor would truly be heartbroken.

At this thought, Xiang Jun wanted to curse.

Xiang Jun sneered. “Does His Majesty consider me a toy to amuse Noble Consort Rong?”

“Who knows what His Majesty is thinking?”

Gu Tingxue stood up, holding the bowl of medicine, and took a few steps closer to Xiang Jun, backing her up against the carved wooden screen.

Xiang Jun had nowhere left to retreat. She shook her head, refusing to drink.

Wait, the emperor’s reaction didn’t make sense.

“The matter with Noble Consort Rong’s punishment has been over for several days. Why has His Majesty only now thought to send me medicine?”

“As I said, who knows what His Majesty is thinking? The palace gates will soon be locked, and I still have to leave to attend to His Majesty’s business. Lady Lian should drink the medicine while it’s hot.”

Xiang Jun refused to drink it.

She knelt down with a thud, clutching Gu Tingxue’s python robe, her eyes filled with tears as she begged, “Eunuch, please help me. I truly cannot drink this.”

Gu Tingxue reached out and pinched Xiang Jun’s chin, lifting her face gently.

“Isn’t Lady Lian quite bold? When serving His Majesty, you dared to look at me openly. Why are you so timid now? It’s just a bowl of medicine. It won’t kill you.”

“This is sterility medicine! If I drink it, what kind of future will I have in this palace?”

“Doesn’t Noble Consort Rong also have no children? Yet her position is stable. In this palace, as long as you have the emperor’s favor, does it matter whether you have children or not?”

“Can I compare myself to Noble Consort Rong?”

Gu Tingxue’s hand lightly slid across Xiang Jun’s face. “Lady Lian has a face like an immortal, and you are clever and bold. Given time, it won’t be difficult to capture His Majesty’s heart.”

“I want His Majesty’s heart for what?” Xiang Jun blurted out.

What was so great about the emperor’s heart? The thought made her sick.

“Oh? I’m truly curious. If you don’t want His Majesty’s heart, what does Lady Lian want?”

“I think Eunuch Gu already knows what I want. What I want has always been the same as what you want.”

Xiang Jun dropped the act. Although she was still kneeling, her eyes no longer held the pitiful look from before.

“Eunuch Gu must have a way to help me, right?”

Gu Tingxue finally smiled in satisfaction. He grabbed Xiang Jun’s arm and pulled her up from the ground.

Xiang Jun almost collided with Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue lowered his head, their faces extremely close, even able to feel each other’s breath.

“Of course I have a way to help Lady Lian. But I always have conditions when I help someone.”

“What conditions?”

Gu Tingxue’s voice was low and melodious. “I only help those who can win in the end.”

chapters.title: The Wager
chapters.content:
Xiangjun’s mind raced with countless thoughts. She asked, "Do you think Noble Consort will win in the end, Your Excellency?"

"Noble Consort has the Emperor’s favor and the support of the imperial court. To win in the end, all she lacks is a child. And isn’t she about to have one soon?"

Xiangjun knew that the child Gu Tingxue referred to was the one in Lady Li’s womb.

"And as for you..." Gu Tingxue sized Xiangjun up.

Xiangjun smiled faintly. "I know. I am but a lowly woman from Yangzhou, with no influence in either the court or the harem. The Emperor’s interest in me is fleeting, treating me as a mere plaything. No one would ever bet on me."

"Since you understand this, why should I help you?"

"Because having nothing is both my weakness and my advantage. If in the future, Noble Consort’s child becomes Emperor, Your Excellency will remain nothing more than a powerful eunuch. The Grand General Wang and Right Chancellor Yun will still stand above you. Are you truly content to remain beneath others forever? I am different. I have only you, and can only rely on you alone. Moreover..."

"Moreover what?"

"Unlike Noble Consort, I do not truly love the Emperor. I have no feelings for him, nor do I desire his heart. Choosing me... Your Excellency need not wait for the Emperor to die."

Xiangjun’s words were nothing short of treasonous.

Yet, instead of reprimanding her, Gu Tingxue’s lips curled into an almost imperceptible smile.

"You are indeed bold, but boldness alone is not enough in this palace."

"I will show Your Excellency my strength."

"How do you plan to demonstrate it?"

"Within a year, I will ascend to the rank of Concubine."

Gu Tingxue finally released his grip on Xiangjun’s arm, stepping back to put distance between them. Then, with a slight flick of his hand, he knocked over the bowl of sterility-inducing medicine he held.

The dark liquid spilled, staining the carpet as the porcelain shattered.

Xiangjun finally exhaled in relief.

"Half a year," Gu Tingxue said, his dark eyes fixed on Xiangjun. "If you can climb to the rank of Concubine within half a year, then from now on, I will be your greatest backer in both the court and the harem."

Xiangjun felt her heart pounding so hard it might burst from her chest.

"Very well, half a year it is. Only..."

"Only what?"

Xiangjun took two steps forward, her soft hands gently resting on Gu Tingxue’s chest, her eyes seductive. "It’s just that Xiangjun is weak and alone. I hope that during these six months, if there are things that are inconvenient for me to do, Your Excellency might help me."

Gu Tingxue pondered for a moment. "Fine. But I will only help you with three matters. And these three things will not include speaking to the Emperor on your behalf, nor will they include helping you rise in rank."

"That is only natural. With Your Excellency’s promise, Xiangjun has nothing to worry about. Only..." Xiangjun glanced at the shattered bowl on the floor. "I did not drink the sterility medicine. How will you explain this to the Emperor?"

Gu Tingxue took her hands from his body and gently pushed them away.

"That is my concern. You need not worry about it. It’s late. You should rest early, Lady Lian."

Gu Tingxue turned and left.

Only after he had gone did Xiangjun slowly sit down on the embroidered stool, her gaze fixed on the broken porcelain scattered across the floor, her expression grave.

Half a year? To rise from Beauty to Concubine?

That was five ranks in six months!

Why didn’t Gu Tingxue just ask her to become Empress in half a year?

...

Late at night, in the Taiji Hall, Gu Tingxue was grinding ink for the Emperor.

The Emperor read the urgent memorials sent from the south, his brows furrowed. After scribbling a few words, he threw down his brush.

"Money, money, money! All they do is ask me for money! They ask for money to fight wars, and after the wars, they still ask for money. Where am I supposed to get so much silver from? And those old fools in the court do nothing but oppose me. Every time I want to do something, all they say is there’s no money. I just don’t understand—where has all the silver gone?"

"Your Majesty, please calm down," Gu Tingxue said in a low voice. "The silver confiscated from the salt merchants earlier this year has already been transported. In a few days, it will be delivered to Your Majesty’s private treasury."

The Emperor raised an eyebrow. "Weren’t their assets already used as military pay?"

"Only the ready cash was used for military pay. Those people also had vast amounts of property—houses, land, pawnshops, stores, gold, silver, jewelry, antiques, calligraphy, and paintings... It took me nearly half a year to properly inventory everything. Apart from some treasures and artworks, the rest have all been converted into silver. There is a total of fifty million taels."

Upon hearing this, Emperor Yanqing let out a cold snort.

"The court’s annual income is only a little over forty million taels, yet a few salt merchants from Jiangnan can raise fifty million taels just by selling their assets. They are richer than I am!"

The Emperor was furious just thinking about those merchants. But when he glanced at Gu Tingxue standing beside him, his mood improved greatly.

Tingxue was still the one who understood him best. No wonder he was the trusted confidant the Emperor had cultivated since childhood. He had handled this matter brilliantly.

Now that there was money in the private treasury, he could do whatever he wanted without having to listen to the nonsense of those old fools.

"You’ve done well. You’ve been busy these days—go rest for a few days before returning to duty." After a moment’s thought, the Emperor asked, "Did you deliver the medicine to Lady Lian?"

"In reply to Your Majesty, it was too late yesterday. I had intended to deliver it today, but I was delayed by some matters. So, I was thinking of handling it tonight."

"What matters delayed you?"

"The Shence Army captured two spies sent by Nanyue. They are connected to the love bug that afflicted Your Majesty earlier."

"Did they reveal anything?"

"It seems they may have some connection to Consort Qin. They are still being interrogated. Once we have results, I will report back to Your Majesty."

The Emperor’s expression remained unchanged, but a deep, sinister glint flickered in his eyes.

"Investigate. I want irrefutable evidence. Go take care of this now. As for Lady Lian’s matter, have someone else handle it."

"Yes." Gu Tingxue hesitated before adding, "Lady Lian’s matter is trivial, but I fear that if someone else handles it carelessly and word gets out, it may lead to criticism of Noble Consort. Her Highness would be heartbroken."

The Emperor’s expression softened. "Yes, Noble Consort is the kindest. If she is heartbroken, she will only blame herself."

"Speaking of which, Lady Lian initially entered the palace for Noble Consort’s sake. Her Highness has always treated Lady Lian well."

The Emperor then remembered that Lady Lian had entered the palace to bear a son for Noble Consort.

"In truth, Your Majesty’s favor toward Lady Lian is also for the sake of giving Noble Consort a son. How could Noble Consort bear to harm Lady Lian? Your Majesty, forgive my boldness, but this time, Noble Consort must be wronged. Perhaps someone in the harem is trying to harm her."

The Emperor suddenly realized something.

He had favored Xiangjun to give his beloved Noble Consort a son.

If Lady Lian could no longer bear children, what reason would he have to continue favoring her?

"Lady Li’s child... we don’t even know if it’s a boy or a girl yet," Gu Tingxue added.

"Forget it. Put Lady Lian’s matter aside for now. She and Noble Consort are close, and I don’t want to upset Noble Consort. You go handle the Nanyue spies."

"Yes. I take my leave."

---

chapters.title: Noble Consort’s Pregnancy
chapters.content:
Xiangjun had stayed in Chengxiang Palace for several days. When no one brought her any more medicinal soups, she knew that Gu Tingxue must have persuaded the Emperor to drop the matter.

If that was the case, Xiangjun would now begin her plans to ascend to the rank of Concubine.

Within half a year, she had to reach the rank of Concubine.

That meant rising from her current rank of Beauty (7th rank) to Concubine (4th rank).

Five ranks in total.

Five ranks! Some palace concubines spent their entire lives without ascending even one rank, yet she had to do it in half a year!

But Xiangjun knew complaining was useless.

She had to act immediately.

In the entire harem, only three people could promote her rank.

The first was the Emperor, the second was the Empress Dowager—both could directly elevate her status.

The third was the Empress. The Empress could recommend her to the Emperor, and as long as it wasn’t too unreasonable, the Emperor would usually grant the Empress face.

Xiangjun decided to pursue all three paths simultaneously. But first, she couldn’t let everyone’s attention remain fixed on her.

Lately, because of her role in Noble Consort’s confinement, the entire harem had been buzzing about her.

Many were watching Xiangjun closely, suspecting she had some bewitching power over the Emperor. Otherwise, how could she have made the Emperor punish his beloved Noble Consort?

To accomplish great things, one must stay low-key and avoid provoking public anger.

In her past life, she had failed to understand this, which was why she had experienced so many rises and falls.

Xiangjun summoned Meng Mei. "How has your brother been faring in Ganlu Palace?"

"My brother has gained Noble Consort’s trust recently. Thanks to your previous scheme, Aunt Caiwei now treats my brother as one of her own. These days, Noble Consort only summons my brother to check her pulse."

Xiangjun nodded. "Then tell him the time is almost right."

...

Ganlu Palace.

Physician Liu had been summoned to check the pulse of the confined Noble Consort.

Seeing Noble Consort’s anxious expression, Physician Liu said, "Your Highness, there is something this humble servant has long wished to report, but I did not know... whether I should."

"Is there something wrong with my body?"

"Your Highness is in perfect health."

"If that is the case, Physician Liu, just speak freely."

Physician Liu knelt and reported, "In reply to Your Highness, this humble servant knows a secret method to aid conception. Using this prescription will surely help Your Highness conceive!"

Caiwei, who was beside her, exclaimed, "If you have such a prescription, why didn’t you tell Her Highness sooner?"

"This medicine, though effective, is potent and forceful. After using it, one may only be able to conceive this once in their lifetime and never again. That is why I did not dare to tell Your Highness before."

"Will it harm the child in the womb?" Noble Consort asked.

"No, it will not."

Noble Consort pondered for a moment, a trace of sorrow flashing across her face before she resolved, "In that case, give it to me."

"Your Highness, you mustn’t!" Caiwei cried. "Didn’t you hear Physician Liu? After using this prescription, Your Highness will never be able to conceive again!"

Noble Consort gave a bitter smile. "Without this medicine, can I have multiple children? All these years have passed, and my womb has shown no sign of life. I can’t wait any longer."

Caiwei had no words to argue.

Indeed, after so many years without child, if they waited any longer, age would make it even harder. Moreover, the Emperor’s favor for Her Highness had already waned compared to before. By next year, when the Emperor selected new consorts, Her Highness’s favor would likely diminish further.

If she didn’t conceive now, it would become even more impossible in the future.

"I know you care for me, but I truly want a child who shares the Emperor’s blood. Only with our child will the Emperor and I be truly bound forever in this world."

Caiwei sighed. "This servant understands. No matter what Your Highness decides to do, I will stand by your side."

...

Although Noble Consort was confined to Ganlu Palace, the Emperor was still able to visit her.

Previously, the Emperor had frequently visited Xiangjun and even punished Noble Consort for her sake.

Now that Noble Consort was confined, the Emperor had not only stopped summoning Xiangjun but had also increased his visits to Noble Consort.

The harem began to speculate once more—perhaps Xiangjun had offended the Emperor over Noble Consort’s punishment.

Whether the Emperor had confined Noble Consort as a punishment or for her protection was unclear.

Thus, everyone’s attention shifted back to Ganlu Palace.

However, when the month of confinement ended, Noble Consort still claimed illness and refused to see anyone.

Then, another month passed in peace, and Noble Consort still did not emerge.

Just as the palace was abuzz with rumors that Noble Consort must be gravely ill, Ganlu Palace finally announced a piece of news that left everyone in the harem stunned: Noble Consort had been pregnant for over a month.

...

In Nanxun Palace, Consort Qin received the news while biting on a wooden plug to practice her pronunciation.

Ever since being mocked by Lady Lian, Consort Qin had practiced daily. Now, she no longer mispronounced words like "ting" instead of "ting."

Upon hearing the news of Noble Consort’s pregnancy, Consort Qin nearly bit the wooden plug in half.

"Zhu Jin!"

"Your Highness..."

"How could Noble Consort be pregnant? Go and investigate. Find out what’s going on!"

...

In Chengxiang Palace, Xiangjun was focused on copying her Buddhist scriptures.

At this moment, Chengxiang Palace was probably the only place in the entire harem that remained calm.

Xiangjun was not surprised that Noble Consort had conceived so quickly.

Xue Jiaojiao was, after all, a favorite of fate. She would possess everything good. The reason she hadn’t been able to bear children before was not because she was infertile, but because the author of the story couldn’t bear to let her suffer such a fate.

Physician Liu’s examination of Noble Consort had proven this. Her Highness was in perfect health, so her lack of pregnancy over the years was indeed strange.

Sure enough, after using the fertility medicine a few times, she had conceived.

Now, Weiyang Palace was likely in chaos.

Noble Consort had enjoyed the Emperor’s favor for many years without a son and had still managed to overshadow the Empress. If she now had a son, where would that leave the Empress?

...

Weiyang Palace.

The sound of shattering porcelain filled the air as objects were smashed to the ground.

The Empress was furious.

Noble Consort without a child was one thing, but with a child? Her position as Empress would be in jeopardy.

Xue Jiaojiao was the granddaughter of the Grand Preceptor. Years ago, the Grand Preceptor’s family had been persecuted for supporting the Emperor’s rise to the throne. The men were executed, and the women exiled. Thus, Xue Jiaojiao was also considered a meritorious subject in the Emperor’s ascension.

Moreover, General Wang and Right Chancellor Song Feijing were also her supporters.

With their backing, combined with the Emperor’s mad infatuation, her second son might never have a chance at the crown prince position.

Even though the matter of establishing the heir was something her father and grandfather could influence in the court, in the end, unless the Yang family wanted to be branded as traitors, the Emperor had the final say in choosing the heir.

The Empress absolutely could not allow Noble Consort’s child to be born.

...

Because the news of Noble Consort’s pregnancy after nearly a decade of favor was so shocking, another unusual event that occurred around the same time seemed almost ordinary in comparison.

Somehow, Lady Lian’s calligraphy had spread beyond the palace and gained fame in the capital.

Many scholars and literati were willing to pay a thousand gold for a single piece of her writing, and her calligraphy had even sparked a small trend in the capital. Many refined ladies were now studying and copying Lady Lian’s handwriting.

The Emperor was overjoyed to discover that his palace housed a calligrapher.

Furthermore, when several self-proclaimed purists in the court praised Lady Lian’s calligraphy, the Emperor felt even more proud.

Thus, after discussing state affairs with his ministers, he happily went to Chengxiang Palace with Gu Tingxue.

chapters.title: Lianhua Xiaozhi
chapters.content:
The last time the Emperor visited Chengxiang Palace was the day Noble Consort was punished.

And from that day onward, the Emperor had never again selected Xiangjun’s name card, likely because he feared Noble Consort still harbored resentment.

In truth, the Emperor did miss Xiangjun, but Noble Consort was still more important to him.

If he had just punished Noble Consort for Xiangjun’s sake and then summoned Xiangjun to his bed every night, wouldn’t that be telling the entire harem that Noble Consort was inferior to Xiangjun?

So, to prevent Noble Consort from being looked down upon, the Emperor endured his restlessness and ignored Xiangjun for two whole months.

Now, having found such a good excuse to visit Chengxiang Palace, the Emperor was naturally in high spirits.

When the Emperor and Gu Tingsue entered the room, Xiangjun was in the middle of writing.

Perhaps she hadn’t noticed their arrival yet, as she didn’t even lift her head.

The Emperor raised his hand, signaling Gu Tingsue to remain silent. The two of them stood under the exquisite wooden carved flower screen, quietly watching the beauty at the desk.

Today, Xiangjun wore only a plain dress, her hair loosely coiled in a simple bun. Her face carried a rare gentle and serene expression, a stark contrast to her usual coquettish and alluring demeanor.

Moreover, as she wrote, her gaze was solemn, even exuding an aura befitting a high-ranking concubine.

Seeing this side of Xiangjun, the Emperor’s smile softened even more.

"Graceful as a flower reflected in water, moving like willow swayed by the wind. That describes my beloved Lian."

Xiangjun seemed to only now realize there were people in the room. She looked up in surprise, and upon seeing who it was, she appeared almost disbelief, her voice choking as she said, "Your Majesty!"

Xiangjun set down her brush and immediately stepped forward to greet the Emperor.

The Emperor quickly helped her up, and as he lowered his head, he saw a face on the verge of tears.

Xiangjun’s eyes were red-rimmed, her expression one of extreme longing for the Emperor.

"What’s wrong?" he asked.

Xiangjun looked up at the Emperor, her voice trembling, "Has Your Majesty finally remembered this concubine?"

"Don’t talk nonsense. Of course I’ve been thinking of you. Now, why are you crying like a child? Everyone outside calls you Scholar Xiangjun. If those refined people in the capital find out that the celebrated calligrapher Xiang Xiangjun is actually a little crybaby, how will you face them?"

"What does this concubine have to be ashamed of… I just like crying…"

Xiangjun naturally wrapped her arms around the Emperor’s waist, leaning against his chest, her face naturally turning toward Gu Tingsue.

Xiangjun blinked at Gu Tingsue with a smug look, but when he didn’t respond, she finally loosened her hold on the Emperor.

"This concubine missed Your Majesty too much. I overstepped. Please don’t blame me, Your Majesty."

"How could I bear to?"

The Emperor already knew she had been wronged last time.

He had expected that after so long without visiting her, Xiangjun would have some grievances to voice. But to his surprise, she was still as bright and lively as ever, which put his mind at ease.

"Enough, stop acting spoiled. Tingsue is still here."

Xiangjun glanced at Gu Tingsue and, following the Emperor’s address, called out, "Oh, why is Lord Tingsue here?"

The Emperor didn’t notice anything amiss with Xiangjun’s way of addressing him and replied, "Tingsue was curious and wanted to see the calligraphy of my beloved Lian."

This was the first time Xiangjun had called Gu Tingsue by his name. Gu Tingsue’s heart stirred, but his expression remained unchanged. He nodded at Xiangjun, and she smiled back at him.

The Emperor sat at Xiangjun’s desk, examining her recent writing, clearly satisfied.

"Today, the Minister of Revenue even came to me begging for your calligraphy. He said his daughter was insisting on it, and he had no choice but to come to me. It was the first time I’ve seen that old man at a loss."

Seeing the Emperor’s smug expression, Xiangjun couldn’t help but look down on him.

This dog Emperor was both inferior and arrogant, so he was extremely concerned with face and desperately craved the recognition of everyone.

But how could he gain the world’s recognition?

By possessing what everyone else desired most.

The highest status, the most wealth, the best women—he wanted it all.

And not only did he want it, but he also had to show it off to the world.

Otherwise, how would the world know he was the most supreme, the most perfect man in existence?

Xiangjun had even suspected that the Emperor’s fondness for Xue Jiaojiao stemmed from the same reasoning.

Prince Jin, General Wang, Song Feijing…

All the men the Emperor had envied had once loved Xue Jiaojiao. So he wanted to use Xue Jiaojiao’s love for him to prove that he was stronger than his brothers.

In this regard, Xiangjun couldn’t compare to Noble Consort. But she could find other ways to give the Emperor face, which was why she had come up with her current plan:

First, under the pretense of Noble Consort praying for blessings, she had many of her hand-copied scriptures sent to Huguo Temple for offering.

Then, "coincidentally," a group of scholars and literati had seen her calligraphy. With a little help from others, she had spread a few stories that the literati would love, giving people beautiful and fanciful illusions about her. Thus, her calligraphy quickly gained fame.

These tactics weren’t particularly novel—this was basically how the flower queens of Jiangnan were promoted, and with even more flair.

Gu Tingsue was indeed formidable. The tasks Xiangjun had given him were completed swiftly.

In just two months, he had successfully built up her reputation, turning her into a "female Sage of Calligraphy." She had suddenly become a master calligrapher, and the price of paper in the capital had even risen because of her.

The Emperor looked at Xiangjun’s calligraphy, growing more pleased the longer he stared.

"That old bastard from the Ministry of Revenue begged me so much that I had no choice but to come to my Xiangjun for help."

Tsk tsk, Xiangjun thought to herself, this dog Emperor hadn’t paid her any attention for two months, and now he was acting so intimate.

"As Your Majesty commands, this concubine will write a piece for the Minister of Revenue."

"You have my gratitude, Xiangjun."

"This concubine is not tired. After all, I have nothing to do all day in the palace." As she spoke, Xiangjun leaned against the Emperor again, softly saying, "Your Majesty, could you give a name to my calligraphy? That way, every time I write, I will think of you."

The Emperor’s expression grew even more tender.

"Very well. I shall bestow a name upon your calligraphy. It will make for a fine story when it spreads."

The Emperor pondered for a moment before writing on the paper: Lianhua Xiaozhi.

"How is it?"

Xiangjun happily nodded. "This concubine loves it! My title of 'Lian the Beauty' was also bestowed by Your Majesty, and now my calligraphy bears a name you have given. This concubine is overjoyed."

At the mention of her title, the Emperor’s heart stirred.

"This title of 'Beauty' is still too humble for our Scholar Xiangjun. I think it would be better to bestow upon you the title of Honored Lady."

Gu Tingsue, who was standing nearby, immediately bowed to Xiangjun with a smile. "Congratulations, Honored Lady Lian. Might this humble servant, riding on this joyous occasion, also ask the Honored Lady for a piece of calligraphy?"

Xiangjun beamed at Gu Tingsue. "Of course, this concubine will write a fine piece for Lord Tingsue."

"Write one for the Minister of Revenue as well. I have other matters to attend to. I will come see you again this evening."

"Yes, this concubine awaits Your Majesty’s return!"

The Emperor stood up and began to leave. After taking a few steps, he stopped.

The Emperor turned to Gu Tingsue, who was following behind him. "You stay here and wait. Once Honored Lady Lian finishes writing, take the calligraphy and leave. Deliver it to the Minister of Revenue soon, so he doesn’t come bothering me again."

"Yes, this humble servant obeys."

The Emperor waved his hand and left with a face full of spring breeze.

As soon as the Emperor left, the maids serving in the room, Meng Mei and Xi Yu, tactfully retreated as well.

Soon, only Gu Tingsue and Xiangjun remained in the room.

"Congratulations, Honored Lady Lian. In just two months, you’ve already risen a rank. I suppose it won’t be long before you’re granted the title of Imperial Concubine."

Xiangjun detected the sarcasm in Gu Tingsue’s voice and couldn’t help but glare at him.

She wasn’t particularly pleased either. After all that effort, she had only been promoted one rank. The Emperor was truly stingy.

"What a waste of time… only a Honored Lady…"

Xiangjun huffed and went back to writing.

Seeing that Xiangjun was upset, Gu Tingsue smiled, walked to the desk, and began grinding ink for her.

"You needn’t be disheartened. You’ve already done very well."

Xiangjun looked up at Gu Tingsue, softly saying, "I must also thank Lord Tingsue for promoting me. To build up my reputation, you must have spent a considerable amount of money."

"As long as you write a few more pieces for me, I’ll earn that money back." Gu Tingsue smiled gently. He didn’t feel he had done all that much. "Your calligraphy is unique. It truly deserves such praise."

Gu Tingsue meant every word.

The first time he had seen Xiangjun’s calligraphy, he had been surprised. He simply couldn’t believe that such a shameless, clingy woman could produce such elegant and refined characters.

They said calligraphy reflected the person, but the difference between her and her writing was too great.

Aesthetics were the hardest things to force upon others.

Though Gu Tingsue had worked behind the scenes to promote her, the fact that Xiangjun’s calligraphy had captivated the capital was also due to her own skill.

Xiangjun didn’t dare claim her calligraphy was unique. She quickly explained, "This script isn’t my own creation. It belongs to my master. I merely studied under her from a young age and worked hard to imitate her, which is why I can write just like her."

Gu Tingsue was somewhat surprised.

Xiangjun was quite honest.

"Who is your master? Which great calligrapher?"

"My master isn’t a great calligrapher. Her name is Wenjun, and she’s fifteen years older than me. She was originally the daughter of an official from a scholarly family, but one day, she fell from grace and became the daughter of a convicted criminal. She ended up in the pleasure quarters… Later, as she grew older, she was sold to the Xu family and tasked with teaching us young girls calligraphy and poetry. Eventually, she caught the eye of the second master of the Xu family and became his concubine… I was lucky enough to earn my master’s favor, and she personally taught me calligraphy and painting."

Mentioning her master, Xiangjun felt a pang of melancholy.

Her master’s days as a concubine to the second master of the Xu family had not been easy. The main wife had been intolerant, making life difficult for her at every turn, even forbidding her from keeping brush and paper in her room.

Thus, her master’s talents had remained buried.

"I’ll borrow my master’s script for now. When the time is right, I will make sure the world knows that Lianhua Xiaozhi was created by my master. I will make sure my master can hold her head high in the Xu family."

Seeing Xiangjun’s determined expression, Gu Tingsue found it almost amusing.

"You really have a lot of people to help. Can you manage them all?"

"I only help those who have been kind to me."

Speaking of helping others, Xiangjun thought of Lady Li.

After Noble Consort became pregnant, even fewer people paid attention to Lady Li’s pregnancy.

Xiangjun quickly asked, "Lord Tingsue, have you looked into the matter I asked you about before? Have Lady Li’s family been found?"

"Is this the second favor you’ve asked of me?"

"Ah, how can such a small matter count as a favor! Isn’t this just something Lord Tingsue can handle with a single word?"

Xiangjun blinked at Gu Tingsue, hoping he would make an exception.

Gu Tingsue lowered his head and continued grinding ink, saying nothing.

Xiangjun muttered under her breath, "Just like that stingy dog Emperor."

Gu Tingsue shot her a sharp glance, and Xiangjun swallowed her words, grumbling, "Fine, consider it the second favor I’ve asked of you. Is that okay?"

"Lady Li has no living relatives in this world. They all perished in the locust plague of Yanqing’s third year."

Xiangjun felt like crying. How could they all be dead?

Hadn’t she wasted a favor for nothing?

Seeing Xiangjun’s despondent expression, Gu Tingsue didn’t offer any comfort. Instead, he coldly mocked, "Kind-hearted people don’t last long in the harem. Lady Li has done nothing for you. You owe her no debt."

Xiangjun couldn’t explain herself to Gu Tingsue. She could only say, "I just think that instead of fighting with others, it’s better to have more allies."

"What kind of help can Lady Li provide you?"

"Lord Tingsue mustn’t look down on the lowly. Sometimes, those whom the nobles despise can, in their desperation, take a bite out of them."

Just like Xiangjun in her past life.

Everyone had looked down on her, but hadn’t she still managed to take bite after bite out of them, leaving them in agony?

Gu Tingsue looked at the sparkle in Xiangjun’s eyes and felt a newfound appreciation for her. His expression softened considerably.

He reached into his official robe and placed a letter on the table.

"What’s this?"

"Lady Li indeed has no living relatives," Gu Tingsue told Xiangjun. "But she has a close friend who considers her a sister. Like her, she was a courtesan raised by the Shen family of Jiangnan. This is a reply letter she wrote to Lady Li."

Xiangjun was overjoyed. She grabbed the letter and was about to go see Lady Li, but Gu Tingsue yanked her back.

"Aren’t you going to finish the calligraphy? How much longer does Lord Tingsue have to wait?"

"Ah, there are plenty in the cabinet. Just take a couple as you like."

"Is that how you treat me?"

Xiangjun blinked at Gu Tingsue, her expression asking: Is that not allowed?

Gu Tingsue was almost amused into anger. He felt that his position as a powerful eunuch was becoming more and more undignified.

Previously, Gu Tingsue had at most two masters.

One was the Empress Dowager, and the other was the Emperor.

Though Noble Consort occasionally asked Gu Tingsue for favors, he only complied out of respect for the Emperor, and only when the Emperor had already agreed.

Even the Empress herself didn’t dare order him around.

And now, Honored Lady Lian, a mere Honored Lady, dared to leave him waiting here?

And expected him to pick for himself?

Gu Tingsue’s expression darkened as he grabbed Xiangjun and pushed her back to the desk.

With a blackened face, Gu Tingsue said, "Write my calligraphy now."

"Write, write, I’ll write it now!"

Xiangjun thought for a moment, then picked up her brush and wrote:

*Knowing you listen to the wind’s desolate howl at night,**At dawn, I gaze at the pavilion, half-covered in snow.**Shaking the branches, yet sparing the willow’s tender eyes,**Sweeping the ground, but leaving the plum blossoms untouched…*

After finishing the entire poem, Xiangjun blew on the paper to dry the ink, then handed it to Gu Tingsue. "How is it? Will this do?"

Gu Tingsue’s gaze fell on his own name, and for some reason, he felt a pang of embarrassment.

"No signature?" Gu Tingsue asked, his face still dark.

"This poem isn’t mine. What signature would I put…?"

"You wrote the calligraphy."

Xiangjun had no choice but to add her own name. She even took out her personal seal and stamped it.

"Is this okay now?"

Gu Tingsue hummed in acknowledgment, took the calligraphy, and turned to leave.

"Wait! The calligraphy for the Minister of Revenue’s daughter isn’t ready yet!"

Xiangjun quickly pulled out a previously written copy of the *Heart Sutra* and handed it to Gu Tingsue.

Gu Tingsue rarely found himself in such a fluster. He took both pieces of calligraphy and left in a hurry.

Xiangjun noticed Gu Tingsue’s strange behavior.

What was going on? Had he… become shy?

But what had she done to him? What did Gu Tingsue have to be shy about?

---

chapters.content:

chapters.title: She Must Be a Patient One
chapters.content:
When Xiangjun arrived at Ganlu Palace, Noble Consort Guifei was refusing all visitors.

Upon hearing that Xiangjun had come to see Li Gengyi, Caiwei’s expression darkened, but she still had someone lead Xiangjun and Mengmei to the side courtyard.

In the side hall, upon seeing the letter from her close friend, Li Gengyi finally showed a hint of will to live.

“Sister, I don’t even know how to thank you.”
