“It wasn’t a difficult matter, no need for thanks. You should focus on giving birth safely. In the future, when your rank rises, perhaps you’ll find a way to bring her into the palace. If she becomes a palace maid, you two can keep each other company.”

“Is that possible?”

“Of course. If you give birth to a prince, you’ll be the prince’s birth mother. After the Emperor passes, the birth mother of a prince can leave the palace to retire.”

“Really? But can I keep this child?”

“Right now, Noble Consort Guifei is pregnant, and you’re already six months along. By the time you give birth, she’ll be heavily pregnant herself—she won’t have the energy to interfere with your child. There’s a good chance she’ll let you raise the child yourself first.”

“And after Noble Consort gives birth?”

“If she gives birth to a prince, she probably won’t want your child.”

“And if it’s a princess?”

“Then it depends on whether you give birth to a prince or a princess…”

Li Gengyi rubbed her belly and said, “Then it’s best if I’m carrying a princess, so this child can definitely stay with me.”

“A prince or a princess would be fine, but the most important thing for you now is to take care of your health. Look at you—six months along and still so thin. Your whole body looks like it’s being swallowed by your belly. You need to eat more.”

Li Gengyi nodded. “Sister, I will definitely take good care of myself from now on.”

“I believe you.”

“Sister, my name is Qinglian. From now on, you can call me Little Sister Qinglian, okay?”

“Alright, then you can call me Sister Xiangjun.”

The two held hands and chatted for a while longer before Xiangjun hurriedly took her leave. She didn’t want to stay too long in Noble Consort Guifei’s palace in case something happened and she was blamed.

...

By that afternoon, the news of Xiangjun’s promotion to Noble Lady had been announced to the six palaces.

But no one paid much attention to it—after all, nothing was more important than Noble Consort Guifei’s pregnancy.

That very evening, the Emperor visited Chengxiang Palace.

In the past, whenever the Emperor summoned Xiangjun, he would have her go to the Taiji Hall. This was the first time he had come to her bedchamber.

Earlier that day, the Emperor had lingered by Xiangjun’s desk for a while, and only now did he have the chance to properly examine her living quarters.

He was somewhat surprised.

Though it was the residence of a concubine, it was furnished as finely as any noble consort’s palace.

“Your things are quite fine,” the Emperor remarked, eyeing the cloud-brocade mosquito net.

Xiangjun blinked and said frankly, “This humble concubine’s father was a salt merchant. Our family had some money.”

Her candor left the Emperor at a loss—he even found it a little amusing.

It made sense.

When Gu Tingxue had confiscated the property of that Jiangnan salt merchant, he had not only secured funds for the southern war but also uncovered a private vault of fifty million taels of silver for the Emperor.

Clearly, the salt merchant had been truly wealthy.

So, it was no wonder Xiangjun’s belongings were of such high quality.

“Who would have thought that my beloved Noble Lady is a little rich girl.”

Xiangjun’s smug little expression was almost adorable.

“If it weren’t for my family’s money, my father wouldn’t have been able to hire good teachers and scholars to teach me music, chess, calligraphy, and painting. Then, I wouldn’t be able to bring honor to Your Majesty now.”

The Emperor pinched Xiangjun’s nose. Previously, he had only found her pleasing in bed, but now he found her girlish charm rather endearing.

“If Xiangjun gives birth to a princess, she will surely be as lovely as you.” The Emperor drew the curtains. “Let me make one with you right now.”

...

The next morning, the Emperor had breakfast with Xiangjun before leaving.

After he departed, Xiangjun had Mengmei and Xiyu replace all her bedding.

Though she found attending to the Emperor tedious, his words from the previous night had given her an idea.

If she became pregnant, perhaps her rank could rise as well?

With that thought, Xiangjun decided to act.

She had Mengmei fetch Physician Liu and obtain several doses of conception-aiding medicine.

She wasn’t using the harsh, tiger-and-wolf-like drugs that Guifei used. Since she was naturally fertile—having given birth to three children in her past life—she only needed mild, harmless medicine.

As for whether she could conceive within half a year, that was up to heaven.

...

Noble Consort Guifei’s pregnancy had stabilized, so the Emperor no longer needed to constantly stay by her side. He began to favor other concubines again.

The one he visited most frequently was still Xiangjun.

The Emperor had truly developed a taste for her.

Xiangjun was a study in contrasts.

On the surface, she was a celebrated calligrapher revered by the scholarly world. The Buddhist scriptures she had copied were widely circulated, and everyone imagined her to be graceful and dignified.

But behind closed doors, she was alluring and passionate—there was nothing she wouldn’t dare to do in bed.

This extreme contrast made the Emperor utterly infatuated. The thought that so many people admired the woman in his arms only excited him further.

The best things in the world should all belong to him.

The Emperor wished he could stay with Xiangjun every night, but she didn’t dare let others know how favored she was.

She didn’t want the resentment of the harem to shift onto her. It was better if everyone continued to direct their anger at Noble Consort Guifei.

So, after each visit, Xiangjun would persuade the Emperor to go sleep with Noble Consort Guifei.

“Noble Consort Guifei has been in the palace for ten years and has only now conceived. She must be both happy and anxious. This humble concubine shouldn’t say this, but there are so many in the palace who envy and resent her. Your Majesty should spend more time with her.”

The Emperor’s expression softened. “If I leave, what will others think of you? The tongues in the harem are sharp—words can wound as much as blades.”

“This humble concubine doesn’t mind. As long as Your Majesty holds me in your heart, and as long as Noble Consort Guifei is happy, I am satisfied.”

“Why do you care so much for Guifei?”

“Your Majesty, you probably don’t know—during the first half-year after I entered the palace, I couldn’t see you, and I suffered many hardships in secret. Everyone dared to bully me… Later, because Noble Consort Guifei often sent me gifts, everyone knew that she remembered me, and they stopped daring to bully me. That was when my days became easier.”

The Emperor was moved by her words.

Back then, he had avoided seeing Xiangjun to prevent Guifei from being upset. He hadn’t realized that this little girl had endured so much hardship in secret.

“You are kind. The women in the harem always resent Guifei for her favor. Over the years, she has had no true sisters by her side. Now that she has you—a good sister who cares for her—I can rest easy.”

“Mmm, Your Majesty can be at ease. This humble concubine will take good care of her and ensure she suffers no grievances.”

“You… first take care of yourself and avoid grievances.”

“Mmm, mmm. Your Majesty, go quickly. If you don’t, she might fall asleep.”

The Emperor sighed in resignation but still went to Guifei’s quarters.

This went on for several days. Even Guifei began to believe that Xiangjun truly cared for her and let down her guard.

Meanwhile, the other women in the harem grew even more convinced that Guifei was the Emperor’s favorite. Some even mocked Xiangjun in private, calling her nothing more than a tool for the Emperor’s pleasure.

And so, Xiangjun gained a new reputation in the harem: she was spineless.

Every time the Emperor went to her, he would end up being “intercepted” by Guifei halfway. How could she endure such humiliation?

Clearly, she had no temper at all.

---

chapters.title: A Man’s Hands
chapters.content:
The Emperor left early that day.

After having her bedding replaced, Xiangjun lay on the bed and happily began reading.

These past few days, the Emperor had visited every night, and Mengmei and Xiyu had been exhausted. So, Xiangjun let them go to sleep.

Free from interruptions, she ignored Mengmei’s warnings and read late into the night.

In her past life, Xiangjun had lost because she only knew how to scheme within the harem, constantly fighting with other women. She had failed to see that the women’s struggles were merely an extension of the political battles in the imperial court.

It wasn’t until she awoke and read the complete story that she realized—many things had been decided long before they began.

For example, Qin Zhaoyi’s downfall and resurgence, Yang Empress’s tragic exit, and Xue Jiaojiao’s ascension to the throne.

None of these were determined by the women’s struggles in the harem. Their actions were merely the spark, not the final deciding hand.

After realizing her shortcomings, Xiangjun made it a point to read historical texts in this life whenever she had the time.

She studied whatever the emperors studied.

Only then could she understand what those at the core of power were thinking.

Xiangjun was deeply engrossed in her reading when a hand suddenly snatched the book away.

Thinking it was Mengmei, she begged for mercy while reaching for the book. “Good Mengmei, let me finish this section.”

Unexpectedly, her flailing hands were caught by someone.

Through the swaying gauze curtains, she saw a figure standing by the window—Gu Tingxue.

“Eunuch Tingxue? Why are you here? How did you get in?”

Gu Tingxue coldly huffed. “If I want to enter silently, the few guards in your palace wouldn’t even notice.”

He glanced at the book Xiangjun had been reading.

She was actually reading *Records of the Grand Historian*, specifically the *Annals of Empress Lü*.

“Noble Lady Lian has great ambitions. Are you planning to become the next Empress Lü?”

“I don’t have that kind of ability, but I will try my best.”

Gu Tingxue was left speechless.

“Women in the harem fear being accused of having the ambition of Lü or Huo. Yet here you are, daring to strive in that direction.”

“How many of those women who fear such accusations have ever been recorded in history? How many have been placed in the annals of emperors?”

Gu Tingxue couldn’t help but look Xiangjun up and down. She was truly the most daring person he had ever met when it came to facing her own desires.

He returned the book to her.

Xiangjun quickly tucked it under her pillow, then sat up on the bed, tilting her head as she looked at Gu Tingxue.

“Did Eunuch Tingxue come specifically to see me? Or did you hear that I’ve become a joke in the harem?”

From her expression, Gu Tingxue could tell she wasn’t upset at all.

“The Emperor treats you this way, yet you don’t seem to mind.”

“What’s there to mind? I don’t even want to sleep with the Emperor. It’s better if he goes to Guifei—I prefer the peace. Otherwise, halfway through the night, he might get… animalistic, and I’d have to tire myself out attending to him. Every time I spend half an hour seducing him, he finishes in the time it takes to drink a cup of tea. There’s no fun in it.”

Gu Tingxue had witnessed many concubines serving the Emperor in bed, but this was the first time he had heard one speak so bluntly about such matters. He felt a rare moment of embarrassment, not knowing where to look.

Xiangjun didn’t mind his silence and continued chattering, “But even if it’s not fun, it doesn’t matter. The matron who raised me once said that if a woman finds physical pleasure, she might develop feelings for the man who gave it to her. Since I never find pleasure, I won’t fall in love with the Emperor. Am I right?”

“I… I wouldn’t know about such things…” Gu Tingxue said impatiently.

Xiangjun noticed the change in his tone.

She narrowed her eyes at him. Why did his ears look a little red?

Was he… embarrassed?

A mischievous idea formed in her mind.

Xiangjun lifted the half-drawn cloud-brocade curtain, knelt on the bed, and leaned halfway out, approaching Gu Tingxue by the window. With her bright, sparkling eyes fixed on him, she said in a soft, lingering tone, “I’ve heard the sisters say that a man’s *thing* is only useful for making babies. Otherwise, a pair of skillful hands can bring a woman more pleasure than anything else.”

Gu Tingxue lowered his gaze, glaring at her. How could a palace concubine speak so boldly?

But then, before he could react, his hand was suddenly grabbed by Xiangjun.

She held his hand, sighing in admiration. “Oh, Eunuch Gu’s hands are so beautiful—so white, so long, and they look so dextrous. Eunuch Tingxue, what do you usually do with these hands?”

Gu Tingxue yanked his hand back abruptly, his face flushing even redder.

He seemed genuinely annoyed now, his voice stiff. “Noble Lady Lian, I came to see you today because I have serious business to discuss.”

“Oh…” Xiangjun pouted slightly, withdrawing her hand. She knelt on the bed and asked, “What is it?”

“Didn’t you ask me to keep an eye on the Second Prince’s movements? There have been some developments.”

“What did you find?” Xiangjun’s voice trembled with excitement.

“The Second Prince’s wet nurse is one of Song Feijing’s people. Recently, it seems Song Feijing is planning to do something to the Second Prince. I’ll find out the details and let you know.”

It was happening! Xiangjun was thrilled. The turning point of the Empress’s complete fall in her past life—the death of the Second Prince—was about to unfold!

In her past life, at this time, Xiangjun had been pregnant and stayed in Guifei’s Ganlu Palace, so she had no idea what was happening outside. All she knew was that the Empress’s legitimate son had somehow ended up in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

The Wenyuan Pavilion was a library, and it had caught fire by accident. The Second Prince had been burned to death.

Later, Xiangjun had read in books that this had been the work of Song Feijing’s people in the palace.

At the time, the Emperor had made it clear that he wanted Xiangjun’s unborn child to be raised by Guifei. To smoothly support Guifei’s child as the crown prince, Song Feijing naturally had to eliminate the Empress’s son.

As for whether Xiangjun’s child was a boy or not, it didn’t matter—Song Feijing had ways to ensure the child would be a prince, even if it meant swapping the baby.

Book reviewers all said Song Feijing was a *bingjiao* (a character archetype often depicted as cold and calculating due to illness).

Xiangjun didn’t know what *bingjiao* meant. She hadn’t seen any “jiao” (spoiled) behavior from Song Feijing, but he was indeed gravely ill.

However, the Empress’s side was not to be trifled with. Behind her stood the entire Yang clan, and nearly half the officials in the imperial court were either Yang’s relatives or his students.

So, not long after, the Yang family discovered that Song Feijing was behind the Second Prince’s death, all for the sake of Guifei in the palace.

Thus, a brutal struggle erupted between the front court and the harem.

In the imperial court, Prime Minister Yang and Song Feijing clashed, while in the harem, the Empress and Guifei fought.

Xiangjun had been incredibly lucky. Originally, she was supposed to be executed while her child was spared, but because of this incident, the Empress not only saved Xiangjun’s life but also planned to use her against Guifei.

That was how Xiangjun had managed to survive another eight years.

But there was one thing Xiangjun didn’t quite understand.

Given what she knew about Gu Tingxue, even without her prompting, he wouldn’t have been unaware of Song Feijing’s actions.

So, in her past life, he must have chosen to turn a blind eye.

Why?

Was he waiting to watch the tigers fight so he could gather more power for himself?

Or had he already silently chosen Guifei’s side? After all, he had said before—*whoever wins, I’ll help them.*

chapters.title: Saving the Second Prince
chapters.content:
"You why suddenly want me to keep an eye on the Second Prince?" Gu Tingxue suddenly asked.

Xiangjun came back to her senses and said, "Isn't it because the Emperor is stingy? I was thinking of trying to see if I could follow the Empress's path to rise in rank. The Empress cares most about her Second Prince. Don't I need to understand the Second Prince's preferences and the people who attend to him? Only then can I find an opportunity to get close to the Second Prince."

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun intently, as if he didn't quite believe her, with a look that said, "You're just making this up. I'll believe you when hell freezes over."

Xiangjun cleared her throat and quickly leaned closer to Gu Tingxue, tilting her head, looking at him with her sparkling eyes, and gently placing her hand on his shoulder.

Sure enough, Gu Tingxue's attention was unconsciously diverted.

"Eunuch Tingxue, is investigating the Second Prince the second or third thing you've done for me?"

Gu Tingxue raised his eyebrows, trying his best to control his gaze from looking at Xiangjun's lips, which were getting closer and closer.

He lowered his voice and asked, "What do you think?"

"I was thinking that the matter with Concubine Li was nothing for you, Eunuch. So, this should be the second thing, right? Isn't it?"

Gu Tingxue looked down at Xiangjun, not speaking for a long time.

Gu Tingxue looked at her, and Xiangjun let him look, returning his gaze. After all, Gu Tingxue was good-looking.

Xiangjun noticed that Gu Tingxue had quite red and white lips.

He was a eunuch, and he didn't apply lip rouge, so how could they be so red and moist?

Gu Tingxue felt uncomfortable under Xiangjun's gaze, and the familiar scent lingered around his nose.

Ever since the first time he saw Xiangjun at the Suzhou General's residence, Gu Tingxue had noticed it.

Every time he got close to Xiangjun, he could smell a strange fragrance, and this scent seemed to disturb his mind, making him unusually irritable.

He took a step back, quickly putting distance between himself and Xiangjun, frowning as he asked, "What is that scent on you? It's so strange."

Xiangjun was a bit confused, "Huh? There's nothing, it's just ordinary perfumed powder. Maybe it's the one I brought from Jiangnan, and it's not available in the palace?"

"It's not the scent of perfumed powder."

Xiangjun was puzzled, lifting her hand to smell her own sleeve, "There's no other scent..."

Gu Tingxue was getting impatient, "Forget it, I'll go first. Don't forget, you have less than four months left."

Gu Tingxue turned to leave.

"Hey! Eunuch Tingxue, you still haven't told me, is this the second or third time you've helped me?"

Gu Tingxue was already at the door when he reluctantly said, "The second time!"

Gu Tingxue told himself that he was just afraid of being pestered by that unreasonable woman. He didn't have time to always argue with her about such trivial matters.

...

In the following days, the harem was finally peaceful.

Xiangjun continued to devotedly serve the Emperor, occasionally checking on Concubine Li.

At other times, Xiangjun played the role of a calligrapher well and finally obtained the Emperor's permission to go to the Wenyuange Pavilion to find books to read.

Thus, Xiangjun would go to the Wenyuange Pavilion every day.

One day, Xiangjun took Xiyu and Xiaoluzhi to the Wenyuange Pavilion to find books again.

But when they arrived near the Wenyuange Pavilion, they found that there was rolling black smoke coming from the direction of the Wenyuange Pavilion.

Xiaoluzhi grabbed a passing eunuch and asked, "What happened?"

"The Wenyuange Pavilion is on fire!"

Seeing the people coming and going, Xiaoluzhi said to Xiangjun, "Noble Lady, shouldn't we go back? Don't get hurt."

"How can that be? If the rare books in the Wenyuange Pavilion are all burned, I'll be heartbroken. Let's go and take a look. I really can't rest assured."

Xiangjun rushed to the Wenyuange Pavilion with Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu, and only then did she realize how terrifying the fire was.

The fire started from the third floor.

Although the first floor had not caught fire yet, it was filled with black smoke, and no one could enter.

Xiangjun looked around, and the Empress's people had not arrived yet.

The Wenyuange Pavilion was in chaos, and all they could hear was a young eunuch kneeling there, crying out to heaven and earth. Beside him lay two unconscious mammy.

Xiaoluzhi went up and asked, only to find out that the Second Prince was in the Wenyuange Pavilion and had not been found yet.

Xiangjun was anxious and said to the young eunuch, "Then why don't you let people go in and look for him!"

"We've all gone in to look. We only found the unconscious mammy on the second floor, but not the Second Prince."

Xiyu reminded Xiangjun from the side, "Noble Lady, the Wenyuange Pavilion is full of bookshelves, and there are many corners. Plus, they've been organizing the books recently. If the Second Prince is unconscious somewhere, it's really hard to find him."

The young eunuch nodded through tears.

Xiangjun was anxious and scolded, "You foolish thing! That's the Second Prince. If something happens to him, you'll all lose your heads! If you can't find him, then send more people in to look!"

"But... the fire is too big, we can't go in."

The young eunuch only knew how to fake cry, showing a hesitant expression.

The fire was so big, who would dare to go in? Servants were also people who valued their lives. The Second Prince was noble, but there weren't many servants who would genuinely exchange their lives for his.

The remaining palace people who were putting out the fire also did not dare to approach easily, only using water dragons to spray water at the Wenyuange Pavilion.

But there were too many books in the Wenyuange Pavilion, and the fire could not be extinguished in a short time.

Moreover, if they waited until the fire was extinguished before going in to look for people, the Second Prince would surely be dead by then.

Xiangjun saw the bright yellow palace dress appearing in the distance from the corner of her eye, along with a group of hurried figures. She stamped her foot, snatched a water bucket from a passing eunuch, and poured it all over herself.

"I'm going to find the Second Prince!"

Xiangjun covered her mouth with a handkerchief and rushed in.

"Noble Lady!"

Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu screamed behind Xiangjun, their hearts breaking.

"Noble Lady! You can't go find the Second Prince, you'll lose your life! Noble Lady!"

By the time the Emperor and the Empress hurried over, all they saw was Xiangjun's figure rushing into the black flames.

"What happened?" the Empress asked.

Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu plopped down on their knees. Xiaoluzhi wailed, "In response to the Empress, our Noble Lady learned that the Second Prince was still trapped in the fire and had not been found, so... so she rushed in to find the Second Prince!"

The Empress staggered and almost fell. The Emperor quickly reached out to support her.

"Go in and save people!"

...

In the storybook, it was written that the Second Prince had fainted due to inhaling the black smoke and fell from the railing on the second floor, directly onto a pile of unorganized books on the first floor.

The people who rushed in went to the second floor to look, so naturally, they couldn't find him. They only dragged out the unconscious mammy who were taking care of the Second Prince on the second floor.

So, as soon as Xiangjun entered the Wenyuange Pavilion, she rushed towards the pile of books mentioned in the storybook.

But the pile of books was too big, and Xiangjun couldn't flip through them with one hand, so she threw away the handkerchief and started flipping.

But as soon as she inhaled a mouthful of the black smoke, Xiangjun felt like she was going to choke to death.

She quickly held her breath and flipped with all her might, finally finding a small person.

Xiangjun covered the Second Prince's mouth with the damp handkerchief, hugged him, and ran out. But the Wenyuange Pavilion was too big.

After running for a while, Xiangjun couldn't hold her breath anymore. She couldn't help but take a breath, and again inhaled a mouthful of black smoke.

Just when Xiangjun was about to collapse, a hand reached out from the black smoke, covering her mouth with a damp sweat towel.

Xiangjun recognized that hand. It was Gu Tingxue's.

chapters.title: The Empress is Still the Most Generous
chapters.content:
The black smoke from the Wenyuange Pavilion was rolling.

Everyone was waiting anxiously.

Then, a pink figure appeared in the black smoke.

"It's the Noble Lady! The Noble Lady!" Xiaoluzhi excitedly shouted, "The Noble Lady has come out with the Second Prince!"

When they reached the entrance of the Wenyuange Pavilion, Xiangjun seemed to have used her last bit of strength, putting down the Second Prince, and then collapsed straight to the ground, completely unconscious...

When Xiangjun chose to open her eyes again, she was already in Chengxiang Hall.

Standing next to her were Xiyu and Spring Mama from the Empress's palace.

The first thing Xiangjun said when she opened her eyes was, "The Second Prince... Is the Second Prince alright?"

Her voice was already a bit hoarse from the black smoke.

Spring Mama immediately came forward, "The Second Prince hasn't woken up yet. The Emperor, the Empress, and the imperial physicians are all guarding him in Weiyang Palace. The Empress couldn't spare the time, but she is grateful to the Noble Lady for saving the Second Prince and is worried about the Noble Lady. So, she sent me here to watch over the Noble Lady."

"Spring Mama, I'm fine. You should quickly go back and accompany the Empress."

Xiangjun propped herself up, and Spring Mama quickly pressed her back down.

"The Noble Lady has woken up, so I can rest assured. Then I will go back and report to the Empress. The Noble Lady can rest assured, your kindness, our Empress will remember."

Spring Mama curtsied to Xiangjun, then turned and left hurriedly.

After Spring Mama left, Xiangjun immediately sat up.

Her body was fine, and her fainting was also an act.

Xiyu quickly put a pillow behind Xiangjun and helped her sit up.

"Noble Lady, you scared me to death today! How could you dare to rush into such thick black smoke?"

Xiangjun had only told part of the story to Xiaoluzhi over the past few days, not to Mengmei or Xiyu.

It wasn't that she trusted Xiaoluzhi more, but she knew that Mengmei and Xiyu didn't have Xiaoluzhi's ruthlessness. If they knew, they wouldn't be able to keep up the act.

"I'm fine, aren't I? Where is Mengmei?"

"Sister Mengmei is watching the medicine for the Noble Lady. I'll go call her over."

When Mengmei entered the room, her eyes were red, as if she was angry with Xiangjun.

Xiangjun smiled and stretched her head to look at Mengmei, "Oh, my Sister Mengmei, what's wrong? Why are your eyes red?"

"You still have the nerve to ask! What does the Second Prince have to do with you? You don't even care about your own life!"

Xiangjun pulled Mengmei to sit beside her, looking pitiful, "Sister Mengmei, you understand me the most. I have no one to rely on in the palace. Only by saving the Second Prince will the Empress protect me in the future."

Mengmei understood Xiangjun's difficulties, but she still felt sad in her heart. With red eyes, she said, "I should have gone with the Noble Lady to the Wenyuange Pavilion today. If I had gone, I would not have let the Noble Lady rush into the fire. If we had to save the Second Prince, I could have gone. I could have gone in your place, and the Empress would have protected you. Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu didn't even know to stop you."

Xiangjun didn't respond.

It was precisely because she knew that Mengmei would definitely do this that Xiangjun had deliberately not brought her along.

Mengmei spoke and tears fell, "Does the Noble Lady know that when I saw you being carried back, I was so scared I almost died? It reminded me of when we were children, and you were punished by the Second Madam because of me. When you were carried back then, you looked just like this..."

"Oh, that was so many years ago. Sister Mengmei, trust me, I would never risk my life recklessly. I have a plan for everything I do. You just have to believe in me."

Mengmei sighed, feeling that she understood Xiangjun less and less.

She could see that today's events were not a coincidence, but since Xiangjun didn't say, she wouldn't ask.

"From now on, the Noble Lady must take me with her wherever she goes," Mengmei said.

"Alright, I'll take Sister Mengmei with me wherever I go from now on."

Mengmei looked at her shameless expression and pinched her face, not in a good mood, "The Noble Lady should talk less. Your voice is hoarse."

"Mhm! I know!"

...

The next news about the Second Prince came two days later.

The Second Prince was quite seriously injured, but he had woken up. However, the Second Prince had still injured his internal organs, and it would take a long time for him to recover.

This was already a great fortune amidst the misfortune.

Another day passed, and it was the day for all the palace concubines to pay their respects to the Empress.

Today, Noble Consort Gu had not come again, still resting in her Ganlu Palace to protect her pregnancy, so the leftmost position was still empty.

Xiangjun was now a titled Noble Lady and no longer had to sit at the very end.

As soon as she took her seat, she felt gazes coming from all directions.

Everyone knew that Noble Lady Lian had risked her life to save the Second Prince. To be honest, even if they knew that saving the Second Prince would bring great benefits, no one would truly risk their life for someone else's son.

Everyone felt that this Noble Lady Lian not only had a good temper but was also too kind-hearted.

Only Qin Zhao Yi felt uncomfortable in her heart. Why hadn't she burned to death? Even if she didn't burn to death, it would have been good if the vixen's face had been disfigured...

Before long, Fang Mama and Chun Mama accompanied the Empress as she walked over.

After everyone had paid their respects, the Empress first looked at Xiangjun and gently asked, "Is Noble Lady Lian's body better now? I wanted to visit you, but the Second Prince hasn't recovered yet, so I could only send Chun Mama to check on you."

Xiangjun immediately stood up and bowed, "This concubine is fine. How dare I trouble Your Majesty to worry about me."

"Sit down quickly. There's no need for you to bow to me every time."

After Xiangjun sat down, the Empress solemnly said, "Noble Lady Lian has merited by saving the imperial son. After discussing with the Emperor, we have decided to promote Noble Lady Lian's rank. From now on, Noble Lady Lian will be Noble Consort Lian."

As soon as the Empress spoke, everyone was surprised.

Even Xiangjun was somewhat shocked.

Sure enough, the Empress was still the most generous, promoting her three ranks at once!

She had originally thought it would be at most a Concubine or a Noble Concubine.

Xiangjun excitedly knelt down to the Empress, as if afraid that the Empress would regret it, and performed a grand gesture of gratitude to the Empress.

"You, look at you, too well-mannered." The Empress smiled and had Fang Mama help Xiangjun up.

The Empress saw the expressions of the other concubines.

Today, she had elevated Xiangjun not only because she had saved her only legitimate son but also because she and Noble Consort Gui were now in a life-and-death struggle.

Her father had already investigated clearly that the accident with the Second Prince was not an accident at all, but the work of the Right Prime Minister, Song Feijing.

It was done to make way for the child in Noble Consort Gui's womb to become the Crown Prince.

Today, she wanted to elevate Xiangjun to let everyone in the palace know that if they sided with her, they could rise rapidly through the ranks. Even if they were just a lowly merchant's daughter, she could elevate them to a position they shouldn't normally reach.

Xiangjun sat down happily, ignoring the envious, jealous, and onlookers' gazes.

The palace concubines all felt that Noble Consort Lian was truly lucky. A small family woman from Jiangnan, with a father who was just a merchant, and not a single imperial official in her family's three generations of direct and collateral relatives, had actually come this far.

But after all, she had saved the Empress's legitimate son, which was a merit to the nation. As long as the Empress wanted to elevate her, it wasn't excessive. After all, a Noble Consort was still not a main position in a palace.

Qin Zhao Yi had never liked Xiangjun. The fact that Noble Consort Lian had made fun of her accent was something Qin Zhao Yi had not yet retaliated for.

So, Qin Zhao Yi said sarcastically, "Noble Consort Lian is truly lucky. The Wenyuange Pavilion is so far from your Chengxiang Hall. How come you were the first to arrive at the fire scene to save the Second Prince? We don't have your good fortune."

chapters.title: Who Else is Behind You?
chapters.content:
Qin Zhaoyi was truly vicious. She spoke as if Xiangjun had known all along that the Second Prince would be in danger.

But now that Xiangjun had the Empress’s support, she would no longer bow her head as she once had.

"Consort Zhao, which *dian* are you referring to?" Xiangjun asked.

The crowd couldn’t help but burst into laughter. Qin Zhaoyi was so furious that she pointed at Xiangjun. "You! How dare you!"

"Enough, what an undignified commotion," the Empress said with a helpless glance at Xiangjun, who immediately lowered her head in grievance and fell silent.

The Empress then glared at Qin Zhaoyi.

"Consort Zhao, just because you don’t read doesn’t mean no one else does. Consort Lian visits the Wenyuan Pavilion every day to read the imperial archives. His Majesty has permitted this."

In truth, the Empress had initially been suspicious of how Xiangjun had saved the Second Prince.

But after investigating, she confirmed that Xiangjun had gone to the Wenyuan Pavilion because the Emperor had allowed her to read there. Xiangjun’s family had no connection to Song Feijing, and the incident had indeed been a coincidence.

If she hadn’t been there that day, her Second Prince might have been lost.

With the Empress’s glare, Qin Zhaoyi had no choice but to shut her mouth.

She shot a venomous look at the smug Xiangjun, wishing she could tear that face apart.

So what if she had the Empress’s backing? Anyone could curry favor with the Empress!

"Where is Noble Consort Rong? Why hasn’t she come today?"

Seeing that no one answered, the Empress let out a cold laugh. She turned to Wan Niangzi, who was sitting next to Xiangjun, and asked, "Wan Niangzi, has Noble Consort Rong not come again today?"

Xiangjun could clearly sense Wan Niangzi’s momentary hesitation—she was caught off guard.

"In response to Your Majesty the Empress, Noble Consort has not been resting well these days. His Majesty has ordered her to continue her pregnancy in the palace."

"Not resting well?" The Empress’s cold laugh continued, a flicker of malice flashing in her eyes. "Noble Consort *should* take good care of her pregnancy. Wan Niangzi, I have here a sutra blessed by a high monk. After this, take it to the Ganlu Palace for me. Tell your Noble Consort sister that this sutra is my gift to her, to bring blessings to the child in her womb."

Xiangjun glanced at Wan Niangzi, whose face was filled with panic.

In the original story, Wan Niangzi was one of Noble Consort Rong’s people. To be precise, she was Song the Chancellor’s person, but she had entered the palace specifically to protect Noble Consort Rong and do the things the Noble Consort was unwilling or unable to do.

But in the story, her true allegiance wasn’t exposed until much later. So how had the Empress already found out?

Wan Niangzi was clearly flustered. She quickly ordered a palace maid to take the sutra.

After handing over the sutra, the Empress dismissed everyone. Since the Second Prince’s health had not yet fully recovered, she had no mind to waste words on these women of the harem.

...

Xiangjun was overjoyed as she returned to Chengxiang Hall with her head held high.

By the time she returned, the palace servants assigned by the Shangong Bureau had already arrived.

Now that Xiangjun had become a *liangdi* (a high-ranking imperial concubine), she had six palace maids and four eunuchs attending to her.

After Meng Mei and Xiao Luzi had introduced the newly arrived servants to Xiangjun, she dismissed them, keeping only Meng Mei and Xiao Luzi behind to give instructions.

"For now, don’t let them serve inside. Observe them for a while longer."

Xiao Luzi quickly replied, "Consort Lian, rest assured. I will investigate thoroughly to prevent any spies from other factions."

Xiangjun trusted Xiao Luzi’s work. Picking up her teacup, she said, "You’ve done well. I won’t mistreat you. In the future, even your clothes will be upgraded."

Xiao Luzi immediately knelt down, grinning as he thanked his mistress.

The implication was clear—upgrading Xiao Luzi’s clothes meant that once Xiangjun became the mistress of her own palace, she could promote him to a higher-ranking eunuch position. His current minor eunuch’s attire would be replaced with that of a chief eunuch.

"Then Xiao Luzi wishes Consort Lian every success!" Xiao Luzi said with a wide smile.

Xiangjun also smiled smugly.

She knew her flaw was that she tended to get carried away when she was happy, but surely it was fine to enjoy a little happiness in her own palace?

"Consort Lian truly has great ambition." A voice came from the doorway.

Xiangjun looked over and saw that it was Gu Tingxue, who had come with another imperial reward.

"Eunuch Gu, why have you come?"

"I’ve come to deliver His Majesty’s reward. Congratulations, Consort Lian."

Xiangjun waved her hand, and Meng Mei and Xiao Luzi led the other eunuchs away to store the Emperor’s reward in the treasury.

Gu Tingxue entered the room, gave a slight nod—his way of greeting Xiangjun.

"Greetings, Consort Lian. In just three months, you’ve risen from a *meiren* (a low-ranking concubine) to a *liangdi*. There is no other concubine in this palace who has achieved as much as you."

"All thanks to Eunuch Gu’s information. If you hadn’t told me that the Second Prince liked to play near the Wenyuan Pavilion, how would I have had the chance to save him?"

Gu Tingxue walked over to the *kang* table where Xiangjun was seated and sat down without hesitation. He picked up the teacup on the table and took a sip.

"What are you doing? That’s my tea," Xiangjun said.

"Before, whenever I came, Consort Lian would pour me tea herself. Perhaps now that you’ve risen in rank, even a cup of tea is beneath you when I visit."

Xiangjun was momentarily speechless, unsure how she had offended him. She had no choice but to stand up and pour Gu Tingxue a cup of tea herself.

"Please, Eunuch."

Gu Tingxue took the cup but didn’t drink. Instead, he placed it on the *kang* table.

Xiangjun couldn’t afford to offend Gu Tingxue. She hurried to his side, looking aggrieved as she said, "Have I done something wrong? Please enlighten me, Eunuch."

Gu Tingxue lifted his gaze to look at Xiangjun, who was standing so close to him that she seemed boneless, as if she wanted to lean her entire body against him.

"Stand properly."

Xiangjun pouted, blinking her eyes as she straightened up.

Even with her head lowered, she could still feel his gaze on her. But Gu Tingxue’s eyes held no warmth—his cold, damp stare made her shiver all over.

How did she get the feeling… that Gu Tingxue wanted to kill her again?

"Forgive my poor eyesight, but I didn’t realize Your Highness had such foresight that you could even see through Chancellor Song’s arrangements."

Xiangjun tilted her head, feigning confusion. "What arrangements of Chancellor Song’s? Eunuch Gu, I don’t understand what you’re saying."

Gu Tingxue’s sharp, sinister gaze remained fixed on Xiangjun, missing none of her expressions.

"From the very beginning, when you asked me to investigate the Second Prince, did you already know what would happen? Speak. Who do you *really* serve?"

"How could I have known what would happen? I’m no immortal! Saving the Second Prince was truly a coincidence. I never expected things to turn out this way. As for who I serve—Eunuch, don’t you already know? I was the one *you* brought into the palace."

It was precisely because Xiangjun had been brought into the palace by Gu Tingxue himself, and her identity had been crafted by him, that he now felt a chill run down his spine.

What kind of power could deceive his eyes, evade the investigations of his surveillance network, and secretly pass messages to Xiangjun?

"Eunuch, Xiao Luzi himself said that there’s nothing in this palace you don’t know. Whether I have someone behind me or not—don’t you already know?"

Gu Tingxue’s logic told him that Xiangjun had no one behind her.

But his instincts screamed that it couldn’t be that simple.

"Is that so?" Gu Tingxue still regarded her with that sinister expression.

Xiangjun was terrified inside.

She couldn’t think too much about it. She grabbed Gu Tingxue’s hand.

"If I *do* have someone behind me, that person is *you*, Eunuch Gu. Think about it—if there really was someone powerful enough to hide from you, why would I struggle so hard for a concubine’s rank? If I had such a powerful backer, why would I risk my life rushing into that fire? I could have just asked them for help. Everything I’ve done, hasn’t it all been to earn *your* favor? Why don’t you trust me?"

---

chapters.title: The Empress Dowager’s Birthday Banquet
chapters.content:
Xiangjun blinked, and tears immediately welled up and fell.

Gu Tingxue suddenly felt a soft sensation in his palm. His eyes widened slightly as he saw that Xiangjun had pressed his hand against her chest.

"Eunuch Gu, feel my heart. See if I’m lying to you."

Gu Tingxue abruptly pulled his hand back, his ears turning red against his will.

"If you’re not, then you’re not. Don’t be so handsy."

Gu Tingxue stood up, ready to leave, but Xiangjun suddenly wrapped her arms around him from behind.

"You… let go!"

Xiangjun held onto Gu Tingxue, her voice aggrieved. "Eunuch Gu, are you leaving just because you’ve wronged me? I won’t allow it."

Gu Tingxue broke free from her grasp and took several steps back, as if fleeing from the plague.

"What do you want?"

Xiangjun pouted, still clinging to him. "Eunuch Gu, don’t you even care if I’m injured? How is my recovery? I’m so heartbroken… I thought that after all this time, I had grown close to you…"

Gu Tingxue sighed helplessly. "Your condition is something I don’t need to ask to know."

"Is that so?" Xiangjun took a step forward, pressing closer to Gu Tingxue. Her bright eyes locked onto his. "Have you been secretly asking others about my health, Eunuch? Do you care about me?"

Gu Tingxue deliberately darkened his expression and took a step back. "Consort Lian, do not speak nonsense."

Xiangjun suppressed her smile, carefully observing Gu Tingxue’s expression.

Sure enough, an unnatural flush crept across his face.

In truth, Xiangjun had thought long and hard about Gu Tingxue.

Even with the Empress Dowager’s trust and the Emperor’s favor, he was only nineteen. To hold so much power—both the Surveillance Bureau and the Divine Strategy Army—he must be busy every day, barely having time to indulge in women.

Moreover, Gu Tingxue seemed like the kind of man who held himself to high standards.

Such a man would not easily open his heart, nor would he give in to base desires.

So…

Gu Tingxue probably hadn’t been with many women.

Even if he was a powerful eunuch, he was still only nineteen. She had lived two lifetimes—surely there were one or two things she could handle better than him.

For example… matters between men and women.

"Eunuch Gu, has anyone ever told you that you’re very handsome? Many palace maids must like you, right?"

Gu Tingxue coldly scoffed. "No."

The palace servants were all terrified of him.

"Really? Then you must be too intimidating. If you smiled more, I’m sure many palace maids would throw themselves at you."

"I am a eunuch. No palace maid would degrade herself by throwing herself at me."

So insecure?

Xiangjun stomped her foot, pouting in anger. "Eunuch Gu, why are you insulting me?"

"When did I insult you?" Gu Tingxue asked, bewildered.

"Just now! You said that anyone who throws themselves at you is degrading themselves. But *I’ve* thrown myself at you so many times!"

"You…" Gu Tingxue was momentarily speechless. He could only pretend to be disdainful, coldly scoffing. "Consort Lian, for the sake of climbing higher, you really are willing to do anything."

"Who says I only throw myself at you to climb higher? The words I said when I first met you—*I still mean them*."

Xiangjun reached out to hook her fingers into Gu Tingxue’s belt, but he slapped her hand away.

"I still have to leave the palace to attend to His Majesty’s business. I’ll take my leave."

"Wait! Eunuch Gu, there’s still something you haven’t done for me!"

"What does Consort Lian command?"

"In a few days, it will be the Empress Dowager’s birthday. I don’t know what she likes, so please help me pick a gift that suits my status and will make Her Highness happy."

Gu Tingxue’s face darkened. "You really don’t plan to use your own brain at all, do you?"

"Eunuch Gu, can you please…?"

"Fine."

With that, Gu Tingxue turned and left without another word.

Xiangjun was delighted and couldn’t help but lie down on her *guifei* couch, basking in her triumph.

She suddenly realized that teasing Gu Tingxue like this was… quite enjoyable.

...

The following days in the palace were calm.

Noble Consort Rong kept to herself, while the Empress devoted all her attention to the Second Prince.

With both of them occupied, the Emperor, heeding the Empress’s recommendation, granted De Consort and Qin Zhaoyi the authority to oversee the Six Palaces. They were put in charge of organizing this year’s birthday banquet for the Empress Dowager.

Both De Consort and Qin Zhaoyi pulled out all the stops, each hoping to use this opportunity to gain favor with the Empress Dowager.

On the day of the banquet, Xiangjun finally saw Noble Consort Rong, whom she hadn’t laid eyes on in a long time.

Noble Consort Rong was now four months pregnant. Perhaps because good fortune had a way of invigorating the spirit, her complexion actually looked better than it had before her pregnancy.

*How infuriating.*

Li Gengyi was now eight months along. Because she had been eating properly these past months, her health had improved, and she had gained some weight. Her belly no longer looked as alarming as it once had.

The two of them arrived together, one pregnant woman after another—an undeniably eye-catching sight.

Xiangjun overheard two concubines whispering nearby:

"Is there some special *feng shui* in Ganlu Palace? One after another, they’ve all gotten pregnant!"

"Hmph, what *feng shui*? If His Majesty visits, then pregnancy follows. Those of us who don’t even see His Majesty once a year—how could we have Noble Consort’s luck?"

Listening to their snide remarks, Xiangjun knew that Noble Consort Rong had incurred the resentment of the others.

Li Gengyi’s seat was some distance from Xiangjun’s. She smiled at Xiangjun from afar before taking her seat.

After all the concubines were seated, the Empress Dowager, the Emperor, and the Empress finally arrived at the banquet.

This was the first time Xiangjun had ever seen the Empress Dowager in this life.

Of course, in her past life, she hadn’t seen her many times either—only once or twice after giving birth, when she had been granted an audience.

Though the Empress Dowager was now elderly, traces of her legendary beauty from her youth were still visible.

The Empress Dowager’s life had truly been extraordinary.

She had started as an ordinary palace maid, but after being favored by the late Emperor, she was promoted to a concubine within three years. From then on, she became the sole favorite, and the late Emperor had barely been able to bear being apart from her.

But when she had accompanied the late Emperor on a campaign against the Mongolian Tatars in the north, she had been captured while saving him.

At that time, the current Emperor had been only nine years old.

The Empress Dowager had spent seven years as a captive among the Tatars before being rescued and brought back to the capital.

Everyone had assumed that this once-beloved concubine would fade into obscurity, but to everyone’s surprise, she not only retained the late Emperor’s favor but also rose step by step to the position of Empress, helping her son, the Sixth Prince, ascend to the throne.

However, this legendary "Sorceress Empress," after her son became Emperor, gradually withdrew from political influence, showing no attachment to power.

Now, she devoted herself to Buddhism, lived in seclusion, and rarely received the other concubines. Only the Emperor, the Empress, and that *Gu* official had regular access to her.

Xiangjun was intently studying the Empress Dowager when she suddenly felt a glare piercing through her.

She looked over and saw Gu Tingxue following beside the Empress Dowager, glaring at her.

Only then did Xiangjun realize that her gaze at the Empress Dowager had been too direct. She quickly averted her eyes and, along with everyone else, rose to pay respects to the three highest figures in the palace.

chapters.title: Sea Eagle
chapters.content:
After everyone was seated, Xiangjun finally stole another glance.

She saw Gu Tingxue standing beside the Empress Dowager, still as straight as a rod.

Today, he wore the qilin robe personally bestowed by the Emperor. To those who didn’t know, they might mistake him for the Emperor’s younger brother.

"Tingxue, you may sit as well," the Empress Dowager said, glancing at Gu Tingxue standing behind her. "You are no longer an ordinary inner attendant. You serve the Emperor in the outer court and are a dignified official. Go sit below."

The Emperor’s expression visibly stiffened.

Gu Tingxue smiled and nodded. "Tingxue rarely has the chance to see the Empress Dowager. Today is Your Majesty’s birthday, so let this humble servant take on an extra share of filial piety on the Emperor’s behalf."

Hearing this, the Emperor seemed pleased and said to the Empress Dowager, "Mother, Tingxue wishes to attend to you. Let him stay here. He understands this son’s heart best."

The Empress Dowager sighed helplessly and smiled. "Then do as you wish."

At this moment, the Empress finally rose, leading the concubines in offering toasts and well-wishes to the Empress Dowager.

With the Emperor’s command to begin the feast, the music and dance performances started.

The first half of the banquet’s program was arranged by Concubine De.

Just like Concubine De herself, the program was neither bad nor particularly interesting.

Xiangjun noticed that the Empress Dowager seemed rather uninterested.

Seeing his mother’s indifferent expression, the Emperor’s face darkened.

Noticing this, the Empress immediately suggested, "The concubines of the harem have all prepared gifts for Mother. Would Mother grace us with a look?"

The Empress Dowager nodded, and the Empress had the shoushan stone she prepared brought forward.

The shoushan stone was a natural "longevity" character, and the Empress Dowager finally showed a slight smile.

"Every year, the Empress’s gift is my favorite."

Seeing his mother smile, the Emperor reached out and held the Empress’s hand, displaying the affection between the imperial couple.

Xiangjun glanced at the Noble Consort, who indeed looked displeased.

Deep down, the Noble Consort believed that only she and the Emperor were truly in love. Yet, the Empress was the rightful wife of the Emperor.

Even if the Emperor treated the Noble Consort well, during palace gatherings or when meeting officials and their wives, the Emperor could only and would only stand beside the Empress.

This was the Noble Consort’s hidden sorrow.

The maid behind the Noble Consort, Caiwei, whispered, "Noble Consort, it’s your turn to present the gift to the Empress Dowager."

The Noble Consort then composed herself, rose gracefully with a smile, and presented her birthday gift to the Empress Dowager—

A falconer entered the great hall with a white sea eagle.

The Empress Dowager’s body visibly trembled.

Years ago, when the Empress Dowager returned from the Northern Mongolia, she had brought back a white sea eagle. She adored it and always fed it herself.

But later, that sea eagle was killed by an arrow from the late Emperor’s Empress. The Empress Dowager had been heartbroken for a long time.

The Noble Consort was indeed skilled at gift-giving. Today’s gift was likely unmatched; even the Empress’s expression turned sour.

But the Empress Dowager did not speak. Instead, she first glanced at her son.

Observing the Empress Dowager’s expression, Xiangjun suddenly had a revelation and thought of something.

The sea eagle was only found in the northern grasslands. How could the Noble Consort, a woman deep in the palace, obtain one? It must have been sent from the north.

Who was in the north?

Wasn’t the Emperor’s ninth brother, the mighty General Wang, there?

So, this sea eagle must have been obtained for the Noble Consort by General Wang.

Only General Wang had the means to get a sea eagle identical to the one the Empress Dowager had raised years ago and safely transport it all the way to the capital.

How could someone as shrewd as the Empress Dowager not see through this?

That was why she didn’t speak but first looked at her son.

Sure enough, the Emperor’s face darkened instantly, his expression stormy and suffocating.

The Noble Consort, however, remained oblivious and smiled at the Empress Dowager. "Mother, this concubine knows you once raised a sea eagle and cherished it deeply. So, I specially found this similar one, hoping to bring a smile to Mother’s face."

The Emperor looked at the Empress Dowager. Mother and son exchanged a glance, both understanding each other’s thoughts.

This mother and son truly had a deep understanding.

They both feared the General Wang in the north—the late Emperor’s son, commanding a powerful army, secretly connected to the Noble Consort in the palace, and not to mention, the Noble Consort was carrying the imperial heir.

No emperor could tolerate this.

But the Empress Dowager also knew that the Emperor loved the Noble Consort dearly, like the apple of his eye, so she couldn’t reprimand her directly. She could only subtly admonish her.

"It’s thoughtful of you. But I am old now, how can I still train a sea eagle? I think..."

The Empress Dowager looked around and then at Gu Tingxue behind her.

"Tingxue, the Emperor has put you in charge of the Censorate and the Shence Army, and now even the Privy Council. I think this sea eagle should be rewarded to you. It suits your status."

The Emperor’s expression improved significantly, feeling somewhat relieved.

The Noble Consort, however, was at a loss and humiliated.

No matter how dignified Gu Tingxue was, he was still a eunuch.

The Empress Dowager had taken the Noble Consort’s carefully prepared gift and given it to Gu Tingxue. Wasn’t this a slap in her face?

Gu Tingxue quickly stepped forward to express his gratitude and then, with a smile, returned to the Empress Dowager’s side.

The Noble Consort felt extremely wronged, but since it was the Empress Dowager’s birthday banquet, she couldn’t make a scene. She could only force a smile and return to her seat.

"Also..." the Empress Dowager called the Noble Consort again, "Noble Consort Rong still needs to learn the rules. In the harem, only the Empress can address me as 'Mother.' Don’t get it wrong."

Noble Consort Rong’s body swayed, almost unable to stand.

She had always addressed the Empress Dowager as "Mother," but today, in front of so many people, the Empress Dowager had humiliated her. She didn’t know what she had done wrong.

Noble Consort Rong looked at the Emperor, but the Emperor was also looking at her with a reproachful gaze. She wished she could cry immediately.

The Empress barely contained her laughter and softly said, "Noble Consort Rong, the Empress Dowager is teaching you out of care."

"Yes, this concubine understands. Thank you for the Empress Dowager’s guidance."

Supported by Caiwei, the Noble Consort sat down. For the rest of the banquet, she didn’t say another word, sitting there like a statue.

Next, the concubines from various palaces presented their gifts according to their ranks.

Fortunately, no more incidents occurred.

Finally, it was Xiangjun’s turn.

Xiangjun walked out holding a pipa and gracefully bowed. "This concubine, Lian Liangdi from Chengxiang Hall, greets the Empress Dowager. May the Empress Dowager have eternal life and boundless joy."

The Empress Dowager’s gaze fell on the pipa Xiangjun was holding.

The Emperor’s face stiffened again.

When the Empress Dowager was young, she was most skilled at playing the pipa. But when she was trapped in Tartary, she suffered greatly, and after returning, she could no longer play.

To avoid upsetting the Empress Dowager, the Emperor had decreed that at any banquet where the Empress Dowager was present, there would be no pipa performances.

Everyone was waiting to see Xiangjun make a fool of herself.

Sure enough, a woman without a prominent family background wouldn’t know the Empress Dowager’s taboos.

The Emperor also blamed her somewhat.

How could both the Noble Consort and the concubines close to her be so out of touch?

chapters.title: Pipa as a Birthday Gift
chapters.content:
Xiangjun also sensed the subtle atmosphere around her.

She naturally knew the Empress Dowager’s taboo—this wasn’t her first life.

But Gu Tingxue had told Xiangjun that the Empress Dowager didn’t like the pipa because her pipa skills had once been unparalleled in the world. After injuring her hand, she could no longer play. If she couldn’t hear the best, she’d rather not hear it at all.

Xiangjun was very doubtful whether her pipa skills could satisfy the Empress Dowager. She didn’t think her pipa skills were at the unparalleled level.

But Gu Tingxue had said, "It doesn’t matter. If your pipa skills were truly unparalleled, the Empress Dowager would be even more dissatisfied. The way you are now is best. She will like it."

Thinking that she should trust him, she had to harden her head and go through with it.

"I would like to play a piece for the Empress Dowager to celebrate Your Majesty’s sacred birthday."

The Emperor didn’t blame Xiangjun. After all, she was from Jiangnan and not from a prominent family, so it was understandable that she didn’t know the Empress Dowager’s taboos.

"Lian Liangdi, Mother doesn’t like the pipa. You may withdraw."

Xiangjun looked at the Empress Dowager, who didn’t seem to have any intention of speaking.

This wasn’t right! Xiangjun quickly glanced at Gu Tingxue. Could he be deliberately setting her up?

Gu Tingxue just calmly looked at Xiangjun, with a slight smile at the corner of his mouth.

Could he really be setting her up?

Xiangjun felt extremely wronged and, with a tearful face, was about to leave with her pipa when she suddenly heard, "Wait."

The Empress Dowager smiled at the Emperor and said, "It’s been many years since I last heard the pipa. Today, I’d like to listen. Emperor, let Lian Liangdi play a piece."

"Yes, this son obeys Mother."

With a glance from the Emperor, someone quickly brought a stool for Xiangjun.

"Lian Liangdi, since Mother wants to listen, you may play."

Xiangjun let out a sigh of relief and quickly sat down with her pipa.

"Do you know how to play *Eighteen Songs of a Nomad Flute*?" the Empress Dowager suddenly asked.

"Yes, I do."

"Then play that piece."

After Xiangjun finished playing, the entire palace fell silent. Even the Emperor was somewhat surprised.

"Although it may not compare to Mother’s skills from back then, Lian Liangdi’s pipa skills are the best in the palace," the Emperor said.

The Empress Dowager also slowly came back to her senses, with a hint of melancholy in her eyes.

The Empress Dowager nodded and praised, "Finally, there is a talented woman among the Emperor’s concubines."

At these words, the Empress couldn’t help but laugh again, her gaze once more falling on the Noble Consort below.

Everyone knew that Noble Consort Rong had always considered herself a talented woman of the capital, but the Empress Dowager had never liked her. This statement was a clear sarcasm, implying that the Noble Consort was not a talented woman at all.

As long as she could embarrass the Noble Consort, the Empress was more than happy.

So, the Empress immediately said, "Mother may not know, but Lian Liangdi’s calligraphy is also excellent. Nowadays, the young ladies of the capital are all learning to write in Lian Liangdi’s style. The Emperor even bestowed a name on her calligraphy, calling it 'Lianhua Xiaozi.' This has already become a famous story among the people."

The Empress glanced at the Noble Consort again. As expected, her face was extremely unpleasant, as if she wanted to cry at any moment.

"Oh? Then I would like to see it for myself."

Xiangjun quickly knelt on the ground and said, "I have heard that the Empress Dowager is devoutly Buddhist. Xiangjun is willing to copy Buddhist scriptures for the Empress Dowager every day."

"You are quite filial. Then you may come to my palace often," the Empress Dowager paused and added, "and bring your pipa with you."

Xiangjun quickly knelt to express her gratitude and then, knowing when to stop, obediently returned to her seat with the pipa.

For the rest of the banquet, there was nothing that concerned Xiangjun.

Having accomplished her most important task, she began to fully enjoy the food, drinks, and performances.

In her previous life, Xiangjun had always been scheming against Noble Consort Rong, but no matter what she did, Noble Consort Rong remained firmly in her position. Instead, Xiangjun herself had gradually fallen out of the Emperor’s favor.

In this life, Xiangjun had realized that the key to dealing with Noble Consort Rong lay with the Emperor, so she was no longer in a hurry.

Thus, she could now truly enjoy the banquet.

The second half of the banquet’s program was arranged by Consort Qin. It had to be said that Consort Qin had gone all out this time.

No one knew where she had obtained an elephant. The beast trainer’s performance with the elephant was quite interesting, and even Xiangjun couldn’t help but applaud.

Moreover, Consort Qin had changed her clothes and personally taken the stage, lying on the ground and letting the elephant press her body with its foot. This terrified everyone, leaving them breathless.

After the performance, the Empress Dowager seemed very pleased and rewarded Consort Qin generously.

The Emperor also watched with delight and praised her warmly.

Thus, after the banquet, the Emperor went to the Nuanxuan Hall to accompany Consort Qin.

As he left with Consort Qin, he didn’t even glance at Noble Consort Rong.

Tsk tsk, these two were likely to have another conflict soon.

As for Consort De, after all her hard work, she received neither rewards nor praise. She was so angry that her nose was almost crooked.

...

Xiangjun left the place of strife early.

She had drunk a bit too much today, so after the banquet ended, she went to Taiye Pool to get some air and sober up.

Xiyu, fearing that Xiangjun might catch a cold, went back to fetch a thicker cloak for her, leaving only Mengmei to accompany her.

It was at this moment that Gu Tingxue arrived.

Gu Tingxue gave Mengmei a look, and she stepped aside to keep watch for the two of them.

Xiangjun sat by the pool, her face flushed, whether from the cold or the alcohol.

"Eunuch Tingxue, why have you come? Have you also drunk too much?"

Gu Tingxue didn’t bother with pleasantries. He directly grabbed Xiangjun and pushed her onto a small boat beside Taiye Pool.

Xiangjun was shoved into the boat and fell with a thud onto the deck.

Wherever she fell, she stayed there, shifting slightly before lying down on the carpet inside the boat to rest.

Gu Tingxue lifted the curtain and entered.

Seeing Xiangjun lying on the floor, he helplessly pulled her up and placed her on the seat.

Drunkard...

"Does Eunuch Tingxue have something to tell me?" Xiangjun asked, tilting her head wearily.

"What were you doing at the banquet today?"

"What did I do? Didn’t I perform well today?" Xiangjun blinked. "Was my pipa playing not good?"

"I’m not talking about your pipa," Gu Tingxue said.

"Then what is it?"

Gu Tingxue said irritably, "At the banquet, why were you always looking at me?"

Xiangjun, with the alcohol affecting her, propped up her eyelids and asked in confusion, "What’s wrong with me looking at you?"

"Do you not know how many eyes are in the harem? Looking at me in front of so many people—are you afraid that others won’t know we’re connected?"

Xiangjun covered her mouth with a handkerchief and let out a giggle. Whether it was because of the alcohol or not, the more she laughed, the louder she became, laughing so hard that she swayed from side to side.

Gu Tingxue, fearing they might be discovered, directly covered Xiangjun’s mouth with his hand.

"What are you laughing at?"

Xiangjun held Gu Tingxue’s hand and removed it from her mouth. With a smile, she said, "Of course, I’m laughing at Eunuch Tingxue being so handsome yet unaware of it. Many people look at you, not just me. It would be strange if I didn’t look at you at all."

chapters.title: The Empress Dowager's Guidance
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue was rarely left speechless.

"You... what nonsense are you talking? Do you think everyone is as lustful as you?"

"Lustful in what way?" Xiangjun said indifferently, "You don't understand. The deep palace is lonely; countless concubines and palace maids are buried here for life. All the women in the harem revolve around the emperor alone every day, and they are all weary at heart. It's rare to have such a young and handsome eunuch; who wouldn't want to take a few more glances?"

"But you are the emperor's favored concubine, not a neglected palace woman."

"So what? Isn't Noble Consort Guifei more favored than me? I saw Noble Consort Guifei smiling at you too. I haven't even smiled at you; I've been very restrained."

As she spoke, Xiangjun moved closer to Gu Tingxue, their noses almost touching.

Gu Tingxue wanted to retreat, but the cabin was narrow, and he had nowhere to go.

Xiangjun squinted at Gu Tingxue and said, "It's strange. So many people look at you, Eunuch, but you only notice me looking at you. I wonder, is it because Eunuch cares especially about me, or is Eunuch just feeling guilty?"

The peculiar fragrance from Xiangjun that irritated Gu Tingxue surged into his nose again, making his mind chaotic.

He pushed Xiangjun away, lifted the curtain, and left.

"What a weird man..." Xiangjun yawned, feeling a wave of drowsiness, and directly collapsed onto the boat, falling asleep.

...

When Xiangjun woke up again, she was already back in her own Chengxiang Palace.

Meng Mei was on night duty today. Seeing Xiangjun getting out of bed, she quickly climbed off the heated brick bed to pour water for her.

Xiangjun drank the water and asked, "I remember I fell asleep on the boat. How did I get back?"

Meng Mei hesitated.

"What's wrong?"

"It... it was Eunuch Gu who carried you back."

"Ah?" Xiangjun was puzzled. "Didn't he leave in a huff?"

Meng Mei finally understood.

No wonder she saw Eunuch Gu lift the curtain and leave with a red face—he had been angered by her mistress!

"Eunuch Gu did leave at first, but after about the time it takes to drink half a cup of tea, he came back for some reason. Seeing that the mistress was asleep, he carried you back. If it weren't for Eunuch Gu, I wouldn't have known how to get you back. I would have had to wait for Xiyu to return before going back to the palace to call for help."

Xiangjun handed the cup to Meng Mei and flopped back into the blankets, but she couldn't fall asleep again.

She just stared at the mosquito net with her bright eyes, lost in thought.

Meng Mei had seen this look on Xiangjun many times. Every time she looked like this, she was up to no good.

Meng Mei sighed, blew out the candle, and lay back down.

She could only pray for Gu Tingxue.

...

Although she still had a slight hangover, early the next morning, Xiangjun hugged her pipa and went to wait at the Empress Dowager's Ren Shou Palace.

When Xiangjun arrived, the Empress Dowager was just about to have breakfast.

She immediately went to attend to the Empress Dowager, helping her eat and rinse her mouth, remaining quiet and proper throughout.

"You've learned the rules quite well."

"Thank you for the praise, Your Majesty."

The Empress Dowager had a very gentle expression. She took the tea Xiangjun handed over, gently skimming the foam, and asked in a calm voice, "Did you know Tingxue before?"

Xiangjun felt a chill run down her spine.

She finally understood why Gu Tingxue had come to bother her yesterday.

So someone had indeed noticed the eye contact between her and Gu Tingxue.

It was just a glance, yet the Empress Dowager was so perceptive?

Xiangjun quickly recalled what had happened yesterday.

Suddenly, Xiangjun realized the reason why the Empress Dowager had suddenly agreed to listen to her performance yesterday...

Could it be that the Empress Dowager had captured her glance at Gu Tingxue?

Thinking of this, Xiangjun decided not to tell any lies, but neither would she tell the whole truth.

Xiangjun, with an unchanged expression, said, "This concubine was selected to enter the palace by Eunuch Tingxue. Her Majesty the Empress praised me for learning the rules well because, before entering the palace, Eunuch Tingxue had invited a matron to teach me etiquette."

"Was it also his idea for you to play the pipa for my birthday?"

"Yes, this concubine's family has no one who has held office in the capital, so I didn't know Your Majesty's preferences. I asked Eunuch Tingxue for advice."

"He is not a kind person; it's surprising he would help you."

"Perhaps because His Majesty once had this concubine present a calligraphy piece to Eunuch, so he was willing to help me once."

"Have you played the pipa for Tingxue before?"

"Yes, when I was in Jiangnan."

"What did you play?"

"Hegemon Removes His Armor."

The Empress Dowager, who had been smiling, suddenly darkened in expression and sighed softly, murmuring, "No wonder..."

Xiangjun didn't know what riddle the Empress Dowager was solving and pretended she hadn't heard.

"Where is your pipa?" the Empress Dowager asked.

"Meng Mei, my pipa."

Xiangjun glanced at Meng Mei, who was waiting outside. Meng Mei immediately brought Xiangjun's pipa over.

"I would like to hear your 'Hegemon Removes His Armor' as well."

Xiangjun said joyfully, "This concubine would also like to receive Your Majesty's guidance."

Xiangjun held the pipa and sat down, then began to play "Hegemon Removes His Armor" once more.

If it had been in her past life, Xiangjun playing this piece might have been even more sorrowful and grievous.

But now, her heart was filled with resentment towards her fate, which actually suited the mindset of the Hegemon.

The strings rang clear and sharp, the Han soldiers had already taken the land, and the songs of Chu surrounded from all sides.

After the piece ended, Xiangjun even saw the Empress Dowager's eyes turn slightly red.

"Turning the formless into form, uniquely outstanding among all schools." The Empress Dowager said, "You play very well. It's no wonder Tingxue had you perform for my birthday. Your state of mind is indeed different from the other women in the palace."

"Thank you for the praise, Your Majesty. This concubine is overjoyed."

The Empress Dowager gently smiled at Xiangjun, waved her hand, and said, "I am tired. Go and copy the sutras."

Xiangjun didn't dare to say or ask more in front of the Empress Dowager. She obediently went to copy the sutras.

She also had lunch at the Empress Dowager's palace that day.

Since the emperor was filial, the food at the Empress Dowager's palace was even better than that at the emperor's Tai Ji Hall.

Xiangjun had managed to freeload today and ate to her heart's content. Her cute demeanor delighted even the Empress Dowager, who ended up eating an extra bowl of rice.

In the afternoon, Xiangjun continued copying sutras, and she spent the entire day doing so.

For the next half month, Xiangjun went to the Empress Dowager's palace every day to "show filial piety." Even the emperor was moved to action.

When the emperor came to the Empress Dowager's palace to accompany her for a meal, he specifically asked about Xiangjun.

"Mother, do you like Consort Lian very much? You usually don't even see Noble Consort Guifei often, so why are you so attentive to Consort Lian? I heard that you even gave her the pipa that Father Emperor gave you?"

"Are you here to plead on behalf of Noble Consort Guifei?"

The Empress Dowager glanced at her son and truly couldn't believe that this was the emperor she had raised.

For the past half month, the emperor and Noble Consort Guifei seemed to have made up again and were now as inseparable as glue.

"I overthought it, Mother. Son is just curious." The emperor awkwardly touched his nose.

"I simply feel that she is teachable, so I have given her a few pointers. If Your Majesty disapproves, I will send her back."

"Son has no such intention."

As they were speaking, Xiangjun arrived.

Xiangjun greeted the Empress Dowager and the emperor, then stood properly to the side to attend to the Empress Dowager's meal, obediently saying, "I am late today."

"It's not your fault. Today, the emperor came, so breakfast was a bit earlier."

The emperor hadn't seen Xiangjun in a long time either.

Xiangjun was usually coquettish and charming in front of him, but it was rare to see her so obedient.

Perhaps because she was attending to the Empress Dowager, Xiangjun was dressed simply and fresh today, her skin tender, and with her quiet demeanor, she somewhat resembled a girl who had not yet married.

The emperor's heart stirred, and he said, "It was my fault, not yours. Today, I will go to Chengxiang Palace to see you."

Xiangjun, while serving dishes to the Empress Dowager, revealed a shy smile. Then, without warning, as soon as she heard these words, Xiangjun covered her mouth and retched.

chapters.title: First Pregnancy
chapters.content:
The Empress Dowager's maid, Wulan, immediately stepped forward to support Xiangjun.

"What's wrong with Consort Lian?" Wulan asked.

Xiangjun's face was pale. "I don't know why, but the smell of this fresh fish is a bit unpleasant. I usually don't feel this way..."

The Empress Dowager and Wulan exchanged a glance. The Empress Dowager quickly said, "Quickly, call the imperial physician."

Xiangjun lay on the Guifei couch as the imperial physician took her pulse.

The imperial physician's face showed joy. He immediately knelt on the ground and reported to the emperor and empress, "Congratulations, Your Majesty, congratulations, Your Majesty the Empress Dowager. Consort Lian has been pregnant for more than a month."

The emperor was overjoyed. "Really?"

"Although Consort Lian's pregnancy is still in the early stages, she has indeed been pregnant for more than a month. However, Consort Lian's fetal condition is unstable, and she needs to rest well."

The emperor burst into laughter. Previously, he had few children, but this year, three concubines had become pregnant. How could he not be pleased?

Let those old fools in the imperial court say whatever they wanted!

The Empress Dowager also happily rewarded Xiangjun with many gifts.

But Xiangjun waited for a long time and did not receive any other decrees. It seemed that neither the emperor nor the Empress Dowager intended to promote her rank.

These mother and son were so stingy; only Her Majesty the Empress was generous!

Because Xiangjun's pregnancy was not yet stable, the emperor granted her a sedan chair to ride back. The Empress Dowager also told her to take good care of her pregnancy and come to Ren Shou Palace to see her after the child was born.

So Xiangjun, carrying a pile of rewards, sat in the sedan chair and returned with a heart full of worries.

At noon, the emperor came to see her again, saying that he would send more rewards later.

However, since Xiangjun was now with child, she could not serve in the bedchamber, so naturally, the emperor would not come in the evening.

That was good. Xiangjun couldn't wait to serve that dog emperor less.

...

The news of Xiangjun's pregnancy soon spread.

After all, it was diagnosed in the Empress Dowager's palace, and the emperor was present. The Imperial Hospital was not airtight, and those with intentions could easily find out.

Soon, the empress and the various palace consorts sent rewards and gifts.

But there was still no promotion in rank!

In the evening, Xiangjun sat on the Guifei couch, eating walnuts and sulking. Gu Tingxue arrived with the emperor's rewards.

Gu Tingxue was followed by a line of young eunuchs, each carrying trays filled with the emperor's rewards, but Xiangjun didn't even glance at them.

"Thank you for your hard work, Eunuch." Xiangjun said lazily, "Meng Mei, put them away."

Meng Mei and Xiao Luzi led the young eunuchs to store the emperor's rewards. Gu Tingxue still stood there, not leaving.

Xiangjun, disheartened, asked, "Does Eunuch Tingxue have anything else to say?"

"Does Consort Lian not want to ask if His Majesty has any other decrees?"

Xiangjun perked up immediately, sitting up straight with an expectant look on her face. "His Majesty has more decrees?"

"No."

Xiangjun rolled her eyes and angrily lay back down.

Gu Tingxue found her inability to remain calm amusing.

He continued, "It's just that His Majesty mentioned to this humble servant that he intends to make Consort Lian the mistress of a palace. However, His Majesty cares for Consort Lian and thinks that Consort Lian's rank has risen too quickly recently. Moreover, since she is carrying an imperial heir, he is afraid that Consort Lian will become a target for public criticism. So, he plans to wait until Consort Lian gives birth before promoting her rank."

Xiangjun didn't believe it. That dog emperor would never consider her feelings!

The dog emperor should have used Xiangjun as a living target to shield Noble Consort Guifei from the open and hidden arrows in the harem!

There must be something wrong here.

"Is Consort Lian happy?"

"Happy my..." Xiangjun restrained her urge to curse, puffing her cheeks angrily and muttering, "Waiting until the child is born, who knows how long that will take? So stingy!"

All her efforts to gain favor were wasted!

Xiangjun saw Gu Tingxue trying to suppress his laughter and immediately changed her expression, putting on a flattering smile. She leaned in and asked, "Once I give birth, I can be promoted to the rank of Pin. Eunuch Tingxue, can't you make an exception?"

"No, our agreement is for half a year. Not a day more, not a day less."

Xiangjun was so angry she could die. Truly, everyone was so stingy!

Gu Tingxue raised an eyebrow and asked, "So, is Consort Lian giving up?"
