"How could I? I won't give up until the very last moment!"

Xiangjun coldly humphed, her eyes filled with defiance, the light in them almost dazzling to Gu Tingxue.

Xiangjun tilted her head back, looking at Gu Tingxue, and stubbornly said, "There's still a month left, isn't there? Eunuch Tingxue, just wait. Xiangjun will definitely not disappoint you."

"This humble servant will wait."

"Eunuch Tingxue must have other duties to attend to. I won't keep you for tea."

Gu Tingxue laughed. She was truly stingy; now that she was angry, she wouldn't even offer him tea.

"This humble servant takes his leave."

Gu Tingxue walked out of Xiangjun's chamber, but before he reached the courtyard gate, he heard a clattering sound from inside—Xiangjun was smashing things.

Soon after, Xiangjun's furious curses could be heard.

Gu Tingxue's smile deepened.

Indeed, no matter how much Consort Lian pretended to have everything under control, she was still just a sixteen or seventeen-year-old girl who couldn't keep her temper.

Gu Tingxue said to Xiyu, who was guarding the door, "Advise your mistress. All this anger is not good for the baby."

Xiyu gave a forced smile. "Thank you for your reminder, Eunuch."

Gu Tingxue left with a smile.

Xiyu was baffled. Why was Eunuch Tingxue so happy when her mistress was throwing a tantrum?

...

Over the next few days, Xiangjun tossed and turned every night, unable to sleep, and was listless during the day.

Moreover, her morning sickness was particularly severe; she vomited almost everything she ate.

Xiangjun was not someone with a good temper to begin with.

In her past life, she could at least run around every day, quarreling and fighting with people, using sarcasm and sharp words to vent her frustration.

In this life, she had to pretend to be honest and pure, which was already stifling. Now, with the torment of morning sickness, her temper was even worse.

However, she didn't punish the palace servants; she just didn't have a good face for anyone.

Meng Mei tried to persuade Xiangjun, "Consort, please drink this blood swallow nest."

"What's the point of drinking it? I'll just vomit it up. I'll give it to you."

"Consort, if you don't eat, how will your body recover? You were good at advising Lady Li, so why can't you take your own advice?"

Xiangjun was so angry she could die. She shouted at Meng Mei, "You only care about the imperial heir in my belly, not me at all! If you don't care about me, go wait outside. I don't want you to attend to me anymore!"

Xiangjun wrapped herself in the blanket, turned her back, and started to cry softly.

Meng Mei didn't know whether to laugh or cry. She quickly tugged at Xiao Luzi and gave him a look, signaling him to quickly coax Consort Lian.

Xiao Luzi immediately stepped forward and tried every means to amuse Xiangjun.

He performed tricks, sang, and even rolled around, finally managing to make Xiangjun stop crying and smile.

But Xiangjun still refused to eat.

Meng Mei had no choice but to secretly call for Physician Liu and told him about Xiangjun's condition.

"Brother, no matter what, you have to find a way to make our Consort able to eat something."

Physician Liu took Xiangjun's pulse, but his expression was somewhat grave.

"What's wrong?" Xiangjun, already too weak from vomiting, said, "Tell me the truth. I'm too tired to keep asking you."

Physician Liu could only say, "Consort's pregnancy is not in a good condition. The contraceptive medicine you took before would have damaged your body. Ideally, you should have recuperated for a year or two before getting pregnant..."

Meng Mei, listening from the side, interrupted Physician Liu anxiously, "Then why did you give Consort the medicine to secure the pregnancy? If you had told me earlier, I would never have let Consort take that medicine."

"Sister, don't be anxious. Consort's physique is better than most people, so at the time, I still gave Consort the medicine to secure the pregnancy. I thought that after Consort became pregnant, with proper care, it would be fine. I just didn't expect..."

"Didn't expect what?" Xiangjun asked.

"Consort, when you saved the Second Prince, you inhaled a lot of black smoke. At that time, you were probably already pregnant with this child. I'm afraid that... the black smoke may have affected this pregnancy."

chapters.title: Morning Sickness
chapters.content:
Physician Liu continued, "If you wish to keep this child, you must be extremely careful. For the next few months, you must not leave your bed, and you must be especially cautious with food and everything you use. Above all, Concubine Liang, remember not to overthink things."

Xiangjun's expression immediately turned serious.

"Keep the matter of my difficult pregnancy to yourself for now," Xiangjun said in a low voice. "Give the prescription to Mengmei. I'll have her secretly prepare the medicine."

"Yes."

Mengmei took the prescription, saw her brother out, and then returned to keep watch over Xiangjun.

Seeing Xiangjun lying in bed, her dark, bright eyes fixed on one spot, Mengmei knew she was lost in thought again.

"Concubine Liang, Physician Liu said you must not overthink. What are you always thinking about? Why won't you tell me? I know I'm not as clever as you, but I can share your burdens."

Suddenly, Xiangjun stared motionlessly at Mengmei, then sat up and grabbed Mengmei's hand.

"Concubine Liang, what's wrong?"

"Mengmei, can you promise me something?"

Mengmei nodded solemnly. "Xiangjun, just say it. No matter what, I will promise."

"Mengmei, promise me that no matter what I do from now on, you will listen to me. Do not act on your own. Even if I were to die, you must not stop me. Do you understand?"

"Why would you want to die? What's happened?" Mengmei exclaimed in distress.

"That was just an example! Just promise me that no matter what I do, even if it seems incomprehensible to you, you will not interfere. Just listen to me, alright?"

Though uneasy, Mengmei still nodded.

"I understand. Rest assured, if I promise you, I will do it. But now you are already Concubine Liang. Once you give birth to a prince, you might even be granted the rank of a consort. Xiangjun, I know you've always been proud and unwilling to be beneath others, but you've already done very well. Why must you climb so high? Sometimes, the higher you climb, the harder you fall. And you..."

Mengmei hesitated before continuing, "Forgive me for saying this, but you are different from the other consorts in the palace. You don't even have anyone to support or help you. One wrong step could lead to irreversible consequences..."

Xiangjun smiled, taking Mengmei's hand.

"I know you mean well, but with my nature, I would rather die than live under someone else's control, unable to grasp my own fate. I will either sit above all or die without a burial place. The only thing I can promise you is that if one day something happens to me, I will ensure a way out for you."

"Xiangjun, don't talk like that..."

Seeing Mengmei on the verge of tears, Xiangjun quickly smiled, patting her hand. "I was just saying that. Don't worry, I will be fine. I will make sure you become the most respected palace maid in this entire palace."

...

Over the next few days, Xiangjun still suffered from severe morning sickness. The Emperor came to visit twice, and seeing her pitiful state, he bestowed many gifts upon her.

To Mengmei's slight relief, Xiangjun was willing to eat again. No matter how uncomfortable she felt, she forced herself to eat every meal. If she vomited, she would eat again.

But watching Xiangjun go through this cycle of eating and vomiting, Mengmei felt heartbroken.

She had no other choice but to steal moments when Xiangjun was asleep to wipe her tears at the doorway.

After a few more days, when Xiangjun had taken the third dose of Physician Liu's medicine, her morning sickness finally eased slightly, and she regained some strength to walk around.

Thinking the weather was nice, Xiangjun decided to visit Concubine Li. Early in the morning, she took Mengmei with her to Ganlu Palace.

Concubine Li was nearing her due date, with less than a month left.

Seeing Xiangjun, Concubine Li was overjoyed. "Sister Xiangjun, look, I embroidered this tiger-head hat for your child."

Xiangjun's smile froze. "Sister Qinglian, aren't you being a bit too hasty? My pregnancy is not even two months along."

Concubine Li smiled warmly. "The earlier I start, the more I can embroider."

"I feel like you're happier about my pregnancy than your own."

"Because then our children can grow up together."

Xiangjun said pitifully, "Unfortunately, my embroidery skills are poor... Sister Qinglian, please don't blame me. I can only give you gold and silver. Don't think I'm not sincere, alright?"

Concubine Li laughed. "Silly, who would dislike gold and silver?"

After chatting for a while, Concubine Li became restless. With her large belly, sitting or standing for too long made her back ache, so she had to lie on her side.

Xiangjun took her leave after seeing Concubine Li settle down. Unexpectedly, as soon as she stepped out, she encountered Noble Consort Rong.

After exchanging greetings, Noble Consort Rong asked about Xiangjun's pregnancy.

"You are fortunate. You conceived soon after receiving favor. You must take good care of yourself."

Since becoming pregnant, Noble Consort Rong had been in high spirits. Unfortunately, there were few in the harem with whom she was close, so she had little with whom to share her joy. It seemed only Xiangjun was somewhat close to her.

Perhaps due to the emotional changes of pregnancy, she often wanted to find someone to talk to. The Emperor couldn't always be by her side, so today, seeing Xiangjun, she wanted to chat more with her.

"However, Concubine Lian, it's only been less than two months for you. Your pregnancy isn't stable yet. Why are you walking around?"

"To be honest with Noble Consort, I've been suffering from severe morning sickness. For the past few days, I've vomited everything I ate. It's been very difficult. The imperial physician told me to walk more, saying that a stroll could alleviate the discomfort."

"Then you should listen to the physician. I was also confined to my room for too long earlier. The physician said that wasn't good for the baby either. He advised me to move around more, which would make delivery easier later. Since that's the case, Concubine Lian, let's walk together. We can keep each other company, and it won't be boring."

"Alright, I'd be happiest to have Noble Consort's company."

Hearing Xiangjun say this, Noble Consort Rong seemed pleased and asked, "Why?"

Xiangjun smiled innocently, her eyes crinkling. "Because Noble Consort, you are so beautiful. I've heard that during pregnancy, if you look at beautiful people more often, your child will be beautiful too! I would be happiest if I give birth to a little princess as beautiful as Noble Consort."

Noble Consort Rong was delighted by Xiangjun's flattery and laughed, scolding her for being smooth-tongued. Then she took Xiangjun's hand and led her towards the Imperial Garden.

Ganlu Palace was in an excellent location, and it didn't take long for them to reach the Imperial Garden.

Although it was already winter, it hadn't snowed yet this year. It was just a bit cold outside, but the paths were still in good condition.

"It's a pity it hasn't snowed yet," Noble Consort Rong sighed. "The snow scenery in the Imperial Garden is beautiful."

"If it snows, the paths will be slippery. With Noble Consort pregnant, it wouldn't be convenient for you to come out and see."

"That's true..." Noble Consort Rong held Xiangjun's hand. "In that case, I'll have to rely on Concubine Lian to come and keep me company more often."

Xiangjun cursed inwardly. She was pregnant too—would the paths be any better for her if it snowed?

"Of course. As long as Noble Consort doesn't find me annoying, I wish I could accompany you every day."

As they chatted, they saw another group approaching from the distance, led by Qin Zhao Yi, dressed in colorful, luxurious attire.

"I wondered who it was. So it's Noble Consort Rong and Concubine Lian," Qin Zhao Yi said.

chapters.title: Xiangjun Falls into the Water
chapters.content:
Qin Zhao Yi had never respected Noble Consort Rong. She gave a perfunctory, far from standard, curtsy to Noble Consort Rong, then looked Xiangjun up and down with a mocking smile.

"Isn't this Concubine Lian?"

Xiangjun reluctantly greeted Qin Zhao Yi. "Greetings, Zhao Yi Qin."

Qin Zhao Yi sneered, "Concubine Lian, you really have a short memory. Have you forgotten who gave you the abortion potion before? Now that you're pregnant, how dare you still stay with Noble Consort?"

Lady Caiwei, infuriated, stepped forward and shouted, "Qin Zhao Yi, what nonsense are you spouting?"

"Where am I talking nonsense?"

"When did our Noble Consort ever do such a thing? The Emperor has already made a decision about Concubine Lian's matter. Are you suggesting that His Majesty is unfair and is covering for our Noble Consort?"

"Whether His Majesty is covering for your Noble Consort, your Noble Consort knows best, and everyone in the harem is clear about it too. Otherwise, why would everyone keep their distance from Noble Consort? Aren't they afraid of being given an abortion potion and having no way to clear their names?"

Noble Consort Rong's face turned pale with anger, but she still bit her lip and remained silent.

She knew that Qin Zhao Yi's father was still fighting wars for the Emperor, so she had to tolerate her.

Hadn't the Emperor himself tolerated Qin Zhao Yi secretly giving him medicine?

If the Emperor could tolerate it, so could she.

Xiangjun observed the two women—Qin Zhao Yi, arrogant and smug, and Noble Consort Rong, her face white with suppressed anger—and felt that Noble Consort Rong was rather pathetic.

With her high birth, the Emperor's extreme favor, and the support of generals and officials from the previous dynasty, how could she be so timid? She was constantly silenced by a princess from a tributary state...

If Xiangjun held a higher rank than Qin Zhao Yi and had support, she would never tolerate such disrespect. A single accusation of "not knowing one's place" would be enough to punish her justly. Why let her own palace servants engage in a war of words? It only made her look weak in the eyes of others.

Seeing that Noble Consort Rong was about to swallow her pride, Xiangjun quickly spoke up, "Zhao Yi, I am the victim in this matter. I know better than anyone that Noble Consort has never harmed me. His Majesty and Her Majesty the Empress personally investigated this matter. You shouldn't believe the rumors. A wise person stops rumors in their tracks."

"Hmph, I'm just reminding you not to trust the wrong person."

Qin Zhao Yi gave a cursory bow to Noble Consort Rong, then turned and left with her entourage.

After they had all left, Xiangjun approached Noble Consort Rong and consoled her, "Noble Consort, don't take Qin Zhao Yi's words to heart. I know you. You are not that kind of person."

"Perhaps I am the only one in the entire palace who thinks so."

"They don't know the truth. It's just a case of rumors spreading. In the end, it's just jealousy over your favor. If you let others' jealousy anger you, it's not worth it."

Noble Consort Rong was somewhat moved.

Over the years, since entering the palace, she had always been the target of public criticism. No one in the harem had truly befriended her, and the rumors about her had never ceased.

There were even rumors about her outside the palace, portraying her as a bewitching concubine who brought disaster to the nation.

This was the first time someone had genuinely believed in her.

Noble Consort Rong took Xiangjun's hand. "May I call you Sister Xiangjun?"

"Of course. I have always regarded Noble Consort as a sister."

"Good, Sister Xiangjun. I take your words to heart. Thank you for saying these things to me."

"There's no need to thank me. Noble Consort, you are too kind."

Noble Consort Rong couldn't help but smile. "You are truly innocent and lovely. It's no wonder the Empress Dowager and the Empress like you. You are indeed a good person. Rest assured, take good care of your child. In the future, I will also protect you."

Xiangjun smiled and nodded, continuing to walk with Noble Consort Rong.

Noble Consort Rong took Xiangjun to Qianli Pond to feed the fish.

After feeding the fish for a while, Noble Consort Rong grew tired and sat down nearby, watching Xiangjun feed the fish alone by the pond.

Today, Xiangjun had her hair in a simple bun and wore a red cloak. The white fur collar made her look like a young, unmarried girl.

For some reason, looking at Xiangjun's bright eyes and lovely profile, Noble Consort Rong was reminded of someone.

"Xiangjun, how old are you this year?"

"Your servant is seventeen this year."

Noble Consort Rong's expression flickered with a hint of trance. "Seventeen..."

Xiangjun turned her head and saw Noble Consort Rong lost in thought, a touch of melancholy on her face.

"Noble Consort, what's wrong?"

"I was just thinking... When I lived among the common people before, I had a sworn sister. If she were still alive, she would be about your age."

For a moment, Xiangjun almost couldn't maintain her expression.

The surging hatred in her heart almost turned into a metallic taste in her throat.

But she suppressed the urge to immediately seek revenge on the woman before her. Instead, she feigned surprise and sorrow. "Has Noble Consort's sworn sister already passed away?"

"Yes... She died ten years ago."

"Ten years ago, she would have been only seven. So young... What happened?"

Noble Consort Rong's expression changed slightly, but the fleeting embarrassment and guilt did not escape Xiangjun's notice.

"She... She and my adoptive parents all died in a fire."

Noble Consort Rong's face was pale, and the complex emotions in her eyes made Xiangjun feel a bitter amusement.

She had already killed them. What was the point of remorse now?

Regret meant nothing to Xiangjun. Only blood could repay blood.

Lady Caiwei noticed that her mistress's expression was amiss and quickly said, "Noble Consort, we've walked enough for today. Let's go back."

Xiangjun also said, "Then I'll go back with you, Noble Consort."

Xiangjun turned to leave, but as she took her first step, she stepped on a round, smooth bead.

Losing her balance, Xiangjun fell backward with a cry from the onlookers, plunging straight into Qianli Pond.

"Oh no! Concubine Lian has fallen into the water!" the palace maids and eunuchs shouted.

Seeing Xiangjun fall into the water, Mengmei hesitated no longer and jumped in to save her.

The people around Noble Consort Rong quickly surrounded her, and no one else jumped in to help Mengmei.

Noble Consort Rong panicked and pointed at her own palace servants, shouting, "What are you standing around for? Hurry up and save her!"

Only then did two young eunuchs jump into Qianli Pond.

Coincidentally, Qin Zhao Yi had just arrived nearby. Seeing the commotion, she quickly ordered her own servant, Zhu Jin, to help with the rescue.

With everyone's combined efforts, they finally managed to pull Xiangjun out of the water.

It was already the last month of the year.

chapters.title: Miscarriage
chapters.content:
When Xiangjun woke up, her Chengxiang Palace was already filled with people.

This was the first time her bedchamber had ever been so lively.

She looked around and saw the Emperor, the Empress, Honored Consort Rong, Virtuous Consort De, Consort Qin Zhao, and their palace attendants all present.

In addition, two imperial physicians stood there with worried expressions—one of them was Physician Liu.

Seeing Physician Liu, Xiangjun felt at ease.

"Consort Lian has awoken!" Consort Qin Zhao said excitedly.

The Emperor looked at Xiangjun on the bed, grabbed her hand, and his face was filled with distress.

"Xiangjun..."

"Your Majesty... your subject's child... is my child alright?"

The Emperor couldn't bear to look at Xiangjun's expression. He averted his gaze, hesitated, and then looked at the Empress.

In the end, it was the Empress who spoke: "Consort Lian, you have miscarried. Do not be too heartbroken. The Empress and His Majesty are here, and we will surely bring you justice today."

Hearing the Empress say this, the Emperor immediately said: "Today's incident was just an accident. Do not be too sad. You are young; you will have more children."

Xiangjun really wanted to curse this dog Emperor to death. His Majesty's words implied that he did not want to investigate the matter further.

Indeed, since she had fallen in front of Honored Consort Rong, the Emperor was probably afraid of implicating her.

But how could Xiangjun let this opportunity slip away?

She continued her act, saying emotionally: "Your Majesty, this was truly not an accident! Your subject tripped over a pearl, which is why I fell. Your Majesty may not care for your subject, but you cannot ignore Honored Consort Rong. I am just a lowly Consort Lian with no influential family background. Who would target me? Today, I was only accompanying Honored Consort Rong on a walk to Qianli Pond. I fear that this entire plot was aimed at Honored Consort Rong, and I was merely an unfortunate bystander. If we do not investigate this thoroughly, what if this person tries to harm Honored Consort Rong again in the future?"

The Emperor's expression was complex.

On one hand, he was touched that Xiangjun was still thinking of Honored Consort Rong at a time like this, with her heart set only on Rong's well-being. On the other hand, he felt helpless because he did not want to investigate this matter at all.

The Empress noticed the Emperor's intentions and refused to give him the chance to back out. She immediately said: "Consort Lian speaks reason. All the palace attendants present saw what happened. Consort Qin Zhao has also found the pearls that fell by Qianli Pond. This matter is absolutely not simple. If Your Majesty does not investigate it thoroughly, I fear the harem will be uneasy."

The Emperor was helpless, his heart filled with irritation. But if he did not investigate, he feared that the officials of the imperial court would once again submit memorials criticizing him. He could only nod at the Empress and say: "Since the Empress has spoken thus, then let it be investigated."

With a signal from Consort Qin Zhao, a eunuch from her palace immediately brought forward a tray and presented it to the Emperor and Empress.

"Reporting to Your Majesty and the Empress, this pearl was picked up by this servant near Qianli Pond in the Imperial Garden."

Seeing the pearl, Consort Qin Zhao immediately covered her mouth and let out an exaggerated "Ah!"

Seeing Consort Qin Zhao's reaction, the Empress and Virtuous Consort De stepped forward to examine it.

The Empress managed to keep her composure, her expression merely turning solemn. But Virtuous Consort De could not control her expression at all and directly looked at Honored Consort Rong.

Honored Consort Rong saw that the Empress, Virtuous Consort De, and Consort Qin Zhao were all looking at her. Only then did she, supported by Caiwei, rise and approach to look at the pearls in the tray.

Both Honored Consort Rong and Aunt Caiwei had their faces change drastically.

"This... how could this be..."

The tray contained dozens of second-grade eastern pearls.

In the palace, pearls were strictly regulated according to rank.

Only the Emperor, the Empress, and the Empress Dowager were allowed to wear first-grade eastern pearls.

Honored Consorts and Consorts were only allowed to wear second-grade eastern pearls.

The palace rules were strict, and there would absolutely be no case of wearing pearls above one's rank. The pearls in the tray were all second-grade eastern pearls. In the entire harem, there was only one Honored Consort.

The Empress saw that the Emperor's face had darkened and quickly said: "They are only second-grade eastern pearls. We cannot be certain they belong to Honored Consort Rong. It is better to investigate thoroughly."

The Emperor wearily waved his hand and said: "Investigate."

Before long, the Emperor's young eunuch sent people to search Honored Consort Rong's palace and had someone check the records of the Department of Imperial Attire. It was discovered that a string of second-grade eastern pearls was indeed missing from Honored Consort Rong's palace.

Only then did the Empress look at Honored Consort Rong. "Honored Consort Rong, do you have anything else to say?"

"I... I do not know how this happened. I have not worn eastern pearls recently."

Consort Qin Zhao chimed in with a sarcastic tone: "Ah, Consort Lian is truly pitiful. She was only thinking of her good sister, Honored Consort Rong, fearing that someone would harm her. Who would have thought that all of this was actually aimed at her? Consort Lian, you must know that people's hearts are hard to fathom. Some people may call you 'sister' to your face, but behind your back, they strike with the intent to take your life..."

"I did not!" Honored Consort Rong interrupted.

Consort Qin Zhao had no intention of letting Honored Consort Rong off the hook and continued: "Why would it be so obvious? Isn't it because no matter what Honored Consort Rong does, she will not be punished and can do as she pleases?"

"Consort Qin Zhao! His Majesty and the Empress are still here. Is it your place to speak?" the Emperor rebuked sternly.

Consort Qin Zhao pouted and closed her mouth.

The Empress glanced at the Emperor, disappointed, and said: "Your Majesty, regarding Consort Lian's miscarriage, please handle it impartially."

The Emperor was helpless and looked at Honored Consort Rong. "Why did you invite Consort Lian to the Carp Pond today?"

Honored Consort Rong could not believe that the Emperor was actually questioning her. Tears welled up in her eyes as she paled and replied: "Consort Lian came to my palace to visit Lady Li. The imperial physician advised us to walk more, so I invited Consort Lian to the Imperial Garden."

"The eastern pearls, how do you explain them?" the Empress asked. "So many pearls fell to the ground. With so many of your palace attendants, not one of them noticed? Why was it that Consort Lian was the one who stepped on them?"

Seeing that Honored Consort Rong could not find the words, Aunt Caiwei explained: "Who steps on them and who doesn't is not something we can control."

The Empress glared at Caiwei and scolded: "Are you saying that Consort Lian was just unlucky? A mere servant dares to interrupt when the masters are speaking! Is this how Honored Consort Rong teaches you the rules? Slap her ten times."

"Your Majesty!" Honored Consort Rong looked at the Emperor, hoping he would stop the Empress from punishing Caiwei. But the Emperor did not want to interfere in the matter of a servant.

Caiwei was slapped ten times by Fragrant Aunt, and both of her cheeks turned red.

Xiangjun felt very satisfied in her heart. In her previous life, she had been slapped by Caiwei many times.

After Caiwei was punished, the Empress asked Honored Consort Rong again: "Honored Consort Rong, since you claim to be innocent, then explain everyone's doubts. Why did the eastern pearls from your palace disappear? Where did that string of pearls go?"

Honored Consort Rong explained: "The items are in the storage. How would I know where they went? Does the Empress usually manage her own storage?"

The Empress coldly laughed: "This Empress has dedicated people managing my storage. But I would never lose such an important item without knowing. So, please tell us, Honored Consort Rong, who is the palace attendant in charge of managing your storage?"

Honored Consort Rong bit her lip and said nothing. Caiwei immediately crawled in front of everyone and said: "It is this servant who manages Honored Consort Rong's storage. But this servant does not know why the eastern pearls disappeared... perhaps..."

The Emperor kicked Caiwei away with his foot. He was so angry with this servant that he could barely contain himself.

Last time, with the matter of the contraceptive medicine, he had already ordered Gu Tingxue to investigate.

That matter was entirely Caiwei's own idea, done behind Honored Consort Rong's back.

Not only had she failed to handle it properly, but she had also tarnished Honored Consort Rong's reputation.

And now, this had happened again, and she had even dared to harm the imperial heir!

If such a person were to remain by Honored Consort Rong's side, one day she would bring disaster upon Rong.

"I think this is all the fault of this wicked servant. She cannot even handle small matters properly, and as a result, Consort Lian fell into the water."

The Empress and Consort Qin Zhao both felt a sense of defeat. Even at this point, the Emperor was still so protective of Honored Consort Rong. It seemed he was determined to treat this as an accident.

"Drag this wicked servant out and beat her to death."

Honored Consort Rong plopped to her knees on the ground and crawled to the Emperor.

"Your Majesty, Caiwei is my dowry servant. I believe Caiwei is not this kind of person! There must be another explanation for this matter. Please, Your Majesty, investigate thoroughly again."

The Emperor was starting to get angry with Honored Consort Rong.

What more was there to investigate?

If they investigated further, it would all be blamed on her.

"Rong, it is not worth it for such a wicked servant. I will bestow a better servant upon you."

"Your Majesty! I beg you!"

Suddenly, Honored Consort Rong's forehead broke out in a sweat. She clutched her stomach, seemingly in great pain.

The Emperor's expression changed, and he said urgently: "Physician!"

Physician Liu quickly supported Honored Consort Rong and had her sit down. After taking her pulse, he said: "Your Highness, you must not get emotional. Be careful not to disturb the fetus."

The Emperor thought of how difficult it had been for Honored Consort Rong to conceive. If he really killed her dowry servant, he feared that her pregnancy would also become unstable. So, he had to suppress his anger for the time being and spare the servant.

"Drag Caiwei away and give her thirty strokes of the cane."

At the same time, Xiangjun's tears fell once more, dropping onto the back of the Emperor's hand with a patter.

The Emperor's heart stirred as he looked at Xiangjun, who was crying so pitifully, as if a needle had pricked his heart.

Consort Qin Zhao, however, was still being sarcastic in a low voice: "Honored Consort Rong is truly formidable. Even after harming someone else's child, she cannot even have a servant executed."

The Emperor's eyes revealed a murderous intent. "I told you to shut up! Did you not hear me?"

Consort Qin Zhao was scared by the Emperor's gaze and could only close her mouth, not daring to say another word.

"What are you still standing there for? Drag this vile servant away and beat her!" the Emperor roared.

"Honored Consort Rong! Honored Consort Rong, save me!" Caiwei cried out.

Honored Consort Rong also knew that the Emperor had already made the greatest concession he could. She could only watch with reddened eyes as Caiwei was dragged away.

The Empress was extremely disappointed.

At this point, the Emperor still refused to punish Honored Consort Rong.

She now fully understood the extent of the Emperor's favoritism toward her.

If this was the case, her subsequent plans would have to be changed.

"Your Majesty, since that is the case, please compensate Consort Lian properly. This subject will take her leave."

Virtuous Consort De and Consort Qin Zhao also took their leave one after another, leaving only the Emperor and Honored Consort Rong.

Honored Consort Rong once again threw herself beside Xiangjun.

"Xiangjun, my sister, you must believe me. It truly was not me. This time, we have been schemed against... Xiangjun, my sister..."

Honored Consort Rong wanted to say more, but she was interrupted by Xiangjun.

Xiangjun looked as if her heart was dead, and she said bitterly: "I know, it was not you, sister. It does not matter. Your Majesty, Sister Rong, I am tired. I want to rest."

The Emperor sighed: "You rest well. Do not overthink. The physician said that if you take good care of yourself, there is still a chance."

Xiangjun gave a bitter smile. "Thank you for your comfort, Your Majesty."

"The physicians will stay here and take good care of Consort Lian's health."

"Yes..."

The Emperor was also unwilling to face Xiangjun in such a state. He took Honored Consort Rong and left.

Only when they reached the door did the Emperor say to the eunuch beside him: "Announce to the six palaces: Elevate Consort Lian to the rank of Imperial Concubine Lian. The ceremony will be held in half a month."

chapters.title: Old Dreams
chapters.content:
After the imperial physician had prescribed medicine for Xiangjun and left, Mengmei finally entered the room.

She looked at Xiangjun, who had her back turned, and said, "Mistress, His Majesty said he will bestow the title of *Pin* upon you. The ceremony will be held in half a month."

Xiangjun, wrapped in her blanket, closed her eyes, too exhausted to speak.

Mengmei consoled her, "Your Highness, my brother said that this pregnancy was already difficult to maintain. Even if you had forced yourself to keep it, the child might not have been healthy. Please don’t be too heartbroken."

"This ceremony will only make me Consort Lian in half a month. For now, I am still *Liangdi*. Mengmei, I’m tired. I want to sleep for a while."

"Yes, *Liangdi*. Rest well. I’ll go check on your medicine."

Mengmei wiped her tears and left.

Xiangjun closed her eyes, feeling nothing but exhaustion. She just wanted to sink into a deep sleep.

Later, she woke up to take her medicine, then fell back asleep. This time, she dreamed of her past life again.

Her first child was named Yuanheng. She had carried him through an extremely difficult pregnancy.

Back then, she had been tormented by the Emperor, and her body had been in terrible condition when she conceived. The morning sickness had been unbearable—worse than this life. She had vomited bile, and later, even blood.

But no matter how much she suffered, she had never thought of giving up on the child.

Because Xiangjun believed that this child had come to save her.

So she endured ten months of agony. By the time she went into labor, she was as thin as Li *Gengyi*, and the birth had been so difficult that she had even fractured a bone.

But as soon as Yuanheng was born, he was taken away by Defu and Caiwei. Every time she tried to see her child, Defu would chase her off. Later, Caiwei and the Emperor convinced her to move out of Ganlu Palace, making it impossible for her to even catch a glimpse of her son.

To reclaim her child, Xiangjun had no choice but to ally herself with the Empress. Even though she knew the Empress was only using her as a pawn, she had no other options.

So she moved into Qin *Zhaoyi*’s palace. By day, she fought for the Empress; by night, she returned to face Qin *Zhaoyi*’s humiliation and torment.

But she endured it all.

Finally, after poisoning *Guifei* and causing Qin *Zhaoyi* to be abandoned and confined by the Emperor, she had found an opportunity to see Yuanheng.

But Yuanheng had pushed her away in disgust.

"Aunt Caiwei said I should stay away from you. You’ll harm me."

"I am your birth mother! Yuanheng, how could I ever harm you?"

"I am *Guifei*’s son. With your lowly background, do you think you’re fit to be my mother? I was only reborn from your womb. I am not your son."

Xiangjun didn’t remember how she had stumbled back to her own chambers that day, her soul shattered.

The child she had fought so hard to bring into the world had rejected her so cruelly.

Perhaps she truly wasn’t a good person. Even knowing that the child was innocent, that he had been poisoned against her by others, she still couldn’t bring herself to forgive him.

From that moment on, Xiangjun pretended the child never existed.

Later, when she awoke to the truth of the story, she realized that Yuanheng had been right.

He *was* *Guifei*’s son—he had merely been reborn through her womb.

So, in this life, when Xiangjun became pregnant again, when the violent morning sickness returned, her instincts told her that Yuanheng had come back.

As long as she endured it like last time, she would surely give birth to him again.

And this time, perhaps she could raise him herself.

But Xiangjun refused.

Her dreams twisted and turned, pulling her back to the night she gave birth to Yuanheng. She had endured the pain of her bones breaking, finally delivering the child who had tormented her for ten months—only for him to save her life in return.

She reached out, wanting to hold her child, but watched as he was taken away.

She stretched her hand further, trying to grab him—only to fall off the bed.

"Child... my child..."

Xiangjun woke up crying, her pillow soaked with tears.

For a long time, she remained dazed, until she noticed the tall figure standing by her bed.

It wasn’t Mengmei.

Gu Tingxue stood before the cloud-brocade mosquito net, staring at her motionless, lost in thought.

Xiangjun sat up and gently lifted the net.

Gu Tingxue gazed at her deeply, instinctively reaching out to wipe the tears from her face.

"Eunuch Gu, why are you here?"

Xiangjun’s voice was hoarse. Gu Tingxue didn’t answer, instead turning to pour her a cup of water.

Xiangjun tried to take the cup, but Gu Tingxue sat down by her bed, supporting her shoulders as he fed her the water.

Still groggy, she let him do as he pleased.

After drinking, she felt much clearer.

Looking at Gu Tingxue, who had returned to the bedside, she asked, "Did Eunuch Gu come in the middle of the night just to feed me water?"

When had he become so gentle?

"I was outside the palace running errands for His Majesty. I only just returned and heard about what happened."

Xiangjun was surprised to see the pity in his expression.

Was Gu Tingxue actually grieving for her?

"What exactly happened?" Gu Tingxue asked. "The imperial physician ordered you to stay in bed for the first four months to preserve the pregnancy. Why did you go looking for *Guifei*? I warned you before—Qin *Zhaoyi* has been cursing you daily in the palace, planning to harm your child to frame *Guifei*. So why did you still go out? Did something happen? Tell me everything."

Xiangjun was slightly taken aback. Was Gu Tingxue treating her as a victim? Sympathizing with her?

Gu Tingxue was certainly not a soft-hearted man.

So why was he reacting so strongly to her losing the child?

"Because I did it on purpose."

Xiangjun saw no reason to lie to Gu Tingxue.

His expression turned sharp. "What do you mean, *Liangdi*?"

"I knew what Qin *Zhaoyi* was planning, but this situation worked in my favor. Blaming the child’s loss on *Guifei* would best gain the Emperor’s guilt and sympathy. Since His Majesty would never punish *Guifei*, he would have to compensate me endlessly instead. Isn’t that why I’m about to be promoted to *Pin*?"

Gu Tingxue looked at her in disbelief.

Xiangjun even caught a flicker of anger in his eyes.

How strange. This Gu Tingxue, who killed without hesitation, was reacting so strongly to this.

"That was your child. You would abandon your own flesh and blood just for a title?"

Gu Tingxue tried to keep his voice steady, but Xiangjun still detected the uncontrollable tremor.

"Children in the palace are different from those outside. If I can’t give him a good future, it’s better not to have him at all. My bond with this child can only go this far. He helped me secure my title—it’s not in vain that I carried him."

Gu Tingxue laughed, his gaze filled with mockery.

"Yes, *Liangdi* is right. In this palace, maternal love can never compare to wealth and honor. It’s just... I once thought *Liangdi* would make a good mother. I never expected you to be so heartless. I only hope you won’t regret this."

"I won’t regret it. As long as I can earn Eunuch Gu’s full support, a child is a small price to pay."

Gu Tingxue could no longer suppress his anger. "Just for my support? Are you mad?"

Xiangjun forced a smile.

"Yes, I will do whatever it takes to achieve my goals, no matter the sacrifice, no matter the pain. I am that kind of crazy, obsessed person. Does Eunuch Gu regret making the bet with me?"

Gu Tingxue stared into Xiangjun’s eyes. They were so bright—even after her miscarriage, even through her tears, they still shone with an unsettling intensity, as if the light in them would never fade.

He couldn’t quite describe how he felt.

His heart seemed to be gripped by an invisible hand, squeezing so tightly he could barely breathe.

"There’s still half a month before you’re officially promoted to *Pin*. Until then, *Liangdi*, be careful."

---

chapters.title: *Guifei*’s Mishap
chapters.content:
After her miscarriage, Xiangjun stayed indoors in Chengxiang Hall, observing the traditional month of rest.

The Emperor visited her twice, but each time he only lingered at the door before leaving.

*Rong Guifei* sent gifts daily, and though Xiangjun accepted them politely, she showed no resentment toward *Guifei*.

The matter of Xiangjun’s lost child was like a stone thrown into a lake—it caused a few ripples, but soon, all traces vanished.

For the next ten days, the rear palace remained calm.

The front court, however, was far from peaceful.

Every day, the Emperor received countless memorials accusing *Rong Guifei* of being a bewitching concubine who harmed the imperial heir.

It was clearly the work of Chancellor Yang.

If the Emperor had been half-convinced before, now he believed it even less.

"Tingxue, what do you think of this?" the Emperor asked.

Gu Tingxue pondered for a moment before replying, "There was no need for *Guifei* to harm *Liangdi* Xiangjun. Even if *Liangdi*’s child had been born, it wouldn’t have affected *Guifei*."

"Indeed..."

Tingxue continued, "Your Majesty, perhaps you should assign more capable palace attendants to *Guifei*. In my humble opinion, Ganlu Palace is full of loopholes. *Guifei*’s kindness is a virtue, but it also gives those with ill intentions opportunities to exploit. In the end, it only troubles Your Majesty."

Seeing the Emperor’s silence, Tingxue paused before adding, "Forgive my impertinence, but *Guifei* has been in the palace for ten years, and such incidents keep happening, growing worse each time. Now it’s even causing trouble in the front court. If *Guifei* is labeled a bewitching concubine, then Your Majesty... what does that make you?"

At these words, the Emperor, who had been feeling sorry for *Guifei* being wronged, couldn’t help but feel a flicker of resentment toward Xue Jiaojiao.

Yes, Jiaojiao was nearly thirty now. After so many years as *Guifei*, how could she still be as naive as she was in her youth, unable to even manage her own Ganlu Palace properly?

He could favor her in everything, take care of everything for her, but he was the ruler of a nation—there were countless matters demanding his attention. He grew weary too.

If *Guifei* was a bewitching concubine, then what did that make him? A foolish ruler?

Emperor Yanqing valued public opinion above all else. He absolutely could not tolerate being seen as a foolish ruler.

With this thought, the Emperor sighed, rubbing his temples. "For now, *Guifei* is with child. Send more people to watch over her palace. Don’t let anyone take advantage of the situation, especially that Caiwei. No more mishaps are to occur. As for replacing the attendants, we’ll do that after the child is born. For now, let it be, to avoid upsetting *Guifei*."

"Understood."

The Emperor closed the memorial and stood up. "Tingxue, accompany me to see the Empress Dowager."

Gu Tingxue followed the Emperor out of the Taiji Hall. Just as they stepped outside, a young eunuch rushed over, kneeling on the ground in a panic. "Your Majesty, it’s not good! *Guifei* is bleeding... it seems she’s showing signs of a miscarriage!"

...

The Emperor and Gu Tingxue hurried to Ganlu Palace, where the imperial physicians had already arrived.

"What happened?!" the Emperor demanded.

Physician Liu reported, "Your Majesty, *Guifei* appears to have ingested a blood-activating medicine, causing vaginal bleeding and premature labor symptoms. We and the other physicians have administered acupuncture to temporarily stabilize the pregnancy."

"How could *Guifei* have taken such a thing? What kind of service is this in Ganlu Palace?!"

With a rustle, the servants of Ganlu Palace all knelt to the ground.

The Emperor was already displeased with Ganlu Palace. If not for *Guifei*’s pregnancy, he would have dealt with these people long ago.

Now that *Guifei* was in trouble, his anger flared. He waved his hand and ordered, "Execute all the attendants who personally served *Guifei*."

"Your Majesty!" From behind the screen, *Guifei*, who was lying on the bed receiving acupuncture, cried out in alarm, "Your Majesty, you must not!"

Gu Tingxue glanced at the Emperor.

This was the first time the Emperor had shown such impatience toward *Guifei*.

Just as the Emperor hesitated over whether to punish the attendants, a voice announced from outside, "Her Majesty the Empress has arrived—"

The Emperor looked toward the door and saw the Empress, accompanied by *De Fei* and Qin *Zhaoyi*, entering.

The three of them had certainly arrived quickly.

The Emperor found their presence irritating.

He was starting to regret granting *De Fei* and Qin *Zhaoyi* the authority to assist in managing the six palaces. The three of them together were always scheming against his *Guifei*.

"Your Majesty, how is my sister *Guifei*?" the Empress asked.

The Emperor sat on a soft couch, his face dark, fingers fidgeting with his court beads.

Gu Tingxue quickly responded, "Your Majesty the Empress, rest assured. *Guifei* initially showed signs of miscarriage, but after the physicians’ acupuncture, her pregnancy has been temporarily stabilized."

Qin *Zhaoyi*’s expression shifted slightly—she clearly didn’t believe it.

The Empress also looked disappointed, but upon seeing Qin *Zhaoyi*’s inability to hide her emotions, she shot her a warning glance.

Qin *Zhaoyi* pursed her lips and fell silent.

"The imperial physicians said *Guifei*’s pregnancy was stable. How did she suddenly miscarry?" the Empress asked.

"She ingested a blood-activating medicine."

The Empress frowned. "The attendants in *Guifei*’s palace are truly negligent. How could they make such a mistake? Your Majesty must not be soft-hearted—you must handle this severely."

The Empress just wanted those responsible dead as soon as possible.

Unexpectedly, Qin *Zhaoyi* interjected, "Could it be that someone is trying to harm *Guifei*? Your Majesty, Your Majesty the Empress, I think we must investigate. *Guifei*’s food must have been inspected by the imperial physicians, so someone must be targeting her. Perhaps *Liangdi* Xiangjun was right all along—last time, when she miscarried, it was actually aimed at *Guifei*. *Liangdi* was just an innocent victim!"

Hearing this, the Empress’s expression changed slightly, as if she didn’t understand why Qin *Zhaoyi* was so insistent on investigating.

But Qin *Zhaoyi*’s words did plant a seed of doubt in the Emperor’s mind.

Two incidents in a row, both targeting *Guifei*—could it be that *Liangdi* Xiangjun’s miscarriage had indeed been a setup to frame *Guifei*?

The Emperor waved his hand, his face filled with anger. "Investigate."

...

Chengxiang Hall.

Xiangjun lay on the *Guifei*’s daybed.

Though she had only been resting for ten days, her body had mostly recovered.

However, the imperial physicians still forbade her from going outside, and Xiangjun was bored to death.

She was simply not the type to endure loneliness. Even while confined, she longed to go out and fight.

Xiaoluzhi brought in the newly prepared medicine. Xiyu and Mengmei, one holding candied fruits and the other tea, fussed over Xiangjun as she drank the bitter medicine, then quickly helped her rinse her mouth and eat the sweets.

As Xiangjun chewed on the cloyingly sweet fruit, a young eunuch from the Emperor’s side arrived with a message.

"*Liangdi* Xiangjun, by His Majesty’s order, you are to come to Ganlu Palace."

Xiangjun put on a weak facade. "Please ask Eunuch to wait outside. I’ll change my clothes and come right away."

"The *Liangdi* need not rush. This servant will wait outside."

Once the eunuch left, the expressions of the four people in the room turned serious.

"Mistress..." Xiyu looked at Xiangjun with concern.

"Xiyu, you and Xiaoluzhi stay in Chengxiang Hall. Do as I instructed earlier. Don’t panic—everything is under control. Mengmei, you will accompany me to Ganlu Palace."

chapters.title: Entering the Game
chapters.content:
The atmosphere in Ganlu Palace was oppressively heavy when Xiangjun entered.

The Emperor and the Empress both had dark expressions, while only Consort Qin wore an unmistakable look of smug satisfaction.

Gu Tingxue stood beside the Emperor, not even lifting an eyelid when Xiangjun entered, as if the matter had nothing to do with him.

Noble Consort Rong lay in the warm chamber, and though she was hidden behind a screen, her voice could be heard.

"Your Majesty, is it Sister Xiangjun who has arrived?"

"Sister Rong, it is I. What has happened to you? Why do you sound so weak?"

Consort Qin chimed in with a sarcastic tone, "Still pretending to be close sisters at a time like this? You two are truly strange—acting like loving sisters in public, yet scheming against each other in private."

The Empress shot Consort Qin a glare. "The matter has not been investigated thoroughly. It is too early to draw conclusions."

The Emperor glanced at Xiangjun. She had lost weight, her face noticeably thinner, which made him even more annoyed with Consort Qin.

Noble Consort Rong’s weak voice came from behind the screen: "Your Majesty, I do not believe Sister Xiangjun would harm me. There must be another explanation for this."

Xiangjun looked confused. "Your Majesty, Empress, what has happened to Sister Rong? What is going on? I do not understand..."

The Empress spoke gravely, "Someone replaced Noble Consort Rong’s medicinal sandpot, nearly causing her to miscarry."

Consort Qin quickly added, "The palace servant of Lady Li has already been summoned. He saw that you took the opportunity while visiting Lady Li, and secretly went to Noble Consort Rong’s small kitchen to replace the sandpot."

Xiangjun had encountered a similar situation in her past life.

At that time, the Empress had lost her beloved son. The Emperor, knowing that Noble Consort Rong was involved, refused to punish her and even wanted to have Xiangjun’s child raised by Noble Consort Rong.

The Empress then developed a murderous intent toward Noble Consort Rong.

Consort Qin, who had been cold-shouldered by the Emperor for poisoning him, had then aligned herself with the Empress.

The first thing she did after joining the Empress was secretly poisoning Noble Consort Rong with a sandpot.

In her past life, at this time, Xiangjun was pregnant and staying in Noble Consort Rong’s palace. Consort Qin had framed Xiangjun for the crime.

The motive was that Xiangjun wanted to kill Noble Consort Rong to raise the child herself.

Xiangjun, of course, denied it. The Emperor, considering the child in her womb, sent her personal palace maid to the Palace Correction Office. The matrons there tortured her maid for seven days straight.

Not until her maid died under the torture without confessing did the Emperor believe Xiangjun.

In her past life, that maid was Xiyu.

Unexpectedly, in this life, a similar incident occurred, and Consort Qin had once again framed her.

Didn’t she think this framing was a bit forced?

In her past life, it was to avoid being separated from her child. What was the reason this time?

There had to be a reason, right?

"This matter, I have not done it. I have a very good relationship with Noble Consort Rong and would not harm her. As for the miscarriage... First, I do not believe Sister Rong would harm me. Second, after my miscarriage, I have not left Chenxiang Hall. How could I have replaced the sandpot used by Noble Consort?"

"It was you who replaced it before your miscarriage," Consort Qin said.

"At that time, Sister Rong and I were on good terms. Why would I harm her?"

"She previously forced you to drink the abortion soup, and you sought revenge, so you harmed her," Consort Qin said triumphantly, looking at Xiangjun. "There is both eyewitness and physical evidence. You cannot deny it."

Consort Qin clapped her hands, and immediately two people came forward.

One was a small eunuch in charge of Lady Li’s meals.

He said he had personally seen that day when Xiangjun came to visit Lady Li, she had lulled Lady Li to sleep, and then, under the pretext of checking on Lady Li’s medicinal meals, went to the small kitchen and replaced Noble Consort Rong’s kitchenware.

"In response to Your Majesty, Noble Consort Rong, being kind-hearted, lent her small kitchen to Lady Li for use because Lady Li, carrying the imperial heir, had a poor appetite. Who would have thought that Noble Consort’s kindness would be exploited by Concubine Lian!"

The other witness was a palace servant from the Imperial Kitchen. She said that half a month ago, a small palace maid named Feicui from Chenxiang Hall had come to her to fetch an identical sandpot, the very one used to poison Noble Consort Rong.

Xiangjun refuted, "The sandpots in the Imperial Kitchen all look similar. How can you be sure it is the same one?"

The palace servant immediately replied, "It is this servant’s fault. When the palace maid from Chenxiang Hall came to fetch the sandpot, she did not give me a tip, so I deliberately gave her one with a slight crack on the lid. That is why I can recognize that this is the same sandpot I gave to Feicui that day."

Consort Qin beckoned with her hand, and another small palace maid was brought forward. Xiangjun recognized her as Feicui, a palace maid assigned to her by the Palace Servants Bureau after she was promoted to Concubine Lian.

The small palace maid Feicui immediately said, "This servant only followed Concubine Lian’s orders. After bringing back the sandpot, this servant did not touch it again and does not know what Concubine Lian intended to do with it. Please, Your Majesty, spare my life! Empress, spare my life!"

Xiangjun remained calm. "This palace maid is not one of my personal attendants. If I were to do something that would cost me my head, would I have her do it?"

Mengmei also quickly stepped forward and knelt on the ground. "In response to Your Majesty, the personal matters of Concubine Lian are attended to by me and Xiyu. If errands need to be run outside, we send Xiaoluzai. Not only does everyone in Chenxiang Hall know this, but the people from the various bureaus in the rear palace who come and go also know it. A little investigation would confirm this. Moreover, these newly assigned palace maids and small eunuchs have always been serving outside. Concubine Lian is the most careful and cautious in her actions. When palace servants are assigned to her, they are thoroughly vetted. If Concubine Lian wanted to harm someone, she would not entrust such an important task to a newly arrived palace maid. Therefore, this must be Feicui deliberately framing Concubine Lian."

The Emperor let out a slight sigh of relief. Fortunately, Xiangjun and her people were not foolish; otherwise, he would not have been able to save her.

"What this palace maid says makes some sense."

Consort Qin became anxious and immediately said, "I think it is just Concubine Lian and her servants using clever words to deceive!"

The small palace maid was quick-witted and swiftly said, "Indeed, it was not Concubine Lian who personally ordered me. It was Sister Mengmei who told me. I thought that Sister Mengmei’s words were Concubine Lian’s intentions."

Mengmei pointed at the small palace maid and said, "Feicui! You are slandering me. Your Majesty, I think we should thoroughly interrogate this girl to see who is secretly instructing her to slander Concubine Lian!"

The Empress became somewhat tense. These palace servants must not be interrogated. If they were, and it came out that Consort Qin was involved, it would implicate her as well.

At this moment, the Empress felt that Consort Qin was truly more trouble than she was worth.

She had only asked Consort Qin to administer the medicine to cause Noble Consort Rong’s miscarriage. It was bad enough that she failed, but why drag Concubine Lian into this?

She was just stirring up trouble for no reason.

The Empress had no choice but to help Consort Qin for the time being.

The Empress immediately said, "Your Majesty, these three witnesses did not know each other beforehand and had no opportunity to collude. It is unlikely that all three would lie simultaneously. Your Majesty, you have already been criticized by the court for favoring Noble Consort Rong. Let us handle Concubine Lian’s matter with fairness."

The Empress’s words struck at the Emperor’s weak point.

He could endure some criticism for Noble Consort Rong, but he could not bear to be labeled a tyrant for Concubine Lian as well.

chapters.title: Palace Correction Office
chapters.content:
The Emperor was displeased but still asked with a dark expression, "Then, what does the Empress think should be done about this matter?"

"Noble Consort Rong was indeed poisoned, and the sandpot is indeed from Chenxiang Hall. If it was not Concubine Lian, then it must be one of her subordinates with ill intentions."

The Empress’s meaning was clear: someone had to take the blame for this matter.

If not Concubine Lian, then her palace maid.

Hadn’t the previous two incidents involving Noble Consort Rong been blamed on palace servants?

The Emperor pondered for a moment. Indeed, that was a solution. After all, it was just a servant girl—if she died, she died. As long as the matter was settled without reaching the court, it would be fine.

"Then send the palace maid Mengmei to the Palace Correction Office for interrogation," the Emperor said with a wave of his hand.

Seeing that someone was about to take Mengmei away, Xiangjun blocked them with one hand.

"Wait!"

Xiangjun knelt down with a thud in front of the Emperor and the Empress.

"Your Majesty, Empress, Mengmei is someone I brought from Jiangnan. She has been with me since she was little and is completely loyal to me. She would never betray me in this lifetime. So even if I did this, she would insist it had nothing to do with me. Instead of torturing Mengmei, it would be better to send me directly to the Palace Correction Office. The result would be the same."

Gu Tingxue, who had been silently lowering his head, suddenly lifted his gaze toward Xiangjun.

He slightly widened his eyes, looking at Xiangjun’s resolute expression with a complex look, as if he did not understand, or perhaps he was shocked by Xiangjun.

"Concubine Lian!" Mengmei’s eyes instantly reddened.

Xiangjun glanced at her and shook her head, so Mengmei had no choice but to swallow all the words she wanted to say.

The Emperor’s face instantly darkened.

Why did Concubine Lian have to learn from Noble Consort Rong? And why did she have to learn even the part about protecting servants?

Moreover, she was even more excessive than Noble Consort Rong, actually willing to take the punishment for a subordinate.

The Emperor could tolerate Noble Consort Rong’s foolishness, but he could not tolerate others in the palace doing the same.

"Concubine Lian, do not make a scene."

The Empress also showed a reluctant expression and advised, "Concubine Lian, this matter has nothing to do with you. You have not even finished your month of rest after the miscarriage. How could you endure the torture of the Palace Correction Office?"

Xiangjun showed not a hint of hesitation. She lifted her head, and for the first time, looked directly at the Emperor and Empress with a completely fearless gaze.

Her expression was stern, and her tone was calm yet firm as she repeated, "This subject is willing to go to the Palace Correction Office to prove her innocence."

Xiangjun was looking at the Emperor, but her peripheral vision seemed to pierce through him, landing on Gu Tingxue standing behind the Emperor.

Gu Tingxue had a dark expression, his gaze almost boring a hole through Xiangjun.

Consort Qin was overjoyed and said excitedly, "Since Concubine Lian is willing, let her go! If she still does not confess after enduring the Palace Correction Office’s torture, it will also silence the public opinion!"

The Emperor still wanted to give Xiangjun a chance and was about to speak to give her a way out, but Xiangjun did not give him the chance. She directly kowtowed to the Emperor.

"Please, Your Majesty, allow Xiangjun to prove her innocence!"

The Emperor was also angered by Xiangjun’s refusal to give him face, actually daring to defy him for a servant. Today, the Emperor was already in a bad mood, and now his anger flared even more.

The Emperor said with a dark expression, "Fine, since you care so much about your servant, you may go to the Palace Correction Office to prove your innocence."

"Your Majesty, you must not!" Noble Consort Rong’s voice was filled with sobs. "Your Majesty! Someone is trying to harm both me and Xiangjun, Your Majesty!"

But the Emperor paid no attention to her, waving his hand to have Xiangjun taken away.

Mengmei wanted to say something but was stopped by Xiangjun’s fierce gaze.

Xiangjun glared at her with reddened eyes, leaving Mengmei speechless.

Mengmei remembered Xiangjun’s instructions: no matter what she did, do not stop her. This was part of her plan.

So, Mengmei could only kneel on the ground with tears in her eyes, watching as Xiangjun was taken away.

...

Lady Li learned of the news from her servants when Xiangjun had already been sent to the Palace Correction Office.

She tried to rush out of her palace but was stopped by her servants.

"I must see His Majesty! Sister would never do such a thing!"

A palace maid blocked Lady Li. "Lady Li, how can you see His Majesty? Even if you do, His Majesty will not listen to you. Even Noble Consort Rong’s plea was ignored..."

Lady Li suddenly felt a sharp pain. She clutched her stomach and looked down to see a pool of water on the floor.

"Quick, call the imperial physician! Lady Li’s water has broken!"

Lady Li gave birth to her child in just a day and a night.

She wanted to save Xiangjun. Gritting her teeth, she finally gave birth to the child late the next night.

Lady Li had a royal son, the Emperor’s third royal son.

The Emperor came to see the third royal son, bestowed the name Yuanji, and even promoted Lady Li to the position of Caiyun.

The Emperor had intended to say a few more words to Lady Li, but she immediately began pleading for Concubine Lian, which angered the Emperor so much that he left immediately.

...

The Emperor had been in a bad mood these past few days.

Even the attendants serving before him could sense the Emperor’s irritability.

In the past, the Emperor would only be this angry for Noble Consort Rong. This was the first time he was this angry for another consort.

Gu Tingxue, seeing the Emperor in this state, took the initiative to speak, "Your Majesty, it is obvious that someone is framing Noble Consort Rong and Concubine Lian."

"Do you think I cannot see that?"

The Emperor was not blind to the framing.

The Emperor could also see that the palace was now divided into two factions: one led by the Empress, Noble Consort De, and Consort Qin, and the other by Noble Consort Rong and Concubine Lian, possibly including Lady Li.

It was clear that the Empress’s faction was more powerful. Moreover, both Noble Consort Rong and Xiangjun were kind and gentle, often framed and unable to prove their innocence.

Sometimes, he was also angry—angry that he had given Noble Consort Rong so much favor and the power to assist in managing the harem, yet she was still repeatedly harmed.

But if she were a different person, perhaps she would have been able to firmly control the harem.

However, upon further reflection, if she were not of this nature, he would not have loved her for so many years.

"Concubine Lian offended Your Majesty this time, but she was even willing to sacrifice her life to protect her servant, let alone Noble Consort Rong. In this servant’s opinion, if she were to die in the Palace Correction Office, it would be a pity."

The Emperor’s hand, which was holding a tea cup, paused.

Yes, what Gu Tingxue said was correct. Noble Consort Rong could not protect herself, so he needed to place someone capable by her side. From her actions that day, Concubine Lian seemed better at managing her subordinates and was more vigilant than Noble Consort Rong. With some promotion and guidance, she might be able to stand up to the Empress and the others in the future.

However, the Emperor did not like the way Concubine Lian had looked at him that day.

She had actually defied him for a servant.

She was his consort, the Emperor’s woman, yet she was willing to risk her life for a servant.

This was something Emperor Yanqing could not tolerate.

Emperor Yanqing thought for a moment, then sighed. "Tingxue, how many days has Concubine Lian been in the Palace Correction Office?"

"Two days."

"How is she?"

"She has not confessed."

"You go to the Palace Correction Office and take a look. If, after three days, Concubine Lian still has not confessed and is still alive... I will release her."

chapters.title: Can't Bear to See Me Die
chapters.content:
Palace Discipline Office.

A basin of cold water splashed Xiangjun awake.

It was the twelfth lunar month, the coldest time of the year. The Palace Discipline Office was already damp and chilling, and with the water poured over her, Xiangjun couldn’t stop shivering.

Qin Zhaoyi had bribed the matrons of the Palace Discipline Office to torment Xiangjun thoroughly.

So, for the past two days, whenever Xiangjun was about to faint or fall asleep, she would be splashed awake.

Just as Xiangjun thought she would continue to be tortured, she heard the matrons of the Palace Discipline Office respectfully address someone, "Lord Gu, why have you come?"

Only then did Xiangjun lift her eyelids slightly.

She saw Gu Tingxue enter, wearing his imperial bestowment of a red robe with golden qilin embroidery. His face, so strikingly handsome it was almost otherworldly, still dazzled even in the dim and gloomy torture chamber.

Xiangjun thought stubbornly that she must look ugly and filthy now, probably not as good as this eunuch dog.

With a wave of Gu Tingxue’s hand, the two matrons retreated and closed the door.

Only Gu Tingxue and Xiangjun remained in the torture chamber.

The dark, damp room was filled with a strong metallic scent of blood.

Gu Tingxue examined Xiangjun.

Her hair was disheveled, and she was strapped to the tiger bench. Her white inner garment was stained with blood, and her smooth, fair feet were splattered with mud. She looked disheveled and pitiful.

Gu Tingxue’s hands, hidden behind his back, unconsciously clenched into fists.

He didn’t know why, but he disliked seeing Xiangjun in this state. Although her persistent, shameless behavior annoyed him, seeing her in such a wretched state angered him even more.

Seeing that Gu Tingxue had entered and stood there silently, just staring at her, Xiangjun grew impatient.

"Lord Tingxue, have you come to see me? Just to stare?"

At least bring her some food...

Gu Tingxue was infuriated by Xiangjun’s unrepentant attitude. "You shouldn’t have defied His Majesty."

Xiangjun scoffed, "Shouldn’t have defied, yet I did. I’m already in the Palace Discipline Office. What more do you want from me?"

Gu Tingxue was so angry that his fists tightened, the veins on his hands bulging. "Do you not value your life at all? If that’s the case, why did you pretend for so long in front of His Majesty?"

"That’s my own plan, none of Lord Tingxue’s concern."

Gu Tingxue laughed in exasperation. "It seems you don’t need me to save you."

Xiangjun looked up at Gu Tingxue, her eyes still bright, but the mockery in them was unmistakable.

"Lord Tingxue is truly jesting. The one who put me in this situation—isn’t it Lord Tingxue himself?"

Gu Tingxue’s eyes darkened as he stared coldly at Xiangjun. "What does Noble Consort Lian mean by that? The one who harmed you is Qin Zhaoyi. Noble Consort Lian mustn’t blame the wrong person."

Xiangjun gave a cold laugh. "Indeed, it was Qin Zhaoyi who schemed against me. She bribed the palace maids of Lady Li, replacing the sandpot used for the medicinal stew meant for Noble Consort Rong. But if she had truly succeeded, why would she use such a small amount of poison, only causing Noble Consort Rong to bleed? Qin Zhaoyi may be foolish, but she is vicious and hates Noble Consort Rong. With her nature, she would rather use too much poison than too little. So, someone must have replaced that sandpot and reduced the amount of poison. I thought long and hard—who in this palace could know Qin Zhaoyi’s every move and have the motive to do this? Only Lord Tingxue."

"Oh?" Gu Tingxue seemed interested in Xiangjun’s words. "What makes Noble Consort Lian say that? Tingxue would like to hear the details."

"Knowing Qin Zhaoyi’s plans is easy to explain. There have always been your people in Qin Zhaoyi’s palace, even among her close attendants. That’s how you knew early on about Qin Zhaoyi’s plot to harm my child. That time, I truly miscarried. Qin Zhaoyi succeeded, so your people weren’t exposed and could continue monitoring her. Naturally, you would know about this incident as well."

"And my motive?"

"That was the part I couldn’t figure out for a long time. Lord Tingxue, knowing Qin Zhaoyi’s plan, could have either done nothing and watched from the sidelines, or helped Noble Consort Rong to prevent her from being poisoned. Or simply exposed Qin Zhaoyi. Why choose to reduce the poison, only causing Noble Consort Rong to bleed, not truly miscarry? Doing so benefits you not at all—it’s completely unnecessary."

"Indeed, it was unnecessary."

"But that day, when I knelt on the ground and said I would go to the Palace Discipline Office, Lord Tingxue, who had always been indifferent, suddenly looked up at me. In that instant, I understood."

"Oh?" Gu Tingxue gazed deeply at Xiangjun. "What did Noble Consort Lian understand?"

"Turns out..." A triumphant smile spread across Xiangjun’s face. "Turns out Lord Tingxue did something so unnecessary and thankless... all for me."

Xiangjun’s smile was so enchanting that it seemed as if they weren’t in a torture chamber, but in her own Chengxiang Palace.

It was as if she was the one looking down on Gu Tingxue, not the other way around.

Gu Tingxue was so angry his fists clenched. "You really have no regard for your own life. If that’s the case, why did you pretend for so long in front of His Majesty?"

"I have my own plans, none of Lord Tingxue’s business."

Gu Tingxue laughed bitterly. "It seems you don’t need me to save you."

Xiangjun lifted her gaze to Gu Tingxue, her eyes still bright, the sarcasm in them impossible to hide. "Lord Tingxue is truly amusing. The one who put me in this situation—isn’t it Lord Tingxue?"

Gu Tingxue’s eyes narrowed as he stared coldly at Xiangjun. "Noble Consort Lian speaks as if I’m the one who harmed you. The one who harmed you is Qin Zhaoyi. Don’t blame the wrong person."

Xiangjun sneered. "It was indeed Qin Zhaoyi who schemed against me. She bribed the palace maids of Lady Li to replace the sandpot for Noble Consort Rong’s medicinal stew. But if she had truly succeeded, why use such a small amount of poison, only causing Noble Consort Rong to bleed? Qin Zhaoyi may be foolish, but she is cruel and hates Noble Consort Rong. With her nature, she would use more poison, not less. So someone must have replaced that sandpot and reduced the poison. I thought long and hard—who in this palace could know Qin Zhaoyi’s every move and have the motive to do this? Only Lord Tingxue."

Gu Tingxue seemed genuinely interested. "What makes Noble Consort Lian say that? Tingxue would like to hear more."

"Being able to know Qin Zhaoyi’s plans is easy to explain. There have always been your people in Qin Zhaoyi’s palace, even among her close attendants. That’s how you knew early on about Qin Zhaoyi’s plot to harm my child. That time, I truly miscarried. Qin Zhaoyi succeeded, so your people weren’t exposed and could continue monitoring her. Naturally, you would know about this incident as well."

"And my motive?"

"That was the part I couldn’t figure out. Lord Tingxue, knowing Qin Zhaoyi’s plan, could have either done nothing and watched from the sidelines, or helped Noble Consort Rong to prevent her from being poisoned. Or simply exposed Qin Zhaoyi. Why choose to reduce the poison, only causing Noble Consort Rong to bleed, not truly miscarry? Doing so benefits you not at all—it’s completely unnecessary."

"Indeed, it was unnecessary."

"But that day, when I knelt on the ground and said I would go to the Palace Discipline Office, Lord Tingxue, who had always been indifferent, suddenly looked up at me. In that instant, I understood everything."

"Oh?" Gu Tingxue’s gaze deepened as he looked at Xiangjun. "What did Noble Consort Lian understand?"

"Turns out..." A triumphant smile spread across Xiangjun’s face. "Turns out Lord Tingxue did something so unnecessary and thankless... all for me."

Xiangjun’s smile was so enchanting, as if they weren’t in a torture chamber but in her Chengxiang Palace.

It was as if she was the one looking down on Gu Tingxue, not the other way around.

"Lord Tingxue, you’re so wicked. We clearly agreed that as long as I rose to the rank of concubine, you would help me. But when you saw me about to reach that position, you regretted it. So even though you knew Qin Zhaoyi was plotting against me, you didn’t warn me. But you also couldn’t bear to see me suffer too much. You were afraid that if Noble Consort Rong truly lost her child, His Majesty would kill me in a fit of rage without investigating further. So you only let Noble Consort Rong bleed, not truly miscarry, preventing me from fulfilling our six-month agreement. Ah... I never expected Lord Tingxue’s thoughts to be even more intricate than mine, a woman’s."

Gu Tingxue suddenly laughed, his face showing no trace of anger at being exposed, but rather a sense of relief.

For a moment, he even felt an inexplicable excitement, as if his blood was boiling.

"If Noble Consort Lian has already figured it out, then Tingxue has no need to deceive you further. But I never intended for you to end up in the Palace Discipline Office. Your current predicament is because of your untimely kindness, insisting on taking the blame for your own maid."

Xiangjun lifted her chin, disdainfully. "I am different from those nobles in the palace who climb over corpses to rise. My people only need to serve me loyally. They don’t need to suffer or die for me. If Lord Tingxue is willing to be my person, it would be the same."

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun with a complex expression, but when he met her bright, startling eyes, he still unnaturally averted his gaze.

"Unfortunately, tomorrow marks the end of the six months. Noble Consort Lian is still a Noble Consort. You’ve lost."

Xiangjun was indifferent. "So Lord Tingxue came to gloat about his victory?"

"I came to tell you that His Majesty said if you don’t change your statement in three days, you will be released." Gu Tingxue said.

Xiangjun raised an eyebrow. "His Majesty is so kind. Could it be that Lord Tingxue spoke on my behalf?"

Gu Tingxue neither confirmed nor denied.

Xiangjun’s smile deepened. She clicked her tongue twice. "It’s strange. I’m a concubine who has offended His Majesty and has no value. Why would Lord Tingxue go through the trouble to save me? Could it be... Lord Tingxue can’t bear to see me die?"

chapters.title: Seeing the Light of Day Again
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue was only stunned for a moment, but that fleeting expression was still captured by Xiangjun.

"Oh! Lord Tingxue really can’t bear to see me die!"

Gu Tingxue seemed to be angered by shame. He coldly huffed, "If I had known, I would have let you die the first time I saw you."

Xiangjun couldn’t help but laugh, her laughter shaking her entire body as if she had discovered something amusing. If her limbs weren’t bound, she might have laughed until she bent over.

"Stop laughing, your wounds will split open."

Xiangjun finally stopped laughing. She tilted her head and looked at Gu Tingxue. "I’ve always found it strange. I clearly didn’t do anything to offend Lord Tingxue, so why does he always want me dead? Now I finally understand. Lord Tingxue must have realized early on that he had some different feelings for me. He thought that if he didn’t kill me early, he wouldn’t be able to bear it later. Lord Tingxue, am I right?"

Gu Tingxue wanted to say no, but looking into Xiangjun’s bright, cunning eyes, he couldn’t bring himself to deny it.

What was the point of denying it?

He truly couldn’t bear to see her die.

This matter, Gu Tingxue had thought through clearly over the past two days while Xiangjun was locked in the Palace Discipline Office.

If he hadn’t figured it out, why would he have spoken to Emperor Yanqing just to get her out and pave the way for a better future for her?

Gu Tingxue walked up to Xiangjun, pinched her chin, and placed a pill into her mouth.

Xiangjun swallowed it without hesitation.

"Aren’t you afraid it’s poison?" Gu Tingxue said displeasedly.

"Doesn’t Lord Tingxue can’t bear to see me die?" Xiangjun asked with a smile. "Lord Tingxue, what kind of medicine is this?"

"A good medicine to preserve the foundation and strengthen the body." Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun’s injuries and said helplessly, "I’ll have the matron apply some ointment for you later. You still have to endure three more days in the Palace Discipline Office. That’s His Majesty’s order. He cares most about the authority of the ruler and dislikes being defied. After being lectured by Chancellor Yang every day, and then you made His Majesty look foolish in front of so many people that day, he is determined to make you suffer a little before leaving the Palace Discipline Office."

Xiangjun nodded in understanding.

That dog emperor is really a dog.

"But I don’t want to wait three more days."

Gu Tingxue frowned and thought for a moment. "Then I’ll think of another way."

"There’s no need for Lord Tingxue to think of a way. Just trouble you to pass a message to Xiaoluzu, have him take the evidence to His Majesty to plead my case. He will prove my innocence."

Gu Tingxue was stunned. "What evidence?"

"The evidence that I didn’t harm Noble Consort Rong."

Gu Tingxue was surprised. "You’ve had evidence to prove your innocence all along?"

"Of course." Xiangjun smiled. "Feicui is in my palace. How could she collude with outsiders without me knowing? From the first time she made contact with Qin Zhaoyi, I knew about it and had someone secretly keep an eye on her."

Gu Tingxue was taken aback. "Then why..."
