Xiangjun smiled brilliantly. "If I didn’t come to the Palace Discipline Office, how could I see Lord Tingxue’s true feelings? I don’t want a partner who is half-hearted and harbors ulterior motives. My people must have only me in their hearts, must be wholeheartedly devoted to me. Even if I fall to the lowest point, they must not give up on me. If they can’t do that, then even if they are as powerful as Lord Tingxue, Xiangjun doesn’t want them. So I came to the Palace Discipline Office of my own accord to see if Lord Tingxue could bear to see me die."

"Just to see if I could bear to see you die? You had to go this far?"

Xiangjun’s smile didn’t fade. "Naturally."

"You’re truly a madwoman."

"Not mad, how else can I conspire with Lord Tingxue for great things? Moreover... Lord Tingxue’s slightest pity is worth me risking my life for."

Gu Tingxue looked up and once again met Xiangjun’s eyes.

Xiangjun’s face was filled with a smug, girlish smile. Despite being covered in blood and dirt, she smiled so triumphantly, so radiantly, like a blooming peach blossom.

Gu Tingxue once again felt his heart being tightly gripped.

From childhood to now, he had seen countless schemes and plots, but this was the first time he had willingly admitted defeat.

"Then I ask Noble Consort Lian to rest well. Tingxue will take Xiaoluzu to see His Majesty."

...

Xiaoluzu presented the evidence.

It was a sandpot identical to the one Feicui had taken from the Imperial Kitchen, with a slight crack on the lid.

To verify, His Majesty had the previously sealed sandpot brought out as evidence.

Upon comparison, although both were sandpots, the clay used was different. The one in Xiaoluzu’s hands was from the official kiln. The one used to poison Noble Consort Rong was not a palace sandpot.

Upon further investigation, it was found that the clay of that sandpot was from Nanyue.

...

Xiaoluzu came to the Palace Discipline Office to take Xiangjun away.

He supported Xiangjun as they walked out, and along the way, he vividly described the scene to her.

Qin Zhaoyi claimed she was wronged, that the sandpot must have been switched by someone else. She had her people take the sandpot from the Imperial Kitchen, so there couldn’t be a mistake.

Xiaoluzu covered his mouth and laughed. "Noble Consort, you should have seen His Majesty’s expression. He looked like he couldn’t believe there could be such a fool in the world. He was so disdainful of Qin Zhaoyi."

Immediately after, several of Qin Zhaoyi’s subordinates confessed everything about her.

Even the matter of Xiangjun’s miscarriage was clarified.

It was all Qin Zhaoyi’s doing. Noble Consort Rong was wronged.

"Still, it’s Noble Consort who is clever. You had slave keep an eye on Feicui and switch the pot. Now Qin Zhaoyi has been demoted to a Noble Lady and is confined to the Nanxun Palace, not allowed to leave."

Xiangjun smiled. Qin Zhaoyi was the princess of the Yue Kingdom. The Emperor definitely wouldn’t let her die. Not letting her die but demoting her to a Noble Lady was considered severe punishment.

In reality, Xiangjun’s scheme was quite crude and wouldn’t hold up under close scrutiny.

But it didn’t matter. In the palace, victories and defeats were never about the truth, but about the Emperor’s intentions.

Whoever guessed the Emperor’s mind correctly would keep winning.

Currently, the Emperor’s intention was that he favored Noble Consort Rong and disliked Qin Zhaoyi’s arrogance in the palace. Although he knew Qin Zhaoyi had tried to poison him, the crime of attempting to harm the Emperor was too severe. If not handled properly, it could lead to war with Nanyue, so he had been enduring it.

The Emperor wanted a suitable reason to punish Qin Zhaoyi without being too harsh. So as long as Xiangjun presented the evidence, the Emperor would definitely "believe" it.

"Noble Consort?" Xiangjun, recalling Xiaoluzu’s words, asked curiously, "Why did you call me Noble Consort?"

"Congratulations, Master. His Majesty said you’ve been wronged and will promote you to Honored Consort."

Xiangjun was still somewhat surprised. A promotion of two ranks? The dog emperor was being unusually generous this time.

It seemed her performance had caught His Majesty’s favor. Perhaps he wanted to promote her to balance the power in the harem?

He wanted to support someone in the harem to help his beloved Noble Consort Rong compete with the Empress.

"When will the enfeoffment ceremony be held?"

"The Empress said that since you haven’t completed your month of rest after the miscarriage and have been injured in the Palace Discipline Office, you should focus on recovering. The enfeoffment ceremony will be skipped, and the golden certificate has already been sent to Chengxiang Palace."

"So I’m already Honored Consort now?"

"Yes, Honored Consort."

"What day is it today?" Xiangjun asked.

"Noble Consort, today is the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month."

The fifth day of the twelfth lunar month, exactly six months.

Xiangjun finally revealed a brilliant smile. She had indeed succeeded.

chapters.title: Apply Medicine for This Palace
chapters.content:
Xiangjun and Xiaoluzhi walked out of the Palace Discipline Office, and the sky outside was already dark.

But today, heavy snow had fallen, and the world outside was a vast expanse of white, which made it quite bright.

As soon as the main gate opened, Xiangjun saw Mengmei and Xiyu holding the large black fox fur cloak, waiting at the entrance. Behind them was a sedan chair, which only those of concubine rank or higher were allowed to use.

She was currently a Guifei, so she could only use a four-person sedan chair.

But this was already a height she had never reached in her previous life.

Mengmei and Xiyu, with red-rimmed eyes, rushed over and wrapped Xiangjun in the large cloak.

"Noble Consort..."

"I'm fine. Let's talk when we get back."

Mengmei and Xiyu helped Xiangjun into the sedan chair.

Xiaoluzhi shouted loudly, "Depart!"

On the long palace road, the servants carrying the sedan chair walked steadily through the heavy snow.

...

When the Empress Dowager learned that Xiangjun had left the Palace Discipline Office unharmed, she was not surprised.

"This time, we lost because of Noble Consort Lian. I'm afraid she knew from the beginning what Qin Guifei had done in her palace. That's why Qin Guifei failed, and Guifei only bled without miscarrying."

Lady Fang, confused, asked, "Then why didn't she speak up directly that day? Why did she have to go to the Palace Discipline Office and suffer?"

"Who knows? Maybe she wanted to put on a show of pure goodness in front of the Emperor, to make the Emperor trust her more. But she's wrong. Our Emperor doesn't care about the lives of servants."

"This Noble Consort Lian has only been in the palace for a year, and she's already risen from a Caifu to a Guifei. Your Majesty, we must be careful with her. With Guifei having her, it's like a tiger with fangs and claws."

"Guifei?" The Empress scoffed. "That fool Guifei can't even hold onto such a good knife. Let's wait and see."

...

Chengxiang Palace.

Xiangjun lay on the bed, and Mengmei applied medicine to her wounds, crying as she did so.

"Noble Consort, do you care so much about Eunuch Tingxue that you would put yourself in harm's way just to see if he cares about you?"

Xiangjun smiled. "I put myself in harm's way not to see if Gu Tingxue cares about me."

Didn't Xiangjun already know whether Gu Tingxue cared about her or not?

"Then why?"

"I did it so that Gu Tingxue himself would realize that he can't bear to see me die."

"Isn't that the same thing?" Mengmei didn't understand.

"It's not the same."

It was completely different...

Although she had entered the Palace Discipline Office voluntarily, Xiangjun had indeed suffered a lot. Even though the injuries were superficial, she was still in her confinement period, so after applying the medicine, she went to sleep.

She hadn't rested properly for three days and thought she could finally get some good rest, but she woke up in pain after only a short sleep due to the wounds on her body.

When she opened her eyes, she saw someone sitting by her bed.

Xiangjun was no longer surprised to see Gu Tingxue silently appearing in her room.

This audacious servant had no reverence for the Emperor or his concubines.

Xiangjun sat up and said to Gu Tingxue in a bad mood, "I'm in pain."

Gu Tingxue took out a bottle of medicine from his bosom.

"This is a secret palace medicine from Nanyue. After applying it, your injuries will heal in three days, and there will be no scars."

Xiangjun took it and looked at it, asking, "Where did you get this?"

"I paid a visit to Qin Guifei today," Gu Tingxue said calmly. "I got this medicine for Noble Consort and took the opportunity to avenge you."

Xiangjun sneered, "Qin Zhaoyi did offend me, but Eunuch Tingxue has also schemed against me. Don't you need to let me take revenge?"

Gu Tingxue smiled and asked, "How does Noble Consort wish to take revenge?"

Xiangjun thought for a moment and handed the medicine bottle to Gu Tingxue.

"You can apply the medicine for this palace."

Gu Tingxue took the bottle and was still in a daze when Xiangjun had already taken off her undershirt, leaving only a stomach cover, and lay down on the bed boldly.

As a palace concubine, although the Palace Discipline Office had used interrogation methods on her, they had not used any punishments that would harm her skin.

The wounds on her back were caused by her delicate body; even with her undershirt on, the rough tiger bench had scraped her skin.

Gu Tingxue looked carefully. Most of her injuries were abrasions, so the affected areas were quite large.

He got up to wash his hands, then sat back down, took a deep breath, scooped out the ointment, and gently applied it to Xiangjun's skin.

Xiangjun subconsciously shivered.

Gu Tingxue's hands were so cold.

Gu Tingxue was very careful with his application. Even at night, even with only a dim lamp by the bed, he managed to tend to every wound on Xiangjun's body, not missing even the smallest abrasion on her ribs.

Xiangjun couldn't help but tremble slightly.

"Does it hurt?" Gu Tingxue asked.

But as soon as he spoke, he realized that his voice had somehow become hoarse.

"It doesn't hurt, it's a bit itchy." Xiangjun said softly, "Continue."

The atmosphere suddenly became strange, and Xiangjun didn't even know who was being punished.

She suspected that Gu Tingxue was doing it on purpose, otherwise why did he always apply medicine to the most sensitive parts of her body...

After about half the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, Gu Tingxue finally closed the medicine jar.

"Done."

Xiangjun sat up and put her undershirt back on.

But when she looked up, she met Gu Tingxue's gaze.

It was strong and aggressive, like a venomous snake staring at its prey, not burning hot, but with an uncontainable madness.

Xiangjun was somewhat stunned, but in the next moment, that look disappeared from Gu Tingxue's eyes. He returned to his usual cold and detached self, got up to wash his hands again, then poured a cup of water and handed it to Xiangjun.

Xiangjun took a sip of water and suddenly remembered that when Gu Tingxue was in her palace before, it was always she who served him water.

Xiangjun smiled and said, "I was conferred the title of Guifei on the 15th of the last month, which happened to be the last day of our six-month agreement. I have done what I promised Eunuch Tingxue. I wonder if Eunuch Tingxue will keep his word?"

Gu Tingxue took a step back and, to Xiangjun's surprise, performed a grand bow of a subject to her.

"Eunuch..."

He knelt on one knee on the footstool by the bed and stretched out his hand to Xiangjun.

Xiangjun was still a bit slow to react. Gu Tingxue didn't even kneel before the Empress.

"Noble Consort..." Gu Tingxue softly called.

Xiangjun finally came to her senses and slowly extended her hand, gently placing it on Gu Tingxue's hand.

Gu Tingxue turned his hand and held Xiangjun's hand tightly, making her a little flustered.

She tried to pull her hand back but couldn't.

"Eunuch Tingxue... what are you..."

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun's somewhat panicked expression and finally smiled, lifting the corners of his mouth.

Suddenly, he let go of Xiangjun's hand and placed it gently on his wrist, like a palace servant supporting his master.

Gu Tingxue, with his deep and melodious voice, slowly said, "Noble Consort, rest assured. No matter what you want to do, Tingxue will make sure you get your wish."

---

chapters.title: Avoiding Favor
chapters.content:
Xiangjun didn't remember how she fell asleep the previous night.

She only remembered that Gu Tingxue seemed like a different person, as if he had truly become a servant in her palace, gently attending to her as she went to bed, carefully ensuring she didn't touch the wounds on her back.

If Xiangjun's eyebrows twitched, Gu Tingxue would know what was wrong and immediately help her adjust.

As her consciousness blurred, Xiangjun thought, no wonder the Emperor always kept Gu Tingxue by his side—indeed, there was no one better at serving others.

Xiangjun slept until the afternoon of the next day before waking up, and she didn't even know when Gu Tingxue had left.

After waking up, Xiangjun felt extremely refreshed, with none of the pain from her confinement or her time at the Palace Discipline Office.

"Noble Consort, you're finally awake. Please eat something."

Xiangjun got up, and the table was filled with easily digestible food.

"Noble Consort, while you were asleep, Lady Chun from the Empress's palace and Lady Caiwei from Guifei's palace both came by and brought many gifts."

"Did they say anything to you?"

Mengmei lowered her voice, "Both ladies spoke to me at length. Although they didn't say it directly, they both seemed to want to win Noble Consort's favor. Should Noble Consort return the gifts or pay a visit to the Empress and Guifei?"

Xiangjun thought for a moment and said to Mengmei, "Tomorrow, go to Ganlu Palace and 'beg' Guifei for me. Say that I want Imperial Physician Liu to help me regulate my body."

...

The next morning, Mengmei went to see Guifei. That same day, Guifei sent Imperial Physician Liu, who had been taking care of her pregnancy, to also look after Xiangjun. From then on, Xiangjun's health was entirely entrusted to Imperial Physician Liu.

When Imperial Physician Liu entered Chengxiang Palace, the news immediately reached Yongchang Palace.

Lady Fang was very angry and advised the Empress, "Your Majesty, this Noble Consort Lian is truly ungrateful. She is clearly choosing to side with Honorable Consort Rong. Shouldn't we... make her suffer a little?"

The Empress looked at the ledger and was not anxious. She calmly said, "There's no rush. Things will proceed as they should. Just don't let those servants mistreat Chengxiang Palace."

"Your Majesty, why are you so lenient with Noble Consort Lian?"

"She saved my second prince. I naturally have to repay that kindness. As long as she doesn't do anything to harm me, I won't make things difficult for her."

"But if she sides with Guifei, how can she not oppose Your Majesty?"

The Empress coldly laughed, "She chose Guifei not to help Guifei, but simply because she doesn't want to help me."

...

In Chengxiang Palace.

Imperial Physician Liu came to check Xiangjun's pulse. After feeling her pulse, he remained silent for a long time and looked at Xiangjun with a strange expression.

Mengmei was anxious, "Brother, what's wrong with Noble Consort? Can you please tell us quickly."

"Noble Consort is in good health."

"If she's in good health, why do you have that expression?"

Imperial Physician Liu looked at Xiangjun, puzzled, "Noble Consort Lian, have you eaten any highly nourishing food these past few days? How come after your trip to the Palace Discipline Office, not only are there no internal injuries, but the deficiencies from your previous miscarriage have also been replenished?"

Xiangjun was also surprised.

No wonder she felt refreshed after sleeping for a night—it turned out that her body's deficiencies had been replenished.

Xiangjun had only taken one pill given to her by Gu Tingxue these past few days.

But she didn't want too many people to know about her relationship with Gu Tingxue, so she simply said, "My father gave me a pill in my dowry, said to be able to preserve the foundation and strengthen the body. I took it."

Imperial Physician Liu was amazed. How could Lord Xu bear to part with such a good thing?

"Is that so... This medicine can replenish the deficiencies from a miscarriage and a trip to the Palace Discipline Office with just one pill. It must be an extremely good medicine. It might even be a life-saving drug in critical moments. Noble Consort, do you know the name of the medicine? I would like to take a look."

Xiangjun fell silent, only then realizing Gu Tingxue's generosity towards her.

A life-saving medicine, and he had given it to her so casually?

"I'll ask Gu Tingxue for you."

Mengmei didn't care about any divine medicine and only asked, "So, is Noble Consort completely better now?"

"Of course, she is completely better."

Xiangjun looked at Imperial Physician Liu and seriously instructed, "The fact that I am completely better must not be disclosed. I do not want anyone to know about my physical condition. Also, please alter the pulse diagnosis."

"How does Noble Consort wish me to write the pulse diagnosis?"

"It must make people think that my body is weak, my menstruation is irregular, and that I not only need to rest for a while but also cannot attend the Emperor's bed."

...

Perhaps because she had slept too much during the day, Xiangjun couldn't sleep at night.

So, she lay there with her eyes open, watching Gu Tingxue, who still smelled of blood, push open the window and climb into her warm chamber.

The two of them stared at each other, neither speaking for a while, which was quite awkward.

Finally, Gu Tingxue made the first move, expressionlessly turning to close the window.

When he turned back, Gu Tingxue had returned to his usual cold and calm demeanor.

"Why aren't you asleep yet?" Gu Tingxue asked.

"Can't sleep."

Gu Tingxue frowned, "Can't sleep, is it because the wounds on your back still hurt?"

"No..." Xiangjun looked straight into Gu Tingxue's eyes, paused, and asked, "Why did you come at this hour, Tingxue?"

Gu Tingxue fell silent again, as if he was struggling to control something.

"Could it be that you missed this palace, so you wanted to sneak in and see me while I was asleep?"

Xiangjun had said this in jest, but when she looked at Gu Tingxue with a smile, she was startled by his gaze.

What was going on? Why did Gu Tingxue have that venomous snake looking at its prey expression again?

But soon, Gu Tingxue retracted his gaze.

"The medicine I gave you can replenish your body's deficiencies. Why does your pulse diagnosis still show heart-blood deficiency and qi-blood weakness?"

"Because the pulse diagnosis is fake. The medicine you gave me is very effective. Imperial Physician Liu told me it should be a life-saving medicine. Do you have any more? Imperial Physician Liu wants to study it."

"Only one pill."

Xiangjun looked surprised, "Only one pill, and you gave it to me? So, am I that important to you?"

Gu Tingxue didn't respond and just stood there looking at Xiangjun.

Xiangjun pouted in a wronged manner, feeling that this man was truly boring.

She propped herself up to get out of bed, and Gu Tingxue immediately stepped forward to help her down.

Xiangjun held Gu Tingxue's hand to stand up, but when she tried to pull her hand back, it was tightly grasped by Gu Tingxue.

Xiangjun looked at Gu Tingxue in confusion, and his gaze darkened as he asked again, "Why did you change the pulse diagnosis? Do you want to avoid the Emperor's favor?"

Gu Tingxue and Xiangjun were standing very close. Xiangjun could smell the strong blood scent on him, not knowing what dirty work he had just done for the Emperor.

Xiangjun indifferently said, "The Empress and Guifei are fighting so fiercely. I must be crazy to go out and get involved... It's better to take this opportunity to lie low and wait until they've fought it out before I step out."

chapters.title: Something’s Off
chapters.content:
“What if those two take three or five years to decide a winner?” Gu Tingxue asked.

Xiang Jun didn’t care at all. “Then it’ll be three or five years. It’s not like I’m short on money.”

“Without the Emperor’s favor in the harem, even if you’re a palace mistress now, you won’t live comfortably. Aren’t you afraid the Emperor will forget you completely?”

Xiang Jun slightly lifted her chin, looking at Gu Tingxue with a smug expression. “This concubine is not afraid. Don’t I still have Eunuch Tingxue?”

Xiang Jun took a step forward, her cunning eyes fixed on Gu Tingxue. “Unless… Tingxue, can you bear to watch me being bullied?”

“Your Highness went through so much trouble—miscarriage, entering the palace as a proper attendant—just to get my help. Is this how you use it?”

Xiang Jun’s eyes gleamed with even more smugness. She tiptoed closer, her warm breath right at Gu Tingxue’s lips.

She exhaled softly, her voice sweet as orchid. “This concubine *wants* to waste it like this. If I don’t waste your help this way, how can I show how special you are to me?”

Gu Tingxue gazed intently at the woman before him, who was so full of herself, and unconsciously tightened his grip on her hand.

“It’s not a waste. Since that’s the case, Your Highness, rest assured in Chengxiang Hall. Tingxue promises no one will dare to make things difficult for you.”

…

Gu Tingxue left through the main gate.

Meng Mei, half-asleep, saw Gu Tingxue walking out of Her Highness’s warm chamber.

She was startled awake. She had intended to pretend she saw nothing, but Gu Tingxue walked straight to the soft couch where she slept.

Meng Mei quickly got up.

“Eunuch Tingxue…”

“Take good care of your mistress. Don’t let her sleep too much during the day. Find her things to do, or she won’t sleep well at night, which isn’t good for her health.”

Meng Mei nodded in a daze. “This servant understands…”

“If Her Highness wants anything, come find me directly.”

“Yes. Does Eunuch Tingxue have any other orders?”

Gu Tingxue looked at Meng Mei deeply, then after a moment’s thought: “Not for now. The tea in the room is cold. Bring your mistress a fresh pot.”

Only then did Gu Tingxue push the door and leave.

It took Meng Mei a long time to come back to her senses.

How come, after coming out of Her Highness’s room, Eunuch Tingxue’s temper had changed?

She carried the hot water and hurried into the warm chamber, only to see Her Highness staring thoughtfully, lost in some new scheme.

“Your Highness?”

Xiang Jun snapped back to reality. “Meng Mei, do me a favor.”

“Your Highness’s command is my duty.”

“Find out about Gu Tingxue for me.”

Meng Mei hesitated. “Eunuch Tingxue has eyes and ears everywhere. Who could possibly know his affairs?”

“Not his current affairs. His past. He grew up in the palace since he was a child. The old palace servants must know something about him.”

Meng Mei nodded. “This servant understands. Your Highness, rest assured.”

…

Emperor Yanqing was disappointed to hear that Xiang Jun was ill and wouldn’t recover for a while. He had intended to promote her, but now he could only let her rest.

Xiang Jun’s Chengxiang Hall was already remote, and usually no one passed by. Now that the harem knew she couldn’t serve the Emperor, and seemed seriously ill, they paid her even less attention.

A woman without family background, unable to bear children, and without favor—had no future in the harem.

Some wanted to take the opportunity to suppress her, but for some unknown reason, a few concubines who had secretly caused trouble for Chengxiang Hall—like taking its palace servants or seizing its supplies—soon suffered misfortune.

The Empress assumed it was the Noble Consort’s doing, and the Noble Consort assumed the Empress was strictly managing the harem. No one suspected anything was amiss.

The few concubines who had suffered setbacks, realizing Xiang Jun had someone backing her, and unable to understand the situation, stopped causing trouble. After all, she was just a concubine from a minor family—she couldn’t stir up any waves.

Soon, Xiang Jun was completely forgotten by the harem. She didn’t even appear at the New Year’s Eve palace banquet.

This year’s New Year’s Eve was much quieter than usual.

The Empress Dowager looked at the concubines seated below and asked the Emperor, “Emperor, why does it seem to Your Subject that there are fewer people this New Year’s Eve?”

The Emperor was somewhat embarrassed. The Empress, sitting beside him, answered for him: “In response to Your Majesty, Noble Consort Rong nearly miscarried last time. The imperial physician ordered her to rest in bed to preserve the child, so she isn’t here today. Consort Lian hasn’t fully recovered, and with the cold weather outside, His Majesty allowed her to rest in her own palace. Imperial Concubine Li just gave birth to the Third Prince not long ago and hasn’t finished her confinement, so it’s inconvenient for her to come out.”

As for Consort Qin, the Empress didn’t mention her—probably because it was inauspicious.

The Empress Dowager sighed and reminded the Emperor, “It seems the Emperor’s harem needs some new faces.”

Emperor Yanqing was already thirty this year. Middle-aged, he didn’t like the harem being so quiet—he preferred it to be livelier.

The Emperor sighed. “Yes, this year’s New Year is indeed dull.”

The Empress Dowager reminded him, “The imperial selection is in July this year. His Majesty should pick more people to enter the palace.”

“Yes, Your Subject will listen to Your Majesty.”

With the Emperor’s decision to hold the imperial selection, countless concubines in the harem couldn’t sleep.

After the New Year, those concubines would strive even harder to win favor. Otherwise, when a flood of young newcomers entered, the old ones would be even less likely to catch the Emperor’s eye.

Only Xiang Jun continued to keep the gates of Chengxiang Hall locked, living her quiet life in her own palace.

But Xiang Jun gradually noticed something was off about her palace.

She had already moved from the side hall to the main hall, and the number of servants in her palace had doubled compared to before. But she found that the new batch of palace servants assigned to her were all highly capable.

Xiang Jun had observed carefully. Even the smallest palace maid serving outside was efficient, thoughtful, steady, and proper.

She, a “disgraced” concubine locked in her palace to recover from illness, shouldn’t have such capable servants.

Good servants were in high demand in the palace. Usually, unfavored concubines could only use the ones others had picked over.

Any ambitious and capable servant would try every means to secure a better position for themselves. Why would they come to her?

This was very strange.

Xiang Jun beckoned to Xiao Luzi. “Xiao Luzi, come here.”

“Your Highness?”

“Find a way to get Gu Tingxue here for me. The sooner, the better.”

Xiao Luzi was shocked and pointed at himself. “Me? How can this servant find Eunuch Gu?”

He wasn’t worthy.

Xiang Jun shot Xiao Luzi an annoyed glance. “Didn’t you used to work for him?”

“Even then, I wasn’t qualified to find Eunuch Gu at any time. Why doesn’t Your Highness wait for him to come?”

Xiang Jun coldly huffed. “I don’t care. You find a way for me.”

Xiao Luzi had no choice. He knew Her Highness’s temper. He had to think of something.

Finding Gu Tingxue was no easy task. Most of the time, he wasn’t even in the palace. Even when he was, he was usually attending to the Emperor, and a lowly eunuch like Xiao Luzi couldn’t get close.

Moreover, he couldn’t openly search for Gu Tingxue. He couldn’t let the whole palace know that their mistress wanted to see Eunuch Gu.

So Xiao Luzi had to take a roundabout way and found the young eunuch who had previously contacted him for tasks.

Then he could only go back and wait for news.

Seven days passed before Gu Tingxue finally found time to come to Chengxiang Hall one afternoon.

---

chapters.title: Hiding Under the Blanket
chapters.content:
Xiang Jun was lying on the noble consort’s couch, eating fruit and reading a book.

When she saw Gu Tingxue enter, she was surprised. “Why are you here?”

Gu Tingxue frowned. “Didn’t you send for me?”

“But it’s daytime…”

Gu Tingxue always came in the middle of the night, didn’t he?

“Aren’t you afraid of being discovered?” Xiang Jun asked.

“I only have time now. I can only stay for half an hour.” Gu Tingxue glanced at Xiang Jun. “Don’t worry, no one will find out. Your Chengxiang Hall is like the Cold Palace.”

Xiang Jun had no retort. Gu Tingxue was right. Chengxiang Hall was remote. The harem concubines, no matter where they went, wouldn’t pass by Chengxiang Hall. Unless someone specifically came looking, no one would run into them.

Meng Mei and Xi Yu each entered, one carrying tea and the other carrying snacks.

They served Gu Tingxue tea, then lowered their heads and left, keeping their eyes down the whole time. They even closed the door on their way out.

“Are your palace maids afraid of me?” Gu Tingxue asked.

Xiang Jun looked at Gu Tingxue, wanting to say something but stopping herself.

Except for those bold enough to covet his face, who in the palace wasn’t afraid of him?

“How can it be called fear? It’s respect.” Xiang Jun’s face was full of false smiles. “Our Eunuch Tingxue may be a little stern, but he looks like a jade-faced young master. Who could bear to be afraid of you?”

Gu Tingxue coldly huffed. “Your Highness need not flatter me. Speak. What’s so urgent that you had to find me?”

Xiang Jun was about to speak when the door was pushed open again by Meng Mei, who rushed in.

“Your Highness, Imperial Concubine Li is here. She’s crying and insists on coming in. We couldn’t stop her.”

Xiang Jun glanced at Gu Tingxue, then quickly said to Meng Mei, “Go and stall her first!”

Meng Mei hurried out. Xiang Jun immediately turned to Gu Tingxue. “Aren’t you leaving? What if you run into her?”

Gu Tingxue remained calm, sitting there drinking tea. “If I leave today, it’ll be a month before I can return. Are you sure you want me to go, Your Highness?”

Xiang Jun helplessly said, “Then hide!”

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiang Jun’s rosy face and smirked. “Your Highness is pretending to be ill. But look at your rosy complexion. You don’t look like someone with weak qi and blood at all.”

Xiang Jun, realizing the problem, quickly let down her hair and rushed to sit in front of the mirror.

She found some pearl powder, whitened her lips, and applied some green to under her eyes and cheeks. Then she hastily climbed onto the bed and lay down.

Seeing that Gu Tingxue was still sitting there, Xiang Jun urgently said, “Didn’t I tell you to find a place to hide? Move!”

“Where does Your Highness want me to hide?”

Xiang Jun looked around her room, then down at her bed, and suggested, “Under the bed?”

Gu Tingxue coldly laughed. “Does Your Highness want to humiliate me so much?”

“How is this humiliation?”

Hearing the hurried footsteps outside, Xiang Jun quickly got up and pulled Gu Tingxue onto her bed, covering him with the blanket. Then she pulled down the bed’s gauze curtain, also crawling under the blanket and leaning against the piled-up soft pillows, shielding Gu Tingxue.

The door was pushed open at that moment.

Imperial Concubine Li rushed in and threw herself at Xiang Jun’s bedside.

“Sister Xiang Jun, I’ve come to see you!”

Seeing that Imperial Concubine Li was about to lift the gauze curtain, Xiang Jun pressed her hand down.

“Good sister, let’s talk through the curtain. Don’t catch my illness. You still need to take care of the Third Prince. If he gets sick because of me, it’ll be my fault.”

Imperial Concubine Li reluctantly withdrew her hand and sat at the bedside, wiping her tears.

Meng Mei and Xi Yu looked around but didn’t see Gu Tingxue. They exchanged a glance and sighed in relief.

“Sister Qinglian, your confinement isn’t over yet. Why did you come to see me?”

“I came as soon as I could walk.”

Imperial Concubine Li stretched her hand into the gauze curtain and held Xiang Jun’s hand.

For a moment, the gauze curtain was lifted, and Imperial Concubine Li caught a glimpse of Xiang Jun’s face—so pale and gaunt. It made her heart ache, and she immediately teared up again.

“Sister Xiang Jun, you’ve suffered. Qinglian is useless and can’t help you.”

Seeing Qinglian cry, Xiang Jun’s heart tightened. She felt terrible for deceiving such a young girl.

But she couldn’t tell Imperial Concubine Li the truth. She could only comfort her. “I’m fine. I just need to rest for a while. It’s you who shouldn’t be running around with your confinement not over. The weather is cold. If you catch a chill and leave a root of illness, what then?”

“But I was worried about you, sister. I couldn’t rest easy without seeing you.”

Xiang Jun leaned against the soft pillow. Gu Tingxue’s head was pressed against her waist under the blanket. Her waist was sensitive, and every time Gu Tingxue moved, she felt a tickle and couldn’t help but let out a soft hum.

At this hum, Gu Tingxue under the blanket also stiffened. All he could smell at his nose was the faint fragrance from Xiang Jun’s body, which made him extremely restless.

“Sister, what’s wrong?”

Xiang Jun quickly pressed her hand on Gu Tingxue’s head to stop him from moving.

With this press, Gu Tingxue was pushed against Xiang Jun’s waist.

Xiang Jun was only wearing a thin inner garment. Gu Tingxue could even feel her soft skin…

“Nothing!” Seeing Qinglian looking at her blanket, Xiang Jun quickly asked, “Sister Qinglian, has the Emperor said who will raise your child?”

This question successfully diverted Imperial Concubine Li’s attention, and she looked away, tears falling.

She wiped the corner of her eye with a handkerchief. “The Emperor ordered the child to be raised in Ganlu Palace for now. Although no decree has been issued to register the child under Noble Consort’s name, the wet nurses are currently raising the child in Noble Consort’s main hall… Noble Consort is kind and allows me to see the child every day…”

“Since no decree has been issued, there’s still room to turn things around. The Emperor probably wants to wait until Noble Consort’s child is born before making a decision.”

Imperial Concubine Li’s face was full of worry. “But I’m still worried. The Emperor told me that once Noble Consort’s child is born, Ganlu Palace will be too crowded, and I’ll have to move palaces… Sister, will I never be able to see Yuanji again?”

“When does the Emperor want you to move palaces?”

“Originally, he said I should move after my confinement. But Her Majesty the Empress said my body isn’t well, and she’s afraid the commotion of moving palaces would disturb the fetal god, which wouldn’t be good for Noble Consort’s child. So she said I should move after Noble Consort’s child is born.”

Xiang Jun thought for a moment and said, “The Empress is helping you. Do you know why?”

Imperial Concubine Li wasn’t stupid. She lowered her head. “I know. Her Majesty wants to use me against Noble Consort. She’s doing me a favor.”

Xiang Jun sat up and held Imperial Concubine Li’s hand.

“Qinglian, let your sister advise you: a person’s life is earned by themselves. Only when you help yourself can others help you.”

Imperial Concubine Li looked at Xiang Jun through the gauze curtain, confused. “But what can I do? I can’t afford to offend either the Empress or the Noble Consort.”

“The true master of this harem is only the Emperor.”

“But the Emperor towards me…”

“Don’t waste all the years of effort you’ve put in. Every skill you’ve learned, every step you’ve taken, hasn’t been in vain.”

Imperial Concubine Li nodded suddenly, as if something had clicked. “Sister, I understand.”

Suddenly, Xiang Jun felt a pinch on her waist. She quickly lay back down and pretended to cough twice.

“Sister…”

“I’m tired today and need to rest. You should go back early too.”

“Then I’ll come see you again tomorrow.”

Xiang Jun didn’t want to paint her face white every day. She quickly said, “Sister Qinglian, our sisterly affection doesn’t depend on seeing each other every day. If you take care of yourself, you’re taking care of me. Don’t come every day to avoid catching my illness. Take good care of yourself and Yuanji. When I’m better, we sisters can reunite.”

Imperial Concubine Li finally nodded, as if she had made up her mind, and tightly held Xiang Jun’s hand.

“Then I’ll go back first, sister. Don’t worry, I won’t let you down.”

Meng Mei and Xi Yu saw Imperial Concubine Li out. After the door was closed again, Xiang Jun lifted the blanket.

Gu Tingxue sat up abruptly, his face a little red.

Xiang Jun said embarrassedly, “Didn’t you suffocate?”

Whether it was from suffocation or not, Gu Tingxue’s lips were an unnatural red, as if he had just sucked blood.

Xiang Jun, as if possessed, stretched out her thumb and brushed it against Gu Tingxue’s lips.

chapters.title: The Alluring Ghost
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue felt a soft fingertip brush against his lips, and his entire body jolted in shock, his eyes widening slightly.

Coming back to his senses, he immediately grabbed Xiangjun’s hand and threw it aside.

"Don’t touch me."

Xiangjun leaned in close to Gu Tingxue, blinking as she asked, "Are you angry? Your lips are all red from holding back..."

Gu Tingxue averted his gaze. "It’s the perfume on you that’s choking me."

Xiangjun blinked. "I haven’t even applied any powder these past few days. Don’t believe me? Smell for yourself."

She reached out to let Gu Tingxue smell.

Gu Tingxue pushed her hand away and quickly got off the bed. Normally composed and dignified, he stumbled slightly—a rare sight.

Xiangjun instinctively reached out to steady him, but seeing that he had regained his balance, she withdrew her hand and couldn’t help but let out a soft giggle.

Gu Tingxue, embarrassed and angry, glared at her. "Wipe that powder off your face. You look like a ghost—it’s annoying just to look at you."

Xiangjun had no choice but to pout as she got off the bed, walking to the mirror. While wiping her face, she muttered under her breath, "Even if this princess looks like a ghost, she’s a beautiful one."

Gu Tingxue sat at the table and downed the now-cold tea in his bowl in one gulp before he finally felt a little better.

Annoyed, he said, "What do you want from me today? Speak quickly."

Only then did Xiangjun remember her original purpose. She turned to Gu Tingxue. "What’s going on with the palace attendants in my quarters? Did you replace them all?"

Gu Tingxue’s expression remained blank. "How do you know they weren’t planted by the Empress or another concubine?"

"Surely not all ten-plus attendants were sent by them? Besides... the ones in my palace are too clever and steady. They must be your people."

"Indeed, they are my people..." Gu Tingxue didn’t hide it. "But there are also some from the Empress and Song Feijing. Don’t worry—my people will keep an eye on them. Nothing will go wrong. You just focus on your own little life."

Xiangjun was furious.

"Why did you replace them all with your people? Do you think I’m incapable of managing Chengxiang Palace?"

Gu Tingxue sneered. "Your Highness is more than capable. Even Xiaoluzhi is now loyal to you. How could Your Highness be incapable?"

"Stop with the sarcasm. What do you mean by this? Are you spying on me?"

"It’s for your protection."

Xiangjun snapped, "I don’t care. Withdraw your people. I want attendants with clean backgrounds. I’ll train them myself, and there won’t be any problems."

Gu Tingxue’s eyes darkened, a hint of gloom flashing in his deep gaze.

His voice turned cold, carrying a warning. "Noble Consort Lian must understand—right now, I am helping you. You need me. I am not your servant."

"Does Tingxue not allow me to have any influence of my own?"

"Your Highness has me—that is enough."

Xiangjun was trembling with anger. How dare Gu Tingxue treat her like this! Did he think she was a caged songbird?

She wished she could smash the rouge on her dressing table onto his head.

But she couldn’t. She had been given a second life and couldn’t afford to lose her temper like she had in her past life.

Gu Tingxue found it amusing to see Xiangjun suppressing her anger, unable to lash out.

He stood up and walked to the dressing table, picking up a comb to brush her disheveled hair.

"Your Highness, rest assured. With my help, your path will be smooth. Why must you struggle so hard, insisting on doing everything yourself and walking the thorny path?"

Xiangjun forced a smile, her eyes fixed on her reflection and Gu Tingxue in the bronze mirror. Suppressing her rage, she said softly, "Then this princess will have to rely entirely on you, Lord Gu."

Gu Tingxue’s smile deepened at the change in her address for him.

He took out a wooden token from his sleeve and placed it in Xiangjun’s hand.

"What is this?" Xiangjun asked.

"I must leave the capital to attend to the Emperor’s business. During this time, if you need anything, send someone with this token to find Wan Lichun, the eunuch in the Office of Imperial Ceremonies. He is my disciple. Whatever you need, he will handle it for you."

"Thank you for your trouble, Lord Gu."

Xiangjun tightly clutched the token, turning her head slightly to refuse Gu Tingxue’s attempt to continue brushing her hair.

"Don’t you have matters to attend to, Lord Gu? This princess won’t keep you any longer."

Gu Tingxue’s smile grew even wider.

"Then I shall take my leave."

Gu Tingxue turned and walked out.

Meng Mei had gone to see Consort Li, and Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu were waiting outside. Seeing Gu Tingxue leave, Xiaoluzhi stepped forward to see him off.

"You two should go attend to Noble Consort Lian. Her Highness is in a bad mood."

Gu Tingxue strode away, and only then did Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu hurry inside.

As soon as they entered, Xiaoluzhi nearly got hit in the head by a wooden token.

The token clattered to the floor, rolled a few times, and ended up right in front of Xiaoluzhi.

He glanced at the intricate pattern, then looked up at Xiangjun. Their mistress was sitting at the dressing table, trembling with rage.

Seeing her like this, Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu quickly knelt down.

Xiangjun was seething.

How dare Gu Tingxue try to control her!

And yet, she couldn’t afford to break ties with him right now.

Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu were used to Xiangjun’s occasional tantrums. Xiyu gave Xiaoluzhi a look, and he quickly stepped forward to soothe her.

"Your Highness, why waste your anger on a wooden token? This servant will burn it for you."

"No!"

Xiaoluzhi froze, waiting for further instructions.

Xiangjun held her breath for a long time, her face turning red from the effort.

Gou Jian could endure humiliation for ten years, Tang Xuanzong could feign stupidity for thirty, and Sima Yi could tolerate for fifty. What was a little patience for her, Xiangjun?

Finally, she swallowed her pride.

"Pick it up."

Xiaoluzhi quickly retrieved the token.

Xiangjun looked at it, let out a cold humph, but still carefully put it away.

Someday, she would make Gu Tingxue willingly become her personal slave!

...

Xiangjun continued to stay obediently in her Chengxiang Palace.

Every day, she read historical books, soaked in milk baths, and gathered gossip about others in the palace.

Gu Tingxue kept his word—everything she needed in Chengxiang Palace was provided without lack. Almost anything she wanted, she got.

Xiangjun didn’t stand on ceremony with Gu Tingxue.

He was powerful, wasn’t he?

Then she would demand things beyond her rank and see what he would do.

As it turned out, the Imperial Household Department still delivered supplies according to her rank, but anything extra she desired was secretly provided by someone else.

Now, she lived in such luxury that she might as well have been a Noble Consort.

By the second month, Xiaoluzhi brought news: Consort Li had been favored by the Emperor for seven consecutive days and had been promoted to Imperial Concubine Li.

Xiangjun had been lying on the Noble Consort’s couch reading when she heard this. She sat up abruptly, excited.

"What happened? Tell me everything!"

Xiangjun had been cooped up for so long that she, a naturally restless person, was starved for fresh news. She wished Xiaoluzhi would repeat every detail over and over.

Xiaoluzhi vividly described:

"That day, His Majesty was originally going to visit Noble Consort Yuan, but when he passed through the courtyard, he heard drumming from Imperial Concubine Li’s quarters. The drumming was so lively that His Majesty grew curious and went to take a look. Who would’ve thought he’d see Imperial Concubine Li dancing under the moonlight?"

"People say His Majesty was so captivated that he stayed the night in her palace. And after that, he visited her every day for seven days straight."

Xiangjun sighed inwardly. Indeed, dancing was the best way to gain favor!

Unfortunately, her own dancing talent was limited. Though she had studied it properly, she couldn’t compare to the most prized dancer from the Shen family of Jiangnan.

Lying on the bed, Xiangjun sighed, feeling a pang of regret. If only she could see it with her own eyes.

Qinglian’s dancing must have been breathtakingly beautiful.

Xiaoluzhi, thinking she was upset, quickly comforted her. "Your Highness, don’t be sad. His Majesty must still have you in his heart. If you want to compete for favor, you’ll surely regain His Majesty’s affection."

Xiangjun made a face. "Who wants to compete for favor? I just regret not being able to see Imperial Concubine Li’s dance."

Xiaoluzhi had already noticed that his mistress didn’t care much for the Emperor.

He quickly smiled. "Since Imperial Concubine Li is so close to you, won’t you have plenty of chances to see her dance in the future?"

Xiangjun thought about it and realized he was right. She cheered up.

She beckoned Xiaoluzhi over and whispered a few words to him before saying, "Make sure to deliver my message to Imperial Concubine Li exactly as I said, understand?"

"Yes, this servant understands."

The next piece of news was that Noble Consort Yuan had given birth.

Though Noble Consort Yuan had tried her best to preserve her pregnancy, the medicine Qin Zhaoyi had given her had still affected her body. As a result, she went into early labor.

She labored all night, and His Majesty, disregarding etiquette, stayed by her side the entire time—a rare display of imperial devotion.

Finally, with the efforts of the entire Imperial Physicians’ Office, Noble Consort Yuan gave birth to a prince the next afternoon. Mother and child were safe.

The Emperor was overjoyed. He named the Fourth Prince Yuanze and announced it to the nation.

This treatment of a public announcement was something even the Empress hadn’t received when she gave birth to her legitimate son.

Xiangjun knew that with the birth of the Fourth Prince, the real storm of bloodshed was about to begin.

Sure enough, a month later, the Empress’s second son died.

This time, the culprit was Wan Niangzi.

Since the royal family’s scandals couldn’t be known to outsiders, Wan Niangzi was declared to have "died of illness." The Emperor didn’t visit Noble Consort Rong for two months, and for a time, Imperial Concubine Li was the sole favorite.

Another month passed. Due to her contributions in the southern expedition and the Empress’s assistance, Qin Guiren was finally released from confinement and restored to her position as Zhaoyi.

Everyone in Chengxiang Palace, except Xiangjun, was furious.

Qin Zhaoyi had caused their mistress so much suffering, and now, after just a few months, she had regained her position.

Xiangjun had long anticipated this day for Qin Zhaoyi. She only instructed them, "The palace is going to remain chaotic. All of you, be careful. Don’t wander around. Stay in the palace."

Sure enough, as soon as Qin Zhaoyi was free, she tried to cause trouble for Xiangjun. But with Chengxiang Palace’s gates tightly shut, and Xiangjun never appearing elsewhere, Qin Zhaoyi had no choice but to return in a huff.

Unexpectedly, two days later, Xiaoluzhi rushed in to tell Xiangjun that Imperial Concubine Li had been poisoned and was on the verge of death.

"Should Your Highness go see Imperial Concubine Li?"

...

Late at night, Xiangjun paced anxiously in Chengxiang Palace, finally waiting for Gu Tingxue’s arrival.

As soon as he entered, Xiangjun rushed up to him.

"How was Imperial Concubine Li poisoned? Who did it?"

Gu Tingxue took Xiangjun’s waving hands in his, gently lowering them.

"Calm down."

"How can I calm down? I went through so much trouble to keep her alive. How can I let her die?"

"Your Highness, rest assured. Imperial Concubine Li’s poisoning was not severe. She is fine now. This matter has already been pinned on Qin Zhaoyi."

Xiangjun asked curiously, "What exactly happened?"

"The Empress wants to adopt Imperial Concubine Li’s child."

Xiangjun sighed. "I warned her. After the Empress lost her legitimate son, she would definitely want to adopt her Third Prince and might turn against her. How could she..."

"You warned her? No wonder..."

"No wonder what?"

"Imperial Concubine Li must have taken your warning to heart."

"She took my warning, so why was she poisoned?"

"If she hadn’t been poisoned, the Third Prince would have already been taken by the Empress."

Gu Tingxue told Xiangjun that the Empress had indeed intended to poison Imperial Concubine Li.

Unexpectedly, Imperial Concubine Li had discovered the Empress’s plan and struck first, taking a small amount of the poison herself. She then framed Qin Zhaoyi for the deed. When the Emperor investigated, he discovered the Empress’s involvement, leaving her with no choice but to suffer in silence.

Xiangjun’s heart eased. Imperial Concubine Li had truly become formidable.

Now that the Emperor felt guilty toward her, he wouldn’t dare to touch her child until she had fully recovered.

Xiangjun smiled and moved closer to Gu Tingxue, flattering him. "What does the Emperor plan to do with Imperial Concubine Li’s child?"

"By palace rules, she cannot raise the Third Prince herself. Previously, he was left in Ganlu Palace for Noble Consort Rong’s sake. But Noble Consort Rong’s attempt to harm the legitimate son has disappointed the Emperor. Moreover, with her heart set only on the Fourth Prince, she certainly won’t be allowed to raise the Third Prince."

"So he will be given to the Empress?"

"The Emperor originally intended to give the child to the Empress to console her over the loss of her son. But now that Imperial Concubine Li has been poisoned, and with His Majesty’s current favor toward her, it wouldn’t be good to immediately agree, lest Imperial Concubine Li feel abandoned."

Xiangjun thought for a moment, her smile deepening. "Tingxue, what if I were to raise Imperial Concubine Li’s child?"

"You?"

"Yes." Xiangjun reached out and tugged at Gu Tingxue’s sleeve. "Tingxue, find an opportunity to suggest this to the Emperor. He will understand. This child... it would be best for me to raise him."

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun with a profound gaze. "Your Highness, what do you mean? What will the Emperor understand?"

"The Emperor dotes on the Fourth Prince and is wary of Empress Yang and her powerful family. Now that the Empress’s legitimate son is dead, why allow another prince with a powerful maternal family to exist in the palace?"

Gu Tingxue stared at Xiangjun’s seemingly innocent and delicate face, feeling an inexplicable stir in his heart. He unconsciously clenched his hand.

Xiangjun didn’t notice Gu Tingxue’s distraction. Thinking he was considering her proposal, she took his hand and continued to act coy.

"Hmm? Tingxue, is it a good idea? Didn’t you say you would help me?"

Gu Tingxue came back to his senses, feeling that this woman was truly duplicitous.

When she was angry, she called him "Lord Gu." When she needed his help, she called him "Tingxue." She changed her tone faster than flipping a page.

"Is it good or not?"

Looking at her pleading expression, Gu Tingxue still couldn’t bring himself to refuse.

"Your Highness, rest assured. You will get what you wish for."

chapters.title: I, This Palace, Wish to Be the Emperor’s Blade
chapters.content:
The Empress had once again brought up the matter of raising the Third Prince with the Emperor. Emperor Yanqing evaded the topic for a while but did not agree directly.

After returning to the Taiji Hall, the Emperor was deeply annoyed. He asked Gu Tingxue, "The Empress has lost the Second Prince; it is only right that I comfort her. But... the matter of Consort Li’s poisoning, though Consort Qin took the blame, both I and Consort Li know that Consort Qin belongs to the Empress. If I hand the Third Prince over to the Empress now, wouldn’t that break Consort Li’s heart?"

Gu Tingxue pondered for a moment and said, "Why doesn’t Your Majesty ask Consort Li for her opinion? If Consort Li is willing to let Her Majesty the Empress raise the Third Prince, Your Majesty won’t have to be caught between them."

The Emperor considered this, then ordered someone to summon Consort Li. To his surprise, as soon as he expressed his thoughts, Consort Li knelt on the ground.

"Your Majesty, this concubine knows her lowly status and cannot raise the Third Prince. This concubine only wishes to serve Your Majesty well. But the Third Prince is my own flesh and blood; this concubine still hopes to secure a bright future for him."

The Emperor’s expression darkened. A bright future? Wasn’t this hoping for her child to become the Empress’s legitimate son?

He had thought Consort Li was a docile one, but it seemed her ambitions were great as well.

"You want the Empress to raise your child?"

"How would this concubine dare? This concubine hopes that Your Majesty will let Noble Consort Lian raise the Third Prince."

The Emperor was taken aback. He hadn’t considered Noble Consort Lian at all.

Noble Consort Lian had been recuperating in the Chengxiang Hall for half a year, never appearing in public. The Emperor had nearly forgotten about her.

"Noble Consort Lian? Why?"

"Elder Sister Xiangjun is a woman of talent and kind nature; she will surely guide my child well. Moreover, Elder Sister can no longer bear children, so she will be able to devote herself entirely to raising my child."

"But Noble Consort Lian is in poor health. If the child is sent to her, I fear she won’t be able to raise him well."

"Elder Sister’s poor health is partly due to her heartache. Perhaps if Elder Sister knows she has a child to raise, she will recover."

The Emperor thought for a moment, then realized that Xiangjun was indeed a good candidate.

Xiangjun was now a Noble Consort, her rank was sufficient. She also lacked a powerful family background, so the Third Prince would not have a mother consort of overly high status, which would prevent the very thing he feared most.

Moreover, since Noble Consort Lian could no longer bear children, having her raise the Third Prince would be reasonable in every aspect. The Empress would have no grounds to object.

"I understand. You only have the best intentions for your son. However, Noble Consort Lian’s illness has not yet recovered. You will raise the child yourself for now. When Noble Consort Lian is well, you may send the child to Chengxiang Hall."

Consort Li was so overjoyed she could barely contain herself. She immediately expressed her gratitude: "Thank you, Your Majesty. May this concubine go tell Elder Sister Xiangjun?"

The Emperor couldn’t help but smile. He had never seen someone so happy about giving their child to someone else to raise.

"Go ahead."

Consort Li left joyfully. The Emperor turned to Gu Tingxue and asked, "When did Consort Li and Noble Consort Lian become so close?"

"In the past, when Consort Li was uncomfortable during her pregnancy, Noble Consort Lian would often show her extra care when she went to pay respects to Her Highness the Noble Consort. Both of them are from Jiangnan, so Noble Consort Lian sent many items from Consort Li’s hometown to comfort her homesickness. That was how Consort Li endured the discomforts of her pregnancy. It seems they became close at that time."

"No wonder..."

The Emperor suddenly remembered that after Consort Li gave birth to the Third Prince, the first thing she did was plead for Xiangjun. At the time, he had thought it was because of what the Noble Consort had told her, but now he realized it probably had nothing to do with the Noble Consort.

The Emperor’s expression darkened. After a moment of silence, he said, "Then, when Noble Consort Lian recovers, let Consort Li move to Chengxiang Hall."

...

That evening, when Gu Tingxue came to see Xiangjun, she was reading *Stratagems of the Warring States*.

Seeing Gu Tingxue approach, Xiangjun immediately beckoned him over. "Tingxue, come here for a moment. There’s a part I don’t understand; come and explain it to me."

Gu Tingxue glanced at the book. Xiangjun was reading the chapter *The Calamity of Handan*.

"Hasn’t Consort Li come to see you?" Gu Tingxue asked.

"She did. She said the Emperor agreed to let me raise the Third Prince. As soon as my health improves, the Third Prince will be sent here."

"Then why aren’t you preparing to leave Chengxiang Hall? You still have the mind to read here?"

"Not so soon. Let’s wait a little longer. It’s not the right time yet." Xiangjun placed the book in front of Gu Tingxue and said, "I’ve heard that Tingxue is very learned. Can you teach me?"

Gu Tingxue’s expression darkened. "Where did you hear that?"

Of course, Xiangjun had asked Mengmei and Xiaoluzhi to find out.

Gu Tingxue had grown up alongside the Emperor since childhood. His knowledge was all taught by the Grand Preceptor, who had even remarked that if Gu Tingxue were a normal man, he would surely have taken the imperial examinations and become a marquess or a minister.

It was a pity...

Xiangjun explained, "Tingxue, aren’t you the Chief Eunuch of the Silian Office? The Chief Eunuch is called the ‘Inner Prime Minister,’ so I thought your knowledge must be good as well."

Gu Tingxue didn’t know whether to believe her, but he didn’t dwell on the question. He glanced at the book in Xiangjun’s hands and asked, "Why are you studying these?"

"Naturally, to win the Emperor’s heart." Xiangjun said this as if it were the most natural thing in the world.

"You don’t need to study these to win the Emperor’s heart."

Xiangjun raised her eyes, not hiding the cunning and ambition in them.

"Because this palace does not want the Emperor to love me. This palace wants the Emperor to *use* me. Compared to being a favored concubine, I would rather be the Emperor’s fine blade."

A man’s love was not useless, but only shared interests could truly bind two people together.

Gu Tingxue suddenly smiled and took the book from Xiangjun’s hands.

"If Your Highness has such ambitions, Tingxue will certainly teach you well."

...

After the July selection of new consorts, the harem became lively once again. News spread constantly, and there was drama to watch almost every day.

Only Chengxiang Hall seemed unaffected.

When Gu Tingxue came to see Xiangjun, she was wearing only a very thin inner garment, lying on the Noble Consort’s couch, fanning herself while reading a book.

During this period, Gu Tingxue often came to guide Xiangjun in her studies. Seeing her like this, he said displeasedly, "Does Your Highness dress so sloppily even during the day?"

"I’m hot." Xiangjun pulled at her collar again and casually asked, "I heard someone else died in the palace?"

Gu Tingxue’s gaze seemingly indifferently passed over Xiangjun’s neck before looking ahead, his eyes fixed straight. "Among the new consorts who entered the palace, one has already died, and another has been sent to the Cold Palace."

Xiangjun exclaimed in surprise, "It’s only been a little over a month, and two are already gone? Are the Empress and Noble Consort fighting so fiercely?"

"Those two were sent into the palace by Song Feijing; they were the Noble Consort’s people."

Xiangjun clicked her tongue. The Noble Consort was indeed useless.

"What about the Empress’s people?"

"The Emperor was displeased with the consorts arranged by the Empress. He only favored one once before setting her aside."

"Does the Noble Consort still have people she can use?"

"For the time being, Song Feijing probably won’t make any more moves. The Empress has been cold-shouldered by the Emperor, so she should also quiet down for a while."

"Your Highness should continue to stay out of it. The Empress and the Noble Consort will likely keep fighting, and it won’t be easy to determine a winner between them."

Xiangjun looked at Gu Tingxue thoughtfully and smiled. "I understand."

Gu Tingxue glanced at the melted ice in the basin in Xiangjun’s palace and said, "I’ll have someone send more ice later. Will one additional basin per day be enough?"

"More than enough!"

The Noble Consort only used this much ice in a day anyway.

"Then I’ll take my leave. I need to go out of the capital for a while. I’ll come see you when I return."

Xiangjun got up to see Gu Tingxue off. As he reached the door, Gu Tingxue stretched out his hand and adjusted Xiangjun’s open collar before leaving.

After Gu Tingxue left, Mengmei entered the room and sighed. "Eunuch Tingxue is so attentive to Your Highness. No matter how busy he is, he always comes to see you. With Eunuch Tingxue’s care, even if we don’t see His Majesty, I think our current life is quite good. At least it’s peaceful; we don’t have to live in constant fear like before."

"Yes, but our peaceful days are about to end soon."

Mengmei was surprised. "Your Highness, you mean..."

"I’ve been resting for most of the year, and my illness should be cured by now. Mengmei, go and inform Physician Liu. Tell him... this palace wishes to serve His Majesty."

---

chapters.title: Regaining Favor
chapters.content:
Xiangjun had thought it through.

The Emperor had already summoned all the new consorts, but none of them had been promoted after serving him. It seemed he wasn’t particularly satisfied with any of them.

Moreover, after summoning all the new consorts once, the Emperor had only summoned Consort Li twice, then hadn’t visited the harem for several days in a row.

Xiangjun knew that the Emperor wasn’t one to live a simple life, so she chose this time to have her name card hung up. Being summoned should be almost certain.

However, after Xiangjun’s name card was hung, she wasn’t summoned by the Emperor for the next half month.

Xiangjun felt something was amiss and sent Xiaoluzhi to investigate.

Xiaoluzhi returned with the news that the people of the Shangqin Bureau had never hung up Xiangjun’s green name card at all.

When Xiaoluzhi asked, the people of the Shangqin Bureau only said that Xiangjun’s card had been unused for so long that it had broken. They had sent someone to have it remade, and it wouldn’t be hung up again until it was finished.

"Even if my card was really broken, it wouldn’t take half a month to remake. Someone must not want me to serve His Majesty."

"The one in charge of the harem now is the Empress, so the Shangqin Bureau is also under the Empress’s management." Xiaoluzhi lowered his voice and asked, "Your Highness, could it be that the Empress doesn’t want you to serve His Majesty?"

"It’s possible."

Mengmei suggested, "Your Highness, should we go pay our respects to Her Majesty the Empress and test the waters? Her Majesty the Empress has always wanted to promote you, hasn’t she?"

Xiangjun firmly refused. "No. If the Empress wants me to do something for her, should I refuse or agree? Moreover... I don’t think it’s the Empress."

Xiaoluzhi was curious. "Why?"

"The Empress has always wanted to bring me under her wing. I haven’t paid any attention to the Noble Consort for the past half year. If she knew I was well enough to serve His Majesty, she wouldn’t have no reaction at all. Even if she first removed my name card, she would at least call me to give some instructions. The Empress isn’t the kind of person who does useless things."

"Could it be that the Empress already has new people to use?" Mengmei asked.

Xiangjun still shook her head.

"The Emperor intends to reprimand the Empress and is unwilling to see the consorts recommended by her."

"Then could it be that Her Highness the Noble Consort doesn’t want you to regain favor?" Xiyu asked.

Xiangjun pondered. "I don’t think so either... But... Noble Consort Rong has a few cunning advisors around her. Who knows? Let’s go see the Noble Consort."

Mengmei was somewhat worried. "Aren’t you afraid that the Noble Consort will also ask you to do things for her? Make you fight against the Empress? The Noble Consort is incompetent; those who do things for her end up dead."

Xiangjun sneered. "What great task could the Noble Consort possibly have me do?"

But the Empress was different.

If the Empress were to force Xiangjun to do something, she wouldn’t leave her any way out.

She wasn’t like Consort Qin, who had a father fighting wars for the Emperor. She couldn’t afford to make trouble.

Mengmei was still uneasy. "But if you see the Noble Consort, what if the Empress targets you? Your Highness has been avoiding this precisely because you didn’t want to become a sacrificial pawn in their struggle, right?"

Xiangjun was indifferent. "It doesn’t matter. The Noble Consort and the Empress have already fought several rounds, both suffering greatly. The Emperor also dislikes their infighting, so they will have to restrain themselves for the sake of His Majesty’s heart. As long as I don’t act recklessly, the Empress has no reason to do anything to me."

...

The next day, Xiangjun went to see the Noble Consort.

The Noble Consort was very happy to see Xiangjun.

"Sister Xiangjun, your health is much improved?"

Xiangjun gracefully curtsied. "In response to Your Highness, Xiangjun’s health has almost fully recovered. Thanks to Your Highness’s care during this time, and the dedicated attention of Physician Liu sent by Your Highness, this concubine was able to recover so quickly."

Xiangjun chatted with the Noble Consort for a long time. The Noble Consort genuinely didn’t seem to know that she had recovered and was able to serve His Majesty.

After Xiangjun left, Caiwei suggested to the Noble Consort, "The people sent by Prime Minister Song have all been ruined. His Majesty tacitly allowed the Empress to deal with them, probably knowing they were chosen by Prime Minister Song for Your Highness. The remaining new consorts aren’t particularly useful either. Why doesn’t Your Highness promote Noble Consort Lian? Given that she came to see us instead of the Empress after recovering, she must be wholeheartedly devoted to Your Highness."

The Noble Consort thought for a moment, feeling a touch of sadness.

"Must I also do the kind of thing where I send someone to the Emperor’s bed?"

"Your Highness, how long has it been since His Majesty summoned you after the Fourth Prince was born? The death of the Second Prince has ultimately caused His Majesty to harbor resentment toward you. To have someone by His Majesty’s side who can speak on your behalf..."

Noble Consort Rong sighed. "I truly didn’t know that Lady Wan was Feijing’s person. I also didn’t expect him to go this far for me."

"Your Highness, it’s already happened, and it’s not entirely a bad thing for you. His Majesty’s feelings for you still remain. As long as you’re willing to make amends, you and His Majesty will eventually reconcile. Now that the direct line has lost the heir, our Fourth Prince is the most noble royal son in the palace. Your Highness must think more for the Fourth Prince..."

"How should I plan for Yuanze?"

"Her Majesty the Empress, with all her power, still couldn’t protect the Second Prince. Your Highness, aren’t you afraid they might target the Fourth Prince as well?"

The Noble Consort panicked. "They want to harm my Yuanze?"

"Your Highness, there’s a saying: ‘A thief can’t steal forever, but the victim can’t guard forever.’ Your Highness is alone and weak in the palace, but the Empress has many people at her disposal."

Noble Consort Rong thought about it and realized it was true. The Empress, despite losing the heir, still held all the power in the harem. She had De Consort, Consort Qin, and Noble Consort Sun by her side, as well as several newly promoted consorts.

Whereas the Noble Consort had only herself.

Noble Consort Rong’s expression darkened. She sighed, "Alright, the Mid-Autumn Night Banquet is in a few days. Have Noble Consort Lian prepare."

...

At the Mid-Autumn Night Banquet, with the Noble Consort’s recommendation, Xiangjun used a *War Drum Dance* to regain the Emperor’s favor.

Over the next three days, the Emperor summoned Xiangjun to his bedchamber every day.

Not only that, the Emperor also ordered Consort Li to move to Chengxiang Hall and entrusted the Third Prince to Xiangjun’s care.

In the following days, the Emperor either summoned Noble Consort Lian or Consort Li.

The consorts in the harem were all seething with jealousy. They privately cursed Xiangjun for her lowly behavior, acting like a dancing girl. They also said it was no wonder she was so close to Consort Li—both of them were of low birth.

Some even said they were like Zhao Feiyan and her sister.

That day, Consort Li was summoned to the Taiji Hall. Xiangjun practiced the dance steps Consort Li had taught her alone in the courtyard.

Xiangjun was the kind of person who, once she didn’t know something, would want to learn it. She wouldn’t stop until she had pushed herself to the limit. She practiced until late at night. Eventually, Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu both dozed off on the steps.

Xiangjun noticed no one was handing her a towel, so she finally stopped.

She had intended to tease Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu, but when she turned around, she saw someone standing under the corridor, staring at her motionlessly.

It was Gu Tingxue.

chapters.title: Confrontation
chapters.content:
Xiangjun was startled.

She was already annoyed with Gu Tingxue, and now he was silently staring at her with such a sinister look, which made her even less willing to acknowledge him.

Xiangjun shot him a disdainful glance and walked away to pour herself some water.

Just as she was about to drink, the cup was snatched from her hand by Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue drank the water.

"How dare you! That was my water!" Xiangjun finally raised her voice, waking Xiao Luzi and Xiyu. Seeing Gu Tingxue, the two quickly stepped forward to greet him.

"Greetings to Lord Tingxue..."

Gu Tingxue waved his hand, and the two glanced at Xiangjun. She nodded, and they tactfully retreated.

The courtyard was left with only Xiangjun, Gu Tingxue, and the pale moonlight.

Gu Tingxue's eyes were cold. "Consort Gui has become quite formidable, secretly meeting with Noble Consort Gui and using her to gain favor."

"How would I dare hide anything from you? Isn't my entire palace filled with your people?"

Gu Tingxue's expression turned grim. "Didn't I tell you to stay put in Chengxiang Hall? Do you not know how fiercely Prime Minister Song and Prime Minister Yang are fighting in the imperial court? The Empress and Noble Consort Gui are also locked in a deadly struggle in the harem. Why are you getting involved?"

"The more the Empress and Noble Consort Gui fight, the more annoyed His Majesty becomes. He won't want to deal with either side, which is exactly why I need to be his 'interpreter of feelings.' Only by staying by His Majesty's side at this time can he remember my good deeds."

"Does Consort not fear getting burned by playing with fire?"

"Do I have any other choice?" Xiangjun glared at Gu Tingxue, irritated. "Aren't all other paths blocked by you, Lord Tingxue?"

Gu Tingxue's eyes narrowed slightly as he looked at Xiangjun. "I do not understand what Consort is implying."

Xiangjun stepped closer to Gu Tingxue, staring at him. "May I ask Lord Tingxue, has my green-headed plaque been remade?"

Xiangjun had suspected that it was Gu Tingxue who had removed her plaque that day. After meeting Noble Consort Gui, she was even more certain it was his doing.

This man was truly treacherous. Even though she had left the capital, he was still guarding against her.

Gu Tingxue knew that his actions would eventually be discovered by Xiangjun, so he didn’t intend to hide it.

"I am helping Consort. Given the current situation, Consort should act with prudence to preserve herself." Gu Tingxue said with a calm expression.

Xiangjun took another step forward, and Gu Tingxue did not retreat. They were almost pressed against each other.

"Is that so? Are you really helping me, or are you trying to guard against me? Are you so afraid that I might stand firm in the palace on my own?"

Gu Tingxue lowered his gaze to look at Xiangjun. No one had ever pressed him like this before.

He felt he should be angry.

But looking at Xiangjun's bright eyes tinged with a hint of anger, he didn't seem to be that angry.

"It's not to guard against you." Gu Tingxue's voice softened. "It is to protect Consort. If my actions have caused Consort to misunderstand, then it is all my fault."

Xiangjun carefully observed Gu Tingxue's expression, feeling puzzled.

She had expected a quarrel today, but Gu Tingxue's attitude left her feeling like she was punching cotton.

Was this man really so good-tempered?

Seeing that Gu Tingxue didn't seem insincere, Xiangjun finally coldly huffed, "Tingxue, if you truly want to help me, you shouldn't guard against me. I hope you can trust me. Although I am insignificant, I still have the strength to protect myself. I won't be blown over by a little wind and rain."

"Now that Consort has gained favor through Noble Consort Gui's recommendation, in the eyes of others, you are already part of Noble Consort Gui's faction. In the future, Consort will also become a thorn in the Empress's eye. How does Consort plan to deal with that?"

"So what if I become a thorn in her eye? If the Empress targets me, how else can I serve His Majesty and Noble Consort Gui?" Xiangjun's expression was rarely serious. "Tingxue, I am just like you—I will help whoever wins. So you don't need to worry about me."

"How does Consort know that Noble Consort Gui will definitely win?"

"Because His Majesty wants Noble Consort Gui to win. Not only because His Majesty loves her, but also because he dislikes Prime Minister Yang and the aristocratic families and the clean-stream officials behind him. The Emperor is in his prime and has been on the throne for ten years. How could he still tolerate being restrained by Prime Minister Yang? Therefore, in the harem, the Empress must lose."

Gu Tingxue was somewhat impressed by Xiangjun's words. She had judged everything correctly.

"Consort has not wasted the past six months of study."

Xiangjun, flattered, glanced at Gu Tingxue. "Don't you know who my teacher is?"

"However, you must understand that Prime Minister Song, who supports Noble Consort Gui, is a ruthless man. Being their pawn is very dangerous."

"Then I must be a useful pawn."

"That's not what I meant."

"Then what does Tingxue mean?"

"You don't need to rely on Noble Consort Gui. You have me."

Xiangjun looked deeply at Gu Tingxue. "Lord Tingxue, you probably don't understand me well enough. The most important things must be held in my own hands. So I cannot entrust my life completely to another. You said before that you are not my servant. Today, Xiangjun also wants to tell Lord Tingxue that I am not your plaything."

Gu Tingxue smiled.

"Consort has great ambition. Then I wish Consort success in all her endeavors."

Gu Tingxue turned to leave but was stopped by Xiangjun.

"Tingxue, my plaque won't be tampered with again, will it?"

Gu Tingxue, with his back to Xiangjun, said in a deep voice, "Consort, rest assured. It won't."

...

Although her conversation with Gu Tingxue that day wasn't particularly pleasant, Xiangjun believed that Gu Tingxue wasn't a petty man. Whatever they had agreed upon, he would certainly follow through.

So in the days that followed, everything went smoothly for her. Gu Tingxue didn't cause any trouble, and within the palace, Xiangjun and Consort Li remained the most favored.

Of course, Xiangjun knew that she was now associated with Noble Consort Gui, so every three days she would persuade the Emperor to visit Noble Consort Gui.

Although the Emperor still did not stay overnight at Noble Consort Gui's, he would visit her for meals almost every other day.

Noble Consort Gui felt somewhat upset, but since Xiangjun had managed to bring the Emperor to her, and it was she who couldn't keep him, she couldn't blame Xiangjun.

The harem was temporarily at peace, but in the imperial court, Prime Minister Yang and Prime Minister Song were once again at each other's throats over the matter of establishing the heir.

In Weiyang Palace, the Empress was also deeply worried. She feared that the Emperor would truly make the Fourth Prince the Crown Prince.

"Lady Fang, I don't understand what His Majesty is thinking. Why would he have the Third Prince raised by Consort Lian, who has such an insignificant background?" the Empress said coldly.

"The Third Prince's birth mother was a lowly dancer, and His Majesty had him raised by Consort Lian, who also comes from an undistinguished family. This clearly tells everyone that the Third Prince can never become the Crown Prince. His Majesty is paving the way for Noble Consort Gui's Fourth Prince."

"Your Majesty, I know you remember the kindness of Consort Lian saving the Second Prince, but now she is Noble Consort Gui's person. We are in a life-and-death struggle with her."

"I know." The Empress looked at her reflection in the mirror, lightly touching the fine lines at the corner of her eyes, and sneered. "The autumn hunt is coming soon. You should go out of the palace to see your father..."

chapters.title: Autumn Hunt
chapters.content:
This year, the Emperor planned to go on an autumn hunt, and the list of consorts included Xiangjun and Consort Li. Among the princes, the First Prince and Yuanji were to accompany them. The Fourth Prince, Yuanze, was not going due to his premature birth and ongoing recovery.

Xiangjun happily made several new sets of riding attire for the two of them.

Consort Li held the Third Prince, Yuanji, and smiled as Xiangjun showed her one outfit after another.

"Which one do you like?" Xiangjun asked with a smile. "There are four sets in total. We each get two. You pick first."

"Sister, you wear them. I don't know how to ride a horse."

"I don't know how to ride either. It doesn't matter if we can ride or not; what matters is that we look good."

"Forget it. I don't want them. I don't want to wear riding attire without riding a horse and be laughed at." Consort Li glanced at Yuanji. "Moreover, Yuanji is going this time, so I should take good care of him to prevent any accidents during the autumn hunt."

Xiangjun sat down next to Consort Li, playing with the adorable Yuanji, and said helplessly, "The children in this palace are really hard to raise. Sister, no matter how careful you are, it's not wrong."
