"Yes, even the Second Prince, the Empress's son, was poisoned to death. Let alone me, a mere Consort."

Consort Li still felt a lingering fear when she thought about it.

"You were sick at that time, so you didn't see it. The Second Prince died at his birthday banquet, in front of everyone, from poisoning—blood flowing from his seven orifices... Although it was later found out that it was Lady Wan who did it, but... people in the palace privately say it was Noble Consort Gui's doing. Xiangjun, the women in this palace hide their true selves so deeply."

Xiangjun comforted Consort Li, "Don't be too afraid. No matter what, our Yuanji won't block Yuanze's path."

"I know. That's why Yuanji will be safe with Sister. If he were the Empress's child, he might be harmed by Noble Consort Gui."

"Why are you so afraid of Noble Consort Gui?"

"Sister Xiangjun, you don't know Noble Consort Gui's methods..."

Consort Li thought for a moment, then called for the attendants. She had the Third Prince taken away first, then dismissed everyone else, and pulled Xiangjun into the inner room to sit down.

"What are you going to tell me? Why be so cautious?"

Consort Li looked worried. "Actually, there's something I've been wanting to tell you."

"Go on."

"Sister Xiangjun, you must be careful around Noble Consort Gui. I know she treats you well, but she is unfathomable. Even the Emperor's trusted eunuch, Lord Gu Tingxue, has been won over by her. That Lord Gu is someone who is only loyal to the Emperor and only does the Emperor's bidding."

"Sister Qinglian, why do you say that? Have you discovered something?"

"When I was in Ganlu Palace, I encountered Lord Gu visiting Noble Consort Gui in the middle of the night twice. He entered Noble Consort Gui's room."

Xiangjun's heart tightened. "Sister Qinglian, are you sure it was Lord Gu?"

"Certain. I saw it with my own eyes. Actually, I shouldn't have encountered him at all. The times Lord Gu went to Noble Consort Gui's palace were always after the palace gates were locked. I should have stayed in my side hall. But during that time, Yuanji was sick, and I was worried. I couldn't sleep at night, so I would sneak to Noble Consort Gui's main hall to check on Yuanji. Also, since I learned dance from a young age, my steps are very light, so I wasn't discovered."

Xiangjun pondered, "If you accidentally encountered him twice, who knows how many times they've met in secret when you didn't see them."

"Exactly... You and I both know who Gu Tingxue is. If even he is working for Noble Consort Gui, you can imagine how dominant she is in the harem. I'm afraid that Sister Xiangjun is being used by her, and if she decides to eliminate you in the future... the example of Lady Wan is right before our eyes."

"I know." Xiangjun took Consort Li's hand. "Sister Qinglian, don't worry. I will be careful. I won't do anything immoral for Noble Consort Gui."

Consort Li noticed that Xiangjun's hand was trembling slightly and quickly held it.

"Sister Xiangjun, I'm sorry. Did my words scare you?"

Xiangjun looked at her hand. She wasn't trembling from fear, but from anger.

Gu Tingxue had actually been secretly colluding with Noble Consort Gui behind her back.

...

Finally, the day of the autumn hunt arrived. A large group set off towards the Nanyuan hunting grounds, preparing for a twenty-day hunt.

In addition to the consorts from the harem, many of the Emperor's close officials from the imperial court were also present. Besides Gu Tingxue, whom the Emperor took everywhere, he also brought Right Prime Minister Song Feijing and several young close officials.

Upon arriving at the temporary palace, Xiangjun and Consort Li were arranged to stay in the same palace hall. After settling in, they accompanied Yuanji for dinner, not expecting the Emperor to arrive.

Xiangjun had thought the Emperor would stay with the Empress tonight, but she learned that the Empress had fallen ill from the journey.

"I've come to see Yuanji. Did he have any discomfort during the journey?"

Xiangjun answered carefully.

The Emperor was satisfied and took Xiangjun's hand. "Shall I stay with you tonight?"

"Your Majesty, why not go and keep Sister Qinglian company? It's the Third Prince's first time out of the palace. This subject wants to spend time with Yuanji. Could you please keep Sister Qinglian company on my behalf?"

"If all the women in the palace were as considerate of each other as you two, I wouldn't be so troubled." The Emperor glanced at Consort Li and said softly, "Then tonight, I will go to Consort Li's."

The Emperor sat for a while longer before going to meet with his officials, saying he would return later.

After the Emperor left, Consort Li pulled Xiangjun aside. "Sister, His Majesty came to see you, but you always push him to me... I don't want to compete with you for favor."

"Silly sister, I know. But Yuanji is your child. Even though he is raised by me, no one can replace his birth mother. You should try to rise higher. Once you reach the rank of a concubine, you can raise your child yourself. So you need to seize the Emperor's favor."

Consort Li hesitated, "With my background... can I really reach the rank of a concubine?"

"Why not? Opportunities must be waited for."

That night, the Emperor arrived with Gu Tingxue.

After the Emperor and Consort Li retired for the night, only Gu Tingxue and a young eunuch remained on guard outside.

At the third watch of the night, Xiao Luzi from the main hall came with several people to invite the palace attendants on night duty to the tea room for some refreshments.

"Our mistress thinks that the attendants guarding the Emperor have had a hard time. Now that His Majesty has fallen asleep, we can take over for a short while. Everyone can go have some tea to warm up before coming back."

Guarding at night was the most tedious task, so everyone was willing to take a short break.

However, with Gu Tingxue present, the attendants all looked at him, waiting for his instructions.

Gu Tingxue waved his hand, allowing them to go. "You may go. I will stay here with His Majesty."

The attendants happily went to have tea and rest.

Once everyone had left, only Xiao Luzi and the others remained, standing at the door with their backs to Gu Tingxue.

Suddenly, a hand reached around Gu Tingxue's waist from behind, pulling him into an embrace.

A voice whispered in Gu Tingxue's ear, "Tingxue, you have such a cruel heart. It's been so long since we've seen each other. Finally, you came with the Emperor to my palace, yet you didn't even come to see me once."

chapters.title: The Sentimental Man
chapters.content:
The Emperor and Concubine Li were inside the room, yet Xiangjun was holding Gu Tingxue at the doorway—truly audacious.

Gu Tingxue had no choice but to pull Xiangjun away quickly.

Xiaoluzi and Mengmei pretended to see nothing, continuing to stand guard outside with their eyes fixed straight ahead.

Gu Tingxue took Xiangjun to her room, shutting the door the moment they entered before throwing her onto the soft couch.

"What madness has come over you?" Gu Tingxue darkened his face.

"Since we parted at Chengxiang Hall, this palace has not seen Tingxue for a long time. I have missed you dearly. Why haven’t you come to see me, Tingxue?"

Gu Tingxue’s expression was cold. "Your Majesty is currently in high favor. It seems you won’t need Tingxue for a while."

"Who said I don’t need you? I need you very much."

Gu Tingxue found Xiangjun’s behavior today truly strange, so he patiently explained, "These days, I’ve been helping His Majesty with matters. There are many things to arrange for the autumn hunt. This humble servant truly hasn’t had the time to visit Your Majesty."

Xiangjun let out a cold laugh, her voice turning icy. "No time, or is it that Tingxue’s time has all been taken by someone else?"

"What does Your Majesty mean?"

"You have no time to see me, but you have time to visit the Noble Consort?" Xiangjun questioned.

Seeing that Gu Tingxue remained silent, Xiangjun took it as an admission.

Xiangjun was so angry her lips trembled. "What has the Noble Consort given you? To make you run to her place every night?"

"When have I gone to the Noble Consort’s every night?"

"If not every night, then you admit you often go to the Noble Consort’s place?"

Gu Tingxue was at a loss, having been cornered by Xiangjun’s words.

Xiangjun was so furious her nose almost twisted. She spoke sarcastically, "No wonder the Noble Consort always smiles at you during palace banquets. Hmph, she doesn’t even bother to hide it. So you two have been involved all along!"

Gu Tingxue was momentarily speechless.

The Noble Consort’s smiles were purely out of courtesy.

"Your Majesty... it’s not what you think."

"Then what is it?"

Gu Tingxue said nothing.

Xiangjun was so angry she laughed. "What’s the matter? Has Eunuch Gu been exposed and left speechless? Let me tell you, the Noble Consort has both His Majesty’s love and the support of Grand General Wang, Minister Song, and the Prince of Jin. In the Noble Consort’s heart, a eunuch like you probably can’t even secure a place. Eunuch Gu, don’t end up heartbroken for nothing!"

Xiangjun’s words were indeed harsh, but Gu Tingxue didn’t feel angry. Instead, he found her angry appearance rather adorable.

Gu Tingxue couldn’t help but curl the corners of his lips.

"Your Majesty used to call me by my name, Tingxue. Now you’re so angry you have to call me Eunuch Gu?"

Xiangjun sneered. "Isn’t it because I fear I’m unworthy of calling you Tingxue? Only those close to you can call you that. You and I are now estranged."

"You’re overthinking, Your Majesty."

"Am I overthinking, or do you have a guilty conscience?" Xiangjun slammed the table and stood up. "Eunuch Gu, my person cannot be unfaithful to me. You can only belong to me alone. If you choose the Noble Consort, then let’s part ways amicably!"

Seeing that Xiangjun was truly angry, Gu Tingxue couldn’t tease her anymore.

Gu Tingxue sighed and softly said, "Your Majesty, I’ve already said I’ve been helping His Majesty. Tingxue hasn’t lied to you."

"Helping His Majesty requires you to go to the Noble Consort’s room every night?"

Gu Tingxue saw she still didn’t understand, so he continued to explain, "His Majesty ordered me to assist the Noble Consort, so I often need to go see the Noble Consort and heed her summons."

Xiangjun finally realized and asked in surprise, "His Majesty ordered you to serve the Noble Consort and work for her?"

Gu Tingxue nodded.

Xiangjun was confused. "Why?"

"His Majesty does not trust Song Feijing."

"Does the Noble Consort know you were sent by His Majesty?"

"Of course not. She thinks I am sincerely pledging allegiance to her."

Xiangjun’s anger instantly vanished. She slowly supported herself against the table and sat back down on the soft couch, pondering.

Xiangjun muttered, "Why didn’t I think of this earlier? As expected, His Majesty is cunning..."

"Are you still angry, Your Majesty?"

Xiangjun felt a little guilty but stubbornly said, "Then why didn’t you tell me earlier?"

"This humble servant had no time."

"How could you have no time? In the past, even if Tingxue only had half an hour, he would find a way to come see me."

Gu Tingxue didn’t answer because he had indeed been deliberately avoiding Xiangjun.

She tugged at Gu Tingxue’s belt. "Tingxue, come see me more often, okay? Please, don’t avoid me."

"When have I ever avoided you?"

"I don’t believe you. His Majesty has had me attend his bed almost every night these days, yet you haven’t come once. You still say you’re not avoiding me?"

Gu Tingxue’s expression suddenly changed. He seemed to want to say something but hesitated, his eyes filled with indescribable pain.

Xiangjun had been so favored lately that she was almost exclusively favored—if not her, then it was Concubine Li from her palace.

Gu Tingxue thought of this and felt as if countless snakes were gnawing at his body.

Xiangjun also froze for a moment.

Because Gu Tingxue looked as if he were about to shatter.

She felt confused and couldn’t understand why Gu Tingxue was looking at her like that.

"Tingxue..."

Xiangjun wanted to place her hand on Gu Tingxue’s shoulder, but Gu Tingxue quickly stepped back, not letting her touch him.

Xiangjun’s hand grabbed the air, and she looked at Gu Tingxue with a wronged expression.

"The palace maids’ tea should be finished. This humble servant will go back to stand guard."

Gu Tingxue turned to leave, but Xiangjun rushed forward and hugged him from behind.

"Their tea is finished, and His Majesty’s place won’t lack attendants. Tingxue, stay here with me. Coax me to sleep, okay? I haven’t seen you for so long, and I’ve been very lonely."

Gu Tingxue took a deep breath, clenched his fists, and endured until the veins on his hands bulged.

He lowered his voice. "Your Majesty is currently the most favored concubine in the harem. How could you still be lonely?"

"Even if someone lies beside me every night, if it’s not the person my heart desires, I will still feel lonely."

Gu Tingxue’s voice became even deeper and hoarse. "Your Majesty is speaking treasonous words again."

Xiangjun moved in front of Gu Tingxue, hooked her arm around his neck, tilted her head, and stared at him with her watery eyes, as if looking at her lover.

But Gu Tingxue knew Xiangjun wasn’t serious.

Gu Tingxue’s gaze turned cold as he broke free from Xiangjun’s hold.

"Tingxue will come to see Your Majesty more often in the future. I’ll take my leave now."

Gu Tingxue still left with a firm attitude, but Xiangjun had caught a glimpse of his true feelings.

When Mengmei entered, she saw Xiangjun sitting smugly on the soft couch, sipping tea, her feet happily swinging lightly.

"Your Majesty? What happened? Why are you so happy?"

Xiangjun narrowed her eyes, unable to stop smiling. "I discovered something interesting."

"What is it?"

"Our all-powerful Eunuch Tingxue seems to have a weakness."

"What weakness?"

Xiangjun smiled mysteriously but didn’t answer.

Because even if she said it, no one would believe her.

Who would have thought that our Eunuch Gu, who kills without blinking, wields immense power, and is seen by everyone as the Emperor’s hound, would turn out to be such a sentimental man?

---

chapters.title: The First Day of the Hunt
chapters.content:
The first day of the autumn hunt.

In Great Qi, noblewomen were expected to be skilled in rites, music, archery, and charioteering, so women of the court also participated in the autumn hunt.

The Empress was unwell and only attended the pre-hunt sacrificial ceremony with the Emperor, with no intention of joining the subsequent hunt. Thus, Noble Consort Rong, as the highest-ranking concubine, naturally took the Empress’s place, mounting her horse to stay by the Emperor’s side.

Today, Noble Consort Rong wore a bright red riding outfit, looking valiant and graceful on horseback like a jewel on the grasslands, drawing countless admiring gazes.

But the Empress’s eyes were fixed firmly on the Noble Consort’s clothes.

Noble Consort Rong’s audacity in wearing bright red, a color reserved for the Empress, was truly outrageous. Yet, no one present seemed to find anything wrong with it.

The Empress was seething with anger but had to endure it to maintain her dignity as Empress.

Xiangjun noticed the Empress’s gaze and then looked at the Emperor, only to find his expression dark—but not directed at the Noble Consort.

Following the Emperor’s line of sight, Xiangjun saw someone staring intently at the Noble Consort.

The man wore a crane robe bestowed by the Emperor, appeared to be around thirty, and exuded an air of elegance and nobility, making him quite the dashing figure.

Xiangjun knew who he was. Since Yang the Prime Minister was absent and too old, this man must be Song Feijing, the current Prime Minister.

This was the first time Xiangjun had seen Song Feijing in either of her lives.

He was truly audacious, staring so boldly at the Emperor’s woman. Did he really think the Emperor couldn’t do without him?

Gu Tingxue, who had been riding behind the Emperor, naturally urged his horse forward a few steps, blocking Song Feijing’s line of sight.

Song Feijing seemed to come back to his senses, withdrawing his gaze and mounting his horse.

The Emperor’s expression improved slightly. If not for the need to use Song Feijing to suppress the Yang family, he would have killed this shameless dog long ago.

The Emperor glanced at Gu Tingxue with satisfaction.

As expected, his servant, whom he had raised since childhood, understood him best.

"Ah! Help!"

Everyone heard a delicate cry for help and looked over.

They saw Xiangjun halfway up her horse, unable to swing her leg over in time, and the horse suddenly reared, throwing her to the ground.

The Emperor cried out, "Consort Lian!"

The captain of the Imperial Guards, Zhou Zidu, was following behind. With quick eyes and hands, he grabbed Xiangjun’s arm and pulled her back just in time, controlling the horse as well. Xiangjun was unharmed, though covered in dust.

The one who had saved Xiangjun was Zhou Zidu, the captain of the Imperial Guards whom the Emperor currently held in high regard.

Zhou Zidu knelt before the Emperor with a righteous expression. "Just now, in my haste, this humble servant acted improperly toward Consort Lian."

"It’s fine. If not for you, Our beloved Consort Lian would have been trampled by the horse."

Xiangjun sat on the ground, covered in dirt, looking pitiful with red-rimmed eyes. "Your Majesty, your humble concubine... your humble concubine has been utterly humiliated."

Everyone burst into laughter. Even the Noble Consort, who had been worried lately, couldn’t help but be amused by Xiangjun’s disheveled appearance.

Only Gu Tingxue, riding beside the Emperor, had a face as dark as Judge Bao’s as he looked at Xiangjun.

Xiangjun pretended not to notice Gu Tingxue’s gloomy expression and continued to wipe her face in a wronged manner. This only made her face look even more of a mess.

The Emperor couldn’t help but laugh. "Aren’t you embarrassed enough? Hurry and stand up."

A young eunuch quickly came over to help Xiangjun to her feet.

Xiangjun stood up unsteadily.

"Is Sister Xiangjun alright?" the Noble Consort asked with concern.

Xiangjun shook her head. "I’m fine."

The other concubines laughed at Xiangjun. Especially Qin Zhao Yi, who said sarcastically, "Don’t laugh at Consort Lian, everyone. After all, she comes from a small family with no background. It’s understandable that she doesn’t know how to ride."

Qin Zhao Yi’s words were truly inappropriate. No matter what, Xiangjun was the Emperor’s woman. To speak of her like this in front of the officials was to embarrass the Emperor.

The Noble Consort immediately said, "Consort Lian is from Jiangnan, where literary culture thrives. It’s normal that she doesn’t know how to ride."

A nearby official added, "This must be the Consort Lian who writes in the 'Lianhua' script. Your Majesty, Consort Lian’s hands are for writing, so it’s no wonder she can’t hold the reins."

With two people helping the Emperor save face, the image-conscious Emperor’s mood improved significantly.

"Since you can’t ride, you should go back and rest."

Xiangjun didn’t get angry. She just looked at the Emperor with a wronged expression. "Your Majesty, although your humble concubine cannot ride, she wishes to learn. There are still over ten days left in the autumn hunt. Your humble concubine will definitely learn. As your concubine, she will not bring shame to Your Majesty."

Qin Zhao Yi said displeasedly, "Are we supposed to wait for you to learn? Your Majesty... you promised me you’d get me a fox to make a hat."

The Emperor was very annoyed by Qin Zhao Yi’s constant interruptions. He glanced at her, and Qin Zhao Yi had no choice but to shut up sulkily.

The Emperor looked back at Xiangjun, whose determined expression made him feel a surge of affection. She was so obedient and knew how to strive for his honor.

The Emperor casually pointed at Zhou Zidu, who was standing next to Xiangjun. "Zidu, your riding and archery skills are the best. You will teach Consort Lian to ride. If you succeed, there will be a reward."

"Yes, this humble servant obeys."

The Emperor led the officials and concubines away on horseback. Zhou Zidu took Xiangjun to the grassland to practice riding.

Once they were alone, Xiangjun immediately changed her expression, smiling at Zhou Zidu. "Captain Zhou, we meet again. Do you still remember me?"

Zhou Zidu’s face turned red from Xiangjun’s smile. He lowered his head. "This humble servant naturally remembers!"

In truth, Zhou Zidu had always been paying attention to Xiangjun.

He had thought that after Xiangjun entered the palace, he would never hear of her again. She would probably disappear into the harem like so many other women, silent and forgotten.

But not long after, Zhou Zidu heard about a Consort Lian in the palace who had exquisite handwriting and had become famous in the capital.

Upon inquiring, he learned that Consort Lian was Xiangjun.

Soon after, he heard she had miscarried, been wrongly accused, and sent to the Palace Discipline Office. After her release, she had been ill for more than half a year.

At that time, he thought she must be having a hard time in the palace.

It made sense. She had come from Jiangnan, had no one to rely on in the capital, and lacked a powerful family background. With her pure and kind nature, she was bound to be bullied by the other women in the harem.

Just now, seeing her in such good spirits, he had thought she was doing well in the palace. But when he saw Qin Zhao Yi humiliating her in front of everyone, he feared that behind the scenes, the bullying would only be worse. This made him feel even more pity for Xiangjun.

"Does Consort Lian live well in the palace?" Zhou Zidu asked carefully.

Seeing Zhou Zidu’s heartbroken expression, Xiangjun felt inexplicably confused.

But since he was already feeling sorry for her, Xiangjun naturally took the opportunity to play along. She lowered her head, looking as if her heart had been struck, and her eyes instantly reddened.

Seeing Xiangjun like this, Zhou Zidu’s heart ached even more.

As expected, she was a pitiful lotus flower.

chapters.title: Applying Medicine
chapters.content:
Xiangjun had been learning horseback riding from Zhou Zidu for half a day. Since she had to pretend to be weak and helpless, she only managed to learn how to mount a horse in that time.

Yet, Xiangjun still felt she had gained something that day—at least she had obtained Zhou Zidu’s promise: *"If Your Highness has any needs, Zhou Zidu will do his utmost to help you."*

On the first day of the autumn hunt, a banquet was to be held.

It was only at the banquet that Xiangjun learned that the one who had taken first place that day was none other than Noble Consort Rong.

Xiangjun couldn’t help but sigh in admiration. Noble Consort Rong was indeed deserving of her favored status. The way she had mounted her horse that day—so graceful and unrestrained—it was no wonder so many were captivated by her.

After all, in the past, Xiangjun had only ever seen her sitting high in her position as Noble Consort within the palace, never like this—so radiant and dashing.

The Emperor looked at Noble Consort Rong with pride and praised her: *"Seeing Consort Rong ride and shoot today reminds me of the first time I saw you. So many years have passed, yet your riding skills are still this excellent—no worse than any man."*

Consort Qin, seeing the Emperor and Noble Consort Rong so affectionate, felt a pang of jealousy and said cuttingly: *"I hear Noble Consort’s riding and archery were taught by Grand General Wang. Truly extraordinary."*

This remark immediately darkened the Emperor’s face. Noble Consort Rong’s expression turned awkward, and when she glanced at Song Feijing, she saw him gripping his wine cup tightly, looking thoroughly displeased.

Xiangjun sighed inwardly. These people were all in their thirties—how could they still be so upset over matters of love and affection every day?

Xiangjun exchanged a glance with Consort Li, and the two tacitly lowered their heads, pretending not to notice the tension in the air.

That night, the Emperor did not go to Noble Consort Rong’s quarters, nor to Consort Qin’s. Instead, he came to the palace where Xiangjun and Consort Li resided, staying the night with Consort Li.

...

The next day, Xiangjun was supposed to continue her horseback riding lessons. She arrived at the agreed-upon location and waited for Zhou Zidu, but after a long time, he still didn’t appear.

Finally, footsteps approached from behind. Xiangjun arranged her face into an innocent and guileless expression, turning to see who it was—only to meet a pair of sinister, cold eyes.

"Who are you?" Xiangjun asked in surprise.

Gu Tingxue’s gaze was icy enough to freeze.

"Does Your Highness find this disappointing? The Emperor felt that Zhou Zidu is, after all, an outer court official, and it is improper for him to teach the ladies of the harem how to ride. So, His Majesty ordered this humble servant to take over for Commander Zhou. Commander Zhou is currently escorting His Majesty. If Your Highness finds this humble servant unsatisfactory, I can go and request His Majesty to send Commander Zhou back?"

"No, no need."

Xiangjun didn’t dare. Just the day before, the Emperor had been angry about the matter of Grand General Wang teaching Noble Consort Rong to ride. She didn’t want to provoke His Majesty’s wrath.

"Truly no need? It seems Your Highness quite likes Commander Zhou. Doesn’t Your Highness need more support in the harem? Wouldn’t an extra ally in the imperial court be beneficial?"

Xiangjun forced an awkward smile. "The imperial court and the harem both have Tingxue, don’t they? This concubine has you alone, and that is enough."

Though Gu Tingxue was still displeased, Xiangjun’s words did somewhat appease him. He coldly huffed and led the horse over.

In front of Gu Tingxue, Xiangjun didn’t need to pretend. And Gu Tingxue was indeed a strict teacher—unlike Zhou Zidu, who would coax her along. Gu Tingxue had no such patience and knew Xiangjun’s abilities, so he drilled her mercilessly all morning.

Xiangjun could endure hardship, and after half a day, though her inner thighs were chafed and painful, she didn’t utter a single complaint.

Gu Tingxue noticed she was enduring the pain and said, "That’s enough for today. His Majesty should be returning soon. Let’s stop here and continue tomorrow."

...

That day, the Emperor had originally intended to rest in Xiangjun’s quarters, but upon learning that she had been injured while practicing horseback riding, he decided it would be inappropriate to share her bed. So, he went to Consort Li’s instead.

However, the Emperor was still very pleased with Xiangjun’s efforts. He promised her that once she learned to ride properly, he would bestow one of his own imperial horses upon her.

That night, Xiangjun finally had the time to examine her wounds. Only then did she realize that not only her thighs but even her calves were chafed raw.

Xiangjun made a pitiful face and was about to have Mengmei fetch some medicinal ointment when Gu Tingxue arrived.

As soon as Gu Tingxue entered, the others in the room discreetly withdrew, leaving only Xiangjun and him.

Xiangjun lay on the bed, covering her legs with a blanket, and watched as Gu Tingxue took out a box of ointment.

"This is the secret medicine you used before. Apply it and rest for two days. Once you’re healed, continue practicing."

"How did you know I was chafed?"

"It’s normal to get chafed the first time you learn to ride."

Xiangjun thought for a moment, then lifted the blanket and said to Gu Tingxue, "Tingxue, help me apply it."

Gu Tingxue’s expression stiffened, and he averted his gaze. "It’s inconvenient."

Xiangjun blinked. "What’s inconvenient about it? Haven’t you seen it before, Tingxue?"

Gu Tingxue’s face changed, and he lowered his head, hiding the darkness in his eyes.

"Your Highness, this humble servant only came to deliver the medicine. Please apply it yourself and rest. You still have to continue tomorrow."

Seeing that Gu Tingxue was not to be teased, Xiangjun had no choice but to grab his hand urgently and say, "I’ll apply it myself, then. Don’t leave in a hurry—I still have something to ask you..."

"What does Your Highness wish to ask?"

Xiangjun opened the ointment jar, scooped out some medicine, and casually asked, "Has Her Majesty the Empress shown any unusual movements?"

Since she needed to apply the medicine, Xiangjun had only draped a thin, knee-length white cloth over her lower body. She pulled the cloth up slightly, exposing the root of her thigh.

Gu Tingxue took a deep breath, subtly shifting his gaze away, his voice hoarse as he asked, "Why does Your Highness ask about the Empress? Have you learned something?"

"I don’t know anything. It’s just that the Empress fell ill as soon as she arrived and hasn’t participated in the hunt. I find it strange and feel uneasy. So I wanted to ask Tingxue."

Gu Tingxue’s gaze kept being drawn to Xiangjun’s hand applying the medicine. He frowned and said, "Does Your Highness have to apply it now?"

"What does my applying medicine have to do with our conversation? Why are you in such a hurry, Tingxue?"

Gu Tingxue had no choice but to suppress the growing irritation in his heart and continue talking about the Empress.

"Prime Minister Yang does have some connections with people here at the hunting grounds, but I haven’t yet discovered what he intends to do."

This surprised Xiangjun. "There are things even you don’t know?"

"This isn’t the palace. My informants can’t uncover every piece of information. The Yang family has stood unshaken for decades—naturally, they have their own capabilities. I’m no immortal."

"Is that so? In my heart, Tingxue, you’re as all-knowing and powerful as a celestial being." Xiangjun closed the ointment box and said to Gu Tingxue, "Trouble you to hand me a handkerchief to wipe my hands."

Gu Tingxue took out a handkerchief and handed it to Xiangjun.

Xiangjun made no move to take it. Instead, she stretched out her hand, expecting Gu Tingxue to wipe it for her.

Gu Tingxue took a deep breath and, without looking at her, wiped her hands.

After finishing, he tried to withdraw the handkerchief, but Xiangjun grabbed his hand again.

"What is Your Highness doing..."

"I remember I once said that you, Tingxue, have a pair of beautiful hands."

Xiangjun caressed Gu Tingxue’s hand, then guided it to the chafed area where she had just applied the medicine.

"Tingxue, the medicine on this concubine’s body hasn’t been rubbed in yet. But this concubine has already cleaned her hands. I’ll have to trouble you to help me rub it in."

---

chapters.title: Consort Yue
chapters.content:
He was a servant. Attending to his master’s medicine was his duty.

Gu Tingxue slowly rubbed in the ointment, but Xiangjun was still restless...

He didn’t know with what frame of mind he finished applying the medicine. By the time it was fully absorbed, he quickly withdrew his hand, took two steps back, and said, "Your Highness, this humble servant must go attend to His Majesty. I’ll take my leave."

"Will Tingxue still come to teach me horseback riding tomorrow?"

"Yes."

Gu Tingxue left swiftly, and Xiangjun finally lay down, satisfied.

What a good mood.

...

The next few days passed uneventfully. By the sixth day, Xiangjun was already able to ride freely across the grasslands.

The feeling of galloping so freely was truly wonderful.

Gu Tingxue even brought his sea eastern hawk, allowing it to soar freely across the grasslands.

Such exhilaration was something neither Xiangjun nor Gu Tingxue had experienced in a long time.

The two finally came to a stop, and Gu Tingxue handed Xiangjun the meat he had prepared in advance to feed the hawk.

"Is this the same sea eastern hawk that Noble Consort Rong gave you for the Dowager Empress’s birthday?"

"Yes."

Xiangjun couldn’t help but sigh, "The Dowager Empress is truly kind to you."

"The Dowager Empress did this because gifting a sea eastern hawk to a eunuch like me was also a way to humiliate Grand General Wang. She only did it to please His Majesty."

Xiangjun thought for a moment, then shook her head. "I think the Dowager Empress simply wanted to give it to you."

Gu Tingxue fell silent.

Xiangjun, not noticing his discomfort, asked eagerly, "Next time there’s a hunt, can I participate?"

Gu Tingxue: "Do you know how to shoot?"

Xiangjun: "No."

Gu Tingxue: "Then how will you hunt?"

Xiangjun thought for a moment. "What if you teach me?"

"Others take years to learn how to shoot from horseback. Do you think you can master it in a few days? Dream on. Focus on learning to ride properly first, then think about the rest."

Xiangjun had no choice but to obediently follow Gu Tingxue for a few more laps around the grassland before returning.

...

Over these days of hunting, Noble Consort Rong and Consort Qin had been evenly matched, and the Emperor had taken turns favoring both. But Consort Qin had still been summoned more often.

The night before, Noble Consort Rong had attended to the Emperor.

However, when the concubines went to pay their respects to the Empress the next day, they found that Noble Consort Rong showed no signs of having received the Emperor’s favor. Instead, her eyes were dark and swollen.

Noble Consort Rong was even mocked by Consort Qin, who said that she was too old to properly serve the Emperor and should step aside for younger concubines.

The Empress played the role of a mediator, lightly reprimanding Consort Qin, but her face clearly showed schadenfreude.

Xiangjun also found it strange. It had been months since the Emperor had last summoned Noble Consort Rong. Now that he finally had, she should have been happy—so why did she look so heartbroken?

Consort Qin, seeing that Noble Consort Rong was in no state to fight back, found it boring and turned her attention to Xiangjun, asking how her riding lessons were going.

Xiangjun replied, "I’ve learned."

Consort Qin raised an eyebrow. "Then shouldn’t Honored Consort Lian be able to join us in the hunt?"

Xiangjun quickly replied modestly, "I’m not ready for hunting. Eunuch Tingxue says my riding skills are far from proficient—I can only keep up with the ladies at most."

A report came from outside, and the Emperor suddenly entered.

The Emperor stood at the door, looking at Xiangjun. "You can already ride? My Honored Consort Lian truly picks up everything with ease."

The concubines immediately rose to greet the Emperor.

The Emperor seemed to be in an exceptionally good mood today. He waved his hand. "All rise."

The Emperor strode to the Empress’s side and sat down, looking pleased.

The Empress noticed the Emperor’s good mood and asked, "Your Majesty seems particularly happy today. If there’s good news, won’t you share it with your concubines and sisters? Let us rejoice together."

The Emperor took the Empress’s hand. "News has come from the border. The combined forces of our Great Qi and Southern Yue have completely annihilated the army of Lankang. The King of Lankang has been executed."

The war in the south had lasted two years, and now it was finally over.

All the concubines knelt to congratulate the Emperor. The happiest among them was Consort Qin—her father had made a great contribution this time.

The Emperor, greatly pleased, looked at Consort Qin. "Your father has made a great contribution this time. And you, in the harem, have served me with all your heart. I should reward you. What does the Empress think?"

The Empress naturally responded, "Consort Qin has been in the palace for two years now. Your Majesty, why not promote her rank?"

"That’s a good idea. Let’s bestow the rank of Consort upon Qin."

Consort Qin was overjoyed and immediately expressed her gratitude.

The Empress glanced at Noble Consort Rong, then looked away before continuing, "Your Majesty, why not also bestow a title upon Consort Qin? That would truly demonstrate the vastness of Your Majesty’s grace."

The Emperor pondered for a moment. "Then let’s bestow the title of Yue. The official ceremony will be held after we return to the palace."

"Thank you, Your Majesty," said Consort Yue.

After delivering this news, the Emperor left. The Empress also said she was tired and dismissed everyone.

As soon as they left the Empress’s palace, everyone began congratulating Consort Yue.

Xiangjun tried to slip away, but Consort Yue walked directly up to her, blocking her path.

Xiangjun had known this day would come. She respectfully bowed. "Congratulations, Consort Yue."

Consort Yue looked down at Xiangjun haughtily. "You come from a lowly background. Being a Honored Consort is already more than you deserve. As for the rank of Consort, it’s only the beginning for me. A person must know their place."

Consort Yue left triumphantly.

After everyone else had gone, Consort Li approached Xiangjun, wanting to say something. Xiangjun simply took her hand and shook her head.

"Don’t worry. With her arrogance, who knows how long she’ll keep that title?"

...

Inside the Empress’s quarters in the temporary palace.

The Empress summoned Lady Fang and handed her a prescription.

"Deliver this to Consort Yue."

"What is this?"

"It’s a prescription my father found for me. It’s a potent medicine for conception. Once taken, it will help her become pregnant."

"Why give it to Consort Yue, Your Majesty?"

The Empress let out a cold laugh.

"It would be meaningless for me to use it. The Emperor doesn’t want my child."

Lady Fang looked at the Empress with a pained expression.

"Take it to Consort Yue. These days, the Emperor will surely be with her often. Let her take this opportunity to conceive quickly."

"But Your Majesty, if she gives birth to a prince..."

"A child born to a foreign princess can never become the crown prince. It’s of no consequence."

...

Over the next few days, the Emperor spent all his time with Consort Yue.

Noble Consort Rong, perhaps heartbroken, began to claim illness and rested in the temporary palace from that day onward.

Perhaps Consort Yue found it lonely without a rival, so she petitioned the Emperor and had Xiangjun join them in the hunt.

chapters.title: Encountering a Bear
chapters.content:
Xiangjun really didn’t want to go. She spent her days strolling happily with Gu Tingxue, but since the Emperor had given face to Consort Qin Yue and spoken, she naturally couldn’t refuse. She had no choice but to harden her head and go along.

When Xiangjun appeared in riding attire, the Emperor’s eyes lit up.

Seeing this, Consort Qin Yue immediately blocked the Emperor’s gaze and addressed him, "Your Majesty, this concubine was speaking to you."

The Emperor came back to his senses. "What did my beloved just say?"

"I said that today, I must hunt a deer and present it to Your Majesty."

Xiangjun listened to Consort Qin Yue’s affected tone and secretly rolled her eyes. Just then, she heard a voice by her ear.

"Be extremely careful today."

Xiangjun turned her head and saw Gu Tingxue standing beside her, as if by chance.

Xiangjun’s heart sank.

Sure enough, Consort Qin Yue had not invited her along with good intentions.

She remembered that in her past life, Honored Consort Rong had been injured during this hunt. It was only because Song Feijing had risked his life to protect her that Honored Consort Rong had survived, and the Emperor had been displeased for a long time afterward.

But she, Xiangjun, did not have Song Feijing to protect her with his life.

A stable hand led a horse over to Xiangjun.

Out of the corner of her eye, Xiangjun glanced at Consort Qin Yue, who was indeed looking in her direction.

A flash of inspiration struck Xiangjun. Her intuition told her she must not ride this horse.

"Your Majesty!"

Hearing Xiangjun’s voice, the Emperor turned around.

Xiangjun spoke in a wronged tone, "This concubine does not wish to ride this horse. This concubine does not like its color."

The Emperor found Xiangjun amusing. "Why are you acting like a child? What matters most is the horse’s temperament. This horse is gentle, and it was personally selected for you by me. It is my imperial steed."

"But the master said that white is inauspicious for this concubine. This concubine does not want this one."

"This is no great matter. Have someone exchange it for another."

With a glance from the Emperor, someone moved to swap Xiangjun’s horse.

Consort Qin Yue signaled the stable hand, who understood and prepared to take Xiangjun’s horse away to exchange it.

But Xiangjun did not let go of the reins.

"Your Majesty, this concubine wants that one."

Xiangjun pointed to the horse beneath Song Feijing.

"Your Majesty, please allow this concubine to swap with Prime Minister Song. This concubine riding Your Majesty’s imperial steed would be a great display of imperial grace."

The Emperor looked at Song Feijing.

Though Xiangjun’s request was somewhat presumptuous, the Emperor had been displeased with Prime Minister Song these past few days and was happy to see his favored concubine make things difficult for Song Feijing.

Song Feijing was taken aback but quickly agreed to swap horses with Xiangjun.

"Very well. Since Prime Minister Song is willing, you may swap. You—Zhen has truly spoiled you."

Xiangjun happily exchanged horses with Prime Minister Song and mounted her new steed with a flourish.

Xiangjun had deliberately practiced her mounting posture. After all, she was a dancer, and her movement was as light as a flying swallow. The Emperor was delighted to see her poised figure on horseback.

"Xiangjun, you are too modest. To have improved your riding to this level in just a few days, you must have worked hard," the Emperor said.

"It is all thanks to Eunuch Tingxue’s teaching."

Gu Tingxue still had a sea east goshawk perched on his arm, and with one hand holding the reins, he looked particularly imposing.

The Emperor was in high spirits. "Excellent! Reward them."

Consort Qin Yue was displeased and shot Xiangjun a glare, silently cursing her as a "vixen."

Zhou Zidu, the Emperor’s guard, stood beside His Majesty, his expression darkening. It should have been him teaching Xiangjun to ride.

The group set off on horseback.

Soon, a deer appeared in everyone’s line of sight. Consort Qin Yue said to the Emperor, "Your Majesty! Look!"

The Emperor and Consort Yue galloped toward the deer.

Though Xiangjun had learned to ride, she was still a beginner and quickly fell behind the Emperor and Consort Yue.

As they pursued the deer into the forest, the group gradually scattered.

At that moment, a bear suddenly appeared in the woods. Startled by the sound of hooves, it ran wildly in a frenzy.

This imperial hunting ground should never have had such a ferocious beast as a bear.

But the Emperor, being the ruler, would not be frightened by the appearance of a bear. Instead, he ordered his men to surround and kill it.

Xiangjun quickly said, "Your Majesty, this concubine is afraid."

The Emperor glanced at Zhou Zidu, who was guarding nearby. "Go and protect Noble Consort Lian."

Zhou Zidu went to Xiangjun’s side, while the Emperor, accompanied by Gu Tingxue, charged forward.

Their Emperor, Yanqing, was not a benevolent man. Xiangjun knew he was a tyrant, not just from their intimate moments but also from the books—after the Empress Dowager’s death, with no one left to control him, he had revealed his true nature.

So, the bear did not frighten the Emperor. Instead, it stirred his bloodlust, and he recklessly gave chase.

The Emperor shot an arrow that struck the bear, which enraged it and sent it charging toward the crowd.

At that very moment, Prime Minister Song’s horse suddenly went mad and threw him to the ground.

The bear immediately turned and ran toward Song Feijing.

Xiangjun actually hoped that Song Feijing would die there.

In her past life, she had suffered greatly from the schemes of the women Song Feijing had sent into the palace. Back then, she had been unable to outmaneuver Honored Consort Rong, largely because Song Feijing had been advising her from the shadows.

"Hurry and save Prime Minister Song," the Emperor ordered.

Though Consort Qin Yue would have liked to see Xiangjun dead, Song Feijing was Honored Consort Rong’s right-hand man. His death would also please Consort Qin Yue.

The bear swiped at Song Feijing with one paw, knocking him to the ground.

Just as the bear was about to pounce on him, a sea east goshawk suddenly swooped down and pecked at the bear’s eyes.

In that brief moment, Song Feijing found an opportunity and rolled away.

Gu Tingxue’s horse also charged forward, and he pulled Song Feijing up in one motion.

The bear charged at them again, but just then, an arrow suddenly shot out, striking the bear’s nose. The bear staggered and then collapsed to the ground.

"Excellent!" the Emperor praised loudly. "What fine archery! Who shot that?"

Xiangjun quickly said, "Your Majesty, it was Commander Zhou who shot it."

Zhou Zidu stepped forward, and the Emperor was greatly pleased.

"Zidu, you have been hiding your skills. With such archery, it is a waste for you to remain by Zhen’s side as a mere guard."

Zhou Zidu came from a marquess’s family, but as an illegitimate son, he had always been careful not to stand out too much. Today, he had no choice but to reveal his abilities in the face of urgency.

Zhou Zidu lowered his head, somewhat embarrassed. "Your Majesty overpraises me. It is my fortune to guard Your Majesty."

The Emperor rode up to the bear, dismounted, and with one stroke of his sword, finished it off.

The bear was now the Emperor’s prey.

The crowd immediately began praising the Emperor’s wisdom and might, and the Emperor, in high spirits, finally noticed Song Feijing sitting on the ground, his back covered in blood.

After this incident, no one was in the mood to continue hunting.

But since they had killed a bear, the Emperor did not feel the day was ruined.

He decided to end the hunt early and had Song Feijing carried back.

By the time they returned, the people at the imperial residence had already received the news. The Empress, along with Honored Consort Rong and others, were waiting there.

Consort Li saw that Xiangjun was unharmed and let out a sigh of relief.

Xiangjun looked at Honored Consort Rong, who, upon seeing Song Feijing being carried back, clearly wore an expression of shock and sorrow. Her gaze also fell upon the Emperor.

---

chapters.title: The Prime Minister Doesn’t Have Feelings for His Majesty, Does He?
chapters.content:
Everyone at the imperial residence waited for the imperial physician’s diagnosis of Prime Minister Song.

"Is Prime Minister Song alright?"

After being carried back, Song Feijing was examined by the imperial physician. Though his life was saved, the bear’s swipe had left his back a bloody mess. His injuries were severe, and he would need to rest in bed for some time.

The Emperor was displeased to see Honored Consort Rong in such a panic.

Xiangjun quickly approached the Emperor, tears in her eyes, and said, "Today, Prime Minister Song took the disaster meant for this concubine. If this concubine had been on that horse, she would have lost her life long ago. That fine imperial steed, usually so gentle, suddenly went mad. It must truly be that the color white is inauspicious for this concubine."

Hearing this, the Emperor instantly realized something was amiss.

Indeed, how could an imperial steed suddenly go mad?

Moreover, encountering a bear was no small matter. The imperial hunting grounds should never have such a ferocious beast.

"This matter is not so simple." The Emperor looked at Gu Tingxue standing below. "Tingxue, investigate this for Zhen."

The Empress quickly interjected, "Your Majesty, uncovering the truth of this matter will take time. You must be exhausted today. Why not rest first?"

The Emperor nodded but then noticed Xiangjun, her eyes red and teary, clearly frightened. His tone softened. "Has Noble Consort Lian been frightened? Zhen will stay with you."

Seeing the Emperor leave with Noble Consort Lian, Consort Qin Yue looked at the Empress with some unease. The Empress gave her a glance, and Consort Qin Yue could only suppress her panic for the moment and return to her own quarters.

...

In the Emperor’s chambers at the imperial residence, Xiangjun clung to the Emperor’s lean but strong waist and said in a wronged tone, "Your Majesty, this concubine is so afraid. If it weren’t for swapping horses with Prime Minister Song today, this concubine would never have seen Your Majesty again."

"You are a fortunate one. Do not overthink it. With Zhen here, nothing will happen to you."

"Will Prime Minister Song blame this concubine?"

"He is Zhen’s minister, and you are Zhen’s concubine. Even if he died for you, it would be loyalty to Zhen. He would not dare hold a grudge."

Xiangjun let out a sigh of relief.

The Emperor’s gaze darkened. "What? Are you very afraid of Prime Minister Song?" he asked. "Prime Minister Song is famous for his fair appearance. What are you afraid of?"

"Prime Minister Song always glares at this concubine. This concubine does not know where she has offended him..." Xiangjun said carefully. "Could it be... the rumors that Prime Minister Song prefers men are true? Could he perhaps admire Your Majesty? That is why he resents this concubine for receiving Your Majesty’s favor recently?"

"Nonsense!" the Emperor snapped.

Seeing the Emperor’s anger, Xiangjun quickly knelt down and said, "This concubine misspoke. But this concubine thinks that everyone in the world, upon seeing Your Majesty, whether man or woman, would admire and worship you. That is why this concubine thought so... Your Majesty, do not blame this concubine. This concubine is just afraid. In the past, this concubine had never even met Prime Minister Song and does not know where she offended him. That is why she spoke recklessly."

Hearing this, the Emperor’s anger subsided.

Who could stay angry at a woman whose heart and eyes held only him, who thought he was the best in the world?

"I am not angry with you. Look at you, so frightened. Get up."

The Emperor pulled Xiangjun back into his embrace, but his displeasure with Prime Minister Song grew.

Why would Song Feijing dislike Xiangjun? It was only because his heart belonged solely to Honored Consort Rong. He was angry on her behalf.

The Emperor thought to himself, *He certainly oversteps his bounds, even meddling in whom Zhen favors.*

At that moment, the young eunuch Wan Lichun entered and reported, "Your Majesty, Lord Gu seeks an audience."

"Let him in."

Gu Tingxue entered in haste.

"Have you discovered anything?"

Gu Tingxue reported, "In response to Your Majesty, the reason for the horse’s madness has been uncovered. This subject came to report immediately."

It turned out that the horse’s feed had been laced with *zuimao* grass.

This *zuimao* grass was addictive to horses. The imperial steed had been fed *zuimao* grass for ten days and had developed a dependence.

But today, the feed had contained no *zuimao* grass, which had caused the horse to go mad from withdrawal. Combined with the bear’s appearance, it had driven the horse into a frenzy.

The Emperor’s expression darkened. Lacing the feed with *zuimao* grass was clearly a premeditated act of sabotage.

Xiangjun knelt on the ground, looking terrified. "Your Majesty, this matter was not aimed at Prime Minister Song. It was aimed at this concubine. Ten days ago was precisely when this concubine first began learning to ride..."

The Emperor had not expected his own harem concubine to be so bold.

It was one thing to cause trouble within the harem, but this hunting event in the Southern Garden was attended by many of the Emperor’s close officials. This was bringing the filth of the harem into the imperial court, making the Emperor lose face.

Though the Emperor knew this matter was not simple, he could not let it become public. If it truly was the doing of a concubine, would it not make the court officials laugh at his inability to govern his own harem?

"Those two stable hands had no reason to harm Zhen’s noble consort. There must be someone behind this."

Gu Tingxue said, "The stable hands initially refused to confess, but under torture, they admitted that it was Palace Attendant Zhu Jin who ordered them to do it."

The Emperor’s face grew even darker.

So it was indeed Consort Qin Yue. No wonder she had insisted on bringing Xiangjun along for the hunt—she had wanted to take this opportunity to harm his Noble Consort Lian.

The Emperor was in a difficult position. Though he was angry at Consort Qin Yue’s arrogance and cruelty, Southern Yue had just achieved a great victory. If he punished the Princess of Southern Yue now...

Xiangjun could see from the Emperor’s expression that, though he was angry, he did not wish to punish Consort Qin Yue.

Southern Yue had just won a battle, and the Emperor could not completely disregard face.

Xiangjun quickly understood and said to the Emperor, "Your Majesty, the horse went mad, but it may not have been because of the *zuimao* grass. Perhaps it was simply frightened by the bear. Though Consort Yue does not like this concubine, she has not actually harmed this concubine’s life. This concubine does not wish to cause Your Majesty trouble over her own sake."

The Emperor glanced at Xiangjun and helped her up.

"In the past, Zhen thought you were gentle and timid. Now Zhen sees that my Xiangjun is the most considerate."

The Emperor’s expression was grave as he turned back to Gu Tingxue. "And what of the bear?"

"The director and the captain of the hunting grounds have admitted to negligence in their duties. There was a lapse in the human encirclement."

The Emperor gave a cold laugh.

This matter was certainly not so simple.

Consort Qin Yue was closely connected to the Empress. It was likely that Premier Yang was also involved.

But since he did not intend to punish Consort Qin Yue, he could not pursue the matter further. Otherwise, if the Empress were implicated, Consort Qin Yue would have to be dealt with as well.

The Emperor looked at Gu Tingxue, his face dark. "Execute the stable hands. Demote the director of the Southern Garden hunting grounds and all the officials involved."

Gu Tingxue accepted the order. "Yes, this subject will attend to it at once."

...

The autumn hunt had to be suspended due to the unexpected incident.

Fortunately, this year’s catch was still substantial.

After tallying the prey, a celebration was to be held, followed by the Emperor distributing the game he had personally hunted as a display of imperial grace.

Consort Qin Yue had the highest tally among the concubines this year.

The mother of the Eldest Princess, Consort Wang Wanyi, raised her cup and said, "Consort Yue is so impressive. No wonder His Majesty favors you so much."

Consort Wang Wanyi was not favored by the Emperor, but she had been lucky—after only a few nights with him, she had conceived and given birth to the Eldest Princess. However, she had always been somewhat invisible in the palace.

Now, it was unclear whether she was trying to flatter Consort Qin Yue, but unfortunately, she had chosen the wrong day.

Consort Qin Yue was naturally pleased and was about to raise her cup to toast Consort Wang Wanyi when she heard the Emperor’s grim voice from the head of the table.

"It is not yet time for the official ceremony. She is not a formally titled consort. Wang Wanyi, after so many years in the palace, how can you still be so ignorant of the rules?"

chapters.title: Visiting Minister Song
chapters.content:
As soon as these words were spoken, the crowd fell silent.

Qin Yuefei's face turned pale. She realized that the Emperor must have found out about how she had harmed Xiangjun.

Wang Wanyi immediately knelt and said, "It is this concubine's fault. Please calm your anger, Your Majesty."

"If you know your mistake, then pour another cup of wine for Qin Zhaoyi."

Wang Wanyi was also frightened. With a pale face, she raised her cup to Qin Zhaoyi and said, "Congratulations, Qin Zhaoyi. During this hunt, you came first among all the concubines. This younger sister offers you a toast."

Qin Zhaoyi had no choice but to stand up with a pale face, enduring the humiliation. She raised her wine cup and gritted her teeth, saying, "Thank you, Wanyi."

After drinking, both sat down with unpleasant expressions.

Qin Zhaoyi looked at the Emperor, but he didn’t even spare her a glance.

Qin Zhaoyi felt uneasy. The Emperor had not mentioned when the enfeoffment ceremony would be held. She feared that he would not bring it up again after returning, meaning she would remain a Zhaoyi.

The celebration ended on this sour note.

Tonight was a significant day, and the Emperor had to accompany the Empress. So, he left with the Empress first.

Once the Emperor left, the remaining guests also felt the mood was ruined and left one by one.

Meng Mei supported Xiangjun as she walked over to Qin Zhaoyi, who was still sitting there in a daze.

"Earlier, Sister Zhaoyi said I only had the fate of a Guifei. But Sister Zhaoyi has only been a Fei for two days and is now a Zhaoyi again. I wonder, does Sister Zhaoyi also only have the fate of a Zhaoyi?"

Qin Zhaoyi glared at Xiangjun with hatred.

Xiangjun gracefully bowed, "Sister Zhaoyi, this younger sister will take her leave now."

Xiangjun left triumphantly, which infuriated Qin Zhaoyi so much that she almost flipped the table. If Zhu Jin hadn’t reminded her that this wasn’t her own palace, Qin Zhaoyi would have likely started cursing loudly.

There were only two days left before returning to the palace.

The Emperor didn’t want to pay attention to Qin Zhaoyi. Moreover, Honored Consort Rong was ill, and there wasn’t much to do in the temporary palace. So, he thought of visiting Xiangjun.

Xiangjun quickly had Li Cairen bring Yuji over, hoping the Emperor would spend more time bonding with his son.

The two women accompanied the Emperor. Xiaoluzi rolled around on the floor, playing with Yuji, filling the room with laughter. This rare warmth touched the Emperor.

Seeing that Yuji could already stand while holding onto a chair, the Emperor was delighted.

"Yuji is so young, yet he can already stand? He truly is my good son."

Xiangjun immediately said, "This is all thanks to Li Cairen raising him well in Honored Consort Rong’s palace. That’s why Yuji has such a good foundation."

Li Cairen was a little surprised that Xiangjun suddenly mentioned the Consort, but she was clever. Regardless of Xiangjun’s intentions, she quickly followed up, "Yes, Honored Consort Rong was extremely kind to me and Yuji in the past."

The Emperor nodded. The Consort was indeed kind-hearted.

In truth, the Emperor had never suspected Consort Rong regarding the death of the Second Prince.

What he despised was Consort Rong’s entanglement with Song Feijing, which had allowed Song Feijing’s influence to reach the imperial harem.

"Your Majesty hasn’t seen Consort Rong in a long time, has he? Why not go visit her today?" Xiangjun suggested.

The Emperor looked at Xiangjun, "You are quite generous, always urging me to visit Consort Rong."

"Consort Rong has been good to this concubine."

The Emperor was also pleased that Xiangjun and Li Cairen had not forgotten Consort Rong’s kindness and support.

His voice softened as he took Xiangjun’s hand, "But today, I came to see you."

"Your Majesty, this concubine hasn’t seen Consort Rong in a long time either. Why not have Your Majesty take this concubine, Li Cairen, and the Third Prince to visit Consort Rong? Perhaps Consort Rong misses Yuji as well."

The Emperor pondered for a moment, "Alright, then I shall take you all there."

...

The Emperor, accompanied by Xiangjun and Li Cairen, went to Bixiao Pavilion, where Consort Rong was staying in the temporary palace. However, upon arrival, they did not find Consort Rong or her senior maid, Caiwei. Only a few junior maids were present.

"Where is your Consort Rong?"

Seeing the junior maids hesitating, the Emperor grew angry.

"How dare you! Where has Consort Rong gone?"

The junior maid quickly knelt and kowtowed.

"Replying to Your Majesty... Consort Rong... Consort Rong went to visit Minister Song."

Xiangjun felt that the Emperor’s head was practically steaming with rage. She finally understood why Gu Tingxue had sent someone to inform her and asked her to lead the Emperor to Bixiao Pavilion.

The Emperor turned and left in a huff. Xiangjun and Li Cairen exchanged glances and quickly followed with the child.

During this autumn hunt, the Emperor had only brought a few trusted officials. To show his care for them, he had also granted them residence in the temporary palace, though their quarters were quite far from the concubines.

Minister Song was staying in the Faxiang Hall next to the garden.

The guards at the entrance saw the Emperor approaching and wanted to announce his arrival, but the Emperor silenced them.

"No need to announce."

The Emperor was furious. Without thinking to send Xiangjun and Li Cairen away, he directly led them inside.

The palace servants along the way did not dare to make a sound. The Emperor strode all the way to the door of Minister Song’s room.

The door was closed.

Caiwei and Minister Song’s young servant stood guard outside.

Xiangjun observed the Emperor. The veins on his neck were about to burst.

Caiwei wanted to loudly announce the Emperor’s arrival, but the eunuch Wan Lichun behind the Emperor was a man cultivated by Gu Tingxue. How could he not understand the Emperor’s intentions?

With a wave of his hand, he immediately had someone cover Caiwei’s mouth.

The door was pushed open, and the Emperor strode inside. Li Cairen was a bit afraid and wanted to wait outside, but Xiangjun, who loved to watch the drama, followed right in.

Li Cairen had no choice but to follow with Yuji in her arms.

As soon as they entered, they saw Honored Consort Rong sitting beside Song Feijing, wiping her tears with a handkerchief.

The two of them were not doing anything improper.

But the way Song Feijing looked at Consort Rong was filled with deep affection. Even Li Cairen, who knew nothing about the situation, could sense something was wrong.

That was a look of uncontrollable, surging love...

Li Cairen felt uneasy. What should she do? Had they seen something they shouldn’t have? Would they offend the Emperor?

Li Cairen quickly looked at Xiangjun, only to see her face filled with excitement.

Li Cairen sighed in her heart. As expected of her sister, she was not the least bit flustered in such a situation.

"How come the Consort is here?" the Emperor said in a dark tone.

Only then did Honored Consort Rong realize the Emperor had arrived. She hastily stood up.

"Emperor... Your Majesty... Why have you come?"

The Emperor did not speak, only staring at the two of them with a dark expression.

The atmosphere in the room was truly bizarre. Xiangjun quickly spoke up, "Minister Song was injured because he swapped horses with this concubine. This concubine begged Your Majesty to bring me here to check on Minister Song’s injuries. Otherwise, Xiangjun would feel uneasy."

The Emperor finally came to his senses upon hearing Xiangjun’s words.

He was so angry about Consort Rong’s actions that his mind was in chaos.

If this matter were to spread, it would only make him look bad.

"Yes, I didn’t expect Consort Rong to be of the same mind as me, coming here first to visit Minister Song on my behalf."

Song Feijing tried to get up to greet the Emperor, but as soon as he pushed himself up, the pain from his wound made him collapse back onto the bed.

"Be careful!"

Honored Consort Rong reached out to support him, and Minister Song instinctively grabbed her hand.

Xiangjun, standing beside the Emperor, could almost feel the dark aura radiating from him.

---

chapters.title: Xiangjun’s Ennoblement as Deyi
chapters.content:
Honored Consort Rong and Minister Song also remembered the Emperor’s presence. Consort Rong quickly withdrew her hand, and Minister Song, losing his balance, fell back onto the bed.

Only when Song Feijing fell back onto the bed, sweating from the pain, did the Emperor’s expression improve slightly.

"Minister Song, there is no need to rise. You are still injured. Just rest."

"Thank you for Your Majesty’s grace."

The awkwardness in the room continued. Xiangjun, always perceptive, took the initiative to ask, "How is Minister Song’s injury? Has the imperial physician said when he will recover?"

"Thank you for your concern, Noble Consort Lian. This subject has only suffered a flesh wound and will recover after some rest."

Xiangjun glanced at Li Cairen, then at Yuji. Li Cairen caught on and pinched Yuji, who immediately started wailing.

"Your Majesty, Yuji is probably tired. It’s time for his afternoon nap."

The Emperor nodded and said to Honored Consort Rong, "Consort, you will return with us."

Honored Consort Rong immediately stood behind the Emperor.

The Emperor glanced at Song Feijing and said darkly, "Minister Song, take good care of your injury. I will come visit you again."

"This subject respectfully sees Your Majesty off."

Xiangjun and Li Cairen were perceptive. Sensing the stormy atmosphere between the Emperor and Honored Consort Rong, they quickly used Yuji’s need for a nap as an excuse and left first.

The Emperor then followed Honored Consort Rong to Bixiao Pavilion.

Later, when they inquired about the news, they heard that all the palace maids serving Consort Rong, except for the one who had voluntarily confessed that Consort Rong had gone to Minister Song’s place, had been punished with a beating.

Apart from Caiwei, whom Honored Consort Rong had protected, all the other maids had been replaced by the Emperor. The little maid who had reported the matter was arranged by Gu Tingxue to serve in Xiangjun’s palace.

Xiangjun also felt sorry for Consort Rong. With all her trusted aides replaced, and only Caiwei left, it would be even harder for her to get things done in the future.

The people around the Emperor kept their mouths shut, as did Minister Song’s people. Those from Consort Rong’s palace who couldn’t keep quiet had been beaten and sent away. For the time being, the rest of the palace didn’t know what had happened between the Emperor and Consort Rong.

But over the years, the Emperor and Consort Rong had quarreled many times, and everyone was used to it. Usually, they would make up after a few days, so no one wanted to provoke Consort Rong’s bad luck.

...

Two days later, the hunt ended, and the group returned to the imperial palace.

However, while they had left in high spirits, the Emperor returned in low spirits.

After returning to the palace, Honored Consort Rong specially summoned Xiangjun and Li Cairen to ask about what had happened that day.

Xiangjun and Li Cairen told the truth.

Xiangjun and Li Cairen repeatedly pledged their loyalty to Consort Rong. Although Consort Rong felt somewhat uncomfortable, she couldn’t find any fault with them.

They had indeed meant well, wanting the Emperor to come see her. They had done such things many times before.

Consort Rong dismissed the two.

After they left, Caiwei said, "Your Highness, do you trust Noble Consort Lian and Li Cairen?"

"They are not capable of knowing every move in the harem. It must have been a coincidence."

Honored Consort Rong sighed.

"I always feel that this matter is too much of a coincidence."

"It’s all my fault. I knew His Majesty’s taboo, yet I still went to see him..."

Caiwei comforted Consort Rong, "Your Highness did the right thing. Minister Song’s support is very important to you. Without Minister Song, who in the imperial court would speak for our Fourth Prince?"

"But His Majesty is truly angry this time."

"The Emperor’s mood will always change. Your Highness, you should be worried about other matters now."

"What do you mean?"

"Your Highness, Noble Consort Lian and Li Cairen are currently the most favored in the harem. Although they are still under your influence now, if they truly become a united force in the future, it will be difficult for you to control them. Why not... have Minister Song investigate whether they still have any relatives in Jiangnan? Have Minister Song find something to hold over them."

...

After returning from the autumn hunt, the harem was quiet for a while.

The Emperor still favored Xiangjun and Li Cairen the most.

Unexpectedly, two months later, news came that Qin Zhaoyi was with child.

Qin Zhaoyi’s pregnancy led the Empress to suggest that the Emperor enfeoff Qin Zhaoyi as a Consort.

The Emperor considered it and decided that in two months, during the New Year, he would hold the enfeoffment ceremony.

But on the day of the New Year, along with Qin Zhaoyi, Xiangjun and Li Cairen were also enfeoffed.

Xiangjun and Li Cairen had indeed benefited from Qin Zhaoyi’s situation. If the Emperor had not disliked Qin Zhaoyi’s actions, they would not have gained this advantage.

Qin Zhaoyi was enfeoffed as a Consort due to her pregnancy, but Xiangjun and Li Cairen were promoted without having done anything—this was purely the Emperor’s favor.

Xiangjun was enfeoffed as Deyi of the third rank, and Li Cairen was enfeoffed as Guiji of the fifth rank, with the title of Jian.

Xiangjun deliberately asked, "Your Majesty, what does ‘Jian’ mean?"

Xiangjun wanted the Emperor to explain it properly. Otherwise, in the future, people like Qin Zhaoyi would mock Qinglian just as they had mocked her before.

"Li Cairen’s dance is not like the usual dancers, who only have softness and beauty. I will always remember Li Cairen’s sword dance, *Leiting Shanhe*. It was as graceful as a startled swan, with a majestic and thunderous momentum, not at all like a delicate woman, but rather with the bearing of a man. At that time, I thought of the line from the *Book of Songs*: ‘Jian xi, Jian xi, methodically performing the myriad dances...’"

Li Cairen immediately expressed her gratitude.

The enfeoffment ceremonies for the three of them were held together. Qin Yuefei’s good mood about being re-enfeoffed as a Consort vanished instantly.

Now, the entire harem knew that Xiangjun and Qinglian were favored.

Chengxiang Hall was truly the center of attention.

Xiangjun had no children, yet in less than two years in the palace, she had become a Deyi of the third rank.

Li Qinglian, a lowly dancer of servant status, had not only given birth to a prince but had now become a Guiji of the fifth rank. With such favor, if she gave birth to another child, rising to the rank of Pin would not be impossible.

Those who had once looked down on Xiangjun and Qinglian now watched Chengxiang Hall with envious eyes.

Even Honored Consort Rong could no longer sit still.

After the last argument with the Emperor, he had not visited her Ganlu Palace again.

In the past, after a quarrel, the Emperor would always be the first to seek reconciliation. But Honored Consort Rong, seeing how much the Emperor favored Xiangjun and Qinglian, felt a sense of unease.

In the entire harem, the Emperor visited Xiangjun and Li Guiji the most.

Consort Rong had originally thought that Xiangjun would, as before, urge the Emperor to visit her often.

But ever since they returned from the hunting grounds, the Emperor had rarely come to see her. In these four months, he had not favored Consort Rong even once, only occasionally coming to see Prince Yuanze.

Consort Rong felt a chill in her heart. She said to Caiwei, "Caiwei, do you think people’s hearts change so easily? Xiangjun... has changed..."

"Yes, when Noble Consort Lian was favored, she would still advise the Emperor to come see you. Now, together with Li Guiji, she has the Emperor so enchanted that he wishes to go to Chengxiang Hall every day. She truly does not know how to repay kindness."

"Enough. Which concubine in the harem does not desire the Emperor’s favor?"

"Your Highness, Noble Consort Lian owes her position to you. If it weren’t for you, during her illness, she might have been bullied to death. Now that she is favored, she should be helping you. Perhaps... you should remind Noble Consort Lian a little."

chapters.title: What Books Does the Noble Consort Read?
chapters.content:
Rong Guifei was somewhat angry.

"You mean, you want me to take the initiative to find Lian Deyi and have her call the Emperor to my place? Do you think that without someone reminding the Emperor, he would forget about me?"

"Noble Consort, this servant does not mean that. But indeed, after you gave birth, the Emperor has rarely come to our Ganlu Palace."

Guifei didn't know why either.

She recalled the day she gave birth, how the Emperor had disregarded all advice and entered the delivery room to accompany her through the birth. This was a favor no other concubine had ever received.

After the child was born, the Emperor had always treated her extremely well. Even when they had quarreled over the matter with Premier Song, it was the Emperor who had taken the first step to make amends.

But why, then, was the Emperor unwilling to stay overnight in Ganlu Palace?

Previously, it could be said that it was because she had given birth prematurely and her body was weak, and the Emperor couldn't bear to trouble her.

But later, her body had already recovered, and that night in the temporary palace, the Emperor had not touched her either.

Just as Guifei was lost in thought, someone announced that the Emperor had arrived.

Guifei was overjoyed and immediately stood up to greet him.

The Emperor saw Guifei coming out and smiled, saying, "Originally, I was going to visit Xiangjun today. I happened to see Xiangjun and Qinglian playing with Yuanji, and then I thought that I haven't seen our Yuanze for a long time, so I came to see him. Where is Yuanze? Bring him to me."

Rong Guifei's heart sank. Had the Emperor come only for Yuanze?

Not for her?

Did she have to resort to the same tactics as those concubines who relied on their children to vie for favor?

...

That night, the Emperor stayed to accompany Rong Guifei but did not have her attend to him in bed.

The next day, Rong Guifei had dark circles under her eyes. She had not slept a wink all night, tossing and turning, unable to understand why the Emperor had changed like this.

Rong Guifei sent someone to find Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue was truly annoyed. This Rong Guifei sought him out over every little thing.

But the Emperor had ordered him to secretly help Rong Guifei. Apart from not trusting Premier Song and his possible collusion with the harem, there was also the intention to protect Guifei and the Fourth Prince.

Gu Tingxue had no choice but to go see Rong Guifei after nightfall, with a dark expression.

Never would he have thought that Rong Guifei's question would leave him at a loss for words.

Rong Guifei actually asked him for details about the Emperor's intimate moments with Xiangjun.

Gu Tingxue knitted his brows and suppressed his irritation as he replied, "Noble Consort, the Shang Qin Bureau keeps records of these things. If you want to know, you can check them yourself."

Rong Guifei's brows were filled with worry.

"The Shang Qin Bureau only records how many times the Emperor called for water. It doesn't have what I want to know."

Gu Tingxue's tone was cold, "What does Noble Consort want to know?"

Rong Guifei seemed not to notice Gu Tingxue's impatience and urgently said, "I want to know why the Emperor always summons Xiangjun. What is so special about her?"

"Noble Consort, this servant is always outside attending to the Emperor's affairs and does not know these things clearly."

"Can you help me find out, Tingxue? Isn't Wan Gong your apprentice? He should know..."

...

When Gu Tingxue left, he was almost driven mad by this foolish woman. After thinking it over, he was still fuming as he went to Chengxiang Palace.

By the time he arrived at Chengxiang Palace, the lights were already out, except for the lamp beside Xiangjun's bed. Xiangjun was lying in bed reading a book again.

At this moment, Gu Tingxue felt that it wasn't hard to understand why the Emperor preferred Xiangjun.

She was always striving to be the best, and every time he saw her, there was a surprise. Even at this late hour, she was still reading by candlelight. It seemed she was more diligent than those scholars and candidates.

Meng Mei saw Gu Tingxue and naturally withdrew from the warm chamber, quietly waiting outside.

Only Gu Tingxue and Xiangjun remained in the warm chamber.

Seeing Gu Tingxue approach, Xiangjun was delighted. She immediately patted the space beside her and said to Gu Tingxue, "You've come at the right time. Come up and read to me."

"How dare Tingxue presume to share your bed, Noble Consort," Gu Tingxue said softly.

Since returning from the hunting grounds, Xiangjun's attitude toward him had suddenly become very intimate. Sometimes, it was even as if... as if she treated him like a lover.

Gu Tingxue knew this was inappropriate, but he didn't want to shatter her attitude.

In his heart, he was also willing for Xiangjun to treat him this way.

"There are only two lamps lit. If you don't come up, how can you see the words clearly?"

Seeing Gu Tingxue hesitate, Xiangjun looked at him pleadingly and said, "Please, my eyes are blurred from reading. Tingxue, won't you help me read a little?"

Gu Tingxue sighed and took the book, sitting down on the edge of Xiangjun's bed.

Xiangjun leaned closer, pointed, and said, "I just read up to here. Start from here."

Gu Tingxue caught the refreshing yet unsettling fragrance from Xiangjun. For a moment, he felt distracted and subconsciously swallowed, feeling an unusual dryness in his throat.

"Start from here and read," Xiangjun urged again.

Gu Tingxue glanced at it. It seemed to be a storybook. Without much thought, reading might help him gather his scattered thoughts.

Gu Tingxue began to read, but the more he read, the more he felt something was wrong.

...

Gu Tingxue snapped the book shut.

"Noble Consort, what kind of things do you usually read?" Gu Tingxue asked with a dark face. "This servant thought you were studying diligently."

"This is also studying. I am a concubine, and there are many areas where I need to apply myself. Don't stop, continue reading!"

Xiangjun pointed at the book again, but Gu Tingxue refused to read any further.

"This book is not good. This servant will throw it away for you."

"No!"

Xiangjun seized the book back from Gu Tingxue when he wasn't paying attention.

"Tingxue, don't be shy. I'll read it to you." Xiangjun cleared her throat and loudly read, "Pa—"

Gu Tingxue quickly covered Xiangjun's mouth.

"Don't read it."

Xiangjun blinked and threw the book away. She reached out and took hold of Gu Tingxue's hand that was covering her mouth, gently rubbing the back of his hand.

Gu Tingxue abruptly pulled his hand back, as if it had been burned.

"Noble Consort is deeply favored by the Emperor. You shouldn't be reading such things." Gu Tingxue still insisted on dealing with the book. "This servant will throw it away for you."

Seeing Gu Tingxue take the book away, Xiangjun said aggrievedly, "It's because the Emperor comes so often that I feel distressed."

Xiangjun reached out to hook Gu Tingxue's belt.

Gu Tingxue took a deep breath and grabbed Xiangjun's hand.
