Three days had passed since the palace coup, and Xiangjun finally saw Gu Tingxue again.

Gu Tingxue was still covered in the stench of blood and looked exhausted.

Xiangjun immediately got up and asked in a low voice, "Why are you here today? I thought you would be very busy these days."

"I originally didn't have time, but I'm a bit tired and want to rest at Your Majesty's place."

Xiangjun didn't ask more questions and reached out to help Gu Tingxue take off his clothes.

"Since you're here to rest, take off your clothes and sleep for a while. Tell me how long you can sleep, and I'll wake you up later."

Xiangjun helped Gu Tingxue take off his clothes and led him to the bed.

But once on the bed, Gu Tingxue did not sleep. He just lay there with his eyes open, staring at Xiangjun.

"What's wrong with you?" Xiangjun asked, puzzled. "Did something happen?"

Xiangjun felt that Gu Tingxue was not quite right today.

"Did you hear that scream just now?"

Xiangjun nodded. "I did. Who was that?"

"It was Song Feijing's mother, and also my wet nurse. I let her see Song Feijing for the last time. Her Majesty the Empress Dowager has pardoned her, but she still took her own life."

Xiangjun was very surprised. There was actually such a relationship between Gu Tingxue and Song Feijing.

Wait, she was even more surprised that Gu Tingxue had a wet nurse.

How could a commoner's family have a wet nurse?

Could it be that Gu Tingxue was a young master from a wealthy family before entering the palace?

Seeing that Gu Tingxue had no intention of continuing, Xiangjun did not pursue the matter further. She just gently held Gu Tingxue's hand.

Suddenly, Gu Tingxue pulled Xiangjun into his arms.

Xiangjun could roughly understand Gu Tingxue's feelings. Gu Tingxue was the emperor's hound, a lone figure with no family or friends. This wet nurse was probably one of the few people close to him in his life.

For a wealthy young master, a wet nurse was a caregiver, and sometimes the bond between a wet nurse and a child could be even deeper than that between a biological mother and child.

Now, the only person close to him was dead, killed by imperial power, and indirectly by his own hand. He was probably in pain.

"Xiangjun..."

Xiangjun was taken aback. This was the first time Gu Tingxue had called her by her name.

"I'm here."

Xiangjun reached out and gently stroked Gu Tingxue's back.

"I won't let you die." Gu Tingxue said.

Xiangjun's heart trembled, and she couldn't help but curl the corners of her mouth and smile.

She buried her head in Gu Tingxue's neck and softly said, "As long as I keep winning, I won't die. Tingxue, you must always help me, okay?"

Gu Tingxue's voice was very low and muffled.

"Okay."

...

The next day, the entire palace learned of Song Feijing's death.

Immediately after, the emperor began to settle scores with the Song family and the Jiangnan faction.

In the front court, the emperor took swift and decisive action, uprooting the entire Song family.

The emperor took the opportunity to arrange many of his own people in power and ordered Gu Tingxue to secretly monitor the officials, keeping their weaknesses in hand.

The Yang family also suffered heavy losses in the palace coup. However, the Yang family and the clean stream faction behind them had deep roots in the court. Even with Yang Jing Shan's death, there were still other officials in the Yang family, and they could still recover. Moreover, since the Song family and the Jiangnan faction were all convicted of treason, the Yang family was still the largest force in the front court.

For a whole month, the front court was filled with executions. Xiangjun occasionally saw Gu Tingxue, and he was always covered in the stench of blood, either having just killed someone or on his way to kill.

Empress Yang and Consort Xue had also both laid low.

Empress Yang, having lost her father and being wary of the emperor, knew she could not provoke the emperor further. She retracted all her claws and meekly stayed in her palace, feigning illness.

Consort Xue had also won a Pyrrhic victory. Although she had gained the emperor's trust, she had lost her assistance in the court with Prime Minister Song's death. Moreover, personally killing the man who had deeply loved her for many years had left her devastated, and it had also created a rift between her and the emperor.

As for Consort Yue, she had a miscarriage in her late pregnancy, which had weakened her body. Naturally, she would not be causing trouble for a while. Although her father, the King of Southern Yue, had meritorious service in protecting the emperor, he was afraid of the emperor turning against him. Seeing his daughter's miscarriage, he immediately requested to return to his fiefdom. The emperor agreed.

It was at this time that Xiangjun informed the emperor that she had been pregnant for four months.

The emperor was in the midst of grief, having first lost the Second Prince, followed by the Fourth Prince Yuan Ze's disfigurement, and then Consort Yue's child. At this moment, the emperor needed a piece of good news to cheer himself up the most.

The emperor was overjoyed. After returning to the imperial palace from the temporary residence, he immediately bestowed the title of Zhaoyi upon Xiangjun.

In just three years in the palace, Xiangjun had risen from a lowly servant girl to a Zhaoyi. The speed of her promotion was astonishing. If this was not a favored consort, what was?

For a time, Xiangjun was the center of attention in the harem. Many low-ranking consorts came to her palace to pay their respects and bring gifts, hoping to get close to her. Xiangjun welcomed them all. After all, she needed people to pave the way for the child in her womb and to do things for her in the future. There was no need to hide her talents anymore. She could start cultivating her own influence.

Every day, Physician Liu still came to check Xiangjun's pulse to ensure the baby was healthy.

This pregnancy was very stable for Xiangjun. Her second child was here to repay her kindness. In her past life, he had been a very well-behaved child. Unfortunately, at that time, her lowly status had caused the child to suffer a lot.

"Your Majesty, here is today's blood swallow nest soup." Meng Mei said.

Xiangjun was about to reach out when she heard the announcement at the door. Gu Tingxue had arrived with the emperor's rewards.

Xiangjun immediately withdrew her hand and leaned on the soft couch, putting on a displeased expression.

As soon as Gu Tingxue entered, he saw Xiangjun pouting, looking like she needed coaxing.

With a glance from Gu Tingxue, Meng Mei and the others withdrew.

"Who has upset Your Majesty again?"

Xiangjun coldly humphed, "Oh, isn't this Lord Gu? What a rare visitor."

Gu Tingxue couldn't help but smile. For the past two months, he had been sent by the emperor to Jiangnan to eliminate the remaining Song party members. He had only returned to the capital a few days ago and had been busy ever since. Today, he finally had the chance to deliver the emperor's rewards and see Xiangjun.

"Are you angry?"

"Would I dare? You are a very busy man. You were gone for two months, and I couldn't see you. Finally, you returned to the capital, but you were still busy. You had time to go to Noble Consort's place but not to see me. Am I not worthy enough?"

Gu Tingxue was now used to Xiangjun's little temper. Since she became pregnant, she had become even more pampered. Gu Tingxue, mindful of her pregnancy, didn't dare not to coax her.

Gu Tingxue sat down next to Xiangjun and stretched out his arm to hold her waist, pulling her into his embrace.

"Get lost. Don't touch me."

Gu Tingxue's eyes were filled with amusement. Rarely using a gentle tone, he explained, "Going to Noble Consort's place was ordered by His Majesty. Otherwise, I wouldn't have time to see her."

"No time to see?"

"Don't want to see."

Xiangjun finally felt a bit better and asked, "Song Feijing is already dead. Why did His Majesty still send you to Noble Consort's place? What

---

chapters.title: Chapter 80
chapters.content:
"Song Feijing is dead, but there are still Grand General Wang and Prince Jin."

Xiangjun pondered for a moment and immediately understood.

The Emperor's love for the Noble Consort was not only due to their childhood affection, the support she had given him in his youth, but also because the Noble Consort was a trophy from his struggles against other men.

From a young age, the Emperor had always lost to the former Crown Prince, now Prince Jin, lost to his younger brother, Grand General Wang, who had a noble mother and was brave and skilled in battle, and lost to Song Feijing, who had become a child prodigy at the age of ten.

But in the end, he won the heart of Noble Consort Xue Jiaojiao and ascended to the most honorable position in the world, becoming the ruler of all under heaven.

However, deep in his heart, the Emperor was still that Zhou Qinghe who had been bullied and humiliated by everyone.

A trophy requires opponents.

Song Feijing, Grand General Wang, and Prince Jin were all his opponents.

As long as they were alive, the Noble Consort would always be his trophy.

One of the three opponents from back then was already dead. When the remaining two were also dead, the Emperor's love game would have no opponents left.

And in this process, the Noble Consort's hypocritical beauty would be torn apart.

When everyone had exited the stage, it would be the time for the Noble Consort to completely fall out of favor.

"Do you think the Noble Consort still trusts you? This time, you and His Majesty worked together to deceive Song Feijing, and you kept it from her. Didn't she blame you?"

"Indeed, the Noble Consort did come to reproach me for not informing her of the Emperor's plans beforehand."

Xiangjun was somewhat curious. Unconsciously, she turned her body, which had been facing away from Gu Tingxue, and now turned her face towards him, looking at Gu Tingxue with curiosity. "Then what did you say? Was she very disheartened?"

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun's face, which seemed to be dripping with water, and found it strange. How come she looked even more tender and lovely after becoming pregnant, more like a young girl?

"Speak." Xiangjun urged.

"I told her that I served her because of His Majesty, and that my first loyalty is to His Majesty alone."

Xiangjun was very happy.

She had a possessive desire towards Gu Tingxue. Every time she thought that the Noble Consort was pleased that Gu Tingxue worked for her, and considered Gu Tingxue as her own subordinate, she felt very uncomfortable.

Now that the Noble Consort knew the truth, she must be very disheartened.

Gu Tingxue saw Xiangjun's happy expression and unconsciously felt joyful as well. He couldn't help but reach out and pinch Xiangjun's face.

Xiangjun frowned and removed Gu Tingxue's hand from her face, looking up at him with a mischievous glint in her eyes.

She probed, "Then what about me and His Majesty? Between me and His Majesty, who do you, Tingxue, owe loyalty to first?"

Gu Tingxue smiled, reached out, and held Xiangjun's soft hand, gently caressing it in his palm.

"His Majesty's affairs are naturally my priority, but in my heart, Your Highness's matters are even more important."

Although Xiangjun didn't know how sincere Gu Tingxue was with those words, she still felt comfortable hearing them. She hummed in satisfaction, proudly withdrew her hand, and glanced at the blood swiftlet nest on the table. "Then this palace will reward you by letting you personally serve me with the bird's nest."

Gu Tingxue smiled and picked up the bowl of blood swiftlet nest, gently saying, "Then this humble servant will serve Your Highness with the bird's nest."

...

By the time Gu Tingxue had finished feeding her the bowl of bird's nest, Xiangjun had already collapsed, disheveled, into Gu Tingxue's arms.

"Even a mother-to-be can't sit properly."

Xiangjun shot Gu Tingxue a glance. Wasn't it because his hands were restless and improper?

Gu Tingxue took a handkerchief and wiped Xiangjun's mouth.

"How long can you stay with me this time?" Xiangjun looked at Gu Tingxue pitifully and asked, "You won't have to leave immediately, will you?"

"Recently, there are many matters to attend to in the imperial court. I'm afraid I won't be able to come to the rear palace. I'll have to wait until the court stabilizes."

"Then how long can you stay today?"

"Half an hour."

Xiangjun thought for a moment, then pulled Gu Tingxue's hand and walked towards the warm partition. Gu Tingxue, seeing Xiangjun's six-month pregnant belly, was afraid she might bump into something.

"Slow down."

"I'm in a hurry."

When Gu Tingxue saw that Xiangjun had pulled him to the bedside, he knew what she wanted to do.

"Your Highness, you are currently..."

"You don't understand. This child has made me very restless. Quickly, we only have half an hour!"

When Gu Tingxue left, his right hand was hidden in his sleeve the entire time.

His fingers were white, afraid that if someone saw them, he wouldn't be able to explain.

Xiangjun finally felt at ease, but she didn't know when she would see Gu Tingxue again.

...

As the matters in the imperial court gradually stabilized, the Empress, who had been feigning illness, finally recovered.

The concubines of the rear palace began to visit the Weiyang Palace to pay their respects once more.

This time, Xiangjun was kept behind by the Empress. After a few hypocritical pleasantries, the Empress got straight to the point.

"Honored Concubine Lian, you should know that without Prime Minister Song, the Noble Consort is like a tiger without claws and teeth, useless."

Xiangjun naturally knew this. This time, almost all of Prime Minister Song's people in the palace had been rooted out and killed. The Noble Consort was not good at managing subordinates and had already lost her influence in the rear palace.

But even a dying camel is bigger than a horse. As long as she had the Emperor's favor, there would still be people willing to risk their lives to serve the Noble Consort.

"Your Majesty, this concubine does not understand your meaning. Whether the Noble Consort is formidable or not, what does it have to do with me?"

The Empress smiled in satisfaction.

"Yes, what does the Noble Consort's situation have to do with you? Honored Concubine Lian, I know that your Xu family is considered wealthy in Jiangnan, but unfortunately, you lack a solid foundation. However, with the help of my Yang family, and with the Song family now destroyed, your Xu family can also establish a firm foothold in Jiangnan. What do you think, Honored Concubine Lian?"

Xiangjun immediately put on an expression of pleasant surprise.

"Your Majesty is willing to help my Xu family. I wonder what you would have me do?"

The Empress glanced at Xiangjun's belly. "You also know that I have lost my second imperial son."

Xiangjun fell silent. Was the Empress perhaps after her child?

But she was already a Concubine Lian. According to the rules, she could raise her own imperial son. Why didn't the Empress find a concubine of lower status to bear a child for her?

"Your Majesty, do you want my child?"

"You are a Concubine Lian, so the child will naturally be yours. It's just that I find the deep palace lonely and want a child for company. Honored Concubine Lian, you are still young and highly favored. What's most important for you now is to secure that favor. I think the child can still be registered under your name, but can be raised in my Weiyang Palace, and I will take care of it for you. What do you think?"

Xiangjun's eyes darkened.

If the child was raised by the Empress, wouldn't it be easy for her to claim the child as her own later?

Moreover, the child in her womb was the one she loved the most. She absolutely could not bear to let someone else raise it.

"Your Majesty, I don't even know if the child in my womb is a boy or a girl yet..."

"You are still young. The imperial physicians all said you couldn't have children, but you managed to conceive, which shows that you are a fortunate one. It probably won't be difficult for you to conceive again in the future. Whether it's a boy or a girl, it will come eventually. Besides, I am just lonely for company. It doesn't matter if it's an imperial son or a princess."

Xiangjun gave an awkward smile and did not respond.

"You can go back and think it over, Honored Concubine Lian. If you are willing, my Yang family will help you and the Xu family. Not only this child in your womb, but also your future children, will receive the support of my Yang family. If you are not willing... the things that Prime Minister Song did to the Xu family, my family can do the same."

chapters.title: Meeting Her Brother Xu Huanwen
chapters.content:
Xiangjun's heart sank.

The Empress was threatening her.

"Honored Concubine Lian, you are with child now. You should go back and rest early. Today, I won't keep you any longer. This statue of the Child-Granting Guanyin is worth ten thousand gold. I bestow it upon you for a safe pregnancy."

"Thank you, Your Majesty, for your generosity."

After returning to Chengxiang Palace, Xiangjun thought for a long time but still couldn't understand why the Empress had made such a request.

She wanted to raise the child herself but not register it under her own name. What did that mean? Even if the child was raised by the Empress, Xiangjun could still visit the child. The child would still be closer to its biological mother. Wasn't she just doing all this work for someone else's benefit?

Moreover, the Empress seemed indifferent to the child's gender. Her words implied that in the future, any other children Xiangjun might have would also be raised by her...

After thinking over and over, Xiangjun still couldn't understand. She decided to ask Gu Tingxue about this matter.

Gu Tingxue didn't have time to see Xiangjun, but he did write her a letter. Inside, there were only two words: "hostage."

Xiangjun had not read the Strategies of the Warring States in vain. After some thought, she understood.

The Empress probably wanted to use the child as a hostage to form some kind of alliance with Xiangjun.

The Emperor was wary of the Yang family. Although the Prime Minister Yang had died, when the Emperor had pretended to be poisoned and unconscious, the Empress had not performed very well. It could be said that there was little affection between them as husband and wife.

Therefore, the Emperor was also unwilling for the Empress to have a child. If the Empress's second imperial son had still been alive back then, perhaps the Yang family would have rebelled even faster than Song Feijing, ordering the imperial physicians to finish off the Emperor and support their own grandson as the new emperor.

Given the Emperor's suspicion and desire for power, he would definitely not allow the Empress to have another child.

Thus, the Empress was using this roundabout method to obtain a child, raising the child as a hostage by her side and forming an alliance with Xiangjun and the Xu family.

In the future, if the Emperor was unwilling to let the child raised by the Empress ascend the throne, she could secretly support another of Xiangjun's children to the throne. Because of the first child as a bridge, the relationship between the two sides would be more stable.

Xiangjun pondered. Although cooperating with Empress Yang had its benefits, it was like trying to skin a tiger.

Empress Yang didn't seem like the kind of person who could tolerate having two empress dowagers in the rear palace.

She feared that when the time was ripe, she would have to give up the child to keep her own life.

To be honest, although Xiangjun despised Noble Consort Rong, she was even more wary of the Empress. She would rather fight with Noble Consort Rong in the future than deal with the ruthless Empress Yang.

No matter what, she would never let anyone take her second child away.

That was the child she loved the most, the child who would secretly cry for her after her death, the child who, because he missed her, would be bullied by his other brothers.

Xiangjun rubbed her belly, thinking of how determined the Empress was to get this child. She knew the Empress could not be kept.

"Mengmei..." Xiangjun called Mengmei over. "You go to Weiyang Palace and deliver a message. Say that I will take the initiative to mention to His Majesty that, once the child is a month old, I will let the Empress take the child to Weiyang Palace to raise."

"Your Highness! No! You are not the same as when you first entered the palace. Our Chengxiang Palace is not at the mercy of Weiyang Palace. Moreover, we have the Noble Consort to help you. Why must you..."

Xiangjun waved her hand, interrupting Mengmei. With a stern face, she said, "Can one be on guard against thieves for a thousand days? The Empress is determined to get this child. It's better to agree to her first and then plan slowly. Don't worry, this palace has a plan. You just go deliver the message. Right now, the most important thing is for us to safely give birth to this child."

Mengmei sighed and nodded, but still went to deliver the message.

The Empress was very happy. Not only did she immediately send many rewards, but she also took the initiative to mention to the Emperor that, to allow Xiangjun to rest easy and nurture the child, her family should be allowed to enter the palace to see her.

Xiangjun's family was all in Yangzhou. Only her convenient "brother" Xu Huanwen was studying at the Imperial College. The Emperor granted a favor and, when Xiangjun was seven months pregnant, allowed Xu Huanwen to enter the palace to visit his "sister."

This was the first time Xiangjun had ever met Xu Huanwen.

Back when she was at the Xu family, she had heard that the old master was very fond of his third son. However, the third brother was a concubine's son, and the madam did not like him, always making things difficult for him and his mother. So, in his early years, the third brother had a very hard time at home.

The internal struggles of the Xu family were also very vicious and dirty.

Even her clever mentor had suffered a lot, let alone Xu Huanwen and his mother.

Unexpectedly, the third brother, a concubine's son, had now established himself in the Xu family through his own efforts.

He was now studying at the Imperial College. Even if he couldn't pass the imperial examinations to become a Juren, his status as a student of the Imperial College meant he could wait for a vacancy in the court and eventually become an official.

There was a heavenly gap between officials and merchants. To go from being the son of a merchant to an official could be described as a leap to heaven.

It seemed that Xu Huanwen would be the future head of the Xu family, and he was only twenty years old.

On this day, Xiangjun got up early, had Mengmei dress her up, and prepared food and drinks, waiting for Xu Huanwen's arrival.

Although she didn't have much affection for the Xu family, they were still her maternal family. They were in a relationship where they would rise or fall together. There was nothing in this world that bound people more tightly than interests and lives.

Therefore, Xiangjun was very much looking forward to meeting Xu Huanwen.

He would be her future ally. If he was capable, she would be like a tiger with wings added. She wouldn't have to rely on Gu Tingxue for everything in the imperial court and could have her own influence.

When the time came, someone announced that Xu Huanwen had arrived.

Xiangjun stood up to welcome him and saw a man in a wide-sleeved, black-bordered, green robe walk in.

Upon seeing Xiangjun, the man immediately knelt on one knee and bowed his head. "This commoner, Xu Huanwen, greets Honored Concubine Lian. May Your Highness have boundless fortune and good health."

"Brother, you are too polite. Xiaoluzhi, why don't you help Brother up? Mengmei, grant Brother a seat."

Xu Huanwen had been somewhat nervous, but hearing Xiangjun's warm and intimate tone, the tension in his heart eased considerably.

Only then did he dare to look up at Xiangjun.

At just one glance, his face turned red, and he quickly lowered his head again.

Compared to before, Xiangjun was even more beautiful now. Previously, when she was at the Xu family, although she was also a beauty, she didn't have this kind of noble demeanor, this innate sense of preciousness that could not be violated.

Only the imperial palace could nurture such a noble peony.

Xiaoluzhi quickly helped Xu Huanwen up, and Mengmei brought an embroidered stool for Xu Huanwen, placing it next to Xiangjun.

After Xu Huanwen sat down, Mengmei, with a smile, warmly served him tea.

A warm current flowed through Xu Huanwen's heart. This "sister" treated him even more warmly and closely than his own sister did.

Xiangjun had chosen not to meet Xu Huanwen in the main hall, precisely to appear more intimate.

She looked at her third brother and found him quite handsome, with a scholarly and upright demeanor.

Although he was not as strikingly handsome as Gu Tingxue, he was still considered elegant and charming among ordinary people.

Not bad. With such looks, if she could secure a better official position for him, she thought it wouldn't be difficult for her to arrange a good marriage for Xu Huanwen in the capital in the future.

chapters.title: A Wealthy Maidens Family
chapters.content:
Being stared at by Xiangjun like this, Xu Huanwen's face turned red.

After taking a sip of tea to cover his embarrassment, he saw that Xiangjun was still looking at him. Only then did he speak, "Why does Your Highness look at this commoner like this?"

"It's the first time I've seen you, elder brother, so I need to look carefully to make sure I recognize you in the future. Elder brother should also look at me clearly, so you don't forget me," Xiangjun said, feigning intimacy.

Hearing Xiangjun say this, Xu Huanwen's face turned even redder. He lowered his eyes and said in a low voice, somewhat embarrassed, "Your Highness, this commoner has actually seen you before."

"Hmm?" Xiangjun was surprised. "Where have we met before?"

Xu Huanwen replied, "At the Xu family residence, I have seen Your Highness many times, but Your Highness didn't know me."

Xiangjun thought for a moment and wasn't surprised. She used to be a thin horse raised by the Xu family and had performed for the masters in the courtyard once or twice. Moreover, she often went to the courtyard to find her master, so it was possible they had encountered each other.

However, Xiangjun didn't care about those unimportant matters. Time was limited, and she needed to quickly discuss important business with Xu Huanwen.

"Elder brother, our time is limited. Let me talk to you about the important matters first."

Hearing Xiangjun say this, Xu Huanwen immediately became serious. He straightened his body and said solemnly, "Please give your orders, Your Highness."

"I ask you, has the Yang family sent someone to see you?"

"They have. The Yang family sent a family minister to see me privately, saying they could directly recommend me for an official position in the court, but I refused."

Xiangjun felt a sense of relief and a satisfied smile appeared on her face. She asked, "Why did elder brother refuse?"

"Although the Yang family is powerful, I have only recently entered the Imperial College and haven't figured out the current situation in the capital. Moreover, there have been many storms in the court recently, and many people have died. I don't dare to easily choose a side, fearing it might affect Your Highness's plans in the palace. If I were to ruin Your Highness's great plans because of my own selfishness, I would be a sinner to the Xu family."

Xiangjun was greatly pleased. This elder brother not only read well but was also clear-headed and cautious. He was indeed a promising talent.

"How did you refuse them?"

"Your Highness can rest assured. I did not offend the Yang family. I only said that I wanted to participate in next year's imperial examination and temporarily focus on my studies. The Yang family did not give up and said they wanted to arrange a position for my father in Jiangnan. I couldn't agree or refuse, so I said I would write a letter to ask my father what kind of official he wanted to be before replying to the Yang family..."

Xiangjun burst out laughing, covering her mouth with a handkerchief, laughing so hard her stomach hurt.

She imagined that the people from the Yang family must be cursing Xu Huanwen to death in their hearts.

They probably thought the Xu family was both greedy and stupid, actually asking their father what kind of official he wanted to be, as if ordering from a menu.

Seeing Xiangjun laughing, Xu Huanwen became a bit flustered.

"Your Highness, did I answer incorrectly?"

"No, you answered very well. Elder brother is a man of strategy. Xiangjun is at ease. However, elder brother, you should still find a way to refuse the Yang family without leaving any traces. Don't offend them either. Although the Yang family is suppressed by His Majesty, they still have a strong foundation. If they want to crush our Xu family, it would be very easy."

"I understand."

"Elder brother, you should also advise father not to get involved with the Yang family. It's better to keep a low profile now, even if it means suffering some losses."

Xu Huanwen said firmly, "Your Highness can rest assured. Father now believes everything Your Highness says. Whatever Your Highness asks us to do, we will obey without question."

Hearing this, Xiangjun was reassured.

Thinking about Xu San Laoye, he was a very slippery old loach, decisive, and could be ruthless when necessary. In the business world, he was considered a hero.

As long as Xu San Laoye could maintain consistency with Xiangjun, with his abilities, it would not be difficult to get rid of the Yang family's entanglement.

After thinking for a moment, Xiangjun reminded again, "Elder brother, you and father must remember that His Majesty will definitely centralize power in his own hands, so the Yang family will certainly fall. You should know what to do..."

Xu Huanwen's expression changed greatly. Such court secrets were absolutely impossible for him and his father to know.

In their eyes, the Yang family seemed all-powerful and not to be provoked. Who would have thought they were already like grasshoppers after autumn?

Seeing Xu Huanwen's expression change greatly, Xiangjun comforted him, "Elder brother doesn't need to worry. As long as my position in the harem is stable, our Xu family will be fine. If father wants to be an official, I can also find a way to ask His Majesty to grant him a position. We don't need to owe the Yang family any favors."

Xiangjun made it sound simple, but Xu Huanwen did not dare to easily agree.

"When I came to the capital, father told me that Your Highness has a difficult time in the palace, and we must not use Your Highness's relationships in the palace for trivial matters."

Hearing Xu Huanwen say this, Xiangjun felt even more at ease.

The Xu family, Xu San Laoye, and Xu Huanwen all had a broader vision than she had expected.

"You can reassure father. This is really a small matter and won't affect me much."

Xu Huanwen's heart also relaxed a bit. It seemed that Her Highness was indeed favored by His Majesty.

After all the reminders were given, Xiangjun also gave Xu Huanwen the rewards she had prepared in advance.

The Xu family was a huge wealthy family in Jiangnan. Even though Xu Huanwen was an unfavored illegitimate son, he had seen all kinds of rare treasures.

So the things Xiangjun gave him were all unique books, tribute brushes, ink, paper, and inkstones.

Among them, there was an inkstone that His Majesty had rewarded Xiangjun for her good handwriting. There were only three of its kind in the world.

Xu Huanwen was naturally very grateful and also gave Xiangjun the gifts he had brought.

In addition to some fashionable trinkets from Jiangnan, there were also some expensive rouge, jewelry, gemstones, fabrics, and the like. Surprisingly, there was also a box of silver notes, amounting to about 200,000 taels.

Looking at the stack of silver notes, Xiangjun felt emotional. The Xu family was really rich.

"Father said that Your Highness needs to grease many palms in the palace, so this money is left for Your Highness to reward others. In the future, father will send 200,000 taels into the palace every year for Your Highness to use for greasing palms. If Your Highness still needs more, just write a letter home. If it's urgent, you can send someone to the Xu family's shop in the capital, and the shopkeeper will immediately provide the silver for Your Highness."

Xiangjun's smile could not be hidden. Having a wealthy maiden family was really good.

Who would complain about having too much money?

Even the emperor in this palace would complain about not having enough money.

---

chapters.title: Does Your Highness Want to Leave the Palace?
chapters.content:
"200,000 taels is not a small amount. Father must not let it affect the turnover of the business or the family's expenses because of me."

"Your Highness can rest assured. Three years ago, after the major private salt case in Jiangnan, our Xu family gradually took over all the salt transportation business in Jiangnan."

"With such a big business in the hands of the Xu family, has anyone made things difficult for you?"

"Your Highness can rest assured. Every year, we pay our respects to Director Gu of the Shence Army, and our Xu family will not monopolize the profits; we will share some benefits. Moreover, in the past year or two, Your Highness has been favored in the palace, and the gentry and merchants in Jiangnan only seek to please our Xu family, not to make things difficult for us."

Xiangjun was also somewhat reassured and, without standing on ceremony, had Mengmei accept all the silver notes.

In the future, she would have many uses for money. She wanted to develop her own power in the harem and to get people to do things for her, she would have to be generous with money.

After a few more words, time was up, and someone from the palace came to remind that Xu Huanwen should leave.

Xu Huanwen stood up to take his leave.

"His Majesty said that after Your Highness gives birth, he will let me enter the palace to see Your Highness again. Huanwen only hopes that Your Highness will have a smooth delivery and that all your wishes come true."

Xiangjun calculated the time and thought that by the time she gave birth, Xu Huanwen would probably be taking the imperial examination.

"Then I also wish elder brother success in the imperial examination and a bright future."

Xu Huanwen left.

After he left, Xiangjun sat in the palace looking at the fashionable trinkets from Jiangnan that he had brought, and suddenly felt a touch of melancholy.

Compared to the capital, which was often sandy and dry, she actually preferred Jiangnan, where she had grown up.

She hadn't felt this way before, but now, after seeing a "old acquaintance," she felt a bit homesick.

"Is Your Highness missing home?"

"Home? Jiangnan can't be considered our home."

Speaking of which, where did people like them have a home?

Perhaps it was due to her pregnancy making her more sentimental. Mengmei, afraid that Her Highness would be unhappy staying in the room, suggested, "Your Highness, the weather is nice today. How about we go for a walk in the Imperial Garden?"

"That's a good idea."

Xiangjun was now seven months pregnant, but she had been controlling her diet and exercise, so her belly wasn't too big. Compared to other pregnant women, her belly looked like it was only six months along.

In her previous life, Xiangjun had suffered from a large belly and difficulty giving birth, which eventually led to a cesarean section. The pain was so severe that she couldn't forget it even after dying once.

So, for this pregnancy, Xiangjun was extremely cautious. Not only did she walk every day, but she also ate carefully and had the imperial physician check her pulse daily.

Xiangjun took her people and prepared to go out. As a noble consort, her entourage was quite large.

A large group of people walked onto the palace road, and by chance, they met Gu Tingxue, who was leading two rows of eunuchs to deliver rewards.

"Why are you delivering rewards again?" Xiangjun looked curiously.

"His Majesty suddenly remembered Your Highness's goodness and asked me to bring some things over. Noble Consort, where are you going?"

Xiangjun felt that His Majesty was being a bit inexplicable. Why did he suddenly remember her goodness?

But refusing rewards would be foolish, so she happily accepted them and had the palace servants take the things back first.

"I was thinking of going out for a walk. Originally, I wanted to go to the Imperial Garden. Since His Majesty has sent rewards, I should go and express my gratitude first."

"His Majesty is meeting with foreign officials and may not be available now. Your Highness might want to go later."

"Then I'll go for a walk on the city wall. Today, I want to look into the distance. After the foreign officials leave, I will go and express my gratitude."

Gu Tingxue dismissed the eunuchs behind him to follow Xiao Luzi and first take the things rewarded by His Majesty back to Chengxiang Hall.

Then, he walked up to Xiangjun and whispered, "Why doesn't Tingxue accompany Your Highness for a walk?"

Xiangjun lowered her voice, "Eunuch Tingxue, do you want to accompany me for a walk? Aren't you afraid of being seen and misunderstood?"

"Your Highness is carrying the dragon's descendant and is favored. Letting this humble servant attend to Your Highness's walk is perfectly fine."

Xiangjun was very pleased and somewhat happy. "You, Gu Tingxue, you want to accompany me, but you still need me to play the villain?"

"Would Your Highness be willing?"

Xiangjun suddenly raised her voice, her tone sweet and proud, with a touch of arrogance from a small person who had achieved their goal. She lifted her small, exquisite chin and said, "Eunuch Tingxue, you have quite the airs. I am now carrying the dragon's descendant, and you can't even attend to me once? I want you to support me. Otherwise, if I sprain my ankle later and hurt the dragon's son, can Eunuch Tingxue afford the responsibility?"

Gu Tingxue smiled, extended his hand for Xiangjun to hold, and said, "This humble servant will attend to Your Highness's walk."

Xiangjun coldly humphed, placed her hand on Gu Tingxue's, but Gu Tingxue turned his hand and firmly grasped hers, startling Xiangjun, who tried to pull her hand back. However, Gu Tingxue held it tightly, and she couldn't pull it away.

"You dog slave, do you want to ruin me?" Xiangjun said in a low voice.

Gu Tingxue then smiled and loosened his grip, obediently letting Xiangjun hold his arm.

The two walked and chatted idly.

Xiangjun secretly glanced at Gu Tingxue.

Where did Gu Tingxue look like a slave? Other eunuchs, when supporting a noble consort, would bend over and bow their heads. Only he stood straight, walking with great momentum, making her look like a concubine.

"Why are you looking at this humble servant?" Gu Tingxue asked.

"What are you being so imposing about?" Xiangjun said unhappily, "Those who don't know might think you are my master."

"How could that be? Your Highness is peerlessly beautiful and noble. One look and it's clear that you are this humble servant's master."

Xiangjun loved to hear such flattering words. She happily accepted them, smiling proudly, lifting her head, and walking even more arrogantly, truly exuding the demeanor of a favored consort.

The two walked to the city wall.

"Why did Your Highness think of coming here today?"

Xiangjun looked into the distance and sighed, "I don't know when I will be able to go out and take a look."

Gu Tingxue's expression darkened. He turned and grasped Xiangjun's arm, applying some force. His voice was dark as he asked, "Does Your Highness want to leave the palace?"

Xiangjun gave Gu Tingxue a speechless look.

Wasn't Gu Tingxue's reaction a bit too strong?

"I just want to occasionally go out and take a look, that's all. Tingxue, don't overthink it. I've worked hard to climb to this position. Who would want to leave the palace..."

Gu Tingxue finally loosened his tight grip on Xiangjun's arm, and the crazy intensity in his eyes also receded, returning to his usual gloomy and cold demeanor.

"Are you afraid that I will leave the palace one day?" Xiangjun smiled and looked into the distance, saying, "Tingxue, you are being too suspicious. Once you enter the palace gate, it's as deep as the sea. I will never be able to leave this place in my lifetime. You must accompany me well."

Palace maids, upon reaching a certain age and with the master's permission, could leave the harem.

But in this harem, only consorts and eunuchs were locked in this place for life.

The two gazed into the distance together and happened to see a group of people leaving the palace.

The man leading the group was tall and mighty, exuding a murderous aura, with a sword hanging from his waist. He was clearly a military man.

"It seems that the foreign official His Majesty was meeting has already left the Tai Ji Hall. Your Highness can go and express her gratitude now."

Was this the foreign official His Majesty had just met?

Xiangjun asked curiously, "Who is that?"

"That is His Majesty's younger brother, Grand General Wang, Zhou Qingchong."

So, this was the famous Grand General Wang who guarded the northern border.

chapters.title: I Grow Fonder of You Every Day
chapters.content:
Xiangjun thought that with the return of Grand General Wang, the Emperor and Honored Consort Rong would likely start quarreling again.

Not long ago, His Majesty and the Honored Consort had been at odds. The Emperor had pressured the Consort to sever ties with Song Feijing, and the Consort had been weeping daily, feeling that the Emperor did not trust her.

The Emperor, in turn, was seething with anger, convinced that the Consort was grieving over Song Feijing.

Now, with the return of another of the Consort’s devoted admirers, it seemed His Majesty and the Consort were bound to have new misunderstandings.

It was no wonder they were the original novel’s male and female leads—they truly knew how to stir up drama, creating so many misunderstandings.

A sudden realization struck Xiangjun, and she turned to Gu Tingxue, her eyes widening slightly.

"Tingxue, could it be that His Majesty suddenly thought to bestow favors upon me because Grand General Wang has returned, and he is jealous of the Consort?"

Gu Tingxue glanced at Xiangjun, his eyes filled with admiration.

"Among all the concubines in the palace, if Your Highness is second in understanding His Majesty’s intentions, then no one could be first."

Heavens, that was true.

Xiangjun’s face twisted in disdain.

Must these people drag her into their emotional games?

She truly despised them all...

Perhaps it was because she had lived too comfortably from childhood that she found it absurd to waste time on such trivial romantic entanglements.

The thought that His Majesty was showing her favor out of jealousy toward the Consort made Xiangjun feel tainted, as if she had been sullied by their petty emotions.

Seeing her disgusted expression, Gu Tingxue’s smile deepened.

"Why does Your Highness look like that? Others would be overjoyed."

"Because this palace finds its rivals beneath contempt."

It lowered the quality of her court intrigue.

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun with a mix of admiration and helplessness.

Most women in the world were easily swayed by emotions, yet the one he favored was above such trivialities.

He should consider himself fortunate that he still had some use to her.

"Did Grand General Wang return for the Honored Consort?" Xiangjun asked again.

Xiangjun knew that Grand General Wang was stationed at the northern border, where his prestige in the military was unmatched. As a prince, he was not supposed to return to the capital lightly.

So why had he suddenly come back at this odd time?

"Grand General Wang returned to the capital to report on his duties. Additionally, his birth mother, the Virtuous Dowager Consort, will soon celebrate her fiftieth birthday. With His Majesty’s permission, he is allowed to stay in the capital for a while to accompany the Dowager Consort. He will return after her birthday next year."

Xiangjun sneered, her tone dripping with sarcasm. "Then we’re in for another good show, aren’t we?"

"Your Highness, rest assured. This humble servant knows you are bored during your pregnancy. If anything interesting happens, I will make sure you are the first to know."

...

Sure enough, within a few days, Xiangjun heard the ridiculous news.

Because the Emperor despised Grand General Wang even more than Song Feijing, the General’s return had reignited His Majesty’s jealousy.

After meeting with Grand General Wang, the Emperor went to the Honored Consort’s chambers, where they had a fierce argument. In a fit of rage, the Emperor forced himself upon her.

Xiangjun could hardly believe it—how could two people in their thirties still behave like this?

Did His Majesty not have enough troubles with state affairs that he still had the energy to force himself on his concubine?

The Emperor visited her for three consecutive days, each time clashing with the Consort. On the third day, the Consort slapped the Emperor. Enraged, His Majesty punished the entire staff of the Ganlu Palace.

Striking the Emperor was an offense punishable by death, but since the Emperor could not bear to punish the Consort, he took it out on her palace attendants instead.

The Consort, seeing her servants punished, lashed out at the Emperor with heart-wrenching words, and the two began a cold war once more.

Xiangjun listened to a young eunuch vividly describe the scene while she snacked on melon seeds.

She had to admit, the young eunuch Gu Tingxue had chosen was a gifted storyteller.

After rewarding the eunuch, Xiangjun ordered Mengmei to prepare some of the Emperor’s favorite dishes.

"Will His Majesty be visiting our Chengxiang Palace today?"

"He should be."

In the past, whenever the Emperor quarreled with the Consort, he would come to Xiangjun to reclaim his imperial dignity.

Sure enough, at dinnertime, the Emperor arrived.

Seeing the table filled with his favorite dishes, the Emperor was surprised. "Did Xiangjun know I was coming?"

"I did not, Your Majesty, but I hoped you would. So every day, I prepare the dishes you love. If you do not come, eating the food you enjoy makes me feel as if you are here with me, and that brings me joy."

The Emperor’s expression softened, and he took Xiangjun’s hand, treating her with the utmost tenderness as they dined together.

What could Xiangjun do?

Naturally, she flattered the Emperor the entire time, letting him bask in the blind adoration and unconditional love of a woman.

But Xiangjun felt she had performed too well, for even though she could not serve him in bed, the Emperor still insisted on staying by her side, refusing to leave.

When Qinglian tried to curry favor and help Xiangjun avoid the Emperor, she was actually rebuffed by His Majesty, who scolded her for competing for the favor of Consort Jieyu.

"Your Majesty, do not blame Sister Qinglian. She only has the best intentions for the child in my womb."

The Emperor sighed. "You are so pure-hearted. Rest assured, I will stay with you. Even if I cannot share your bed, being with you brings me joy."

Xiangjun could only bitterly smile in her heart. She truly did not want to sleep with the Emperor, and the Emperor was not the one she wanted to serve.

She wanted to sleep with Gu Tingxue.

As they lay in bed, Xiangjun, with her large belly, had to sleep on her side. The Emperor faced her, gazing at her youthful, radiant, and beautiful face. His withered heart softened for a moment.

"I find myself growing fonder of you every day," the Emperor said, gently caressing Xiangjun’s face with tenderness and deep affection.

Xiangjun forced herself to suppress her discomfort and put on a shy and touched smile.

She did not believe in the Emperor’s love.

Their Emperor, Zhen Qing, loved no one. He was simply using his favor toward her to spite the Consort.

But Xiangjun was always quick to seize an opportunity. She immediately asked with implied meaning, "Why does Your Majesty grow fonder of me? I wish to know so that I may continue to strive and make Your Majesty love me even more."

"You are never satisfied," the Emperor chuckled, pinching Xiangjun’s nose. "I like how your heart and eyes are filled only with me."

Xiangjun rolled her eyes internally. Sure enough, the Emperor’s affection for her was just for the Consort’s benefit.

The Consort had many admirers at her beck and call, so the Emperor wanted to favor a woman who had only him and could rely solely on him.

"Of course, in my heart, Your Majesty is the tallest, the most extraordinary, the most handsome man in the world. You are the only one Xiangjun can depend on in this life. No one can compare to you."

The Emperor’s gaze deepened. "Yes, I am your only reliance."

The Emperor sighed. He was Xiangjun’s only reliance, but not the Consort’s. Without Song Feijing, there was still Grand General Wang, Prince Jin...

From childhood to adulthood, for Xue Jiaojiao, he, Zhou Qinghe, had never been her sole dependence. She had too many choices.

If he were not the Emperor, where would Xue Jiaojiao be?

Seeing the Emperor lost in thought, Xiangjun immediately took his hand and placed it on her belly.

"Your Majesty is not only my reliance but also the reliance of our child. I am different from the other concubines in the palace. My father is merely a merchant, and my family background is humble. If not for Your Majesty’s favor, how could I have the life I have now?"

Hearing Xiangjun mention her family background, the Emperor realized that, with her pregnancy and her current rank as Jieyu, her father was still just a merchant—a status unworthy of imperial dignity.

Since the Emperor thought highly of Xiangjun, he was willing to grant her and her family honor.

"Shall I bestow an official position upon your father?" the Emperor asked.

---

chapters.title: Being a Father to the Child
chapters.content:
Xiangjun had not expected it to be this easy. She had thought she would need to subtly remind him a few more times.

The Emperor was indeed quick to act.

Xiangjun was not one to feign modesty. Without hesitation, she immediately accepted, her eyes welling with tears.

"Really? Then, on behalf of my father, I thank Your Majesty! Your Majesty has been so kind to me!"

The Emperor chuckled and pinched Xiangjun’s nose. "Others would at least pretend to refuse, but you are quite direct."

"I won’t refuse! The sisters in the palace often mock me behind my back, saying I come from a lowly merchant family. Your Majesty bestowing an official position upon my father is an act of care and support for me. It gives me dignity, and I am overjoyed. I am only grateful for Your Majesty’s kindness. Rest assured, my father will not disappoint Your Majesty’s good intentions. He will be a good official."

Seeing Xiangjun’s delighted expression, the Emperor found it not the least bit annoying—in fact, he rather liked it.

With just a wave of his hand, he could completely change the fate of this woman’s family and bring her such joy.

Compared to the Consort’s cold demeanor, Xiangjun’s elation was far more endearing.

...

Soon after, Xiangjun received a letter from her father, along with a large sum of silver notes.

The Emperor had appointed her father as a magistrate. Although a magistrate was not a high-ranking official, the counties of Suzhou were wealthy, and serving as a magistrate in such a prosperous place made her father very happy.

Xiangjun did not wish for her father to hold a higher position. Given his abilities, being a capable magistrate was already impressive. Holding too high an office might invite trouble.

As for the family business, her father had entrusted it to his eldest son. After all, officials were not allowed to engage in commerce.

Now, Xiangjun was only waiting for next spring’s imperial examinations to see if Xu Huanwen could pass and become a Jinshi.

If he succeeded, Xiangjun was confident she could secure a position in the capital for him.

These days, Xiangjun was truly content.

The Emperor visited often, the higher-ranking concubines avoided provoking her, and the Empress was not causing trouble. The Consort Ye was still grieving the loss of her child and had not recovered. Xiangjun’s pregnancy was peaceful.

But what pleased Xiangjun the most was that, because the Emperor had been busy and unable to spend time with her, he felt guilty and often sent Gu Tingxue to deliver gifts.

Xiangjun’s pregnancy was advanced now, and for some reason, she often felt restless. She truly needed Gu Tingxue.

So much so that Gu Tingxue had to prepare extra handkerchiefs to wipe his hands.

"Let’s stop here for today. You should take care of your body," Gu Tingxue said helplessly.

Seeing Gu Tingxue’s teasing expression, even someone as shameless as Xiangjun felt a little embarrassed.

"Ah!"

Xiangjun suddenly exclaimed, startling Gu Tingxue. He immediately leaned in anxiously. "What’s wrong? Did you stir the fetus? I knew I shouldn’t have indulged you."

Seeing his worried expression, Xiangjun burst out laughing. She grabbed Gu Tingxue’s hand and placed it on her belly.

"The baby is moving."

Gu Tingxue felt a small hand pressing against his palm through her belly, a strange sensation that left him stunned.

His eyes widened in disbelief as he stared at Xiangjun.

A look of pure joy and surprise flickered in his eyes—such a bright expression was the first time Xiangjun had ever seen on Gu Tingxue’s face. For a moment, the formidable and intimidating eunuch seemed to have the youthful cheerfulness appropriate for his age.

"He really likes you, Tingxue. He must think you’re his father since you come every day."

But at her words, Gu Tingxue’s expression suddenly darkened. He tried to pull his hand back, but Xiangjun noticed and firmly pressed his hand against her belly.

She knew what Gu Tingxue was thinking.

Gu Tingxue had always considered himself a eunuch, feeling ashamed of his own body. He believed he was unworthy of being a prince’s father.

"Your Highness... you must not say such things."

"Does Tingxue not want to?"

"I am but a humble eunuch. If the prince, upon growing up, learns of the relationship between Your Highness and me, I will have no place to be buried."

"You underestimate yourself, Tingxue. With your power, if he dares look down on you, it will be he and I who have no place to be buried."

Gu Tingxue looked up at Xiangjun, his dark eyes betraying a surge of emotion.

"You know I would never treat you and the child that way."

"And you should know that we would never treat you that way either." Xiangjun held Gu Tingxue’s hand, moving it gently over her belly. "Look..."

Gu Tingxue felt it—the child in Xiangjun’s womb was responding to him.

Xiangjun dropped her fierce expression and spoke softly, soothing Gu Tingxue’s unease.

"Tingxue, remember this: this child is ours. He is the one who will help us achieve our dreams."

This... was his child?

Gu Tingxue’s gaze darkened as he lowered his head, his long lashes hiding the turmoil within.

"The prince in your womb is the most noble child in the world. I am but a lowly eunuch. To be able to care for and assist the prince is already my great fortune. I ask for nothing more."

"I know my child. Whoever is kind to him, he will be kind to in return. He is the most clever and filial child in the world. As long as you devote yourself to him, he will be your son. Trust me."

Gu Tingxue looked up at Xiangjun.

Her gaze was so firm, as if she truly knew what the child was thinking.

"Tingxue, the imperial family has no father-son affection, only ruler and subject. I also know that my child will not receive much affection from the Emperor. But my prince needs a father who truly loves him. Would you be willing?"

Xiangjun saw the emotion in Gu Tingxue’s eyes. She had intended to say more, but in the next moment, Gu Tingxue reached out and pulled her into an embrace.

Gu Tingxue placed his hand on Xiangjun’s lower back, and his head gently rested on her belly, his eyes filled with infinite tenderness.

Xiangjun’s lips curled into a smile, and she couldn’t help but laugh.

With one hand supporting her back and the other stroking Gu Tingxue’s hair, they looked like a family of three.

Xiangjun knew that Gu Tingxue was a eunuch, but eunuchs also longed to be normal men.

So he needed the feeling of being a husband and a father.

As long as she could give Gu Tingxue a home and fill the void of those two roles for him, she could firmly grasp his heart. He would always be at her service, paving the way for her prince.

"Your Highness, rest assured. This child will have everything he desires," Gu Tingxue said softly.

Gu Tingxue could not see Xiangjun’s expression from his angle.

Xiangjun couldn’t help but reveal a satisfied smile.

"With your promise, I have nothing to worry about."

Gu Tingxue’s gaze darkened. How could he not know what Xiangjun was doing?

But Xiangjun understood what he needed so well that he was willing to step into the dream she had woven for him.

However, Xiangjun had underestimated Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue wanted much more than what Xiangjun was willing to give.

It didn’t matter. Gu Tingxue thought, she would get what she wanted, and so would he.

chapters.title: Water Breaks
chapters.content:
In the blink of an eye, Xiangjun’s due date arrived.

Long before, the palace midwives and wet nurses had been prepared. All of them were personally selected by Gu Tingxue—reliable, trustworthy, and absolutely loyal.

Xiangjun’s father had also sent two medical women from Jiangnan in advance. They would stay in the palace to assist Xiangjun and help her recover after childbirth.

The entire Chengxiang Hall was bustling in preparation for Xiangjun’s delivery. Everyone was orderly and efficient—except for Xiangjun, who was thoroughly annoyed.

Her due date had passed by several days, yet the child still showed no sign of arriving. Was it so comfortable in her belly that it refused to come out?

The imperial physicians said her condition was fine, and a delay of a few days was normal. It was better not to induce labor with medicine for now; she should wait a little longer.

But Xiangjun couldn’t bear to wait another moment. She wanted the child out immediately and tried every method to induce labor—eating chili peppers, walking around, even jumping up and down. Yet the child remained snug inside her.

Xiangjun wasn’t afraid, but she terrified everyone in Chengxiang Hall. No one could stop her, and no one dared defy the Consort’s temper.

After a whole day of this, Xiangjun still showed no signs of labor.

Late at night, unable to sleep from frustration, she started smashing things in the palace, finally summoning Gu Tingxue.

As soon as Gu Tingxue arrived, Meng Mei and the others treated him like a savior, rushing forward to report the Consort’s condition.

Consort Lian had been unpredictable throughout her pregnancy. The servants in Chengxiang Hall had no solutions—every time, they relied on Lord Tingxue to soothe her.

"Lord Tingxue, please advise our Consort," little Luzi pleaded pitifully. "She’s been eating chili peppers and jumping around. If something happens to the prince, we servants won’t have enough heads to lose!"

"All of you, withdraw," Gu Tingxue ordered.

Everyone immediately retreated, closing the door behind them, leaving only Gu Tingxue to face Consort Lian’s wrath.

Gu Tingxue sighed helplessly. The people in Chengxiang Hall were getting quicker at locking the door.

Now, only Xiangjun and Gu Tingxue remained in the room.

He picked up the soft pillow she had thrown to the floor, set it aside, then sat beside her, gently asking, "Why are you angry again? Who upset you?"

*Him!* Xiangjun pointed at her own belly.

"How can you be mad at him? He hasn’t even been born yet."

"Can I not be angry? He only cares about his own comfort, ignoring his mother’s hardship carrying him!" Xiangjun grumbled. "Try carrying a watermelon in your belly for ten months and see if you’d still be happy!"

Xiangjun raised her hand as if to punch her own stomach, but Gu Tingxue grabbed her wrist.

"What are you doing!" Gu Tingxue’s voice was tense. "What if you hurt him?"

Seeing his anxiety, Xiangjun felt wronged. Her lips trembled, and she whined tearfully, "I knew it! You all only care about my child, not me!"

"Nonsense. I care because he is your child. Don’t make trouble—you’ll only hurt yourself."

Xiangjun looked at Gu Tingxue with grievance, then suddenly her expression changed.

Her eyes lit up as she blinked at Gu Tingxue.

Seeing that look, Gu Tingxue knew something was wrong. Sure enough, Xiangjun pulled him toward the bed.

"What is the Consort doing?"

"I heard there’s another way to induce labor. Come, let’s try it."

"Consort!" Gu Tingxue’s face flushed crimson. "At a time like this, how can you still be thinking of such things?"

"Do you think I’m joking? It really can induce labor. Hurry, take off your clothes."

With that, Xiangjun went to the cabinet beside the bed, rummaged through it, and pulled out a small box, handing it to Gu Tingxue.

"Take this," Xiangjun said.

"What is this?" Gu Tingxue asked.

"It’s for you."

Gu Tingxue opened it, his face turning even redder. He quickly snapped the lid shut.

"Consort... where did you get this?"

"So what if I did? I was going to use it after giving birth, but I can’t wait anymore. This child has to come out tonight—I can’t wait any longer!"

Xiangjun began untying Gu Tingxue’s belt, determined to see this through.

Gu Tingxue unconsciously swallowed, then opened the box again. Inside was a jade "Lord Root."

"I’ll go call the imperial physician for you," Gu Tingxue said, closing the box.

"Why?"

"It’s not good."

Gu Tingxue still couldn’t bring himself to be as shameless as Xiangjun. If the child came out this way, how would he face the child in the future?

Seeing Gu Tingxue hesitate, Xiangjun tugged at her own collar, exposing her fragrant shoulder. She reached out to embrace him, intending to seduce him properly.

But her belly was too large. When she tried to hug him, her stomach got in the way, and instead of embracing him, she awkwardly bumped into his leg.

Seeing Gu Tingxue struggling to hold back laughter, Xiangjun felt utterly humiliated.

Perhaps it was the hormones of pregnancy making her emotional, but tears suddenly streamed down her face.

She was so pitiful! Before pregnancy, she had been so alluring, able to seduce with just a glance. Now, with this huge belly, even her attempts at seduction were ridiculous!

At the sight of her tears, Gu Tingxue panicked.

"My Consort, why are you crying all of a sudden?"

He quickly sat down, holding her and wiping her tears.

"I know, it must be because I’m pregnant and my belly is too big, making me ugly. That’s why Tingxue doesn’t like me anymore and won’t touch me."

"Nonsense, I don’t think that."

"Then why won’t you help me? Don’t you see how much I’m suffering? These past few nights, I haven’t been able to sleep well. I wake up in discomfort after just a little rest and have to keep changing positions!"

"I know, it’s my fault. Don’t cry."

Xiangjun was undoubtedly the most persistent person Gu Tingxue had ever met.

Seeing her cry so sadly, Gu Tingxue’s heart softened. He cupped her face and kissed away her tears.

Gu Tingxue sighed. "Stop crying. I’ll help you."

At his words, Xiangjun’s tears stopped instantly, so quickly that Gu Tingxue suspected she had been faking.

Xiangjun immediately reached for Gu Tingxue’s belt, her tears not yet dry but already replaced with a smug smile.

"Hurry, tonight, this child *must* come out of my belly!"

Gu Tingxue watched helplessly as Xiangjun’s hands wandered over him. But suddenly, she froze.

"What’s wrong?" Gu Tingxue thought she had come up with another way to torment him.

But Xiangjun only widened her eyes, then slowly looked down.

"Tingxue... my water broke."

---

chapters.title: Sacrifice the Mother to Save the Child
chapters.content:
Deep into the night, Chengxiang Hall was brightly lit.

A woman’s piercing screams echoed throughout the palace. Servants and midwives carried copper basins in and out—clear hot water went in, bloody water came out.

The palace servants were all deeply anxious. Several young maids secretly crouched in the corners, wiping their tears. Consort Lian was known throughout the palace as a kind mistress; none of her servants wished her harm.

Noble Consort Jian, Li Qinglian, stood outside, holding the Third Prince, pacing in distress.

"Has His Majesty arrived yet? Send someone to summon him again!"

A young maid was about to step out when she heard the announcement that the Emperor had arrived.

Tonight was the fifteenth, and the Emperor had been staying in the Empress’s quarters, so the two had come together.

As soon as the Emperor entered, he heard Xiangjun’s agonized screams. He immediately asked Noble Consort Jian, "How is Consort Lian? Why is she screaming in such pain?"

Noble Consort Jian, still cradling the Third Prince—who had just finished crying—bowed slightly and reported with concern, "Your Majesty, Consort Lian’s baby is in the wrong position. The midwives are currently massaging her belly to try and correct it. The process is extremely painful, which is why she is screaming so terribly."

As she spoke, Noble Consort Jian’s eyes reddened.

The Emperor furrowed his brows. Seeing his distress, the Empress consoled him, "Your Majesty, Consort Lian is a fortunate one. Previously, the imperial physicians said she might never bear children again, yet she has still conceived an imperial heir. Clearly, Heaven favors her. She will surely turn misfortune into fortune today."

The Emperor sat down, his voice heavy. "Yes, my Xiangjun will surely be fine."

The Empress was taken aback by the Emperor’s reaction. Could it be that His Majesty truly cared for Consort Lian? For so many years, the only one he had ever shown affection for in the harem was Noble Consort Rong.

Suppressing her unease, the Empress sat beside the Emperor.

After another cup of tea’s time, Noble Consort Rong arrived as well.

It was clear she had rushed over as soon as she received the news, her hair simply pinned up with a single hairpin.

"Greetings to Your Majesty, greetings to Her Majesty the Empress," Noble Consort Rong said without much preamble. She glanced at the birthing room before asking Noble Consort Jian, "How is Sister Xiangjun?"

Noble Consort Jian repeated the situation.

Noble Consort Rong and the Emperor were still estranged, so she didn’t say much. She sat to the side, quietly waiting for news from inside.

Ever since the incident where Prime Minister Song had forced his way into the palace, Noble Consort Rong had truly come to regard Xiangjun as one of her own. In that life-or-death moment, Xiangjun had protected her. Such loyalty was rare.

Over the years, Noble Consort Rong had few in the harem she could truly confide in. The Emperor had once been sincere with her, but the longer he ruled, the colder his heart grew. With no living relatives, having Xiangjun by her side like a sister was something she cherished deeply.

Today, with Xiangjun in labor and hearing that the Empress had also come to Chengxiang Hall, Noble Consort Rong had to come—she feared the Empress might harm Xiangjun.

Another agonized scream echoed from inside.

Noble Consort Rong and Noble Consort Jian both stood up.

They exchanged a glance. Knowing that Noble Consort Jian, with the child in her arms, would be inconvenienced, Noble Consort Rong took the initiative to request the Emperor’s permission to enter.

"You and Xiangjun are close. Go and see her for me."

Noble Consort Rong nodded and immediately entered the birthing room.

Inside, Xiangjun was drenched in sweat, groaning in pain.

"What’s happening?" Noble Consort Rong asked.

The midwife replied, "Your Highness, the baby is still not in the correct position. The Consort cannot endure it, so we are letting her rest before trying again."

Noble Consort Rong’s heart raced. Having given birth herself, she knew the pain all too well. She also knew how dangerous a breech birth could be.

Seeing Xiangjun in such a state, she felt as if she were looking at her own sister. She took a handkerchief and wiped the sweat from Xiangjun’s face, comforting her. "Don’t worry. We’ll try again soon. The palace midwives are the best. They will surely correct the position."

Xiangjun suddenly grabbed Noble Consort Rong’s hand.

"Noble Consort... tell His Majesty that if the child cannot be born, do not hesitate out of old feelings—perform a cesarean section to save the child."

"Sister Xiangjun!" Noble Consort Rong was shocked and pained. "You must not think like this! You will certainly give birth safely. Do not speak of such things as cesarean sections again!"

"Please, Sister Rong, deliver my words to His Majesty!" Xiangjun pleaded. "Tell His Majesty that Xiangjun is humble. In this life, to have met His Majesty and received his favor is already more than enough. I have no regrets, no resentment. His Majesty has few heirs—if I can leave a prince or princess for him, I will die without regret. I only beg His Majesty... do not hesitate because of me. *Sacrifice the mother to save the child.*"

Noble Consort Rong was deeply moved. Though it pained her, she wiped her tears and went out to relay Xiangjun’s message.

The Emperor listened in silence for a long moment, saying nothing.

Instinctively, he moved to rise and go to Xiangjun’s birthing room, but the Empress and Eunuch Wan stopped him.

"Your Majesty must not!"

The Emperor had no choice but to sit back down, remaining silent for a long while.

He had never expected Xiangjun to love him to this extent.

In this world, no one truly wished to die. Even if a subject was ordered to die, he knew that most of them harbored their own thoughts.

Even his own mother, he doubted, would be willing to die for him.

Yet now, his concubine—the woman who had devoted herself entirely to him—was willing to die for him.

The Emperor glanced at Noble Consort Rong, then recalled the day of the forced palace entry, when Noble Consort Rong had threatened suicide to stop Prime Minister Song.

No wonder Noble Consort Rong and Xiangjun were so close—they were of the same nature.

But between his son and his beloved concubine, which should he choose?

Another piercing scream came from inside, and the Third Prince in Noble Consort Jian’s arms began to wail.

The Emperor finally snapped out of his thoughts. Already irritable, he looked at Noble Consort Jian with impatience. "Why did you bring the child to the birthing room? How thoughtless!"

The Emperor was taking his frustration out on Noble Consort Jian.

The Empress intervened on her behalf. "Your Majesty, the Third Prince is raised in Consort Lian’s palace and is considered her child. Noble Consort Jian was likely just helping Consort Lian look after him."

Only then did the Emperor realize that the Third Prince was officially under Xiangjun’s care and raised by her.

Though Noble Consort Jian was the birth mother, the Third Prince was not her child.

The Empress deliberately added, "Your Majesty, let Noble Consort Jian take the Third Prince to her own palace to rest for now. She is helping Consort Lian by looking after the child."

The Emperor waved his hand, dismissing Noble Consort Jian.

Qinglian was reluctant to leave—she feared the Empress had ill intentions. But she dared not disobey the Emperor’s order. After exchanging a glance with Noble Consort Rong, who gave her a reassuring look, Qinglian had no choice but to take the Third Prince and leave.

The Empress watched as Noble Consort Jian took the Third Prince away, then feigned indifference. "Children always end up closer to their birth mothers. Even if raised by a wet nurse, they ultimately rely more on their natural mother."

chapters.title: Don't Let Her Die
chapters.content:
The Empress's words carried a hidden meaning.

She was hinting to the Emperor that even if she raised Xiangjun's child, it wouldn't matter. A child is always closer to their birth mother. She would only be raising the child to alleviate her loneliness.

How could the Emperor not understand what the Empress was thinking?

Ever since Xiangjun conceived, the Empress had repeatedly expressed her desire to raise Xiangjun's child. She even said it wouldn't be under her name, that she simply wanted a child to comfort her loneliness in the rear palace, for otherwise, she would be haunted night after night by the memory of the late Second Prince, and her heart would ache.

The Emperor did feel guilty towards the Empress about the Second Prince. But he also worried that if the Empress raised the child, she might develop improper thoughts, which was why he had never agreed.

"Where is Physician Liu?" The Emperor didn’t want to engage, so he called for the imperial physician instead.

Physician Liu was summoned, and despite the winter chill, he was sweating profusely from anxiety.

"How is Consort Lian?"

"The midwives are still trying to turn the baby, but... it's not going smoothly..."

"How much longer until the birth?"

"It might take a while... Your Majesty, if it truly comes to a point where a choice must be made, what would you—"

The Emperor darkened his face. "Consort Lian and the child—*We* want both."

Physician Liu looked troubled and glanced at the Empress and Noble Consort for help.

The Empress, upon learning of Xiangjun's difficult labor, was even willing to sacrifice the mother to save the child. She was pleased inside. Her original plan was to first tempt Consort Lian into willingly giving her the child to raise. Then, when the time was right, she would separate the mother from the child.

But if Consort Lian died now, the Emperor would likely refuse to let her raise the child.

"Your Majesty, Consort Lian has been nothing but devoted to you. You should cherish her more," the Empress said.

Noble Consort Rong was surprised that the Empress would speak up for Xiangjun, but the words resonated with her. She added, "Your Majesty, we haven’t reached the point of having to choose between mother and child. Why not go back with Her Majesty to rest? I’ll stay here with Xiangjun during the birth."

The Emperor trusted Noble Consort Rong. During the palace coup, Xiangjun had sincerely helped the Noble Consort, and their bond was undeniable.

As the Emperor, he could never say the words "sacrifice the child to save the mother."

The imperial heir was a matter of national importance, the foundation of the state. If he were to abandon the heir for a favored concubine, not only would he be condemned, but Xiangjun would likely be impeached by the court officials as well.

But if Noble Consort Rong stayed here, and he wasn’t present, then he wouldn’t have to choose between his beloved concubine and the imperial heir.

Fine. He would give Xiangjun this chance.

He trusted that Noble Consort Rong would choose Xiangjun.

The Emperor gave Noble Consort Rong a meaningful look. They exchanged glances, understanding each other’s intentions.

"Then I’ll trouble you, Noble Consort, to watch over Consort Lian for *Us*."

"Your Majesty, rest assured."

"Empress, you will return with *Us* as well."

The Empress didn’t want to leave, but the Emperor was uneasy about her staying, so she had no choice but to follow him.

Once the Emperor left, Noble Consort Rong immediately took a seat in the main hall. She summoned the physicians and midwives, and sternly ordered, "Listen carefully. If anything happens to Consort Lian, *I* will take your lives. Nothing is more important than Consort Lian’s life. At all times, prioritize her safety. Understood?"

The crowd trembled as they acknowledged the order.

After warning them, Noble Consort Rong settled in at Chengxiang Hall.

By the time of the Ox Hour (1-3 AM), Gu Tingxue arrived with the Dowager Empress’s decree.

The Dowager Empress had bestowed a five-hundred-year-old ginseng to Xiangjun to sustain her life, and specifically sent Gu Tingxue to deliver it.

"Noble Consort, why not go back to rest? The Dowager Empress has ordered me to stay and attend to Consort Lian’s birth. Once there’s news, I’ll send someone to Ganlu Palace to inform you."

"No need. *I* will stay here." Noble Consort Rong refused firmly.

She didn’t trust Gu Tingxue to stay here alone.

Although the Dowager Empress was now devoted to Buddhism, in her youth, she had been decisive and ruthless. Noble Consort Rong had no doubt that the Dowager Empress would choose the imperial heir.

Gu Tingxue was anxious. He wanted Noble Consort Rong to leave so he could go in and see Xiangjun, but he hadn’t expected her to be so insistent.

Helpless, Gu Tingxue could only sit in the hall with a dark expression, waiting nervously for news.

After a brief silence from inside, Xiangjun began to scream in agony again.

Gu Tingxue and Noble Consort Rong both stood up in alarm.

Noble Consort Rong glanced at Gu Tingxue. Why was he so anxious? She had never seen him so panicked before.

Gu Tingxue realized his loss of composure and darkened his face as he called for Physician Liu. "How is the prince? Why is Consort Lian in so much pain? Has something happened to the heir?"

Ah, so he was concerned about the heir. Only then did Noble Consort Rong shift her gaze back to Physician Liu.

Physician Liu bowed his head. "The baby has turned. The Consort is trying to give birth."

"That’s good!" The Noble Consort’s face lit up, and she let out a slight sigh of relief.

Gu Tingxue’s heart settled a little, and he silently sat back down.

But just as his tension eased slightly, it surged again.

Because one basin after another of bloody water was being carried out from the room.

Gu Tingxue clenched his fists tightly. For the first time in his life, he felt true fear.

Although Xiangjun had faced many dangers before, he had never thought that this tenacious woman, as resilient as wild grass, could die.

She was so full of life, as if she would always bloom brilliantly.

But at this moment, seeing so much blood, Gu Tingxue truly realized—Xiangjun could die.

Xiangjun could die.

The thought terrified him.

Gu Tingxue wanted to rush in recklessly, but with Noble Consort Rong here, he could only sit expressionlessly in his chair, gripping his hands even tighter.

"Something’s wrong!"

Meng Mei rushed out and knelt before Noble Consort Rong with a thud.

"Noble Consort, our Consort is in trouble! She’s lost so much blood. If she doesn’t give birth soon... Noble Consort, please, ask His Majesty to come and see our Consort!"

Both the Noble Consort and Gu Tingxue stood abruptly.

This time, even the Noble Consort was so shocked that she didn’t notice Gu Tingxue’s reaction.

The Noble Consort’s maid, Cai Wei, whispered, "It’s the Ox Hour. His Majesty is likely asleep by now. If we send someone to request His Majesty, the eunuchs at Weiyang Palace might not relay the message."

"I will go myself to request His Majesty!" Noble Consort Rong declared, taking her people with her as she left.
