As soon as she was gone, Gu Tingxue immediately tried to enter the birthing room, only to be stopped by Meng Mei.

"Eunuch Tingxue, our Consort said you’re not allowed to watch her give birth."

Gu Tingxue suddenly remembered the day Xiangjun had joked with him, saying that when she gave birth, she absolutely wouldn’t let him watch, afraid it would traumatize him.

Gu Tingxue felt as if his heart was being clenched tightly in someone’s grip, a dull ache spreading through him.

"How is she?"

"Our Consort said that if Eunuch Tingxue can’t bear to let her die, then she definitely won’t die. She told Eunuch Tingxue not to worry, that she will surely give birth to the prince for our future."

With that, Meng Mei returned to the inner chamber.

Gu Tingxue sat back down in a daze, not even realizing that his palm was bleeding.

The last time, in the Palace Administration Office, when he saw Xiangjun being tortured, he realized he didn’t want her to die.

This time, outside the birthing room, Gu Tingxue realized she could die. He might lose her.

At that moment, Gu Tingxue, who had never believed in gods or Buddha, couldn’t help but pray in his heart. He begged the heavens to protect Xiangjun. He was willing to descend into the eighteenth level of hell, as long as Xiangjun lived.

He made up his mind—no more struggle. If she wanted his heart, he would give it to her. Just don’t let her die.

As if the heavens had heard Gu Tingxue’s prayer, a loud cry rang out—the child was born!

From inside, they heard, "The Consort has given birth! It’s a prince!"

---

chapters.title: This Man Might Have Truly Fallen for Her
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue stood up again, pacing anxiously. Soon, Meng Mei came out carrying a child. Before Gu Tingxue could react, she placed the baby in his arms.

Gu Tingxue stiffened, holding the small, soft infant, frozen in place.

Looking at the tiny baby in his arms, Gu Tingxue was momentarily at a loss.

"This... this is the Fifth Prince?" he asked.

Meng Mei nodded with a delighted smile, lowering her voice. "Our Consort said to let Eunuch Tingxue see him first."

Gu Tingxue was speechless. He looked down at the child, his expression a mix of shock and the bewilderment of a new father.

If Meng Mei didn’t know Gu Tingxue was a eunuch, she would have suspected the child was the Consort’s with Eunuch Tingxue.

She hadn’t expected Eunuch Tingxue to look so lost and foolish. She would definitely have to tell the Consort about this later.

Following Gu Tingxue’s gaze to the Fifth Prince, Meng Mei smiled at Gu Tingxue, only to be shocked when she noticed his eyes were red.

This time, Meng Mei was truly stunned.

Was Eunuch Tingxue about to cry?

"How is your mistress? How is she?" Gu Tingxue asked, his voice hoarse.

Seeing his state, Meng Mei didn’t dare joke anymore. She quickly said, "Eunuch Tingxue, rest assured. Our Consort is fine."

"But earlier you said she wasn’t well!"

"That was what our Consort told me to say to Noble Consort Rong. Our Consort said that apart from those in the birthing room, she wanted Eunuch Tingxue to be the first to see the child, the first to hold him. So she had Noble Consort Rong sent away first."

Gu Tingxue didn’t know how to react for a moment.

Only Xiangjun would do something like this.

He knitted his brows and asked again, "So your mistress is truly unharmed?"

"Yes, our Consort is in perfect health. She’s just a little tired from the birth."

Gu Tingxue couldn’t say whether he was more angry or relieved. In the end, all the complex emotions in his heart turned into a sigh.

Xiangjun was tormenting him.

Meng Mei saw Physician Liu, the midwives, and the medical attendants all exit the birthing room. She quickly took the Fifth Prince from Gu Tingxue’s arms.

Lowering her voice, she said, "I’ll take the child to the wet nurse first. The Consort should be almost ready. While His Majesty hasn’t arrived yet, Eunuch Tingxue, why don’t you go in and see her?"

Once everyone had dispersed, Gu Tingxue finally entered the birthing room.

Inside, only Physician Liu and Xi Yu were attending. When they saw Gu Tingxue enter, they tacitly withdrew.

Xiangjun lay on the bed with her eyes closed, her face exhausted, her complexion as pale as paper.

Although she had a strong constitution, having just given birth, her energy and blood were certainly depleted.

Hearing the rustling sounds by her ear, Xiangjun finally opened her eyes.

She saw Gu Tingxue kneeling on the footstool beside the bed, his eyes red as he gently held her hand.

Feeling the moisture in her palm, Xiangjun turned over Gu Tingxue’s hand and saw that his palm was bleeding—clearly from clenching his fists too tightly, his nails piercing his skin.

"Are you stupid?" Xiangjun looked up at Gu Tingxue. Seeing him staring at her with red-rimmed eyes, she said helplessly, "Didn’t Meng Mei tell you? I’m perfectly fine. The part about me being in danger was all an act."

"Meng Mei told me," Gu Tingxue said, his voice hoarse.

"The malpositioned fetus and difficult labor were also lies. All those basins of blood were prepared in advance. Didn’t I tell you about this before the birth?"

Xiangjun had deliberately faked the difficult labor to put on a show for the Emperor—how she loved him so much she would risk her life.

She knew that to pry open even a small crack in the heart of this heartless emperor was not easy, so she had to seize every opportunity to perform for him.

She had told Gu Tingxue about this plan when her water broke.

"I know," Gu Tingxue said.

"Then why..." Xiangjun wanted to ask why he looked so heartbroken, as if she were truly dying.

But she stopped mid-sentence.

Because she actually saw a tear fall from Gu Tingxue’s eye.

Xiangjun reached out and touched Gu Tingxue’s face. The warm sensation confirmed it—those were real tears. She hadn’t been mistaken.

Gu Tingxue once again took Xiangjun’s hand and pressed it to his lips, kissing it lightly.

Looking at Gu Tingxue’s red-rimmed eyes, Xiangjun suddenly realized something.

This realization filled her with joy.

She had succeeded.

After all this planning, this man might have truly and completely fallen in love with her.

Xiangjun stared at Gu Tingxue, a smile spreading across her face.

"What are you smiling about?" Gu Tingxue asked.

"I’m happy. Tingxue cried for me. You must care about me deeply. Tingxue, can you tell me now? Do you have feelings for me?"

Gu Tingxue’s gaze darkened.

"Forget it if you won’t say." Xiangjun’s face took on that smug look again. "I know even if you don’t say it."

"Yes," Gu Tingxue said.

Xiangjun froze. She hadn’t expected Gu Tingxue to admit it so bluntly.

Xiangjun had once told Gu Tingxue that she wanted to capture the Emperor’s heart.

But what she hadn’t told him was that the heart she truly wanted to capture wasn’t the Emperor’s—it was her lover’s.

What Xiangjun was planning was treasonous. She needed an ally who would be completely devoted to her.

Now, she had finally succeeded.

Gu Tingxue kissed Xiangjun’s hand as if it were a priceless treasure, then carefully tucked the blanket around her.

When Gu Tingxue looked up again, his eyes had returned to their usual coldness, though the redness at the corners still betrayed his earlier panic.

"Your Majesty, I am not a good man. I have feelings for you, but I am not one who loves without complaint or regret. Taking my heart comes with a price."

The charcoal brazier in the room was burning strongly, yet Xiangjun inexplicably shivered.

"What does Tingxue want?" Xiangjun asked.

Gu Tingxue glanced at her red lips and smiled.

His expression suddenly became aggressive, reminding Xiangjun of a venomous snake.

Gu Tingxue lowered his head and gently kissed Xiangjun’s forehead.

"Your Majesty need not worry. What I want, I will take for myself."

Gu Tingxue stood up and straightened his robes.

"His Majesty should be arriving soon. I need to leave first. Your Majesty, rest well."

Gu Tingxue left. Xiangjun couldn’t quite put her finger on what felt off, but she had a nagging feeling that perhaps she had celebrated too soon.

This Gu Tingxue—even in love, he was so sinister and frightening.

chapters.title: Fifth Prince Yuan Lang
chapters.content:
Not long after Tingxue left, the Emperor was summoned by the Noble Consort.

As soon as the Emperor and Noble Consort Rong arrived, they learned that the child had been born and that Concubine Lian was unharmed. Both were overjoyed.

The wet nurse showed the child to the Emperor briefly. His Majesty was delighted and rewarded all the palace attendants in Chengxiang Hall.

"Your Majesty, Concubine Lian is truly blessed. She can turn danger into safety, and the Fifth Prince is so adorable. Your Majesty, you must reward her handsomely this time!"

"And it's all thanks to you for staying here all this time."

The Emperor and the Noble Consort exchanged a smile, and because of Xiangjun, they seemed to be on the verge of reconciling.

Holding hands, they entered the room to see Xiangjun. She looked too weak to even speak, but whispered faintly, "It makes Xiangjun so happy to see Your Majesty and Noble Consort Sister reconciled."

The Emperor and Noble Consort exchanged another glance. When it came to genuine loyalty, no one in the palace surpassed Xiangjun.

"You... just gave birth, and you still have the energy to worry about others," the Noble Consort said, wiping the corners of her eyes. "Xiangjun, you've given birth to a prince. Sister is truly happy for you."

Xiangjun tried to say more, but the Noble Consort pressed her hand down.

"Save your strength. Don’t speak. Rest well."

The Emperor also took Xiangjun’s hand, his face full of joy. "Just now, the Noble Consort and I discussed giving you the title of Consort! Once your confinement is over, I will personally hold the investiture ceremony for you."

"The investiture ceremony must be held on an auspicious day," the Noble Consort added.

"That goes without saying."

The Noble Consort then asked, "Has Your Majesty decided on a name for the Fifth Prince?"

"I’ll think about it now!"

Xiangjun watched as the imperial couple casually decided her affairs. She quickly spoke up, "Your Majesty, the Fifth Prince’s name must be chosen carefully. You cannot pick just any name."

The Emperor looked somewhat embarrassed and said helplessly, "Then I’ll have the Ministry of Rites come up with several good names for you to choose from. Will that do?"

Xiangjun nodded in satisfaction.

The Noble Consort let out a soft laugh. "It would be most honorable for Your Majesty to name him yourself. You’re being too picky, Xiangjun. Your Majesty, our sister Xiangjun has been spoiled by you."

The Emperor also laughed. Normally, he would have been displeased, but given how difficult Xiangjun’s labor had been, he couldn’t bear to be angry with her now.

"Yes, I’ve spoiled her. What, Noble Consort, are you jealous?"

"How could I be? I treat Xiangjun like my own sister. If Your Majesty dotes on her, I’d be happy for her."

Although Xiangjun felt no physical discomfort, she was still exhausted from childbirth. She was too tired to watch the Emperor and Noble Consort Rong display their affection in front of her.

Fortunately, Mengmei understood her. She entered at the right moment and described to the Emperor and Noble Consort the dangers and difficulties of Xiangjun’s labor. Finally, the Emperor allowed her to rest first, then left with Noble Consort Rong for Ganlu Palace.

After they left, Mengmei said, "Simple Noble Lady Jian has been waiting all along. When she heard that Your Ladyship had a safe delivery, she was so overjoyed that she cried. She wants to come see you."

"I’m too tired. Tell her to come tomorrow. Don’t let her take it to heart. It’s precisely because I’m close to her that I don’t want to see her now. I truly need to rest."

"Yes, this servant will explain it to Simple Noble Lady Jian."

After everyone had left, Xiangjun finally closed her eyes, exhausted, and fell into a deep sleep.

She slept very deeply.

In her dream, she relived the scene of giving birth to her second son in her past life.

It was also a winter night. Due to poor prenatal care and harassment from Consort Qin, the second prince was born tiny, like a kitten, almost too frail to survive.

That year, Xiangjun had cared for him day and night until the child grew plump.

But because her rank was too low, once the child was better, he was sent to Nanxun Palace to be raised by Consort Qin.

Consort Qin already disliked her, so she certainly wouldn’t care for her child. Though the child wasn’t starved or frozen, he was neglected. The second prince, already weak, became even thinner and smaller under Consort Qin’s care. At two years old, he still couldn’t speak.

Xiangjun couldn’t bear for her child to be mistreated. She nearly lost her life but finally managed to bring down Consort Qin and take her child back.

When the second prince was returned to her, he was always timid and plagued by nightmares.

Even someone as jealous of favor as Xiangjun ignored the Emperor, staying by her child’s side every night. Though she had little money, she found ways to get tonics to strengthen the child.

He stayed with Xiangjun until he was four.

But by then, Consort Qin had regained favor, and the Emperor ordered her to send the child back to Consort Qin.

Xiangjun remembered the day the people from Nanxun Palace came to take the child away. He cried so bitterly, screaming, "Mother, Mother, I don’t want to go to Nanxun Palace. Mother, don’t abandon me..."

Xiangjun had also cried until her voice was hoarse, promising the child that she would bring him back.

But in the end, she was cut open to deliver her next child and still couldn’t bring him back to her side.

Xiangjun woke up crying. When she awoke, the sky outside was already bright.

She immediately had the wet nurse bring the child to her.

Looking at the Fifth Prince in her arms, Xiangjun couldn’t help but let tears fall again.

The Fifth Prince looked exactly like the child in her memories.

Heaven had taken pity, and this child had returned to Xiangjun’s side.

"Why are you crying?"

A voice sounded beside her. Xiangjun looked up and saw Gu Tingxue entering the room.

Gu Tingxue had come to deliver rewards from the Empress Dowager. He sat by the bed and reached out to wipe Xiangjun’s tears.

For some reason, seeing Gu Tingxue made Xiangjun feel even more wronged. With a sob, she burst into tears, leaning on Gu Tingxue’s shoulder and crying uncontrollably.

Perhaps due to the connection between mother and child, the baby also started crying. For a moment, Gu Tingxue didn’t know who to comfort first.

Fortunately, Xiangjun stopped crying first.

Gu Tingxue quickly took the child, cradling him and asking Xiangjun, "What’s wrong? Did a servant not do their job properly? Or did a noble lady from another palace bully you? Tell me, and I’ll avenge you."

Xiangjun shook her head. How could she explain the grievances from her past life?

Gu Tingxue soothed the child for a while until he stopped crying. Seeing that the child had fallen asleep again, he carefully placed him back in the cradle, then wrung out a damp cloth to wipe Xiangjun’s face.

"What’s wrong? Tell me."

"It’s nothing... I’m just afraid... afraid that the Fifth Prince won’t have a good name." Xiangjun came up with a poor excuse, then asked, "Has the Ministry of Rites chosen the name? Have they picked any good characters?"

Gu Tingxue laughed helplessly. He had heard that women’s emotions could be volatile after childbirth, but he hadn’t expected such a small matter to upset Xiangjun so much.

"Are you worried about this?"

"Can I not be worried? A name is the most important thing."

Sometimes, a name could determine whether a child would have the chance to inherit the throne.

"You can rest assured. The Ministry of Rites is under my control. They will definitely find a good name for the Fifth Prince."

"I don’t want the Ministry of Rites to name him. Can you come up with a name for our prince?" Xiangjun tugged at Gu Tingxue’s sleeve.

Gu Tingxue was somewhat taken aback, but his gaze softened as he looked at the child in the cradle.

"Would that be alright?"

Gu Tingxue thought for a moment and asked, "How about Yuan Lang? What do you think of this name?"

"Which character? What does it mean?"

"Lang means bright and clear, as in a bright and peaceful world."

---

chapters.title: The Empress Cannot Be Kept
chapters.content:
Xiangjun thought about the meaning of the name and immediately turned her sorrow into joy. She smiled, nodded, and said happily, "I think this name is perfect!"

Yuan Lang—bright and clear world, peace under heaven. It sounded like the name of a future emperor.

In her past life, her second son was named Yuan Zuo because the Emperor hoped he would assist his elder brother, the son of Noble Consort Rong, whom Xiangjun had raised.

Xiangjun had always disliked that name, which was why she didn’t let the Emperor name the child this time.

After thinking for a moment, Xiangjun asked worriedly, "Will His Majesty not choose this name?"

"Don’t worry. The Ministry of Rites will find a way to make sure His Majesty picks this name."

Hearing Gu Tingxue say this, Xiangjun was reassured.

Gu Tingxue always kept his promises to her.

Sure enough, the next day, the Emperor came to see Xiangjun in high spirits, saying he had thought of a good name for her child: Yuan Lang.

"Now that the world is at peace, our Great Qi is strong and prosperous, and the people live in peace. This 'Lang' means a bright and clear world. Our Fifth Prince, born at this time, is truly blessed."

Xiangjun smiled at the Emperor and said, "Indeed, the name Your Majesty chose is the best. This concubine likes it very much."

The Emperor played with Yuan Lang for a while before handing him to the wet nurse.

The palace attendants, seeing the Emperor’s expression, tactfully withdrew.

"Your Majesty, is there something you wish to discuss with me?"

The Emperor looked somewhat troubled.

"Your Majesty, is there anything you cannot tell me?"

The Emperor sighed and said, "The Empress wants to raise Yuan Lang in Weiyang Palace. She doesn’t need to register him under her name; Yuan Lang will still be your son. It’s just that he would be raised in Weiyang Palace. The Empress says she day and night misses the Second Prince and truly wants a child by her side, so..."

As expected, it was about this.

Xiangjun had known this day would come.

The Emperor didn’t actually want to give a child to the Empress, but with Prime Minister Song and the Jiangnan faction destroyed, and Minister Yang having died for the country, the court had dug up the matter of the Second Prince’s death and made a fuss for a long time.

The Emperor did need to appease the Empress and the clean-stream literati behind her.

Xiangjun naturally knew that the Emperor wasn’t here to ask for her opinion, but to make her feel guilty, she still put on an expression of disbelief.

"Why... There are other princes in the harem. Why must Her Majesty the Empress take my child?"

The Emperor had considered this. Actually, he could give the Third Prince, Yuan Ji, to the Empress.

But Simple Noble Lady Jian’s status was too low, with no distinguished family background. She would never be able to control the Empress, and there was a risk that the Empress might even harm the child.

Xiangjun, on the other hand, held a high rank and was capable. Moreover, she had a brother with limitless potential. If her child were given to the Empress, he wouldn’t have to worry about the Empress completely taking the child away.

"Then, do you want to give Yuan Ji to the Empress?"

"No!" Xiangjun immediately said, "Although Yuan Ji is not my biological son, he is still my child. And... how could this concubine bear to make Sister Qinglian sad?"

Xiangjun wiped her tears and could only cry and sob through the performance. But in the end, she still "reluctantly compromised" to put the Emperor at ease and agreed to send the child to the Empress.

The Emperor felt guilty toward Xiangjun, so he said that after Xiangjun finished her confinement, Weiyang Palace could come to take the child. He also bestowed many gifts upon Xiangjun and promised her that he would allow her brother to enter the palace to see him again.

"Don’t worry," the Emperor said, holding Xiangjun’s hand and solemnly promising, "You consider me so much, and I will not treat you poorly. If your brother passes the imperial examination, I will certainly promote him. Even if he doesn’t pass, I will still arrange for him to enter the court."

Xiangjun leaned against the Emperor’s shoulder and said sorrowfully, "Thank you for your kindness, Your Majesty. As long as Your Majesty has Xiangjun in your heart, Xiangjun is willing to do anything for you."

...

That evening, when Gu Tingxue arrived, Xiangjun was holding Yuan Lang and soothing him.

The soft candlelight bathed Xiangjun, making her usually unparalleled beauty appear gentler and more maternal.

It was a warm scene, but when Xiangjun looked up at Gu Tingxue, there was a clear murderous intent in her eyes.

"Tingxue, Yuan Lang must stay with me. So the Empress cannot keep him. Will you help me?"

Gu Tingxue slightly lifted the corner of his mouth and smiled.

He really liked the way Xiangjun looked when she was plotting harm—like a rose stained with blood.

"Does Your Ladyship already have a plan?"

"I have a way, but without you, Tingxue, it cannot be accomplished."

Gu Tingxue walked to Xiangjun’s side and reached out to touch Yuan Lang’s tiny hand.

Yuan Lang’s little hand immediately gripped his finger tightly.

Looking at Yuan Lang’s round, bright eyes, Gu Tingxue’s expression was gentle, but his words were filled with killing intent.

"For our Yuan Lang, there is nothing I cannot do. In this world, anyone who stands in Yuan Lang’s way should die."

...

The New Year was approaching. The Emperor looked at the tax revenues collected this year, the tribute from the southern countries, and the well-stocked treasury. He was in high spirits, feeling as if he were the greatest emperor of all time.

"Last year’s victory in the southern war, and my handling of Prime Minister Song and the Jiangnan faction behind him, can be considered both literary and martial achievements," the Emperor said with satisfaction.

Gu Tingxue, of course, flattered the Emperor, describing the Great Qi under his rule as a paradise on earth.

Thus, under the flattery of the eunuchs, the Emperor actually conceived the idea of holding a ceremony at Mount Tai to offer sacrifices to heaven and earth.

The next day, during the court session, the Emperor brought up this matter to the officials, but to his surprise, he was met with opposition from the ministers.

The civil officials in the court were arguing loudly, completely unaware of how dark the Emperor’s face had become.

Our Emperor Yanqing was extremely concerned with his dignity.

He was already annoyed by the interference of these officials in his affairs. Whatever he did, there was always a group of people who would complain. Now, even for something as minor as his desire to hold a ceremony at Mount Tai, they still disapproved.

And no matter how they phrased it, the reasons they gave all boiled down to one thing: he was not worthy!

The Emperor was furious. He wanted to deal with these officials, but he couldn’t find a reason to do so immediately. For the sake of his reputation as a great emperor for the ages, he couldn’t force the issue of the ceremony. He had to suppress his anger and drop the matter.

Though he didn’t bring it up again, the Emperor’s mood remained foul. Every eunuch serving in the Taiji Hall was trembling with fear.

Thus, after the Emperor smashed another cup, Gu Tingxue dismissed everyone and presented the Emperor with a brilliant strategy: replace the Empress.

chapters.title: Seizing the Child
chapters.content:
Emperor had observed the Queen's reaction to the palace coup in the Xia Garden. She and Prime Minister Yang did not care about his life or death; all they thought about was how to control the prince and manipulate the court.

"Your Majesty can use the opportunity of deposing the Queen to suppress those puritan officials. These officials are truly ridiculous. In the ten years since Your Majesty ascended the throne, the northern borders have been peaceful, and the southern states have all submitted. Such achievements, and yet they only wish to perform the Fengchan ceremony. They, however, have nothing but sour remarks. This humble servant believes that these officials are all useless, and it is they who should be restrained."

The Emperor felt that Gu Tingxue's words had struck a chord with him.

The Emperor pondered for a moment and said, "How can We not want to deal with them? But to deal with Song Feijing and to pacify the court, We have already declared that Yang Jingshan died for the country. Now, if We deal with his relatives and disciples, We fear that We cannot silence the scholars of the world."

The power of the civil officials lay in their control over the scholars' voices. The Emperor was not afraid of them, but he feared that they would ruin his reputation as a wise ruler.

"Your Majesty, to depose the Queen, it does not necessarily have to be for the sake of the front court. It can also be for the sake of the harem. The Queen has no children, and the imperial physician has said that she will never have children in the future. However, Noble Consort Gui has a son. If Your Majesty does not bring it up, many in the front court will advise Your Majesty to depose the Queen and establish Noble Consort Gui as the new Queen for the sake of the nation's foundation."

The Emperor understood Gu Tingxue's meaning.

He could use the opportunity of changing the Queen to have the forces behind Noble Consort Gui suppress the forces behind the Queen for him.

Just like how he had used Song Feijing to balance Yang Jingshan.

"Noble Consort Gui's grandfather was a three-dynasty veteran and the Taizi Taishi. Although he has passed away, there are still many in the court who remember the old Taishi's kindness. As long as Your Majesty wishes, there will definitely be many people willing to help with this matter."

The Emperor glanced at Gu Tingxue with a faint look, then averted his gaze, his expression somewhat embarrassed.

This servant understood his taboos well.

In reality, it was not about remembering the old Taishi's kindness. Clearly, there were many officials in the court who were under Noble Consort Gui's influence. Now that General Wang had returned, he represented the power of the nobility and the military. They would definitely support Noble Consort Gui.

The nobility and military forces were most at odds with the civil officials. If he let them fight like dogs, the Emperor could take the opportunity to reclaim some power.

"This is indeed a way. However, Yuanze's face..."

"General Wang said he brought a shamanic physician from the north, and has already sent someone to present him to Noble Consort Gui. Perhaps the Fourth Prince's face can still be cured."

The Emperor's expression darkened for a moment, but soon returned to normal.

"If that's the case, then do as you say."

...

After the Emperor had the idea of deposing the Queen, he began to frequently visit Ganlu Palace.

For a time, Noble Consort Gui once again enjoyed the Emperor's exclusive favor.

The Queen did not show any jealousy. Instead, she often sent people to Chengxiang Palace to visit Xiangjun and Yuanlang, as if she couldn't wait a month to see them.

One day, the Queen came to visit Xiangjun again. Xiangjun was holding Yuanlang, and when the Queen wanted to hold Yuanlang, she was refused.

"I had a difficult labor when I gave birth to Yuanlang, and his health is not good. The imperial physician said not to let anyone touch him casually, for fear that the child would easily fall ill."

Xiangjun's tone was distant.

The Queen's expression was somewhat embarrassed, but she still managed to maintain a smile. She comforted Xiangjun for a few words before leaving displeased.

As soon as she left Chengxiang Palace and got into the sedan chair, Fragrant Auntie said, "This Concubine Lian seems unlikely to easily hand over the child to Your Majesty. She wouldn't have changed her mind, would she?"

"Mother and child are connected by heart. Before she gave birth, it was easy for her to agree. Now that she has gone through life and death to give birth to the child, it is understandable that she is reluctant to part with him."

"Your Majesty has softened your heart?"

"As a mother myself, I can naturally empathize. But I am the Queen. Now that my father has passed away, I must strive for my maternal family. So even though I know Concubine Lian is pitiful, I still must have this child."

"Your Majesty, rest assured. Since the Emperor has already agreed, the child will definitely be raised by you."

"I hope so."

The sedan chair headed towards Weiyang Palace.

Knowing that Xiangjun did not want to see her, the Queen did not visit Chengxiang Palace again. However, rumors began to spread in the palace that the Queen wanted Concubine Lian's child.

Some even said that the Queen was domineering, and even at the rank of Concubine, her child could be taken away just like that.

The Queen was very angry and ordered a thorough investigation. However, they could not find the person who started the rumor. They only caught a few unlucky ones, gave them a beating, and the rumors finally subsided, with no one daring to discuss it again.

Thus, Xiangjun's confinement period ended smoothly.

To the Queen's surprise, on the day she went to take the child, Xiangjun did not obstruct or use any tricks. She just cried, packed Yuanlang's things, gave a few instructions to the wet nurse, and let the child be taken away.

Xiangjun had a cold face, as if her heart was dead.

"Xiangjun only hopes that Your Majesty will treat Yuanlang well." Xiangjun said through tears.

The Queen felt uncomfortable. If Xiangjun cried like this, wouldn't others think that she had forcibly taken her child?

The Queen put on a loving appearance and looked at Xiangjun, saying, "Look at what you're saying, sister. I just thought that you were weakened from childbirth, so I'm helping you raise the child. As the mistress of the harem, I will definitely protect the concubines and children of the harem. You can rest assured. In the future, whenever you have time, you can come and see Yuanlang. I also hope that you will come."

But Xiangjun only smiled bitterly.

"Your Majesty, there is no need to test me. Since you have taken the child away, he is your child now."

"You..." Fragrant Auntie wanted to say something, but was stopped by the Queen.

"Your Majesty, I have not yet recovered and wish to rest."

"Very well," the Queen said with a dark face, "Concubine Lian, you rest well."

After returning to Weiyang Palace, the Queen still had a dark face, and Fragrant Auntie cursed Xiangjun for being ungrateful.

"Enough, she is angry, so let her say a few words. But you must watch the mouths in the harem and not let people talk nonsense."

Xiangjun continued to recuperate, while the Queen happily raised Yuanlang.

The lonely Weiyang Palace also became lively because of Yuanlang. The Emperor also visited the Queen more often because he wanted to see Yuanlang.

As for Concubine Lian, she had never visited Weiyang Palace, not even once. Even when she paid respects to the Queen during the palace gathering, she only greeted her and left, never once mentioning seeing Yuanlang.

Even the Queen thought that Concubine Lian was heartless, able to give up her child so thoroughly.

The Queen set her mind at ease, feeling that her plan had succeeded and that Xiangjun was quite sensible.

But one month later, on the day of Xiangjun's official investiture as a concubine, before she could be formally invested, she vomited blood and fainted in front of the palace concubines and the several officials who were the investiture envoys.

The imperial physician diagnosed that Concubine Lian had been poisoned.

The Emperor was furious.

"With so many concubines in the palace and three of my officials present, someone dared to harm my concubine during the investiture ceremony! This is truly audacious and lawless! Investigate! Find out who did this!"

The Emperor ordered a thorough investigation, and the entire palace was in an uproar.

chapters.title: Sacrificing the Pawn to Save the General
chapters.content:
Weiyang Palace.

The Queen looked at the kneeling Fang Auntie on the ground, her face seemingly showing a trace of reluctance.

Fang Auntie knelt on the ground, her face full of panic.

The Queen sighed and looked at Fang Auntie with a reproachful tone.

"I warned you to use the medicine slowly. Concubine Lian had a difficult labor, and her body was already weakened. In a few years, her body would gradually weaken, and she would slowly die from exhaustion of qi and blood. That would be normal, and no one would suspect or investigate carefully. How could you use such a heavy dose? Now that the Emperor has ordered a thorough investigation, how can I protect you?"

"Your Majesty, it's a misunderstanding. This slave did use the medicine as per your instructions. I really don't know why Concubine Lian would be poisoned and faint."

"How else could it be?" The Queen's eyes flashed with a hint of ruthlessness. "I have underestimated Concubine Lian. Perhaps she discovered that you were poisoning her and turned the tables on you."

Fang Auntie asked incredulously, "Your Majesty, do you mean that Concubine Lian poisoned herself?"

"I do not believe in such a coincidence. She just happened to have a poison attack during the investiture ceremony. Apart from herself, I cannot think of anyone else who would do this. Perhaps, because I took Yuanlang from her, she still resents me and came up with this poisonous plan to put me in a deadly situation!"

"Your Majesty, if that's the case, why don't you report the truth to the Emperor?"

The Queen's cold gaze swept over Fang Auntie, with a trace of impatience in her eyes.

"You did poison her, and there is evidence. Once it is found out that you poisoned Concubine Lian, regardless of whether the poison that caused her attack was administered by you or not, it will be considered your doing. So, even if I go to the Emperor, the final result will still implicate you."

"Your Majesty, since this slave is wronged, please, save this slave!"

The Queen's expression was stern. "How do you expect me to save you? If it were just a matter within the harem, it would be fine. But Concubine Lian's incident happened during the investiture ceremony, with so many court ladies and officials present. Given the Emperor's face-conscious nature, he will definitely not let this matter rest and will certainly want to give an explanation to the court ladies and officials. Now that the Emperor is furious, and with that eunuch Gu Tingxue investigating, with his abilities, it is only a matter of time before he traces it back to us. Currently, I have no other way but to hand you over to the Emperor to calm this matter..."

"Your Majesty! Your Majesty, spare my life! Please, Your Majesty, this slave is truly wronged!"

Fang Auntie kowtowed desperately, crying her eyes out.

But the Queen's gaze remained cold.

"Fang, you and I grew up together since we were young. You should know the difficulties my Yang family is currently facing. If the Emperor finds out that we did this, he will use this opportunity to suppress my Yang family. My father is already gone, and I am currently walking on thin ice in this harem. If it were not for dire circumstances, how could I bear to hand you over?"

"But Your Majesty... what this slave did is no different from what Your Majesty did. Your Majesty, please, spare this slave!"

The Queen's gaze darkened and grew colder.

"Fang, when the nest is overturned, no egg remains intact. If I am found guilty, you will die too. If the Yang family is in trouble, your family will also be implicated. Think carefully about what you should do."

Fang Auntie closed her eyes, tears of despair falling.

She knelt on the ground and kowtowed to the Queen. "This slave understands. Your Majesty, rest assured. Before the Emperor, this slave will take full responsibility for this matter. I only hope that Your Majesty will treat my family well."

...

That very night, the Queen sent Fang Auntie to the Emperor.

The Queen wore plain clothes and took off her hairpin to plead guilty, tearfully saying that she had failed to govern her subordinates properly, leading to this incident. She truly did not know that Fang Auntie would do such a thing.

The Emperor was indeed caught off guard by the Queen's move of sacrificing the pawn to save the general.

He had originally intended to use this opportunity to shift the blame onto the Queen and use it as an excuse to depose her, thereby suppressing the Yang family and the puritan officials in the court.

Unexpectedly, the Queen reacted quickly and pushed Fang Auntie out to take the blame.

Since the Queen had not been involved in the matter, and Fang Auntie, even under torture, did not implicate the Queen, saying that she had acted alone, the Emperor was frustrated. However, he could not just let the Queen off like this, so he ordered the Queen to be confined to her palace for her failure to govern her subordinates properly.

The Fifth Prince, Yuanlang, who was being raised in Weiyang Palace, was first taken to the Renshou Palace to be cared for by the Empress Dowager.

The Queen knew that being confined was the best result she could achieve. She only hated herself for being outmaneuvered and underestimating Xu Xiangjun, falling into the trap she had set.

In Weiyang Palace, Spring Auntie combed the Queen's hair and saw the white hair on the Queen's head, her hand freezing for a moment.

The Queen smiled, reached out, and plucked her white hair.

"Your Majesty... will we be alright this time?"

The Queen gave a bitter smile. "If my father and my second son were still alive, how would the Emperor treat me like this? Even if I can survive this calamity, I fear that sooner or later, I will still be held accountable by the Emperor. Let's take it one day at a time."

...

Xiangjun was deeply poisoned, and the detoxification process was slow, so she spent most of her time unconscious and was not involved in the affairs of the front court and the harem.

Although the Emperor had not been able to pin the blame for harming Xiangjun on the Queen, he still used this incident to propose in the front court to depose the Queen and establish Noble Consort Rong Gui, Xue Jiaojiao, as the new Queen.

The front court was in an uproar. The puritan officials and the nobility and military forces represented by General Wang began to fight in the court over this matter.

The civil officials believed that there was no evidence that the Queen was involved in the attempt to harm Concubine Lian. The Queen had already taken the initiative to catch the mastermind, so she should not be blamed for this kind of incident. The Queen had once given birth to an imperial heir and had been in the position of Empress for more than a decade, setting an example for all the women in the world. She had never made a major mistake, and deposing her would bring instability to the nation.

The nobles believed that there was no difference between what the Queen's close maid did and what the Queen herself did. They absolutely could not allow a woman who harmed concubines to continue being the Queen. Xue Jiaojiao, whether in terms of background or offspring, deserved the position of Queen.

The two sides argued daily in the court, but the arguments did not lead to any clarity. It only made the Emperor tired.

However, there were still things that pleased the Emperor.

Because the puritan officials and the noble group not only attacked each other in the court but also dug up each other's faults in private, many officials were implicated and imprisoned due to this storm of changing the Queen. The Emperor took the opportunity to place many of his own people in the front court.

Just as the two sides were fighting fiercely, a palace maid from Weiyang Palace exposed that the Queen practiced witchcraft in the harem.

Gu Tingxue led people to turn Weiyang Palace upside down and indeed found cursed objects.

The Emperor was furious and ordered a thorough investigation, determined to catch all those involved.

chapters.title: The Deposed Empress
chapters.content:
Due to the witchcraft incident, almost all the palace attendants in Weiyang Palace were killed.

The imperial palace was filled with panic every day, with bodies being carried out almost daily, scaring the concubines so much that they didn’t dare to step outside.

The gates of Weiyang Palace were sealed, leaving only Chun Gu to continue serving the Empress.

Many in the imperial court and harem were also implicated—some had their families confiscated, others were beheaded.

The Yang family was purged, and a century-old aristocratic clan vanished completely because of a single witchcraft doll.

In just one year, the Emperor had dealt heavy blows to his two biggest headaches: Prime Minister Song and the Jiangnan Faction behind him, as well as Chancellor Yang and the Pure Stream Faction behind him.

The Emperor took this opportunity to reclaim most of the power into his own hands.

Superficial observers believed the Emperor had turned against the Empress out of disappointment over the poisoning of Concubine Li and the witchcraft incident.

Those with deeper insight thought the Emperor was suppressing the Yang family to favor his beloved Noble Consort Rong.

Only those who truly understood the Emperor knew how long he had planned for this day.

Years ago, the Emperor had ascended the throne with the support of the Jiangnan Faction, led by his mother, and his father-in-law, Yang Jingshan.

Because of their "merit in aiding his rise," over the years, the Jiangnan Faction and the Pure Stream officials had formed a powerful force in the court, often restraining the Emperor’s actions.

Thus, from the day he ascended the throne, the Emperor had longed for the day he could fully consolidate his power.

This storm of replacing the Empress finally settled after countless heads had rolled.

It was only when everything was over that Xiangjun slowly "recovered" from her illness.

The poison in Xiangjun’s body was never life-threatening. The reason it took so long to heal was that the Emperor had forbidden the imperial physicians from curing her.

Perhaps feeling guilty for using her, the Emperor had Gu Tingxue deliver many rewards to her.

Xiangjun idly flipped through the treasures, feeling a little disinterested.

"Has His Majesty said when he will return Yuanlang?"

"His Majesty feels deeply guilty toward Your Grace. After all, it was he who poisoned you and ruined your enfeoffment ceremony. So, he wants to hold a new enfeoffment ceremony for you. Once you are fully recovered and officially become a concubine, he will personally go to Renshou Palace to bring back the Fifth Prince."

"Well, it’s fine. Yuanlang staying a little longer in the Dowager’s palace to cultivate a relationship with her is also good."

That Dowager of ours was no ordinary person—she was a politician with her own power at her disposal. If Yuanlang could win the Dowager’s favor, it would only be beneficial.

Xiangjun was determined to pave a broad path for Yuanlang.

She picked up a jade bracelet from the tray, its green hue vibrant, and slipped it onto her wrist.

Having spent days lying in bed and only consuming broths and liquids, she had indeed lost a lot of weight.

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun’s slender wrist and the loose jade bracelet, his heart aching as he took her hand in his.

"Your Grace has lost so much weight. You must regain it properly."

"Being thinner is better. His Majesty prefers a slender waist."

Gu Tingxue’s expression darkened for a moment, a flicker of malice flashing in his eyes, but Xiangjun was too busy admiring the clear jade bracelet to notice.

Xiangjun smiled and asked Gu Tingxue, "Does it look good?"

Gu Tingxue’s eyes held a smile as he reached out, pulling Xiangjun into his embrace, and softly said, "Your Grace looks good in anything."

Xiangjun was pleased and didn’t mind Gu Tingxue’s familiarity. Leaning against him, she casually asked, "How is the deposed Empress Yang faring now?"

Xiangjun had no real feelings for Empress Yang.

In her past life, their relationship had been one of mutual exploitation, but Xiangjun had been outmaneuvered by Empress Yang, leading to her own tragic fate.

In this life, she had played her cards better, so it was Empress Yang who was deposed.

A gamble was a gamble—losers had to accept their fate.

"His Majesty granted her poisoned wine. But Yang refused to drink it. Today, Noble Consort Rong went to Weiyang Palace, saying she wanted to see the Empress off on her final journey. They should be talking now." Gu Tingxue replied.

Xiangjun was truly at a loss for words and couldn’t understand.

In the novel, every time a "villain" was defeated, Noble Consort Rong would go see them, have a conversation with them—so-called killing them emotionally as well.

Xiangjun didn’t understand. What was there to say to a defeated opponent?

The Empress had been brought down by her, Xiangjun. Whether it was poisoning herself or placing the witchcraft doll in the Empress’s palace, it had all been Xiangjun’s schemes—she had just had Gu Tingxue suggest them to the Emperor.

She had stayed hidden in the background the entire time. No one in the harem knew she was involved.

She had not only gained the Emperor’s guilt but also reclaimed her child, all while keeping her hands clean.

If she was going to do something bad, shouldn’t everyone do it the way she did?

Why did Noble Consort Rong have to go see the Empress? Was it to make people think the Empress had been brought down by her, to make people fear her?

"Does Noble Consort Rong think she’s the one who won?"

"Many nobles and military officials helped with the Empress’s downfall, acting as the Emperor’s tools. Of course, Noble Consort Rong thinks it was she who brought down the Empress. As for the Fourth Prince’s poisoning, it was officially the work of Consort Qin, but Noble Consort Rong knows the Empress was behind it. Now that she has avenged her great grievance and been promoted to Imperial Noble Consort, she is naturally basking in her success."

Xiangjun sighed. Noble Consort Rong’s way of thinking wasn’t wrong.

It was just that she didn’t understand—Empress Yang had been deposed not because of the harem women’s schemes, but because the Emperor had wanted to depose her.

At this thought, Xiangjun’s heart sank again.

Even though Yang Jingshan, the Empress’s father, was dead, the Yang family was still far more powerful than her own Xu family. But even so, as soon as the Emperor wanted Yang to die, she had to die.

What good was a noble birth? What good were powerful backers? Without true power, one could still be crushed to death.

Xiangjun couldn’t follow in Empress Yang’s footsteps. She had to grasp real power.

But how could a woman in the harem ever grasp real power?

Xiangjun thought long and hard and decided she had to learn from the Dowager.

If only she knew how the Dowager had put the Emperor on the throne back then… but she couldn’t just ask her directly.

If she inquired about this, she feared her Yuanlang would never be returned to Chengxiang Palace.

"How is the Fourth Prince’s face now?" Xiangjun asked.

"That witch doctor is quite skilled. The black spots on the Fourth Prince’s face have faded a lot. He said that in half a year, they can be completely removed. In another year or two, he’ll look normal."

"Hmph, I’m afraid His Majesty has even less regard for our Yuanlang now."

"His Majesty naturally favors Yuanze the most." Gu Tingxue played with Xiangjun’s hair, his tone indifferent. "Your Grace need not worry. With me here, Yuanlang won’t lack anything compared to Yuanze."

Xiangjun coldly huffed, feeling very dissatisfied. "It’s a pity that although we’ve brought down the Yangs, we’ve only paved the way for others. Once Xue Jiaojiao becomes Empress, her Fourth Prince will be the legitimate heir—both a legitimate son and favored by the Emperor. How can my Yuanlang compare?"

"Your Grace need not worry. His Majesty is still wary of the powerful factions behind Xue Jiaojiao. Otherwise, he wouldn’t have first established the Imperial Noble Consort instead of directly making her Empress."

Xiangjun’s gaze was resolute. "It seems I need to recover quickly. This palace cannot let His Majesty need someone to use, only to find no one available. This palace is determined to be the Emperor’s blade."

---

chapters.title: Enfeoffment as Consort
chapters.content:
In Renshou Palace.

The Dowager held Yuanlang in her arms, her expression full of affection.

"This Yuanlang is just like his mother—so clever. He will surely grow up to be intelligent."

Seeing how much the Dowager liked Yuanlang, the Emperor’s filial piety was stirred. "If Mother truly likes the Fifth Prince, why not raise him by your side? Consort Lian is the most filial and considerate—she won’t be unhappy."

The Dowager’s face still held a kind expression, but she handed the child to the matron beside her, having someone take the child away first.

"It’s still best for a child to be raised by his own mother." The Dowager said indifferently, "No one can care for a child as wholeheartedly as their own mother."

The Dowager’s casual words struck a sore spot in the Emperor’s heart.

Years ago, when the Dowager was exiled to Bei Meng, he had been raised in the Imperial Concubine’s Palace. The Imperial Concubines hadn’t mistreated him, but he had still suffered humiliation and hardship in the palace.

He couldn’t complain to the Imperial Concubines either, because no one would offend the powerful concubines and princes in the palace for the sake of a child with no blood relation to them.

Thus, the Emperor understood better than anyone the suffering of not having a birth mother.

"Mother is right. Only a birth mother will do everything for her child, just as Mother did for me back then."

The Emperor could be said to have been placed on the imperial throne single-handedly by his mother.

He wasn’t the most outstanding prince, nor was he the former Emperor’s favorite child. But because of his mother’s superb political maneuvering, he had defeated all his rivals, taken revenge on all who had humiliated him, and become Emperor.

The Dowager patted the Emperor’s hand.

"Those past events need not be mentioned again. You’ve done well as Emperor."

"Thank you, Mother..." No one’s praise meant as much to the Emperor as the Dowager’s.

"But, I still need to remind you of a few things."

"Please enlighten me, Mother."

"Your Majesty, you have now dealt with the Jiangnan Faction, suppressed the Pure Stream officials, and consolidated imperial power. All of this is well done. But now, in the harem, Imperial Noble Consort holds unchecked power. She has the support of nobles and the military in the imperial court. It can be said that Imperial Noble Consort is now more powerful than the former Empress Yang..."

The Emperor’s expression turned serious.

"Mother is right. This son understands Mother’s intentions. But Imperial Noble Consort is different from the former Empress Yang. She loves me wholeheartedly. During the Song Feijing incident, she was willing to die to save me."

"I naturally believe in the affection you’ve cultivated over the years. But Your Majesty, you must know that people’s hearts can change. Ask yourself—do you feel the same about Imperial Noble Consort as you did before?"

The Emperor fell silent.

The Emperor was the best at empathizing with others, so he began to doubt whether Imperial Noble Consort felt the same about him as before.

The more he thought about it, the more evidence he found.

Yes, who could remain exactly the same as before?

Even if Imperial Noble Consort was willing to die for him now, who could guarantee she wouldn’t change when faced with the temptation of power?

Even if Imperial Noble Consort didn’t change, what if the people around her forced her to do things she shouldn’t?

Seeing the change in the Emperor’s expression, the Dowager knew her son had taken her words to heart.

The Dowager continued, "In my opinion, the people of Jiangnan should still be used when needed. Back then, I was able to become Empress, and you were able to ascend the throne smoothly, all thanks to the support of the Jiangnan officials. Although they have been a bit presumptuous in expecting rewards after your enthronement, on the whole, they are still loyal. Song Feijing’s rebellion was also for the sake of Imperial Noble Consort and the Fourth Prince. There are still some useful and loyal people in Jiangnan."

Hearing the Dowager say this, the Emperor’s face darkened.

He knew of the Dowager’s deep connections with the Jiangnan gentry.

He had handled the Jiangnan Faction, and the Dowager wasn’t particularly pleased. But the Dowager blaming this on Imperial Noble Consort still made the Emperor uncomfortable.

"How did Consort Lian’s brother do in the imperial examinations?" the Dowager suddenly asked.

The Emperor returned to his senses and thought for a moment before replying, "Consort Lian’s brother did quite well. He ranked fifth in the second class in this year’s spring examinations."

"Not bad for a young man. Is he married?"

"He is not."

The Dowager seemed lost in thought. After a pause, she said, "What does Your Majesty think of Consort Lian?"

"She is clever and gentle, and she is completely loyal to me. This time, with the deposed Empress incident, I made her suffer grievances. I intend to compensate her well."

The Dowager’s face showed a knowing smile. "Consort Lian is meticulous. Your Imperial Noble Consort can’t even manage her own Ganlu Palace properly. If she is to manage the entire harem, it might end up in chaos. Why not wait until Consort Lian is officially enfeoffed, and have her assist Imperial Noble Consort in managing the harem?"

The Emperor also felt the Dowager’s suggestion made sense. Imperial Noble Consort’s handling of affairs was indeed not thorough enough.

He did need to promote another concubine. Xiangjun’s family background was ordinary, so there was no fear of her following in Empress Yang’s footsteps. Moreover, she and Imperial Noble Consort were like sisters, so she wouldn’t disrespect the Noble Consort just because she gained the power to assist in managing the harem.

As for her family background...

Didn’t she have a brother who was a Jinshi? As long as the Emperor willed it, the Xu family could be promoted immediately and put to use.

"Mother is right. This son understands."

...

Xiangjun only waited half a month before she emerged from Chengxiang Palace once more.

The Emperor held a grand enfeoffment ceremony for her, even sending two imperial princes as envoys for the ceremony, one of whom was Prince Jin.

After the enfeoffment ceremony, the Emperor granted Xiangjun the power to assist in managing the harem, allowing her to work alongside Imperial Noble Consort.

All the concubines in the palace watched Xiangjun—some with envy, some with jealousy, some with disdain.

But no matter what they thought, from now on, Consort Lian was a favored concubine with real power in the harem. No one could afford to slight or neglect her.

After receiving the golden certificate and seal of her concubine rank and completing the intricate enfeoffment ceremony, Xiangjun returned to Chengxiang Palace to accept the kowtows of all her palace attendants.

The heavy court attire weighed her down, forcing her to sit upright, or she wouldn’t be able to support the heavy crown on her head.

When Gu Tingxue entered, he saw Xiangjun in her consorts' court attire, beautiful yet imposing, sitting upright in the main hall, looking down at the kneeling palace attendants with a commanding gaze.

For a moment, Gu Tingxue felt a sense of disorientation.

He recalled the first time he had seen Xiangjun, holding a pipa, kneeling before him, so cunning.

Now, Xiangjun was like a meticulously cultivated peony, blooming in the most honorable place in the world with unparalleled splendor.

Seeing Gu Tingxue enter, Xiangjun dismissed the other attendants.

The attendants understood and quickly withdrew.

Once everyone was gone, Xiangjun didn’t move. She remained seated in the main hall, slightly tilting her head up, looking at Gu Tingxue with a smug, self-satisfied expression.

"Look at you, Gu Tingxue. I am now a Consort. Won’t you even kneel and pay your respects to me?"

Gu Tingxue had received the Emperor’s permission—he didn’t have to kneel before any concubine in the harem, nor did he have to refer to himself as a servant. Instead, he could refer to himself as "this humble official" and perform the rites of a subject to the concubines.

So, Xiangjun didn’t actually expect Gu Tingxue to kneel to her. She just wanted to tease him a bit and then take the opportunity to get some nice gifts from him as a celebration of her promotion to Consort.

Therefore, when she saw Gu Tingxue approaching her with a serious face, Xiangjun panicked slightly. "What are you doing? I was only joking. Even if you don’t want to kneel to me, can’t you at least say some auspicious words?"

But before Xiangjun could react, Gu Tingxue flicked his sleeve and knelt on one knee, performing a grand bow to her.

Before Xiangjun could process what was happening, she heard Gu Tingxue’s deep and melodious voice say something that pleased her greatly.

Gu Tingxue said, "This humble servant, Gu Tingxue, pays his respects to Consort Lian."

chapters.title: Is This About Reputation? This Is About Our Lives
chapters.content:
That single word "slave" made Xiangjun's heart skip a beat.

Then, a wild joy surged within her.

Slave—Gu Tingxue had addressed himself as her slave.

He called himself "Your humble servant" before the Emperor, yet to her, he called himself a slave. What did this mean?

Didn't this mean he was completely surrendering himself to her, ready to be entirely at her disposal?

Xiangjun suppressed the excitement in her voice, feigning nonchalance. "Get up."

Xiangjun extended a hand to Gu Tingxue, and he took it, rising to his feet.

But even after standing, Gu Tingxue did not let go of her hand.

"Dog slave, how dare you! Let go at once!"

If anyone else in the harem dared call Gu Tingxue a dog slave, they would surely be killed by him. But when Xiangjun said it, he found it pleasing to the ear.

"Ah!" Xiangjun gasped in shock, cursing, "Dog slave, what are you doing?"

Without warning, Gu Tingxue scooped her up in his arms.

"Since Your Highness calls this humble servant a dog slave, I must naturally do what a dog slave does."

...

"Your Highness, it's time to rise."

The next morning, Xiangjun was awakened by Mengmei's voice outside the bed curtains.

Xiangjun groggily opened her eyes and saw a bewitchingly handsome face.

Normally, seeing this face would make her happy, but at this moment, it startled her.

With a cry of alarm, Xiangjun scared Mengmei, who was about to lift the bed curtains. "Your Highness, what's wrong?"

"Nothing! Don't lift the curtain."

Xiangjun grabbed the curtain just as Mengmei's hand was reaching in, forcing her to pull it back.

"You wait outside."

Though confused, Mengmei obeyed and went outside to wait.

Xiangjun quickly pushed Gu Tingxue, who was still asleep.

"Tingxue, wake up!"

Gu Tingxue frowned, slowly opening his beautiful phoenix eyes.

"Why are you still here?" Xiangjun whispered urgently.

Only then did Gu Tingxue sit up helplessly, his cascading black hair, like a waterfall, spilling over the brocade, entangled with Xiangjun's long hair.

"Who was it that wouldn't let me leave last night?"

"Well... that doesn't mean you should stay until now..." Xiangjun stammered. "You used to leave before dawn. Look at the time now! There are people outside."

"It's fine, I'll just be careful when I leave."

Xiangjun panicked, feeling Gu Tingxue was being reckless. "How can you be so careless lately? If I hadn't woken up early just now, Mengmei would have seen you."

Gu Tingxue lifted the bed curtain and sat up. "Your Highness, you jest. How could the palace servants close to you not know about us?"

Xiangjun's heart skipped a beat, and she fell silent.

She had suspected that everyone probably guessed something, but since no one had asked, she had pretended that no one knew.

Gu Tingxue put on his shoes and picked up the scattered clothes from the floor, putting them on.

Seeing the clothes strewn all over the floor, Xiangjun felt even more helpless.

Mengmei must have seen the python robe on the floor just now. She was so calm and composed—she must have known for a long time but simply chose not to ask.

Gu Tingxue fastened the buttons of his robe and glanced at Xiangjun, who was frowning with her beautiful willow-leaf eyebrows, looking worried.

"What's wrong? Does Your Highness not want others to know about our affair?" Gu Tingxue's eyes turned cold. "To share a meal with a eunuch is indeed a stain on Your Highness's sacred reputation."

"Why are you being so sarcastic?" Xiangjun thought Gu Tingxue was being unreasonable. "Is this about reputation? This is about our lives! Don't be so affected with me!"

Xiangjun shot Gu Tingxue a glare and got out of bed.

She felt that both she and Gu Tingxue had been too careless. They must never be so reckless again.

If someone with ill intentions found out and reported it to the Emperor, they would both be doomed to a fate worse than death.

Gu Tingxue had already dressed. Seeing Xiangjun get up, he called out, "Someone, attend to Her Highness."

Xiangjun's eyes widened in shock as she watched Gu Tingxue casually let Mengmei and Xiyu enter.

Mengmei and Xiyu didn't even bat an eyelid, quickly entering to help Xiangjun wash up. Meanwhile, Gu Tingxue sat down at Xiangjun's dressing table, tied his own hair, put on his black velvet smoke-stand hat, and left majestically through the main door.

It wasn't until Gu Tingxue had left that Xiangjun snapped out of her daze.

She looked at Mengmei, then at Xiyu, and asked, "Gu Tingxue got up from my bed, and you two aren't surprised at all?"

Mengmei and Xiyu exchanged an awkward glance. Mengmei then lowered her voice and replied, "Your Highness, every time it's me, Xiyu, and Xiaoluzhi on night watch. Although Lord Tingxue always enters through the window, we're not blind. We can see him coming and going every time."

"Then why have you never asked me about it?"

"Lord Tingxue is good to Your Highness, and Your Highness is happy. Why would we ask?"

Of course, the three of them had discussed this matter privately and reached a consensus: they must guard this secret. That was why they had never let any other palace servants take the night watch.

Xiangjun didn't know what to say for a moment, feeling somewhat embarrassed.

She glared at the expressionless Mengmei and Xiyu, complaining, "Don't you think Gu Tingxue has been acting strangely lately? He's been far too reckless, sleeping here until the sun is high in the sky! He may not care about his life, but I still do."

"Your Highness, please don't worry," Xiyu comforted Xiangjun. "Our Chengxiang Palace is as tight as an iron bucket. Everyone is of one mind, and no one can extract any information from us. Besides, Lord Tingxue is an inner attendant. It's not strange for him to leave our palace at this time."

"Lord Tingxue is only more relaxed in our palace. He's very cautious outside," Mengmei added.

Xiangjun frowned, feeling displeased.

"Has Gu Tingxue given you some benefits? You're all speaking up for him. Don't forget who your mistress is."

Xiyu smiled and said, "Our mistress is naturally Consort Lian. Your Highness, please don't be angry."

Although Mengmei and Xiyu weren't worried, Xiangjun still felt that Gu Tingxue's behavior was off, though she couldn't pinpoint what was wrong.

But before she could figure it out, the Empress Dowager sent someone to summon her.

"Greetings to Consort Lian. The Empress Dowager requests your presence at the Ren Shou Palace."

Xiangjun was delighted. Was the Empress Dowager going to return Yuanlang to her?

Xiangjun quickly had Mengmei fetch some fine gifts from Jiangnan from the storeroom and, carrying the gifts, went to Ren Shou Palace.

---

chapters.title: The Empress Dowager Plays Matchmaker
chapters.content:
As soon as she arrived at Ren Shou Palace, the Empress Dowager had someone bring Yuanlang for Xiangjun to see.

Xiangjun held Yuanlang, her tears almost falling, but in the end, she didn't cry. Instead, her eyes reddened as she smiled with relief and gratitude.

"The Empress Dowager is deeply blessed. Yuanlang has been under your care for some time and has benefited from your grace. He has grown so plump and round."

The Empress Dowager was very pleased with Xiangjun's reaction. If she had come in holding Yuanlang and wept, the Empress Dowager would have been displeased.

Now, Xiangjun's demeanor showed both her love for Yuanlang and her gratitude, which was exactly what the Empress Dowager wanted to see.

She was a child with a good sense of propriety.

"Since you have recovered, take the child back with you. I am old and cannot look after this little monkey you've given birth to."

Xiangjun looked at the Empress Dowager with gratitude, wiped her eyes, handed Yuanlang to the wet nurse behind her, and had Mengmei present the gifts she had prepared.

"Empress Dowager, this is a copy of the *Amitabha Sutra* I transcribed. I had it blessed by a highly virtuous monk at Huguo Temple. I hope it can bring you good fortune and longevity. And in this box are some trinkets from Jiangnan, sent by my father. They are not valuable, but I found them interesting and thought you might enjoy them."

The Empress Dowager glanced at the items: natural rainflower stones, Suzhou embroidered fans, Huishan clay figurines, sandalwood Suzhou fans, Hu pens from Suzhou, and combs from Changzhou...

None of them were particularly valuable, but they were all exquisite items from Jiangnan.

The Empress Dowager was originally from Jiangnan, and as she grew older, her homesickness deepened. Seeing these items now, she was genuinely delighted.

"You have a filial heart," the Empress Dowager said with a kind smile, glancing at the maid behind her. "Put them away."

The maid stored Xiangjun's gifts.

The Empress Dowager continued, "I know you are a good child. Now that you have the authority to assist in managing the six palaces, you must help the Noble Consort well. If there's anything you don't understand, come ask me."

Xiangjun was overjoyed. She knelt and bowed. "Thank you, Empress Dowager. Xiangjun will frequently bring Yuanlang to seek your guidance. I only hope that you won't find us bothersome."

"You... I certainly don't mind you. I'm just afraid you'll find it boring here."

"Not at all. I even want to ask the Empress Dowager to teach me the pipa. I can't discuss such things with anyone else."

The Empress Dowager smiled, looking Xiangjun up and down, and said softly, "Don't stand. Sit."

"Thank you, Empress Dowager."

Xiangjun didn't stand on ceremony and sat down beside her, picking up a piece of Ding Sheng cake from the table and taking a bite.

"You're quite bold. Even as a mother, you still have such a sweet tooth."

Xiangjun smiled. "It's because the Empress Dowager dotes on me that I dare to indulge."

Xiangjun chatted with the Empress Dowager for a while longer, sharing amusing stories about Yuanlang's time in the Yongchang Palace. The room was filled with laughter.

Just as Xiangjun was about to take her leave, the Empress Dowager suddenly said, "Oh, by the way, I heard your brother passed the imperial examination?"

Xiangjun beamed. "Yes, my brother studies very hard. Now that he has passed, I am also happy for him."

"Did the Emperor say what position he would give him?"

Xiangjun blinked in confusion. "I don't know. I didn't ask."

"You're too carefree about such an important matter."

Xiangjun smiled awkwardly.

She wasn't carefree at all. She was trying to appear virtuous. As someone in the harem, she shouldn't interfere in politics. Having just gained the authority to assist in managing the six palaces, if she were to meddle in the Emperor's decision to assign her own brother a position, wouldn't she be risking her life?

The Empress Dowager sighed and patted Xiangjun's hand. "You are a sensible one, which is good. However, you should still manage the things you need to. I asked the Emperor, and your brother is alone in the capital with no one to look after him. As his sister, you should make more arrangements for him."

Xiangjun knew her brother was alone in the capital, but the Xu family was extremely wealthy. With money paving the way and a favored sister in the palace, how could her brother truly be without care? Were the servants in his courtyard not people?

"Yes, I understand," Xiangjun replied obediently, though she didn't truly grasp the Empress Dowager's meaning.

"You must truly understand. Your brother is not young anymore. You already have a child, but has your brother taken a wife?"

"Not yet."

"Now that he has passed the examination and has a sister who is a consort, he must choose carefully and find a good match."

Xiangjun nodded, smiling at the Empress Dowager. Then, noticing the affectionate look in the Empress Dowager's eyes, Xiangjun suddenly had a revelation.

Had the Empress Dowager called her here today to arrange a marriage for her brother?

...

After leaving the Yongchang Palace, Xiangjun was still in a daze.

The Empress Dowager actually wanted to marry her grandniece to her brother and had even instructed Xu Huanwen to find an opportunity to meet the Empress Dowager's grandniece when he came to the palace to see Xiangjun.

Was the Empress Dowager trying to support the Xu family?

Xiangjun pondered this repeatedly, her heart unsettled. She decided to go to the Tai Ji Hall to see the Emperor and find out more.

When she arrived at the Tai Ji Hall, the Emperor was pleased to see Xiangjun bringing cakes. He took her hand and led her to sit beside him.

"Yuanze was ill yesterday, so I couldn't come see you. Are you angry with me?"

Xiangjun scoffed inwardly. No wonder Gu Tingxue had been so certain that the dog Emperor wouldn't come to see her—it turned out the Emperor's precious son was sick.

Xiangjun replied gently, "How could I be? Your Majesty has a compassionate father's heart. I only think Your Majesty is a good father."

"Rest assured, I feel the same way about our Yuanlang."

Xiangjun mentally spat in disdain.

How many times had the Emperor visited Yuanlang since his birth?

In the Emperor's heart, only the sons he had with the Noble Consort were truly his. The others were merely heirs to the throne.

After flattering the Emperor's paternal heart to satisfy his vanity, Xiangjun brought up the topic of her brother and mentioned that the Empress Dowager wanted to arrange a marriage between her grandniece and Xu Huanwen.

The Emperor was very pleased that Xiangjun had come to discuss this matter with him.

Xiangjun's caution had its benefits. Such an important matter, and she had come to ask for his opinion.

But her caution also had its advantages. This was an opportunity to connect with the Empress Dowager, yet she had come to inform him, the Emperor, first. It showed that she was different from other power-hungry consorts.

"The Empress Dowager has discussed this with me. Her grandniece is the daughter of a Grand Master of the Second Rank. Such a marriage would be a good thing for your Xu family."

"I know it is a good thing, but... I'm afraid..." Xiangjun looked pitiful. "I'm afraid my brother is not good enough for the Empress Dowager's grandniece. What if she looks down on him?"

The Emperor chuckled. "Your brother is a new Jinshi, good-looking, young, and the brother of Consort Lian in the palace, as well as the maternal uncle of my fifth imperial son. How could he not be good enough for the Empress Dowager's grandniece? You are already a consort. There's no need to be so overly cautious."

chapters.title: I Still Spoil You Too Much
chapters.content:
Xiangjun nodded with a look of having been taught a lesson.

Seeing Xiangjun’s obedient and cautious demeanor, the Emperor’s heart softened. He reached out and pulled her into his embrace.

"You can rest assured. With me backing you, you don’t need to be so overly cautious."

Xiangjun leaned against the Emperor’s shoulder, her gaze forward firm and cunning, yet her voice remained soft and humble.

"This concubine thanks Your Majesty. The glory of my family is all bestowed by Your Majesty. It is truly my great fortune to have encountered Your Majesty in this life."

Xiangjun still knew who her real superior was.

Although this favor came from the Empress Dowager, she still had to express gratitude to the Emperor.

The Emperor was indeed very pleased with Xiangjun’s attitude. After some thought, he said, "Rest assured. There are many vacant official positions in the court now. I won’t let your brother be sent away. He will stay in the capital. I’ll have him enter the Hanlin Academy first. After half a year, I’ll transfer him to the Ministry of Rites."

Xiangjun pondered. The Ministry of Rites...

The Ministry of Rites was good. The Ministry of Rites could help our vain and self-important Emperor with his affairs. As long as he pleased the Emperor, wasn’t promotion guaranteed?

"Thank you, Your Majesty. As long as it does not wrong the Empress Dowager’s grandniece, this concubine will be at ease."

After fawned over the Emperor for a while, Xiangjun returned to Chengxiang Palace to hold her son, Yuanlang.

Children in the palace didn’t require much attention from their mothers. Everything was handled by wet nurses and nannies, so even after taking the child back, Xiangjun wasn’t too tired.

Over the next few days, aside from handling palace affairs, Xiangjun spent her time with Qinglian, playing with Yuangi, holding Yuanlang, embroidering tiger-head hats, eating and drinking. Occasionally, Qinglian would even dance for her. The two of them found their own joy in Chengxiang Palace.

However, recently, Gu Tingxue had been visiting her far too often. Sometimes, even when Qinglian hadn’t left, Gu Tingxue would arrive. Even Qinglian, who had always been afraid of Gu Tingxue, found it strange and privately asked Xiangjun about it.

"Why does Eunuch Tingxue keep coming to Chengxiang Palace to deliver things from His Majesty and the Noble Consort?" Qinglian was still afraid and wary of him. "Sister, you must be careful. Eunuch Tingxue is the Noble Consort’s man. The way he looks at you, it’s as if he wants to devour you. It’s creepy. I fear he already suspects you."

Xiangjun felt a little embarrassed and pretended not to understand. "Suspects me of what?"

"Naturally, he suspects you of being disloyal to the Noble Consort. Sister, now that you have the authority to assist in managing the six palaces, the Noble Consort will naturally be wary of you. You must be careful not to reveal any flaws in front of this eunuch."

Xiangjun could only pretend to take it to heart and reassure Qinglian.

Unexpectedly, Gu Tingxue also complained to Xiangjun about Qinglian.

Because Qinglian refused to leave, Gu Tingxue would deliver the items and leave, only to sneak back to Chengxiang Palace to sleep at night.

As soon as he arrived, Gu Tingxue said, "I’ll think of a way to have Consort Jian move out of Chengxiang Palace. Your Majesty is now the favored concubine and assists in managing the six palaces. Living alone in a palace will highlight Your Majesty’s uniqueness."

Xiangjun shot Gu Tingxue a glance. "Don’t think I don’t know what you’re thinking. What’s wrong with you and Consort Jian? She hasn’t provoked you."

Gu Tingxue coldly scoffed, "I naturally can’t stand her. A consort who doesn’t think about how to vie for favor, but instead spends her days in another consort’s room—what kind of example is that? Doesn’t Consort Jian have her own matters to attend to?"

Seeing Gu Tingxue take off his outer robe and get into bed, Xiangjun kicked out at him, but Gu Tingxue caught her ankle and tucked it into his embrace, covering it.

"Tch, what right do you have to talk about Qinglian? Look at yourself! Don’t you come running here every day? They say your residence outside the palace is more magnificent than a prince’s mansion, yet I never see you go back to sleep. You always come here to crowd me. It seems I still spoil you too much, allowing you to be so presumptuous."

No one knew which of her words struck a chord with Gu Tingxue, but he curled his lips into a bewitching and seductive smile.

Gu Tingxue kissed the sole of Xiangjun’s foot. Seeing the change in his eyes, Xiangjun quickly came to her senses and kicked him again.

"It’s not even that late. Don’t cause trouble."

It was indeed still early in the night. Gu Tingxue thought for a moment, then retracted his seductive gaze. He asked, "Where is Yuanlang? Has he fallen asleep?"

"He should still need to be fed at this hour. I’ll have Mengmei bring the child over."

Mengmei brought the child over, and Gu Tingxue coaxed Yuanlang. Yuanlang’s bright eyes kept looking at Gu Tingxue, smiling happily. He was truly adorable.

Gu Tingxue rarely showed such a gentle expression. He held Yuanlang and coaxed him for a long time, even ignoring Xiangjun.

Xiangjun didn’t mind. She lay on the bed reading, enjoying the leisure.

She read by the lamp, while Gu Tingxue played with the child. For a moment, Xiangjun felt as if she were the husband, and Gu Tingxue were her wife...

She became so absorbed in her book that it wasn’t until Gu Tingxue lay down on the bed that she realized Yuanlang had been taken away.

Gu Tingxue took the book from her hands and pulled her into his embrace.

"You’re being too clingy."

Gu Tingxue kissed Xiangjun’s hair. His gaze darkened for a moment, but he quickly concealed the fleeting obsession.

"Has Your Majesty forgotten? This servant once said, what I want, I will take for myself."

...

Gu Tingxue came every day. Although Xiangjun was also happy, she gradually began to feel some worry.

"Mengmei, how long has it been since His Majesty visited our Chengxiang Palace?"

"His Majesty came to accompany Your Majesty for lunch just the day before yesterday."

"I mean, how long has it been since His Majesty summoned me to his bedchamber?"

Mengmei quickly realized something was wrong. After a moment of thought, she said seriously, "Counting the days, it has been over a year since Your Majesty last attended His Majesty in his bedchamber."

Xiangjun’s expression darkened. Since she became pregnant, the Emperor had not summoned her to his bed.

It was natural that she couldn’t attend him during pregnancy.

Later, after her confinement, she had staged the poisoning incident. The Emperor was busy dealing with Empress Yang and the Yang family, so it was understandable that she hadn’t attended him.

But now, her body had recovered, she had been granted the title of consort, Yuanze’s body had recovered, and Yuanlang had been brought back to Chengxiang Palace. If the Emperor still didn’t summon her, something was wrong.
