The Emperor hadn’t seen her give birth, so it wasn’t as if he had a psychological shadow because of it, right?

So why wasn’t His Majesty coming?

Xiangjun felt that Gu Tingxue probably knew the reason. Otherwise, he wouldn’t be so bold as to come to her place to sleep every time he was free.

So, when Gu Tingxue came again, Xiangjun asked him about it.

"Tingxue, His Majesty hasn’t summoned me for a long time. Do you know why?"

Gu Tingxue was currently embracing Xiangjun from behind, one hand around her waist, the other playing with her soft, beautiful hand.

Hearing Xiangjun’s question, Gu Tingxue’s movements paused. Then, he tightened his grip on her waist.

"Does Your Majesty wish to be summoned by His Majesty? It seems this servant has not been serving Your Majesty well enough."

---

chapters.title: The Chank Shell Bracelet
chapters.content:
The next morning, when Xiangjun woke up to an empty bedchamber, she realized that Gu Tingxue had left, and the most important matter remained unresolved.

However, Xiangjun didn’t have time to dwell on it. Today, Xu Huanwen was entering the palace. Having received the Emperor’s favor, he was to first pay respects to the Empress Dowager in Renshou Palace.

Xiangjun had to go to Renshou Palace early to wait.

Xiangjun had her maids come in to help her wash up and dress. While they were helping her put on her clothes, Mengmei noticed a new white bracelet with faint patterns on Xiangjun’s wrist.

"Your Majesty, when did you get this bracelet?"

Only then did Xiangjun notice the additional bracelet on her wrist.

After some thought, she vaguely remembered that Gu Tingxue had put it on her wrist the previous night.

"It was given to me by Tingxue."

Xiyu, curious, said, "What kind of bracelet is this? It looks a bit like pearl, but it has faint pink patterns... And look, it shimmers with iridescent light under the sunlight."

Xiangjun didn’t know either. She had never seen such a thing before.

She lifted her wrist to examine it. The bracelet had an ancient elegance and indeed shimmered with rainbow light in the sunlight. She reached out to touch it. It felt hard, but not cold. Instead, it was smooth and delicate, with a warm and moist texture.

However, since it was from Gu Tingxue, it was certainly something good, so she didn’t think there was anything strange about it.

Xiangjun didn’t dwell on it. Seeing that it was getting late, she hurriedly had her maids finish dressing her and rushed to Renshou Palace.

When Xiangjun arrived at Renshou Palace, the Empress Dowager was having breakfast. Seeing Xiangjun, she invited her to join.

Xiangjun wouldn’t miss an opportunity to deepen her bond with the Empress Dowager. She happily joined her.

The Empress Dowager also noticed the bracelet on Xiangjun’s wrist. A flicker of surprise flashed in her eyes, but she quickly composed herself and asked gently, "Where did you get this bracelet? Such a fine chank shell bracelet is rarely seen even by me."

Only then did Xiangjun learn that the bracelet was made of chank shell.

Chank shell bracelets were one of the seven treasures of Buddhism. Since chank shells grew in the sea and grew very slowly, it took hundreds of years for a large specimen to form. Moreover, each one had unique patterns and colors, making them extremely rare and precious. It wasn’t surprising that Xiangjun had never seen one before.

The Empress Dowager was a devout Buddhist, so she must have liked the bracelet. Without hesitation, Xiangjun took it off to offer it to the Empress Dowager.

"This was given to me by my father. This concubine did not know its value. If I had known it was a chank shell bracelet, I would have offered it to Your Majesty long ago."

The Empress Dowager smiled and put the bracelet back on Xiangjun’s wrist.

"Am I to take things from you? Keep wearing it. It seems this bracelet is destined for you. As one of the seven treasures of Buddhism, it symbolizes perfection. Consider it my blessing for you."

Xiangjun felt that the Empress Dowager’s words were a bit odd, but she didn’t have time to think about it. The Empress Dowager’s grandniece had arrived.

This Miss Li was sixteen years old this year. She was cute and lively, and her personality was also cheerful and lovable. She got along very well with Xiangjun.

After a while, Xu Huanwen arrived.

Xu Huanwen and the Empress’s grandniece met in Renshou Palace.

Seeing Miss Li’s blush, Xiangjun knew the matter was settled.

She truly heaved a sigh of relief.

Indeed, a man’s appearance was very important. Miss Li had only taken one look at Xu Huanwen and immediately looked shyly at the Empress Dowager, giving her an affirmative glance.

The Empress Dowager was naturally very happy.

Perhaps at a certain age, one enjoyed matchmaking. Seeing that her grandniece had taken a liking to Xu Huanwen, she was overjoyed. On the spot, she bestowed many gifts upon Xu Huanwen.

However, the Empress Dowager was considerate and knew that the siblings hadn’t seen each other in a long time. She didn’t keep Xu Huanwen but instead granted him another favor, allowing him to have lunch in the palace before leaving so he could properly see his nephew, Yuanlang.

Back in Chengxiang Palace, Xiangjun had the small kitchen prepare lunch.

Xiangjun had never dined with her brother before. In fact, they had barely spoken to each other. Now, suddenly having to spend time alone together, they both felt a bit awkward.

Fortunately, Xiangjun wasn’t afraid of awkwardness. She first inquired about Xu Huanwen’s life, asking how his living conditions were, whether the servants at home were competent, and if there was anything making him uncomfortable.

Xu Huanwen answered each question one by one, and then they fell into silence again.

But it was fine. Xiangjun had another idea. She quickly had someone bring Yuanji and Yuanlang over.

Sure enough, as soon as the two children arrived, their laughter and playfulness livened up the atmosphere.

Seeing how much Xu Huanwen liked children, Xiangjun said, "Brother, since you like children so much, you should quickly find a wife, bring her home, and have a few nephews for me."

Xu Huanwen’s expression stiffened. Xiangjun thought, *This isn’t good.*

Could it be that her brother didn’t like the Empress Dowager’s grandniece?

"Brother, what do you think of Miss Li?" Xiangjun asked.

Xu Huanwen’s tone was indifferent, giving no hint of his feelings. "The Empress Dowager’s grandniece is naturally excellent."

Xiangjun was too lazy to beat around the bush. "Brother, do you not like Miss Li? Do you know that the Empress Dowager intends to bestow a marriage between you and Miss Li?"

"I dare not. I am not worthy of Miss Li. The Empress Dowager’s intention to bestow this marriage is a great honor for the Xu family. Naturally, I have no objections."

Xiangjun was speechless.

Her brother was too wooden. Miss Li was a beautiful and refined woman. All he talked about was the Empress Dowager’s grace and the Xu family’s future. Did he have no personal feelings at all?

"Apart from the Empress Dowager’s decree, what do you think of Miss Li herself? Do you like her?"

"In matters of marriage, whether one likes the other is not important."

Xiangjun sighed. Judging by Xu Huanwen’s demeanor, he didn’t seem very interested in Miss Li. Probably, he was only willing to accept this marriage for the sake of the Empress Dowager’s favor and the Xu family’s future.

No, he didn’t have the right to be willing or unwilling.

The Empress Dowager and the Emperor’s wishes were not something they could refuse.

Xiangjun thought for a moment, sighed again, and still asked, "Brother, do you have someone you love?"

Xu Huanwen looked up at Xiangjun and then lowered his head. "Your Majesty is overthinking. This subject has always been focused on my studies, only thinking about bringing honor to the family and securing a title for my mother. I have never considered other matters."

"You’re a year older than me. How could you have never liked a girl?"

Xu Huanwen still kept his head down and said seriously, "Never."

Seeing that Xu Huanwen was unwilling to talk, Xiangjun didn’t press further. Why did asking him about a girl he liked feel like torturing him?

"Brother, Miss Li is a good person. I’ve inquired about her. She’s easy to get along with and not arrogant. Whether you like her or not, please treat Miss Li well."

"Your Majesty can rest assured. This subject is not so ungrateful. Since I have agreed to marry Miss Li, I will naturally treat her well."

Xiangjun was reassured. If they ended up as a resentful couple and Miss Li suffered, the Xu family would likely incur the Empress Dowager’s displeasure.

chapters.title: She Cannot Lose Favor
chapters.content:
At mealtime, it was said that Xu Huanwen was having lunch in Chengxiang Hall, and the Emperor had even bestowed several dishes upon him.

Brother and sister ate while discussing serious matters.

Xiangjun served her brother food and asked, "The Emperor told me that he wants to keep you in the capital."

"Yes," Xu Huanwen replied. "The Emperor has already ordered me to enter the Hanlin Academy."

"The Emperor also told me that he plans to promote you to the Ministry of Rites in half a year. Do you understand His Majesty's intentions, brother?"

Xu Huanwen was puzzled and humbly asked, "This humble official does not understand His Majesty's intentions. I beg the Noble Consort to enlighten me."

Xiangjun smiled and said, "The Emperor wants to perform the Fengshan ceremony at Mount Tai, but the ministers are all unwilling to support him. They believe His Majesty's achievements are not yet sufficient for such a ritual. The Emperor values face greatly, so naturally, he is furious. The former Empress Yang was deposed, and while it was said to be because the Yang family was too arrogant, this matter also played a role... So, do you understand His Majesty's intentions now, brother?"

Xu Huanwen frowned in thought. Having just entered officialdom this year, he was naturally unaware of the complexities involved. Upon hearing this, his understanding of the Emperor deepened significantly.

"This humble official understands, but regarding the Emperor's desire to perform the Fengshan ceremony..."

Xiangjun interrupted Xu Huanwen by serving him more food.

"Brother, I am but a mere woman, and as a concubine in the harem, I am not supposed to interfere in politics. However, having accompanied the Emperor, I can be considered to have gained his favor. So, I have a few words of advice for you, brother, and I hope you will take them to heart."

"Please, Noble Consort."

"I know you are an ambitious man and do not wish to be a sycophantic courtier. I also know how harsh the scholars in the imperial court can be with their words. But you must understand that only with power in hand can you truly realize your ambitions. The Emperor's decision to place you in the Ministry of Rites is a test. Only by proving that you are one of His Majesty's own will he continue to promote you. What others say does not matter. They criticize you only because you have not yet risen high enough. When the day comes that you hold the power of life and death over them, all you will hear are words of praise."

Xu Huanwen was taken aback and asked, "Has the Noble Consort heard something?"

Xiangjun merely smiled and did not answer.

This matter had been told to Xiangjun by Gu Tingxue.

Upon entering the Hanlin Academy, Xu Huanwen was immediately appointed as a compiler, receiving the same treatment as the top scholar, while other second-class scholars had to start as junior compilers and endure hardships. Naturally, this led to some snide remarks directed at Xu Huanwen, with people saying he relied on the pity of the Noble Consort in the palace rather than his own talent.

Moreover, someone had somehow discovered the previous incident where Xu Huanwen had been framed by Song Feijing for examination fraud. They brought it up again, even spreading rumors that Xu Huanwen had indeed cheated and was only released because of his sister.

Xu Huanwen naturally felt wronged. After years of hard study, he had achieved the rank of fifth in the second class at a young age, yet instead of praise, he received suspicion and slander.

Being alone in the capital with no one to confide in, he had drowned his sorrows in drink several times.

Upon learning of this, Gu Tingxue asked Xiangjun whether he should go and advise Xu Huanwen, and perhaps also teach those ungrateful junior compilers a lesson.

Xiangjun refused.

Xu Huanwen was a scholar, and being accused of relying on family connections was already hard enough for him. If he were also accused of colluding with eunuchs, it would be even worse.

"This capital is smaller than you think, brother. There are no secrets under the Emperor's feet," Xiangjun said.

Xu Huanwen's expression turned serious. He cupped his hands and bowed, saying, "This humble official understands. Thank you for your guidance, Noble Consort. Actually, I do not care what those people say, nor am I troubled by their sour words..."

This surprised Xiangjun.

"Then why are you upset, brother?"

"Although this humble official can be considered a young master from a wealthy family, my mother was of humble origins. From a young age, I have known the hardships of the common people. I thought that by becoming an official, I could fulfill my ambitions. However, whether it is the Imperial College or the Hanlin Academy, they are not what I expected. I have found that the people here are no different from the shrewish women in the marketplace. Very few truly care about the people or the nation; they only think about how to climb higher. Hence, I feel a sense of disillusionment."

Xiangjun felt a sense of relief.

If this was the reason for his distress, then he was indeed a good brother.

"Who says otherwise? It was only after becoming a palace concubine that I realized the desires of those noble and high-ranking people are no different from those of the lowest in the world. Since this is the case, why should we feel inferior? What they can have, we can also have. There is nothing that we do not deserve."

Xu Huanwen's expression was moved. "May I ask, how does the Noble Consort handle these matters?"

"I only focus on what I want; nothing else matters. Since these people possess only the basest desires, I use their desires to achieve my own goals. You need not concern yourself with those opportunistic people, brother. You should be happy. You see their desires, but they cannot understand yours. Therefore, they can be used by you."

"Your words have enlightened me, Noble Consort."

Xiangjun raised her cup. "Brother, as long as you have the world in your heart, why worry about temporary gains and losses? When the day comes that you gain the Emperor's favor, why worry about not being able to change the officialdom and improve your reputation?"

"You are right, Noble Consort. It is I who have been narrow-minded."

"I do not know when I will see you again, brother. I toast to you, hoping that your official career will be smooth and prosperous."

"Official career be smooth and prosperous" was such a commonplace blessing.

Yet, Xu Huanwen felt a surge of emotion in his heart.

"Yes, this humble official will not disappoint the Noble Consort's expectations."

...

A few days later, the Empress Dowager issued an imperial decree for a marriage.

Many well-informed palace concubines came to Xiangjun's palace to congratulate the Xu family on securing a good marriage.

The people in the harem were very politically sensitive and naturally understood the intentions behind the Empress Dowager and the Emperor's actions.

This was to elevate the Xu family. In a few years, the Xu family would likely become the new nobility of the court, forming a new power.

Some families had already instructed their concubines in the harem to pledge loyalty to Xiangjun, hoping to gain some benefits from this opportunity.

However, Xiangjun did not indulge in the flattery of the crowd.

She was worried because the Emperor had still not summoned her to his bedchamber.

She clearly knew that the Emperor did not love her; he only saw her as a plaything.

But that was fine. People who spent a lot of time together would develop feelings, especially men, who would have some affection for the women they had been intimate with.

Even if this affection was not love, but merely a man's possessive desire for his belongings, it did not matter.

Because men's minds could not distinguish between love and possessiveness. So, as long as Xiangjun received more of the Emperor's favor, she could remain a favored concubine for a long time.

Therefore, she could not afford to not attend to the Emperor's bedchamber...

Xiangjun looked in the mirror, suspecting that she might have become ugly after giving birth.

Meng Mei, Xi Yu, and Xiao Luzi all swore oaths that the Noble Consort had not only not become ugly but was even more radiant and beautiful than before her childbirth. Only then did Xiangjun feel slightly reassured.

But Xiangjun was not one to passively wait. Since Gu Tingxue was unwilling to tell her the reason, she decided to find out for herself.

So, Xiangjun changed into a thin dress, carried some snacks, and went to the Taiji Hall to see the Emperor.

chapters.title: This Slave Will Never Change His Heart
chapters.content:
In Taiji Hall.

Xiangjun and the Emperor were affectionately entwined on the dragon throne.

Any other concubine who dared to sit on the Emperor's lap while he was seated on the dragon throne would incur his anger.

But Xiangjun did so without consequence.

Because in the Emperor's heart, Xiangjun was a woman without ambition, and her timely displays of charm distracted him.

The Emperor was aroused by Xiangjun's teasing. If he did not have to meet with foreign officials soon, he would have taken Xiangjun to the bedchamber right then.

Seeing the Emperor in such a state of urgency, Xiangjun was completely at ease and eliminated the possibility she feared most.

Fortunately, the Emperor had no ill feelings toward her.

The Emperor promised to visit Xiangjun at Chengxiang Hall that evening.

Xiangjun hurried back to Chengxiang Hall to prepare. She was determined to make the Emperor linger and forget to leave.

But in the evening, after Xiangjun had bathed and changed into clean clothes, Eunuch Wan from the Emperor's side came to announce that the Emperor had matters to attend to and could not come. He had already gone to Nanxun Hall to visit the ailing Noble Consort Yue.

Noble Consort Yue had been in poor health since her miscarriage in the later months of her pregnancy, with continuous menstrual bleeding, and was unable to attend to the Emperor's bedchamber.

Nowadays, Nanxun Hall was practically a cold palace.

The palace servants were the most prone to flatter the powerful and bully the weak. Noble Consort Yue, let alone trying to vie for Xiangjun's favor, could not even get a message to the Emperor.

This was not right.

If Xiangjun could not see the problem here, she would have lived her two lives in vain.

After politely seeing off Eunuch Wan, Xiangjun ordered Meng Mei and Xi Yu to come in and help her change back into the formal attire of her concubine rank, with all the hairpins and jewelry properly worn, dressing herself in a dignified and noble manner.

"Noble Consort, it's almost time to sleep. Why are you dressing up again?"

Xiangjun did not answer. She merely stared coldly at her reflection in the mirror. Seeing that the Noble Consort seemed to be in a bad mood, the two did not dare to ask further.

After she was dressed, Xiangjun did not stay in the bedchamber but instead sat in the main hall, quietly waiting.

When Gu Tingxue arrived, as usual, he went to Xiangjun's bedchamber but was stopped by Xiao Luzi.

Xiao Luzi bowed his head respectfully and said, "Lord Gu, Noble Consort Lian is waiting for you in the main hall."

Gu Tingxue raised an eyebrow and looked at Xiao Luzi.

Although Xiao Luzi was very anxious inside, he appeared calm on the outside, only bending his waist a little lower.

"Lord Gu, please."

Gu Tingxue never made things difficult for the servants of Chengxiang Hall. Without asking further, he turned and went to the main hall.

The door to the hall was closed behind him, with Meng Mei standing guard outside.

Inside the main hall, Xiangjun sat alone on the high throne, dressed in full regalia, adorned with magnificent jewels and ornaments.

It seemed as if she was reminding Gu Tingxue that she was the only mistress of Chengxiang Hall.

If it were anyone else putting on airs for Gu Tingxue, he would certainly be disdainful. But he had always liked Xiangjun in this manner. The more proud and arrogant she was, the more at ease Gu Tingxue felt in his heart.

Gu Tingxue smiled, walked forward, and prepared to greet Xiangjun. But as soon as he bent slightly, something hard hit his hat.

The object fell to the ground. Gu Tingxue looked down and saw that it was the agate bracelet he had given to Xiangjun.

Gu Tingxue's expression changed, and his gaze immediately darkened.

When he looked up again at Xiangjun, there was a trace of anger in his eyes. But seeing Xiangjun's face flushed with anger, that trace of anger easily dissipated.

"Noble Consort, why are you throwing a tantrum without reason?"

"Without reason? Gu Tingxue, do you not know what you have done?"

Gu Tingxue remained calm, his expression unchanged. "This humble servant does not understand the Noble Consort's meaning."

"Do not pretend with me. Why did the Emperor not summon me to his bedchamber? And why did the Emperor go to Noble Consort Yue's palace today? Do not say you do not know. Are you eating from both sides, trying to help Noble Consort Yue?"

Gu Tingxue's gaze darkened as he realized Xiangjun was confronting him over this matter. He was not angry.

"How could that be? This slave's heart belongs only to the Noble Consort. I would never abandon you to help someone else."

Gu Tingxue bent down to pick up the bracelet and walked to Xiangjun's side.

He lifted his robe and knelt on one knee beside Xiangjun, gently taking her hand and successfully putting the bracelet back on her wrist.

Xiangjun glared angrily at Gu Tingxue, but Gu Tingxue was unhurried, as if he did not feel her fiery gaze at all.

Gu Tingxue kissed Xiangjun's hand, looked up at her with a smile, but his voice was full of threat.

"This bracelet is very important. Do not throw it around. If the Noble Consort does so again, this slave will be angry."

Although Gu Tingxue was kneeling, he exuded a strong sense of pressure. Xiangjun tried to pull her hand back, but he held it extremely tightly.

Xiangjun suppressed her anger, took a deep breath, and said, "Since you did not help Noble Consort Yue, why did the Emperor go to Nanxun Hall today?"

"I sent the Emperor to Nanxun Hall only because I did not want him to come to Chengxiang Hall."

As expected, Xiangjun's heart sank.

"Tingxue, this is the second time. Why are you blocking me from gaining favor? I am the Emperor's concubine, and this fact will not change."

Gu Tingxue caressed Xiangjun's soft hand, looking at her with an undisguised gaze of attachment.

"Noble Consort, you now have power, a prince, and this slave to help you. Why must you vie for favor? Did you not tell this slave that you do not care about the Emperor at all?"

Xiangjun looked at Gu Tingxue's gloomy and profound eyes, seeing the deep affection that he made no effort to hide.

Xiangjun knew that she had guessed correctly.

Gu Tingxue had fallen in love with her, but he had also developed an inappropriate possessiveness toward her.

This was a trouble she had to face in order to tame this venomous snake of a man.

This damned slave was really difficult to handle. If she did not capture his heart, he would not serve her wholeheartedly. But if she did capture his heart, he would try to dominate her.

"Tingxue, do not get it wrong. I am not your possession. It is true that I do not care about the Emperor, but I do care about what the Emperor can give me."

Xiangjun was determined to continue vying for favor.

Her path would not stop here. There was power that only the Emperor could give her, and she would absolutely not allow Gu Tingxue to always be above her.

She wanted to be Gu Tingxue's master, not Gu Tingxue's possession.

Xiangjun looked down at Gu Tingxue, her face rarely cold and stern.

Although Xiangjun had a delicate and charming face, years of being pampered in the palace had given her a noble demeanor. Now, dressed in the formal attire of a concubine, with her hair adorned with cold jewels and golden hairpins, she exuded an air of dignity and majesty.

Gu Tingxue recalled the first time he had seen Xiangjun. She had been kneeling on the ground in fear, begging him to spare her life and offering to serve him.

Now?

Their positions were reversed. Xiangjun was seated, while Gu Tingxue was kneeling.

Gu Tingxue did not mind kneeling by Xiangjun's side for the rest of his life, but he was not a selfless man...

"Noble Consort, I have said before that if you want my wholehearted devotion, you must give something in return."

"Is this what you want? Do you want me to be a woman exclusive to you?"

"Why not?" Gu Tingxue stood up, putting one hand behind his back. He looked down at Xiangjun once again. "I can give you everything you want, Noble Consort. Even if you cut off the Emperor's favor in the future, I can still make our child, Yuanlang, the crown prince."

"If that is the case, I can only rely on your loyalty. If one day you change your mind, Yuanlang and I will be like fish on a chopping block."

"This slave will never change his heart. As long as the Noble Consort is willing, I, Gu Tingxue, will be your slave alone. I can live for you and die for you."

chapters.title: But I'm Not a Man, I'm a Eunuch
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun, his tone calm but his gaze solemn.

Xiangjun met his eyes, and for a moment, she felt he was telling the truth—that he would do as he said.

But unfortunately, even if he was sincere, she didn’t want that kind of devotion.

She was tired of being someone else’s possession, even if she was a cherished one.

Xiangjun stood up as well.

She was seated on the higher platform, so she was now at eye level with Gu Tingxue, who stood on the step below.

"Tingxue, I understood a truth when I was very young: love is unreliable. Only what is in your own hands can be trusted. I believe you are wholeheartedly devoted to me now, but the world is unpredictable. Who can say what will happen in the future? Why must we test each other’s hearts?"

"Does Your Highness not trust me?"

"It’s not that I don’t trust you. It’s that I’ve seen too many faithless men—men who give everything when in love, only to discard it like trash when they fall out of love. So, I only trust the power I hold in my own hands."

Xiangjun’s mother, Xiangjun’s mentor—they had both been ruined by love.

In this world, men always had something more important than love, yet women had been deceived for centuries, spending their entire lives chasing fleeting affection.

Xiangjun would never make the same mistake.

She would spend her life pursuing what men pursued.

"Tingxue, I will never entrust my fate to any man. Don’t force me."

"Including Yuanlang?"

"Including Yuanlang, including any of my children. The only one I am willing to rely on is myself. Tingxue, my trust in you is already the limit of what I can give to a man. I cannot give more. If you demand more, you are forcing me to lie to you, but I don’t want to lie to you."

Gu Tingxue listened to Xiangjun’s words and laughed.

He stepped up, standing on the same level as her again.

Xiangjun was forced to retreat a step, nearly stumbling, but Gu Tingxue wrapped an arm around her waist, pulling her against him.

He looked down at her mesmerizing eyes, his other hand tracing the softness of her lips.

"Your servant knows Your Highness doesn’t trust men, and Your Highness is right not to. But Your Highness forgets—I am not a man. I am a eunuch."

Gu Tingxue smiled at her, his lips inching closer to hers, his voice soft yet full of temptation. "My dear Highness, since you’ve already made up your mind, why bother courting men? Don’t trust any man, don’t let any man near you. From now on, trust only me. Whatever Your Highness desires, I will place it in your hands."

Xiangjun was left speechless.

Her anger, which had been burning fiercely, now flickered uncertainly.

Gu Tingxue was truly a shameless eunuch.

Weren’t eunuchs supposed to hate being called not a man? Yet he said it so smoothly.

But even if Gu Tingxue placed himself in such a lowly position, Xiangjun still couldn’t agree to him.

She knew that today, she had to settle things with Gu Tingxue once and for all.

If she let him dominate her today, she would never rise again.

So, even if it meant destroying all the effort she had put into Gu Tingxue, even if it meant losing his support from this day forward, she could not submit to him.

This man was mad—he truly could make her his exclusive possession.

"Gu Tingxue, I do not like being controlled. If you want me to live like this, you might as well kill me."

"Is Your Highness threatening me?" Gu Tingxue’s cold, venomous gaze coiled around her, his voice dark. "Do you think I can’t bear to lose you, so you try to manipulate me?"

Xiangjun lightly placed her hand on Gu Tingxue’s shoulder.

"Tingxue, what do you really want? Is confining me what you desire? If I truly became what you wanted, would you even like that version of me?"

Gu Tingxue gripped her chin.

"Your Highness wants my devotion, so naturally, I want yours. Unfortunately, Your Highness refuses to give it to me. I have no choice but to resort to this."

"Tingxue, how do you know I don’t have true feelings for you? If you’re willing, I can promise you this: in public, I am the Emperor’s consort; in private, I am your woman. I will serve you, make you happy, and one day, share the world with you. Isn’t that enough?"

Gu Tingxue said nothing. He stared into Xiangjun’s deceptive eyes, trying to catch a glimpse of genuine affection.

But he saw nothing.

Of course. This woman didn’t even have true feelings for the most noble man in the world—how could she have them for a castrated man like him?

"Tingxue, I must stand higher if we are to go further. When the day comes that I achieve my goals, I will naturally stay with you forever. Trust me, won’t you?"

Gu Tingxue’s smile was full of mockery, devoid of warmth.

"Your Highness doesn’t trust me, yet you ask me to trust you. How can I be sure that when Your Highness holds all the power, you won’t eliminate me, this shameful eunuch? After all, associating with a eunuch is a stain on Your Highness’s reputation that can never be washed clean."

Hearing this, Xiangjun was so angry she almost laughed.

She didn’t trust Gu Tingxue, and Gu Tingxue didn’t trust her.

Perfect. Absolutely perfect.

She had wasted so much effort just to win Gu Tingxue’s heart, but who would have thought his heart was full of holes? In the end, he didn’t truly trust her either.

"Director Gu is right. A consort who can conspire with a eunuch cannot be a person of virtue. It’s only natural that Director Gu doesn’t trust me."

"Why must Your Highness say such heart-wrenching things? Must you hurt me like this?"

"Am I the one hurting you, or are you hurting me? When have I ever considered being with you a stain? It’s your own dark heart that makes you assume the worst of me! You promised to help me, yet time and again, you’ve harbored ulterior motives and schemed against me in secret! I never held it against you, yet you turn around and blame me!"

"I only want you to depend on me. What’s wrong with that?" Gu Tingxue tightly grasped Xiangjun’s hand, his eyes turbulent with emotion. "It was you who made me fall in love with you. Now you regret it?"

"I do regret it. Because you’re blind—can’t you see everything I’ve done for you? Is your love nothing but keeping me locked up in Chengxiang Hall, deaf and blind, nothing but your puppet? If that’s your idea of devotion, I’d rather do without it!"

"What have you done for me? Pretended to be my wife at night?" Gu Tingxue’s voice was bitter. "You demand my devotion, yet you give me none in return. I guard against you, and suddenly it’s my fault?"

"Yes! It is your fault. If you truly cared for me, you wouldn’t be so calculating!"

Gu Tingxue had never met someone so unreasonable.

"Xiangjun, do you even have a heart?"

Xiangjun let out a cold laugh. "Maybe I really don’t have a heart—at least not the kind of undivided, single-minded love you want. Tingxue, when you first met me, you should have known: I will do whatever it takes to achieve my goals, without shame, without restraint. Did you only just realize what kind of person I am?"

Xiangjun locked eyes with Gu Tingxue, her voice venomous. "If Director Gu regrets giving me his heart, it’s not too late to take it back. Don’t cling to me while nitpicking every little thing, only to later accuse me of deceiving your feelings."

---

chapters.title: Then Let Us Part Ways
chapters.content:
Xiangjun’s words were truly harsh.

Each one struck Gu Tingxue’s heart like a knife.

No one had made him feel this much pain, this much rage, in a long time.

Yet Gu Tingxue found that this knife-like agony was almost… addictive.

How could someone make him feel so tormented, so helpless, yet still leave him powerless?

So how could he regret giving his heart to this selfish, calculating woman? In truth, he adored every bit of her nature.

Gu Tingxue fixed his gaze on Xiangjun, staring until her defiance wavered.

By all rights, after saying such cruel things, he should be furious. But he only looked at her deeply, his emotions churning beneath the surface, silent and still.

Had she driven him mad?

"You’re not speaking. What does that mean?"

"I have nothing to say. Your Highness is selfish, opportunistic, ruthless—even I am just another part of your schemes. I know this, and I don’t mind."

Hearing this, Xiangjun’s tone softened instantly.

"I know, Tingxue, you’re different from others. You understand me better than anyone. You promised to support me. Do you remember? You won’t go back on your word, will you?"

Gu Tingxue smiled. Indeed, he was willing to be used by Xiangjun. He would help her reach the heights she desired. He didn’t even mind if she killed him after achieving her ambitions, or if her sons disposed of him once he was no longer useful.

But he couldn’t bear the thought of other men by her side.

He knew Xiangjun too well—she would not tolerate loneliness.

But Gu Tingxue was petty. He could endure being abandoned, but he couldn’t stand the idea of another man standing beside her. The mere thought filled him with a jealousy so fierce it could consume him alive.

He didn’t like gambling.

"What if I do go back on my word? What if I don’t want you to rise to power? What if I just want you to be my woman, and mine alone?"

At these words, the fire in Xiangjun’s heart flared up again.

"Then Tingxue must choose: continue helping me, or become my enemy."

"Your Highness is so unwilling to be with me?"

"I have said before: I will never be controlled by anyone. Director Gu, your influence is vast. If you insist on this, I won’t hesitate to fight you to the death. At worst, I’ll die."

Gu Tingxue’s eyes suddenly turned fierce. He grabbed her hand, his voice venomous. "You’re threatening me with your life?"

"Yes. If you force me, then it’s either you or me."

Gu Tingxue was so angry he could spit blood, but he swallowed the metallic taste in his throat.

He released her hand, and Xiangjun stumbled, nearly falling.

Gu Tingxue’s smile was desolate.

"Your Highness knows full well that I cannot bear to harm you, nor would I become your enemy. Didn’t you already prove that with your life once before? Why must you say such things to hurt me?"

Xiangjun seemed affected by his desolation. Her voice trembled, but she hardened her heart. "In that case, let us part ways for good."

Gu Tingxue’s eyes burned as he stared at Xiangjun, unable to believe she could say those four words so coldly.

*Part ways for good.*

Xiangjun took off the agate bracelet once more.

"Director Gu may wield great power, but I, Xiangjun, am no longer the penniless courtesan from Yangzhou I once was. Even if the road ahead is fraught with peril, I dare to walk it alone."

"Is that so?" Gu Tingxue’s eyes were bloodshot as he glanced at the bracelet, then at Xiangjun’s radiant face. "After Your Highness and I part ways, will you not seek another reliable ally? Who will it be? Xu Huanwen? Zhou Zidou? Or perhaps the Prince of Jin, with whom you had a brief encounter?"

"That is my concern. If Tingxue is determined to part ways with me, why bother asking?"

Xiangjun placed the bracelet into Gu Tingxue’s hand.

She didn’t know what the bracelet meant, but judging by his reaction, it must be important to him.

"If Tingxue is unwilling to help me wholeheartedly, then take back the bracelet. But if you are willing to help me, I will never remove it. Though I may not have the kind of devotion you want, I have always kept my word to those I consider mine."

Gu Tingxue lowered his gaze, his eyes suddenly turning icy, like a venomous snake coiled in the cold.

That chilling stare wrapped around Xiangjun, making her feel as if her throat were being squeezed.

"Your Highness gave up so much to gain my help—even abandoning a child. Now you say you’re giving up, just like that?"

"I am the kind of person who, once decided, never looks back."

After a long silence, Gu Tingxue finally suppressed his surging emotions.

His gaze turned indifferent. Calmly, he took the bracelet from Xiangjun’s hand.

Xiangjun’s heart sank.

Had she lost the gamble?

A wave of loss washed over her—was it because she had failed to tame Gu Tingxue, or because from this day forward, she would lose him?

Lose the only person from her past life who had helped her, the only one who had given her dignity without asking for anything in return.

But Xiangjun knew herself. Once she made a decision, she would never turn back. It was better for them to part now than to become enemies later.

Xiangjun turned her head away and sat back on her throne, refusing to look at Gu Tingxue again.

But in the next instant, she felt a warmth around her wrist.

Gu Tingxue had put the bracelet back on her.

"Your Highness, rest assured. It was I, your servant, who overstepped. I dare not presume again. From now on, I will obey Your Highness completely and support you with unwavering loyalty."

Gu Tingxue fastened the bracelet securely, then turned and left without another word.

Only after he had been gone for a long time did Xiangjun let out a deep sigh, feeling as if that short confrontation had drained all her strength.

She stared blankly at the agate bracelet on her wrist, so lost in thought that she didn’t notice Mengmei entering.

"Your Highness, Director Tingxue has left."

"I know."

Mengmei saw Xiangjun staring at the bracelet, lost in thought, and sighed heavily.

"Your Highness, why did you say those things?"

Mengmei had been waiting outside and had overheard their conversation.

She advised, "Your Highness, given how much Director Tingxue cares for you, if you just coax him a little, he would listen."

"Coaxing might work for a while, but not forever. Sooner or later, he and I would have had this confrontation."

"Your Highness, perhaps you’re overthinking. Director Tingxue would never betray you."

"I don’t want to test human nature, nor do I want to give him the chance to betray me. I’d rather be the one with the power to choose betrayal. Because I know—I would never abandon someone who has helped me."

Mengmei looked at Xiangjun with pity.

Though Mengmei was clever and steady, she was also honest and simple-minded. In her heart, a woman finding a man she could rely on was the best possible outcome.

But Xiangjun insisted on relying only on herself, being the one others depended on. It was exhausting.

"When Tingxue left just now, what did he look like?" Xiangjun asked.

Mengmei sighed. "Director Tingxue… he seemed very heartbroken. Should Your Highness go and comfort him?"

Xiangjun rubbed the agate bracelet on her wrist, her voice calm. "Oh? Didn’t you notice? I’m heartbroken too."

chapters.title: That Damn Slave, Really Holds a Grudge
chapters.content:
Meng Mei was startled by Xiang Jun’s words.

She knew Xiang Jun’s temper well. From childhood to now, Meng Mei had rarely seen Xiang Jun cry.

No matter what happened, Xiang Jun was always full of fighting spirit.

The word "heartbroken" seemed to have nothing to do with this woman.

Meng Mei’s voice even stuttered.

"Noble Consort... do you... truly have feelings for Eunuch Tingxue?"

Xiang Jun tugged at the corner of her mouth and smiled. She lifted her gaze and looked at Meng Mei.

That look was stern and cold, filling Meng Mei with a strong sense of awe.

"True feelings? Meng Mei, you must remember, true feelings are a very dangerous thing. They make you lose your calm, make you panic when you care, make you unable to control your emotions, make you neglect yourself for others, make you trust someone completely, make you give up everything, even your life. In this imperial palace, which of these things is not fatal? With a master like that, wouldn’t you be afraid?"

Meng Mei broke out in goosebumps from Xiang Jun’s words.

Xiang Jun withdrew her gaze and looked at the string of chestnut beads on her wrist.

"Meng Mei, we have been in the palace for nearly four years. Now, it seems I am surrounded by prosperity, favored by the Emperor, the Empress, and the Empress Dowager, and I have even helped my maternal family rise. But since I entered the palace, every step I’ve taken has been a life-and-death struggle. This is the imperial city, where everyone must tread carefully. One wrong step can lead to eternal ruin. Do you understand?"

Meng Mei slowly nodded.

Yes, Noble Consort handled everything with ease, even matters of life and death, brushing them off with a smile and never mentioning them again. Sometimes, Meng Mei even forgot how difficult it had been for Noble Consort to achieve all this.

"Noble Consort..." Meng Mei knelt down beside Xiang Jun, reaching out to hold her hand. "Since true feelings are so dangerous, don’t give yours to others. Just keep our true hearts. I can’t speak for others, but everyone in Chengxiang Hall truly likes you. You treat your servants well, treating us as equals, and we all know it in our hearts. Rest assured, for you, I will risk my life without hesitation. Meng Mei will stay by your side until the very end."

Xiang Jun’s eyes reddened slightly. She choked up a little and gently squeezed Meng Mei’s hand back.

"Good sister, I believe you. But you must also believe me. As my person, you don’t need to risk your life. Remember, at any time, your own life is the most important. I don’t want anyone to die for me."

Meng Mei also teared up.

"Good Noble Consort, with you here, Chengxiang Hall will only get better. No one will die."

Meng Mei wiped the corner of Xiang Jun’s eyes with a handkerchief.

"Noble Consort, don’t be sad anymore."

Xiang Jun quickly steadied her gaze.

She had endured the pain of a cesarean section—what was a little heartache compared to that?

Xiang Jun took a deep breath and slowly stood up. She said to Meng Mei, "I am tired. Let me rest first. Starting tomorrow, we’ll be busy again. My position as a consort is still not secure enough. The Xu family hasn’t risen high enough either. It’s far from the time when I can relax."

...

In the days that followed, Gu Tingxue indeed kept his word and no longer blocked Xiang Jun from seeing the Emperor.

When Xiang Jun had tasks for Gu Tingxue, he still did his best to complete them for her. But he no longer secretly visited Chengxiang Hall to see Xiang Jun.

Occasionally, he would come, but only to see Yuan Lang, hold the child for a while, and leave, not even passing by Xiang Jun’s bedchamber.

Many times, it was only the next day that Xiang Jun learned from Meng Mei that Gu Tingxue had come to Chengxiang Hall the night before.

Previously, when the Emperor came to see Xiang Jun, Gu Tingxue would always find a way to follow, and when it came to delivering rewards to Xiang Jun, he would always take the initiative. Now, all of that was done by others!

For many consecutive times, Xiang Jun couldn’t even catch a glimpse of Gu Tingxue. Seeing him was even harder than seeing the Emperor.

Xiang Jun was both angry and helpless.

"That damn slave, really holds a grudge!"

With no one interfering, Xiang Jun smoothly attended the Emperor’s bed.

The Emperor, having not experienced Xiang Jun’s passion and skills for a long time, the next day when he left, his legs were so weak he almost fell, making the nearby Eunuch Wan not dare to look around.

For a whole month, the Emperor practically lived in Chengxiang Hall, rushing there right after morning court.

Xiang Jun was skilled with the pipa, and Noble Consort Jian was skilled in dance. There were also two adorable children. The palace servants were all sweet-tongued, and everyone was cheerful. Even the servants in Chengxiang Hall didn’t fear the Emperor much, unlike the servants in other palaces who trembled in fear, afraid of making mistakes.

The Emperor, born in this dead and oppressive palace, for the first time felt a place so full of vitality. It made him feel years younger. Often, in Chengxiang Hall, watching the chattering servants and the children Yuan Ji and Yuan Lang crawling all over, the Emperor unexpectedly felt a sense of ordinary happiness.

At this moment, he felt like a wealthy man with everything going his way.

With the Emperor in such a good mood, he naturally treated Xiang Jun’s family well.

So, without waiting for the six-month period, the Emperor promoted Xiang Jun’s elder brother to the Ministry of Rites, making him a sixth-rank principal official.

At this position, Xu Huanwen could attend court and discuss state affairs.

Xu Huanwen had also come to realize that he didn’t care if others said he rose to power through his sister’s influence.

As long as he could rise, the method didn’t matter. In the officialdom, where everyone was driven by ambition, why should he pretend to be noble?

The scholars who entered the imperial examination at the same time as Xu Huanwen, and even those from previous years, all secretly envied him.

A second-class Jinshi, upon entering the Hanlin Academy, became a compiler.

Others had to slowly build seniority in the Hanlin Academy, but in less than two months, he was personally promoted by the Emperor to become a principal official in the Ministry of Rites, a sixth-rank official.

Moreover, he was about to marry the niece of the Empress Dowager and the daughter of a Grand Master of Ceremonies.

His younger sister was the Emperor’s favored Consort Lian in the palace, and he was the maternal uncle of the Fifth Prince.

Without a doubt, everyone knew that this younger brother of the Emperor would soon become a rising star in the court, just like when the Emperor had promoted Song Feijing back then.

With her brother promoted, Xiang Jun naturally reciprocated by expressing her gratitude to the Emperor, making him extremely happy.

Thus, in recent days, the Emperor exclusively favored Noble Consort Lian, and even the newly promoted Royal Noble Consort Xue Jiaojiao could not compare to Xiang Jun’s prominence in the harem.

As she flipped through the records of the Shang Qin Bureau, Royal Noble Consort Xue Jiaojiao’s eyes dimmed considerably.

Such exclusive favor had once been hers alone.

Although she regarded Xiang Jun as a sister, she was still a woman. How could she not be heartbroken when the man she loved showered such favor on another woman?

"Caiwei, how long has it been since I had a proper conversation with the Emperor? When was the last time the Emperor visited Ganlu Palace to see me?"

---

chapters.title: Who Knows What They’re Even Loving
chapters.content:
Seeing the Noble Consort’s sadness, Nurse Caiwei comforted her: "Noble Consort, you are busy managing the affairs of the Six Palaces and truly cannot spare the time. Having Consort Lian attend to the Emperor is not a bad thing—it’s better than having some woman with ill intentions steal the Emperor’s favor..."

Xue Jiaojiao sighed, knowing there was no better solution.

In the past, when Empress Yang controlled the harem, Xue Jiaojiao, as a Noble Consort, had the authority to assist in managing the Six Palaces, but Empress Yang had been unwilling to relinquish any power.

Thus, Xue Jiaojiao had no idea managing the Six Palaces would be so exhausting.

But after waiting so many years, she had finally obtained the power of the central palace. She was unwilling to let others take over.

She wanted to be the Emperor’s wife, to be the queen of the nation. These were responsibilities she should fulfill. She also wanted to show those who thought she was a disastrous beauty that she could be a virtuous empress.

"You’re right. Fortunately, it’s Xiang Jun. Forget it..."

Xue Jiaojiao thought that Xiang Jun was loyal to her, willing to protect her with her life, and she had also protected Xiang Jun during her difficult childbirth. Such a bond was something others could not compare to.

If it were another woman, she would truly have to be on guard.

Xiang Jun naturally knew how conspicuous her exclusive favor was, so she would often visit the Royal Noble Consort’s palace.

Seeing that the Royal Noble Consort had no intention of sharing her authority, Xiang Jun did not take the initiative to ask for it either. She simply served the Royal Noble Consort faithfully.

When the Royal Noble Consort was reviewing the accounts, Xiang Jun would pour her water, fan her, or bring Yuan Ji and Yuan Lang over to play with Yuan Ze.

Watching the three children babbling and playing together in the courtyard, Xue Jiaojiao couldn’t help but sigh. "No wonder the Emperor likes to go to your Chengxiang Hall. Even I feel relaxed when I’m with you all."

"Noble Consort, the Emperor always goes to my place. Do you blame me?"

"Why would I blame you? It’s the Emperor who favors you."

"Noble Consort, you are far more important to me than the Emperor. If you dislike it, next time the Emperor comes, I’ll drive him away."

Xiang Jun spoke sincerely, but the Royal Noble Consort only found it amusing and helpless. Pinching Xiang Jun’s nose, she said, "You’re a mother now. Why do you still act like a child? The Emperor is the Son of Heaven. How can you drive him away?"

"Noble Consort, don’t blame the Emperor either. Perhaps he sees that you are busy managing the harem and have many things to handle, so he lets me attend to him for now."

When Xiang Jun brought up the matter of managing the Six Palaces, the Royal Noble Consort recalled that the Empress Dowager and the Emperor had also ordered Xiang Jun to assist in managing the harem.

The Royal Noble Consort asked Xiang Jun, "Now that you also have the authority to assist in managing the Six Palaces, how about I give you some tasks to do?"

How could Xiang Jun dare to accept?

Even if Xue Jiaojiao was not someone who enjoyed wielding power, she had just become the mistress of the harem and had not yet secured her position. If she were to share her power now, how could she not feel resentment toward Xiang Jun?

This was human nature.

Therefore, it was not yet the right time for Xiang Jun to take on palace authority.

She had to make the Royal Noble Consort beg her for help, rather than reluctantly sharing it like this.

"The Empress Dowager and the Emperor did instruct me, but as you know, Sister, my background is not noble. How could I possibly manage so many high-born consorts and concubines in the palace? If I truly took on the palace authority, I fear I would be resented to death. Noble Consort, please spare your poor sister. If you really want to give me tasks, let them be unimportant ones, all right?"

Hearing Xiang Jun say this, Xue Jiaojiao laughed.

"You just know how to avoid work. Alright, with me here, you don’t need to worry about it."

Seeing how obedient Xiang Jun was, the Royal Noble Consort, under the pretext that Xiang Jun’s palace was raising two imperial sons, doubled the allowances for Chengxiang Hall.

Delighted by this unexpected gain, Xiang Jun happily returned.

As soon as she boarded the palanquin, Meng Mei couldn’t help but ask, "Noble Consort, why didn’t you ask the Royal Noble Consort for some tasks to do? We’ve always wanted to place our own people in the palace. Having palace authority would make things much easier."

"Even though the Empress Dowager and the Emperor have ordered me to assist in managing the Six Palaces, if I were to really seize the Royal Noble Consort’s authority, the Emperor would not be happy. He would only think that I am like those women who go mad for power, and he would be even less likely to help me."

"But the Empress Dowager is on your side."

"Even if the Empress Dowager wants to help me, if I make a scene, she will think I am incompetent. So, this matter is not urgent. We must take it slow."

...

In the following days, Xiang Jun focused on serving the Emperor and found opportunities to have her father promoted again.

The Emperor also felt that since Xiang Jun was his beloved consort, it would be a loss of face for him if her father remained a mere county magistrate. Thus, he gave Xiang Jun’s father an idle sixth-rank position as an assistant prefect.

As for palace affairs, although Xiang Jun held the title of assisting in managing the Six Palaces, she did nothing.

However, whenever she encountered injustices in the palace, she would step in to uphold justice, earning herself a good reputation.

Over time, she gained a reputation for sympathizing with the servants and treating all palace servants equally.

Apart from this, Xiang Jun did not say or do anything extra.

Even the picky Emperor could not find any fault with Xiang Jun, only feeling that his Consort Lian was truly a person who did not seek power and was sincerely pure-hearted.

Because the former Empress Yang had managed the harem extremely strictly, even after her death, the palace servants remained obedient for the time being.

Without understanding the new Royal Noble Consort’s management methods, everyone continued to work diligently.

Thus, in the early days of the Royal Noble Consort’s management of the harem, apart from being a bit tired, no major incidents occurred, as everyone was still feeling their way.

Seeing that both the front court and the harem were running smoothly, the Emperor once again brought up his desire to perform the Fengshan ceremony at Mount Tai during morning court.

However, the officials still disagreed.

Although they were not as direct as before in saying the Emperor was unworthy, they still subtly advised him to reconsider, warning him not to damage his fortune.

Wasn’t this still saying the Emperor was unworthy?

Especially the Emperor’s royal brothers and the generals in the military—none of them spoke kindly.

Naturally, the Emperor was angry and gradually became impatient with the Royal Noble Consort.

The Emperor now completely ignored all consorts except Xiang Jun.

Although Xiang Jun served him well, the main reason was that he was giving the Royal Noble Consort the cold shoulder.

Xiang Jun felt that the Emperor probably hoped the Royal Noble Consort would understand his hints, but at the same time, he was worried that if she truly understood the intricacies, she would not be as simple as he imagined. Hence, his behavior was so awkward.

This damn Emperor, truly wanted everything and was impossible to serve.

In the blink of an eye, two months passed, and the Royal Noble Consort finally realized something was wrong.

The Emperor had deposed Empress Yang to make her the Empress.

But now, so much time had passed since Empress Yang’s death, why had the Emperor not brought up the matter of enthroning a new empress?

Xue Jiaojiao had originally thought that after defeating Empress Yang, she had become the mistress of the harem and was finally the Emperor’s rightful wife in name and reality.

But the Emperor not only had not made her Empress, but also left her to guard an empty bed every day. Moreover, because she was not the Empress but only the Royal Noble Consort, the Emperor did not even need to visit her Ganlu Palace on the first and fifteenth of each month.

She seemed to have become nothing more than a steward of the harem.

Xiang Jun learned of the Royal Noble Consort’s secret sorrow and knew her chance to pledge loyalty was coming.

Even if Xiang Jun did not remind her, according to the original plot, General Wang would soon realize why the Emperor was reluctant to enthrone an empress.

It would be better for Xiang Jun to do this favor.

Thus, when Xue Jiaojiao once again sighed over the accounts and tentatively asked Xiang Jun about the Emperor’s recent health, Xiang Jun bluntly told the Royal Noble Consort that the Emperor was displacing his anger over the Fengshan ceremony onto her.

Xue Jiaojiao seemed shocked.

"How could that be? The Emperor is not that petty."

Xiang Jun almost couldn’t control her expression.

The Emperor wasn’t petty?

The Emperor was just good at enduring, but in his heart, he held grudges more deeply and was far more narrow-minded than anyone.

Xiang Jun truly felt that this couple did not understand each other at all.

Who knew what they were even loving after loving so deeply for so many years.

chapters.title: The Coronation of the Empress
chapters.content:
"Your Highness, I am just a concubine in the harem and do not understand these matters. But my brother is an official in the Ministry of Rites. He told me that His Majesty truly wants to go to Mount Tai for the Fengshan ceremony. I think His Majesty may not be stingy, but... if Your Highness can help His Majesty resolve his worries, he will know that you and he are as one, and he will naturally feel at ease to bestow the title of Empress upon you."

"But... the harem must not interfere in politics..."

Seeing that Consort Xue Jiaojiao was still hesitating, Xiangjun said again, "Your Highness, the Emperor does not love you any less; he is just afraid that someone else is more important to you than he is. In this matter, you must not stand on the side of the powerful officials and military officers. You must stand on the Emperor's side. This is not interfering in politics; it is just a wife caring for her husband."

Sure enough, those in love have their own way of thinking. Hearing Xiangjun say this, the Noble Consort immediately believed her.

"Yes, those people support me as Empress but oppose the Emperor's Fengshan ceremony. Naturally, the Emperor would feel that I am not of one mind with him. No wonder these days, the Emperor has been so cold to me. It turns out... it was my fault for hurting the Emperor's feelings."

Xue Jiaojiao did not believe that the Emperor was petty, narrow-minded, arrogant, or vain, but she did believe that the Emperor cared for her.

Xiangjun held her teacup and drank, concealing her complex emotions.

She was afraid she might not be able to resist rolling her eyes.

Indeed, those in love have their own ideas, which she could not understand.

...

Under Xiangjun's guidance, Consort Xue secretly contacted General Wang and expressed her hope that General Wang would support the Emperor's Fengshan ceremony.

Thus, on the Mid-Autumn Festival, General Wang presented a white deer, a symbol of good fortune, to the Emperor...

Xu Huanwen, as an official of the Ministry of Rites, immediately declared that this heavenly omen signified peace and prosperity, implying that the current Son of Heaven was blessed by the heavens. Therefore, our Emperor should perform the Fengshan ceremony.

The Emperor was greatly pleased. It was said that during the morning court session that day, the Emperor said "good" three times in a row.

The matter of the Fengshan ceremony was finally settled. The Ministry of Rites began preparations, waiting for the Emperor to set off for Mount Tai in March of the following year.

Next, the officials began writing memorials, stating that the harem could not be without a mistress for a day, and suggested that the Emperor establish an Empress as soon as possible.

The Emperor finally agreed in court to establish a new Empress soon.

"Tingxue..."

In the Taiji Hall, the Emperor looked at General Wang's memorial requesting the early establishment of an Empress, and a shadow passed over his eyes.

"Was it really Noble Consort Xue who asked General Wang to present the auspicious omen?" the Emperor asked.

"Yes."

"I do not know now whether General Wang is my subject or Noble Consort Xue's."

At this moment, Gu Tingxue couldn't help but admire Xiangjun. A woman from a humble background in Yangzhou, through her own relentless study, had actually developed such a keen political sense.

With just a few words, she had won the favor and trust of Noble Consort Xue and sown discord between the Emperor, General Wang, and Noble Consort Xue.

It was a pity she couldn't become Empress.

Although Xiangjun had done this without informing Gu Tingxue, Gu Tingxue understood the significance of her actions and was willing to help her succeed.

"Your Majesty, General Wang and Noble Consort Xue have a brother-sister bond from growing up together. It is not surprising that Noble Consort Xue can influence General Wang; this has happened before."

The Emperor's face darkened further. Seeing his expression, Gu Tingxue knew the Emperor was about to lose his temper.

But it was better to suppress the anger than to vent it.

Only by suppressing it would the Emperor remember it deeply in his heart.

Gu Tingxue added, "However, General Wang is defending the northern border. The Northern Mongols have been peaceful for so many years out of fear of General Wang. Your Majesty cannot be too harsh on General Wang. The turmoil in the south has just ended, and the north cannot be in chaos. Your Majesty needs more time to cultivate his own generals. Furthermore... Noble Consort Xue and Your Majesty are of one mind. She knows what Your Majesty is anxious about and thinks what Your Majesty thinks. Therefore, General Wang's loyalty to Noble Consort Xue is also loyalty to Your Majesty."

On the surface, Gu Tingxue was speaking for Noble Consort Xue, but in reality, he was driving a wedge between her and the Emperor.

Sure enough, the Emperor's eyes darkened further, but he suppressed his anger because of Gu Tingxue's words.

Gu Tingxue was right; the north could not be in chaos.

He was the Emperor; the stability of the empire was always more important than a woman.

Thus, Emperor Yanqing heavily closed the memorial and said in a low voice, "Then, Tingxue, you shall deliver the imperial decree to confer the title of Empress. Announce to the world that I will establish Noble Consort Xue Jiaojiao as Empress."

"Your servant obeys."

...

After receiving the imperial decree to confer the title of Empress, the first thing Xue Jiaojiao did was to call Xiangjun to Chengxiang Palace to talk.

Xue Jiaojiao held the imperial decree in her arms and shed tears.

"Sister Xiangjun, I have loved the Emperor for many years. Now, I have finally become his true wife."

Xiangjun felt disdainful in her heart. What was so happy about being a man's wife? It was worth crying for joy only if one became a man's master.

But of course, Xiangjun could not ruin the mood. She quickly wiped her tears with a handkerchief, pretending to be happy for Xue Jiaojiao.

"Seeing my sister's wish fulfilled, Xiangjun is also happy for you."

...

The coronation ceremony of Empress Xue was extremely grand.

For several days, the entire palace was busy preparing for the coronation. Even Xiangjun, as the assistant manager of the Six Palaces, was pulled in to handle many tasks.

On the morning of the coronation, the Honglu Temple set up the book case, node case, certificate case, and treasure case in front of the throne. The Ministry of Rites arranged the wild geese and gifts below the Danbi Platform. The colorful palanquin was set up outside the Bao'tian Gate. The Imperial Household Department arranged the Empress's retinue, chariots, and gifts south of the palanquin.

The palace servants protected the imperial decree, certificate, and treasure with umbrellas and canopies as they walked out of the central gate of the imperial palace. General Wang was the chief envoy for the conferment, and Gu Tingxue and the Assistant Minister of Rites were the deputy envoys, following behind.

The concubines of the harem and the commandery princesses, dressed in heavy court attire, stood on both sides, watching the Empress, dressed in auspicious clothes, slowly enter the main hall under the support of the female officials and palace servants.

Xiangjun had thought that being Empress was nothing special, but seeing such a grand scene, she couldn't help but feel envious.

It was so luxurious and glorious.

One should live a life with such glory at least once to make it worthwhile.

Seeing the Emperor and Empress standing hand in hand, gazing deeply into each other's eyes, Xiangjun felt extremely jealous.

But she was not jealous of their deep gaze or hand-holding; she was jealous that they stood the highest.

Xiangjun averted her gaze, and her eyes fell on Gu Tingxue, the deputy envoy for the conferment, standing behind the Emperor and Empress.

Today, Gu Tingxue was the deputy envoy, so he was wearing official attire.

The purple robe made him look even paler, and with his lips as red as blood, he exuded an alluring charm. The jade belt accentuated his slender waist, making Xiangjun's heart burn with anxiety.

That damn slave, he didn't even glance at her, wasting all her efforts to dress up so beautifully today.

Gu Tingxue kept his eyes forward, and although he felt Xiangjun's gaze on him from the corner of his eye, he showed no change in expression and had no intention of looking at her.

Xiangjun was so angry that she gnashed her teeth.

Suddenly, she felt a gaze on her and looked over to see Zhou Zidu, who was in charge of the guard, looking at her.

Xiangjun immediately changed her expression and smiled at Zhou Zidu.

Zhou Zidu's face changed slightly, seeming to blush, but he quickly looked away.

Xiangjun was satisfied.

Indeed, not everyone was blind.

Xiangjun, feeling pleased with herself, decided to look at Gu Tingxue again to satisfy her craving. Unexpectedly, this time she met Gu Tingxue's gaze.

Gu Tingxue looked at her coldly. When he saw her looking at him, he indifferently averted his gaze, as if disdaining her.

Xiangjun became even angrier.

What was he disdaining? Was she not beautiful enough today?

chapters.title: Let the Sisters in the Harem Be Happy
chapters.content:
Xiangjun waited angrily until the ceremony ended and everyone dispersed.

She had thought to take this opportunity to say a few words to Gu Tingxue, but Gu Tingxue walked away without so much as a glance, as if he hadn't seen her at all.

Xiangjun was furious. She returned to Chengxiang Palace in a huff and threw all the pearl and jade hairpins from her head onto the ground, throwing a big tantrum.

Outside, Xiao Luzi asked Mengmei, "Mengmei jiejie, should I go find Lord Tingxue and ask him to come see Her Highness? Her Highness's temper has been so bad lately, and we really can't soothe her."

"If you can bring him here, then do so. If not, Her Highness will only get angrier."

Xiao Luzi thought about it and realized that their mistress was very concerned with face. He didn't dare mention it again.

Everyone in Chengxiang Palace lived in fear until the Emperor promoted Xu Huanwen again, and Her Highness became pleased once more. Only then did the palace servants breathe a sigh of relief.

However, after Xue Jiaojiao became Empress, the Emperor began to favor Xiangjun even more.

Not only did he bestow gifts upon Xiangjun, but he also gave many rewards to her family. He even specially sent imperial eunuchs to arrange a marriage for Xiangjun's brother.

This kind of favor was only given to a truly beloved concubine.

How could Xiangjun not understand the Emperor's intentions?

Empress Xue held onto the power of the harem and would not let go. She was also entangled with General Wang and had a beloved son, the Fourth Prince Yuanze. Someone in the harem was needed to balance the Empress's power.

Therefore, Xiangjun deliberately sought more favor, much more fiercely than before, determined to be the Emperor's useful tool.

Xiangjun even deliberately said in front of the Empress that the Emperor favored her because the Empress was busy with the affairs of the Six Palaces and was truly exhausted, so the Emperor pitied Her Majesty.

Empress Xue also felt distressed and began to doubt the meaning of being Empress. Every day, besides handling palace affairs, she dealt with various matters.

At first, she had the joy of holding power, but later, only the sorrow of an empty bed remained.

If she had entered the palace like this from the beginning, she could have endured the loneliness of the deep palace.

But she had been the most favored concubine for ten years. How could she endure such loneliness?

"I used to always hope that one day I could become Empress, to be the Emperor's wife. But now that my wish has come true, I feel it's not as good as when I was just a favored concubine."

Lady Caiwei advised, "Your Majesty, doesn't Concubine Lian have the right to assist in managing the Six Palaces? Why doesn't Your Majesty assign her some tasks? You can also relax, and Concubine Lian won't always be clinging to His Majesty."

Although Lady Caiwei was very grateful to Concubine Lian for saving the Noble Consort in the past, she still felt that Concubine Lian was being unreasonable with her constant seeking of favor.

The Empress hesitated, "But I am the Empress..."

"Your Majesty, the Empress also needs to use people. You also need to raise the Fourth Prince. It's fine to let others handle some matters."

...

The next day, Xiangjun was assigned the token for the Shang Qin Bureau.

When she learned that the Empress had put her in charge of the Shang Qin Bureau, Xiangjun was somewhat confused.

Was this a coincidence, or was the Empress deliberately hinting at her?

Now that Xiangjun was the sole recipient of the Emperor's favor, managing the Shang Qin Bureau meant she had to take on responsibilities. She could no longer seek favor every day; otherwise, she would not be fulfilling her duty to assist in managing the Six Palaces.

After all, the Shang Qin Bureau required the Emperor to distribute his favors evenly.

So, if Xiangjun managed the Shang Qin Bureau, she could no longer always cling to the Emperor, let alone maintain her exclusive favor. Otherwise, before long, the officials of the imperial court would start writing memorials to criticize her.

If this move was thought up by the Empress herself, Xiangjun would have to admire the Empress.

"Your Highness, what do you plan to do? His Majesty is currently most favorable to our Chengxiang Palace," Mengmei asked.

Xiangjun smiled and indifferently played with the palace token in her hand.

"Since Her Majesty the Empress has put me in charge of the Shang Qin Bureau, I must make sure all the sisters in the harem are happy. His Majesty's favors should be shared by everyone."

After all, His Majesty's favors were not anything good.

Xiangjun had already arranged for her brother and father. With the Xu family being heavily favored by the Emperor, she might as well take this opportunity to push the Emperor towards others in a reasonable manner.

She only needed to be the Emperor's useful tool.

...

A small eunuch named Li Fu from Ganlu Palace secretly made his way to the Si Li Monitor.

Gu Tingxue had just changed his clothes and was preparing to leave the palace when he saw Li Fu approaching. He immediately asked, "What task has Her Majesty the Empress assigned to Concubine Lian?"

Li Fu boasted of his merit, "Following Lord Gu's instructions, this servant advised Lady Caiwei. Now, Lady Caiwei has already sent someone to deliver the palace token of the Shang Qin Bureau to Chengxiang Palace."

...

Without Xiangjun desperately seeking favor, and with her careful arrangements, the other sisters in the harem also gradually began to receive the Emperor's favors.

Her Majesty the Empress thought that with Xiangjun having some tasks to do, she wouldn't always be clinging to the Emperor.

But without Xiangjun, there were others seeking favor.

If it wasn't Consort Jian dancing, it was Noble Consort Jiang reciting poetry.

Or some unknown little talent would be singing by the Qianli Pool and happen to be heard by the Emperor.

The Emperor was also surprised. He had never realized that there were so many talented and artistic concubines in his harem, and each one seemed to know how to read the situation.

In the end, within a month, the Empress still only saw the Emperor twice.

As the selection of new concubines was about to begin, and new people would soon enter the palace, Empress Xue sat in front of the mirror and sighed, asking Lady Caiwei, "Caiwei, do you think I have grown old?"

Before Lady Caiwei could respond, a voice came from outside.

"How could Her Majesty the Empress be old? Your Majesty has a phoenix-like grace that no one in the palace can compare to."

It was Xiangjun, coming to Ganlu Palace in high spirits.

"Sister has arrived. Why wasn't I informed?" the Empress asked in surprise.

"You were informed, but Her Majesty was too engrossed in looking at the mirror to hear it."

Xue Jiaojiao felt a bit embarrassed and pulled Xiangjun to sit on the wooden couch to talk.

Xiangjun was supposed to report on palace affairs to Empress Xue every other day, so her visit was not surprising.

After discussing palace affairs, Xiangjun noticed the dark circles under Empress Xue's eyes and couldn't help but advise, "Your Majesty, why did you sigh today? Did you not sleep well last night?"

Empress Xue gave a bitter smile, "It's nothing. It's just that I feel the Emperor treats me differently than before."

"Your Majesty, you must not belittle yourself. Your relationship with the Emperor is unparalleled. If I may be so bold, I think it is only after you became Empress that you and the Emperor are not as close as before."

Hearing Xiangjun say this, Empress Xue's eyes reddened.

"I don't know why it has become like this..."

"Perhaps, Your Majesty cares too much about the title of Empress and has forgotten that you are the one His Majesty loves." Xiangjun held Empress Xue's hand and advised, "Your Majesty, ask yourself: do you want to be the Empress, or do you want to be the Emperor's wife?"

That day, Xiangjun stayed in Ganlu Palace for the entire afternoon.

After Xiangjun left, the lights in Ganlu Palace remained lit all night.

chapters.title: Consort Lian's Phoenix-like Grace
chapters.content:
The next day was the 15th, a grand occasion, and the Emperor would certainly visit Ganlu Palace.

By the 16th, rumors spread through the palace that on that day, Her Majesty the Empress had dressed as the Luo River Goddess and danced under the moonlight in Ganlu Palace.

It was said that when the Empress was still a young maiden, she had already captivated the capital with her Luo River Goddess dance.

Perhaps it had awakened the Emperor’s buried memories, for in the days that followed, he stopped summoning concubines with palace tokens and stayed night after night in Ganlu Palace with the Empress.

Dream Mei was intensely curious: "It was just dressing as the Luo River Goddess—how did she manage to ensnare the Emperor? In this entire harem, who can dance better than Noble Consort Jian?"

Ever since the Empress and Emperor had reconciled, the Empress had entrusted Xiangjun with many minor but tedious palace duties. Though none were particularly important, Xiangjun still managed them meticulously.

In the harem, even the smallest matters could have great consequences.

Xiangjun flipped through the annual records, casually remarking, "This has nothing to do with the Luo River Goddess. You wouldn’t understand—this is called 'white moonlight.'"

She had come across the term in a book and found it remarkably fitting.

Xiangjun explained to Dream Mei: "Her Majesty the Empress has captured the Emperor’s memories, reminding him of the purest emotions from his most innocent years. At his age, isolated and alone, he begins to long for the purest kind of love. Besides, when a man of his years falls in love, it’s like an old house catching fire—impossible to extinguish."

"What will you do, Your Highness?"

"Next month is the imperial selection. What can I do? I’ll just watch the show."

After the selection, the harem buzzed with activity once more.

This year, the Emperor had chosen only eight new consorts, most from humble backgrounds. The few with notable family status were there only because their fathers were officials the Emperor currently favored.

It was clear the Emperor had arranged it this way to prevent the harem from colluding with the imperial court.

If Xiangjun were the Empress, she would have been immediately alert. Unfortunately, their Empress was so lost in the Emperor’s affection that she remained blissfully unaware.

These new consorts were more curious about Consort Lian of Chengxiang Hall than they were about the Empress.

This woman of humble Jiangnan origins had entered the palace half a year ago and been granted the title of Concubine. After falling ill for over a year, when everyone assumed she would lose favor, she had recovered and immediately regained the Emperor’s favor. Within two years, she had borne a child and been promoted to Consort, enjoying unparalleled favor.

So, when Xiangjun passed by in her palanquin, these new consorts stood to the side, watching as the graceful and radiant Consort Lian departed, their hearts filled with admiration and surging hope.

Perhaps one of them, too, could one day rise to great heights like Consort Lian and bring honor to their family.

However, a month passed, and not a single new consort had seen the Emperor.

Even the mighty Empress, day after day, charmed the Emperor so thoroughly that he stayed in Ganlu Palace every night.

The Emperor seemed to have rediscovered the feeling of first love, returning to the days when he had favored only Xue Jiaojiao. The two were inseparable, whispering sweet nothings to each other daily.

Xiangjun wasn’t worried. After all, the Emperor and Empress were the male and female leads of the original story. In the book, their relationship was just like this—when they were good, it was earth-shattering, and when they fought, it was world-ending.

Anyway, the Emperor and Empress wouldn’t stay happy for long before another conflict arose. Xiangjun had no intention of breaking them up.

Gradually, rumors began to spread in the palace that the Empress was jealous.

Among the high-ranking consorts, Virtuous Consort De and Noble Consort Shu had children but no favor, while Consort Yue was frail and rarely left Nanxun Hall. So, some of the lower-ranking consorts began to pay visits to Consort Lian’s palace.
