But remembering that Consort Lian disliked her crying, she quickly bit her lip, preventing the tears from falling.

Seeing that the white palace maid understood the severity, Xiangjun's anger subsided a bit.

"How do you know about herbs?" Xiangjun asked, somewhat curious.

"Replying to Consort Lian, when I was a child, my family was poor. My father and mother died early, and it was hard for my brother to raise me. So I often went to the mountains to pick herbs and sell them to the town's pharmacy. Over time, I learned a bit about herbal medicine."

"Wasn't your brother a minor official in the yamen before? Raising you shouldn't have been that difficult."

"Mistress may not know, but my brother can eat a whole bucket of rice in one meal. His small salary wasn't even enough for his own meals. I had to be thrifty to ensure both my brother and I had enough to eat. Sometimes, we had no choice but to dig wild vegetables in the mountains to eat. Once, I dug up a ginseng and sold it to the pharmacy for a lot of money! That's when I started learning to identify herbs."

After saying this, the white palace maid embarrassedly added, "I must have made Mistress laugh."

Xiangjun, however, was quite indifferent. "Why would I laugh at you? You know how to care for your brother. At such a young age, you knew how to find ways to earn money to support your family. That proves you're a good girl."

And what was there to laugh about in digging wild vegetables? Before Xiangjun had sold herself to the Xu family as a skinny horse, she had fought dogs for food in the slop bucket. She had no right to laugh at others.

Hearing the mistress praise her as a good girl, the white palace maid beamed with joy, lowering her head and smiling happily.

Seeing the white palace maid's carefree and artless demeanor, Xiangjun and Meng Mei exchanged another glance.

They finally understood why Wang Wanyi bullied the white palace maid.

With Wang Wanyi's background, she probably despised such "vulgar" yet "cheerful" girls the most.

In her previous life, Xiangjun had experienced this as well. Back then, she hadn't learned the rules, and the other concubines in the palace all disliked her, feeling that having such a woman as a fellow concubine was an insult. They had given her a hard time.

However, Xiangjun had a fiercer temper than the white palace maid. When bullied, she would fight back tooth and nail, so those people eventually stopped bothering to argue with her to avoid getting bitten by a dog.

Xiangjun thought for a moment, then said to Meng Mei, "Give the white palace maid some things to take back, the same as last time."

"Yes."

"You can go back early as well. I won't keep you."

The white palace maid looked at the two small boxes Meng Mei brought, her eyes widening. Meng Mei, seeing her curiosity, opened one for her to see.

As the white palace maid expected, there was indeed silver inside.

Overjoyed, the white palace maid thanked Xiangjun. Then, unable to help herself, she asked, "Mistress... can I... can I come see you again? I like Mistress. I want to see you more often."

Xiangjun laughed in exasperation, "Do you want to see me, or do you want my silver?"

The white palace maid stammered, "Ca... can't I want both?"

Xiangjun, for the first time in her life, felt she had met her match. Looking at the white palace maid's sparkling eyes, Xiangjun's heart softened for once.

"White palace maid, did you attend the Emperor last night?"

The white palace maid nodded shyly.

"Did the Emperor like you?"

The white palace maid's face turned even redder. Lowering her head, she said, "The Emperor didn't say much to me."

"What did you say to the Emperor?"

"I remembered my brother's advice. The Emperor is the Son of Heaven. In front of the Emperor, one must not speak recklessly, so I didn't dare to speak recklessly."

Xiangjun stared motionlessly at the white palace maid, deep in thought.

In her previous life, had the white palace maid never been favored by the Emperor, or had she died early?

That day in the Imperial Garden, she had so openly given a sachet to Gu Tingxue. Xiangjun didn't believe no one else had seen it. If someone with ill intentions had followed and seen it, and then reported it after the white palace maid attended the Emperor...

Given the Emperor's temper, Gu Tingxue was more valuable to use, and since he hadn't accepted the sachet, even if the Emperor was displeased, he wouldn't blame Gu Tingxue but would blame the white palace maid instead.

And the white palace maid's brother was supposed to be someone the Emperor wanted to promote. Yet, later on, he wasn't given any important position. It was possible that the white palace maid had caused trouble in the palace.

As for Gu Tingxue, he was the kind of person who, even when he had some affection for Xiangjun, could still scheme against her, getting her sent to the Palace Correction Office for punishment. It was likely that even if he knew what the Emperor was going to do, he wouldn't care about the life or death of a mere palace maid.

So, after much thought, Xiangjun concluded that in her previous life, the white palace maid had probably died quietly not long after entering the palace.

chapters.title: Seizing Palace Authority
chapters.content:
Bai Cainü blinked her large, doe-like eyes, making Xiangjun feel a flutter in her heart.

"Your Highness... is there something on my face?"

"You don’t need to address me as Your Highness anymore. Just continue calling me as you did before."

"Ah?" Bai Cainü was confused but still nodded. "Oh..."

Xiangjun sighed and said, "In the future, when you’re with His Majesty, just say whatever is on your mind. Don’t worry about being crude or fear his reproach. Speak your mind—His Majesty will appreciate it."

Bai Cainü was surprised. "Really...? I’m afraid His Majesty won’t like me. My brother said that if I make a mistake, His Majesty will blame him too."

"He won’t. There’s no one like you in the palace. His Majesty will find it novel and amusing."

Bai Cainü smiled happily and nodded again.

After a moment’s thought, Xiangjun added, "The other day in the Imperial Garden, when you gave the sachet to Minister Gu, I doubt I was the only one who saw it. Remember, walls have ears. If His Majesty ever asks you about it, do you know how to respond?"

Bai Cainü panicked and said nervously, "I... I’ll beg His Majesty for forgiveness, say I didn’t understand the rules... I know I was wrong, I won’t dare do it again."

"Don’t say that. Tell the truth. Remember, if His Majesty asks, say that you embroidered the sachet yourself to save money, that you couldn’t bear to spend money on a gift, and that even the herbs inside were ones you secretly picked from the Imperial Garden yourself. Understand?"

"Ah?" Bai Cainü thought for a moment but, trusting Xiangjun’s judgment, nodded obediently. "I’ll remember."

"Alright, go. Don’t come bother me unless it’s important." Xiangjun paused, then added, "Come back when you’re out of money to ask for rewards."

...

After Bai Cainü left, Xiangjun called over the palace attendants who had been laughing earlier.

"Do you resent me for silencing you on someone else’s behalf?"

They all shook their heads. Xiyu quickly said, "She is still a palace maid, a mistress of the palace. Mocking a mistress is indeed our fault. It’s only right that Your Highness is angry."

"I don’t blame you. With my personality, it’s not surprising that those under me act a little arrogantly. But you must understand when it’s appropriate to be bold and when it’s not. There are things I can do that you cannot. In this imperial harem, the hierarchy presses down layer by layer, each vying against the other. Though I’ve reached the rank of consort, there are still mistresses above me. If one day you make a grave mistake, I may want to protect you but be powerless to do so."

"Yes, Your Highness, we understand our mistake."

"Chengxiang Palace has indeed grown lazy. Starting today, all of you must be on your toes. Anyone from Chengxiang Palace must not give anyone outside a chance to criticize us. Whatever you do, you must act with reason. Understood?"

The attendants all agreed.

Xiangjun dismissed the others, keeping only Mengmei, Xiyu, and Xiaoluzhi.

She beckoned Xiaoluzhi over and pinched his chin, examining him. "Why hit him so hard?"

"Your Highness was angry. It’s only right that this slave be punished."

Xiangjun shot Xiaoluzhi a look and turned to Xiyu. "Xiyu, did you hear that? Xiaoluzhi is indirectly criticizing you."

Xiyu had only touched her own face earlier, acting cleverly.

Xiaoluzhi and Xiyu stifled their laughter. Xiangjun continued, "Today, I reprimanded the attendants for a reason. Chengxiang Palace is about to undertake a major task. Control yourselves and those under you. Be careful and prudent. Don’t let the mistakes of your subordinates ruin my plans."

Xiaoluzhi was curious. "Your Highness, what is Chengxiang Palace going to do?"

Xiangjun smiled at Xiaoluzhi. "Yesterday, when you went to Liangyi Palace to punish Wang Wanyin’s attendants, did it feel good?"

Xiaoluzhi had once offended Wang Wanyin, the noble consort, which cost him a good position and got him sent away.

"It felt great."

"Good. Just wait. I’ll get you a dust-whisk to hold sooner or later."

Xiaoluzhi could barely contain his excitement. No one in Chengxiang Palace could resist stirring up trouble.

"Your Highness, you mean...?"

"Naturally, we’re going to seize palace authority. This harem must be firmly in my grasp."

...

After a few days of rest, the news of Jiang Guiren from Yan’ying Palace and Deng Cainü from Hanbing Palace being with child spread through the Six Palaces.

His Majesty was naturally overjoyed, and the other consorts were envious.

Over the past year, the Emperor had rarely favored any consort except the Empress and Consort Lian. It was surprising that two had managed to conceive.

Moreover, these two had been personally promoted by Xiangjun after she took over the management of the Shangqin Bureau.

Upon hearing the news, the first thing Xiangjun did was summon the head of the Shangshi Bureau. She gave him a stern talking-to, using both threats and incentives, ordering him to serve with the utmost care.

Now that the Shangshi Bureau was under her control, food was the easiest area for problems to arise. If anything happened to the imperial heir due to negligence in the Shangshi Bureau, even if His Majesty didn’t blame her, he would consider her incompetent.

In addition, Xiangjun ordered people to keep a close watch on Yan’ying Palace and Hanbing Palace. Any irregularities were to be reported immediately.

The harem was not as stable as it appeared. The incident with Bai Cainü showed how difficult it was to live peacefully in the palace.

Now, the Emperor and Empress were in a sweet phase. Although two low-ranking consorts were pregnant, His Majesty was happy but not overly concerned, as these were not his first children. After bestowing some casual rewards, he paid no further attention.

The consorts still had to rely on the Empress to look after them.

The previous Empress Yang had taken care of the pregnant consorts, but Empress Xue was different. She was kind and would not harm others’ children, but her love was too important to her. She couldn’t see the difficulties of other consorts and only believed that the harem had its rules, and everyone would follow them.

But the harem could not be left unmanaged.

The palace attendants, seeing that the current mistress was incapable, began to harbor their own ideas. Many places saw cases of servants overpowering their masters.

Although Xiangjun had recently dealt with the attendants of Liangyi Palace, her authority was limited, and she couldn’t manage everything.

In her past life’s memories, neither of these two children had survived.

It couldn’t be that a problem arose from an area under her management...

This time, Xiangjun kept a close watch, but one of the children was still lost. Only Jiang Guiren’s child was saved.

His Majesty was naturally furious and ordered a thorough investigation.

The investigation revealed no malicious intent—just the chaos in the harem. Due to the laziness of the servants, the task of repairing the pathways had not been done properly. A loose brick on the palace path had caused Deng Cainü to fall.

Jiang Guiren also mentioned that she had almost eaten contaminated food a few days earlier. Fortunately, Consort Lian had been closely supervising the Shangshi Bureau. Jiang Guiren knew that the soup had not come from the imperial kitchen, so she didn’t eat it, avoiding disaster.

Hearing this, De Fei’s expression flickered with embarrassment for a moment, but she quickly regained her composure.

Xiangjun glanced at De Fei, then calmly averted her gaze without exposing her.

After all, even if she exposed her, His Majesty wouldn’t do anything to De Fei—she was the mother of the eldest prince.

This harem truly had no regard for reason.

---

chapters.title: Someone Actually Gives Up Power for Love
chapters.content:
His Majesty listened to the women’s arguments until his head ached, and he couldn’t help but miss the days when Empress Yang had managed the harem.

He blamed the Empress for not fulfilling her duty to protect the harem, and the two had another argument over this.

Since the two imperial heirs had nearly been lost, the matter was finally brought to the Dowager Empress.

"I have never interfered in your harem affairs, Emperor. But now that I’ve had it investigated, I see that your harem is in chaos. The Empress is unwilling to manage the harem, yet she clings to power without the ability or virtue. Does she intend to let your imperial heirs perish?"

The Dowager Empress had never liked Xue Jiaojiao. The previous Empress Yang had been forced upon the Emperor by the Dowager.

In the past, the Emperor had always protected Xue Jiaojiao, but now that she was Empress, things were different. She hadn’t done her job well, and he couldn’t speak up for her.

"I am aware of this. It’s just that I haven’t found a suitable candidate yet."

"I think Consort Lian would be a good choice. She was the one who quelled the unrest when Bai Cainü was bullied by the palace attendants. And it was because of her carefulness that Jiang Guiren’s child was saved. Consort Lian didn’t harm others’ children despite having her own son, and she knows how to protect the palace consorts. She is sensible."

The Emperor had considered Xiangjun before, but he thought she was too young. Helping the Empress with some tasks was one thing, but entrusting her with the entire harem alone might lead to trouble. After all, she wasn’t like those noble ladies who had been trained in such matters since childhood.

"Xiangjun is still a bit young."

"She will learn with experience. If you’re worried, assign a few people to assist her. De Fei used to help Empress Yang manage the Six Palaces. Let the two of them manage it together. In any case, the harem cannot remain under the Empress’s management. I still want to see more grandsons born while I’m alive."

"Yes, I understand, Mother. Please rest assured."

...

When the Empress handed over the command tallies to De Fei and Xiangjun, her expression was complex.

Especially seeing De Fei’s satisfied look, the Empress felt even more distressed.

Fortunately, there was still Xiangjun—Xiangjun was her person.

So, the Empress entrusted almost all the important matters to Xiangjun, leaving only minor palace affairs to De Fei.

"Xiangjun can handle the miscellaneous matters for the Empress for now. Once the Dowager Empress’s anger subsides and Jiang Guiren’s child is safely born, you can mention to His Majesty that the palace authority should naturally return to the Empress. During this time, I will come to report the palace situation to the Empress every day. Your Majesty can rest assured."

Hearing this, De Fei had no choice but to agree. "This concubine will also frequently report to Your Majesty."

Only then did the Empress feel a little better. She patted Xiangjun’s hand with relief. "It’s good to have you."

Due to her distrust of De Fei, the Empress still placed the most important Shanggong Bureau under Xiangjun’s control.

The Empress was someone who cared only for love and had little time to manage the harem.

Thus, after the initial displeasure, she quickly adapted and even felt that not managing affairs wasn’t so bad. After all, she was still the Empress, the mistress of the harem.

Consort Lian was diligent and reported to her daily. When things were handled well, if His Majesty or the Dowager Empress asked, she would always credit the Empress. Over time, the Dowager Empress’s attitude toward the Empress improved.

As for Xiangjun herself, she was so busy that she hadn’t attended the Emperor’s bedchamber for a whole month.

Additionally, the Emperor felt that if he took away the Empress’s palace authority but didn’t show her extra favor, others might think the Empress had fallen out of favor and disrespect her. So, as if to compensate, he spent every day with the Empress.

As a result, the harem now had only the Empress standing out alone.

Thus, when Xiangjun next visited Ganlu Palace, the Empress held her hand and expressed her gratitude, even bestowing many rewards upon her. Xiangjun didn’t care much for the rewards and quickly used them to seek benefits for her sister, Jian Guiji.

"Currently, there are very few princes in the harem. De Fei, as the mother of the eldest prince, is quite pleased with herself. Your Majesty, Jian Guiji has always been loyal to you and has given birth to the Third Prince. Now she also helps me with many matters. Your Majesty should also show more concern for her."

The Empress thought for a moment. It was true. Promoting Jian Guiji would also let the harem know that she was still the Empress and could control the fate of the palace consorts.

"What position do you think I should bestow upon Jian Guiji?"

"Your Majesty, titles and positions are secondary. What Jian Guiji truly cares about is her child."

"You’re right. Now that you have your own child, even if you treat Yuanji well, you can’t be everywhere at once. Jian Guiji must want to be Yuanji’s rightful mother."

"You’re absolutely right, Your Majesty."

"Don’t worry. I can promote the consorts. I’ll speak to His Majesty about this and let Jian Guiji raise the child by her side."

After returning from Ganlu Palace, the rewards from the Empress arrived.

Mengmei looked at the pile of rewards and sighed. "Your Highness took the Empress’s palace authority, yet the Empress still rewards you..."

Xiangjun didn’t understand why the Empress would give up power for love.

With so much palace authority given to others, she was actually happy.

But Xiangjun respected her choice and was also happy. She took this opportunity to frantically place her own people in the harem.

Power was like an aphrodisiac, especially for Xiangjun.

She kept her people so busy their feet barely touched the ground. When money ran short, she wrote to her brother outside the palace for more. She spent lavishly to win people’s loyalty, determined to seize this opportunity to firmly grasp the Six Palaces in her hands.

This way, even if she had to return the palace authority later, she would still be the true master of the harem.

...

Because the Emperor and Empress were still inseparable, the harem had grown much quieter.

After all, no one could compete with the Empress for favor, and the newly arrived consorts had lost their fighting spirit.

Except for the major festivals when they had to visit Ganlu Palace to pay respects to the Empress, on other days, everyone preferred to stay at Xiangjun’s place. Of course, not everyone went there—some went to curry favor with De Fei, who was currently out of power.

For example, Wang Wanyin and several high-ranking consorts were closer to De Fei.

Xiangjun sat in the main hall, with Jian Guiji on her left and Sun Guipin on her right.

Sun Guipin, the mother of the Second Princess, held a higher rank than Jian Guiji, but in Chengxiang Palace, she had given the more honorable seat to Jian Guiji. This showed she was flexible and farsighted.

After all, Jian Guiji had a prince, and her future prospects would be better.

The palace consorts were all quite lonely. Visiting Xiangjun was also a chance to see the two children in Chengxiang Palace. Bai Cainü, in particular, was quite popular with the children.

Xiangjun cleared her throat and spoke. "Today, I received some news. Let me be the first to congratulate Jian Guiji. Her Majesty the Empress, in her kindness, has spoken to His Majesty, who has agreed to promote you to the rank of Pin. She has also arranged for you to take Yuanji back to raise him yourself. After the ceremony, Yuanji will be officially registered under your name. From now on, Jian Pin, you will be the rightful mother of the Third Prince."

chapters.title: Would You Be Willing to Be My Eyes?
chapters.content:
In the past, Yuan Ji was not allowed to call Jian Pin "Mother Consort"; she could only address her as "Consort Jian."

Jian Pin almost burst into tears in front of everyone.

At this moment, a thousand words welled up in her heart, yet she forced herself to hold them back.

Back then, when she had been left alone in a maid’s room, waiting for death, her heart had been filled only with grief and despair. It was Sister Xiangjun who had saved her life and taught her how to survive.

Later, even though she had miraculously survived, her heart had still been as cold as ash. Again, it was Sister Xiangjun who had given her hope to live once more.

And now, Sister Xiangjun had even helped her reclaim her own child.

Back then, Sister had promised to make her a mistress of a palace, and now, it had truly come to pass.

Jian Pin was overwhelmed with emotions, while others could only feel envy and jealousy.

Everyone looked at Jian Pin with admiration. A mere dancer had actually become the mistress of a palace. In this palace, following the right person was indeed crucial.

Seeing Jian Pin so happy that she was on the verge of tears, fawning over Xiangjun so much, the others disdained her in their hearts but maintained polite faces, and they became even more flattering toward Xiangjun.

Xiangjun had one flaw: she was easily pleased. Although she knew this in her heart, hearing so many people praise her still made her unable to suppress her joy, and the smile on her face was impossible to hide.

"All of you, my sisters, as long as you serve His Majesty wholeheartedly, you too can have such a day."

Finally, someone noticed the key point in this matter.

Then, they heard Yun Guiren ask, "There can only be one mistress in a palace. So, does that mean Consort Jian will have to move out of Chengxiang Hall? I wonder which sister will be so lucky as to move into Chengxiang Hall and become a person under Consort Lian's palace. I truly hope that I will be the one blessed with such fortune."

"I! I!" Bai Cai'nü excitedly almost jumped up, raising her hand. "I want to be a person under Consort Lian!"

Xiangjun glared at Bai Cai'nü, who then reluctantly sat back down. Only then did she notice Consort Jian in front of her, whose eyes were already red.

Ever since Jian Pin learned she had to move out of Chengxiang Hall, she had been heartbroken for several days. It was only when Xiangjun chose a palace closer to her that her mood improved slightly.

The one who was happiest about Jian Pin's departure was Gu Tingxue.

To get Jian Pin to leave sooner, the new palace was prepared in just one day, and it was done extremely well. When Jian Pin wanted to say it wasn't ready and she shouldn't move yet, she found herself unable to say it.

In the end, she could only think that the palace servants worked so efficiently and meticulously because her Sister Xiangjun managed the harem so well. Indeed, her sister was extraordinarily capable.

...

Finally, the wedding day of her brother, Xu Huanwen, arrived. Xiangjun had been looking forward to this day for a long time.

Although the imperial palace was the most luxurious and magnificent place in the world, the world of a palace consort was indeed too small. Being able to go out made Xiangjun genuinely happy, and she had people prepare everything early.

She had originally planned to bring Meng Mei, Xi Yu, and Xiao Luzi along, but Meng Mei worried that there would be no one to take charge in the palace if they all left, so only Xi Yu and Xiao Luzi were allowed to follow.

Xiangjun only had two hours, and including the time to leave and return to the palace, she feared she would have less than the time it takes for a stick of incense to burn to spend at the Xu residence.

After dressing up, Xiangjun first went to the Tai Ji Hall to express her gratitude, but she hadn’t expected that although it had been agreed that Gu Tingxue would escort her to the Xu family, when she arrived at Tai Ji Hall, she found that it was Zhou Zidu waiting for her instead.

"Didn't His Majesty say that Lord Gu would send me?" Xiangjun asked.

His Majesty looked at Xiangjun helplessly and smiled. "I know you find him annoying. Since you two don’t get along, on this joyous day, I won’t let him upset you. With Zhou Zidu escorting you, I can rest assured."

It was only after sitting in the carriage that Xiangjun couldn’t help but feel a little regretful.

Ah, she had played her game too far.

In the future, even the task of delivering rewards to him might not be something Tingxue would fight to do.

The marriage of the Xu family was a bestowal from Her Majesty the Empress Dowager, personally arranged by His Majesty, who sent an inner court official from the palace. Consort Lian herself attended the Xu residence to witness the ceremony.

Such favor, such honor, such immense imperial grace made Xu Huanwen and the Li family’s wedding the most lively event in the capital recently.

The wedding was arranged perfectly. Although Xiangjun was not an elder, the distinction between monarch and subject meant she sat in the seat of honor and accepted the bows of the two new spouses.

This time, Xiangjun’s adoptive father had also come, along with the mistress of the Xu household. As for Xu Huanwen’s birth mother, she could only stand to the side, wiping her tears as she watched her son get married.

Xiangjun could only stay for the time it takes for a stick of incense to burn. After witnessing the ceremony, she had to leave.

The Xu family saw Xiangjun off together to the door. Old Master Xu even wiped away a few tears, and in front of everyone, performed a scene of deep father-daughter affection.

Xiangjun was a little surprised. This father could really act.

But since Father had acted, it wouldn’t be good if she didn’t play along. So she also cried a good cry.

"Father, Mother, after this daughter returns to the palace, who knows when I will see you again..."

Old Master Xu, with tears streaming down his face, said, "Your Highness, rest assured. Everything is fine at home. You must take care of yourself in the palace."

Perhaps Xiangjun’s crying was too moving, because the scene of the family parting touched the onlookers, and their eyes also reddened.

Especially Zhou Zidu, who was in charge of the guard. Seeing Xiangjun cry so sadly, he took the initiative to step forward and softly said to Xiangjun, "Your Highness, if you want to spend more time with your family, this humble official can find a way to let you stay for another half hour."

Xiangjun’s hand, which was wiping her tears, paused.

She didn’t want that. With that extra half hour, how wonderful it would be to stroll around the capital.

Xiangjun shook her head. "No need. His Majesty’s grace is immense. This concubine is already satisfied to have seen my parents. I must not be greedy."

Consort Lian led a grand procession back to the palace.

The capital was also lively at night. Shengjing had no curfew, and many restaurants and small shops were still open, extremely bustling.

Thinking that in her two lifetimes, this was the first time she had seen the prosperity of the capital, Xiangjun couldn’t help but sigh.

Xiangjun lifted the carriage curtain and looked at the lively streets outside. Suddenly, she saw a small stall selling dough figurines.

When she was a child, her dear elder sister would always buy her dough figurines.

"Stop the carriage."

The carriage stopped, and Xiangjun whispered a few words in Xiao Luzi’s ear before sending him to buy a dough figurine.

Xi Yu also wanted to see the lively scene, so Xiangjun let her go buy some things she liked, and she gave her money.

Zhou Zidu rode his horse next to the carriage window, watching Xiangjun stretch her neck to look outside. He couldn’t help but ask, "Your Highness, do you envy this free life?"

"Why does Lord Zhou ask that?"

"Just now, I saw Your Highness crying so sadly. This humble official thought... if Your Highness had married into an ordinary family, perhaps you wouldn’t be so unfree. Even wanting to see your parents would not be so difficult."

Xiangjun glanced at Zhou Zidu and smiled faintly.

"If this concubine had married into an ordinary family, would I truly be free? In this world, women are unfree because their eyes are covered. Their thoughts and concerns are confined to a single room. Even if this concubine has become a palace consort and assists in managing the six palaces, what I can see is still limited to the affairs of one palace. Men, however, can look beyond to the entire world. Compared to spending my life in an ordinary family, I would rather be a palace consort. At least I stand higher. Even if my eyes are covered, through the occasional gaps, I can see farther than ordinary women."

Zhou Zidu was somewhat shocked. In the past, the Consort Lian in his heart had been an innocent and naive girl, a bird caged by high walls on all sides.

But now, he felt that Consort Lian was different.

Perhaps it was the imperial capital’s nurturing influence, but now she was unparalleled in nobility, shedding her former immaturity. She was not only beautiful but also had an untouchable majesty.

Facing Xiangjun’s gentle yet imposing smile, Zhou Zidu was once again dazzled by this new side of her.

Seeing Zhou Zidu’s expression, Xiangjun smiled. She looked deeply into his eyes and softly asked, "Lord Zhou, you care so much for this concubine. Tell me, Lord Zhou, would you be willing to be my eyes and see the world for me?"

---

chapters.title: Spitting Out the Truth
chapters.content:
Xiangjun returned to the palace a little late that night. By the time she arrived back at Chengxiang Hall, it was already past the time when the palace gates were locked.

Xiangjun sat in front of the mirror, closing her eyes to rest while Meng Mei and Xi Yu removed her hairpins and ornaments for her.

Suddenly, she felt the person behind her pause, but soon, a hand began gently removing her hairpins again.

A few footsteps faded away, and the door to the bedchamber was closed. Only then did Xiangjun open her eyes, and sure enough, she saw Gu Tingxue standing behind her, removing the pearls and jade from her hair.

Seeing Gu Tingxue’s darkened expression and his silence, Xiangjun felt something was amiss.

"What’s wrong? His Majesty didn’t let you escort me to the Xu family today. Are you unhappy?"

Xiangjun reached out to remove her own hairpins, but Gu Tingxue grabbed her hand.

Gu Tingxue groped at Xiangjun’s palm, looking at their reflections in the mirror, and said in a sarcastic tone, "Be your eyes? Hmm?"

Tsk, this dog slave, his information network was truly efficient.

Xiangjun pulled her hand away from Gu Tingxue and continued removing the hairpins, saying as she did so, "It seems you still haven’t changed your old habits. How dare you have the audacity to spy on me?"

Gu Tingxue placed his hands on either side of Xiangjun, trapping her between himself and the dressing table.

He looked at their reflections in the mirror with a sinister expression, his lips lightly brushing against Xiangjun’s ear. "This slave has always been bold. Your Highness should be careful, or else, without realizing it, you might get bitten by the snake you’ve raised."

Gu Tingxue bit Xiangjun’s earlobe, his hand slowly sliding to the golden snake hairpin in her hair.

He removed the last hairpin from Xiangjun’s hair, and immediately, her hair cascaded down like a waterfall.

"Tingxue, you’re scaring me again."

"I wouldn’t dare. Your Highness has such a temper. If one day you decide to part ways with me, this slave couldn’t bear it."

"So why did you come to me tonight to spout all this sourness?"

"Naturally, to be Your Highness’s eyes."

Gu Tingxue took out a red silk ribbon from his sleeve and gently tied it over Xiangjun’s eyes.

"Your Highness, rest assured. With this slave as your eyes, you won’t bump into anything."

...

The following days passed without anything special, except that it was heard Bai Cai'nü had been summoned by His Majesty again, and the next day, Bai Cai'nü became Bai Niangzi.

After Bai Niangzi’s position was elevated, the first thing she did was come to Chengxiang Hall to find Xiangjun.

"Consort Lian! After serving His Majesty last night, he really asked me about the embroidered pouch! Who do you think told him?"

Xiangjun glanced at Bai Niangzi and said slowly, "In this palace, there are eyes everywhere. You may think no one is around, but behind the rockery, behind the big trees, beside the flower bushes, under the palace walls, and also..."

Bai Niangzi blinked and nervously asked, "And also?"

"And also behind you... there are eyes everywhere."

Bai Niangzi was so startled she shivered, instinctively swallowing a mouthful of saliva.

"Fortunately, Your Highness warned me. I told the truth as you said, and not only did His Majesty not get angry with me, he even elevated my position and rewarded me with a lot of silver!"

Seeing Bai Niangzi so happy, Xiangjun couldn’t help but tease, "His Majesty rewarded you with so much silver, and you didn’t think to take some out to show your respect to your elder sister?"

Bai Niangzi’s smile stiffened. As if suddenly remembering something, she stood up abruptly. "Your Highness, I... I just got promoted and haven’t paid my respects to Her Majesty the Empress yet. The palace rules say I must visit Her Majesty, so I’ll take my leave now."

Bai Niangzi hurried out in a flash.

Xiangjun couldn’t help but let out a soft laugh. "What a treasure."

Unexpectedly, as soon as Bai Niangzi left, Jian Pin arrived.

Seeing Bai Niangzi happily running out, and even giving her an incomplete, improper bow as she ran, Jian Pin’s lips twitched. Only then did she enter the main hall.

Seeing Xiangjun’s smiling face, the smile on Jian Pin’s face became even stiffer.

"Your Highness seems to be on good terms with Bai Niangzi now. I thought Your Highness didn’t like Bai Cai'nü."

"In the past, I found her crying and whining very annoying, but now I think she’s just a little girl who loves to cry and laugh. She’s only fifteen. I treat her like a little sister."

Seeing Jian Pin’s expression change, Xiangjun immediately glanced at Meng Mei, who took out a pair of bracelets.

"These bracelets were rewarded to me by Her Majesty the Empress Dowager. The quality is excellent. Do you like them?"

Jian Pin’s lips twitched, and she nodded.

Seeing her expression, Xiangjun added, "How about we each take one?"

Jian Pin’s eyes lit up, and she happily nodded, immediately putting one on.

Xiangjun also put on the other one. Only then did Jian Pin stop making a long face, and she began to tell Xiangjun the interesting news she had heard.

"This morning, after the news of Bai Cai'nü’s promotion to Bai Niangzi was announced to the six palaces, Wang Wanyi in the Two Instruments Hall threw a huge tantrum."

"Oh? What kind of tantrum?"

"I inquired about it. I heard that she went to His Majesty to report something, but the person didn’t say what it was about. They only said she was reporting on Bai Cai'nü." Jian Pin lowered her voice. "I reckon it’s about the incident in the imperial garden that day. It’s likely she told His Majesty that Bai Cai'nü was privately exchanging gifts with Lord Gu, giving him an embroidered pouch."

Xiangjun raised an eyebrow. Sure enough, she had thought Wang Wanyi wouldn’t let Bai Cai'nü off.

With Bai Cai'nü embroidering pouches and looking for medicinal herbs in the palace, if Wang Wanyi had someone keep an eye on her, how could she not know what Bai Cai'nü was up to?

Jian Pin took a sip of tea and continued, "I guess His Majesty didn’t believe her. Look, he summoned Bai Cai'nü to his bed, and the next day, not only did he not punish her, but he also promoted her by two ranks. Sister, don’t you think Wang Wanyi would be furious?"

Xiangjun smiled slowly, leisurely playing with the agate bracelet on her wrist. "The women in this palace always mistake their enemies. They always like to see other women as their opponents. Little do they know, the only person we need to deal with is just one."

Xiangjun and Jian Pin exchanged a glance, and both smiled.

Xiangjun put down her tea cup and asked again, "His Majesty’s birthday banquet is coming up soon. Would you like to make a splash this time? I can arrange it."

"I think I’ll pass. Such a good opportunity should be left to the younger sisters."

...

His Majesty favored Bai Niangzi for a few days, but after the novelty wore off, he spent more time with the Empress again.

As for organizing the birthday banquet, that was a tedious and thankless task, especially since their Emperor had rather high standards.

And Her Majesty the Empress, busy being intimate with His Majesty, encountered such a major event for the first time since becoming Empress, yet she threw all the responsibilities onto Xiangjun.

Xiangjun was so busy that she was at her wit’s end, cursing people in the palace every day. Then, she suddenly heard that Her Majesty the Empress was pregnant again.

"How is that possible?"

chapters.title: The Zhou Family’s Downfall
chapters.content:
Xiang Jun urgently summoned Physician Liu to question him.

"Didn’t you say that the medicine you gave would ensure the Empress could never conceive again?"

"That is indeed the case. This pregnancy is truly peculiar."

Physician Liu hesitated before replying, "This humble servant cannot say for certain, but it may be related to the recent arrival of the noble consort from Nanxun Palace."

"Consort Yue?" Xiang Jun was surprised. "Her child was killed by the Empress. Aren’t they enemies?"

"It’s hard to say. Your Majesty the Empress is, as you know, the kindest. If Consort Yue were to bow and plead, speaking of her grief over losing her child, the Empress might take pity on her. Moreover, Consort Yue is a princess of Nanyue."

Xiang Jun pondered. If it were her, she would be willing to cooperate with Consort Yue.

Consort Yue might not be clever, but her father was a cunning old fox.

Physician Liu continued, "Furthermore, Nanyue is a place where one can find all sorts of things—gu poison, secret medicines, curses, and dark arts. It’s possible Consort Yue offered some secret technique."

"If there truly is such a powerful technique, why didn’t Consort Yue use it to save herself? Why has she been slowly restoring her health in the palace using our mild tonics?"

Physician Liu looked up and exchanged a glance with Consort Lian. Neither spoke, but they both understood the meaning in each other’s eyes.

Physician Liu immediately said, "This humble servant will pay close attention to the Empress’s pregnancy. If there are any issues, I will report to Your Grace first."

Xiang Jun thought for a moment and then said, "Previously, I had been preventing Consort Yue from fully recovering. But now, I think it’s fine to let her get better. Have the Imperial Physicians slowly restore her health, little by little."

"Yes."

...

Since Xiang Jun knew there was something wrong with the Empress’s pregnancy, she naturally kept her distance.

She still devoted herself entirely to the Emperor’s birthday banquet, summoning the concubines to Chengxiang Hall daily to instruct them. She made them all help her come up with new ways to amuse the Emperor.

"Our duty as concubines is to keep the Emperor happy. Since His Majesty enjoys liveliness, our harem must be vibrant and flourishing."

So, Xiang Jun had each concubine prepare a performance.

Lady Liu had a slender waist and was a skilled dancer, so she was to perform the Flying Apsaras Dance.

Lady Yun played the xiao beautifully, so Xiang Jun arranged a set of clothes for her that resembled those of a Taoist nun, determined to make the Emperor see her as ethereal and otherworldly.

As for Bai Niangzi... Bai Niangzi had no talents, but Xiang Jun thought her features had a touch of heroism. So she ordered her to dress as a man, stick on a small mustache, and sing folk tunes for the Emperor. The lyrics were written by Xu Huanwen at Xiang Jun’s request, filled with excessive flattery, guaranteed to make the Emperor beam with delight.

However, when the day came to inspect their progress, Xiang Jun was so angry her face turned black.

She stood with her hands on her hips, glaring at the three trembling young concubines as she paced back and forth in front of them.

The three concubines shivered in fear.

"Consort Lian, we were wrong!"

"Wrong?" Xiang Jun stopped in front of Lady Liu. "A few days ago, I saw you dancing quite well. How is it that today you’ve regressed?"

"I..."

"Don’t think I don’t know why. You live in Consort De’s palace. She scolded you for dancing like a courtesan, bringing shame upon yourself, lacking the demeanor of a palace concubine, acting like a vixen, always scheming to seduce the Emperor, isn’t that right?"

Lady Liu nodded.

"She wasn’t wrong to scold you."

Lady Liu’s face paled even more.

"Remember this: to live with dignity in this palace, you must fight for yourself. You are not like Consort De. She has the Eldest Prince, a high birth, and her family’s support. Even if the Emperor doesn’t favor her, she still has dignity. But you... hmph, you had better have the skills of a vixen. Otherwise, if you can’t even hold the Emperor’s interest, you won’t even qualify as a courtesan—you’ll end up as a foot-washing maid."

"Consort Lian, I understand. I will practice diligently."

"You’d better. If you can catch the Emperor’s eye this time, I’ll have you moved to Concubine Jian’s palace. If not, you can continue being Consort De’s foot-washing maid."

Xiang Jun shot a glare at the pale-faced Lady Liu before turning to Lady Yun.

Lady Yun looked at Consort Lian with a confused and cautious expression, thinking she had performed quite well today.

Unexpectedly, Xiang Jun coldly smiled and pinched Lady Yun’s chin.

"Have you been eating a lot of braised pork trotter? It’s only been a few days, and your face has already rounded out."

Xiang Jun forcefully let go of Lady Yun’s chin, but Lady Yun didn’t even stumble.

Xiang Jun was so angry she almost laughed. "I told you to have the bearing of an immortal, an immortal! Look at you—you’ve even developed a double chin. How am I supposed to pass you off as a fairy? Xiaoluzu..."

"Your servant is here!"

"Order the imperial kitchen: from today on, Lady Yun’s meals are to be halved. No rich or greasy dishes are to be served to her. And stop all the pastries from her daily portion."

"Yes!"

Lady Yun was on the verge of tears.

Xiang Jun then approached Bai Niangzi.

Bai Niangzi looked as if she were about to cry.

"Smile for me!"

Bai Niangzi could only force a hollow smile.

"Remember, in front of the Emperor, you are only allowed to smile, not cry. You must always be cheerful, never gloomy."

Bai Niangzi nodded with a forced smile.

"As for the rest..." Xiang Jun’s expression softened slightly. "Not bad. Go back and keep practicing."

This time, Bai Niangzi’s smile was genuine and radiant. Nothing made her happier than receiving praise from Consort Lian.

"Enough. All of you, leave. Looking at you makes me annoyed."

The three quickly left.

Jian Pin, who had been watching from the side, immediately stepped forward to soothe Xiang Jun. "Sister, don’t be angry. They’re still young, just girls in their teens. As for Lady Yun, I’ve been coaching her. There’s still half a month left—she won’t disappoint His Majesty."

Xiang Jun wrapped her arm around Jian Pin’s waist and said aggrievedly, "It’s good to have you, Qinglian, by my side. Otherwise, I’d have no one to confide in. You wouldn’t believe what Consort De and the old servants in her palace say about me—they claim I’m using young concubines to flatter the Emperor."

"Your Grace, rest assured. They all know you have a kind heart. You’re helping them. They will surely redouble their efforts."

The three did not disappoint Xiang Jun.

In just a few days, they had transformed completely.

As for Lady Yun, who had grown pale from hunger, Xiang Jun quickly sent her fine rouge and powder, then had the imperial kitchen gradually adjust her diet.

After dismissing the three, Xiang Jun finally had a moment to herself. She picked up her teacup and took a sip, only to see Xiaoluzu rush in.

Xiaoluzu’s face was grave as he whispered to Xiang Jun, "Your Grace, Lord Xu has sent someone to deliver a message from outside the palace."

Xiang Jun raised an eyebrow. "What message?"

"The Zhou family is in trouble."

"Which Zhou family?"

"The Grand Commander of the Imperial Guards, the Marquis of Cheng’en, Zhou Zidu’s family."

...

As the New Year approached, the capital city suddenly imposed a three-day martial law. Soon after, two prominent families in the capital were raided: the Marquis of Cheng’en, the Zhou family, and the hereditary imperial merchant, the Ning family.

The reason for their downfall was their illegal salt and iron trade with the Northern Mongols.

If there was one thing the current Emperor hated most, it was the Northern Mongols. He wished for their utter destruction. Even mutual trade with the Northern Mongols was forbidden, let alone the strictly prohibited salt and iron trade.

These two families were destroyed overnight due to the Emperor’s wrath.

It was said that the Marquis of Cheng’en had long been in decline. A few years ago, due to the misconduct of its descendants, the family had nearly lost their marquisate over a deficit of more than a million taels of silver. Later, they formed a marriage alliance with the imperial merchant Ning family, which temporarily saved them.

In recent years, thanks to the Emperor’s favor toward a concubine-born son from the third branch, the family had shown signs of recovery. Who would have thought that the Marquis of Cheng’en would dare to secretly collude with the Northern Mongols?

Now, the entire clan was destroyed overnight.

Naturally, the official handling this case was Director Gu of the Censorate. The raid was carried out by Director Gu’s Shence Army, and the Zhou family members were imprisoned in a place under Director Gu’s jurisdiction.

chapters.title: Will Your Grace Still Treat This Servant as Before?
chapters.content:
The first snow of winter in the imperial capital finally arrived, albeit late.

The lights in Chengxiang Hall remained lit throughout the night.

By midnight, Xiang Jun finally received the arrival of Gu Tingxue, who carried a faint scent of blood.

Gu Tingxue seemed to be in high spirits today. When he entered, there was still a smile on his lips, though his face bore traces of blood that had not been wiped clean, making his smile appear somewhat sinister.

Noticing Xiang Jun staring at his mouth, Gu Tingxue reached up to touch it.

Upon seeing the blood on his fingertips, Gu Tingxue feigned surprise, smiled, and said, "Your Grace summoned me, and I came in such a hurry that I didn’t even clean the blood off my face."

Xiang Jun sat regally in the seat of honor in the main hall, her face adorned with a perfectly composed smile.

"Is that so? It’s such a cold night, and it’s snowing—the first snow of winter. You’ve truly gone through a lot to come here, Director Gu."

"Your Grace has grown distant with me. You used to call me Tingxue, but now it’s Director Gu." Gu Tingxue took out a handkerchief, wiped the blood from his mouth and hands, and smiled. "Does Your Grace not want to ask whose blood this is?"

"Perhaps it’s the blood of the new pair of eyes I sought outside the palace?"

At Xiang Jun’s words, the smile on Gu Tingxue’s face stiffened for a moment before his eyes turned even colder.

"Your Grace, rest assured. It’s not Director Zhou’s blood. It’s the blood of his uncles. Your Grace’s eyes are far too precious. This humble servant, naturally, will save the best for last and deal with him slowly."

Gu Tingxue drew out the word "slowly" with particular emphasis.

Xiang Jun let out a sigh of sorrow, took out a handkerchief, and pretended to dab at the corners of her eyes, squeezing out a couple of tears as she put on a grieving expression.

"Director Gu, you truly know how to hurt a person’s feelings. In the past, when we were close, you addressed yourself as this servant every time. Now, you call yourself ‘this humble servant.’ It seems that in this world, no servant is truly willing to remain a servant—they all want to climb above their master and wield power."

Gu Tingxue walked over to Xiang Jun’s side. With a slight flick of his official robes, he knelt on one knee on the footstool beside her seat.

He took the handkerchief from Xiang Jun’s hand and gently wiped away the tears at the corners of her eyes.

"Your Grace, please don’t cry. Your eyes are far too precious. The eyes outside the palace are gone, but the ones inside must be cherished. What if they are ruined by tears? If Your Grace wishes to hear me call myself a servant again, what difficulty is there? This servant is here to attend to Your Grace."

After wiping her tears, Gu Tingxue smelled the handkerchief. How fragrant.

Watching as Gu Tingxue tucked her handkerchief into his own sleeve, Xiang Jun tilted her head slightly and stared fixedly at him.

But there was not a trace of the false sorrow or helplessness from before in her eyes—only a piercing sharpness that seemed to see through everything.

And Gu Tingxue’s gaze, as always, coiled around his Consort Lian like an icy venomous snake.

The two of them stared at each other, their eyes locked in a silent battle.

In each other’s gaze, they saw the same emotion.

Neither of them intended to yield.

"Since Your Grace no longer wishes to cry, then let us be direct. Tell this servant what urgent matter has brought Your Grace to summon me. This servant still has to return early to attend to the Emperor’s business."

Xiang Jun smiled. "Very well. Then I shall be direct. Tingxue, do you know that Zhou Zidu is of great use to me? He is someone I intend to employ."

"I am well aware. His Majesty intends to promote Zhou Zidu and send him to the northern frontier for training. If he proves himself capable, he may one day become a great general in the military. Who knows, perhaps before long, his influence in the army could rival my own."

"So, Tingxue did this intentionally?"

Gu Tingxue gave a cold laugh, his eyes filled with mockery. "I never expected that my Shence Army would still fail to satisfy Your Grace, forcing you to go through such trouble to find a mere Imperial Guard commander who may or may not ever rise to prominence."

Xiang Jun laughed, her eyes also filled with ridicule. "If Zhou Zidu were truly so incompetent, why would Director Gu be in such a hurry to eliminate him now? Doesn’t this just prove that I have a good eye for people?"

Gu Tingxue smiled. "Indeed. It seems Your Grace’s judgment of character is on par with mine."

"Unfortunately, all the planning I did for Director Gu has now been ruined by you."

"Oh? Your Grace finding another backer is for my benefit?"

"Yes. Director Gu, you must know that His Majesty cannot be relied upon. Today he may use you, but tomorrow he may very well kill you. Military power is far too important. But if Zhou Zidu can be brought under my control, then if one day His Majesty decides to discard you like a worn-out donkey, and both you and Zhou Zidu are my people, I could save your life. That would be a double guarantee."

"Is this a double guarantee for me, or for Your Grace?"

"You are my person. My double guarantee is your double guarantee."

Gu Tingxue’s smile was devoid of any warmth. "Your Grace certainly knows how to say pleasing words."

"I never joke. On the contrary, every word I say, every promise I make to Director Gu, I have kept. It is you, Director Gu, who has gone back on your word, scheming against me behind my back more than once. No wonder you don’t trust me, Director Gu—it’s because you assume others are like yourself."

"Your Grace, rest assured. Even if you were to play the role of the foolish old man from the fable, this servant would not be the wolf. Your Grace has my best interests at heart, but am I not also looking out for Your Grace? Since you already have me, why go to the trouble of finding another simple-minded fool to be your confidant?"

"Director Gu, you certainly know how to joke. Given your actions, how can you expect me to believe you won’t betray me again in the future?"

"You no longer trust me?"

"Director Gu, you are a powerful eunuch who strikes fear into the hearts of officials, a man who has killed countless people. If I, a mere palace concubine, were to place my full trust in you, I would be throwing my life away. You promised to be my servant, yet you secretly bit me, destroying the person I had painstakingly cultivated. Tell me, Director Gu, how am I supposed to trust you?"

Gu Tingxue was still kneeling beside Xiang Jun. Suddenly, he grabbed her hand.

"Actually, there’s something I’ve never understood. I’ve been so good to Your Grace, giving you my whole heart. Why won’t you trust me in return? Why won’t you give me your true heart? But I’ve finally figured it out."

Xiang Jun lowered her gaze to look at Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue held her hand, his eyes closed, gently caressing it.

He treated her hand as if it were some rare treasure.

"What did you figure out?"

"I finally understand why Your Grace is unwilling to wholeheartedly follow me. It’s because I love this ambitious side of you. Everything in this imperial city is dead, but you are alive. You’re so intelligent—how could you not understand why I love you? So, Your Grace knows that if you were to meekly stay by my side, living an ordinary life, waiting for me day after day, would I truly be able to treat you as I did at the beginning?"

Gu Tingxue kissed the palm of Xiang Jun’s hand and finally opened his eyes.

He stared fixedly at her.

His gaze was like a giant python ready to strangle its prey, suffocating to behold.

"So, putting myself in your shoes, if I were not Your Grace’s greatest reliance, would Your Grace truly be able to treat me as you did at the beginning?"

Xiang Jun and Gu Tingxue continued to stare at each other in silence.

Then, Xiang Jun was the first to smile—a smile so gentle, yet utterly devoid of emotion, false and hollow.

"I would naturally treat Tingxue as I did at the beginning."

Gu Tingxue released Xiang Jun’s hand and stood up.

"This servant will also always treat Your Grace as I did at the beginning."

chapters.title: Let This Demon Concubine and This Treacherous Eunuch Have a Duel
chapters.content:
Xiangjun and Gu Tingxue simply stared at each other in silence.

Finally, Xiangjun was the first to look away. She gazed ahead, her voice still as coquettish and soft as ever. "The hour is not early, and Tingxue still has urgent matters to attend to for His Majesty. This concubine shall not detain you."

Gu Tingxue smiled, his hand gently caressing the cold pearl and jade ornaments in Xiangjun's coiled hair. "Your Majesty's affairs are naturally the most important. If Your Majesty wishes, why shouldn't this humble servant keep you company?"

"I have my monthly courses and wish to rest early today."

"Very well, then this humble servant shall come to keep Your Majesty company in a few days."

"Very well, then this concubine shall wait for Tingxue," Xiangjun said with a forced smile. Then she raised her voice and called out, "Xiaoluzi."

At Xiangjun's call, Xiaoluzi immediately pushed the door open and entered.

"It is snowing heavily outside. You will hold an umbrella for Lord Gu. The paths are slippery in the snow; do not let Lord Gu fall."

Gu Tingxue descended the steps, his expression unchanged. "Then this humble servant thanks Your Majesty for your grace."

Gu Tingxue bowed to Xiangjun and turned to leave.

Outside, snowflakes filled the sky. Xiangjun watched as Gu Tingxue and Xiaoluzi's figures disappeared beyond the palace gates.

Mengmei entered softly. She had thought that Her Majesty would be in a foul mood, but to her surprise, Xiangjun was not angry. Instead, she smiled—a smile that seemed genuinely pleasant. Moreover, her eyes sparkled so brightly that it made Mengmei uneasy.

It had been a long time since Mengmei had seen Her Majesty like this, except perhaps when she first entered the palace.

Her Majesty only had such a look in her eyes when she was deeply contemplating something or when she had hatched some wicked scheme.

After staring blankly for a long while, Mengmei finally heard Her Majesty speak.

"All day long, the hunter hunts the goose, only to be pecked in the eye by it. In the end, it was I who made a misstep and let my guard down," Xiangjun said with a smile.

"Your Majesty, are you referring to Lord Gu?"

"Mengmei, I have said before that the women in this palace always mistake their enemies. They fight among themselves, only to end up as fish on the chopping block. The reason is simple: our true enemy is only one—the one who sits high upon the dragon throne, His Majesty the Emperor. But I never expected that I, too, would make the same mistake. It seems that my final opponent may not be His Majesty... but him."

Xiangjun had lived a second life and understood almost everyone—except for Gu Tingxue, who had only been briefly mentioned in the original story.

She had analyzed his character, calculated his true feelings, and thought she had succeeded. But she had lost because she did not truly understand Gu Tingxue's nature.

Now, reflecting on it, she realized she had fallen into her old habit of becoming complacent. She had thought that once she obtained the hardest heart to win, everything would be smooth sailing from then on.

But she had overlooked one thing: the person who gave that heart was Gu Tingxue.

A eunuch with countless lives on his hands; a man raised amidst schemes and intrigue, steeped in blood until it became second nature; a man entrusted with great responsibilities by the Emperor, standing above all others, yet treated as a slave, an object, a dog by the Emperor.

Even his love was poisonous.

This was good.

For the first time in a long while, Xiangjun felt her blood boiling once again.

But Xiangjun was curious—before, she had burned with hatred. Now, what was it that fueled her?

And this feeling... it was different from hatred.

Hatred filled her with indignation and determination.

But this feeling—it gnawed at her heart and soul, making her both excited and restless, yet she did not know how to make it stop.

But it did not matter. She guessed that once she and Gu Tingxue settled their rivalry, this gnawing feeling would cease.

So be it. Let this demon concubine and this treacherous eunuch have a duel.

Originally, Zhou Zi had not been so important, but now, she was determined to save him.

...

After this incident, Mengmei assumed that Her Majesty would be in a bad mood for the next few days.

Mengmei warned the palace servants of Chengxiang Hall to be careful and not to provoke Her Majesty.

But strangely, not only did Her Majesty not lose her temper, she suddenly became extremely calm. In fact, she had been sleeping very well these past two nights.

However, the calmer Her Majesty appeared, the more worried everyone became.

But soon, it was time for the Emperor's birthday banquet, and everyone was too busy to speculate about what Her Majesty was thinking.

This year's birthday banquet was exceptionally lively. The Emperor's brothers had all arrived in full force for the first time.

Great General Wang and the Prince of Jin were both in attendance.

As soon as these two entered, they engaged in a verbal sparring match. Xiangjun did not even dare to imagine how much excitement there would be to watch tonight!

As usual, the Emperor, the Empress, and Her Majesty the Grand Dowager were the last to arrive.

Gu Tingxue, as per custom, followed behind the Grand Dowager.

As soon as he entered, he quickly located Xiangjun's position.

They had not seen each other for several days. Their eyes met briefly before quickly looking away.

There was no affection, only coldness and cunning.

Xiangjun lowered her gaze and, along with the other concubines, greeted their masters.

The Emperor entered hand in hand with the Empress. It had been a long time since he had seen Xiangjun, and upon suddenly laying eyes on Consort Lian, he was momentarily stunned.

"Consort Lian, you are different today."

Xiangjun raised her eyes, her gaze filled with affection. "How is this concubine different?"

"In the past, Our Consort Lian was naturally charming, but though beautiful, she lacked a certain bearing. Now, Our Consort Lian is truly a beauty of celestial grace."

The Emperor praised Xiangjun without reservation. Xiangjun also gazed at the Emperor with tender affection.

Everyone now looked at Xiangjun because of the Emperor's words. Gu Tingxue, too, could stare at Xiangjun without restraint.

The Emperor was right. The current Xiangjun exuded a noble and imposing demeanor. Though she still carried an alluring charm, there was an aura about her that made one hesitate to treat her lightly. At a single glance, one could tell that only the most exalted place in the world, nurtured by the offerings of the entire nation, could cultivate such a golden peony.

It was a pity that beneath the gilding, it was all black.

"That is all thanks to Her Majesty the Empress's teachings."

Xiangjun's words finally made the Emperor realize that the Empress was still by his side.

The Emperor looked at Empress Xue Jiaojiao, then at Xiangjun, and was very satisfied.

A beloved wife and a beautiful concubine—such good fortune. This birthday could be considered a perfect celebration.

The Emperor held the Empress's hand and, looking at her slightly protruding belly, softly said, "Jiaojiao, in My heart, you will always be the most beautiful."

Only then did the Empress smile sincerely.

Xiangjun also genuinely felt that the Empress had become even more beautiful lately. However, while the Empress bloomed because of love and pregnancy, Xiangjun bloomed because of power.

"Your Majesty, Grand Dowager, Her Majesty the Empress, please take your seats."

Only when the three true masters of the harem were seated did the banquet officially begin.

Xiangjun looked at the area where the princes and nobles were seated.

With so many people present this year, the uniqueness of the Prince of Jin and Great General Wang became even more apparent.

While the other princes had arrived with their princess consorts and heirs, only Great General Wang and the Prince of Jin had come alone. This was because neither of their residences had even a single concubine or maid.

Xiangjun could not help but glance at the Empress on the stage. In her heart, she truly admired her.

If she had the Empress's abilities, she might have already become the Emperor.

It was the same world, but different fates.

Xiangjun glanced at Gu Tingxue, who was standing beside the Grand Dowager, serving her food. She shot him a vicious glare.

Hmph, she only had one black-hearted slave.

---

chapters.title: If Your Majesty Holds This Concubine Tightly, She Will Not Be Cold
chapters.content:
The birthday banquet began.

The banquet was held at Linde Palace.

The initial songs, dances, and rituals were all customary. Xiangjun did not want to make things too abrupt, so she waited until everyone had drunk some wine and were in high spirits before presenting the performances she had prepared.

The imperial kitchen had put great effort into today's dishes. Xiangjun had even specially arranged for some fashionable and interesting cooking methods from Jiangnan.

However, Xiangjun had never expected that no one would notice her clever ideas, because Great General Wang was truly a bull in a china shop.

In full view of everyone, this Great General Wang actually toasted to the Empress, his words filled with hopes that the Empress would have her wishes fulfilled, be at peace, and live happily. He spoke with such deep emotion.

Xiangjun even felt embarrassed for the Emperor.

Then there was the Prince of Jin, who remained calm and simply drank alone in silence.

Xiangjun examined Xue Jiaojiao.

If the Empress had any sense, she would maintain the Emperor's dignity. But seeing the Empress's moved expression, with tears welling in her eyes, Xiangjun suspected that pregnancy had addled her brain.

Seeing that the Empress was about to pick up her wine cup and stand, Xiangjun raised her own cup first.

"Your Majesty..."

Xiangjun's call to the Emperor was so affected that everyone in the palace turned to look at her.

Xiangjun held up her wine cup and began to toast the Emperor.

Unexpectedly, Great General Wang tried to interrupt Xiangjun.

"Consort Lian, I am in the middle of toasting His Majesty and Her Majesty the Empress. Please allow me to finish first."

Xiangjun shot him a disdainful look, then raised her cup to the Emperor again. "Your Majesty, the toasts can wait, but the sisters in the palace have prepared songs and dances for Your Majesty. It is very cold outside; we must not let the sisters waiting outside freeze."

The Emperor looked at Xiangjun with satisfaction. Her sly expression made it clear she had done this on purpose.

"As My beloved concubine says."

"Thank you, Your Majesty!"

Xiangjun clapped her hands, not giving Great General Wang a chance to interrupt. Music and drumbeats began, and Lady Liu led her Flying Apsaras Dance.

Following that, the concubines of the harem took turns showcasing their talents, much to the Emperor's delight.

Especially the little tune performed by Lady Bai. The Emperor loved it the most.

Although Lady Bai was dressed in men's clothing with a small fake mustache, which was somewhat undignified, the Emperor was in a good mood today and did not mind these small details. Moreover, Lady Bai had humble origins, so this made it all the more amusing.

"Who wrote the lyrics for you?" the Emperor asked Lady Bai.

"It was Consort Lian," Lady Bai replied.

Xiangjun immediately said, "I do not have such literary talent. It was my brother who wrote it."

"Very well, reward them all!"

Tonight, the Emperor was thoroughly entertained. Watching the Emperor's gaze as he looked at the concubines, the Empress could not hide her melancholy. She excused herself early, citing discomfort from her pregnancy.

The Grand Dowager also left early, taking Gu Tingxue with her.

After leaving Linde Palace, the Grand Dowager had Gu Tingxue support her hand as they walked slowly ahead, while the palace servants followed behind.

Looking at Gu Tingxue's expressionless face, the Grand Dowager smiled.

"It is rare to see you dislike someone so much."

"This humble servant does not understand what Her Majesty the Grand Dowager is saying."

The Grand Dowager laughed. "The entire palace is abuzz with rumors that you and Consort Lian are on bad terms. Today, I saw for myself that it is true. At the banquet, you glared at Consort Lian many times, as if you wanted to devour her. Consort Lian also glared at you several times. It is a pity that every time, your eyes missed each other. You truly are a pair of feuding enemies."

Gu Tingxue remained silent. The Grand Dowager smiled without speaking, her eyes filled with mockery.

"This humble servant still has matters to attend to in the imperial prison. After escorting Her Majesty the Grand Dowager to Ren Shou Palace, I must take my leave."

"What matter is so urgent that it cannot wait until tomorrow?"

"It is His Majesty's business."

"His Majesty's business is not so important. Today is also your birthday. My body grows weaker each year; how many more birthdays can I celebrate with you?"

Gu Tingxue was silent for a moment before replying, "Yes."

...

The banquet had only just passed its midpoint, but the Emperor, accompanied by his beautiful concubines, was already drinking merrily. In the end, he even pulled Xiangjun to sit beside him.

That was the seat meant for the Empress, but Xiangjun pretended to be drunk and sat down next to the Emperor without hesitation.

The Empress's current pregnancy was very unstable, and she was often anxious. The Emperor had no choice but to stay by her side.

Today, he could finally openly favor another concubine, and the Emperor happily held Xiangjun's hand. "My beloved, I enjoyed the birthday banquet you prepared for Me. Shall I visit your palace tonight?"

Xiangjun nodded shyly and continued to serve the Emperor wine, hoping he would drink more and bother her less that night.

Just as she was pouring wine, she noticed the young apprentice of Xiaoluzi approach him and whisper a few words. Xiaoluzi's expression changed abruptly, and he immediately looked at Xiangjun.

Xiangjun gave Xiaoluzi a glance, and he promptly brought over a plate of peeled grapes, giving her a signal that he needed to speak.

Xiangjun then looked at Consort Jian, who immediately took Prince Yuanji's hand to toast the Emperor, distracting him.

Xiaoluzi took the opportunity to whisper a few words into Xiangjun's ear.

Xiangjun glanced at the area where the imperial relatives were seated and noticed that, at some point, Great General Wang was no longer there.

Prince Jin, however, had been silently drinking alone the entire time.

Prince Jin truly had remarkable composure.

No wonder he was the only one who had not been killed by the Emperor in the end.

The banquet was more than halfway over when Xiangjun, with a shy and coy demeanor, leaned close to the Emperor's ear and whispered a few words. The Emperor's expression changed—it was clear that Xiangjun's words had captivated him.

He took Xiangjun's hand, his expression darkening slightly, his voice hoarse as he said, "I have had enough to drink. I wish to retire. My beloved, would you be willing to leave with Me?"

Xiangjun nodded, and the Emperor took Consort Lian and left early.

The remaining concubines naturally found the atmosphere less enjoyable.

Consort De looked at Lady Liu, who had just been praised by the Emperor, and said sarcastically, "Consort Lian had you dance, play the xiao, and sing, but in the end, she was the one who lured His Majesty away."

Lady Liu smiled sweetly. "At least His Majesty praised me today and spoke many kind words to me. He even said that in a few days, he would have me wear this outfit and dance for him again. I wonder, how many words did His Majesty say to Consort De? When will he visit Consort De?"

Consort De glared fiercely at Lady Liu, but Lady Liu did not mind.

In any case, she absolutely refused to be Consort De's foot-washing maid. Consort De's feet smelled terrible.

...

The moonlight was beautiful tonight.

Inspired by Xiangjun's line, "May I be a star and you the moon, shining together night after night," the Emperor did not take a palanquin. Instead, he held Xiangjun's hand as they walked slowly toward Chengxiang Hall, taking the opportunity to sober up.

The paths in the palace could be quite intricate at times.

Thus, as they took a detour, the Emperor and Xiangjun, hand in hand, arrived at the Thousand Carp Pond.

Xiangjun seemed to suddenly think of something and whispered in the Emperor's ear.

The Emperor looked down at Xiangjun, his Adam's apple bobbing—clearly, he was moved.

"It is cold. On the pleasure boat, I fear you will catch a chill."

"If Your Majesty holds this concubine tightly, she will not be cold."

The Emperor led Xiangjun toward the pleasure boat by the Thousand Carp Pond.

However, upon approaching, they saw two young eunuchs from Empress Xue's palace standing guard by the boat.

chapters.title: General Wang, You Judge People Well
chapters.content:
When they saw someone approaching, the two little eunuchs had wanted to speak up, but Eunuch Wan glared at them with a sinister look and made a throat-slitting gesture. The two immediately became too scared to make a sound.

These two little eunuchs were former disciples of Eunuch Defu from Ganlu Palace, so they knew the Empress very well.

Offending the Empress might not lead to death, but offending the Emperor meant the Empress definitely couldn’t protect them.

The two didn’t dare to speak, keeping their heads down and not moving an inch.

Eunuch Wan stepped forward and pulled the two little eunuchs away. The Emperor’s and Xiangjun’s people also retreated far away.

Only the Emperor and Xiangjun remained standing by the pond.

The Emperor and Xiangjun took a few more steps forward, and finally, they heard voices coming from inside the boat.

To their surprise, the voices belonged to Empress Xue Jiaojiao and Great General Wang Zhou Qingchong.

Xiangjun’s eyes widened slightly in shock.

She cautiously glanced at the Emperor, expecting to see anger or shock, but the Emperor’s face was ashen and cold as ice.

Xiangjun couldn’t help but sigh. The Emperor was truly no ordinary man—he could endure even this.

Xiangjun pricked up her ears, and to her surprise, she heard the Great General cursing her.

“That Xu Xiangjun is nothing but a lowly merchant’s daughter. How dare she, a mere concubine, steal the Empress’s limelight today? Your Majesty is too kind.”

“Xiangjun isn’t like that. She only wants to make the Emperor happy. She treats me with great respect too. During the palace coup, she even shielded me.”

“Your Majesty, you’re too easily fooled. Who knows if she found out about the Emperor’s lies and is just putting on an act for you. Even I had to stage a ruse of self-inflicted pain when sending spies to Bei Meng.”

The Empress fell silent. Xiangjun cursed the Great General furiously in her mind.

How did he guess so accurately when he wasn’t even there?

The Empress hesitated. “But Xiangjun has always been respectful to me since she entered the palace. I think… she is sincere to me.”

“Your Majesty, you’re still too naive. She has taken all the power in the palace from you. How can that be sincerity? This world is full of honey-tongued, scheming, and vicious people, especially those lowly women. They are the best at deception. Just like how my mother was deceived by someone she considered a good sister. Your Majesty, don’t be fooled. A concubine of low birth like Lian Fei is not to be trusted.”

Hearing this, the Emperor glanced at Xiangjun indifferently. Xiangjun blinked innocently and pinched the Emperor’s arm.

But in her heart, she cursed Great General Wang fiercely.

Hmph, where did this dog general come from? He sure judges people well!

The Emperor withdrew his gaze and continued listening to the two inside.

“If Your Majesty doesn’t want to hear me say these things, I won’t. Today, I finally found a chance to see you alone. I just want to know… does he still treat you well?”

“The Emperor has always treated me very well.”

Great General Wang coldly scoffed.

“If he treats you well, why does he still favor other concubines? Before, it could be excused for the sake of heirs, but now you’re already carrying your second child. Did you see how he looked at those women at the banquet, how he looked at Lian Fei? Did any of that look forced? Jiaojiao, do you see yourself in his eyes anymore?”

“The Emperor has his own difficulties.”

“What difficulties? In the past years, you were the only one by his side, and I could bless you for that. But now, he has broken his promise. Now, Lian Fei is in high favor, and there are even rumors outside the palace that the Emperor wants to elevate the Xu family. Why would the Emperor elevate the Xu family? Don’t you know what that means, Your Majesty? Empress Yang’s fate might be your fate in the future…”

“Qingchong, don’t say that. The Emperor won’t do that to me. You don’t understand my relationship with the Emperor. How can my situation with the Emperor be the same as Empress Yang’s?”

“Jiaojiao! Don’t be angry. You know I’m just too…”

Afraid that Great General Wang might say something he shouldn’t, Xiangjun pretended to step on a branch.

*Crack.*

The sound was very clear.

Xiangjun wasn’t trying to help Great General Wang and the Empress. She was afraid they might say something she shouldn’t hear, which could cost her her life. Their Emperor was someone who could turn on you in an instant.

But the two inside were too emotional to notice the noise outside.

Hearing that the Great General was about to say the word “love,” Xiangjun had no choice but to pretend to sprain her ankle. With a cry, she threw herself into the Emperor’s arms.

This time, the two inside finally reacted.

“What’s going on outside?” the Empress asked from inside the boat.

The Emperor glanced at Xiangjun, said nothing, turned, and left.

Xiangjun quickly followed the Emperor.

When the Great General and the Empress walked out of the boathouse, only two little eunuchs were standing outside.

“What happened just now? I seemed to hear a woman’s voice,” the Empress asked.

The two little eunuchs nervously replied, “In response to Your Majesty, just now… the Emperor and Consort Lian were here. The woman’s voice you heard was Consort Lian’s. Consort Lian was standing there when she somehow stepped on a branch, sprained her ankle, and fell into the Emperor’s arms, which is why she cried out.”

The Empress’s expression changed drastically. “Why didn’t you announce their arrival?”

The two little eunuchs exchanged a glance. One of them said, “Your Majesty, we wanted to speak, but Eunuch Wan covered our mouths, so we couldn’t say anything.”

The Empress slightly furrowed her brows but didn’t blame the two little eunuchs. She only said to the Great General, “Qingchong, I need to return to the palace now. Don’t come looking for me again in the future.”

Great General Wang, however, grabbed the Empress’s hand.

“Jiaojiao, you can regret this. As long as you regret it, I’ll take you away anytime.”

Empress Xue Jiaojiao forcefully pulled her hand back.

“I don’t regret it, and I never will.”

The Empress left with her people.

Only Great General Wang was left standing by the Thousand Carp Pond, his hand tightly gripping the hilt of the sword at his waist.

On the other side, Xiangjun followed the Emperor. She had been pretending to have sprained her ankle, but limping along, she couldn’t keep up with the Emperor’s pace, so she had to hurry and take a few quick steps to catch up.

The Emperor suddenly stopped, and Xiangjun also abruptly halted.

“What’s wrong? Didn’t you sprain your ankle? Are you better now? No longer pretending?”

Xiangjun smiled awkwardly.

“You sure are good to the Empress, even covering for her.”

“I was afraid that Great General Wang might say something that would anger Your Majesty. Now that the Empress is pregnant, I don’t want Your Majesty and Sister to develop a rift over such an insignificant person.”
