The Emperor sighed and extended his hand to Xiangjun. She took it, and the two walked slowly under the moonlight.

Xiangjun could sense the Emperor’s melancholy. Seeing that he didn’t seem angry, she asked, “Your Majesty, aren’t you angry?”

“When I married Jiaojiao, I promised Jin Wang and Great General Wang that I would always give Jiaojiao a chance to regret her choice.”

chapters.title: I Am Like a Rat in This Palace
chapters.content:
Heavens, Xiangjun was shocked. The Emperor was so generous?

How could she not be suspicious?

Was he just putting on an act?

The Emperor turned to look at Xiangjun. Her shocked and disdainful expression instantly turned into one of deep emotion, and her eyes reddened.

“Why are you crying?”

“I… I’m just envious of the Empress. Your Majesty’s deep affection for the Empress… I am truly… both moved and envious…”

The Emperor reached out and gently stroked Xiangjun’s hair, softly saying, “I will also treat you well.”

Xiangjun’s eyes shimmered with tears as she nodded, tightly gripping the Emperor’s hand, and followed him back to Chengxiang Palace.

However, after returning to Chengxiang Palace, the Emperor, perhaps still dwelling on his deep affection, did not have Xiangjun attend him in bed that night. Instead, he held her hand and lay quietly beside her.

In the past, the Emperor had never treated Xiangjun like this. It seemed he was seeking some balance with Xiangjun after being hurt by the Empress.

After all, Xiangjun had always portrayed herself as a woman deeply devoted to the Emperor.

It had been a long time since Xiangjun had slept so chastely beside a man, and she found herself unable to fall asleep.

She turned her head and saw that the Emperor was also awake.

Xiangjun rested her small head on the Emperor’s shoulder and softly asked, “Your Majesty, can’t you sleep either?”

“I just thought of some things from the past.”

“What did Your Majesty think of?”

Instead of answering, the Emperor suddenly asked, “Today, Great General Wang insulted you like that. Aren’t you angry?”

Xiangjun’s mind raced. Why was the Emperor asking this now?

And why now, of all times?

Wasn’t he just thinking about the past?

Unless…

Xiangjun thought back to what Great General Wang had said about her that day.

Oh, she remembered. Over and over, he had just said she was of low birth. Nothing new.

Xiangjun realized that Great General Wang’s disdain for those of low birth probably wasn’t just directed at her. It was possible that in the past, he had also insulted the Emperor.

The current Empress Dowager was a palace maid by birth and had been captured by Bei Meng for seven years. It was possible that when the Emperor was a prince, he had been called the son of a lowly woman by this arrogant Great General Wang.

“I’m not angry,” Xiangjun quickly came up with the most appropriate answer. “Great General Wang is right. I am indeed of low birth. My father was a merchant, and among the four occupations—scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants—merchants are the lowest. I also know that all the noble consorts in the palace have better backgrounds than me. But it doesn’t matter. If I can’t compare to them, I can work hard to learn. Besides, I’ve already become a concubine now, haven’t I? Your Majesty is not blind. It must be because I’ve done better than those high-born sisters that Your Majesty promoted me.”

“Why don’t you say it’s because I favor you?”

“I don’t care about the reason, only the result. The result is that I am now a concubine, overseeing the six palaces, and have Your Majesty’s favor. My family has also been elevated by Your Majesty. Now, I am better than all of them. Even if it’s just luck, even if it’s because Your Majesty favors me, why haven’t they had the same luck? Why haven’t they received Your Majesty’s favor? If Heaven favors me, that is also my own ability.”

The Emperor’s eyes softened as he smiled. He gently turned to face Xiangjun and took her hand.

“My Lian Fei is not inferior to anyone. Xiangjun, you are the best in this harem in every way.”

In his heart, the Emperor even thought that Xiangjun handled palace affairs better than the Empress.

She was the one who truly had the bearing of an imperial concubine, much like his mother, the current Empress Dowager.

Xiangjun also smiled gently at the Emperor and said softly, “I am grateful to Your Majesty. Everything I have now is given by Your Majesty. I should thank Your Majesty.”

“Thank me for what? Didn’t you say that Heaven favors you and it’s your own ability?”

“Your Majesty, I thank you for being different from those people. Some people, like that so-called Great General Wang, hmph, he will forever judge people based on their past. But Your Majesty has always seen me with fresh eyes. All my changes are because of Your Majesty’s cultivation. Your Majesty is the best person in this world.”

The Emperor felt deeply comforted by her words and was genuinely moved.

Yes, he was now the Emperor. But some people still didn’t know how to look at him with new eyes.

The Empress, Great General Wang, and the deposed Crown Prince Jin Wang—they had once been the biggest shadows in his youth.

If it weren’t for the former Crown Prince breaking Empress Xue Jiaojiao’s leg, if it weren’t for Great General Wang’s mother losing to his own mother, perhaps he, Zhou Qinghe, would never have become Emperor.

But so what? As Xiangjun said, even if it was luck, it proved that he was destined by Heaven.

Now, he was the most noble person in the world, the master of them all.

Their view of him should indeed change.

The Emperor even felt a deep connection with Xiangjun because of her words.

The Emperor gently caressed Xiangjun’s cheek, and the way he looked at her seemed to hold a trace of genuine affection.

“Xiangjun, you and I are the same.”

Xiangjun feigned innocence. “How am I the same as Your Majesty? Your Majesty is a man, and I am a woman. Your Majesty is the Son of Heaven, while I am just a humble reed, living well only because of the sunlight and rain Your Majesty provides.”

The Emperor smiled. “That’s not what I meant… Xiangjun, do you know that the Empress comes from an excellent background?”

Xiangjun nodded. “I know. The Empress’s grandfather was the Grand Preceptor, her grandmother was a princess, her father was the leader of the scholar-officials, and her mother was the most noble Princess Zhang.”

The Emperor’s expression became somewhat distant, as if lost in memories.

“From a young age, she was the most radiant and noble girl in the entire capital. All the princes revolved around her. Even the Emperor’s own daughters couldn’t compare to her. Back then, to me, she was like a goddess from the heavens. I would even feel shy just looking at her. And I was just a insignificant prince struggling to survive in the palace. My father didn’t want to see me because looking at me reminded him of the woman he had betrayed and abandoned in Bei Meng. The other princes looked down on me because my mother was a palace maid who had been exiled to Bei Meng and was certainly no longer chaste. Even the palace servants bullied me. Back then, I was like a rat in this palace…”

Xiangjun’s eyes reddened as she took the Emperor’s hand, a tear gently sliding down her cheek.

“I have always admired and loved Jiaojiao, but in the end, she is the same as Zhou Qingheng and Zhou Qingchong. They don’t understand someone like me. But you, Xiangjun, you do understand me.”

This was the first time the Emperor had used the word “I” when speaking to Xiangjun.

Xiangjun gently squeezed the Emperor’s hand.

“Your Majesty, I am happy that you say I understand you. But you are wrong. You and I are not the same.”

chapters.title: I Want You to Be My One and Only Noble Consort
chapters.content:
Seeing the Emperor's expression darken with a trace of gloom, Xiangjun remained fearless, firmly grasping the Emperor's hand.

Xiangjun looked at the Emperor with her bright, sparkling eyes.

"Your Majesty, this concubine does not know what those princes and palace attendants said to you back then. But you should know that you are the son of the Emperor, with the most noble birth in this world. They humiliated you because of the Empress Dowager’s past, but it is not your fault—it is their stupidity. The Empress Dowager was in Mongolia to save her husband, to save the Son of Heaven of Great Qi. That was loyalty, that was devotion. That is why, after her return to the palace, no one in the imperial court dared to speak ill of her. Only those foolish women in the harem would judge a woman who had served her country with such absurd notions of chastity. Your Majesty, you are the son of the Son of Heaven. You have a mother who is unparalleled in loyalty and wisdom. The blood flowing in your veins is nobler than all of theirs from the moment you were born. That is why you won, that is why you became the Son of Heaven."

Xiangjun did not discuss the Emperor’s tragic childhood with him. She only spoke of his nobility.

Because she knew that what weighed heaviest on the Emperor’s heart was that period of his life when he had been as lowly as a rat.

She wanted the Emperor to know that, in her heart, he had never been lowly.

So, before her, the Emperor did not need to hide even a little. She accepted all of him, affirmed all of him, admired all of him.

The Emperor looked into Xiangjun’s bright eyes, and his own eyes seemed to be lit by her.

A flame seemed to burn in the Emperor’s chest.

"Xiangjun, I want you to be my Noble Consort. I want you to be my one and only Noble Consort."

...

The next morning, an imperial edict was announced throughout the six palaces.

Our palace had gained another Noble Consort.

The Emperor said he wanted Xiangjun’s Noble Consort to be unique.

But there had already been a Noble Consort Rong before, and she had been initially bestowed with the title of Noble Consort. Xiangjun had climbed up step by step, so in comparison, the former Noble Consort Rong was still more special.

The Emperor pondered and decided that he could only make an exception with the title of Noble Consort.

Usually, titles were one character long, but the Emperor wanted to give Xiangjun two.

The character "Lian" (怜) was retained, but it was still too soft and tender, not noble enough.

So, the Emperor decided to add another character, "Zhao" (昭), to Xiangjun’s title.

"Zhao" means brightness, like the sun.

"倬彼云汉，昭回于天" (The vast Milky Way, shining brightly in the sky) — it is the radiance of the morning light, bright and beautiful.

She was his one and only Noble Consort Lian Zhao.

A two-character title was usually only bestowed posthumously as a posthumous title for a concubine. Throughout history, there were very few concubines who had received a two-character title during their lifetime.

Each one was an absolute favorite, the lifelong beloved of the reigning emperor.

Ganlu Palace.

When the Empress heard of this, she sat down on the throne in disbelief.

"Your Majesty, be careful! You are still carrying the prince!" Caiwei supported the Empress to sit properly.

The Empress’s face was pale.

Did the Emperor favor Xiangjun so much?

Was what Qing Chong had told her yesterday true?

Or had the Emperor heard her conversation with Grand General Wang on the boat last night, been hurt, and thus promoted Xiangjun?

Just like before, was the Emperor only doing this to spite her?

"Your Majesty..." Caiwei hurried in to report: "Noble Consort Lian Zhao has arrived. She is waiting outside the main hall. Will Your Majesty see her?"

The Empress had not expected Xiangjun to come so quickly. Normally, she would only come to pay her respects after the official ceremony.

Xue Jiaojiao thought for a moment and still let Xiangjun in.

As soon as she entered, Xiangjun performed a grand bow to the Empress.

"Your Majesty, do not be angry with Xiangjun. I also do not know why the Emperor suddenly made me a Noble Consort. Last night, by the Qianli Pool... After returning, the Emperor said he wanted to make me a Noble Consort."

The Empress’s heart sank. So it was indeed because of her meeting with Qing Chong.

"Forget it. It’s not your fault. Do not take it to heart. Becoming a Noble Consort is a good thing. Why come to apologize?"

"Your Majesty, even if this concubine becomes a Noble Consort, you are still my Empress sister. Xiangjun’s feelings for sister will not change."

However, today the Empress was truly distracted and only said a few words before dismissing Xiangjun.

When Xiangjun left, the Empress had Caiwei see her out.

She did not know whether the Empress believed her declaration of loyalty. In the past, whenever Caiwei saw Xiangjun off, Xiangjun would give her silver, and Caiwei would accept it. But this time, she did not take Xiangjun’s purse.

When she returned to Chengxiang Palace, Xiyu said that many concubines had come to visit her after hearing the news of her becoming a Noble Consort, but since she had gone to the Empress’s palace, they would come later.

Meng Mei saw that Xiangjun was so worried and could not help but feel confused.

"Your Majesty, now that you are so favored, you should be happy. Why are you not happy?"

Xiangjun knitted her brows. "It’s too fast."

Even Xiangjun had not expected the Emperor to suddenly elevate her status and give her such a unique title.

Now she was too conspicuous. It would be impossible to pretend to be harmless any longer.

Even if the Empress believed her words, the people around the Empress would not.

If the words Grand General Wang had said yesterday were revealed, they would plant a seed of doubt in the Empress’s heart. Sooner or later, she would realize the ambition of her good sister.

"Your Majesty, the Empress’s temperament is such that she probably cannot do anything to you."

"My opponent has never been the Empress. Meng Mei, you must remember, we are in the imperial palace. My child may become the emperor in the future. Whether Yuan Lang or Yuan Ze becomes the crown prince, who can tolerate the existence of a royal son whose mother holds a noble position and has the support of civil officials in the imperial court? Even if the Empress can tolerate it, can the people behind her tolerate it? The men behind her are not easy to deal with. So, we should not be naive. Our Chengxiang Palace and Ganlu Palace will have to compete sooner or later."

"But our Fifth Prince is only one year old, and the Emperor is still in his prime. Don’t you not want to show your ambition in front of the Emperor?"

"That was before. After yesterday, the Emperor’s expectations of me may be different... I cannot always be the same as before. Otherwise, the Emperor will only think that this concubine has not made any progress." Xiangjun said with a firm gaze: "Only by perceiving the opportunity first can one win decisively..."

"Has Noble Consort been reading history books and now even studying the Art of War?"

Gu Tingxue walked in, still with his sinister, lifeless expression.

Xiangjun had ordered that when Gu Tingxue came to Chengxiang Palace, he did not need to be announced for the time being, just like before.

Gu Tingxue was also somewhat surprised. He walked up to Xiangjun and bowed.

"This humble official greets Noble Consort Lian Zhao."

Xiangjun looked up at Gu Tingxue and said sarcastically, "Isn’t this Official Gu? Aren’t you busy torturing prisoners in the imperial prison? How do you have time to come to my Chengxiang Palace?"

chapters.title: Can You Trouble Tingxue to Take My Measurements?
chapters.content:
"I naturally came to deliver the rewards to Your Majesty."

Xiangjun glanced at Gu Tingxue, not sure if it was because he had been busy interrogating prisoners recently, but he did seem to have lost some weight.

Xiangjun lowered her eyelids, idly playing with the agate bracelet on her wrist, and said lazily, "Why would it be you delivering the rewards?"

"Naturally, because this humble official requested to do so."

"Has Official Gu forgotten? You and I are not on good terms. If you requested to deliver the rewards, wouldn’t the Emperor suspect something?"

"The Emperor did have some suspicions, but when he saw that I had chosen only some old junk from his private vault, he stopped suspecting."

Xiangjun immediately looked up and glared at Gu Tingxue fiercely.

"I do not want junk!"

Seeing Xiangjun’s reaction, Gu Tingxue could not help but smile slightly.

Even though Xiangjun was glaring at him fiercely, in Gu Tingxue’s eyes, she still looked beautiful.

It was better than her fake smiles at him.

Gu Tingxue took a few steps forward and stood next to Xiangjun, pushing Meng Mei aside.

Meng Mei had no choice but to step aside.

"The Emperor was displeased with the things I had chosen and ordered me to exchange them for better ones. Knowing the Emperor’s temper, I picked out the best from his private vault." Gu Tingxue extended his hand to Xiangjun. "Would Your Majesty like to see them?"

Xiangjun could not help but let out a soft laugh, covering her mouth with her handkerchief, and gently placed her hand on Gu Tingxue’s wrist.

"Then let me see them."

The servants brought in all the rewards bestowed by the Emperor, arranged them properly, and then quickly left.

Meng Mei also hurried out.

In the hall, only Xiangjun and Gu Tingxue remained.

Xiangjun, supported by Gu Tingxue’s hand, stood up and walked over to look at the treasures he had chosen for her.

Gu Tingxue was indeed ruthless; all of them were treasures from the Emperor’s private vault.

Especially those few famous calligraphy and paintings, which Xiangjun appreciated greatly.

Xiangjun casually flipped through the treasures. Whenever she saw something she liked, she would say a few words to Gu Tingxue. The two of them chatted and laughed, just like old times.

Xiangjun stood in front of the several pieces of keshi silk.

An inch of keshi silk was worth an inch of gold. Keshi silk was the pinnacle of Suzhou’s silk weaving craftsmanship. A large piece like this would take artisans several years to complete.

"This keshi silk is quite extraordinary. The lotus pond and duckling pattern on it looks like a painting. It can be made into a bed quilt for me."

"I will order someone to make it."

"How can I trouble Official Gu with such matters?"

"Your Majesty’s matters are never a trouble."

"Is that so? I also want to make a few sets of sleeping garments. However, I seem to have gained some weight recently. I may need to have my measurements taken again. Can I trouble Tingxue to take my measurements?"

Xiangjun suddenly turned around and spread her arms wide in front of Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue was stunned and did not know what Xiangjun was up to.

"What? Taking my measurements is too difficult for Official Gu?"

"Naturally not."

Gu Tingxue took a step closer to Xiangjun and stretched out his hands, placing them on Xiangjun’s waist.

The two of them were very close. It had been a long time since they had been this intimate.

Xiangjun turned her head and whispered in Gu Tingxue’s ear, "This might not be accurate. I am having sleeping garments made."

Gu Tingxue’s earlobes turned red, and his breathing became heavy. He slightly turned his head and met Xiangjun’s teasing eyes.

"Is Your Majesty teasing me?"

"How is this teasing? Tingxue used to help me change clothes very quickly."

Seeing Gu Tingxue avert his gaze, Xiangjun placed her hand on his shoulder and whispered in his ear, her breath as fragrant as an orchid, "What’s more, it’s just a few words of disagreement between me and Tingxue. Do you really want to distance yourself from me? You haven’t come to see me for so many days. Don’t you miss me at all?"

Seeing that Gu Tingxue did not respond, Xiangjun smiled and took a step back. She lightly undid the button at her neck.

The exposure of her fair shoulders caused a hint of crimson to appear in Gu Tingxue’s eyes.

The heavy clothes slipped off one by one.

"Tingxue, take my measurements again."

...

Zhou Zi was imprisoned in the imperial prison, his heart already as cold as ash.

He was an unpopular concubine-born son from the third branch of the Zhou family. Even if the first and second branches were all dead, the family’s title would still have nothing to do with him. His mother was also not favored, and the main wife was a vicious woman. From childhood, his mother had suffered endless humiliation because of him.

Finally, Zhou Zi had relied on himself to earn a future. Even the people from the first and second branches, who had always looked down on everyone, had started to treat the third branch with courtesy.

The vicious main wife of the third branch had also started to speak gently to his mother, showing great care for her.

Zhou Zi had thought that he was about to rise in status and could earn a title for his mother.

But in the end, he had destroyed his life because of the people who had always tormented him.

He, Zhou Zi, had never received any benefits from the Marquis’s mansion, but he was about to die because of its downfall.

In the dark and cold imperial prison, Zhou Zi lay on the dirty bed, filthy and disheveled, unresponsive to everything.

Until the door of the imperial prison was opened, and a person appeared before him.

Zhou Zi lifted his dirty face and looked at the person.

"Does Zhou Zi recognize who I am?"

"Official Xu?"

The visitor was the principal official of the Ministry of Rites, the elder brother of the palace’s Noble Consort, Xu Huanwen.

Zhou Zi’s deadened heart began to beat again involuntarily.

He remembered that night, under the fading lantern lights, the noble and beautiful palace-dressed woman who had said to him, "Would you be willing to be my eyes..."

But now that he was in prison, how could he be her eyes?

Xu Huanwen did not speak but instead handed Zhou Zi a letter.

"Take a look."

Zhou Zi opened the letter. He did not see the handwriting of Noble Consort, but he did see the handwriting of his own mother.

His hands trembled as he read the letter. His eyes turned red, and with a thud, he knelt on the ground, bowing deeply to Xu Huanwen.

"Thank you, Official Xu, for saving my mother’s life."

"Your mother is still of slave status. Originally, she was to be sent to the Yeting. But because of her poor health, my wife found a way to buy her back. Although she is officially a servant, she is well taken care of in the courtyard. My wife is a very considerate and kind-hearted person. You can rest assured."

"Thank you, Madame Xu, for her planning, and thank you, Official Xu, for saving my life. Zhou Zi has nothing to repay you with in this life. In the next life, I will definitely repay your kindness..."

Xu Huanwen interrupted Zhou Zi, "Zhou Zi, Noble Consort has not given up on you. Do you want to give up on your own life?"

chapters.title: How Dare a Stray Dog Like Me Stay by Your Side, Your Highness?
chapters.content:
Week Zidu looked up in shock at Xu Huanwen.

Xu Huanwen calmly stated, "If you can make the Emperor see your loyalty, not only will you regain His Majesty's favor, but you can also bring your mother back and earn her a title. Then, your mother, free from the main wife's control, can live respectfully as a proper matriarch in your residence. Wouldn't that be better than her past life in the Marquis's mansion?"

Week Zidu cupped his fists and bowed deeply to Xu Huanwen. "Please enlighten me, Lord Xu!"

"This is a list of officials involved in the illegal salt trade."

Week Zidu looked at the list and asked, "Are these all the ones who colluded with the Marquis's mansion in the illegal salt trade?"

"Of course not. Do you think the Marquis's mansion is the only one in the court involved in illegal salt trading?" Xu Huanwen explained, "My Xu family is the largest salt merchant in Jiangnan. It's not hard to find a few officials with shady dealings. Whether they are connected to the Marquis's case doesn't matter. The Emperor is furious and won't investigate thoroughly. Since they are already corrupt, a little investigation will confirm their guilt. You can present this list to the Emperor as a tip-off to earn merit."

"Is that all it takes?"

"That is far from enough. This is just a decoy. What will truly save you is a letter."

Week Zidu looked confused. "What letter?"

"A petition letter. Her Highness the Noble Consort said that the letter must detail how you and your mother were mistreated in the Marquis's mansion. Describe in detail how your legitimate brothers humiliated you and how the cunning servants in the Marquis's mansion bullied you and your mother. It must be heart-wrenching, moving all who read it. Even if you have to fabricate, make it as tragic as possible."

"My mother and I have indeed suffered. But why does Her Highness want me to write this?"

"If Her Highness tells you to write, then you write. She is the closest to the Emperor and knows best what will move him."

Xu Huanwen took out a piece of cloth and handed it to Week Zidu. "Her Highness said that a blood letter would be best."

Without hesitation, Week Zidu bit his own hand until it bled. "Yes, I will follow Her Highness's instructions!"

...

The next day, Week Zidu's letter of accusation and petition reached the Emperor's desk.

In the letter, Week Zidu claimed he had been secretly gathering evidence to expose the entire group but hadn't had the chance to report to the Emperor before the Zhou family was raided.

He submitted a list of nobles and officials involved in the illegal salt and iron trade with the Zhou family. Coincidentally, these names were exactly the ones the Emperor wanted to deal with but lacked a reason for.

But more importantly, Week Zidu also wrote a heartfelt petition.

In it, he expressed his hatred for the entire Marquis's mansion, recounting the sufferings of his childhood, each word dripping with blood and tears.

After reading the letter, the Emperor remained silent for a long time.

He did want to use Week Zidu, precisely because of his identity.

As a bastard son, unrelated to the title, he wouldn't collude with the powerful and could serve solely the imperial authority.

But if he had connections with the Northern Mongols, how could the Emperor dare to use him or send him to the northern border to lead troops in battle?

Yet, the letter was so sincere, and the Emperor had experienced similar hardships himself. So, he believed that Week Zidu truly hated the Marquis's mansion and thus refused to be complicit with them.

However, Emperor Yanqing was suspicious and wouldn't easily let go of his doubts.

So, he summoned Gu Tingxue and showed him the blood letter.

Gu Tingxue looked at the blood letter, instinctively clenching his hand, almost tearing the cloth to pieces.

"How does Your Majesty intend to handle Week Zidu?"

"You go and interrogate Week Zidu. I need to confirm that he has indeed severed ties with the Marquis's mansion and has not participated in the illegal salt and iron trade."

"Yes."

"As long as it doesn't cripple him or affect his ability to lead troops in battle, feel free to use torture. I want to see Week Zidu's true heart."

"Your Majesty, rest assured. No one can lie in my imperial prison."

...

Late at night, the lamps in Chengxiang Hall were still lit. Xiangjun, with her hair down, waited in the bedchamber, fiddling with a wooden token in her hands.

She knew that tonight, after Gu Tingxue found out, he would surely come to confront her.

Finally, at the Zi hour (around midnight), Gu Tingxue appeared at the palace gates of Chengxiang Hall.

Gu Tingxue stood at the door for a while, wanting to go in but feeling it meaningless, then turning to leave. However, the palace door behind him was opened.

Xiaolu stood at the door, respectfully gesturing for Gu Tingxue to enter.

Since that was the case, Gu Tingxue no longer hesitated and walked into Chengxiang Hall.

The palace door locked again.

As soon as he entered, Xiangjun smelled a strong metallic scent. In the past, Gu Tingxue might have had a hint of blood on him, but tonight, he was wearing clothes stained with blood.

He did it on purpose.

Without guessing, Xiangjun knew whose blood it was.

"Does Your Highness not want to know whose blood this is? This time, the blood on me is truly Week Zidu's. Does Your Highness feel heartbroken?"

Xiangjun glanced at Gu Tingxue indifferently, her voice devoid of emotion. "This palace is heartbroken for Tingxue. It's so cold, yet you have to stay in the imperial prison."

Xiangjun stood up, took a pre-prepared hand warmer, and placed it in Gu Tingxue's hand.

"Tingxue, warm your hands."

Gu Tingxue slammed the hand warmer onto the table with a thud.

"Does Your Highness treat me this way to plead for Week Zidu, to make him suffer less?"

"Can't this palace be concerned about you?"

Gu Tingxue gave a cold laugh. "Your Highness deceived me to stay in Chengxiang Hall, then had Xu Huanwen use the token I gave you to enter the imperial prison and make Week Zidu write a blood letter. Your Highness, to save Week Zidu, you really go all out."

"Tingxue misunderstands me."

Xiangjun walked up to Gu Tingxue and wrapped her arms around his neck.

"It's not hard to keep you away. While you were busy with the Emperor's tasks, Xu Huanwen could have taken the token to the imperial prison. There was no need for me to sacrifice myself to keep you away. That day, I seduced you to kill two birds with one stone. Not only could I save someone, but I could also satisfy my longing for Tingxue."

Gu Tingxue lowered his gaze, his long eyelashes hiding the painful and complex emotions in his eyes.

"Your Highness is really good at coaxing people. But why bother coaxing me now? Your Highness no longer needs me. You have Xu Huanwen for civil matters and Week Zidu for military affairs. You have the Emperor's favor, a royal son, firm control over the harem, eyes and ears everywhere in the palace, and a steady stream of silver from Jiangnan. A stray dog like me, how dare I stay by Your Highness's side?"

Xiangjun looked up, staring into Gu Tingxue's eyes.

"Lord Gu says I am a smooth talker, but when have you not been deceptive? Lord Gu, are you putting on this act to test me? If I truly dared to treat you like a stray dog, if I truly dared to abandon you, I fear it wouldn't be long before I met a gruesome end. Lord Gu is not a stray dog; Lord Gu is a wild wolf that bites. I am very afraid of you."

"Do you think I would harm you?"

Xiangjun's arm rested on Gu Tingxue's shoulder as she stood on her tiptoes, gazing into his eyes.

"Wouldn't I?"

---

chapters.title: This Hatred for Her Makes Him Unable to Stop
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue suddenly laughed. He reached out and wrapped his arm around Xiangjun's waist.

"Indeed, groveling won't get Your Highness's favor. I need to make Your Highness fear me to avoid being abandoned."

Xiangjun scoffed inwardly. Sure enough, he was an ungrateful, venomous snake.

Gu Tingxue tightened his grip on Xiangjun's waist, pulling her tightly into his embrace.

"Your Highness knows my nature, so why do you oppose me? Why insist on saving Week Zidu? Is Week Zidu so important to Your Highness that you would risk angering me for him?"

"I am not doing it for Week Zidu. I am doing it to win Week Zidu over. I want him to be eternally grateful to me, willing to die for me. I should thank Lord Gu for giving me this opportunity; otherwise, how could I have made him completely loyal to me?"

"Are you asking me to spare Week Zidu?"

"Hasn't His Majesty already spared Week Zidu?"

Gu Tingxue laughed, his cold and sinister expression reminding Xiangjun of their first meeting, when his eyes had been equally cold.

"The Emperor doesn't want Week Zidu to die, but I naturally have ways to ensure he lives, but not for long."

"How long is not for long? Can Tingxue give me a specific time so I can calculate how to use him to the fullest?"

Gu Tingxue sneered. "Your Highness says this only to hope that I spare Week Zidu."

Xiangjun was almost amused into anger. "He is just someone I need. Why are you so intolerant of him? The Emperor is still my husband; why don't I see you being intolerant of him? Why don't you think about killing the Emperor?"

This was the first time Xiangjun had mentioned killing the Emperor in front of Gu Tingxue. She had expected at least a strong reaction from him, but Gu Tingxue's response was surprisingly mild.

Gu Tingxue's expression flickered slightly, but not with fear or shock—it was...

Xiangjun pondered the fleeting expression on Gu Tingxue's face.

If she hadn't misread, Gu Tingxue's expression was a slight embarrassment, as if caught in the act.

No way.

Xiangjun's eyes widened suddenly. "You actually thought about killing the Emperor..."

Gu Tingxue abruptly covered Xiangjun's mouth with his hand.

"Your Highness must not speak recklessly."

The Emperor was Xiangjun's greatest reliance now and had been good to her. Gu Tingxue had thought that Xiangjun, upon learning of his intentions, would at least be angrier about this than about his handling of Week Zidu. But...

He actually saw a hint of... excitement in Xiangjun's eyes?

Gu Tingxue slowly removed his hand from Xiangjun's mouth.

The two stared into each other's eyes, each trying to fathom the other's thoughts.

Xiangjun had previously thought that Gu Tingxue was just jealous, possessive, and intense in his way of loving. But she hadn't expected him to consider killing the Emperor so quickly.

Was it for her, or had he always had such plans?

Xiangjun felt she couldn't be sure. After all, she didn't know Gu Tingxue well enough.

Gu Tingxue had previously thought that Xiangjun simply loved power and wanted to become the Empress Dowager after the Emperor's death. But he had never considered that a mere concubine would dare to entertain such thoughts against a vigorous and powerful Emperor.

Moreover, the Emperor had shown Xiangjun great favor. How many women could remain clear-headed amidst such imperial affection?

Yet, Xiangjun seemed to have no hesitation at all.

Gu Tingxue felt that he had a new understanding of Xiangjun.

"I underestimated Your Highness."

"Tingxue, you sure know how to joke. It is I who underestimated Lord Gu."

It seemed that what they were contending for was not just each other's hearts, but something else as well. Only time would tell who would emerge victorious.

In the past, Xiangjun had hoped that Gu Tingxue would join her in killing the Emperor.

But now, Gu Tingxue's ambition had become a thorn in her side.

Because Gu Tingxue's ambition was too great.

Killing the Emperor seemed difficult, but as two of the people closest to the Emperor, if they truly sought the right opportunity, it might not be so hard.

The real challenge was surviving and securing their position afterward.

After all, concubines and eunuchs were highly dependent on imperial power. Their interests were too deeply intertwined with the Emperor's, with most of their benefits overlapping with his.

Thus, none of them dared to act lightly.

Whoever made a move would have to be fully prepared and possess the strength to seize the throne.

"When I was just a minor Beauty, Lord Gu once made a bet with me. If I could rise to the rank of Concubine within half a year, Lord Gu would become my greatest ally in both the front court and the harem. Now, Lord Gu, are you still willing to make another bet with me?"

"I am not a trustworthy gambler, Your Highness. Do you still dare to bet with me?"

"Of course. Because this time, the loser will lose everything and be at the mercy of the winner."

After all, they were gambling with the imperial throne.

Gu Tingxue smiled lightly, his demeanor relaxed. "Alright, then let us make another bet, Your Highness. If I win, you will still become the Empress Dowager as you wish, and I will get what I want. If I lose, I will not die a good death."

Xiangjun laughed, raising her eyebrows. "Why would I want you to not die a good death? Wouldn't that be a waste of Tingxue's handsome face? Rest assured, if I win, I will train you well and make you my most loyal servant."

With that, Xiangjun took out the wooden token she had been keeping in her sleeve.

She dangled the token in front of Gu Tingxue.

It was this token that allowed Xu Huanwen to enter and exit the imperial prison freely.

It was also this token that allowed Xiangjun to command Gu Tingxue's people in the palace at will.

Xiangjun walked to the charcoal brazier and casually tossed the token into the fire.

The fire crackled, and soon the token was consumed by the flames.

Xiangjun turned around to face Gu Tingxue. "So, shall our bet officially begin?"

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun. Even though they were separated by some distance, he felt as if his heart was gripped in her hand.

"Sometimes, I truly hate how ruthless Your Highness is."

Gu Tingxue took a step forward, closing the distance between them. His eyes seemed to pierce through Xiangjun's, delving into her soul.

He wanted to see what kind of heartless woman could be so cold and calculating, willing to discard even the reliance she had risked half her life to obtain.

And yet, this hatred for her made him unable to stop.

Gu Tingxue kissed Xiangjun fiercely on the lips, pressing hard as if he wanted to devour her lips. Xiangjun wrapped her arms tightly around Gu Tingxue, kissing him back with even greater force.

Xiangjun somewhat understood why the Emperor always sought the Empress's company after their arguments.

Kissing a powerful opponent was indeed more stimulating than kissing a devoted servant who loved only you.

chapters.title: The Woman I Love is Naturally the Most Extraordinary
chapters.content:
In the imperial prison, Zhou Zidu had just endured a round of torture.

In his semi-conscious state, someone placed a pill in his mouth.

He heard a prison guard whisper in his ear: "This is from Lord Xu. He also asked me to deliver a message: as long as you endure all the torture without changing your statement, you will be released. He urges you to hold on."

The guard left hurriedly, and Zhou Zidu lapsed back into unconsciousness.

When he awoke again, it was to a bucket of ice water splashed on his face.

Opening his eyes, Zhou Zidu saw Gu Tingxue once more—the man whom all the court officials secretly despised yet feared.

This time, Zhou Zidu truly experienced firsthand the brutality of the emperor’s hound. When it came to tormenting people, there was likely no one in the world more ruthless than this eunuch.

"Lord Zhou, did you sleep well last night? I, on the other hand, am well-rested."

Zhou Zidu remained calm. "Lord Gu, if you have any methods, feel free to use them."

"I found something in Lord Zhou’s home. Please enlighten me—what is this?"

Gu Tingxue took out a handkerchief.

At the sight of it, Zhou Zidu’s eyes widened.

It was the handkerchief the current Noble Consort had used to wipe his sweat when he escorted ten Jiangnan beauties to the capital years ago.

But he had selfishly kept it instead of returning it to her.

"This handkerchief... I feel like I’ve seen it before. It seems I encountered it when I was sent as an imperial envoy to Jiangnan..."

Zhou Zidu’s body broke out in a cold sweat.

Even the earlier bucket of cold water hadn’t made him this terrified.

This was just an ordinary handkerchief—Gu Tingxue shouldn’t recognize it. It had been four years; how could Gu Tingxue still remember?

"Lord Zhou must know that my relationship with the Noble Consort in the palace is hostile. We are at each other’s throats; we look for trouble with each other at every turn."

"I have heard of it, but I don’t see how Lord Gu’s feud with the Noble Consort has anything to do with me?"

"Nothing to do with you? Lord Zhou is of marriageable age, yet you remain unmarried. Why is that?"

"I am a concubine’s son. My mother is not kind, so my marriage has been delayed."

"This handkerchief belongs to a woman. Lord Zhou keeps it so carefully—could it not be a gift from a woman you love?"

"It’s just an ordinary handkerchief. It proves nothing."

"True. I’ve checked. This is indeed a Suzhou embroidered handkerchief sold in a famous shop in Jiangnan. They sell hundreds a year."

Zhou Zidu let out a slight sigh of relief.

"But... I seem to recall that years ago, when the Noble Consort first arrived in the capital, she had a handkerchief just like this."

Zhou Zidu’s heart leapt again. He glanced at Gu Tingxue, trying to see if he was bluffing.

But Gu Tingxue’s cold eyes showed no flicker of emotion.

"The Noble Consort is from Jiangnan. It’s not strange for her to have one."

"Is that so? Then who gave you this handkerchief, Lord Zhou?"

"I once knew a young lady briefly, but we lost touch in the vast sea of people. I have not seen her since."

"Oh? Is that so? Why not describe her to me? Perhaps I can find her and help you fulfill a romantic destiny."

"There’s no need. In my current state, how could I dare seek her out? I only hope she is happy and has forgotten me."

"I didn’t expect Lord Zhou to be such a romantic."

Zhou Zidu raised his eyes and looked at Gu Tingxue with disdain.

"A eunuch like you would naturally not understand true love between a man and a woman."

Gu Tingxue didn’t get angry. He merely curled his lips into a smile, with a hint of self-satisfaction. "How do you know I don’t understand? Even as a eunuch, I too have a woman I love."

Zhou Zidu laughed, his face full of mockery. "Lord Gu is famous for staying away from women. So many officials and nobles have sent you all kinds of women, yet you’ve refused them all. I wonder, what kind of woman could capture Lord Gu’s heart?"

Gu Tingxue’s perpetually icy gaze actually softened slightly. A smile played on his lips as he fiddled with the handkerchief in his hand. In his deep, melodious voice, he said, "The woman I love is naturally the most extraordinary."

"Please, enlighten me."

In truth, Zhou Zidu didn’t care who Gu Tingxue loved.

He just didn’t want Gu Tingxue to keep harping on about the handkerchief’s owner.

"She..." Gu Tingxue smiled, his expression ambiguous and dark. "She is selfish, self-serving, wild and untamed, vain and frivolous. She has a bit of cunning, willing to risk her life to win, yet she lacks any composure, gloating over the smallest victory. She demands that everyone around her love her, cherish her, and give her their whole heart, yet she responds with false affection, without a shred of sincerity. She scorns all the virtues a woman should have—she is not chaste, not humble, not gentle, not submissive. Her eyes are full of desire, her heart full of schemes. Love is mere decoration to her; power is her true pursuit. Isn’t that... very special?"

This time, even Zhou Zidu struggled to maintain his calm demeanor.

"Why would Lord Gu like such a woman?"

Gu Tingxue’s eyes gleamed, his tone filled with delight.

"Doesn’t Lord Zhou think that such a woman is different from those dull, lifeless women? She is vibrant and full of vitality. Being with her, one never feels bored. Isn’t that enchanting?"

"But a woman who is not loyal—doesn’t Lord Gu fear being cuckolded?"

Gu Tingxue continued to play with the handkerchief in his hand.

"It doesn’t matter. Most men in this world cannot accept such a woman. Only I understand her, pity her, love her, respect her, and offer her my loyalty. She is very particular. Only with my kind of devotion can I remain by her side in the end."

Zhou Zidu could no longer hide his disgust. He couldn’t help but mutter, "Madman."

Gu Tingxue laughed, then slowly stood up and picked up the whip with barbed spikes again.

"Since Lord Zhou is not interested in the woman I love, let’s return to the topic of the woman you love. If Lord Zhou is willing to admit that this handkerchief was given to you by the Noble Consort, I promise you can leave this imperial prison unharmed and return to serving His Majesty. How about it?"

"Even if you kill me, I will not falsely accuse any innocent woman."

Gu Tingxue sneered. "Fine. I still have twenty-one more tortures prepared. Lord Zhou, enjoy them."

---

chapters.title: If I Were the One Who Harmed You, Would You Still Remain Loyal to Me?
chapters.content:
The ceremony for Xiangjun’s elevation to Noble Consort was held with great modesty.

This was because the court was busy with the recent turmoil—His Majesty was enraged by the conspiracy to collude with the Northern Mongols, and many officials and nobles in the capital had been removed from power as a result.

Outside the palace, rumors flew, but inside, all was calm.

The Empress was pregnant, and though she had begun to feel wary of the highly favored Noble Consort Lian Zhao, as Advisor Caiwei had pointed out, she had to wait until the child was born before she could reclaim her authority in the harem.

Caiwei had said that if, when the Empress requested the return of her powers, Xiangjun refused, it would prove that Xiangjun’s past loyalty had been false—that perhaps Xiangjun had always wanted to climb to a high position.

Though the Empress was reluctant to think this way, she followed Caiwei’s advice and focused on preserving her pregnancy.

Caiwei had been by her side since childhood and would never harm her.

Moreover, if Xiangjun truly cared for her, she wouldn’t fear this test.

This year, His Majesty had little interest in celebrating the New Year.

Xiangjun, now a Noble Consort, naturally had to find ways to ease His Majesty’s worries.

But she wasn’t thinking of securing favor for herself. Instead, every day, she arranged for a different beauty to be sent to His Majesty.

For an entire month, the women at His Majesty’s side changed daily.

His Majesty found this strange—many of the concubines, whom he had previously found dull, now seemed more interesting after a long absence.

What he didn’t know was that before each woman was sent, the Noble Consort would first warn them: *I can send you to the Emperor once, but whether there is a second time depends on your own ability.*

Furthermore, the Noble Consort would tailor their attire and words to each concubine’s personality.

That month, His Majesty visited the harem twenty times. Thanks to the Imperial Physicians’ careful care, he showed no signs of fatigue.

By the second month, when the green-headed cards were delivered again, His Majesty found himself spoiled for choice, appreciating the unique charm of each concubine. After some thought, he simply let the Noble Consort continue arranging them for him.

For a time, the Noble Consort became the benefactor of the entire harem.

When the Empress heard the rumors from the harem, her heart ached even more.

"Caiwei, do you think the Noble Consort manages the harem better than I do?"

"Your Majesty, His Majesty favors you deeply. How can it be wrong for you to ask His Majesty to spend more time with you?"

"But the Noble Consort can arrange for all the concubines to attend His Majesty, and they all remember her kindness."

"That is because they do not truly love His Majesty, and neither does the Noble Consort. Only Your Majesty truly loves His Majesty, and His Majesty knows this in his heart."

"Before, His Majesty only had me... But now... His Majesty showers different concubines with favor every day. His treatment of me... is truly different."

Since the incident at the Thousand Carp Pond, His Majesty had not visited the Ganlu Palace except on the first and fifteenth of each month.

When the Empress tried to bring up what had happened that day, His Majesty merely dismissed it with a cursory, "I trust the Empress," and sent her away.

In the past, he would have been angry with her over such a thing.

"His Majesty is only upset about the matter between you and General Wang. It is because he loves you that he reacts this way. Your Majesty, you are carrying the imperial heir—you must not worry excessively. Do it for the child in your womb. I believe that once the prince is born, your relationship with His Majesty will improve."

...

Xiangjun also knew that she and the Empress had grown distant.

She still visited the Ganlu Palace every other day to report on palace affairs to the Empress.

But the Empress no longer wished to listen. She always cited fatigue from her pregnancy and asked Xiangjun to leave.

Later, she simply told Xiangjun not to come anymore.

Xiangjun saw Zhou Zidu again a month later.

He was still in charge of guarding the palace, but according to her brother, the Emperor planned to appoint him as the deputy military commissioner in a northern fortress after the imperial sacrifice ceremony.

Xiangjun timed it perfectly and "accidentally" encountered Zhou Zidu near the Donghua Gate during his patrol.

Zhou Zidu had a group of soldiers behind him. Xiangjun removed one of her earrings, and her maid, Meng Mei, immediately took it and loudly declared, "Oh no! Her Highness’s earring has fallen! Please, honored guards, help us find it. It is an imperial gift—we cannot afford to lose it!"

Zhou Zidu, upon hearing this, glanced at the guards behind him. With a single look, they scattered to search the courtyard.

He then approached Xiangjun, bowed, and said, "This humble official greets Noble Consort."

After ensuring no one was around, he lowered his voice. "This humble official thanks the Noble Consort for saving my life."

Xiangjun smiled. "If Lord Zhou does not mind, accompany me a little further."

Thus, Xiangjun, along with her maid Xiaoluzhi and Zhou Zidu, ascended the city wall.

Xiaoluzhi stepped back a few paces but did not go far, maintaining a distance where she could still hear their conversation.

This was the Noble Consort’s order—no one must catch them in a compromising position.

The three of them stood on the city wall, watching the people below searching for the earring.

After a long silence, Xiangjun finally spoke. "Lord Zhou, how do you intend to repay me for saving your life?"

Zhou Zidu might be simple when it came to matters of the heart, but he was no fool in politics. Having clawed his way out of the filthy Marquis’s estate and secured his place in the military through his own efforts, he was not without political acumen.

"I know that though Your Highness has risen in status, you still need reliable people. I am willing to serve you."

"Is that so? No matter what happens, you will stand by my side?"

"Yes. Your Highness saved my mother and me—you are my benefactor. As long as it does not involve harming the people or betraying the nation, I will obey your commands."

"I would never harm innocent people. It’s just..."

Xiangjun turned to look at Zhou Zidu, a faint smile on her face.

Zhou Zidu, still dazzled by her, blushed and lowered his head.

"Does Your Highness have any doubts?"

"It’s just that I want to know—if you were to learn that the Zhou family’s downfall, the executions, the exiles, were all because of me, would you still remain loyal to me?"

Zhou Zidu was stunned.

"How... how could it be Your Highness?"

Though Xiangjun had not personally orchestrated it, the Zhou family’s ruin was indeed connected to her. She did not want someone else to tell Zhou Zidu the truth later—it was better to admit it herself now.

"It wasn’t directly my doing, but it happened because of me. So, it’s no different from if I had done it myself. Your family suffered without cause."

Zhou Zidu was too shocked to react.

"If that’s the case... why did Your Highness save me?"

"Because I need you."

"I don’t understand. If Your Highness needs me, why harm my family?"

"Because the Zhou family was indeed guilty of illegally trafficking salt and iron—crimes deserving of death!"

Xiangjun suddenly turned, slightly lifting her chin as she looked down at Zhou Zidu.

"There’s a question I’d like Lord Zhou to answer. If the Zhou family’s crimes of trafficking salt and iron had not been exposed now, but instead were revealed later, when you had become His Majesty’s confidant or a high-ranking official in charge of a province... what would you do?"

chapters.title: Cherry Pork
chapters.content:
Zhou Zidu remained silent, offering no response.

Xiangjun asked again, "And suppose, at that time, the Emperor still didn’t know about the Zhou family’s affairs, but the Zhou family, fearing exposure, used your mother as leverage to force you to cover for them—would you help or not?"

Zhou Zidu once again didn’t know how to answer.

If the truth only came to light then, with the Emperor’s suspicious nature, he would be doomed.

Even if he won battles, the Emperor might suspect that his victories were due to secret deals with the Northern Mongols.

By then, he might truly have no choice but to cover for the Zhou family—to protect himself, his mother, his brothers-in-arms, and his subordinates.

But that would mean betraying his country, betraying the common people slaughtered by the Northern Mongols at the border.

Xiangjun’s gaze on Zhou Zidu was sharp and piercing.

"Lord Zhou, the Zhou family was raided today because of my involvement. I saved you only to repay the kindness you showed me when you escorted me to the capital. But whether you choose to serve me or remember my favor is your decision—I will never force you."

"Your Highness, I—"

"You don’t need to answer me now. If you don’t wish to remember my kindness, then from now on, you will have nothing to do with me. Whether I live or die, where I go in this palace, will be none of your concern. But if you do remember my kindness… then go to the Xu family and find my brother."

"Your Highness…" Zhou Zidu hesitated. "Why tell me this? If you hadn’t, I never would have known."

"Because I want true loyalty."

Little Luzhi suddenly stepped beside Xiangjun, whispering in her ear, "Your Highness…"

Xiangjun frowned and followed Little Luzhi’s gaze.

In the distance, a figure was walking toward the palace gates.

It was Gu Tingxue.

At the sight of Gu Tingxue, Zhou Zidu tensed as well. He moved to Xiangjun’s side and whispered, "When Gu Tingxue interrogated me in the imperial prison, he kept trying to force me to falsely accuse Your Highness."

"Accuse me of what?"

Zhou Zidu’s face flushed. "He… he wanted me to admit to having an affair with Your Highness."

Xiangjun let out a soft laugh.

"I see."

She reached out and took Little Luzhi’s hand, leading her down from the city wall.

As soon as Xiangjun descended, Meng Mei ran over, holding an earring. "Your Highness, the earring has been found."

Xiangjun was about to take it when a hand reached out first, snatching the earring away.

Gu Tingxue examined the earring, then glanced up at Zhou Zidu, who was still standing on the city wall. A smirk played on his lips.

Zhou Zidu instinctively clenched his fists. He wanted to go down, but that snake of a man had always suspected him of having an improper relationship with the Noble Consort. If he acted too familiar now, Gu Tingxue would only cling to the suspicion more.

So Zhou Zidu could only stand on the city wall, watching from above.

Gu Tingxue shifted his gaze back to Xiangjun, his smile mocking. "Noble Consort, your grace and bearing are unmatched in the palace. You walk with such stability—how did you manage to lose an earring?"

"It’s just a small trinket. Losing it happens."

"Does it? Allow me to help you put it on."

Xiangjun froze. In broad daylight, she quickly refused, "No need. How could I trouble Lord Gu? His Majesty has repeatedly instructed me not to treat you like a servant. You are His Majesty’s trusted official."

"I can serve His Majesty, so naturally I can serve you as well."

Before Xiangjun could protest, Gu Tingxue stepped forward, closing the distance between them.

Tall and imposing, he nearly enveloped her. He reached out and roughly jammed the earring into her ear.

"Hiss—" Xiangjun winced, sucking in a sharp breath. She glared at him. "That hurts!"

Gu Tingxue took a step back, then glanced once more at the man on the city wall before smirking. His tone was sarcastic. "Seems I’m still not good at serving palace consorts. I’ll have to learn more, try more, practice more. I must go see His Majesty now. Farewell."

He turned and left, but not before shooting another mocking look at Zhou Zidu on the city wall.

Xiangjun had no idea what had gotten into him. She shot him a glare, then darkened her face and led her attendants away.

The guards watching the scene took it as confirmation of the rumors—these two favorites of His Majesty truly did not get along.

To publicly clash like this, they clearly had no intention of giving each other any face.

...

After returning, Xiangjun grew angrier the more she thought about it. She yanked the earring from her ear, and blood trickled from her left ear.

"Your Highness!" Meng Mei and Xi Yu were both startled.

But Xiangjun remained expressionless. She put the earring back on, her face cold. "Bring a tray of snacks. We’re going to the Tai Ji Hall to see His Majesty."

When she arrived at Tai Ji Hall, His Majesty was still in discussion with Gu Tingxue. Xiangjun waited at the door for a while before Eunuch Wan announced her entry.

Gu Tingxue walked out just as Xiangjun entered.

He noticed the blood on her ear. He knew his own strength—he wouldn’t have hurt her. So he quickly realized why Xiangjun had come to Tai Ji Hall.

He couldn’t help but smirk. As they passed each other at the doorway, neither knew whose hand had reached out first.

Their hands brushed briefly before parting.

His Majesty had been particularly gentle with Xiangjun lately. He noticed her ear immediately.

"What happened? Which careless servant did this?"

Xiangjun threw herself into His Majesty’s arms, aggrieved, and proceeded to lodge a complaint against Gu Tingxue.

That night, His Majesty came to Cheng Xiang Hall, bringing Gu Tingxue with him.

Xiangjun knew His Majesty was saving her face. As she entered the room, arm in arm with the Emperor, she shot Gu Tingxue a triumphant glance before saying coyly, "Your Majesty, this concubine personally cooked two dishes for you today. You must have several bites."

She also wanted to see what His Majesty’s true attitude toward her was now.

"Your Majesty, try this wine-steamed lamb first."

The Emperor glanced at Eunuch Wan, who picked up his chopsticks to taste the dish.

The moment the food touched his lips, Eunuch Wan’s mouth twitched visibly.

"Your Majesty… perhaps this dish should be skipped…"

Xiangjun feigned hurt. "What? Is it poisoned?"

"Not poisoned… it’s just…"

Curious, the Emperor picked up his chopsticks and took a bite. His expression darkened, but he still swallowed it.

"Is it good?"

The Emperor shot Xiangjun a look. "You worked hard cooking. Such things… Xiangjun, don’t do this yourself in the future."

Xiangjun pouted, on the verge of tears. "Does Your Majesty dislike what this concubine made?"

"Like it." The Emperor lied through his teeth. "I just feel bad for you. I don’t want you to tire yourself out."

Xiangjun’s face lit up. She served him another piece. "If Your Majesty likes it, then have more."

The Emperor looked pained. Xiangjun let out a soft laugh, and only then did the Emperor realize she had been teasing him.

He couldn’t help but pinch her nose. "You little troublemaker, daring to play tricks on me?"

The room filled with laughter and warmth.

Xiangjun glanced at Gu Tingxue, who had been standing coldly to the side the whole time. She pointed to another dish on the table. "This cherry pork is for Lord Gu. Your Majesty, what do you think?"

The Emperor knew Xiangjun was still angry about Gu Tingxue hurting her ear earlier. He waved his hand in agreement.

A young eunuch carried the plate of cherry pork to Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue maintained his indifferent expression. He picked up his chopsticks and took a bite, his face betraying a slight change.

He looked up at Xiangjun, but she wasn’t watching him—she was pouring wine for the Emperor.

It was so sweet, tender, and soft—even better than the imperial kitchen’s version.

From the corner of her eye, Xiangjun saw Gu Tingxue’s expression. Her smile deepened. She had gone to great lengths to find out from the palace maids in the Dowager’s quarters that cherry pork was Gu Tingxue’s favorite dish.

She had practiced making it for a long time.

---

chapters.title: What Is the Secret Between the Emperor and Gu Tingxue That She Doesn’t Know?
chapters.content:
The lamps in Cheng Xiang Hall had all been extinguished.

His Majesty had drunk quite a bit that night and was sleeping soundly.

It was a time of lingering cold, so a charcoal brazier was still burning in the room.

But tonight, the brazier was burning too hot. Xiangjun woke up in the middle of the night, parched with thirst.

She carefully got out of bed, tiptoeing to the table. She took the thermos from the stove and poured herself a cup of hot water.

Just as she was about to drink, a hand suddenly reached out from the darkness, wrapping around her waist from behind.

Xiangjun gasped in shock.

His Majesty was still asleep in bed, breathing evenly.

She took a slow, deep breath and slowly placed the cup back on the table.

Xiangjun lowered her voice, speaking to the person behind her. "What are you doing, going mad?"

Gu Tingxue sighed softly, his breath warm against her ear. "This servant saw that Your Highness was not satisfied earlier. Allow me to serve you properly now."

Xiangjun looked at the Emperor, still asleep in bed, and her heart leapt to her throat.

She tried to say something, but Gu Tingxue covered her mouth.

"Shh, don’t make a sound."

...

In the silent bedchamber, a sudden noise broke the quiet—the sound of the table being moved.

When the Emperor opened his eyes, he saw this scene: Xiangjun was sitting at the table, her face flushed with anger. She had taken the hot water from the table and splashed it onto Gu Tingxue’s face, scalding him so badly that he couldn’t help but cry out.

"So hot—how am I supposed to drink it? Does Lord Gu serve His Majesty like this too?"

"Serving His Majesty is different from serving Your Highness."

The Emperor was deeply annoyed. He sat up, rubbing his temples.

"What’s going on now?" He waved his hand wearily. "Tingxue, you go outside. Let Wan Li Chun attend inside."

Gu Tingxue shot Xiangjun a cold, resentful glance before complying with a curt, "Yes."

After Gu Tingxue left, the Emperor beckoned Xiangjun over.

She lay down beside him, putting on the act of a wronged little wife.

"Why do you always provoke Gu Tingxue? Do you take everything I say as mere suggestions? In this entire palace, you’re the only one who dares ignore my words."

Xiangjun wrapped her arms around the Emperor’s neck. "Your Majesty clearly dislikes Lord Gu—why do you always side with him?"

"Nonsense. When have I ever disliked Tingxue?"

Xiangjun whispered, "Isn’t that the case? What kind of emperor would allow a favored official to attend while a consort is in bed? Your Majesty is clearly trying to humiliate Lord Gu. This concubine thought Your Majesty disliked him, so I was just venting for you."

The Emperor chuckled at her words, not angered in the least.

"So you blame everything on me? Everything you do is for my sake?"

Xiangjun’s heart skipped a beat. The Emperor hadn’t denied what she’d said.

Did His Majesty truly dislike Gu Tingxue?

Her gaze darkened. She tightened her hold around his neck, pouting. "Your Majesty is impossible. If you dislike him, why don’t you just send him away? Why keep him around?"

"You wouldn’t understand."

"I *don’t* understand. I dislike him. I don’t want him serving at Your Majesty’s side."

"Whether you like him or not doesn’t matter. What matters is that I trust him. That’s enough. Alright, as long as you don’t go too far in the future, I won’t say anything. Know your limits. Now go to sleep."

The Emperor pulled Xiangjun back into his arms and closed his eyes.

But Xiangjun’s heart sank.

This Emperor’s thoughts were truly inscrutable.

Normally, an emperor wouldn’t place such trust in someone he disliked. Yet His Majesty both trusted Gu Tingxue completely, entrusting him with heavy responsibilities, while also harboring deep disdain for him in his heart.

What kind of strange feeling was this?

Why?

There had to be something between the Emperor and Gu Tingxue that she didn’t know.

...

The next morning, when His Majesty left, Gu Tingxue was already gone.

Two days later, Xiangjun’s sister-in-law, Lady Li, entered the palace as a commanding wife. After paying her respects to the Dowager, she came to Cheng Xiang Hall.

The two women exchanged pleasantries for a while before Lady Li smiled and said, "My husband told me he finds it inconvenient to move about the palace, so he asked me to visit Your Highness often and spend more time in Cheng Xiang Hall."

Xiangjun heard the subtext in Lady Li’s words.

She was to be the messenger between Xiangjun and her brother.

The couple had been married for several months now. Xu Huanwen must have made this arrangement after getting to know Lady Li better.

Xiangjun was willing to place her trust in Xu Huanwen and give this sister-in-law a try.

"Sister-in-law, as the Dowager’s niece, shouldn’t you visit the Dowager’s palace more often?"

Lady Li smiled gently. "The Dowager is in poor health and dislikes receiving outsiders."

At the word "outsiders," Xiangjun raised an eyebrow.

"And…" Lady Li continued, "Now that I’ve married my husband, I am part of the Xu family. In terms of closeness, Your Highness and I are the true kin."

In her past life, Xiangjun had been of low birth and often envied these noblewomen.

But in this life, she had let go of such obsessions and come to appreciate them more.

They were perceptive, understanding the meaning behind others’ words. Most had been trained to be clever and courteous, speaking with ease and always knowing where their core interests lay.

Except for Xue Jiaojiao, Xiangjun hadn’t met a single noblewoman who wasn’t sharp.

Sometimes, Xiangjun even wondered—was that why men adored Xue Jiaojiao so much? Because she was different?

Snapping back to the present, Xiangjun decided to trust Lady Li completely.

She picked up her teacup and took a sip, then smiled. "Did my brother send you to see me because he has something to discuss?"

"Not particularly urgent," Lady Li also took a sip of tea before suddenly remembering something. "Oh, there’s a funny story I must tell Your Highness. Yesterday, Commander Zhou came to speak with my husband. They got along so well that they drank too much. Commander Zhou even taught my husband how to wield a sword in the courtyard. But my husband is a scholar—how could he possibly handle a sword? Yet he insisted on showing off. After practicing for a long time without success, this morning, he couldn’t even lift his arm."

Xiangjun and Lady Li exchanged a glance, both covering their mouths with handkerchiefs as they laughed.

"My brother is already so old—why does he still act like a young boy? Sister-in-law, you should hurry and give him children. Once he becomes a father, he’ll be more steady."

Lady Li laughed coquettishly, finally showing a hint of girlishness.

Only then did Xiangjun beckon Little Luzhi to bring over a token.

"This is a palace entry pass. Sister-in-law, you won’t need to submit a calling card in advance for future visits. I look forward to your company."

After Lady Li left, Xiangjun’s heart was completely at ease.

Just as she was about to call Little Luzhi over for a massage, Meng Mei entered and announced, "Your Highness, Consort Jiang is in labor. Will you go see her?"

chapters.title: The Dog Emperor Has a Vile Heart
chapters.content:
Xiangjun kept vigil all night, and finally, Jiang Guiren gave birth.

It was a little princess.

The Emperor did not even come to see her once. It was not until the next day after court that he came to see Jiang Guiren and the Third Princess.

Since several princes had been born in the palace recently, and it had been a long time since a princess was born, the Emperor also took a liking to this princess. Thus, he elevated Jiang Guiren’s status.

Jiang Guiren was now Jiang Guiji.

The Empress Dowager also arrived late. Seeing Xiangjun and the Emperor gathered around Jiang Guiren, laughing and chatting, it looked as if they were the true couple of the harem.

Cui Jiaojiao’s heart ached. She recalled what General Wang had said to her.

When Xiangjun saw the Empress approaching, she immediately stood up and made way.

After the boat incident, there seemed to be a barrier between the Emperor and the Empress.

Xiangjun watched as the two now spoke comforting words to Jiang Guiren. She recalled when she gave birth to Yuanlang. She realized that now, the Emperor and Cui Jiaojiao also had the air of a superficial marriage.

Just like the Emperor and Empress Yang back then.

Even after visiting Jiang Guiren, the Emperor directly took Xiangjun’s hand and, in front of the Empress, went to Chengxiang Palace.

Even Mengmei noticed something was amiss. The next day, as soon as the Emperor left, she said to Xiangjun, “Your Majesty, this servant feels that the Emperor seems to have changed toward you.”

“How so?”

Mengmei thought carefully about her wording before cautiously saying, “This servant feels that the Emperor seems… to have some genuine affection for you now.”

“What does it matter if he has genuine affection or not?”

Xiangjun needed the Emperor’s favor, but she did not care how he truly felt about her.

Mengmei did not understand and asked, “Isn’t Your Majesty the one who cares most about sincerity?”

“That is only for my own people. The Emperor can like whoever he wants. As long as he doesn’t block my path, it’s fine.”

Mengmei hesitated before saying, “Your Majesty, if the Emperor truly treats you well, this servant shouldn’t say this, but if the Emperor is truly good to you, it would be better for you and the Emperor to be on good terms…”

Xiangjun knew what Mengmei was about to say.

“Better than being ambiguously involved with a eunuch, is that it?”

Mengmei nodded.

Xiangjun laughed.

“Our Emperor cannot be trusted. When he likes someone, he showers them with affection, but when he stops liking them, he can be very heartless.”

In her past life, Xiangjun dared to be so arrogant in the harem and offend so many people, partly because she had misunderstood the Emperor’s favor as love.

Xiangjun was not stupid. If the Emperor had not made her feel loved in her past life, how would she have dared to provoke those concubines of higher rank?

But the Emperor, when he liked her, could have three children with her.

If she accidentally angered him, he could quickly turn cold. With just a casual order to cut open her belly to take the child, he could end her life.

So Xiangjun knew that the Emperor’s love was dangerous.

Xiangjun held up a new hairpin sent by Sizhenfang, trying it on her head. If she did not like it, she threw it aside.

Mengmei watched Xiangjun frown as she picked through the items, thinking her mistress was as cute as a child.

After picking and choosing, she finally settled on the newly made serpent bracelet.

“This one will do. I don’t want the others.”

…

A few days later, an event occurred that made Mengmei completely believe Xiangjun’s words.

The Emperor was about to go to Mount Tai for the Fengshan ceremony, but he suddenly decided to take the Empress with him.

Although the Empress was now stable in her pregnancy, she was still carrying a child. Despite the hardships of travel, the Emperor insisted on taking her along. Those who did not know might think the Emperor and Empress were deeply in love. But those who knew…

Xiangjun truly did not understand.

Mengmei sighed, “Just a few days ago, the Emperor was still cold and detached toward the Empress. How come now they are suddenly inseparable?”

“Who knows!”

Xiangjun was very annoyed. Unexpectedly, Gu Tingxue arrived.

As soon as he came, he had someone bring Yuanlang to him.

Watching Gu Tingxue hold Yuanlang and take out a cloth tiger from somewhere to amuse him, Xiangjun’s heart was filled with annoyance.

“Have the Emperor and the Empress reconciled?”

Gu Tingxue glanced at Xiangjun.

“Your Majesty is now my opponent. Why are you asking me for news?”

Xiangjun said irritably, “I’m still holding my child. Why be so calculating? It’s not a big deal. I’m just curious.”

Gu Tingxue smiled, continuing to amuse Yuanlang as he said, “Officially, the Emperor says he is taking the Empress to Fengshan because the Empress has been anxious since her pregnancy, and this child is unstable. Only the dragon’s energy can ensure a safe delivery. The Emperor must accompany the Empress at all times, so he has to take her along.”

“I don’t want to hear those empty words. Say something useful.”

Gu Tingxue finally looked at Xiangjun, his eyes cunning. “The Emperor still fears General Wang.”

“What does General Wang have to do with this again?” Xiangjun furrowed her beautiful willow-leaf brows. “Could it be that the Emperor, to appease General Wang, must favor the Empress?”

Gu Tingxue scoffed. “The imperial city is heavily guarded, with hundreds of thousands of Shence Army troops and the Emperor’s personal Twelve Guards. But once outside the imperial city, at Mount Tai, it will be close to General Wang’s troops. If General Wang has any other ideas…”

Xiangjun suddenly realized, “The Emperor is using the Empress as a hostage. With the Empress by his side, General Wang won’t dare to rebel, is that it?”

Gu Tingxue nodded.

Xiangjun sat on the soft couch, feeling that many things she had not understood before now made sense.

She had known that the Emperor was not some lovesick fool.

It turned out the Emperor did not tolerate the Empress out of love. He was using her.

It was easy to see how useful Cui Jiaojiao was. With her, the Emperor effortlessly controlled his two biggest rivals by dangling her in front of the two Wangs.

Prince Jin and General Wang did not even take concubines. In their thirties, they did not even have children.

Children and in-laws were very useful.

Even if General Wang and the former Crown Prince, Prince Jin, had some influence now, if they died without descendants, their power would quickly dissipate.

Xiangjun had always wanted to be the Emperor’s blade, hoping to rise step by step in the palace. She never expected that this path had long been taken to the extreme by Cui Jiaojiao, unknowingly.

Cui Jiaojiao was the Emperor’s most useful blade.

She never expected that even in being a blade, she still lost to Cui Jiaojiao.

Xiangjun coldly humphed, “That dog Emperor has a truly vile heart.”

Gu Tingxue gently covered Yuanlang’s ears.

Only after Xiangjun finished cursing did he let go.

Xiangjun thought for a moment and asked again, “If General Wang does not lead troops to rebel but instead tries to assassinate the Emperor, is that possible?”

Gu Tingxue looked up, “Why does Your Majesty ask this?”

“I’m just curious…”

---

chapters.title: The Little Debt Collector is Going to Doom His Own Mother!
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue finally averted his gaze and continued to play with Yuanlang using the cloth tiger.

“The Emperor’s personal army, apart from the Shence Army, includes the Twelve Guards. The Emperor personally commands the Twelve Guards. Among them, the Longxiang Guard has secret guards and death attendants. Even I cannot come into contact with these people.”

Xiangjun sighed in her heart. That dog Emperor was quite hard to kill.

Xiangjun put on a melancholic expression. Realizing Gu Tingxue was observing her, she quickly hid her disappointed look and asked, “The Emperor is leaving for Fengshan in a few days. Why aren’t you busy? How do you have time to play with the child here?”

“This time, the Emperor has appointed Zhou Zidou and Bai Fan to be in charge of the escort. I am to stay in the capital to guard the imperial city.”

“Ah?”

Xiangjun’s disappointment was too obvious.

Gu Tingxue coldly glanced at her.

“Is Your Majesty disappointed?”

“How could that be?”

Gu Tingxue coldly smiled, “That’s true. If I stay in the imperial city every day, how can Your Majesty conveniently replace my people in the palace with yours?”

Xiangjun forced a smile, “Where did that come from? I’m happy that Tingxue is staying in the imperial city.”

Forget it. Xiangjun resentfully tugged at the handkerchief in her hand.

If that was the case, she would first replace the others with her own people. She would leave Gu Tingxue’s people alone for now.

He couldn’t stay in the palace forever.

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun’s secretly angry little expression and couldn’t help but smile. Then he continued to play with Yuanlang.

…

Soon, the day of the Emperor’s departure arrived. Just before leaving, he vaguely felt that the Noble Consort and the other concubines in the harem seemed somewhat pleased.

As soon as the Emperor left, everyone relaxed.

With three masters gone and two remaining, the Empress Dowager was unwell and rarely went out, and the Noble Consort was generous. The sisters had a good time playing and making merry.

But Xiangjun was still well-behaved and did not act as if she were the sole mistress of the harem.

Taking advantage of the two months while the Emperor was at Mount Tai for the Fengshan ceremony, she went to Renshou Palace every day to accompany the Empress Dowager.

“The Emperor and Empress are both gone. Why don’t you relax in your Chengxiang Palace instead of coming to me, an old woman, to follow rules every day?”

Xiangjun immediately pledged her loyalty to the Empress Dowager, “Previously, this concubine had to attend to the Emperor and Empress. Although I often came to Renshou Palace to pay my respects, it was not like now, where I can accompany Your Majesty every day. Your Majesty, please don’t send this concubine away.”

Xiangjun had thought that the Empress Dowager would probably not want her to come every day, especially since Yuanlang was quite noisy.

But unexpectedly, upon hearing Xiangjun’s words, the Empress Dowager simply patted her hand and said, “It’s fortunate that you have such filial piety. No wonder the Emperor favors you. You are sensible. Since you don’t find this old woman boring, I am also happy to see you every day.”

Xiangjun actually quite enjoyed spending time with the Empress Dowager.

She felt that spending more time with the previous winner might allow her to absorb some of the Empress Dowager’s good fortune.

Xiangjun brought Yuanlang with her every day to accompany the Empress Dowager.

Yuanlang could now babble a few words. He couldn’t speak in full sentences, but he constantly babbled, which was quite adorable.

One day, the Empress Dowager and Xiangjun were watching Yuanlang toddle unsteadily on his short legs.

Yuanlang was very fair and tender. The little child walked while clapping his hands, babbling continuously, as if he had endless words to say.

The Empress Dowager laughed so hard her eyes narrowed. She clearly adored this child.

Even though she didn’t understand what Yuanlang was saying, she still responded to him.

“Yes, our Yuanlang walks well.”

“That’s right, our Yuanlang has strong legs.”

As if responding to the Empress Dowager, Yuanlang stomped his short legs a couple more times.

Coincidentally, Gu Tingxue arrived at Renshou Palace at this moment.

Seeing Xiangjun there as well, Gu Tingxue’s expression remained calm. He did not even glance at the Fifth Prince, only greeting the Empress Dowager.

Unexpectedly, as soon as he finished greeting, Yuanlang’s short legs moved quickly, and he directly pounced onto Gu Tingxue, hugging his leg and starting to babble at him. As he babbled, he also twisted his little bottom.

Gu Tingxue’s body stiffened, and Xiangjun’s smile froze.
