Only Yuanlang continued to reach out his hands, asking Gu Tingxue to hold him.

At this moment, every hair on Xiangjun’s body stood on end.

She suddenly realized that she had made the mistake of becoming arrogant and careless.

She had actually overlooked this little debt collector, Yuanlang.

He was only one year old. How could he act?

He simply liked whoever he liked.

Xiangjun subconsciously swallowed her saliva but still managed to steady her emotions. She smiled and said, “I didn’t expect Yuanlang to like Lord Gu so much.”

The Empress Dowager still had her kind and benevolent expression, smiling as she watched Yuanlang and Gu Tingxue. She sighed and said, “Tingxue has a heavy killing aura. In the past, he was the least liked by children. The palace’s princes and princesses would cry when they got close to him. It’s rare that Yuanlang is not afraid of him. It must be fate.”

The Empress Dowager’s words made cold sweat break out on Xiangjun’s back.

She tightly gripped the agate bracelet on her wrist and glanced at Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue understood and smiled at the Empress Dowager, saying, “This official has killed many, so naturally, I carry some malevolent energy. The Fifth Prince is truly a dragon’s son. He is not afraid of the malevolent energy on me. In the future, he will surely be a very impressive prince.”

As if deliberately defying Gu Tingxue, Yuanlang, after stretching out his hand for so long without being picked up, pouted and burst into tears.

Xiangjun was so angry she gnashed her teeth. What an impressive prince indeed!

Little Luzi saw this and quickly stepped forward to take Yuanlang away.

But Yuanlang tightly grabbed Gu Tingxue’s trouser leg and refused to let go, crying so hard that snot bubbles came out.

The Empress Dowager, seeing this, only smiled kindly and said to Gu Tingxue, “Tingxue, the Fifth Prince wants you to hold him. Then you should hold him.”

“This official obeys.”

Gu Tingxue then obeyed and picked up the Fifth Prince.

Unexpectedly, as soon as Gu Tingxue held him, the Fifth Prince stopped crying. He rested his little head on Gu Tingxue’s chest, nuzzled his neck a couple of times, hummed twice, and immediately quieted down.

Xiangjun took a deep breath and quickly stood up, smiling awkwardly.

She walked up to Gu Tingxue and softly said to her son, “Alright, Yuanlang, be good. Don’t bother Lord Gu. He has business to discuss with the Empress Dowager. Come, let Mother hold you.”

Unexpectedly, Yuanlang glanced at Xiangjun, turned his head away, and completely ignored her. He stretched out his hand and focused on playing with the tassel on Gu Tingxue’s hat.

Xiangjun felt like hitting Yuanlang at this moment.

This little debt collector was going to doom his own mother!

chapters.title: Let's Just Die Together
chapters.content:
Xiangjun felt the hair all over her body stand on end.

She heard the Empress Dowager let out a soft laugh, her voice gentle as she said, "Alright, I am tired too. Tingxue, you take the Fifth Prince back to Chengxiang Palace for me. After the midday rest, you may return."

"Yes, this humble servant obeys."

After leaving the Empress Dowager's Ren Shou Palace, Xiangjun sat in the palanquin with a dark expression.

Gu Tingxue stood beside Xiangjun, holding Yuanlang.

Seeing Yuanlang still happily babbling in Gu Tingxue's arms, Xiangjun was so angry that she pinched Yuanlang's arm hard.

Yuanlang burst into tears, and only then did Xiangjun order the palanquin to be lifted.

The group continued toward Chengxiang Palace.

Whenever Gu Tingxue managed to soothe Yuanlang, Xiangjun would immediately give Xiao Luzi a look, signaling him to pinch Yuanlang again.

How could Xiao Luzi dare? On one side was the Consort's threatening gaze, and on the other was Gu Tingxue's murderous stare. He was truly torn.

Why did the Consort always make him do such things?

After much deliberation, Xiao Luzi decided to go all the way. Once he became the Consort's man, he had to do the Consort's bidding!

So, along the way, Xiao Luzi kept his eyes and ears open, always managing to unexpectedly pinch the Fifth Prince.

Finally, the Fifth Prince cried all the way back to Chengxiang Palace.

The palace servants who witnessed this scene couldn't help but sigh. Truly, Master Gu was not liked by children. Look how he had scared the Fifth Prince.

...

Xiangjun didn't say a word the entire way. When they returned to Chengxiang Palace, Yuanlang was still babbling in Gu Tingxue's arms, drooling and asking to be held.

This time, Xiangjun was truly angry. She sharply ordered Xiao Luzi, "What are you waiting for? Hurry up and take Yuanlang away!"

Yuanlang pouted and started crying again, but since they were in Chengxiang Palace and the Consort was furious, no one dared to pity the Fifth Prince. They immediately took him away to the wet nurse.

Meng Mei and Xi Yu, seeing Gu Tingxue there and that the Consort seemed to have something to say to him, quickly excused themselves.

Only Xiangjun and Gu Tingxue remained in the room.

Xiangjun's face was dark, like a storm was brewing.

"Why are you so worried?" Gu Tingxue, on the other hand, was indifferent and even poured a cup of tea for Xiangjun.

Xiangjun took the tea and placed it heavily on the table. "That is the Empress Dowager. She managed to return after seven years in Bei Meng and became Empress from a mere palace maid, eventually helping our current Emperor ascend the throne. Do you think we haven't revealed enough today? The Empress Dowager has noticed something. She asked you to take Yuanlang back because she already suspects us."

Xiangjun was deeply worried, tightly clutching her agate bracelet.

"I just don't know how much the Empress Dowager has guessed."

"The Empress Dowager, having experienced the struggle for the throne, would naturally consider it normal for a concubine and a eunuch close to the Emperor to collude—it's just for the sake of the Fifth Prince."

"Yuanlang is so close to you. Can our relationship be just a collusion? Do you think the Empress Dowager is as easy to placate as the Empress? We have been careless. This small flaw could cost us our lives."

Xiangjun was truly worried.

"The Empress Dowager won't do anything to us."

"Why are you so sure?"

"The Empress Dowager is indeed different from ordinary women. Even if she guesses something about us, in her eyes, it's not a big deal. The Empress Dowager only considers matters that shake the foundation of the nation or the Emperor's throne as serious. This trivial matter between us is nothing. Do you think the only concubine in the harem who has an ambiguous relationship with a eunuch is you? In the deep palace, with its loneliness, who doesn't find a little fun for themselves?"

Xiangjun hadn't expected such cautious Gu Tingxue to say something so bold.

"I am the Emperor's favored concubine and have borne him a son. You are the Emperor's close confidant, commanding the Shence Army, the Privy Council, and the Censorate. If the two of us collude, isn't that enough to shake the foundation of the nation?"

"I am just a eunuch who can only wield power by relying on the Emperor. You are just a concubine who has some dignity because of the Emperor's favor. What do people like us amount to?"

Xiangjun felt that this reasoning wasn't quite right, but Gu Tingxue was so certain, and he knew the Empress Dowager better than she did. For a moment, Xiangjun was somewhat swayed.

"Is the Empress Dowager really not going to do anything to us?"

"No."

"Why are you so sure?"

"Because I wouldn't joke with our lives. You can rest assured."

Xiangjun still frowned. "This time, the Empress Dowager saw us, and there's still a chance to fix it. But if next time, in front of the Emperor, Yuanlang acts the same way towards you... I'm afraid the two of us..."

Hearing the words "the two of us," Gu Tingxue finally looked up at Xiangjun.

Xiangjun let out a cold, self-deprecating laugh, looking ahead with worry. "If the Emperor really finds out, let's not fight over who is higher. Let's just die together."

Gu Tingxue's lips curled up slightly. He picked up the teacup and slowly said, "Dying together with you, Consort, wouldn't be so bad."

"Don't even think about dying!" Xiangjun glared at Gu Tingxue fiercely. "No matter what, you must be more careful in the future. It's best if no one sees you interacting with Yuanlang. Avoid him from now on. He's still young; in a few months, he'll forget you. When Yuanlang is older and knows how to pretend, then we can reconsider. Today's incident should serve as a warning for us."

Gu Tingxue didn't speak, lowering his gaze to look at the tea in front of him.

After a long while, he spoke in a somewhat low and sinister voice, "Yes, I am indeed something that cannot be seen by others."

"This isn't about whether I can be seen or not. This is a matter of life and death."

"I understand." Gu Tingxue stood up. "I will go to Ren Shou Palace first to see what the Empress Dowager thinks. You shouldn't worry, Consort."

Gu Tingxue left.

But how could Xiangjun be at ease?

She tossed and turned all night, thinking about how to explain herself if the Empress Dowager made a move, how to defend herself if the Empress Dowager told the Emperor.

But the Emperor would never believe her over the Empress Dowager.

The Empress Dowager had once held great power but still handed it over to her own son.

What reason would she have now to deceive the Emperor?

So the Emperor would definitely believe the Empress Dowager.

But then she thought, the Empress Dowager didn't have real evidence.

She was now a Noble Consort. Even if the Emperor and the Empress Dowager wanted to deal with her, it wouldn't be that simple. They would need a reasonable excuse.

Before that, they would probably bide their time. After all, there was still the Fifth Prince to consider; they would have to handle things with some decorum.

So she still had time to plan.

If it really came to a dead end, she would have to fight to the death, risking everything for a chance.

She thought groggily until midnight when she suddenly felt movement behind her.

"Who is it!"

Xiangjun's eyes snapped open, but she quickly smelled a familiar scent.

"Who else could it be?" Gu Tingxue's voice came from the darkness. "Why are you so panicked today, Consort?"

chapters.title: The Consort Will Surely Sacrifice My Life to Save Herself
chapters.content:
Xiangjun let out a sigh of relief and glared at Gu Tingxue hatefully.

"Naturally, I'm afraid the Empress Dowager sent someone to kill me."

Xiangjun thought that she should also get a couple of secret guards to protect herself. If that didn't work, she could ask her father to find a couple of skilled women to enter the palace as palace maids.

"If the Empress Dowager wanted to kill you, she wouldn't be in such a hurry, nor would she use a method that could easily leave evidence. Just sleep peacefully, Consort."

Hearing Gu Tingxue say this, how could Xiangjun be at ease?

She got up anxiously and saw Gu Tingxue lying on the bed with his eyes closed, hands crossed over his chest, as if ready to sleep. She kicked him in frustration.

"Why are you only coming now? I've been waiting anxiously!"

"Running errands for the Empress Dowager outside the palace."

"What errands?"

Seeing that Gu Tingxue wasn't speaking, Xiangjun pushed him again.

"Speak!"

Gu Tingxue had no choice but to open his eyes and sit up, explaining, "The Empress Dowager doesn't want the Emperor to know that she has been in contact with the forces in Jiangnan, so she has me handle these matters privately for her."

This was something Xiangjun hadn't expected. It seemed that the Empress Dowager and the Emperor, this mother and son, were not without suspicions of each other.

"Why doesn't the Emperor want the Empress Dowager to be in contact with the forces in Jiangnan?"

"Song Feijing's mother was the Empress Dowager's person. Given the Emperor's attitude towards Song Feijing, you should know how much the Emperor despises the Jiangnan faction. The Jiangnan gentry has deep roots and is impenetrable. Even if Song Feijing's faction has been eliminated, that was only the Jiangnan forces in the capital. The roots of the Jiangnan clans remain untouched."

"Why didn't the Emperor take the opportunity with Song Feijing's matter to deal with the old forces of Jiangnan?"

"It's not that he didn't try; it's that he couldn't. Even if the people on the surface are replaced, new ones will take their place immediately. Those century-old clans are the core of Jiangnan, and their foundations are not easily shaken."

"The Emperor has imperial power and military control. If he is determined, can't he still deal with the Jiangnan clans?"

"Is it that easy? Jiangnan cannot be in chaos. The taxes from the three provinces of Jiangnan account for one-third of the court's annual revenue. If Jiangnan is in turmoil, the entire country will be in chaos. Bei Meng in the north will immediately turn against us. The Emperor is currently at a loss for what to do with them."

These were things Xiangjun hadn't understood before. Now, after careful thought, it did make sense.

It seemed that even the most powerful people in the world were still constrained by various matters. The affairs of the world were interconnected, and pulling one thread could move the entire web. Sometimes, even an ant could take advantage of the situation and shake a great tree.

Seeing Xiangjun lost in thought with a furrowed brow, Gu Tingxue said, "These matters don't concern you. Don't worry about them."

"I was just thinking that the Empress Dowager relied on the Jiangnan clans to secure her position as Empress, and later, as Empress Dowager, she must have given Jiangnan many benefits. They have mutually achieved success. Now that the Emperor despises the Jiangnan clans, doesn't that mean the Emperor and the Empress Dowager inherently have conflicting interests? Is it because the Empress Dowager has you secretly handling matters for her that you think she won't do anything to us?"

"Something like that."

Xiangjun was still somewhat uneasy.

"I still feel a bit panicked. After all, the Empress Dowager and the Emperor are mother and son, while we are outsiders. I'm afraid the Empress Dowager will settle scores with us later..."

"If I tell you that starting tomorrow, the Empress Dowager has ordered me to come to Chengxiang Palace every morning to take Yuanlang to Ren Shou Palace and bring him back in the evening, will you still be worried?"

Xiangjun immediately tensed up. "Why would the Empress Dowager do that? Is she trying to take my child away? If the Empress Dowager takes the Fifth Prince away, she must be preparing to get rid of me."

"If she wanted to take Yuanlang away, why would she have me bring him back in the evening? I am under the Empress Dowager's orders to take Yuanlang back and forth every day until the Emperor returns from the Fengshan ceremony in two months. After two months of daily contact, even if the Emperor later discovers that Yuanlang likes me, what's so strange about that?"

Xiangjun realized and asked in surprise, "The Empress Dowager is helping you? Why?"

Gu Tingxue closed his eyes, as if tired, and said indifferently, "Because I am handling matters for the Empress Dowager."

Xiangjun's intuition told her that things weren't that simple.

But given the circumstances, the fact that the Empress Dowager was willing to cover for them was already the best outcome.

She really didn't dare to investigate further.

Xiangjun had some suspicions about the relationship between the two, but since Tingxue wasn't willing to talk, it was either something he couldn't say or something that would cause trouble for Xiangjun if she knew.

The Empress Dowager's matters were better left unasked.

Curiosity could lead to trouble.

"Not worried anymore. Can we sleep now? I'm very tired." Gu Tingxue said with his eyes closed.

Xiangjun couldn't help but kick him.

"What are you doing? Aren't you breaking up with me? Then why are you here to sleep?"

"I haven't broken up with you, Consort. It's you who wants to break up with me. Tomorrow, I still have to take Yuanlang to Ren Shou Palace. Running back and forth is troublesome, so I'll just borrow your bed for a night."

Seeing Gu Tingxue lying down beside her without a care, Xiangjun lost her temper.

Listening to Gu Tingxue's steady breathing, Xiangjun couldn't sleep at all.

She realized that she had accidentally gotten involved in the royal family's most hidden secrets.

She was afraid she had really brought trouble upon herself.

Suddenly, she heard Gu Tingxue's voice.

With his eyes still closed, as if talking in his sleep, Gu Tingxue asked, "If the Empress Dowager had chosen not to help us today but instead planned to expose our collusion to the Emperor, how would you, Consort, have handled the matter?"

Xiangjun fell silent, not speaking. But her gaze towards Gu Tingxue deepened.

Gu Tingxue gave a self-deprecating smile, still not opening his eyes, his hands crossed over his chest as if he might fall asleep at any moment.

"Without thinking, I know that the Consort would surely sacrifice my life to save her own."

The room was very quiet, so quiet that the sound of their breathing rising and falling could be heard.

After a long time, seeing that Gu Tingxue's breathing had steadied and he seemed to have fallen asleep completely, Xiangjun finally spoke in a very soft voice, "As long as you are still my person, I will not let you die. I will do everything in my power to protect you until the very end, even if it means a fight to the death with the Emperor and the Empress Dowager, exhausting every possible means. I keep my word."

Seeing that Gu Tingxue did not respond, Xiangjun slowly closed her eyes.

After a long while, Gu Tingxue opened his eyes.

He gently turned his head to look at the sleeping Xiangjun, then turned back, continuing to lie flat on the bed, staring into the dark void.

Only his eyes, in the darkness, were extremely bright.

chapters.title: Xiangjun Has Never Felt This Guilty in Her Life
chapters.content:
In the days that followed, Xiangjun no longer visited the Empress Dowager’s palace every day.

Otherwise, Gu Tingxue’s daily trips to pick up and drop off Yuanlang would seem too deliberate.

Xiangjun shook off her weariness and focused her energy. With the Emperor and Empress away, she needed to properly reorganize the harem. She would remove others’ people and replace them with her own.

However, the Empress Dowager’s and Gu Tingxue’s people still couldn’t be touched lightly, but placing a few of her own people to share the power was harmless. How far they could go would depend on their own abilities.

Though Concubine De also had the authority to assist in managing the six palaces, it was merely a title. The truly important positions were all in Xiangjun’s hands.

As she reorganized the harem, she unexpectedly discovered that three more concubines were pregnant.

Xiangjun couldn’t help but marvel— the Emperor’s diligent efforts over the past few months had not been in vain.

Moreover, in her previous life, the Emperor’s harem had never had so many children.

It turned out the truly impressive one wasn’t the Emperor, but she, Xu Xiangjun.

Before the Emperor returned, Xiangjun had the news of the concubines’ pregnancies kept secret.

With the power of the harem now in her hands, she absolutely would not allow any harm to come to the concubines.

The children had to be kept safe and sound.

Physician Liu and his colleagues from the Imperial Physicians’ Office were kept busy day and night.

Taking this opportunity, Xiangjun found a pretext to punish the female officials from the Shanggong Bureau and replaced them with her own people.

Life in the palace became quite peaceful after that.

Except for Gu Tingxue’s unwavering habit of picking up and dropping off Yuanlang every morning and evening, which made Xiangjun uneasy, these past two months had been quite comfortable for her.

But since the Empress Dowager had not taken any further action, Xiangjun had to let the matter rest for now.

After all, since the Empress Dowager hadn’t exposed anything, she couldn’t confront her either, right?

This unspoken understanding was mutual. As long as the Empress Dowager didn’t expose her, Xiangjun was happy to accept the favor.

However, a shadow lingered in Xiangjun’s heart— what secret did the Empress Dowager, the Emperor, and Gu Tingxue share that she didn’t know?

Finally, the imperial procession returned to the palace.

The Emperor had finally returned with the Empress.

It was said that the journey had been smooth, and the Emperor was in high spirits, believing it to be heaven’s approval of his achievements in both governance and military prowess.

But unexpectedly, as soon as he returned, someone came to cause trouble.

Concubine De hurriedly went to the Taiji Hall to report that Xiangjun had taken advantage of the Emperor’s absence to replace several key eunuchs and female officials in the palace, accusing her of abusing power for personal gain and monopolizing authority.

Before Concubine De could finish, Xiangjun coincidentally arrived at the Taiji Hall as well.

When Xiangjun joyfully informed the Emperor that three concubines were pregnant and their pregnancies were stable, the Emperor was so overjoyed that he stood up immediately.

The Emperor walked over to Xiangjun and, in his excitement, took her hand. “Beloved Consort, is this true?”

“How would this concubine dare deceive Your Majesty with such matters?”

The Emperor was naturally delighted to hear Xiangjun’s news.

It seemed he was indeed in his prime, and the flourishing of imperial heirs also proved the stability of his rule and the prosperity of the nation.

“Your Majesty has just returned from the Mount Tai ceremony, and now the palace has three more pregnant concubines. Isn’t this a great auspicious sign? It shows that Your Majesty is truly accomplished in both governance and military affairs. The gods are blessing Your Majesty.”

Xiangjun’s words greatly pleased the Emperor.

Concubine De’s face turned green with envy.

In the past, there had only been two imperial sons in the harem, but now, aside from the Second Prince, there were four others, and with three more concubines expecting, the palace would soon be filled with children.

Her eldest son would only become less noticeable.

Xiangjun glanced at Concubine De and asked, “Just now, as this concubine entered, I happened to overhear Concubine De mentioning the palace’s chief eunuchs. Since Concubine De and I share the duty of managing the six palaces, if there’s anything unclear, she can ask me directly. Why trouble Your Majesty with such trivial matters?”

Seeing that Concubine De had nothing to say, Xiangjun quickly reported to the Emperor about her reorganization of the six palaces.

She justified the replacements by saying that some of the previous servants had been too cunning, and the newly entered concubines, coming from humble backgrounds, had been bullied by those shrewd servants.

To ensure the three pregnant concubines could rest peacefully, she had no choice but to punish a few people.

With the news of the three pregnancies, the Emperor didn’t mind Xiangjun replacing a few eunuchs and female officials.

“If they’ve been replaced, then so be it. It’s not a serious matter. Even if they did nothing wrong, you are my Noble Consort. If you want to replace a few servants you dislike, what’s there to be so cautious about?” The Emperor held Xiangjun’s hand and said, “With you managing the harem, I am at ease.”

Concubine De could only force an awkward smile.

“Yes, Your Majesty is right. This concubine was indeed too hasty. I hope Noble Consort will not hold it against me.”

The Emperor shot Concubine De a cold glance.

“You’ve been in the palace for over a decade. How can you still be so immature? If you can’t manage the harem properly, then don’t manage it at all.”

After reprimanding Concubine De, the Emperor took Xiangjun with him to pay respects to the Empress Dowager.

The Empress Dowager had just learned the news and was naturally overjoyed. She looked at Xiangjun affectionately and said, “You are good at keeping secrets. Such wonderful news, and you waited until the Emperor returned to share it with me.”

Xiangjun was startled by the Empress Dowager’s remark about her being “good at keeping secrets.” She quickly knelt and said, “It is this concubine’s fault. I only wanted Your Majesty to be the first to know. Please punish me, Empress Dowager.”

“If I were to punish you, then there would be no one in this palace deserving of reward. You’ve done well.”

Seeing that the Empress Dowager was not angry, Xiangjun finally breathed a sigh of relief.

“The Empress Dowager isn’t angry with you. Get up,” the Emperor said.

As Xiangjun was about to rise, someone grabbed her arm and helped her up.

She looked up and saw the Emperor gazing at her tenderly with a smile. For some reason, his gaze made her feel uneasy.

The Empress Dowager noticed the Emperor helping Xiangjun up and smiled. Then she asked, “Why isn’t the Empress here?”

“Jiao’s pregnancy is advanced, and the journey back was tiring. She’s feeling unwell, so I had her rest. She’ll come to pay her respects to Mother tomorrow.”

“If she’s not feeling well, let her continue resting. There’s no need for her to come see me.” Then, turning to Xiangjun, she said affectionately, “The Noble Consort has truly fulfilled her duties as a concubine. With so many imperial heirs, I can rest assured. Even if I were to meet the late Emperor now, I would have no regrets.”

“Mother, you are in good health. You must live to see your grandchildren grow up.”

The Empress Dowager sighed and reached out to pat the Emperor’s hand gently. “I know my own body best. I may look fine on the outside, but inside, I’ve been unwell for a long time. However...”

The Empress Dowager then looked at Xiangjun, her gaze seemingly piercing through her.

“With the Noble Consort by the Emperor’s side, I am at ease.”

Xiangjun had never felt this guilty in her life.

What was the Empress Dowager trying to do?

Was she genuinely promoting her in front of the Emperor, or was she deliberately hinting at something?

---

chapters.title: Love Extends to the Crow
chapters.content:
Xiangjun’s back broke out in sweat again, but she had no time to dwell on it, because at that moment, Gu Tingxue entered, leading Yuanlang by the hand.

The Emperor was quite surprised by this scene.

His gaze flickered to the small hands clasped between Yuanlang and Gu Tingxue, then shifted to the Empress Dowager.

“Why is the Fifth Prince in the Empress Dowager’s palace today?”

“The Noble Consort is a filial daughter. During the time the Emperor was away, she brought Yuanlang to see me every day. Knowing that the Noble Consort is busy managing the harem, I had Tingxue bring Yuanlang over each day and send him back in the evening. This way, not only does it fulfill the Noble Consort’s filial piety, but it also gives her some relief.”

The Emperor’s expression softened considerably. He nodded and said, “Mother truly cares for the Noble Consort.”

The Emperor glanced at Gu Tingxue, then beckoned Yuanlang over.

“I haven’t held the Fifth Prince in a long time. Yuanlang, come to your imperial father.”

Xiangjun’s heart leapt into her throat once more.

The Empress Dowager glanced at Xiangjun, then at Gu Tingxue, before settling her gaze on Yuanlang.

She wanted to see what scheme Gu Tingxue and Yuanlang were plotting by coming at this particular moment.

Yuanlang looked at the Emperor, hesitated for a moment, and then, just as the atmosphere grew tense, he let go of Gu Tingxue’s hand.

Next, everyone watched as Yuanlang, with his short little legs, ran toward the Emperor with a beaming smile, giggling as he happily threw himself into the Emperor’s arms.

Yuanlang’s adorable antics amused everyone in the Ren Shou Palace. The Empress Dowager’s gaze swept over Xiangjun, giving a satisfied smile before looking affectionately at the Emperor and the Fifth Prince in his arms.

Xiangjun let out a long sigh of relief.

The past two months of hard work had not been in vain.

Yuanlang kicked his legs joyfully in the Emperor’s arms, coaxing a rare paternal smile from him.

“It’s been two months since I last saw Yuanlang. He’s gotten chubbier.”

Yuanlang babbled incoherently, not making much sense.

The Emperor’s eyes crinkled with laughter.

“Does Yuanlang miss his imperial father?”

Seeing Yuanlang kicking his legs and still babbling, his expression changing, Xiangjun quickly said, “It’s better to let the wet nurse hold him. Don’t let his appearance fool you— though he’s small, his legs are strong. He might kick Your Majesty.”

The Emperor smiled and handed the Fifth Prince back to the wet nurse.

Xiangjun immediately placed a pastry in Yuanlang’s hand.

The wet nurse held Yuanlang, who happily munched on the pastry, a sight that truly stirred the Emperor’s paternal heart.

“The Fifth Prince is so well cared for, thanks to your dedication. Everyone in Chengxiang Hall will be rewarded.”

After the thanks were given, Xiangjun quickly took Yuanlang and excused herself.

“Your Majesty and Empress Dowager likely have more to discuss. This concubine will take Yuanlang back first.”

“Tingxue, escort the Fifth Prince for me. Return after you’re done.”

Once everyone had left and only the Emperor and Empress Dowager remained, the Emperor asked, “Mother, do you favor the Noble Consort?”

“It’s just love extending to the crow.”

The Emperor smiled. “Then why don’t I see Mother showing the same love to Jiao? Jiao and the Noble Consort are both people I cherish.”

The Empress Dowager gave a faint smile. “If the Empress fulfills her duties as a concubine, I wouldn’t have to be so harsh with her. In the past, being a favored concubine, a little foolishness didn’t matter. The Emperor could dote on her, and it wasn’t a big deal. But now that she’s the Empress, she must understand her responsibilities.”

“The Empress has just returned to the palace. What has she done to displease Mother?”

The Empress Dowager’s expression turned cold, and a rare flash of sharpness appeared in her eyes.

“During your pilgrimage to Mount Tai, General Wang secretly sent people to protect your Empress. Over the years, the Empress has maintained contact with General Wang. Don’t think I’m unaware.”

“General Wang is untouchable right now. The Empress did it for me.”

“Bian Wanrong is ill, and the Empress sent an imperial physician to visit her. Was that for Your Majesty as well?”

The Empress Dowager rarely spoke to the Emperor in such a severe tone.

Bian Wanrong was the birth mother of General Wang Zhou Chongkun, and she had been the Empress Dowager’s greatest rival in the past.

“That woman is the one I hate most in my life. If not for her, Tingxue would never have...”

At the mention of this, the Empress Dowager felt a surge of bitterness in her throat. She coughed twice, and a nearby maid quickly stepped forward to soothe her.

The Empress Dowager took a deep breath to regain her composure.

The Emperor’s expression darkened.

“Mother, don’t upset yourself. The Empress was indeed wrong in this matter.”

“I’ve let that wretched woman live until now for the Emperor’s sake. But my health is declining day by day. I’m afraid I will die before she does.”

The Emperor clenched his fists.

“Mother, don’t say such sad things. The debts owed by Bian Wanrong and her son to our family— I have never forgotten. It’s just that the timing isn’t right. It’s not that I don’t know about many things, but that I can’t act yet...”

The Empress Dowager looked deeply at her son, wanting to say something but ultimately holding back.

“Forget it. The Emperor has his own difficulties.” The Empress Dowager returned to her usual affectionate demeanor, patting the Emperor’s hand. “The small kitchen has prepared your favorite dishes. Stay and have dinner with me.”

...

Gu Tingxue escorted Xiangjun and Yuanlang back to Chengxiang Hall.

After returning, Yuanlang still refused to let go of Gu Tingxue, even when Xiangjun tried to hold him.

It was as if he didn’t know who his real mother was...

Upon seeing Xiangjun’s return, Xiaoluzi, who had been waiting in Chengxiang Hall, immediately rushed forward. “Noble Consort, how did it go?”

Xiangjun snatched Yuanlang into her arms. When Yuanlang started to cry, Gu Tingxue seemed about to soothe the child, so she quickly had the wet nurse take Yuanlang away.

Gu Tingxue had no choice but to exchange a look with Yuanlang, who was reaching for him, then silently sat down and poured himself a cup of tea.

Beside him, Xiaoluzi let out a sigh of relief and whispered to Xiangjun, “Noble Consort, since the matter is already done, can we burn that dress now? Having it in Chengxiang Hall makes this servant uneasy.”

Xiangjun nodded. “Be careful. Don’t leave a single trace.”

Xiaoluzi quickly left.

Left alone with Gu Tingxue, Xiangjun sat beside him, still worried.

“What did the Empress Dowager mean today? Why did she keep praising me? Was she trying to warn me?”

Gu Tingxue set down his teacup. “The Empress Dowager simply dislikes the Empress. If you want to win her favor, dealing with the Empress would be a good approach.”

Gu Tingxue stood up, preparing to leave.

“Are you returning to Ren Shou Palace?”

“First, I’ll go check on Yuanlang. I’ll return later.”

Gu Tingxue went to find Yuanlang.

Xiangjun coldly huffed and rolled her eyes at Gu Tingxue’s retreating figure. He really acts like Yuanlang’s father.

chapters.title: Truly Shameless
chapters.content:
Under the cover of night, Meng Mei, Xiao Luzi, and Xi Yu burned a bright yellow robe together.

For the past month, the three of them had taken turns wearing the robe in front of Yuan Lang. Whenever Yuan Lang pounced into the arms of the person wearing the yellow robe, they would let the Fifth Prince lick a piece of candy.

Thus, the person in the yellow robe became the Fifth Prince’s favorite.

As the bright yellow fabric gradually turned to ash, Xiao Luzi crossed his arms and let out a long sigh of relief.

Only he knew how anxious he had been this past month. Several times, he had woken up in the middle of the night from nightmares, dreaming that the robe in his room had been discovered.

"I never expected Her Highness’s plan to actually work… Now, the Fifth Prince’s favorite must be His Majesty."

Xi Yu, however, remained calm. She had always been the boldest among them.

"Her Highness said that raising a son is like raising a dog. Once you have the right method, they’re easy to train."

Meng Mei shot Xi Yu a glare. "Her Highness has truly spoiled you. She can say such things, but we cannot. The Fifth Prince is your master—how can you compare him to a dog?"

"Understood. It’s just that Her Highness always calls the Fifth Prince her ‘dog son,’ so I momentarily forgot. I won’t do it again."

Xi Yu gave an embarrassed smile and continued staring at the brazier.

Meng Mei had nothing more to say. Lately, Her Highness had been secretly cursing the Fifth Prince for favoring outsiders.

Even Lord Gu was strange. Though he had some conflicts with Her Highness, he had been even kinder to the Fifth Prince.

The three of them watched the brazier until the contents burned to nothing. Xiao Luzi stirred the ashes a few times to ensure nothing remained, then they dug a pit and buried the remnants.

As he stomped down the earth, Xiao Luzi sighed. "Our mistress is truly extraordinary. She casually does things that could wipe out nine generations, and even we, her servants, have grown bolder under her influence."

Meng Mei and Xi Yu silently watched the filled pit, nodding in approval.

Yes, making a dragon robe, burning a dragon robe—all to train the Fifth Prince, to make him happy whenever he saw the Emperor.

Our mistress truly has no reverence in her heart. She’s led the entire Chengxiang Palace to become daring alongside her.

...

After the Emperor returned to the palace, Zhou Zidu and Bai Fan were sent to the north.

Perhaps because there were no other military officers around, Gu Tingxue was once again summoned by the Emperor so frequently that he was never seen.

The harem, tightly controlled by Xiang Jun, was peaceful—so much so that even Xiang Jun found it boring.

The only interesting thing was that Yuan Lang had started talking, and the first word he learned was "Dadie" (a term of endearment for father).

The son was just as flattering as his mother, which delighted the Emperor. He rewarded the Fifth Prince generously.

The Empress was also nearing her due date. Her belly was unusually large, and Physician Liu said she was carrying twins.

Xiang Jun always felt something was off. How could Lady Yue, of all people, be so kind? She didn’t seek revenge for her lost child and instead genuinely helped the Empress have a smooth delivery?

But until she figured things out, Xiang Jun wouldn’t act recklessly.

Then came the night the Empress went into labor.

Xiang Jun didn’t sleep at all that night. She stayed awake, waiting.

Early the next morning, news came from Ganlu Palace:

Xue Jiaojiao had given birth to twins—a boy and a girl.

Xiang Jun was so angry she almost laughed.

So this was the female lead blessed by heaven?

Her luck was truly incredible. Not only could she give birth under such circumstances, but she had also smoothly delivered twins. No wonder she could be the female lead while Xiang Jun was just a cannon fodder.

The twins brought immense joy to Ganlu Palace. Great General Wang began lobbying for the Empress, and soon, rumors spread that the Empress’s pregnancy was a sign of good fortune.

Even officials from the imperial court suggested that the power of the harem should be returned to the Empress. It was improper for the Noble Consort to manage the harem in her place—it was overstepping her authority.

The people of Chengxiang Palace were furious.

Especially Xi Yu, who said through gritted teeth: "Her Highness worked so hard to manage the harem properly, and now the Empress wants to take back the power just because she had two children. Truly shameless."

Xiang Jun raised her eyes to look at Xi Yu.

Xi Yu realized her mistake and pouted. "This servant was just venting frustration for Her Highness."

"What’s there to be angry about? She is the Empress after all. As long as she holds that position, I must defer to her. It’s only right for her to reclaim the harem’s authority."

Xiao Luzi chimed in: "This was also Great General Wang’s doing. And His Majesty—why hasn’t he let Great General Wang return yet? Didn’t he say that after the New Year, once Great General Wang’s birth mother’s birthday had passed, he would leave? It’s almost the Mid-Autumn Festival now, so why is he still here?"

Xiang Jun gave a cold laugh. "I suspect His Majesty doesn’t want Great General Wang to leave. But don’t worry, he will have to go sooner or later."

If Xiang Jun remembered correctly, trouble would soon break out in the north. When that happened, the Emperor would have no choice but to send Great General Wang away.

"Is Her Highness not going to counterattack?" Meng Mei was also worried.

"Something about this still feels wrong to me. Let’s observe a little longer. Anyway, we have our people everywhere. Send someone to keep a close eye on Ganlu Palace, especially those two children. Remember, do not act recklessly, and leave no evidence. Report any situation to me first."

"Yes."

...

After the Empress finished her month of confinement, she could no longer resist the urging of those around her and took the initiative to ask the Emperor to return the harem’s authority to her.

Xiang Jun had originally come to visit the Empress and the two children, but unexpectedly, the Empress said in front of her: "Your Majesty, Sister Xiang Jun has worked hard managing the harem on my behalf, yet she has been criticized by the imperial court. I think that now that I have finished my confinement, I should no longer trouble my sister with the harem’s affairs."

The Emperor had been looking at the two infants in the cradle with Xiang Jun. Hearing the Empress’s words, he raised his eyes to glance at Xiang Jun.

Xiang Jun’s expression remained unchanged. She smiled at the Emperor, then continued looking at the two children.

The Empress’s two children were unusually well-behaved—neither crying nor fussing, just lying there quietly. They were much easier to handle than Yuan Lang had been as a baby.

Yuan Lang had needed someone to hold him at all times when he was first born.

However, Xiang Jun felt these two children were not as clever as Yuan Lang. They seemed a bit dull.

The Emperor’s expression softened as he looked at the Empress. "Yuan Ze is growing up and is at his most mischievous age. You also have two infants to care for. I’m afraid it will be too much for you. How about letting the Noble Consort continue to assist you with some trivial matters?"

Now that the Empress had accomplished a great feat by giving birth to twins, the Emperor couldn’t show too much favoritism toward Xiang Jun.

But if the Empress were to continue managing the harem, the Emperor still had some reservations.

"Yuan Ze doesn’t cause much trouble, and these two children are very well-behaved. Besides, there are wet nurses to take care of them, so it won’t take much effort on my part." The Empress then turned to Xiang Jun. "This matter still depends on what my sister thinks."

Xiang Jun didn’t hesitate for a moment. "Sister is the Empress. The authority of the harem was always yours. Previously, it was because you were pregnant, but now that you’ve safely given birth, I should indeed return the authority to you."

chapters.title: A Pledge of Allegiance to the Empress Dowager
chapters.content:
Xiang Jun’s immediate willingness to relinquish the harem’s authority surprised not only the Empress but also the Emperor.

The Emperor glanced at Xiang Jun and finally decided, "It is only right for the Empress to manage the harem. But as the Noble Consort, I will still grant you the right to assist in managing the six palaces."

"Thank you, Your Majesty. After returning, I will immediately send someone to deliver all the palace tokens to Her Majesty the Empress."

As soon as they left Ganlu Palace, the Emperor couldn’t help but ask Xiang Jun, "You are quite generous."

Having grown up in the harem, the Emperor was well aware of the importance of its authority.

Yet Xiang Jun had shown no attachment to it at all. If he hadn’t taken the initiative to grant her the right to assist in managing the six palaces, she might have given up even that without a second thought.

"Your Majesty, I have heard that some in the imperial court have spoken ill of me. I may disregard my own reputation, but I cannot disregard yours. I do not wish to be called a bewitching concubine, nor do I wish for Your Majesty to be slandered by those with ulterior motives because of me. I know that Your Majesty favors me, which is why I must not act selfishly and disregard Your Majesty."

Who else could be behind those slanderous remarks in the imperial court, accusing the Emperor of favoring a concubine and neglecting the Empress?

Regardless of whether the Empress had ordered Great General Wang to do this, the fact that she had taken the initiative to reclaim the harem’s authority meant she was siding with others to pressure him.

Wasn’t this the same as what Empress Yang had done back then?

Jiaojiao was indeed different from her.

The Emperor sighed helplessly and took Xiang Jun’s hand. "You always think of me."

...

Although the Emperor had decided to retain Xiang Jun’s right to assist in managing the six palaces, Xiang Jun showed no reluctance. That very day, she personally delivered all the palace tokens and records to the Empress at Ganlu Palace.

Xiang Jun didn’t care either way. After all, she had already placed her people where they needed to be.

Let Her Majesty the Empress busy herself with the tedious affairs of the six palaces and the care of three children.

As for Xiang Jun, she had never intended to keep her focus solely on the harem.

However, within a month of the Empress reclaiming the harem’s authority, one of the three pregnant consorts who had been with child suffered a miscarriage, and another nearly had a premature birth, forcing her to be extremely careful to preserve the pregnancy.

Only Consort Liu, whom Xiang Jun had been protecting, remained safe and sound, with no issues at all.

Although it was determined to be an accident, the Empress Dowager still severely reprimanded the Empress.

This time, even the Emperor did not speak up for the Empress.

Seeing the Emperor’s disappointed expression, the Empress could only promise to fulfill her duties as Empress properly and ensure that such incidents would not happen again.

Even Cai Wei couldn’t help but advise the Empress: "Your Majesty, how is it that when the Noble Consort was managing the harem, nothing ever happened, but as soon as you took over, these incidents occurred?"

The Empress had not been sleeping well these past few days. She rubbed her temples and said wearily, "Yes, could it be that I am truly not as capable as the Noble Consort?"

"That’s not what I meant, Your Majesty. What I meant was..." Cai Wei lowered her voice. "If the Noble Consort is secretly causing trouble and scheming against you, then it would make sense why so many palace consorts have had mishaps."

"How could that be? Xiang Jun is not that kind of person." The Empress said, "Back then, she handed over the harem’s authority to me without the slightest hesitation. Didn’t you say that this very act would show whether she had any ill intentions toward me? Xiang Jun has already proven herself, hasn’t she?"

"Your Majesty... How many times has His Majesty visited Ganlu Palace since then?"

This question finally silenced the Empress.

What she cared about most was still the Emperor’s love.

...

Upon learning that the Empress suspected her of causing trouble behind the scenes, Xiang Jun burst out laughing, spraying the tea from her mouth.

"I would never stoop so low as to harm someone else’s child. The Empress can’t even manage the consorts under her and now she’s blaming me?"

"Your Highness, should we do something?"

"No need. Just take good care of Consort Liu. Let the Empress scare herself."

Xiang Jun didn’t care about the others; she only protected Consort Liu’s child.

Taking advantage of the recent incidents involving the two consorts, Xiang Jun directly requested a favor from the Emperor and had Consort Liu moved to Jian Pin Palace.

Although Xiang Jun hadn’t deliberately caused trouble for the Empress, when Xiang Jun had been in charge, she had spent generously and used a combination of rewards and punishments.

Everyone knew that no matter how difficult the task or how troublesome the work, as long as they did it well, the Noble Consort would reward them handsomely.

Moreover, not only were there rewards for good work, but if they encountered any problems that weren’t caused by intentional negligence, the Noble Consort would always stand up for them.

Now, with a new mistress in charge, there were no more generous rewards. If problems arose, they would be in trouble. Naturally, they didn’t dare to take initiative, only doing the bare minimum to get by, and never going beyond that.

Furthermore, since the good mistress had been replaced by a less capable one, the servants would subtly sabotage things, making it difficult for the Empress to carry out her tasks smoothly.

The Empress found managing the harem increasingly difficult.

She certainly wouldn’t go to Xiang Jun for help, so she turned to De Fei and Wang Wan Yi.

Xiang Jun didn’t mind at all.

While the Empress was struggling, Xiang Jun kept the Emperor occupied in Chengxiang Palace for half a month, then began sending him to visit the other consorts in their respective palaces.

Even without the authority to manage the six palaces, it was still easy for her to elevate a few sisters.

During this time, the sisters in the palace were all happy, except for the Empress.

Whenever they went to pay their respects to the Empress, they could see the dark circles under her eyes.

Xiang Jun sighed. Asking someone with a "love brain" to manage the harem was truly difficult for her. Especially now, with so many people and so many children in the harem.

Especially the Empress’s twins—reports said they had been very restless lately, crying day and night. The Empress, with her compassionate heart, naturally had to endure this with them.

In just a few months, the Empress seemed to have aged several years.

But the Empress’s misfortunes were far from over.

Next came the scandal involving the Empress’s promoted chief eunuch, who had abused a palace maid in the kitchen, driving her to attempt suicide.

The Noble Consort, with her kind heart, had saved the maid in time. Since the Noble Consort still had the authority to assist in managing the six palaces, a thorough investigation revealed that this old eunuch had been responsible for the deaths of many palace maids and young, handsome eunuchs over the years.

This incident was extremely disgraceful. Since the eunuch had been promoted by the Empress, Xiang Jun had no choice but to hand him over to the Empress Dowager for punishment.

The Empress Dowager usually didn’t interfere in harem affairs, but that didn’t mean she couldn’t.

The Empress Dowager summoned the Empress to Ren Shou Palace and gave her a severe scolding. When the Emperor arrived, he heard the Empress Dowager say: "Empress, you are thirty-two years old now, aren’t you? You’re old enough to be a grandmother, yet you still haven’t improved at all after all these years."

Xiang Jun stood silently beside the Empress Dowager, saying nothing.

Ever since she learned that the Empress Dowager genuinely disliked the Empress, Xiang Jun had decisively chosen to align herself with the Empress Dowager, completely severing ties with the Empress.

Today’s actions could be considered a pledge of allegiance to the Empress Dowager.

The Emperor glanced at Xiang Jun, clearly displeased.

The Emperor didn’t like Xiang Jun going over his head to ingratiate herself with the Empress Dowager.

Xiang Jun also sensed the Emperor’s gaze, but this was a choice she had made after careful consideration. Since she had done it, she was prepared to anger the Emperor.

It didn’t matter. She could coax him back later. After all, their Emperor was quite fickle.

The Emperor finally shifted his gaze to the Empress.

Xue Jiaojiao stood with her head lowered in front of the Empress Dowager, her eyes welling with tears of grief.

The Emperor chose to silently walk to the Empress’s side and took her hand.

The two of them stood there as if the Empress Dowager and Xiang Jun were the villains.

Xiang Jun remained unmoved, even feeling a hint of joy.

Look, Your Majesty the Empress Dowager—your own son does not stand with you, but I have chosen you! I even risked offending the Emperor and the Empress by delivering the Empress’s weakness into your hands.

The Empress Dowager felt the scorching gaze beside her. She glanced at Xiang Jun and met her cunning eyes, then helplessly looked away.

chapters.title: What the Empress Dowager Can Give You, the Emperor Cannot
chapters.content:
"Is the Emperor blaming me for interfering in your harem affairs?"

The Emperor immediately bowed his head slightly and said, "This subject does not dare. It's just that the Empress was unaware of this matter. It was merely the subordinates who did not handle things properly. I beg the Empress Dowager not to blame the Empress too harshly."

Xiangjun felt inexplicably confused. Clearly, the Emperor had not shown much favor to the Empress these days, so why was he acting as if he loved her deeply now?

Could it be that he wanted the Empress to win someone over for him again?

Xiangjun stood silently beside them, her gaze lowered.

The Empress Dowager suppressed her anger, her sharp gaze piercing through the Emperor to the Empress, who was half-hidden behind him. "The Empress cannot even manage her own people, and yet she thinks she has done nothing wrong? As the mother of the nation, she dare not take responsibility for her own actions. When something happens, she hides behind the Emperor. Is this how you uphold the dignity of the Empress?"

The Empress took a deep breath, let go of the Emperor's hand, walked to the Empress Dowager, and knelt in a grand gesture. Gathering her courage, she said, "This concubine has erred. I beg the Empress Dowager to punish me."

"How dare I? You are the apple of the Emperor's eye. If I punish you, will the Empress Dowager and the Emperor still be mother and son?"

"Mother..." the Emperor said urgently, "This subject would never think that way."

The Empress also hastily said in fear, "This concubine is willing to accept the punishment."

"If the Empress cannot manage the harem properly, then let someone who can manage it take over."

Hearing the Empress Dowager say this, the Empress's body swayed.

The Emperor did not speak. In truth, he did not oppose this.

But the Empress's attitude was unusually firm this time.

"Empress Dowager, this concubine knows that this matter has disappointed you. If you wish to scold or punish me, this concubine is willing to accept it. I promise that from now on, I will manage the harem well without any negligence. If such disgraceful things happen again in the harem, this concubine will voluntarily relinquish her authority without any further words."

Upon hearing this, Xiangjun was somewhat surprised.

When did our Empress become so ambitious, even fighting for herself?

Seeing the Empress speak thus, the Emperor could not say much more. After all, she was the Empress and his true love; the Emperor was still willing to give her another chance.

"Mother, since that is the case, please give the Empress another chance."

The Empress Dowager coldly glanced at the Empress before looking back at the Emperor, her tone softening slightly.

"You are the Emperor. The matters of the harem are naturally for the Emperor to decide. I am tired. Emperor, take the Empress away. Noble Consort, stay here and attend to me for my nap."

The Emperor left with the Empress.

Xiangjun dutifully attended to the Empress Dowager for her nap, removing the Empress Dowager's hairpins and gently combing her hair.

"Regarding today's matters, you did not inform the Emperor but came to report to me first. Are you not afraid of making the Emperor unhappy?" the Empress Dowager suddenly asked.

Xiangjun's movements were steady and gentle as she continued combing the Empress Dowager's hair. She smiled and said, "Who can truly understand the Emperor's mind? Today, the Emperor may favor the Empress as if she were his own flesh and blood, but tomorrow, who knows, he might be angry with her and grow cold. The Emperor treats this concubine the same way. Therefore, this concubine prefers to attend to the Empress Dowager."

The Empress Dowager smiled and said, "But the Emperor can give you things that I cannot."

"Does the Empress Dowager mean the Emperor's favor? Rest assured, when it comes to competing for favor, this concubine is the most skilled."

Xiangjun smirked mischievously, wanting to say something witty, but the Empress Dowager in the mirror looked as stern as when she faced Xue Jiaojiao.

Xiangjun quickly stopped smiling.

"I am not talking about the Emperor's favor. Noble Consort should know what I am referring to."

Xiangjun's hands paused for a moment before she continued combing the Empress Dowager's hair with a smile.

"What the Emperor can give this concubine, this concubine will strive for herself. But in this harem, the person this concubine respects and admires the most is still the Empress Dowager. If this concubine can learn even a little from the Empress Dowager, how could she worry about not getting what she wants? Therefore, even if it makes the Emperor angry with this concubine, I still think that making the Empress Dowager happy is more important."

The Empress Dowager's expression finally softened again. She patted Xiangjun's hand, signaling her to stop.

Xiangjun put down the comb and obediently helped the Empress Dowager towards the bed.

The Empress Dowager looked at Xiangjun, smiled gently, and her tone became earnest.

"The late Emperor was a benevolent ruler, but our Emperor..." The Empress Dowager sighed bitterly, "Even I, his mother, am someone he is wary of. Therefore, the path ahead for you will be much harder than mine."

Xiangjun had not expected the Empress Dowager to be so blunt. She supported the Empress Dowager as she sat down and consoled her, "The nature of emperors is often like this, but our Emperor is still very filial to the Empress Dowager and holds you, his mother, in his heart."

"I know. Back then, when I was stranded in Bei Meng for many years, the Emperor suffered a lot. He has complaints about me as his mother. His character has also become somewhat extreme because of what happened back then. But as long as I am alive, I can still control the Emperor. What I fear is, when I am no longer here..."

"Empress Dowager, please do not speak like this anymore. It invites misfortune..." Xiangjun helped the Empress Dowager sit down and knelt obediently at her feet. "As long as you take care of yourself and live well, you will have many more years ahead."

Although she said this, Xiangjun knew that if the plot did not change significantly, the Empress Dowager probably only had a couple of years left.

In her previous life, after the Empress Dowager's death, the Emperor indeed became even more unpredictable and prone to outbursts.

It seemed that if the Empress Dowager had not died, with her presence, the Emperor would not have done something as cruel as cutting open her belly to take the child in her previous life.

"How much longer I can live does not matter much to me. In this life, I have seen prosperity, been to hell, held great power, and had the world in my hands, but I still have many regrets. As for our Emperor, I have done my best for him without reservation. The only thing I cannot let go of in this life..."

Xiangjun felt a sense of tension. She felt that the Empress Dowager was about to tell her something very important.

But after a moment, the Empress Dowager still did not finish her sentence. She just looked somewhat sorrowful and sighed heavily.

Finally, the Empress Dowager patted Xiangjun's hand and said gently, "Alright, I understand your intentions. With me protecting you, you can do as you wish. Although the Emperor can give you things that I cannot, there are things I can give you that the Emperor cannot. In the future, do not come to see me so often. Your good intentions are enough. Go back and properly coax your Emperor."

---

chapters.title: No More Pretending
chapters.content:
After the Empress Dowager fell asleep, Xiangjun left the Palace of Benevolence and Longevity.

Along the way, Xiangjun furrowed her brows in thought, and Mengmei did not dare to say or ask much.

Xiangjun was becoming more and more convinced of her guess. She felt that the person the Empress Dowager could not let go of was none other than Gu Tingxue.

"Noble Consort..."

Unexpectedly, before she reached her own palace, Chengxiang Palace, she was stopped by someone—a small eunuch from the Empress's palace.

Xiangjun waved her hand, and the sedan chair stopped.

The small eunuch respectfully said, "Noble Consort, our Empress requests your presence at Ganlu Palace."

Mengmei immediately looked at Xiangjun warily, her eyes asking if she should send the eunuch away.

Xiangjun slightly shook her head and then said to the eunuch, "Since the Empress requests my presence, I naturally must go. Please, go ahead."

The eunuch left, and Mengmei asked anxiously, "Your Highness, the Empress likely wants to confront you. Should we seek the Empress Dowager's help? She will surely support you."

"No need. The Empress Dowager has just fallen asleep. It's a small matter; there's no need to trouble her. If the Empress truly dares to pin me down in Ganlu Palace and beat me, I might even develop some admiration for her. However, our Empress likely cannot bring herself to do such a thing. Let's go."

The sedan chair turned towards Ganlu Palace.

The Empress was waiting for Xiangjun in the main hall, with four palace maids and four eunuchs standing beside her. The atmosphere suggested they were ready to interrogate Xiangjun.

Xiangjun, however, remained at ease, as if she had not noticed their hostile demeanor. As usual, she greeted the Empress with a flower-like smile and, without waiting for permission, sat down beside her.

"How dare you! Did the Empress allow you to sit?"

Xiangjun glanced at Caiwei. "In the past, the Empress always treated me this way. Now, am I not allowed to sit?"

The Empress raised her hand, signaling Caiwei to step back.

The Empress rarely had such a serious expression. She stared at Xiangjun and asked bluntly, "Sister Xiangjun, today I invited you here to hear the truth from you. Recently, the harem has been in turmoil. First, two pregnant concubines met with misfortune one after another, and only the Willow Beauty by your side remained unharmed. Then, the Grand Supervisor I promoted caused trouble. All these incidents—were they your doing?"

The harem had been in constant turmoil.

At first, the Empress could disregard Caiwei's words, but now that the matter had reached the Empress Dowager, and it was Xiangjun who had handed the Empress Dowager the evidence, the Empress could no longer remain in denial.

She began to believe that what Caiwei and General Wang had said was true.

Perhaps Xiangjun had changed.

But she and Xiangjun had been like sisters for so long, and she had truly been good to Xiangjun. Therefore, she needed to hear it from Xiangjun herself.

Faced with the Empress's direct question, Xiangjun was at a loss for words.

Could such a question be asked so directly?

Who would admit to it?

If she admitted it in front of so many people, wouldn't that give them leverage against her?

Xiangjun blinked innocently and said aggrievedly, "Empress, this concubine is the most honest. When you were unwell, I wholeheartedly managed the harem for you. When you recovered and wanted to reclaim your authority, I handed everything back without a word. Now that the harem is in constant turmoil, how can you blame me? I am wronged! Even if I had such intentions, without the authority, how could I cause such chaos in the palace?"

The Empress felt only disappointment upon seeing Xiangjun's refusal to admit.

"Then what about the eunuch and the palace maid's matter? Wasn't that your doing? Didn't you report it to the Empress Dowager?"

Indeed, it was Xiangjun who had made the eunuch's abuse of the palace maid known to everyone.

But could that be blamed on her?

Should that palace maid have died silently? If they did not make a fuss, even if they saved this palace maid, other palace maids and eunuchs would still suffer at his hands.

"Your Highness, that Grand Supervisor was your man. I do not have the ability to instruct him to abuse the palace maids. I merely stood up for the innocent palace maid. Does the Empress think I did wrong?"

Xiangjun stared directly at the Empress, and Xue Jiaojiao felt an inexplicable sense of guilt.

"This matter... indeed cannot be considered your fault. But you could have told me."

"Empress, if I had told you, would you have killed that Grand Supervisor?"

The Empress fell silent.

Xiangjun glanced at Caiwei and sneered, "He is from the same hometown as your Caiwei. I'm afraid that with a single plea from Caiwei, our merciful Empress would not bear to punish him. If he were let off so lightly, how could the unruly practices in the harem be eliminated? This concubine reported it to the Empress Dowager not to harm you, but to help you, to preserve the Empress's reputation."

Caiwei could not help but say, "Sophistry! You did this precisely to make the Empress lose face in front of the Empress Dowager."

"The one who made the Empress lose face is not me, but that shameless slave, and those who cannot judge character and recklessly recommend people to the Empress."

Xiangjun's words made Caiwei's face turn red, but Xiangjun did not care. She wanted to drink some tea but found that Ganlu Palace had not even offered her a cup of tea.

How petty.

The Empress was also unable to keep her composure after Xiangjun's words.

She signaled Caiwei to step back and looked at Xiangjun again.

"What has happened cannot be undone. But, Noble Consort, in the past, I truly regarded you as a sister. For the sake of our years of sisterhood, tell me, do you resent me for reclaiming the palace authority?"

Xiangjun fell silent. She thought for a moment about how to respond.

It was not that she did not know how to prevaricate with the Empress; she was just hesitant about whether to keep up the pretense.

In fact, it would be better to keep pretending.

But she also understood that she could not keep it up for much longer.

She had openly aligned herself with the Empress Dowager today. If the Empress were a bit smarter, she would not need to call her here for a confrontation.

After much consideration, Xiangjun decided to stop pretending.

She was naturally bold, and after years of playing the submissive role, she had had enough.

Xiangjun smiled at the Empress, her tone still respectful, but her words were quite blunt.

"What does Sister mean by asking this? Could it be that if I desire Sister's authority, Sister would be willing to give it to me?"

The Empress was shocked, and Caiwei beside her glared at Xiangjun with a fierce look.

"How dare you! The Empress is the mistress of the harem. How can you covet what belongs to the Empress?"

Xiangjun covered her mouth with a handkerchief and laughed.

"Empress, it was you who asked me, and I told the truth. But your Caiwei is angry. Since you already have the answer in your heart, why bother asking me? Why put on that earnest and persuasive act just now?"

The Empress looked at Xiangjun in disbelief.

Xiangjun's demeanor was unfamiliar to Xue Jiaojiao.

"Sister Xiangjun, everyone tells me you are not a good person, but I do not believe them. Now, why... why have you become like this? Could it be that power truly changes a person?"

"It truly does."

Xiangjun admitted without hesitation.

chapters.title: How Did the Emperor Become So Easy to Please
chapters.content:
Xiangjun winked at the Empress, still feigning innocence, her smile as pure as an ignorant girl.

The Empress felt her blood boiling.

Before the Empress could speak, Xiangjun spoke again.

"Your Majesty the Empress, if you don’t care about power at all and don’t want to be changed by it, then why were you so anxious when the Empress Dowager tried to reclaim the harem’s authority? If you truly cherish me as a sister and value our sisterhood, then since I’ve already asked, why not just hand over the harem’s authority to me?"

Seeing the Empress’s choked expression, Xiangjun couldn’t help but sneer.

"Look, Your Majesty, don’t you also care deeply about the power of the central palace? So, is it really so surprising that I, who have managed the harem for so long and worked tirelessly, am reluctant to give up power?"

Xiangjun stood up and took a few steps toward the Empress.

For a moment, even Xue Jiaojiao was overshadowed by Xiangjun’s momentum.

"Your Majesty the Empress, allow me, your younger sister, to advise you: be true to yourself. Don’t deceive even yourself. Wanting power is nothing to be ashamed of. As the Empress, at the center of power in the Great Qi Dynasty, it would be dangerous if you didn’t want anything at all."

Xiangjun bowed to the Empress.

"If Your Majesty has no further orders, this concubine will take her leave and return to Chengxiang Palace. I am very thirsty. Farewell."

Xiangjun turned and left with Meng Mei.

The Empress remained seated on her throne in the central palace, lost in thought for a long time.

"Your Majesty, General Wang was right. For a concubine like the Honored Consort, you need not trouble yourself over her."

But the Empress ignored Cai Wei.

For a moment, a sense of confusion arose in her heart.

Xiangjun had told her to be true to herself and not deceive herself.

What was she deceiving herself about?

Vaguely, the Empress felt that Xiangjun might be right. She wanted to grasp this fleeting emotion, but Cai Wei’s incessant chatter by her ear distracted her.

"Your Majesty, you now have two princes and a princess. Even if you don’t want to fight, for the sake of your children, you must. Your Majesty..."

The mention of her three children finally snapped the Empress back to reality.

Yes, she still had three children.

Even if she didn’t want to fight, had the storms of the harem ever truly ceased?

For the sake of her own children, she had to summon some fighting spirit.

...

As soon as they left, Meng Mei asked Xiangjun nervously, "Your Highness, now that we’ve spoken openly with Her Majesty the Empress, aren’t you afraid she’ll say bad things about you to His Majesty?"

"Do you really think the Empress and His Majesty are still as close as they once were? Besides, I’m not afraid of His Majesty finding out."

Xiangjun intended to gradually change the Emperor’s perception of her.

She wanted him to know that she was willing to fight, that she had ambitions.

Sure enough, the next day, the Emperor visited Chengxiang Palace to see Yuan Lang.

After Yuan Lang made a fuss for a while, Xiangjun had the child taken away and personally served the Emperor his lunch.

The Emperor casually mentioned, "I heard from Cai Wei, the Empress’s maid, that you went to Ganlu Palace yesterday and said some disrespectful things to the Empress?"

"I did not disrespect Her Majesty. I merely felt that with Her Majesty managing the harem, yet constant turmoil persists, and I couldn’t bear to see His Majesty troubled. I only wanted to help Her Majesty share the burden."

Xiangjun’s direct admission left the Emperor with little to say.

"I heard that the Empress was deeply hurt by your words."

"I did not say anything to hurt Her Majesty’s feelings. I only spoke the truth. Her Majesty’s management of the harem is indeed not as good as mine."

The Emperor’s expression turned serious, glaring at Xiangjun. "Is that something you should say?"

"In front of others, I would naturally not dare. But Your Majesty has told me before, hasn’t he? In Your Majesty’s heart, I am no worse than anyone else. Your Majesty values me, and I want to strive for Your Majesty. I want to prove to Your Majesty that your favor toward me is justified, because I can share your burdens. Is it wrong for me to do this?"

Xiangjun spoke with a grievance in her tone, but there was not the slightest hint of retreat in her words.

This was the first time Xiangjun had shown such ambition to compete with the Empress in front of the Emperor.

She did it on purpose, because she knew that the Emperor would appreciate her ambition now.

Not only because the Emperor needed someone in the harem to counterbalance the Empress, but also because the Emperor probably didn’t dislike women who climbed up from the bottom.

After all, her mother was such a person.

And so was he.

The Empress, who had been high and mighty from the start, was not the same kind of person as the Emperor.

Sure enough, faced with Xiangjun’s honesty, the Emperor did not get angry.

"So, you went to curry favor with the Empress Dowager and reported the Empress behind my back, is that it?"

Xiangjun lowered her head, tears welling up in her eyes.

"Xiangjun also wants to rely on Your Majesty, but Xiangjun knows that in Your Majesty’s heart, I can never compare to Her Majesty the Empress. Although Your Majesty has been very good to me, no matter how much you favor me, as long as my sister asks, Your Majesty will give her whatever she wants. So, when my sister asked me for the harem’s authority, I didn’t dare say a word and immediately returned it to her."

The Emperor’s expression showed a moment of embarrassment.

He had wondered at the time why Xiangjun hadn’t tried to refuse, but now he realized it was because she had misunderstood his intentions.

"I never had that intention."

"Your Majesty is just comforting me... I know that Your Majesty met my sister first. She is the most important woman in Your Majesty’s heart. In the past, I could happily watch Your Majesty shower her with affection... But now... I... I don’t know what’s wrong with me. Sometimes, when I see Your Majesty favoring my sister, my heart feels a pang of jealousy."

"Then why do you always urge me to favor other concubines in the harem? The Empress has never pushed me toward others."

"That’s different!" Xiangjun pouted, looking displeased. "How can it be the same? The Emperor is the ruler of a nation. The imperial lineage is the foundation of the country. Advising Your Majesty to share your favor equally is a virtue of the concubines. I don’t mind who Your Majesty favors. What I care about... what I care about..."

Xiangjun’s voice trailed off.

"What I care about is Your Majesty’s heart." Tears fell from Xiangjun’s eyes, her pitiful appearance enough to move anyone. "My devotion to Your Majesty is no less than my sister’s. I know I shouldn’t be jealous, it’s all my fault. Please forgive me for overstepping, Your Majesty."

Xiangjun knelt on the ground, asking for forgiveness, but her expression showed not the slightest hint of submission.

The Emperor was silent for a long time before heaving a deep sigh.

"It’s not your fault. When you truly like someone, it’s only natural."

The Emperor reached out, took Xiangjun’s hand, and helped her up.

But Xiangjun did not stand. Instead, she threw herself into the Emperor’s arms.

"I know I’m not good, but sometimes I just want to compete with Her Majesty the Empress. I want Your Majesty to see that I am no worse than her. My devotion to Your Majesty is even more genuine. I can not only make Your Majesty happy but also help you solve your worries."

The Emperor gently patted Xiangjun’s back.

"It’s my fault for neglecting your feelings. From now on, rely on me. I will support you. If you want to compete, then compete."

Xiangjun wiped her tears.

"Will Your Majesty not think I’ve changed, that you no longer like me?"

"No. People always change. I promise you, I will always look at you with fresh eyes."

Xiangjun’s eyelashes trembled slightly, tears falling once more as she tightly embraced the Emperor again.

She didn’t know if it was her imagination, but she felt that the Emperor had become so much easier to please lately.

---

chapters.title: Grand Bestowal Upon the Six Palaces
chapters.content:
After her confrontation with Xue Jiaojiao, Xiangjun’s days became much more comfortable.

First, she no longer had to manage so many affairs of the harem, which gave her more free time.

Second, because Her Majesty the Empress considered herself a good person and didn’t want others to think she was petty, the more openly Xiangjun opposed her, the more cautious the Empress became, not daring to let her subordinates mistreat Xiangjun.

However, this peaceful period didn’t last long before the harem was stirred up again.

The Empress made a blunder by promoting Yue Fei.

Just as she had once let Xiangjun dance at the Mid-Autumn Banquet to steal the limelight, the Empress repeated the same trick, this time letting Yue Fei make a grand entrance.

The Emperor hadn’t seen Yue Fei in a long time. After so much recuperation, Yue Fei’s beauty remained undiminished. That very night, the Emperor bestowed his favor upon her.

For the next three days, the Emperor stayed with Yue Fei.

In Chengxiang Palace, Meng Mei was worried.

"Your Highness, Yue Fei is in favor again. Aren’t you concerned? In the past, she caused you no small amount of trouble."

Xiangjun ate her sweet melon while flipping through a book.

"If I were afraid of Yue Fei, I wouldn’t have let her recover so well. Her Majesty the Empress may have forgotten, but I have not. It was the Empress and her lackey, Song Feijing, who caused Yue Fei to lose her child. Yue Fei’s true enemy is the Empress, not me. The Empress harmed her and then forgot, yet still promotes her... I don’t care to meddle in the Empress’s affairs. If she wants to keep a tiger by her side, let her."

Soon after, the Empress proposed elevating Yue Fei’s rank, reasoning that Yue Fei could no longer bear children, and as a princess of Nanyue—a region that had contributed to Great Qi—it would be appropriate to fill one of the vacant positions of the four consorts.

To Xiangjun’s surprise, the Emperor did not immediately agree. Instead, he came to ask for her opinion.

"I fear you might misunderstand and think I’ve forgotten about you, Honored Consort, because I favor Yue Fei." The Emperor reassured Xiangjun, "Yue Fei is, after all, a princess of Nanyue, and the King of Nanyue has been loyal to me. In the future, when I set out to destroy Beimeng, I will need Nanyue to stabilize the south."

Xiangjun was somewhat surprised. The Emperor was actually explaining himself to her?

"Why would I misunderstand? Yue Fei has indeed suffered a lot, and it’s only right for Your Majesty to elevate her rank. However, there are also many sisters in the palace who have princes or are carrying imperial heirs. Your Majesty should promote them as well."

The Emperor realized that it had indeed been many years since the six palaces had been rewarded. With so many concubines now bearing children or with child, it was indeed time for a proper bestowal of titles.

"You’re quite generous, wanting to help everyone," the Emperor said.

"Your Majesty flatters me. Her Majesty the Empress is the truly generous one. As for Yue Fei’s past miscarriage..." Xiangjun trailed off, then smiled and continued, "Her Majesty’s ability to let bygones be bygones truly showcases her noble character as the mistress of the harem."

The Emperor also caught the implication in Xiangjun’s words.

He found the whole situation baffling. The Emperor had never shown mercy to his enemies, yet the Empress could still treat others as sisters and even promote Yue Fei...

"I only hope that Her Majesty the Empress and Sister Yue Fei can truly coexist peacefully. Otherwise, they’ll only bring displeasure to Your Majesty. But if they do, it will only make me look better, and Your Majesty will like me even more."

The Emperor pinched Xiangjun’s nose. "You little troublemaker, don’t I already like you enough?"

In the end, the Emperor still elevated Yue Fei’s rank, making her one of the four consorts as the Virtuous Consort.

As for the others, the Emperor couldn’t be bothered to think about it and told Xiangjun to draft a list for his approval.

Xiangjun didn’t dare to be excessive.

Jian Pin was definitely to be promoted—she was a sister who had walked the same path as Xiangjun. So she was elevated to Consort Jian.

The Chang Within who had previously miscarried was promoted to Honored Lady.

Two others who were pregnant: one, a Selected Attendant, was promoted to Lady; and Liu Meiren, who was Xiangjun’s own person, was promoted three ranks at once to Honored Lady Liu, as Xiangjun reasoned that she wouldn’t be promoted again after giving birth.

Jiang Guifei had given birth to a princess and, since she was raising the child herself, needed the rank of a Pin to do so properly. So promoting her to Pin was only fair.
