Xiangjun knew when to stop. The Emperor glanced at the list and felt that Xiangjun was being quite bold.

But considering that the harem’s authority had been given to the Empress, Xiangjun promoting her own people was a way to maintain balance, so he agreed.

However, thinking of Bai Fan’s usefulness in the north, he took the initiative to promote Lady Bai to Honored Lady Bai.

Xiangjun hadn’t expected it to go so smoothly. How had the Emperor become so generous?

Several sisters came to express their gratitude, all overjoyed.

Not everyone in the harem had a family backing them financially like Xiangjun did. Their quality of life in the palace was directly tied to their rank.

Who wouldn’t want a better life?

Honored Lady Bai was the happiest. She had thought only concubines with children would be promoted this time, so she specially brought her decree of enfeoffment to show off to Xiangjun.

"Sister Honored Consort, look! I’m a Honored Lady now! Thank you, Sister Honored Consort!"

"This has nothing to do with me. It’s because your brother is favored by His Majesty."

"I don’t care. It’s because of you, Sister Honored Consort. Otherwise, His Majesty wouldn’t have thought to promote everyone’s ranks."

Xiangjun took the decree from Honored Lady Bai and only then learned her name was Bai Yiyi.

"What a nice name, Bai Yiyi."

Honored Lady Bai looked like she wanted to say something but hesitated.

"What’s the matter now?"

"Honored Consort, I want to tell you a secret. Just you."

"What secret?"

"I’m not actually called Bai Yiyi. Bai Yiyi is the name my brother gave me before I entered the palace. He was afraid His Majesty wouldn’t like my original name."

"What was your original name?"

Bai Yiyi said somewhat embarrassedly, "I... I was originally called Fu Bao."

Xiangjun was momentarily speechless.

Bai Yiyi did have a rather heroic appearance, but her demeanor was delicate and moving. The name Bai Yiyi did suit her temperament and looks.

As for Fu Bao...

"Who gave you that name?"

"My parents. A fortune teller said I was very fortunate. I really am lucky. I always find ginseng when I go to the mountains! Though my fate is strange—maybe because I’m too fortunate, I face a calamity every three years."

"Do you really face a calamity every three years?" Xiangjun asked curiously.

Bai Yiyi nodded. "Yes, but the fortune teller said I have a noble person in my life who will turn misfortune into fortune. I entered the palace at fifteen. My brother was worried I’d meet with disaster as soon as I entered, but instead I met you, Honored Consort. So I know, you are my noble person."

Xiangjun felt a surge of pride at Bai Yiyi’s words.

"Rest assured. With me, you are indeed fortunate."

...

Not long after, Xiangjun learned something.

De Fei, Wang Wan Yi, Sun Guipin, and several other noble concubines in the harem were visiting the Empress daily.

Li Shi entered the palace to inform Xiangjun that General Wang and the Prince of Jin had exerted influence in the background, rallying the families behind these concubines.

The rise and fall of the imperial concubines were always tied to their families, so naturally, they had all sided with the Empress.

Sun Guipin had originally wanted to side with Xiangjun, but for the sake of her family, she had no choice but to choose the Empress.

Upon hearing this news, Xiangjun only gave a cold laugh.

As long as the Emperor was not a foolish ruler, what could these women in the harem accomplish with their petty squabbles?

As long as the Emperor still needed General Wang, still feared the Prince of Jin, and had not yet dealt with those powerful old ministers, the Empress’s position would be as stable as Mount Tai.

And as long as Xiangjun and the forces behind her still served as a counterbalance to the Empress, her position as Honored Consort would be just as secure.

So, what was there to fight over?

It was simply a waste of time.

Moreover, that group of people sticking together was nothing more than a bunch of incompetent cobblers.

In her past life, they had never been able to defeat her, let alone in this one.

But looking at her own side... She was satisfied with Consort Jian and Lady Jiang. As for the remaining three...

Chu Guifei, Yun Guiren, and Bai Guiren...

Forget it. Her side wasn’t much better.

chapters.title: Can't She Have a Better Opponent?
chapters.content:
One day, Xiangjun took her sisters to the Imperial Garden to appreciate the flowers, and also brought along several children to play together.

In the future, if Yuanlang were to ascend to the throne, he could not do it alone—having a few trustworthy brothers and sisters would be very important.

The bond formed from growing up together was different, so Xiangjun always deliberately arranged for the children to spend time with one another.

Xiangjun brought Consort Jian, Concubine Jiang, Concubine Liu, Concubine Yun, and Bai Niangzi, along with the Third Prince, Fifth Prince, and Third Princess, as well as a large entourage of palace attendants, to the Imperial Garden.

Unexpectedly, the Empress was also appreciating chrysanthemums in the Imperial Garden that day, and had invited many concubines. However, the newly promoted Virtuous Consort Qin was not present, while the other noble concubines like De Fei were all there.

The two groups kept their distance.

The Empress glanced at Xiangjun from afar before looking away.

But that single glance was strange—it made Xiangjun feel as if she were a heartless man who had abandoned her.

*How absurd...*

Consort Jian, beside Xiangjun, said, "Our Empress is being far too petty. As the mistress of the harem, she hosts a chrysanthemum-viewing banquet yet only invites half the concubines, leaving the other half out."

"Do not criticize the Empress," Xiangjun said with a smile to the concubines behind her. "Even though the Empress did not invite us, we must still be courteous. Come, let us go pay our respects to the Empress."

Xiangjun led the concubines toward the Empress.

De Fei and the others watched Xiangjun approaching from a distance. They didn’t know why, but the way the Noble Consort carried herself was so bold and overbearing that it exuded an oppressive aura, even though she hadn’t done anything.

The palace attendants couldn’t help but stare as the group of concubines walked over.

It had to be said—Noble Consort Xiangjun and the concubines beside her were all young, beautiful, and full of youthful vitality, each one stunning in her own way.

This group of different beauties walking together was truly a feast for the eyes, so much so that they outshone the flowers of the Imperial Garden.

Caiwei, the Empress’s attendant, saw that the palace attendants were practically mesmerized. She cleared her throat, and only then did they lower their heads, pretending to be busy with their own tasks.

Seeing how arrogantly Noble Consort Xiangjun walked, De Fei and Wang Wanyi were furious.

*How could someone walk so boldly?*

But they could do nothing about it. They could only glare coldly, their discontent evident in their huffs.

Xiangjun held her head high, one hand resting on Xiao Luzi’s shoulder, the other swaying a round fan. She walked with such grace and poise that it was breathtaking.

The smile on Xiangjun’s lips never faded.

She loved the feeling of everyone’s eyes on her.

This short walk was utterly delightful to her.

When she finally reached the Empress, Xiangjun slightly raised her hand, and the large group behind her came to a stop.

Xiangjun respectfully greeted the Empress. Even though her words and posture were flawlessly respectful, her gaze and expression still gave the Empress the impression that she was not submissive.

The concubines beside Xiangjun had also been well-taught by her and knew their manners. Each of them properly greeted the higher-ranking concubines.

Seeing that De Fei and the others had no intention of greeting her, Xiangjun did not get angry. She merely gently fanned herself, looking at the Empress with a mocking gaze.

"No wonder the Empress Dowager often reprimands the Empress. If I may be so bold, Your Majesty, you are far too lenient with the concubines of the harem. Look at them—when they see a higher-ranking concubine, they don’t even know how to pay their respects."

The group immediately looked at the Empress. Seeing that she remained silent, they knew she had no intention of protecting them.

Though furious, De Fei, Wang Wanyi, and the others had no choice but to grit their teeth and give Xiangjun a perfunctory greeting.

Only Sun Guipin willingly paid her respects.

Xiangjun smiled at Sun Guipin, then shifted her gaze to Wang Wanyi.

Wang Wanyi was especially perfunctory toward Xiangjun, even rolling her eyes at her when she thought no one was looking. But Xiangjun had seen it.

"Wang Wanyi hasn’t learned her manners well. White Guiren, come and teach Wang Wanyi how to properly greet a higher-ranking concubine."

White Guiren immediately stepped forward and properly greeted Xiangjun.

"See? Even the people in your palace understand manners better than you do." Xiangjun said with a smile to White Guiren, "Rise. Your brother is greatly favored by His Majesty these days, and you know your manners. Who will be the mistress of the Liangyi Palace in the future is truly hard to say."

Wang Wanyi was so angry she could have smoked, but what could she do?

She was facing the Noble Consort!

Wang Wanyi had no choice but to step forward again and properly greet Xiangjun in front of everyone.

Just as Wang Wanyi was about to rise, Xiangjun’s sharp gaze swept over her once more.

"Did I say you could rise?"

Wang Wanyi gritted her teeth but had no choice but to kneel again.

Xiangjun turned her gaze back to the Empress. "Wang Wanyi does not know her place. I’ve had her kneel for a while. The Empress won’t take her side, will you?"

"Why must you do this?" the Empress couldn’t help but ask.

Xiangjun merely smiled and said nothing. Beside her, Consort Jiang spoke softly, "Noble Consort has been taught by the Empress Dowager to value the rules of the palace the most. Normally, when we sisters don’t know our manners, Noble Consort punishes us the same way. The Empress mustn’t misunderstand our Noble Consort."

By invoking the Empress Dowager, Consort Jiang left the Empress with nothing to say.

The Empress turned her face away, unwilling to look at Noble Consort Xiangjun any longer.

Only then did Xiangjun lead her sisters in greeting the Empress.

"Sisters, we won’t disturb the Empress’s elegant flower-viewing any longer. We’ll take our leave."

Xiangjun then left with her head held high. The Empress found the whole situation so uninteresting that she had nothing to say to De Fei and the others. She hastily ended the flower-viewing and returned to the Ganlu Palace.

Only Wang Wanyi remained kneeling there, not daring to leave.

It wasn’t until two hours later, when Xiangjun sent Xiao Luzi to the Imperial Garden to let Wang Wanyi rise, that she was finally carried back by the palace attendants.

Xiangjun didn’t really care about Wang Wanyi. She just wanted the concubines of the harem to see the Empress’s character, and for her own people to understand: don’t follow the wrong person. In the future, don’t be incited by others. Some masters cannot protect their subordinates.

So, Wang Wanyi rolling her eyes at Xiangjun today was just her bad luck—she had picked the wrong fight.

The Empress, however, hadn’t thought of any of this.

What Xiangjun saw was the factional struggle in the harem, but what the Empress saw was the lost sisterhood between them.

After returning, the Empress was deeply melancholic.

"Caiwei, I truly wanted to treat Xiangjun as a sister. We used to be so close. Why have we come to this? Is it all because of power? If I had known that regaining power in the harem would turn Xiangjun into this, I shouldn’t have listened to you..."

Seeing that her mistress was once again hesitating, Caiwei urgently said, "Your Majesty, things have come to this. You and the Noble Consort can never return to how things were. You must properly exercise your power as Empress, or else the Noble Consort will walk all over you!"

The Empress knew this was true, but...

"Caiwei, I... just feel a little... lonely..."

This melancholy of the Empress still reached Xiangjun’s ears.

Xiangjun was truly impressed.

The Empress was always like this. She was about to lose her fighting spirit. Couldn’t she have a better opponent?

But soon, Xiangjun regained her motivation.

Because something happened in the imperial court.

---

chapters.title: Mother and Son at Odds
chapters.content:
For the next month, the Emperor did not visit the harem even once.

This year, after autumn began, the empire was truly restless.

First, news came that locust plagues had appeared in several counties near Luoyang and North Zhili.

Just as the autumn harvest was about to begin, the sudden locust infestation ruined the year’s labor of the common people.

*Rains fly, silkworms devour a thousand miles, no green shoots left, only bare earth.*

The people starved. Food reserves were exhausted, and large numbers of refugees began fleeing south.

As they fled, they reached the Hubei and Hunan regions.

But misfortune struck again—this year, Hubei and Hunan suffered floods. Though not catastrophic, many people died, and the region already needed imperial relief. How could it possibly accommodate so many refugees?

The refugees had no choice but to continue south.

But when they reached the five prefectures of Jiangnan, trouble arose again.

Jiangnan refused to let the refugees enter the city. The refugees, in turn, began to riot.

With so many refugees gathered nearby, fearing they might cause chaos inside the city, some official—no one knew who—decided to break the river embankment.

As a result, tens of thousands of refugees drowned, their bodies floating on the river—a tragic sight.

The Emperor was furious. He immediately dispatched an imperial envoy to Jiangnan, determined to overhaul the local bureaucracy.

But before the envoy even reached Jiangnan, the Empress Dowager suddenly fell gravely ill and was confined to her bed.

Disaster struck both the front court and the harem.

Rumors began to spread among the people.

They said that the first half of the year had been peaceful, but in late summer, floods struck Hubei and Hunan, and in autumn, locust plagues hit Luoyang and North Zhili. The Empress Dowager had also fallen ill—all because the Emperor had insisted on holding the Mount Tai enthronement ceremony earlier that year.

The Emperor, in his pursuit of grandeur, had achieved less than the emperors of old who had performed the ceremony, thus inviting divine retribution.

Soon after, a censor from the front court boldly submitted a memorial, urging the Emperor to issue a self-reproach edict. He suggested that the Emperor follow the example of Emperor Taizong of Tang, who had personally visited the affected fields and eaten locusts to pray for Heaven to transfer the disaster to himself, thereby protecting the people.

The Emperor, enraged by this, had the censor beaten with a rod. But far from silencing the critics, this only emboldened more officials to condemn him.

The Emperor was so infuriated that he couldn’t sleep at night, and in the Taiji Hall, he smashed several teacups every day.

As a result, for over a month, the Emperor not only failed to visit the harem but also did not go to see the ailing Empress Dowager.

As soon as Xiangjun heard that the Empress Dowager was ill, she immediately tried to visit her, but each time she was stopped at the entrance and persuaded to return by her aunt.

After this happened several times, Xiangjun began to sense something amiss.

Xiangjun could only return to the Chengxiang Palace and take out *The Governance of the Zhenguan Era*, carefully reading the part about Emperor Taizong eating locusts.

After finishing, Xiangjun felt that the officials were truly making things difficult for the Emperor.

If the Emperor really went and ate locusts, but the disasters did not end, how would he save face?

Their Emperor was so concerned with dignity that he would never admit he was inferior to Emperor Taizong.

Moreover, Emperor Taizong’s compassion for the farmers was likely genuine. Their Emperor, however, probably lacked such benevolence. Locusts were poisonous—how could he be willing to eat them for the sake of the refugees?

*Which official with a screw loose came up with this idea?*

Xiangjun sent someone to investigate and was shocked by what she discovered.

It turned out to be someone from the Li family, her maternal relatives, who had advised the Emperor thus.

Connecting this with the Empress Dowager’s sudden illness, Xiangjun had an epiphany.

"So that’s how it is?"

"How is it?" Xiao Luzi and Mengmei asked curiously.

"It’s our Empress Dowager playing a game of wits with her own son."

The Empress Dowager was truly formidable. For years, she had stayed out of politics, completely leaving the reins to the Emperor. But with just one move, she had seized the Emperor’s weakness, leaving him unable to act.

Though Xiangjun didn’t know why the Empress Dowager was at odds with the Emperor, she could take this opportunity to stir the waters and secure some benefits for her own family.

The next day, Xiangjun summoned Li.

Normally, Li would not ask questions after receiving Xiangjun’s instructions and would simply return to inform her husband. But today, she asked an extra question.

"Noble Consort, must my husband really handle this himself? Shouldn’t we first have someone draft a few memorials to gauge the Emperor’s intentions?"

"No need. We want Elder Brother to be the first to submit a memorial. That way, it will show that our Xu family is willing to share the Emperor’s burdens."

"But the Emperor’s deep love for the Empress is known to all. Won’t this action anger the Emperor?"

Xiangjun could see that Li was genuinely concerned for her husband.

"I won’t harm my brother. No matter how much the Emperor loves the Empress, he cannot place her above his own eternal reputation. If someone can shift the blame for the heavenly disasters away from the Emperor, he will be grateful to that person."

Li still seemed doubtful.

Xiangjun didn’t blame her. After all, the Emperor’s love for the Empress was legendary, a love story that had lasted over a decade.

Perhaps Li and the other young ladies of the capital had grown up hearing tales of their love.

"You just deliver my message to my brother. As for how to proceed, he can decide for himself. I won’t force him."

Xu Huanwen did not disappoint Xiangjun.

The next morning, at the early court session, Xu Huanwen submitted a memorial stating that the Emperor’s journey to Mount Tai for the enthronement ceremony was due to a celestial blessing.

"Since it was a celestial blessing, how could Heaven then send down disasters?"

Therefore, if there was anything amiss with the enthronement ceremony, it was because the Empress had accompanied the Emperor to Mount Tai.

Since ancient times, enthronement ceremonies were not supposed to include empresses or concubines. The Empress, due to her pregnancy and restless thoughts, had insisted that the Emperor accompany her, and thus had followed him to Mount Tai. This was the true cause of the disasters.

To support his argument, Xu Huanwen even summoned the Imperial Astronomical Bureau.

The Imperial Astronomical Bureau also confirmed that the Empress and the child in her womb had indeed clashed with the spirit of Mount Tai.

General Wang was still in the capital. How could he allow Xu Huanwen to attack the Empress like this?

Because of this, General Wang argued daily with the civil officials in court. If it weren’t for the rule against bringing weapons to court, he might have already drawn his sword and killed Xu Huanwen.

Xiangjun listened to Xiao Luzi’s vivid description of how "our Xu family’s uncle" had exchanged hundreds of furious retorts with General Wang in court without backing down. Meanwhile, she clumsily sewed a cloth tiger for Yuanlang.

The cloth tiger was a gift from Gu Tingxue to Yuanlang. Yuanlang insisted on sleeping with it every night and had somehow torn a hole in it.

Yuanlang refused to let anyone else sew it—he wanted his own mother to do it.

Xiangjun had no choice but to pick up her needlework, a skill she was not particularly good at, and sew the cloth tiger for her son.

Before she could answer Xiao Luzi’s question, someone else answered for her.

Gu Tingxue walked in, smiling. "He won’t. The fact that the Emperor allows Lord Xu to argue with General Wang in court is already a form of support."

chapters.title: Has Your Highness Ever Thought of This Servant?
chapters.content:
Gu Tingxue entered.

It had been some days since Xiangjun had seen Gu Tingxue. Recently, the Emperor had been in a foul mood, and the Empress Dowager had fallen ill, so Gu Tingxue had naturally been busy with affairs of the front court and the harem.

Xiangjun glanced at Yuanlang, who was napping on the bed, and said to Gu Tingxue, "Speak softly. If he knows you're here, he'll start making a fuss again."

These days, Xiangjun had been careful not to let Gu Tingxue spend time alone with Yuanlang in private.

Now that Yuanlang could speak, though not clearly, it was still dangerous if he accidentally said the wrong thing in front of the Emperor or other concubines.

Gu Tingxue glanced at the sleeping Yuanlang and lowered his voice.

"Greetings, Your Highness."

Xiangjun gave Xiao Luzi a look, and Xiao Luzi immediately bowed to Minister Gu with a smile.

"It's been a while since we last saw Minister Gu. This humble servant will go pour tea for you right away."

Xiao Luzi quickly exited, then returned with tea for Gu Tingxue before stepping out again and closing the door.

Gu Tingxue smiled and said, "Your Highness is wise, and your subordinates are clever too. I was wondering how Minister Xu came up with such a brilliant idea, but it turns out it was Your Highness's doing."

"What clever idea? I merely understand the Emperor, that's all."

Xiangjun knew that natural disasters were no one's fault.

But no matter whose fault it was, the Emperor could not be at fault. So Xiangjun searched around and found that this matter could only be the Empress's fault.

She had merely asked Xu Huanwen to voice what the Emperor had in mind.

"You've done well this time, Your Highness. But Xu Huanwen must win against Grand General Wang and his lackeys to prove his worth to the Emperor. If he wins, he will gain the Emperor's true trust. But if he loses, won't Your Highness be afraid that the Emperor will let Minister Xu bear the brunt of Grand General Wang's wrath alone? Your Highness only has one useful brother."

Xiangjun smiled. "Brother is a smart man. If he decided to do it, he must have considered the consequences. He not only needs to prove his worth to the Emperor but also to me, that he can be my brother."

"Your Highness is indeed decisive."

"I don't think Brother will necessarily lose."

Xu Huanwen and Xiangjun were similar in that they had both climbed up from the bottom. People like them were best at finding opportunities in crises.

"Let's hope Your Highness hasn't misjudged him. This humble servant has heard that Grand General Wang has privately stated he will definitely get rid of Xu Huanwen."

Xiangjun finally felt a pang of tension.

"Surely he wouldn't dare? Killing a court official in the capital—is Grand General Wang not afraid the Emperor will find a reason to punish him?"

"Doing it openly is indeed not possible, but there are ways to do it secretly."

Xiangjun fell silent.

Sometimes political struggles weren't all about schemes and plots. Assassinations and intimidation were often the most direct and effective methods.

"Your Highness need not worry. I have already sent people to protect Minister Xu. Moreover, Minister Xu is not foolish. I've heard he has brought many martial arts experts from Jiangnan to guard him day and night. He is usually very cautious."

Xiangjun let out a sigh of relief. Indeed, someone like Xu Huanwen would not be careless.

Xiangjun then looked at Gu Tingxue and asked, "Why are you helping me?"

"Being Your Highness's opponent doesn't prevent me from helping you. Otherwise, if Your Highness loses too quickly, wouldn't that be rather boring?"

Xiangjun coldly huffed, "Be careful not to lift a rock only to drop it on your own foot."

Xiangjun, puffing with indignation, continued sewing the cloth tiger.

Gu Tingxue watched as Xiangjun sewed the cloth tiger crookedly and couldn't bear to look.

"Your Highness's embroidery is rather poor."

Xiangjun coldly huffed again, "I didn't need to learn needlework as a child because of my beauty. Besides, I am Yuanlang's mother. Would he dare to complain about my sewing?"

Gu Tingxue couldn't bear to watch Xiangjun's needlework any longer. He took the half-sewn cloth tiger from her and started sewing it himself.

Xiangjun leaned over to look and was surprised to find that Gu Tingxue's embroidery was quite good.

"How do you even know how to do this?"

It wasn't strange for a eunuch to know how to sew and mend, as eunuchs were pitiful people who had to learn to do everything themselves.

But Gu Tingxue was no ordinary eunuch, so he shouldn't need to do such things.

"When I was a child, my mother had a hard life. I learned to do anything that could help her. My mother was excellent at embroidery, and I learned from her."

This was the first time Gu Tingxue had mentioned his mother.

Xiangjun felt a little tense and casually probed, "Where is your mother now? Why haven't I heard you mention her before?"

Gu Tingxue didn't answer. Instead, he continued to focus on sewing the cloth tiger.

Xiangjun sighed silently and didn't press further.

Perhaps it wasn't the right time yet.

Soon, Gu Tingxue finished sewing.

"Done."

Gu Tingxue handed the cloth tiger to Xiangjun.

Xiangjun looked at it. Since Gu Tingxue hadn't removed the part she had sewn earlier, the stitches on the back of the cloth tiger were half jagged and half neat.

"Why didn't you remove the part I sewed?"

"A mother's stitches are always different." Gu Tingxue rarely showed such a tender expression. He glanced at Yuanlang on the bed and said, "Next time it breaks, don't mend it. When I have time, I'll make a few more for Yuanlang."

Xiangjun was surprised. "Did you make this cloth tiger?"

Gu Tingxue's expression changed slightly, and he looked a bit embarrassed.

Xiangjun hadn't seen Gu Tingxue look so shy in a long time. She found it amusing but didn't have the heart to tease him. She immediately said, "You're so busy, yet you found time to make a cloth tiger for Yuanlang. You're too good to him."

Gu Tingxue's expression finally improved a little.

"I can always find time to sew a cloth tiger."

"You take better care of Yuanlang than I do, his mother. I haven't even sewn anything for him. You're really going to outdo me..."

"What Your Highness plans for Yuanlang is far more than a cloth tiger can compare to."

"That's just how we adults think," Xiangjun said, looking at the peacefully sleeping Yuanlang. "I'm afraid that in Yuanlang's heart, no matter how grand my plans are, they can't compare to the importance of his cloth tiger."

Hearing her say that, Gu Tingxue's expression softened.

He looked at Yuanlang on the bed and asked, "How has Yuanlang been these past few days? I heard he had a cough a few days ago."

"He played too wildly and caught a chill, that's all. It's already better. Children occasionally get sick; it's nothing to be too worried about."

Seeing Gu Tingxue's doting gaze on Yuanlang, Xiangjun couldn't help but feel a pang of jealousy.

"You only ask about Yuanlang. You've been here so long, and I haven't seen you ask about me..."

Gu Tingxue's movement as he looked at Yuanlang paused for a moment. Then, without warning, he suddenly stood up and walked behind Xiangjun.

Before Xiangjun could react, she felt Gu Tingxue's arms wrap around her from behind, his hands pressing against the table, enclosing her in his embrace.

She felt his hot breath by her ear.

"Even if I don't ask, I know how Your Highness is doing. But since Your Highness blames me for not caring, I want to know... has Your Highness thought of this servant at all these days, hmm?"

---

chapters.title: Why Ask When You Already Know?
chapters.content:
Xiangjun didn't know what Gu Tingxue was doing.

It had been a warm moment, but now he was provoking her. And Yuanlang was still here.

Xiangjun turned her head, intending to scold Gu Tingxue, but suddenly met his gaze.

Rarely, Gu Tingxue's snake-like eyes held no malice. The way he looked at her was unusually gentle and solemn.

He stared at her intently, as if he might draw closer at any moment, yet he maintained that distance—neither too far nor too close.

Such a gaze made even Xiangjun, who was usually unflappable, feel a rare sense of discomfort.

Xiangjun didn't like her current predicament and tried to slip out of Gu Tingxue's embrace. But as soon as she moved, Gu Tingxue's arms suddenly tightened, pulling her into his arms.

"Your Highness always does this—teases this servant and then tries to run. So naughty."

Xiangjun looked at Gu Tingxue again. This time, the strange tenderness in his eyes was gone, replaced by his usual fierce and lustful expression.

Seeing Gu Tingxue like this, Xiangjun actually felt a sense of relief.

Gu Tingxue noticed her relaxation and smiled. He reached out, roughly wiping her lips to remove the lip rouge, then kissed her.

But just then, a sound came from the bed.

Both of them froze, then quickly separated. Gu Tingxue let go, and Xiangjun stepped back several paces.

Yuanlang sleepily opened his eyes on the bed.

The first thing he saw upon opening his eyes was Gu Tingxue standing right in front of him.

Yuanlang rubbed his eyes and, still half-asleep, reached out his arms for Gu Tingxue to hold him.

Gu Tingxue picked up Yuanlang more smoothly than he had ever picked up Xiangjun, lifting him into his arms and handing him the cloth tiger.

Yuanlang turned the cloth tiger over in his hands a few times, then suddenly giggled. He stretched out his hand and pointed at Gu Tingxue, saying, "Xue... Xue..."

Gu Tingxue looked at Yuanlang with such tenderness, even softer than the gaze he had given Xiangjun moments before.

Xiangjun's usually unshakable heart was slightly melted by the scene.

Gu Tingxue's care for Yuanlang was genuine, far more sincere than his treatment of her.

But when Xiangjun saw how dependent Yuanlang was on Gu Tingxue, she couldn't help but feel a sense of danger. Why was Yuanlang closer to Gu Tingxue than even his own wet nurse?

When Yuanlang grew up, whose word would he listen to? It was truly uncertain.

In history books, there were emperors who trusted their eunuchs more than their own mothers...

Xiangjun's suspicious nature flared up again.

She called Meng Mei in and, while Yuanlang was still drowsy from just waking up, quickly had Meng Mei take Yuanlang away.

Yuanlang was very reluctant, but Gu Tingxue coaxed him, saying he would eat with him soon, before Yuanlang finally, albeit unwillingly, left with Meng Mei.

Xiangjun felt even more upset.

He didn't listen to her but listened to Gu Tingxue.

When she was pregnant, Xiangjun had told Gu Tingxue that this child was also his. She didn't know if Gu Tingxue had taken it to heart, but Yuanlang seemed to have.

After being disturbed by Yuanlang for a while, Xiangjun had no mood to engage in any more banter with Gu Tingxue. Seeing that Gu Tingxue had no intention of leaving, she directly asked, "With the front court in such chaos lately, you must be very busy. How do you have time to come here today? Do you even have time to eat with Yuanlang later?"

"Originally, I was busy, but thanks to Your Highness's clever maneuvering, the Emperor has been in a better mood these days and no longer drags the ministers to discuss affairs in the Tai Ji Hall all the time. That's how I managed to free up some time to come to Chengxiang Hall to specially praise Your Highness."

Hearing Gu Tingxue say this, Xiangjun felt a little uneasy.

Now that the Emperor and the Empress Dowager were at odds, if she made the Emperor happy, wouldn't that make the Empress Dowager unhappy?

"Did my actions ruin the Empress Dowager's plans? Did the Empress Dowager say anything to you?"

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun, his eyes full of admiration.

"Your Highness's insight is becoming sharper. You've even seen through that this is a struggle between the Empress Dowager and the Emperor. Your Highness might understand this better than the ministers of the front court."

Xiangjun didn't feel particularly clever. On the contrary, this matter had made her more vigilant.

The mother-son relationship in the imperial family was different from that of commoners.

She certainly didn't want the day to come when she and Yuanlang ended up like the Empress Dowager and the Emperor.

"It's not that my insight is sharp. It's just that I have a royal son and know that the mother-son relationship in the imperial family is different from others."

Seeing Xiangjun's solemn expression, Gu Tingxue comforted her, "Your Highness need not worry. The Emperor is the Empress Dowager's own son, and the Empress Dowager won't truly let the Emperor bear the blame for eternity. What Your Highness has done is fine. Even if Your Highness hadn't had Minister Xu submit the memorial, the Empress Dowager would have ended up using the Empress to help the Emperor out of the predicament. You two actually had the same idea."

Xiangjun finally let out a sigh of relief. She didn't want to offend the Empress Dowager.

"Do you know what the Empress Dowager and the Emperor are quarrelling about now?"

"The flooding in Jiangnan that killed many disaster victims has enraged the Emperor. Now the Emperor can no longer tolerate the people in Jiangnan and plans to take action against them. But Jiangnan... is the Empress Dowager's foundation."

Years ago, when the Empress Dowager helped the Emperor ascend to the throne, she held great power. If she had wanted to control the court, it would not have been difficult.

But the Empress Dowager had no such attachment. After helping the Emperor take personal control of the government, she stopped interfering in the affairs of the front court, staying in the Ren Shou Palace to chant sutras and pray.

Yet even so, the Emperor was still wary of the political power the Empress Dowager possessed.

Xiangjun carefully scrutinized Gu Tingxue.

She thought to herself that perhaps the Emperor was not wary of the Empress Dowager's power in Jiangnan, but rather, he was wary that in the future, the Empress Dowager would pass this power to Gu Tingxue.

And Gu Tingxue was someone the Emperor did not trust.

Hence, the Emperor was determined to act against Jiangnan.

These three people were indeed mutually dependent yet mutually distrustful.

However, Xiangjun had realized the truth but dared not speak of it.

To this day, she still didn't dare to delve too deeply into the relationship between the Emperor, the Empress Dowager, and Gu Tingxue. It was simply too dangerous.

Xiangjun changed the subject and asked again, "How is the situation in Jiangnan now? Are the disaster victims causing a lot of trouble?"

"Many have died, and there are still disaster victims continuously fleeing to Jiangnan. It will probably be chaotic for a while longer. The Emperor has already sent an imperial envoy to deal with the stubborn old fools in Jiangnan and to requisition grain from Jiangnan to send to the disaster areas."

"The Emperor didn't send you? In the past, matters concerning Jiangnan were always handled by you."

Gu Tingxue looked at Xiangjun, his eyes sharpening again. "Why does Your Highness ask when you already know the answer?"

Xiangjun was taken aback by Gu Tingxue's words. She helplessly met his gaze, and then both of them silently looked away.

In truth, when the Empress Dowager had noticed the relationship between Gu Tingxue and Xiangjun but chose to cover for them, even beginning to help Xiangjun, Xiangjun had already understood some things without needing to be told.

Gu Tingxue, of course, also knew that with Xiangjun's intelligence, she wouldn't be completely in the dark.

But neither of them had poked through that window paper.

Some things could still be muddled through if they pretended not to know. But if they poked through it...

That would be too painful.

Neither Xiangjun nor Gu Tingxue was ready to have that conversation with the other.

chapters.title: The Children Indeed Have Problems
chapters.content:
"Today I want to spend more time with Yuanlang. Is that alright?" Gu Tingxue suddenly said.

"You're going out of the palace again?"

Every time Gu Tingxue had to leave the palace for a while, he would always make time to spend with Yuanlang.

"The locust plague has caused so many refugees, and the treasury doesn't have much silver left. Even if I don't go to Jiangnan, I still have to help His Majesty raise grain. This time, I'll be away from the capital for several months. I probably won't return until before the New Year."

"But in previous years, you killed so many salt merchants for His Majesty and obtained so much silver. Even if His Majesty is extravagant, he shouldn't have spent it all so quickly, right?"

"That was His Majesty's private treasury. His Majesty naturally has other uses for it."

Xiangjun cursed silently in her heart, truly a despicable emperor.

"His Majesty really knows how to use people. Why does he always make you handle these thankless and difficult tasks?"

"What else is His Majesty keeping me, his hound, for? Isn't it to do the dirty work for the emperor?"

In the past, when Xiangjun heard Gu Tingxue say such things, she didn't feel much.

Weren't eunuchs supposed to do the tasks that ministers didn't want to do for the emperor?

But now, hearing Gu Tingxue say this, Xiangjun felt a pang of sadness.

No matter how well the Empress Dowager treated Gu Tingxue, it couldn't change his disreputable status.

Originally, Xiangjun was petty and didn't want Gu Tingxue to be too close to Yuanlang. But now, she felt a bit softened. After all, he had just finished sewing a cloth tiger for Yuanlang.

"I've sent away the wet nurse. Today, you can sleep with Yuanlang. He'll be happy."

Just as Xiangjun finished speaking, Xiao Luzi entered with his head lowered.

Whenever the noble consort and Gu Tingxue were alone in the room, Xiao Luzi never dared to look around.

After entering, Xiao Luzi cautiously glanced and saw that both were sitting properly dressed. He sighed in relief before saying to the noble consort, "Noble Consort, Consort Xian is outside the hall. She says she has urgent matters and wants to see you."

Xiangjun raised her eyebrows. Consort Xian would actually come to see her?

"Have Consort Xian wait for me in the main hall."

Gu Tingxue went to Yuanlang first. Xiangjun tidied herself up a bit before going to the main hall to see Consort Xian.

After Consort Xian lost her child years ago, she had been in seclusion for a long time.

Now that she had returned to His Majesty's side, she seemed much steadier than before. Even the naive innocence she once had was much reduced.

Indeed, hardship could make one grow.

However, Consort Xian was after all a princess of Nanyue. The arrogance was in her bones. Even though Xiangjun was now above her, she still lifted her chin when greeting Xiangjun.

Xiangjun couldn't be bothered to argue with Consort Xian.

Xiangjun granted Consort Xian a seat and even complimented her, "Consort Xian, you have been quite diligent in Nanxun Palace these days. Now, there isn't a trace of your Nanyue accent when you speak."

Hearing Xiangjun say this, Consort Xian couldn't help but recall the past.

The first time she met Xiangjun was in the imperial garden. At that time, Xiangjun was still a selection attendant.

Because Xiangjun had made fun of her accent, and also because she thought Xiangjun was someone under the current empress, she had held a grudge against Xiangjun and made her kneel in the imperial garden for several hours.

But now, in just a few short years, the once lowly selection attendant had become a noble consort.

And she, a princess of Nanyue, could only be in a lower position, addressing someone as Noble Consort.

Consort Xian gritted her teeth for a long time, but remembering why she came today, she endured it. She bowed to Xiangjun and said, "Thank you for your praise, Noble Consort."

Xiangjun held back her laughter and softly said, "Consort Xian, please sit."

Only then did Consort Xian sit down.

Seeing her hesitant look, Xiangjun dismissed the extra palace attendants, leaving only Meng Mei by her side.

"Consort Xian, we are old acquaintances. We know each other's temperaments all too well. Today, if you have something to say, feel free to speak directly."

Consort Xian was not someone who overcomplicated things. Hearing Xiangjun say this, she got straight to the point: "In the past, I had many misunderstandings with you, Noble Consort, and some small grievances. Now, I have truly changed and wish to get along well with you in the future."

Xiangjun smiled slightly. Her expression was still gentle, but her words were not very polite.

"Oh? So Consort Xian thinks that making me kneel in the imperial garden for several hours was a misunderstanding, and framing me for plotting against the imperial heir, causing me to be sent to the Palace Correction Office for punishment, was a small grievance? Consort Xian's heart is truly broad."

Consort Xian choked on her words, knowing she was in the wrong. She glanced at Zhu Jin beside her.

Zhu Jin immediately spoke for Consort Xian: "Indeed, our consort was in the wrong before. But that was so long ago. When our consort was ill, she also received much care from Noble Consort. So, we thought that Noble Consort, being magnanimous, has already let go of our consort's past mistakes, which is why we dared to come see you."

Zhu Jin tugged at her consort, and Consort Xian finally stood up. She took a deep breath and finally made up her mind, giving Xiangjun a deep bow.

"In the past, it was my fault. But after all, I didn't truly harm Noble Consort. Noble Consort need not be so petty."

Zhu Jin tugged at Consort Xian from behind, and Consort Xian changed her words again.

"If Noble Consort is displeased with me, I can also kneel in the imperial garden for a few hours to appease you."

Xiangjun smiled, "I am not that petty. But, do you not understand why I would take care of you?"

Consort Xian looked at Xiangjun. She didn't understand, but Zhu Jin did. Zhu Jin had told her that Noble Consort and the Empress were on the surface harmonious but at heart at odds. Noble Consort had also seen that Consort Xian's submission to the Empress was feigned, which was why she was willing to help her.

"I understand, Noble Consort. Naturally, you hope that I can help you relieve your worries. Noble Consort, you are straightforward, so I will speak directly as well. I came today to seek your patronage."

"Aren't you under the patronage of Her Majesty the Empress now?"

"The Empress is my enemy. If the Empress doesn't understand this, does Noble Consort not understand either? Now, Noble Consort and the Empress are on equal footing. In the front court, Great General Wang and Noble Consort's brother are also fighting fiercely. I know something that can help Noble Consort and also help Lord Xu. I wonder if Noble Consort is interested in hearing it?"

Xiangjun finally took some interest in Consort Xian's words.

"What is it?"

"If I can help you, Noble Consort, then if in the future, Her Majesty the Empress wants to settle scores with me, would you be willing to show me some favor and protect my life?"

"Consort Xian, you really think too highly of me. I am only a noble consort and don't even have authority over the palace. How can I help you?"

"You are too modest, Noble Consort. Who doesn't know that although the harem is managed by the Empress, the one who truly has the final say is you, Noble Consort?"

Xiangjun thought for a moment, her expression becoming serious. "Then it depends on whether what you say can truly help me."

"Noble Consort, rest assured. When you hear this news, you will definitely be very happy."

Xiangjun gestured for Consort Xian to come closer.

Consort Xian approached Xiangjun and whispered a few words in her ear.

Xiangjun's expression changed drastically, looking at Consort Xian in disbelief.

Sure enough, her guess was correct. Consort Xian hated the Empress so much, how could she truly help her?

Those two children indeed had problems.

---

chapters.title: Idiotic Children
chapters.content:
"Is this true?" Xiangjun asked in a low voice.

"Naturally. Noble Consort can verify it."

Xiangjun felt a bit shocked inside and had Meng Mei and Zhu Jin go out to guard, not allowing anyone to approach.

After they both left, Xiangjun looked at Consort Xian and asked, "How did you do it?"

"I gave her a secret formula from Nanyue. The Empress's body is no longer suitable for pregnancy. Even if she conceives, it would still harm the fetus. I originally thought the Empress would give birth to a deformed child, but she was lucky. She only gave birth to two idiots, which is the mildest side effect."

"But didn't the Empress have someone check the formula you gave her?"

"Since it's a secret formula, naturally, those who are not from the Nanyue royal court cannot find out."

Xiangjun still found it somewhat incredible.

"Then how did she dare to use it?"

"That's because Noble Consort hasn't seen how I've been groveling in front of the Empress these past two years. I almost knelt on the ground to lick her feet." Consort Xian's tone was somewhat self-deprecating.

But this time, Xiangjun was truly a bit impressed by Consort Xian.

A person like Consort Xian, who found it hard to change her nature, being so arrogant and domineering, even more so than Xiangjun herself, could actually lower herself due to hatred. She was indeed ruthless to herself.

It wasn't hard to understand why the Empress ultimately chose to trust her. Didn't King Fuchai of Wu also trust King Goujian of Yue?

Xiangjun couldn't help but sigh, "Consort Xian, your methods are truly ruthless. I admit I'm not your match."

The hatred in Consort Xian's eyes was impossible to conceal.

"Me, ruthless? My child was already eight months old back then. He was an imperial prince! That wretched Empress caused my child to die in my womb. I almost lost my life. If it weren't for the divine medicine from Nanyue that kept me alive, I would have died. But even so, I can never have children again in this lifetime. With such a deep grudge, I didn't flay her alive. I only made her give birth to two idiots. I'm already doing a favor for my dead child by showing mercy."

The hatred in Consort Xian's eyes was undeniable. Xiangjun said solemnly, "I will have someone verify this matter. Consort Xian, you may return first. I also promise you, if this is true, even if the Empress finds out the truth, I will never let her harm you. You will still be able to remain as Consort Xian."

Only then did Consort Xian feel at ease and bowed to Xiangjun.

"Then I will wait for your good news, sister."

After Consort Xian left, Xiangjun immediately called for Physician Liu to inquire about the condition of the Empress's twin children.

"In response to Noble Consort, the Sixth Prince and the Fourth Princess are indeed a bit... sluggish compared to other children. However, with children this young, it's hard to tell if they are clever or not. We might have to wait until they are a bit older."

Xiangjun frowned. She knew that the imperial physician had to be cautious with his words.

"Physician Liu, just tell me, do you think these two children are more like idiots or more like normal children? You don't need to have any concrete evidence. Just tell me your judgment."

Physician Liu hesitated for a while before saying, "Noble Consort, this humble official has long felt that something is wrong with these two children. But since they are the Empress's children and are twins, a auspicious birth recognized by His Majesty, even if everyone feels something is wrong, no one dares to say anything."

"How can you tell?"

"For example, the Fifth Prince at this age was already very good at smiling and playing with adults. But the Empress's two children never seem to react much to others. They don't make eye contact with adults, not even with the Empress or their wet nurses."

"Hasn't the Empress noticed? This isn't her first child."

"The Empress is busy with palace affairs every day and doesn't spend as much time with the children as the wet nurses do. Moreover, the Empress has a mother's heart, so she hasn't noticed anything unusual about the children. She just thinks they are particularly well-behaved."

Xiangjun thought for a moment and asked again, "Are there any other signs?"

"Yes. The wet nurses of the Sixth Prince and Fourth Princess have privately complained that these two children are particularly difficult to feed, unlike normal children. Also... children at four months old should be able to lift their heads, but these two still cannot. This humble official originally wanted to wait until the children were older to confirm before speaking to Noble Consort. But since Noble Consort asked today, I dare to speculate that... these two children indeed have some problems."

Xiangjun now believed eight parts out of ten that the two children were idiots.

Initially, she had thought that Consort Xian wouldn't be so kind.

But she hadn't expected Consort Xian to be so ruthless.

Xiangjun even felt a bit sympathetic towards the Empress.

How tragic...

The most tragic thing wasn't that the children were idiots, but the contrast before and after.

Although Consort Xian had intended for the children to be born deformed, in reality, giving birth to two idiots was more heartbreaking than giving birth to deformed children.

If they were deformed, with His Majesty's temperament, he would have had them buried alive immediately.

But now, the Empress had already developed feelings for the two children. To have her give them up would be heart-wrenching.

Consort Xian, unintentionally, had dealt a heart-wrenching blow to the Empress.

Xiangjun gave Physician Liu a few more instructions before letting him leave.

After he left, Meng Mei said, "Noble Consort, my brother is the most cautious person. If he dares to say this, it's likely that the Sixth Prince and Fourth Princess are indeed somewhat off. Should we inform His Majesty or Lord Xu about this?"

"I know. But this matter cannot be brought up by us. It's better to have the Qin Tian Jian handle it."

Meng Mei reminded Xiangjun again, "Noble Consort, if this matter is confirmed, will you really protect Consort Xian?"

"I've already promised, so naturally I will protect her."

Meng Mei thought for a moment and still reminded, "Noble Consort, this servant knows that you always keep your word. But the favor Consort Xian has done for you is not enough to guarantee her life. Even if she doesn't say anything, in a while, everyone will find out. But once the Empress knows the truth, she will definitely seek revenge against Consort Xian. Why must you get involved?"

"I promised Consort Xian to protect her from the Empress, but I never promised to protect her forever."

Meng Mei asked, "What does Noble Consort mean?"

"As long as the Northern Mongols are not destroyed, the south cannot be in chaos. The Emperor still needs the King of Nanyue to balance the small countries in the south. Even if I don't protect Consort Xian, His Majesty will not punish Consort Xian for this matter. He might even try to cover it up for her. So, if Consort Xian understands the court situation, she wouldn't have needed to come to me today."

"Does Noble Consort mean that His Majesty will still deal with Consort Xian in the future?"

"He definitely will. His Majesty is not a generous person. He is very petty. Consort Xian has caused a lot of harm in the palace, even harming His Majesty. The King of Nanyue is not truly loyal either. He only follows the Great Qi for his own interests, actually hesitating between sides and harboring ulterior motives. His Majesty has always known this, but he can't deal with it now. He's just waiting for the right time to settle the score."

Only then did Meng Mei sigh in relief.

"That's good. I thought Noble Consort had forgotten how Consort Xian had bullied you in the past. This servant will never forget how you were sent to the Palace Correction Office for punishment."

"Rest assured, I will not let Consort Xian off. But my reason for not letting her off is not because I hold a grudge against her for past injuries."

It wasn't that Xiangjun was particularly magnanimous, but the higher she climbed, the more she realized that personal grievances were often less important than interests.

If one always acted based on their emotions, they would definitely ruin things.

"Noble Consort, if you don't hold a grudge against Consort Xian, why won't you let her off?"

"It's because today's matter between the Empress and Consort Xian has made me realize that we must either be hypocritically kind to others or eliminate them completely. Showing mercy and harboring fantasies towards someone who has had conflicts with you in the past will ultimately only harm yourself. So, Meng Mei, you must remember this: from now on, in Chengxiang Palace, we either don't do something, or we do it thoroughly. We must never leave any hidden troubles."

chapters.title: The Dog Slave, How Dare He Deceive This Palace
chapters.content:
Xiangjun had finished all the important matters and given all her instructions. It was already past the time when the palace gates were locked.

She wanted to go see Yuanlang and Gu Tingxue, but then heard Xiyu report softly, "Your Majesty, Lord Gu... Lord Gu carried the Fifth Prince to your bedchamber to sleep."

Xiangjun glared at Xiyu. "Do you just let him do whatever he wants?"

"Didn't Your Majesty say that in Chengxiang Hall, everything with Lord Gu remains as it was before? We never paid him any mind in the past," Xiyu replied.

Xiangjun had no choice but to dismiss Xiyu and enter the bedchamber alone.

Lifting the bed curtains, Xiangjun saw a warm scene: Gu Tingxue was lying flat, his sleeping posture impeccable. Yuanlang, on the other hand, was twisted in his sleep, his little feet almost kicking up to his head.

At the sight of Yuanlang, Xiangjun couldn't help but laugh. She reached out and gently touched Yuanlang's little face.

But looking at Yuanlang, a hint of melancholy arose in her heart.

"What's wrong, Your Majesty?" Gu Tingxue's voice suddenly rang out.

Xiangjun looked up and saw that Gu Tingxue had opened his eyes at some point and was watching her.

"You weren't asleep?"

"I was waiting for you." Gu Tingxue asked, "What happened? It was just a meeting with the Virtuous Consort. Why did it take so long?"

Xiangjun told Gu Tingxue what the Virtuous Consort had said and Doctor Liu's speculations.

Gu Tingxue wasn't too surprised. Given his understanding of Nanyue, such underhanded methods weren't uncommon.

"If the Empress's children have issues, that's a good thing for Your Majesty. Why are you so melancholy?"

"I'm just a little afraid."

"Afraid of what?"

"Afraid that Yuanlang is a fool."

Gu Tingxue was rendered speechless by Xiangjun's words, a mix of laughter and exasperation. He glanced at Yuanlang affectionately and whispered, "Our Yuanlang is the smartest. Your Majesty shouldn't compare our Yuanlang to other people's good children."

Xiangjun knew Yuanlang was fine, but as a mother, she could never stop worrying about her child.

Xiangjun kissed Yuanlang and moved his leg, which had been resting beside his head, back into place.

The two of them lay on either side of Yuanlang, gazing at him with soft expressions. After a long while, Xiangjun felt the atmosphere was a bit off.

This seemed to be the first time the two of them had slept with Yuanlang together.

"Why did you bring Yuanlang here to sleep?"

"Yuanlang insisted on coming."

"Don't try to fool this palace. Normally, Yuanlang sleeps with his wet nurse. He doesn't have the habit of sleeping with me."

"Then it was I who wanted to sleep with you. Is that alright?"

Xiangjun felt something was off with Gu Tingxue. He was unusually tender today, which was not like him at all.

"When are you leaving?"

"Tomorrow."

"So soon?"

"The Emperor originally wanted me to leave today, but because of the Dowager Empress's condition, he allowed me to bid her farewell tomorrow morning before departing. This trip will take at least two or three months, round trip."

Xiangjun thought for a moment and said, "By the time you return, Yuanlang will probably have forgotten you."

Gu Tingxue's eyes darkened.

"Does Your Majesty hope that Yuanlang forgets me?"

"I'm afraid that one day Yuanlang might tell the Emperor that we both slept holding him at night! This palace still wants to live. Of course, it's better if Yuanlang forgets you. What are you afraid of? When you return, spend some time with him, and he'll remember you again."

Perhaps their voices were too loud, as they seemed to have woken Yuanlang.

Suddenly, Yuanlang puckered his lips, rubbed his eyes, and began to whimper as if about to cry.

Gu Tingxue immediately picked up Yuanlang and soothed him. He stood up and shot Xiangjun a cold glance.

"I'll take Yuanlang back to his room to sleep."

Gu Tingxue left with Yuanlang before Xiangjun could even try to stop him. She sat on the bed, bewildered.

Everything had been fine. Why was he angry again?

But Xiangjun's mind was filled with thoughts of the Empress and her two children. She had no energy to ponder why Gu Tingxue was upset with her.

The next morning, when Mengmei brought Yuanlang over, Gu Tingxue was already gone.

According to Xiaoluzi, Gu Tingxue had left in the middle of the night. He first went to the Ren Shou Palace, then left the palace directly.

It wasn't until the morning, when Li came to the palace and Xiangjun had finished giving her instructions, that Li mentioned the news outside. Only then did Xiangjun learn what Gu Tingxue was really going to do.

"I heard that things are chaotic outside. Not only is Jiangnan in turmoil, but Northern Zhili is as well. My husband says that in the disaster-stricken areas, people have already rebelled. The leaders are quite formidable... However, the court has been suppressing this news, not daring to let the common people know, fearing it would cause even greater chaos. Now, the Emperor has dispatched Lord Gu and the Shence Army to quell the rebellion."

Xiangjun's heart sank. "It's just a rebellion by disaster victims. Surely Lord Gu's Shence Army can handle it. There shouldn't be any problem, right?"

"If it were just a rebellion, that would be fine..." Li lowered her voice. "But so many people have died, and there's talk of a plague. Lord Gu's trip to quell the rebellion is quite dangerous. The plague doesn't care who you are."

...

After Li left, Xiangjun was so angry that she cursed Gu Tingxue from head to toe in Chengxiang Hall.

"Dog slave! He even hid such a thing from this palace! No wonder he acted so strangely yesterday! How dare he deceive this palace!"

Xiaoluzi and Xiyu didn't dare to breathe loudly.

Xiangjun suddenly let out a cold laugh.

"That's not right. This palace misspoke. Of course, he dares to deceive this palace. This isn't the first time that dog slave has lied to this palace."

Xiangjun was furious, and she smashed the teacup in her hand onto the ground, her anger boiling over.

"Your Majesty, please don't be angry. Lord Gu is blessed with good fortune. This time, when he goes to quell the rebellion, he will definitely be safe."

"This palace doesn't care about his life or death. It would be better if he died, saving this palace the trouble of dealing with him in the future."

Xiaoluzi and Xiyu exchanged a glance and said nothing.

Finally, Mengmei hurried in and whispered to Xiangjun, "Your Majesty, this servant has asked around. Lord Gu's Shence Army set out from Anding Gate at noon today."

"What time is it now?"

"Noon," Mengmei replied. "Lord Gu should have just departed..."

Xiangjun was silent for a moment, her gaze falling on Xiaoluzi.

Xiaoluzi felt a chill run down his spine and immediately averted his eyes, wishing he could tuck his head into his pants.

"Xiaoluzi."

Xiaoluzi sighed heavily in his mind but still stepped forward.

"Your Majesty, this servant is here."

"This palace remembers you can ride a horse?"

"This servant can."

"Then you will do this palace a favor. Leave the palace immediately and go to Baihua Gaoyun Fang to buy a portion of almond cheese for this palace."

---

chapters.title: The Emperor’s Heart is Truly Ruthless
chapters.content:
After leaving the city, Xiaoluzi chased for several more miles before finally catching up with the Shence Army.

It was fortunate that Xiaoluzi wasn't carrying any heavy baggage, or he might not have been able to catch up with the Shence Army.

When the guards brought Xiaoluzi before Gu Tingxue, Gu Tingxue didn't recognize him at first glance.

It was only when Xiaoluzi took off his hat and tore off his fake mustache that Gu Tingxue recognized him.

Gu Tingxue raised an eyebrow and looked down at Xiaoluzi. "How did Eunuch Liu come here?"

Xiaoluzi approached Gu Tingxue's horse and bowed to him.

"Upon learning that Lord Gu was going on a long journey, the mistress specially sent this servant to deliver a few words to you."

Gu Tingxue dismounted, his expression rarely showing some warmth.

"What did Her Majesty ask you to do? Speak."

Unexpectedly, Xiaoluzi gave Gu Tingxue a slap across the face. Even someone as composed as Gu Tingxue couldn't help but twitch the corner of his mouth.

"What are you doing?"

Xiaoluzi grinned. "Her Majesty ordered me to give Lord Gu a slap when I see you."

"Is this slap for me?"

"Yes, this servant has given Lord Gu a slap. It's just one slap, so please don't make things difficult for this servant."

Gu Tingxue rarely smiled, but he did so now, waving his hand. "Alright, what else did Her Majesty ask you to say?"

Xiaoluzi took an oil-paper package from his bosom and handed it to Gu Tingxue.

Gu Tingxue opened it and saw two small dough figurines inside: one of a palace concubine and one of a eunuch.

"These figurines were bought by this servant when Her Majesty attended Lord Xu's wedding outside the palace. They were supposed to be given to you earlier, but some misunderstandings delayed it. Her Majesty says to ask Lord Gu to take good care of yourself while away. Her Majesty is sentimental and doesn't like to replace those who are familiar and reliable."

Gu Tingxue looked at the figurines in his hand and smiled softly.

Xiaoluzi studied Gu Tingxue's expression, momentarily dazzled by the sight of Gu Tingxue's gentle smile.

"Please trouble Eunuch Liu to convey this to Her Majesty: Tingxue will definitely return safe and sound. My bet with Her Majesty is not yet settled, so how could I bear to die? I am still waiting for Her Majesty to grant my wish."

With that, Gu Tingxue tucked the figurines into his bosom and mounted his horse again.

...

Xiaoluzi managed to return to Chengxiang Hall just before the palace gates were locked.

Upon hearing Xiaoluzi's message, Xiangjun still couldn't help but curse, "Dog slave."

She rewarded Xiaoluzi. When only Xiangjun and Mengmei remained in the hall, Mengmei spoke softly, "Your Majesty, rest assured. Lord Gu will definitely return safely."

Xiangjun couldn't say for sure. She felt that someone like Gu Tingxue wouldn't die so easily.

But...

Xiangjun sighed. "Yesterday, the last thing I said to him was... it would be better if Yuanlang forgot him... Thinking about this, this palace feels truly uncomfortable..."

No wonder Gu Tingxue had been angry when he heard those words yesterday.

He was going to a plague-stricken area; his life was uncertain. Yet she had hoped that Yuanlang would quickly forget him.

Xiangjun felt she was truly wicked.

If something really happened to Gu Tingxue, and the last words she had said to him were those, she would feel terrible.

"Your Majesty, you have said many harsh words to Lord Gu before. He must be used to it by now and won't take it to heart."

Xiangjun glared at Mengmei.

Mengmei smiled gently and consoled her again. "Your Majesty, don't take such a small matter to heart. Yuanlang likes Lord Gu so much. Even if he forgets you, he won't forget Lord Gu."

Xiangjun felt as if a knife had been plunged into her heart.

But her mood did lighten a bit.

"Enough. Since things have come to this, whether he returns alive or not is up to heaven's will." Xiangjun's expression changed. "The most urgent matter for this palace right now is still the Empress's children."

Mengmei's expression also turned serious.

"Your Majesty, rest assured. My brother's side is all prepared."

...

The next day, Great General Wang and Xu Huanwen were still arguing fiercely.

After court, Xu Huanwen once again took the astronomers to the Tai Ji Hall.

No one in the palace knew what Xu Huanwen had said to the Emperor, but it was said that the Emperor had flown into a great rage and then summoned several imperial physicians.

It wasn't until the palace gates were about to be locked that Xu Huanwen and the astronomers left the imperial palace.

That very night, the Empress in Ganlu Palace had a huge argument with the Emperor. It was said that the Emperor had even slapped the Empress.

Some had seen the Emperor kicking over several palace servants as he left Ganlu Palace.

The Emperor had rarely visited the rear palace, and this time he had come in a fit of rage, leaving the concubines who had been hoping for imperial favor very disappointed.

For the next half month, the doors of Ganlu Palace remained closed.

The rear palace was as quiet as if it were inhabited by the dead.

Great General Wang, who had been locked in a fierce struggle with Xu Huanwen in the front court, suddenly fell silent.

Finally, after half a month of cold war, the doors of Ganlu Palace opened.

The Empress removed her court attire and wore plain clothes. She took off her hairpins and knelt at every step as she made her way to the Tai Ji Hall to plead guilty.

The Empress "voluntarily" took the blame for the natural disasters and requested to go to the grand Buddha hall in the imperial palace to observe a fast, until the disasters ended and heaven forgave her sins.

And she was willing to endure such humiliation all for the sake of her two children.

The Emperor granted the Empress's request. Thus, the palace authority that the Empress had tightly held onto was once again lightly returned to Xiangjun's hands.

Although Xiangjun and the Empress were at odds, seeing the Emperor's attitude toward the Empress and her two children, Xiangjun still felt a sense of shared adversity.

Those two children were the Emperor's own flesh and blood, and he had truly cherished them.

When they were first born, the Emperor had doted on the twins so much that he had even granted a general amnesty across the land.

The Emperor's affection for the two children was genuine.

But this was the most terrifying part of the whole affair.

Xiangjun had never imagined that the Emperor could be so ruthless.

The Emperor truly loved the two children, yet upon learning that they might be imbeciles, he disregarded all fatherly affection and intended to kill them.

Several imperial physicians had told the Emperor that it would take a few more years to confirm whether the children were truly imbeciles. For now, it just seemed more likely.

But the Emperor wasn't even willing to wait a few more years.

If not for the Empress threatening to take her own life and agreeing to take the blame for the natural disasters, along with Great General Wang's concession in the front court, the two children would likely already be dead.

"Now that the Empress is fasting in the grand Buddha hall, where are the Sixth Prince and the Fourth Princess?" Xiangjun asked Doctor Liu.

"The Emperor had the children sent to be raised in the place where the imperial concubines live. The Emperor ordered that if the children are fine in a few years, they will be returned to the Empress. But if they are truly imbeciles... the imperial family cannot allow such a disgraceful thing to happen."

Hearing Doctor Liu's account, Xiangjun felt a chill run down her spine.

Even tigers do not eat their own cubs. In the common households, not everyone would kill a child with problems.

Even if the prince and princess were imbeciles, with people to attend to them, they could live a stable life until their natural end. It would just require a few more attendants.

Looking at the palace token and ledger that had been returned to her hands, Xiangjun felt no joy of victory. Instead, she only felt a deep wariness toward the Emperor.

The Emperor was truly a ruthless man.

chapters.title: Today, the Grand Dowager Empress let her in, likely to say something very important to her.
chapters.content:
The Empress had written a letter of self-reproach, and with the astrological office's endorsement, the Emperor finally managed to shift the blame for the natural disaster away from himself.

Now, the Emperor was in a better mood to visit the imperial harem again.

During this period, the Emperor had been especially good to Xiangjun and Yuanlang, as if Xiangjun had become the Emperor's new true love, and Yuanlang had replaced Yuanze as the Emperor's most beloved child.

And Yuanze...

The Fourth Prince was now old enough to understand things.

When such a great calamity suddenly befell the Ganlu Palace, he more or less understood what had happened.

Yet the Emperor had not even gone to see the Fourth Prince once. If it weren't for Xiangjun managing the imperial harem, and everyone daring not to overstep their bounds, Xiangjun could imagine what kind of life the Fourth Prince would have in Ganlu Palace.

The Emperor himself had experienced the days when his birth mother was slandered, and he had no mother to protect him.

Now, he had made his "most beloved" woman the sinner of Dai Qi, despised by all, and he didn't care about the Fourth Prince's fate. It showed how cold and selfish the man was.

In this world, only his pain was pain; the Emperor didn't care about others' at all.

So when the Emperor gazed at Xiangjun with eyes full of affection and doted on Yuanlang like a kind father...

Xiangjun not only didn't feel happy, but instead felt as if she was being constricted by a python, unable to breathe.

The more the Emperor favored them mother and son, the more suffocated Xiangjun felt.

The Emperor's love was truly unbearable for ordinary people. Even the Empress, who was destined to be the female lead, had to suffer greatly. Xiangjun didn't think she was luckier than the Empress.

However, it seemed the Emperor was not having a good time this year. He had returned to the imperial harem for less than half a month when another incident occurred in the front court.

The Emperor's envoy sent to Jiangnan had been killed...

The Emperor began spending his nights alone in the Taiji Hall again.

Even when two concubines in the imperial harem gave birth one after another, the Emperor did not come to see them once.

The palace had a new Seventh Prince and a Fifth Princess.

Xiangjun resumed managing the imperial harem, but unlike before, she was no longer as proud. Instead, she became more cautious. Even Mengmei noticed that although the Noble Consort appeared the same on the surface, she often couldn't sleep at night and was not as carefree as before.

It was said that the Grand Dowager Empress had been calling for imperial physicians frequently these days. Although she had been turned away many times before, Xiangjun still went to the Renshou Palace, hoping to pay her respects to the Grand Dowager Empress.

Unexpectedly, this time, the Grand Dowager Empress did not refuse and allowed Xiangjun to enter.

Xiangjun had originally thought that the Grand Dowager Empress was feigning illness. But when she saw her, she realized that the Grand Dowager Empress's complexion was indeed not good. She had lost a lot of weight, and there were even many white hairs at her temples.

Xiangjun hurriedly stepped forward and asked, "Grand Dowager Empress, are you really ill?"

The Grand Dowager Empress even looked a bit helpless. She smiled weakly, her face worn and haggard, and said, "You clever little thing, do you think I'm faking my illness?"

Xiangjun nodded embarrassedly.

With a glance from the Grand Dowager Empress, everyone in the hall withdrew, leaving only Xiangjun to attend to her.

The Grand Dowager Empress leaned against the soft pillow on the bed, while Xiangjun sat on the embroidered stool by the bed.

"If I had known that the Grand Dowager Empress was truly ill, even if the other consorts had stopped me, I would have come in to keep you company."

"At that time, I was indeed not ill. But the Emperor..." The Grand Dowager Empress's eyes darkened, and her voice carried a hint of coldness. "To force me, the Emperor sent Tingxue to the epidemic area to suppress the rebellion. He wants to cut out my heart."

The Grand Dowager Empress coughed a few times, and Xiangjun quickly stood up to hand her a cup of tea.

After drinking the tea, the Grand Dowager Empress's breathing finally calmed down a bit.

"So the Grand Dowager Empress fell ill because of Tingxue's matter. But if the Grand Dowager Empress cares so much about Tingxue, why did you still let him go to suppress the rebellion? I heard that many people died in Beizhili."

"Do you think that if I compromise with the Emperor this time, Tingxue will be safe?"

Xiangjun fell silent. She could see that the Emperor would eventually deal with Gu Tingxue. The Grand Dowager Empress was trying to buy time for Gu Tingxue.

Thinking of how the Grand Dowager Empress still had to work so hard, Xiangjun couldn't help but feel a sense of sorrow.

"Tingxue will be fine. He is not without the means to protect himself. Tingxue can take care of himself. The most important thing is for the Grand Dowager Empress to take care of your health. Only if you live well can you protect him for a few more years."

The Grand Dowager Empress looked at Xiangjun and asked meaningfully, "Aren't you curious why I care so much about Tingxue?"

"Not curious." Xiangjun answered almost without hesitation.

"Why?"

"Because this subject knows that curiosity can be fatal. If there are things you want me to know, the Grand Dowager Empress will naturally tell me. This subject only needs to know that the Grand Dowager Empress cares about Tingxue and, for Tingxue's sake, is willing to look after me. So I will also reciprocate your kindness. That is enough."

"You are no longer pretending to be foolish in front of me."

Xiangjun smiled and said, "This subject thought the Grand Dowager Empress liked my honesty."

"I do like it..." The Grand Dowager Empress sighed and took Xiangjun's hand. "Talking to you is the most relaxing for me. In this Emperor's imperial harem, there are few sensible people. Especially the Empress, every time I talk to her, I get a headache."

Xiangjun was left speechless by the Grand Dowager Empress's teasing.

Speaking of the Empress, Xiangjun tentatively asked, "While the Grand Dowager Empress is recuperating in the Renshou Palace, have you heard about the Sixth Prince and the Fourth Princess?"

"I have heard."

The Grand Dowager Empress's face showed even deeper worry. She looked into the distance with a profound gaze and sighed heavily.

"The Emperor has been quite cold to those two children. If he treats his own flesh and blood so cruelly, I fear he will be even more ruthless to his siblings."

Xiangjun immediately said, "As for the other princes, as long as they behave and do not provoke the Emperor, he will not do anything to them. The Emperor is wary of his siblings, such as the Prince of Jin and the Grand General Wang, but they have their own power, and the Emperor does not dare to act against them lightly. So, the Grand Dowager Empress can rest assured. Even the Emperor's siblings, as long as they have their own power—whether it be the support of officials, military power, or a good reputation—the Emperor will not act recklessly. Moreover, the Emperor's brothers are not as fragile as the Grand Dowager Empress thinks; they are not without the means to protect themselves."

The Grand Dowager Empress understood Xiangjun's implied concerns.

The Grand Dowager Empress looked at Xiangjun deeply and nodded in satisfaction.

"Indeed, you are a clever and sensible child. If I entrust Tingxue to you, I can also rest assured. In the future, if I am no longer around, perhaps you are the only one in this world who can protect him."

The Grand Dowager Empress said this very calmly, but it weighed heavily on Xiangjun's heart.

This time, it was Xiangjun's turn to be shocked.

Could it be that the Grand Dowager Empress had been so kind to her all along because she intended to entrust Gu Tingxue to her care?

Xiangjun's intuition told her that today, the Grand Dowager Empress had let her in because she had something very important to say to her.

chapters.title: The filthiest child in the world
chapters.content:
Although the Grand Dowager Empress had the intention of "entrusting an orphan," Xiangjun still did not dare to probe lightly.

"Grand Dowager Empress, you are in good health. Don't always say such inauspicious things. As long as you take care of yourself, we, as your juniors, will have someone to look after us, won't we?"

The Grand Dowager Empress gave a bitter smile and shook her head helplessly.

"I know my own body best. When I returned from the north years ago, the doctors all declared that I would not live past forty. Although I have managed to prolong my life by more than a decade with the best medicines in the world, I am now nearing the end. My body can only last a year or two more."

Xiangjun felt a pang of sadness upon learning that the Grand Dowager Empress did not have much time left.

She was not someone who easily showed emotion, but she felt a kind of kinship with the Grand Dowager Empress.

The Grand Dowager Empress looked at Xiangjun again and asked, "Can I entrust Tingxue to you?"

"Grand Dowager Empress, may I ask you a question first?"

The Grand Dowager Empress nodded.

"Grand Dowager Empress, why did you choose me?"

"First, because Tingxue chose you. Second... because I think you and I are somewhat alike."

Xiangjun hurriedly said, "How can I compare to the Grand Dowager Empress?"

"I never misjudge people. We are the same kind of people; we are not willing to admit defeat." The Grand Dowager Empress's expression was very kind, and her tone was calm as she said, "You have also heard about what happened to me back then, haven't you?"

Xiangjun hesitated and nodded. What happened to the Grand Dowager Empress back then could be considered a scandal of the imperial family.

"This subject knows a little, but the Emperor also does not allow people to discuss the Grand Dowager Empress's past, so I do not know the details very clearly."

The Grand Dowager Empress smiled self-deprecatingly and said, "Back then, I was the beloved concubine of the late Emperor.
