Although I was of low birth, the late Emperor did not care about these things and only showered me with affection. In those years, the late Emperor would take me everywhere, and even planned to make my child the Crown Prince... At that time, I was at the peak of my glory, like flowers in full bloom. But such days made me forget the danger... Due to the schemes of a vile person, the late Emperor and I fell into a trap. I fought to the death to let the late Emperor escape, but I was captured by the enemy nation... In those years, I suffered endless humiliation. At the most tragic times, I was not even as good as a camp follower; I lived in a sheep pen, subjected to unspeakable horrors..."

The Grand Dowager Empress's whole body trembled uncontrollably as she spoke.

Xiangjun unconsciously tightened her grip on the agate bracelet in her hand. Just listening to the Grand Dowager Empress's narrative made Xiangjun's heart burn with a rage.

The Grand Dowager Empress took a deep breath to calm herself down.

She looked into Xiangjun's eyes and smiled, "But even at my most tragic moments, I never thought of ending my life. I struggled desperately to survive because I had a breath of air left in me. Because of that breath, I clung to life and finally waited for the opportunity to return to Dai Qi. After I returned, the people in the imperial harem tried to use propriety and shame to force me to my death. Everyone said that I should have killed myself in Northern Mongolia to preserve the dignity of the imperial family. They said that my return was shameless and brought disgrace to the late Emperor..."

A cold glint flashed in the Grand Dowager Empress's eyes.

"But I refused to conform to their wishes. After suffering so much, why should I end my life to make those vile people happy? Since I had crawled out of hell, I would not go back. Even if I had to return, I would take everyone with me to hell. It was because of that breath, because of that hatred, that I was able to hold on and live until now."

For a moment, Xiangjun felt as if the Grand Dowager Empress in front of her had changed, as if she had become twenty years younger, returning to the time when she was the late Emperor's beloved concubine.

The hatred burning in her eyes did not make her look terrifying; instead, it made her seem to regain her youth for an instant.

Hatred, it seemed, was also a tenacious life force.

But soon, the light in the Grand Dowager Empress's eyes faded.

"Now, almost all of my enemies are dead. Only Jiang Wanrong remains, living a life worse than death. But before I die, I will definitely take her with me."

Xiangjun knew of this Jiang Wanrong. She was the birth mother of the Grand General Wang and had always been kept in the capital's Wang Mansion by the Emperor.

Jiang Taifei's health had always been poor. Although she was alive, her life was more painful than death.

The Grand General Wang had so many "divine doctors" around him. Apart from helping Xue Jiaojiao, the more important reason was that the Grand General Wang had always wanted to cure Jiang Taifei, so he searched everywhere for skilled doctors.

Xiangjun strongly suspected that Jiang Wanrong's miserable life was the doing of the Grand Dowager Empress.

The Emperor did not allow Jiang Taifei to die, using her to threaten the Grand General Wang and prevent him from rebelling easily.

So the Grand Dowager Empress could only torment her in her own way.

The Grand Dowager Empress looked at Xiangjun again. "I don't know what you have experienced in the past, but I can see that you also have a breath of air in your heart. This breath can take you far and allow you to... protect my Tingxue."

When the Grand Dowager Empress said "my Tingxue," a hint of moisture appeared in her eyes.

"Grand Dowager Empress..."

Xiangjun finally asked the question she had always wanted to ask.

"Tingxue... is he... your... child?"

Finally asking this question, Xiangjun was shocked by her own courage. Her heart was beating so fast it felt like it would jump out of her throat.

The Grand Dowager Empress's lips trembled.

She tried to speak several times but ultimately could not hide her sorrow. She lowered her eyes, and tears fell.

Those tears fell one by one onto the bedding, wetting the luxurious brocade.

"Tingxue is indeed the child I gave birth to in Northern Mongolia."

Although Xiangjun had already guessed the truth, hearing the Grand Dowager Empress say it herself was still shocking.

So Gu Tingxue was indeed the Grand Dowager Empress's child.

"And Tingxue's biological father..."

The Grand Dowager Empress gave a cold laugh. "I don't know who Tingxue's biological father is either. Maybe he was a lowly groom, or maybe a Northern Mongolian soldier... In any case, he is one of the filthiest and most despicable people in this world."

Xiangjun felt a chill run down her spine, and the hairs on her body stood on end.

This unspeakable background made Xiangjun feel a coldness in her heart.

The Grand Dowager Empress's tone turned cold.

"I found out I was pregnant two months after being captured. At first, I truly hated the child in my womb because I knew that the child I carried was the filthiest child in this world, a child who should never have been born. But at that time, I was really too miserable. I didn't want to continue living in the sheep pen; I didn't want to be tortured anymore. So I calculated the days and lied to the King of Northern Mongolia, telling him that the child I carried was the late Emperor's offspring."

Xiangjun couldn't help but admire the Grand Dowager Empress. Even in the most desperate situations, she could use everything at her disposal to improve her situation and find a chance to survive.

"If the King of Northern Mongolia knew I was pregnant, his attitude indeed changed. If I gave birth to a prince, then the child in my womb might be of great use to Northern Mongolia. Finally, I was taken out of the sheep pen and placed under temporary house arrest. I knew that if I gave birth to a daughter, my future and my daughter's future would be endlessly tragic. So I prayed to the heavens every day to give me a son. The heavens truly helped me once again, and I gave birth to a son."

chapters.title: Tingting Xue, Without the Green Pine
chapters.content:
"The envoys from Beimeng want to use the prince to demand more benefits from Daqi, but..."

Seeing the Empress Dowager fall silent,

"Do the late emperor know that this is not his child?"

The Empress Dowager's eyes held a touch of sorrow as she nodded.

"The late emperor was a benevolent ruler. He did not expose me."

"Then why did it take so many years to bring you back?"

"The imperial bloodline must never be confused. Even if the late emperor did not expose me, the timing of my pregnancy was too coincidental. Therefore, no matter what, the royal family of Daqi would not acknowledge me, and the court would also oppose compromising with Beimeng for my sake."

Xiangjun understood.

The late emperor was a benevolent ruler, so he did not expose the Empress Dowager's lie to let her live.

But also because the late emperor was a benevolent ruler, facing the opposition of the royal family and the court, he could not insist on bringing the Empress Dowager and Tingxue back.

"The late emperor was not a good emperor, but he was indeed a very good man. However, good people are often weak. Tingxue and I endured six more years before the late emperor finally brought me back. In the first year, Tingxue and I still had enough to eat and wear, but later, we lived the life of the lowest servants."

The Empress Dowager seemed to be lost in memories.

"Tingting Xue, without the green pine, the distant clouds, the world hides the white bird. On the day Tingxue was born, the snow in the north was heavy, and the world was so clean as if untouched by dust. In fact, at the moment Tingxue was born, I no longer resented this child. Because I knew that no matter who his father was, he was not a dirty child. He was my child, the child sent by heaven to save me."

Tears welled up in the Empress Dowager's eyes, falling one by one.

"My Tingxue is indeed as clean as the heavy snow on the day he was born. When he was a child, he was the purest and gentlest child in the world. He was very thoughtful and knew how to care for his mother. At a young age, he knew how to help me with chores and knew how to feel sorry for my frostbitten hands... I always felt that heaven sent him to my side to accompany me. Because of Tingxue, I was able to endure those seven years that were worse than death. But..."

The Empress Dowager reached the most painful part, and tears fell from her face like broken beads.

"I knew that if Tingxue followed me back to Daqi, he would be in danger. The royal family would not allow such a child to exist, and the emperor would not truly make him a prince. So I only said that he died on the way back and arranged for him to stay with the Gu family in Jiangnan. Originally, my Tingxue could have lived a carefree life as a young master, without worries, with children and grandchildren... But that Jiang Wanrong..."

The Empress Dowager's eyes were filled with hatred that pierced through her tears.

"If it weren't for her... how could my Tingxue have come to this!"

The Empress Dowager's chest was filled with grief and indignation, and she coughed up a mouthful of blood.

Xiangjun quickly stood up, using a handkerchief to catch the blood coughed up by the Empress Dowager. She was about to call someone in, but the Empress Dowager grabbed her hand.

"It's fine, I'm alright. Don't call anyone. I still have breath left, I won't die."

Xiangjun wiped the blood from the corner of the Empress Dowager's mouth and gave her a sip of water. The Empress Dowager's emotions finally calmed down.

Xiangjun took out a handkerchief and gently wiped the tears from the corners of the Empress Dowager's eyes.

At this moment, Xiangjun's eyes were also somewhat moist. The Empress Dowager's grief was too infectious, making it impossible for anyone to resist feeling sad with her.

Moreover, she was also a mother. How could she not understand the Empress Dowager's pain?

Seeing Xiangjun in tears, the Empress Dowager gently took her hand.

"Good child, from now on, you can call me Mother Empress, alright?"

Xiangjun was taken aback. The title of Mother Empress was only for the empress.

But she quickly realized.

This Mother Empress was not to be called with the emperor, but with Gu Tingxue.

Previously, Xiangjun had also wondered why the Empress Dowager could accept her son's concubine being entangled with another son, but now Xiangjun understood.

The Empress Dowager's feelings for Gu Tingxue were much deeper than her feelings for the emperor.

In fact, it would not be an exaggeration to say that the Empress Dowager was partial.

Moreover, the Empress Dowager had already secured the throne for the emperor, but she could not give anything to Gu Tingxue. She could only watch her son serve as a slave to another son, which naturally made her feel more guilty and want to compensate.

Therefore, whatever Gu Tingxue did, the Empress Dowager would protect him.

And the Empress Dowager's deep feelings for Gu Tingxue were seen by the emperor. With the emperor's nature of only caring about his own feelings, he would surely have many emotions about it.

No wonder the emperor's attitude towards Gu Tingxue was one of trust on one hand, and disgust and suppression on the other.

"You don't want to?" the Empress Dowager asked again.

"Mother Empress, your child is willing."

The Empress Dowager smiled gently, her gaze falling on Xiangjun's wrist.

"Do you know that the agate bracelet on your hand was originally mine?" the Empress Dowager asked.

Xiangjun quickly accepted this matter.

No wonder the Empress Dowager had such a reaction when she saw her wearing this bracelet before...

It turned out that it was not Yuanlang who exposed her relationship with Gu Tingxue. From the bracelet, the Empress Dowager had already known.

It's just that the Empress Dowager had been pretending to be ignorant until Yuanlang's attitude towards Gu Tingxue was exposed that day, and she began to bring this matter into the open.

The Empress Dowager's thoughts were deep and she was good at hiding things.

"Tingxue gave you this bracelet, which means he has chosen you. Since Tingxue has chosen you, I also consider you as one of my own. I have said before that I can give you what the emperor cannot. Now is the time to give it to you."

"What does Mother Empress want to give me?"

"Before I give it to you, I want a promise from you."

"What promise?"

"I hope that when Tingxue is in a life-and-death situation in the future, you can save Tingxue's life for me and not let him die."

Xiangjun became worried, "Is Tingxue in some kind of danger? Is it related to this rebellion suppression?"

The Empress Dowager slowly shook her head.

"This lifetime, I have figured out everyone, but I miscalculated my own son. The emperor appears to be filial and values feelings, but in reality, he is depressed and selfish. Back then, to preserve the mother-son relationship, I chose to wholeheartedly help the emperor secure his throne and consolidate power. I asked the emperor to take Tingxue with him, hoping that the emperor would take care of his younger brother and that the emperor would have someone useful and trustworthy in the future... But look at what the emperor has made Tingxue do over these years..."

The Empress Dowager sighed heavily.

"Since ancient times, how many eunuchs in power have had a good end? I am afraid that after I am gone, sooner or later, the emperor will forget his brotherly feelings and kill Tingxue."

---

chapters.title: I Will Give You the Qualifications to Fight Our Emperor
chapters.content:
The Empress Dowager's concerns were something Xiangjun had always had.

Even before knowing the relationship between the emperor and Gu Tingxue, she still did not approve of the emperor's attitude towards Gu Tingxue.

Because our emperor, like the empress, treated those who worked for him as slaves, not as people.

Xiangjun had realized this when reading history books.

Those powerful eunuchs and disastrous concubines were all the same. Since ancient times, they had to bear the blame for the foolish emperors.

Men were never wrong.

Only women and eunuchs were wrong.

Men were just tempted and deceived. As long as the wicked concubines and treacherous ministers were killed, there would still be loyal ministers and generals willing to serve and fight for them. They could still sit firmly on the throne and leave a decent reputation.

The Empress Dowager looked at Xiangjun's thoughtful expression and asked, "Have you thought of it too?"

Xiangjun nodded.

"It's not just Tingxue. Mother Empress, look at where the Empress is now? I used to think that His Majesty loved Xue Jiaojiao dearly, but now it seems... His Majesty's love for Xue Jiaojiao is no different from Emperor Xuanzong of Tang's love for Yang Guifei..."

And Yang Guifei died at Mawei Slope.

"Our emperor can sacrifice anyone for himself."

"What I am worried about is not just the emperor..." The Empress Dowager's gaze darkened.

"Is there someone else who wants Tingxue's life? Are you worried about the officials that Gu Tingxue has offended?"

"I am not worried about those people. What I am worried about is Tingxue himself. In the past, there were many things that Tingxue did not have to do for the emperor. With me here, the emperor could not truly force him. But Tingxue still did them. At that time, I knew that in his heart, he always had a thought, which was... he wanted to destroy himself."

With that, the Empress Dowager sighed heavily and looked at Xiangjun again.

"In the past year or two, he has been better and knows how to cherish his life. So, I can only beg you, don't let him die. Let him live well and happily."

"Mother Empress, even if I agree with you now, how do you know that I won't regret it in the future? I am just a concubine of the emperor. What can I use to fight against the emperor?"

"What I use to fight against the emperor, you can use to fight against him as well."

The Empress Dowager smiled calmly. That look of strategic planning made her shed her kind appearance and become sharp.

"You are different from others. I can see that you do not look down on Tingxue for being a eunuch... You treat him as a normal man. I am very grateful to you for that." The Empress Dowager looked at Xiangjun with satisfaction. "So, I believe in your words."

The Empress Dowager once again took Xiangjun's hand.

"Good child, can I trust you? Will you take care of Tingxue for me?"

This time, Xiangjun nodded without hesitation.

"This concubine is not a good person, nor a gentleman. I cannot be trusted with my words, and I am even somewhat selfish. But I have one good point, which is that I am very protective of those I care about. Once I have chosen someone, I will protect them to the end. I promise that I will not let Gu Tingxue die before me."

The Empress Dowager tightly held Xiangjun's hand.

"Good, I knew I did not misjudge you. Since that is the case, I will give you a gift that will also give you the qualifications to fight our emperor."

...

After leaving the Ren Shou Palace, Xiangjun did not speak the entire way.

Although she had received the Empress Dowager's promise and a great gift, Xiangjun still could not feel happy.

After returning to Chengxiang Palace, Yuanlang came to pester Xiangjun again. But now, looking at Yuanlang, Xiangjun felt a different kind of emotion.

Mengmei noticed that her mistress was unhappy and had Xiaoluzi take Yuanlang away to play, while she brought Xiangjun her favorite tea.

"This slave sees that you seem unhappy. Did the Empress Dowager say something to you? Mistress, don't take it to heart..."

Xiangjun shook her head.

"I am just feeling a bit emotional. The mother-son relationship in the royal family is not easy. Mengmei, I am worried that one day, Yuanlang and I might end up like the Empress Dowager and the emperor..."

"You are overthinking, Mistress. The Fifth Prince has such a good temperament, like a little sun. He is not like our emperor at all."

"But power can change a person." Xiangjun's gaze was deep. "When Yuanlang grows up, for the sake of the throne, he might turn against me."

"Although power can change a person, I think that you, Mistress, are the same as when I first met you. You have not changed."

Xiangjun gave a bitter smile. "Have I really not changed?"

"You treat us slaves like humans and are protective of your own people. Although you are usually sharp-tongued, you value feelings the most. You were like this as a child, and you are still like this now. So in this slave's heart, you have always been good."

Xiangjun was slightly comforted and sighed, "Mengmei, do you know? Our Empress Dowager is a much more formidable person than me. But now, she does not hesitate to reveal her pain to me just because she does not trust the emperor, her own son. The Empress Dowager, such a formidable person, has won against everyone but lost to her own maternal heart. I cannot help but be alert."

The Empress Dowager, in order to protect one child, had to fight against another.

Even as her life was coming to an end, she still had to scheme with all her heart.

This was still the case when the Empress Dowager had left herself a way out. If the Empress Dowager had truly given everything to the emperor without reservation, Xiangjun dared not imagine what kind of life the Empress Dowager and Tingxue would be living now.

Xiangjun grabbed Mengmei's hand and said, "If one day, I scheme against my own child for my own sake, or even... Mengmei, will you still be as good to me as you are now and be loyal to me?"

"Mistress, Mengmei is your slave and will naturally be loyal to you for a lifetime." Mengmei gently patted Xiangjun's hand. "Mistress, just do what you want to do. You can also rest assured that children need to be taught. You and the Fifth Prince are connected by love, and you will not come to that point."

"I hope so."

Just then, Xiaoluzi came in carrying the giggling Yuanlang.

"Mistress, the Fifth Prince picked a small flower and insists on giving it to you."

Yuanlang twisted his body, wanting Xiangjun to hold him.

Xiangjun pulled Yuanlang into her arms and took the small flower. Her expression finally softened again.

Forget it. It was not worth being sad over something that had not happened yet.

...

In the following days, Xiangjun, under the pretext of helping the emperor show filial piety, almost stayed at Ren Shou Palace.

Xiangjun also occasionally visited the Tai Ji Palace to see the emperor and inform him of the Empress Dowager's condition, while also bringing some tonics for the emperor.

The emperor ate the tonics brought by Xiangjun but showed some indifference to the Empress Dowager's illness.

The emperor felt that the Empress Dowager blamed him for sending Gu Tingxue to suppress the rebellion, which caused her illness.

Moreover, to force him, the Empress Dowager even had someone kill the envoy he sent to Jiangnan. This was simply slapping the emperor in the face.

"The Empress Dowager has a heart condition. You don't need to worry too much. You are now managing the harem and have so many children to take care of. You have many things to worry about. Don't tire yourself out. I will worry about you."

chapters.title: Following the Empress Dowager Truly Teaches You Things
chapters.content:
The smile on Xiangjun’s face almost froze at the emperor’s words.

Seeing the emperor’s displeasure, Xiangjun quickly said, "Though this subject is weary, Your Majesty has always governed the land with benevolence and filial piety. Now that the Empress Dowager is ill, Your Majesty cannot visit her daily due to state affairs. If this subject does not spend more time with the Empress Dowager, those meddlesome censors might criticize Your Majesty again. Only by fulfilling filial duties on Your Majesty’s behalf can you focus on governing the nation in the front court."

Only then did the emperor realize Xiangjun’s concern was valid.

Indeed, he had been too busy clashing with the Empress Dowager and had forgotten the importance of his own reputation.

"You are right, my beloved. It was an oversight on my part. You have done well."

Because of Xiangjun’s words, the emperor issued a decree: as he was concerned for the people and could not personally attend to the Empress Dowager’s illness, the palace consorts would take turns tending to her in his place.

With this imperial edict, no one could fault the emperor.

Xiangjun continued to visit the Empress Dowager daily.

Through this constant interaction, a hint of genuine affection did develop between Xiangjun and the Empress Dowager.

However, the emperor seemed reluctant for Xiangjun to grow too close to the Empress Dowager. So, Xiangjun limited her visits to a morning greeting before leaving, arranging for other consorts to attend to the Empress Dowager at other times.

Among the many consorts, the Empress Dowager favored Consort Bai the most.

Perhaps it was due to Consort Bai’s fortunate destiny, but every time she visited, the Empress Dowager’s spirits improved significantly, and she could even eat a little more.

Because Consort Bai served her well and knew how to please her, the Empress Dowager elevated Fu Bao’s status and bestowed upon her the title of "Fu," making her Consort Fu.

When she had entered the palace as a palace maid, and now, without any children, she had cheerfully and effortlessly become Consort Fu. Xiangjun had to admit that Fu Bao was indeed blessed with good fortune.

Moreover, because the Empress Dowager favored Consort Fu, the emperor no longer paid much attention to Xiangjun’s daily visits to the Ren Shou Palace.

With Consort Fu keeping the Empress Dowager company, Xiangjun finally had time to attend to other matters.

Xiangjun received news that Great General Wang had already set off to return to the northern border.

This news surprised Xiangjun. The emperor clearly did not want Great General Wang to return, so why had he suddenly changed his mind?

Fortunately, the Empress Dowager was there.

The Empress Dowager knew everything and was willing to enlighten Xiangjun.

The Empress Dowager immediately explained the underlying reason to Xiangjun.

"This year’s severe drought and locust plague mean that the Northern Mongols must also be struggling. In the past, whenever there was a natural disaster, the Northern Mongols would raid the border. It seems that the border disturbances have been severe this year, and with problems arising, the emperor had no choice but to allow Great General Wang to return."

"Hasn’t Your Majesty sent Zhou Zidu and Bai Fan there?"

"In the military, soldiers only recognize their own commander. Even if Zhou Zidu and Bai Fan are highly capable, they have only been there for less than a year. How can they replace Great General Wang? Great General Wang must return. Furthermore, for the emperor’s people to gain the soldiers’ recognition in the army, they need a victory."

Xiangjun understood.

The Empress Dowager glanced at her and smiled before asking, "Do you know why the imperial envoy sent to Jiangnan died?"

Xiangjun shook her head.

Her understanding of court politics was far inferior to the Empress Dowager’s. In fact, much of the information she received came from her brother, Xu Huanwen, through Lady Li.

"The emperor’s decision to send Great General Wang back to the northern border was not a sudden one. As soon as the locust plague began, the emperor noticed the unrest in the north. However, to fight on the front lines, military pay and provisions are needed. Disaster relief requires food, and war requires money and grain. The emperor thought of raising funds and grain from Jiangnan in advance. But the gentry of Jiangnan refused to contribute grain. Not only that, the scholars even gathered at the Temple of Literature, clutching the spirit tablets of the sages, weeping and cursing the emperor for not being a wise ruler. On the day of the temple protest, it is said that several scholars even died from knocking their heads."

Xiangjun was unaware of these events. Even her brother, Xu Huanwen, probably did not know about the developments in Jiangnan as quickly as the Empress Dowager did.

"The emperor’s envoy was poisoned when he tried to arrest those who had wept at the temple."

Xiangjun was still somewhat shocked. What kind of den of dragons and tigers was Jiangnan? The emperor’s decrees could not be enforced there, and these people even dared to kill an imperial envoy?

"You seem surprised?" the Empress Dowager asked with a smile.

Xiangjun nodded.

"Imperial authority is not as absolute as it seems. Throughout history, there have been many emperors who were reduced to figureheads. True centralization of power is rare, and those who achieve it are almost always wise rulers. My son, I fear, does not have that ability."

"Wouldn’t those people in Jiangnan be afraid after killing an imperial envoy? Wouldn’t the emperor punish them?"

"When the emperor is about to disrupt the interests of the entire Jiangnan gentry, what do they have to fear? Moreover, the officials and gentry in Jiangnan protect each other, forming an impenetrable network. The emperor sent another envoy to investigate, but so much time has passed, and the culprit has yet to be found. However, disaster relief is still unresolved, and winter is approaching. If the court does not act promptly, countless lives will be lost. With the north about to go to war, Jiangnan cannot afford to be in chaos. No matter how angry the emperor is, he has to swallow this insult and yield to me."

Xiangjun truly admired the Empress Dowager.

From the moment the locust plague appeared, the Empress Dowager had accurately predicted the emperor’s every move.

The Empress Dowager had only done two things. First, she had the officials link the natural disaster with the emperor, forcing him to take the situation seriously.

To handle the disaster, money and food were needed. Jiangnan had both, but the emperor could not control Jiangnan’s affairs. If he could not control it, he had to find someone who could.

Who could do that?

Naturally, it was Gu Tingxue, who represented the Empress Dowager.

The Empress Dowager was setting up a trump card for Gu Tingxue.

But the emperor refused to concede. He sent a trusted envoy to Jiangnan and dispatched Gu Tingxue to Beizhili to suppress a rebellion, determined to fight the Empress Dowager to the end.

So, the Empress Dowager took advantage of the impending war in the north to have the emperor’s envoy killed.

This move was truly ruthless.

With the Northern Mongols raiding Da Qi, Jiangnan could not afford to be in chaos, nor could it truly pursue the matter of the temple protest and the dead envoy. But if it was not pursued, and another envoy was sent, who would dare to risk their life investigating Jiangnan’s affairs? After all, the emperor had not pursued the death of the previous envoy.

Soon, the emperor would have to yield. Perhaps he would soon issue an edict sending Gu Tingxue to Jiangnan to raise funds and provisions.

This way, Gu Tingxue could not only leave the plague-stricken area but also more smoothly connect with the Empress Dowager’s forces, securing the political capital the Empress Dowager had prepared for him.

Xiangjun realized that following the Empress Dowager truly allowed one to learn valuable lessons!

If the Empress Dowager had not supported the emperor out of maternal affection all those years ago, but instead ruled from behind the curtain herself, where would the emperor be now?

Perhaps the entire kingdom would have been under the Empress Dowager’s control.

It was possible that the Da Qi under the Empress Dowager’s rule would have been much better governed than under the emperor’s.

The Empress Dowager looked at Xiangjun’s sparkling eyes and knew she had understood.

"I have said before that I can give you what the emperor cannot. Now, the time has come. However, obtaining this is not easy. Are you willing to take the risk and try?"

Xiangjun’s heart was pounding with excitement.

"I am willing."

---

chapters.title: My Beloved Would Be More Suited to Be This Envoy
chapters.content:
Soon, news came from the Tai Ji Hall.

The emperor issued a decree: he transferred Bai Fan, Consort Fu’s brother, to Beizhili to suppress the rebellion, and ordered Gu Tingxue to immediately leave Beizhili for Jiangnan to handle the unrest there and raise provisions for the northern war.

That night, Xiangjun brought ginseng soup to the Tai Ji Hall to visit the emperor.

After waiting for the time it took to drink two cups of tea at the entrance, Xiangjun saw her brother, Xu Huanwen, emerge from the Tai Ji Hall.

Xu Huanwen had recently been promoted, but though it was a good thing, he had been so overworked by the emperor that he had lost a lot of weight.

Xiangjun joked, "Brother, you must take care of your health. If you lose more weight, Sister-in-law will be heartbroken."

Xu Huanwen lowered his head and smiled shyly.

Seeing his expression, Xiangjun knew that her brother and his wife had a good relationship.

"Your Highness is here to visit His Majesty? His Majesty is angry about the affairs in Jiangnan. Be careful."

Xiangjun nodded, bid farewell to her brother, and had Meng Mei wait outside while she carried the food box into the Tai Ji Hall.

As soon as she entered, Xiangjun saw the emperor sitting on the dragon throne, his brows furrowed, a storm brewing on his face.

The emperor was in a foul mood.

The attending palace servants were all trembling. Seeing Noble Consort Xiang arrive, they all let out a slight sigh of relief.

These days, if there was anyone who could lighten the emperor’s mood, it was Noble Consort Xiang.

"Your Majesty, Noble Consort Xiang has arrived."

The emperor finally opened his eyes and looked at Xiangjun, his expression softening slightly.

"You’re here."

Xiangjun glanced at Eunuch Wan, signaling him to wait outside. Then she approached the emperor and softly said, "Your Majesty, allow this subject to give you a massage."

Seeing that the emperor did not refuse, Xiangjun reached out and gently began massaging his temples.

Though the emperor was annoyed, he still had some patience for Xiangjun.

"Why have you come at this time?"

"This subject heard that Your Majesty was troubled by the affairs in Jiangnan and was worried that Your Majesty might neglect your health in your distress. So, I brought ginseng soup to see you."

The emperor slowly opened his eyes and lightly took hold of Xiangjun’s hand that was massaging him. His gaze darkened for a moment.

"So, my beloved, you are well-informed about the court’s affairs? You even know that I am troubled by Jiangnan?"

Xiangjun’s expression remained calm.

"This subject was attending to the Empress Dowager’s medicine at night and accidentally overheard the Empress Dowager and her ladies-in-waiting discussing it."

The emperor’s gaze grew even darker, but he withdrew his hand, allowing Xiangjun to continue massaging his head.

"Does the Empress Dowager often talk about these things?"

"Not really. She occasionally mentions something to her ladies, and since this subject visits the Ren Shou Palace often, I have overheard a thing or two. But it’s mostly about Director Gu. Your Majesty knows that this subject and Director Gu do not get along, so the Empress Dowager stops talking whenever I am around. Today was the same, but my mind was not on these matters. As soon as I heard that Your Majesty was troubled, I came immediately."

"You are the most considerate of me."

"This subject cannot do much to help Your Majesty. Both I and my brother are from Jiangnan. With such a big incident happening there, this subject feels guilty toward Your Majesty."

The emperor gave a helpless smile.

"I won’t take my anger out on you."

However, Xiangjun’s words reminded the emperor that she was indeed from Jiangnan.

"Jiangnan is truly a good place, with talented people and beautiful landscapes. It’s a pity that not everyone in Jiangnan is like you, my beloved, bringing me joy and peace of mind."

"Jiangnan is a good place, but not all its people are good. Especially those clans—they form tight-knit groups through connections like classmates, disciples, and old acquaintances. They are very good at bullying others. My father, a mere merchant, suffered greatly at their hands."

Hearing this, the emperor became somewhat interested.

"Recently, some things have happened in Jiangnan. I would like to hear your thoughts."

The emperor briefly mentioned the death of the imperial envoy.

"This subject is not surprised. Your Majesty, you don’t know how those scholars and literati in Jiangnan behave. Because of their literary reputation and the support of their followers, they dare to interfere with court decrees, always speaking sarcastically. What’s so strange about weeping at the temple? They say even more disrespectful things in private. Moreover, they are backed by powerful clans who control everything in Jiangnan. It’s said that not even a needle can be inserted nor water poured in. Now that an imperial envoy has died in Jiangnan, this subject thinks it’s something they would dare to do. Your Majesty should take this opportunity to properly deal with them."

The emperor was genuinely surprised this time.

Xiangjun’s understanding of the Jiangnan gentry even surpassed that of many court officials.

"Your knowledge of those people in Jiangnan surprises me, my beloved."

"Your Majesty, have you forgotten this subject’s background? My father was once a great salt merchant in Jiangnan and had many dealings with those people. This subject and my brother know very well what kind of people they are."

The emperor realized that yes, Xiangjun had grown up in a wealthy family in Jiangnan, and with her intelligence, it was not surprising that she understood these things.

"If that is the case, I would also like to hear your thoughts. Jiangnan is refusing to contribute grain, and an imperial envoy has died there. What do you think I should do?"

Xiangjun felt a hidden excitement in her heart.

She knew that the opportunity she had been waiting for had finally arrived.

She must answer carefully.

"Forgive this subject for speaking out of turn, but this subject thinks that the gentry of Jiangnan all deserve to die. These people control local governments, monopolize land, evade taxes, and oppress the common people. They are capable of every kind of evil... Your Majesty, do not be fooled by Jiangnan’s prosperity. The people there live in misery."

The emperor had not expected Xiangjun to speak so passionately.

"Your father was a wealthy merchant. How can you, my beloved, have such deep sympathy for the plight of the poor?"

"Precisely because my father was a salt merchant, I know exactly what is happening in Jiangnan. My father’s courtyard was filled with many Yangzhou thin horses, all meant to be gifts for the Jiangnan gentry. Each of these women has a tragically miserable background."

Seeing that the emperor’s reaction was lukewarm when she spoke of the people’s suffering, Xiangjun began to describe the extravagant lifestyles of the Jiangnan clans.

This time, the emperor finally reacted.

Previously, the emperor had only considered the Jiangnan clans a major thorn in his side, but after hearing Xiangjun’s description, he realized that those Jiangnan clans were even wealthier than he, the emperor.

Hearing Xiangjun describe courtyards overflowing with gold, silver, and jewels, and their secret maritime trade earning countless taels of silver without paying a single tax, the emperor was furious.

These people were perhaps more like emperors than he was.

Xiangjun said angrily, "This subject thinks that Your Majesty should take drastic measures and kill all of them."

The emperor, though angry, could not help but laugh at Xiangjun’s words. He said helplessly, "The spittle of those scholars could drown me. If I do that, I fear I will be cursed for a thousand years and be remembered as a tyrant."

Xiangjun was speechless. What was the importance of one’s reputation?

So what if he was a tyrant?

She would rather be infamous for eternity than live an unremarkable life.

"Yes, Your Majesty’s concerns are valid. The people of the five prefectures in Jiangnan are all in cahoots, protecting each other as compatriots. To kill them would indeed require a bloodbath, and if the world does not understand, they might mistake Your Majesty for a tyrant... It would be better if they could be made to turn against each other, like dogs fighting among themselves."

The emperor’s expression changed suddenly, and he looked at Xiangjun with a sharp gaze.

"My beloved speaks without intention, yet you have hit the nail on the head. Yes, Jiangnan is impenetrable because the people of the five prefectures share common interests. The previous envoy, though loyal to me, did not understand Jiangnan, which is why he made such a mess of things, putting me in a passive position."

The emperor looked at Xiangjun with an almost satisfied expression.

He studied her for a long time before smiling. "I think, my beloved, that you would be more suited to be this envoy than he is. Perhaps I should send you to Jiangnan."

chapters.title: When You Return from Jiangnan, You Shall Be My Imperial Noble Consort
chapters.content:
Xiangjun pretended not to understand the emperor’s hint, putting on a coy look. “If this concubine were a man, I would surely serve Your Majesty as an imperial envoy, solving your worries and easing your burdens. I would let Your Majesty rest easy, so you wouldn’t have to toil day and night in the Tai Ji Hall. Alas, I am but a woman—all I can do is bring you ginseng soup.”

Xiangjun presented the ginseng soup to the emperor. “Your Majesty, it will grow cold if you don’t drink it soon.”

The emperor took it but set the soup aside. “I’ll drink it later.” He looked at Xiangjun, took her hand, and gently caressed it, speaking softly. “My beloved, as a woman, you cannot be an envoy, but you *can* go to Jiangnan for me and help resolve a great trouble that weighs on my heart.”

“Ah?” Xiangjun feigned shock, blinking rapidly. “But this concubine is a consort—how can I leave the palace? There has never been such a precedent.”

“Years ago, the late empress accompanied the late emperor on his military campaigns, and the empress has traveled with me to Mount Tai. As long as I permit it, the Imperial Astronomer can find a suitable excuse. It’s nothing unusual.”

Xiangjun still refused. “But what can this concubine do for Your Majesty? I know nothing. My brother is far more knowledgeable about Jiangnan—why not send him instead?”

The emperor pondered for a moment. “If I send another envoy, Jiangnan will be on guard again, and all my efforts to pacify them will have been in vain. The empire is unstable now—Jiangnan *must* not fall into chaos.”

Suddenly, the emperor lifted his gaze, fixing it on Xiangjun. His expression was one of feigned deep affection, but Xiangjun was a master of pretense herself—how could she not see through the falsity?

“My beloved, do you not wish to ease my burdens?”

The emperor’s affection concealed something darker—coldness, threat, and murderous intent. Xiangjun’s skin prickled.

Had the emperor looked at Consort Xue Jiaojiao the same way when he sent her on errands?

“You once told me you loved me with all your heart, that you would do anything for me.”

Xiangjun immediately assumed a look of fear and grievance, dropping to her knees with a thud.

“I did say that. I want to make Your Majesty proud. For you, I am willing to do anything, learn anything. I only fear I will fail and disappoint you. But if Your Majesty commands it, I shall go.”

“My Xiangjun is so clever—you can handle anything.” The emperor took her hand, helping her up. His expression softened as he soothed her. “Don’t be afraid. I will send my most trusted men with you. If you have any questions, consult them.”

“But Your Majesty’s trusted man is Minister Gu, and he has already gone to Beizhili.”

“He is not the one I mean. I will send the Tiger and Leopard Guards with you.”

Xiangjun blinked. “I’ve never heard of them. Will they be harder to work with than Minister Gu?”

The emperor smiled. “If you’re still uneasy, I’ll have Xu Huanwen go with you.”

Xiangjun slowly nodded, satisfied.

“Your Majesty, what must this concubine do in Jiangnan?”

“You won’t be going to Jiangnan first, my beloved. You will go to Beizhili.”

Xiangjun was confused—why Beizhili now?

“This locust plague began because of the empress. It should be the empress who goes to the afflicted areas to perform the ritual of swallowing locusts, to properly conclude the matter and silence the public. But the empress is currently in seclusion at the Grand Buddha Hall, fasting and praying. She cannot fulfill her duties, and besides… she is not favored by the heavens. It would be most inappropriate for her to do this. I think, since the Noble Consort is like a deputy empress in the palace, it would be most fitting for you to go to Beizhili and perform the ritual.”

Xiangjun cursed the emperor in her mind. If he wanted to silence the public, why didn’t *he* go swallow the locusts? Wasn’t he afraid she’d be poisoned and leave him with no one to do his bidding?

“After this is done, I will grant you great honor. You may return to Jiangnan to visit your family, and I will have a temporary palace built for you there. During your visit, you can act in the empress’s stead, distributing porridge to the refugees and pacifying the people of Jiangnan on my behalf. What do you think?”

Xiangjun cursed the dog emperor in her heart.

Though the locust-swallowing ritual provided a plausible excuse, making it hard for Jiangnan to suspect her, was there truly no other pretext? Did it *have* to be locusts?

Clearly, he wanted to kill two birds with one stone, exploiting her to the fullest.

“I… I am a little afraid. I’ve heard the locusts in the plague are poisonous.”

“The plague is over. The locusts now should not be poisonous. My beloved need not worry.”

Xiangjun gave a bitter smile. Of course *he* wouldn’t worry—he wasn’t the one swallowing them.

But since things had come to this, she wouldn’t back down over a little danger.

Xiangjun nodded. “Even if they are poisonous, for Your Majesty, I am willing.”

The emperor was pleased. He took her hand. “Over the next few days, I will gradually explain what you must do in Jiangnan. Rest assured, my beloved—you toil for me, and I will not fail you. When you return from Jiangnan, you shall be my Imperial Noble Consort, with a rank equal to the empress. I will also name our Yuanlang as crown prince.”

Historically, there had never been an Imperial Noble Consort when an empress still lived.

The emperor had just dangled an enormous carrot before Xiangjun.

Xiangjun’s eyes welled up.

“Why the tears?”

“I haven’t even left yet, and I already miss Your Majesty. I’m afraid… what if I never return and can never see you again?”

The emperor smiled. Fear was also one of Xiangjun’s virtues.

“You are the woman I love most. I will protect you. And the people of Jiangnan bear you no ill will. The Dowager Empress is unwell—who knows when she will no longer be able to shield them. You are the Noble Consort, a woman of Jiangnan, from a humble background, a newly risen family. Many in Jiangnan will want to align themselves with you. You must take the initiative to rally their support. There is no need to fear.”

The emperor watched as Xiangjun, though hesitant, steeled herself and nodded. He was very satisfied.

Xiangjun was different from the other consorts. Though gentle, she had the courage to take risks. The emperor could see that.

And she was ambitious.

A consort who dared to vie with the empress for power in the palace—how could she remain unmoved by such an opportunity?

Moreover, the Noble Consort had no one to rely on but the emperor himself. Her family’s status depended entirely on his favor. So using Xiangjun was the safest choice.

The empress had the support of the capital’s noble families and military factions behind her. Giving his dependent Noble Consort some influence in Jiangnan was nothing to him.

“I trust you, and I will help you. But how far you go depends on your own ability.”

The emperor looked at Xiangjun meaningfully. She slowly, but firmly, nodded.

The emperor smiled in satisfaction. He hoped his beloved consort would become his new, sharp blade.

…

After leaving the Tai Ji Hall, Xiangjun’s complex emotions had yet to settle.

Just as the Dowager Empress had predicted, it had worked.

She was actually going to leave the palace.

When she first entered the imperial city, Xiangjun had thought she would never leave. But now, she would be leaving the capital alone, to carry out the emperor’s orders.

Mengmei saw that her mistress was trembling slightly and assumed she was afraid.

“Your Grace, did the emperor frighten you?”

Xiangjun shook her head, a smile tugging at the corner of her mouth.

She looked up at the dark night sky and let out a deep breath.

“I am not afraid. It’s just… I am about to walk a path I have never trodden before. I am simply… too excited to contain myself.”

---

chapters.title: To Love Her Is to Slaughter Her Family
chapters.content:
Preparations for Xiangjun’s trip to Beizhili and Jiangnan would take some time.

These days, Xiangjun continued to attend to the Dowager Empress in the Ren Shou Palace, diligently managing the affairs of the rear palace, behaving as she always had.

The emperor was quite pleased with her calm and composed demeanor.

When the Dowager Empress learned of the emperor’s plan, she stopped mid-sip of her medicine and laughed in exasperation at her son.

She pushed away the medicine Xiangjun was feeding her, a rare cold mockery appearing on her face.

“The emperor is so considerate—even sending you all the way to Beizhili… The plague there isn’t over yet. Isn’t he afraid something might happen to you? And he even wants you to swallow locusts… Tsk. My son has always been cruel to the women he loves.”

“Your Majesty, the emperor treats Empress Xue quite well, doesn’t he?”

The Dowager Empress gave Xiangjun a sidelong glance. “Do you know why the Prince of Jin’s leg became crippled?”

Xiangjun’s curiosity was piqued. “I heard it was because he saved Empress Xue?”

“Then think—why did Xue Jiaojiao nearly die?”

Xiangjun fell silent, a chill creeping over her.

“Back then, if Xue Jiaojiao hadn’t been lucky, she would have died long ago. That woman has come close to being killed by our emperor *twice* in her life.”

“Ah?” Xiangjun covered her mouth with a handkerchief, blinking. She leaned closer to the Dowager Empress and whispered, “When was the other time?”

The Dowager Empress looked at Xiangjun’s expression and couldn’t help but laugh in disbelief.

She smiled and said, “Xue Jiaojiao’s family is a century-old noble clan. Her grandfather once supported the Prince of Jin. Even after the prince’s leg was crippled, he was still intended to become emperor. The late emperor valued the Xue family’s opinion, and Old Master Xue was certain to continue as a high-ranking official assisting the throne. So, our emperor used Xue Jiaojiao’s relationship with him to frame the Xue family for colluding with Nan Yue, plotting regicide to seize the throne, and supporting the crown prince to gain merit as a founding official…”

Xiangjun’s smile froze on her face.

“The Xue family was a pillar of the court, and Old Master Xue was a man of unyielding integrity… Though Xue Jiaojiao’s father was a bit arrogant and unrestrained, Old Master Xue was a true and loyal minister, a true pillar of the nation. The emperor should not have targeted the Xue family back then… Actually, I should have seen it then—my son has only ever cared for himself, never for justice. But… he is still my son. I had no other choice but to continue helping him.”

Xiangjun bowed her head in thought. None of this was in the book.

Was this the love the book praised so highly? On the surface, it was all flowers and moonlight, but beneath, it was filthy beyond belief.

To love someone was to slaughter their entire family, then keep them under his protection?

If that was the case, the emperor had indirectly caused the death of Xiangjun’s sister as well.

Seeing Xiangjun’s silence, the Dowager Empress thought she had frightened her.

She gently patted Xiangjun’s hand. “Are you afraid?”

Xiangjun shook her head. “No. Even so, does Your Majesty still believe the emperor truly loves Xue Jiaojiao?”

“The men and women of this world are different. When a woman’s heart is set on someone, she gives everything—love, family, country, enmity, all intertwined. But men are different. They can separate things. In matters of love, they may adore you, but that doesn’t stop them from using you to achieve their own ends. Each is its own account.”

Xiangjun was impressed. If not for the Dowager Empress, no one would understand men better than her.

The Dowager Empress suddenly furrowed her brows, as if deep in thought. After a while, she continued, “I wonder if it’s because Xue Jiaojiao survived those near-death experiences that the emperor now favors those with good luck. This time, sending you to Beizhili might also be a test—to see if you can make it through safely. If you, like Xue Jiaojiao, have good fortune…”

The Dowager Empress didn’t finish her sentence, but Xiangjun understood.

If she, too, had good fortune, the emperor would use her even more recklessly in the future, just as he had with Xue Jiaojiao.

Xiangjun’s heart sank further.

If the emperor were a thorough fool, that would be one thing. But he wasn’t.

He was intelligent, ruthless, cunning, selfish—and he held supreme power.

He was not a good man, nor a good emperor, but he was a formidable ruler.

There was no more troublesome opponent than him.

The Dowager Empress saw Xiangjun’s expression and reached out to pat her hand.

“Don’t be afraid. With me here, your journey will go smoothly. But be careful in Beizhili—the plague is still raging there, and it may worsen in winter. The physician who tends to me has gone with Tingxue. I will send a message by carrier pigeon to Tingxue, asking him to leave the physician with you before he goes to Jiangnan. You are a blessed one—don’t be afraid.”

Xiangjun nodded. “Your Majesty, rest assured. I am not one who fears death. I have gambled with my life before—this won’t be the first time. I will see this through.”

The Dowager Empress nodded, very pleased with Xiangjun’s spirit.

She truly was like her.

“Your Majesty, there is one more thing I am curious about. How did you know the emperor would definitely send me to handle this matter?” Xiangjun couldn’t help but ask.

Truthfully, when the Dowager Empress had told her to go to the emperor, Xiangjun hadn’t been entirely sure it would work. She had only tried.

She hadn’t expected it to go so smoothly.

The Dowager Empress smiled. “People in this world always rely on methods that have worked in the past. Once it succeeds, they like to use it a second time, a third time. When the emperor was just a prince, he was unremarkable among his brothers. But because of me, his mother, he gained the late emperor’s favor and nearly became crown prince. Then, after losing me, he endured hardship in the rear palace… Later, with my support, he ascended the throne. The late emperor’s capable sons were all watching him like tigers. He relied on Xue Jiaojiao, his wife, to secure his throne and suppress his political enemies. Now, I and Empress Xue are no longer useful to him—we’ve even become constraints. He wants to use you, his favored consort, to once again suppress his opponents and consolidate his power. What’s so strange about that? The emperor is simply doing again what he has done before.”

“Your Majesty truly understands the emperor.”

“Yes. So, if you do not wish to be predicted by others in the future, do not grow dependent on any person, any matter, or any method. Always leave yourself multiple paths to take, so you may forever stand unvanquished. Otherwise, you will end up like my son—after more than a decade as emperor, he is still being manipulated and calculated against.”

Watching the Dowager Empress speak so calmly about scheming against her own son, Xiangjun thought of her own Yuanlang.

“Your Majesty, do you blame the emperor?”

The Dowager Empress seemed to have anticipated this question. She smiled. “No. Emperors are supposed to be like this. Otherwise, why do all the emperors under heaven call themselves ‘the lonely one’ or ‘the widowed one’? I only have some regrets.”

“Do you regret giving up power to the emperor?”

The Dowager Empress shook her head.

“I regret giving the power of choice to the emperor. I regret believing in Tingxue’s childhood memories of the emperor’s kindness to him, misjudging the emperor’s true feelings… I was undone by my own delusions, my excessive hope that the brothers would support each other. If I could do it over, I would keep the power of choice in my own hands.”

The Dowager Empress looked at Xiangjun and gave a self-deprecating smile.

“But regret is the most useless thing. So, I hope you will not make the same mistake.”

chapters.title: You Win
chapters.content:
Xiangjun took the advice and asked again, "Your Majesty, this time when I go to Jiangnan, what do you hope I will achieve?"

The Empress Dowager pondered for a moment before replying, "Back then, it was with the support of Jiangnan that I helped my son ascend to the throne. Over the years, I have given them many benefits. What they have received far exceeds what they have given me. Now, I feel that the power in Jiangnan has become increasingly uncontrollable. Clear water harbors no fish—I do not forbid them from being greedy, but they cannot ignore the people's livelihood, as that would destabilize the nation. So, how you act and to what extent is up to you; I won’t interfere. Just one thing: Jiangnan must not fall into chaos. The Haishi trade must not be cut off."

Xiangjun nodded, understanding in her heart.

"Let me give you a few more reminders; don’t blame me for being long-winded."

"Your subject eagerly hopes for Your Majesty to teach me more."

"If the Emperor sends you, it is the same as when he used Tingxue. If you do well, he can use your hands to deal with a group of people. But if you do poorly, even if Jiangnan truly descends into unrest beyond control, it will be your fault. Sacrificing a Guifei with no background is a price he is willing to pay. Don’t forget that Empress Xue is still kneeling in the Grand Buddha Hall. So, this trip is very dangerous for you. You must grasp the balance well. Doing too well or too poorly will both be unacceptable."

"Xiangjun understands and will be careful. From the matter of the imperial envoy, I already saw that when doing tasks for His Majesty, doing well may not necessarily be rewarded, but doing poorly and dying means the Emperor will not care."

The Empress Dowager then took out a jade pendant from under her pillow and handed it to Xiangjun.

Xiangjun took it out and saw that the jade pendant was inscribed with the character "Gu" in a very special script.

"Keep this with you. When you go to Jiangnan, someone will help you. From today on, you don’t need to come to my palace anymore. Prepare well."

...

The news that Xiangjun would replace the Empress in going to Beizhili to perform the locust-swallowing ritual quickly spread throughout the harem.

Some were worried about Xiangjun, while others couldn’t wait for her to die in Beizhili.

Now, Xiangjun truly didn’t care much about the thoughts of the other women in the harem. No matter how much they cursed her, she would definitely come back alive.

She was born with a much tougher fate than ordinary people.

Unexpectedly, the Empress, who had been fasting in the Grand Buddha Hall, sent someone to find Xiangjun, saying she hoped to see her.

Xiangjun felt that the Empress’s fasting was not very sincere; she was not at all detached from worldly desires.

But since it was the Empress, Xiangjun still went to see her.

When Xiangjun arrived, the Empress was dressed in plain white clothes, kneeling before the Buddha, with her hands clasped together. She looked extremely devout and very beautiful, even more so than her usual heavily made-up appearance.

Xiangjun thought for a moment. Since this trip out of the palace was also very dangerous, she lit three incense sticks and then knelt devoutly on the prayer mat next to the Empress, praying that Heaven would protect her and ensure everything went smoothly on her journey.

"I thought you would come to see me on your own initiative," the Empress suddenly said.

Xiangjun clasped her hands together, looking at the Buddha statue in front of her, and calmly asked, "Why should your subject come to see Your Majesty?"

"Because you have won."

Xiangjun fell silent, not knowing what to say for a moment.

She didn’t have Xue Jiaojiao’s bad habit of flaunting her victory in front of the loser.

Moreover, she knew that Xue Jiaojiao had not lost yet.

Xue Jiaojiao was still useful, and the Emperor would eventually bring her out.

Xiangjun estimated that if she could return successfully from Jiangnan and accomplish her mission, the Emperor would immediately let the Empress leave the Grand Buddha Hall and continue as Empress. Perhaps he would even return the power of the harem to her.

So, Xiangjun felt there was really nothing to be proud of. She and the Emperor still had a long struggle ahead.

"Do you think the Emperor truly loves you? If he really loved you, how could he send you to perform the locust-swallowing ritual?"

Xiangjun turned her head to look at the Empress and was surprised to meet her gaze.

There was even a trace of pity in the Empress’s eyes, as well as the aloofness of a victor.

Xiangjun was shocked. Did the Empress think she had won again?

"I only now realize that having me fast in the Grand Buddha Hall is actually the Emperor’s way of protecting me. Beizhili is a plague area. The Emperor is sending you to perform the locust-swallowing ritual in my place. Can’t you see the Emperor’s intentions?"

Xiangjun was truly at a loss for words, whether to laugh or cry.

She finally understood why the Empress Dowager was annoyed with Xue Jiaojiao.

It was probably not just because of Xue Jiaojiao’s entanglement with the mother of the Grand General, Jiang Wanrong. It was also because Xue Jiaojiao’s thoughts were truly different from those of normal people.

But on second thought, Xiangjun felt she didn’t need to be so superior. She could also understand why the Empress thought this way.

In this world, women were trapped by heavy shackles, their eyes blinded. What the world allowed them to see was nothing more than love.

In her previous life, wasn’t Xiangjun the same?

If it weren’t for Heaven’s enlightenment, giving her a chance to start over, wouldn’t she have been confused and thought the Emperor loved the Empress?

If Xue Jiaojiao also had the opportunity to know that it was the Emperor who killed her entire family...

Xiangjun thought for a moment...

Forget it. Xiangjun wasn’t sure how Xue Jiaojiao would react upon knowing the Emperor killed her family. Maybe she would still think the Emperor had his reasons.

In the end, after years of pushing and pulling, chasing and being chased, they would still make up.

Xiangjun stood up, not wanting to waste her time with the Empress.

Xiangjun turned to leave but was called back by the Empress.

"Xiangjun, turn back. Let’s not fight anymore. I have taken full responsibility for this natural disaster. Why do you have to struggle so? If you are willing, I can go and tell the Emperor that I will perform the locust-swallowing ritual myself."

Xiangjun sighed deeply and turned to look at the Empress.

"Why would Your Majesty go in my place?"

"It’s not for you. This is my responsibility. I don’t want you to lose your life because of me."

Xiangjun truly didn’t understand. The Empress spoke as if she cared deeply about her life.

"Would it be bad if I died in Beizhili?"

"Xiangjun, I truly regarded you as a sister."

"If Your Majesty is so sentimental, why haven’t I heard you ask about the Fourth Prince even once since I’ve been here?"

The Empress was momentarily speechless.

"The Fourth Prince is in Ganlu Palace. Adopting Wei is looking after him for me. I am very at ease."

"If the harem is now my domain, do you think the Fourth Prince would be fine if I don’t let Ganlu Palace have a good time?"

"Yuanze is the Emperor’s most beloved child."

"If the Emperor truly loved Yuanze, he wouldn’t have separated him from his mother. Your Majesty, you don’t need to come find me again. I have nothing more to say to you. What I dislike most is people like you—wanting to be good but lacking the sentiment, wanting to be bad but not daring, deceiving yourself and others all day, putting on a pretentious show. It’s truly tiresome."

The Empress’s chest heaved, not knowing if it was from anger or incomprehension.

"Wait until you, Your Majesty, come to your senses and find me again. At that time, perhaps I will give you a chance to learn the truth."

"The truth? What truth?"

"The truth about you and me."

---

chapters.title: Killing Three Birds with One Stone
chapters.content:
The meeting with the Empress truly stirred no waves in Xiangjun’s heart.

As she walked out of the Grand Buddha Hall, Xiangjun even felt as if she had already begun to forget how much she had once hated the Emperor and the Empress.

Perhaps because in this life, she had gained and seen too much, making her previous life feel like a dream, like a past life.

Even regarding the Emperor, the man who had once humiliated and tormented her, Xiangjun felt more apprehension than hatred.

Before leaving, Xiangjun stood outside the door and looked back at the huge, solemn Buddha statues in the hall.

The Bodhisattva’s eyes were lowered, as if listening to the prayers of all beings. Empress Xue Jiaojiao, dressed in plain white, knelt among the many gods and Buddhas, yet she did not look up at them, did not seek their salvation. Instead, she stared resentfully and foolishly at the door.

At that moment, Xiangjun suddenly realized that the deep hatred she once felt for Xue Jiaojiao had vanished.

Xiangjun looked at the Buddha statue again, clasped her hands together, then turned and took Xiao Luzi’s hand.

"Let’s go. From now on, unless it’s urgent, there’s no need to report every little thing about the Empress and Ganlu Palace to me."

...

With the Emperor personally overseeing, Xiangjun’s departure from the palace was quickly arranged.

Xiangjun flipped through the intelligence reports on the prominent families of Jiangnan sent by Xu Huanwen while listening to Xiao Luzi’s report on the movements in the Six Palaces.

"Noble Consort, Consort Jian, Concubine Jiang, and Concubine Fu have arrived," Xiyu reported.

"Let them in."

Tomorrow, Xiangjun would leave the palace. Although all necessary arrangements had been made, she still needed to give some final instructions.

Consort Jian and Concubine Jiang were Xiangjun’s people, both steady and careful. Moreover, neither of them would ever side with Xiangjun’s enemies, so entrusting the harem to their joint management put Xiangjun most at ease.

"Other matters are trivial. If there are any minor conflicts among the consorts, handle them yourselves. The people in the palace now can’t stir up much trouble. But there is one thing: the Empress Dowager’s health is the most important. Concubine Fu, you must spend more time accompanying the Empress Dowager. Also, take good care of the children in the palace. Don’t let anyone with ill intentions take advantage of my absence to cause trouble."

Since Yuanlang would be alone in the palace, Xiangjun was not at ease, so she left Xiao Luzi and Xiyu behind, taking only Mengmei with her.

"Consort Jian, I entrust Yuanlang to you."

"Noble Consort, rest assured. Yuji knows that the Fifth Prince will be staying in our palace and was so happy last night that he couldn’t sleep. I will take good care of the Fifth Prince."

After instructing Consort Jian and Concubine Jiang, Xiangjun reminded Concubine Fu to take good care of the Empress Dowager, to keep her amused, and to encourage her to eat more.

"This time, when I go to Beizhili, I might see your brother, General Bai. Do you have any message you’d like me to deliver to him?"

Concubine Fu nodded eagerly, took out a letter, and handed it to Xiangjun. She also mentioned a small box, asking if it would be too much trouble for Xiangjun to take it to her brother.

Xiangjun agreed but, to avoid unnecessary trouble, had someone carefully inspect the items Concubine Fu wanted to give to her brother. When the box was opened, it turned out to be full of silver that Concubine Fu had saved, along with some rare medicines only available in the palace.

Normally, Concubine Fu was so frugal, but she was very generous with her brother.

Finally, the day of departure arrived. Since this trip to Beizhili was related to the natural disaster, a sacrificial ceremony was held before leaving the palace.

The Emperor had arranged a grand send-off for Xiangjun. Officials from the imperial court, noblewomen, and concubines from the harem were all present.

Xiangjun finally met the people who would accompany her to Beizhili and Jiangnan.

The Emperor had bestowed upon Xu Huanwen the rank of a third-grade official, Director of the Imperial Household Department, to accompany her as an imperial envoy.

In addition, the Emperor had dispatched an entire elite unit of the Tiger and Leopard Guards to protect Xiangjun.

The Tiger and Leopard Guards were the elite of the Emperor’s personal troops. The Emperor’s decision to send the elite of the elite to protect Xiangjun moved the civil and military officials, as well as the noblewomen of the court. Everyone felt that the Emperor’s love for Noble Consort was no less than his love for the Empress in the past.

The major general leading the Tiger and Leopard Guards was Wei Zhi, also known as General Wei.

Xiangjun had investigated him. General Wei was thirty-three years old this year. He had only one wife at home, not even a concubine. His relationship with his wife was excellent, and they had three sons. Although many people said his wife was a "shrew," General Wei still respected her greatly.

This showed that General Wei was an upright man with a moral standard much higher than ordinary people.

Such a person was difficult to sway; nine times out of ten, he would be extremely loyal.

Moreover, this kind of person was usually loyal to the imperial power, to the great cause of the nation in their hearts. So even if they discovered the Emperor was not a good man, they would still die for him.

This kind of pure and loyal minister was the most difficult to deal with and could not be bought.

Now that Xiangjun finally saw General Wei, she found him even sharper than she had imagined—not just an ordinary martial man.

Although he was tall and imposing, looking no different from the rough soldiers in the army, he had a pair of hawk-like eyes, extremely sharp and cautious. One look was enough to tell he was a meticulous man.

This was troublesome.

It seemed he was not only a loyal and pure minister but also a capable one.

After the sacrificial text was recited, the Emperor gave another impassioned speech in front of everyone, praising Xiangjun’s great righteousness, which gave Xiangjun goosebumps.

The Emperor’s implication was that Xiangjun was going to Beizhili to swallow locusts for the nation...

Although she felt much disdain in her heart, Xiangjun still used all her acting skills to play along with the Emperor.

When she felt the Emperor had performed enough, Xiangjun reluctantly and tearfully glanced at the Emperor, then turned and boarded the carriage without looking back, leaving through the Meridian Gate.

The carriage slowly traveled along the main road of the capital. The common people coming and going saw the procession and without exception knelt and bowed.

As they left the palace, the closer Xiangjun’s carriage got to Beizhili, the more she could feel the devotion of the common people. There were always people kneeling along the road.

Xiangjun felt something was wrong and immediately ordered Xu Huanwen to investigate. Soon, Xu Huanwen reported that the Emperor had long ago sent an urgent message by eight-hundred-li express post, informing the people of the empire that the Noble Consort was going to Beizhili to perform the locust-swallowing ritual.

The Emperor had made such a grand spectacle, as if once Xiangjun went and swallowed the locusts, the natural disaster and plague would completely end.

The closer they got to Beizhili, the harder the lives of the common people became.

The more suffering the people endured, the more devoutly they knelt and bowed.

Seeing the people’s devotion, Xiangjun’s mood grew heavy.

If she performed the locust-swallowing ritual this time, but the natural disaster did not end and instead became even more severe, no one would blame the Emperor. They would only blame her.

The Emperor had elevated Xiangjun so highly that when she fell, she would fall even harder.

In the end, the natural disaster would once again become the fault of this Guifei.

With this trip accomplished, no matter how the natural disaster developed, it would have nothing to do with the Emperor.

The Emperor’s decision to send Xiangjun out of the palace was not killing two birds with one stone—it was killing three.

The weather was already very cold. Xiangjun saw in the distance a commoner wrapped in tattered clothes, with straw stuffed inside, devoutly kowtowing toward the procession.

For some reason, the image of the Bodhisattva statue with lowered eyebrows that she had seen in the Grand Buddha Hall before leaving the palace appeared in her mind.

She didn’t know if the heavenly gods and Buddhas had heard so many devout prayers, but she had.

"Mengmei, have someone send clothes and some loose silver to that person."

"Yes."

After lowering the carriage curtain, Xiangjun closed her eyes solemnly.

Xiangjun could not save all the unfortunate people before her. But sooner or later, the source of that misfortune would die by her hand.
